ITID-11111.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing email — sent to many unrelated recipients with no individual tailoring — whose delivery mechanism or payload type has not yet been determined.
ITID-11111.purpose: Catch-all for reported mass/bulk phishing emails that do not yet contain enough detail to classify under a more specific Mass Phishing Attacks leaf.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported bulk phishing email before the delivery mechanism has been examined
Bulk campaigns spanning multiple mechanisms that don't cleanly fit one sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Any case where the delivery mechanism has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11112 through ITID-11118
Phishing individually tailored to a specific person or small group (Targeted (Spear) Phishing Attacks, ITID-1112x)
ITID-11111.severity: Low-to-Medium by default; reassess once the delivery mechanism and any interaction are known.
ITID-11111.escalation: Escalate if any recipient confirms interaction or campaign volume suggests a coordinated push against the organization.
indicators: Multiple unrelated employees reporting near-identical unsolicited emails
SEG bulk-similarity clustering flags a spike in structurally similar messages
vectors: Bulk email sent from spoofed or throwaway sending infrastructure
rootCauses: Email delivered despite gateway filtering due to novel sending infrastructure or content evasion
controls: Secure email gateway (SEG) filtering
User-reported phishing button/mailbox
ITID-11111.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting and SEG bulk-clustering heuristics until a mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-11111.response: Triage promptly to determine delivery mechanism and reclassify to the appropriate sibling leaf; block sender/domain at the gateway.
metrics: Count of unclassified mass phishing reports pending reclassification
Time-to-reclassify from initial report
ITID-11111.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one — cases here should be reclassified within a short SLA once the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified Mass Phishing Triage
playbook.description: Short triage-to-reclassification playbook — resolves a mass phishing campaign's delivery mechanism and hands it off to the matching sibling ITID's own playbook rather than carrying full response steps of its own.

steps.title: Confirm this is mass (non-targeted) phishing
steps.desc: Check recipient count and pattern to rule out spear phishing or whaling.
steps.outcome: Confirmed broad, non-individualized targeting.

steps.title: Block sender/domain pending reclassification
steps.desc: Block the sending domain or infrastructure network-wide as a precaution while classification is pending.

steps.title: Reclassify into the matching sibling ITID
steps.desc: Update the case's ITID to the specific sibling (Attachment, Link, AiTM, QR, Brand Impersonation, Fake Update, or Malvertising) and hand off to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Case now carries a specific, actionable ITID.
steps.abort: If no sibling fits after full review, leave classified here and document why in case notes.

steps.title: Confirm no recipient interaction occurred
steps.desc: Check click/open telemetry before closing under this catch-all classification.

steps.title: Log the reclassification outcome
steps.desc: Record which sibling ITID was ultimately used — a persistently high count of unresolved cases here signals a triage gap, not rising mass-phishing volume.

steps.title: Identify the delivery mechanism
steps.desc: Review message content for attachment, link, QR code, or brand-impersonation lure pattern.
steps.guidance: Check for a macro-enabled attachment, a link (static vs. proxying), an embedded QR image, or a recognizable brand/service impersonation theme.
steps.outcome: Delivery mechanism identified, or confirmed genuinely unresolvable within this triage cycle.

ITID-11112.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing email carrying a malicious attachment (macro-enabled document, malicious archive, disguised executable, etc.) intended to compromise the recipient's device on open.
ITID-11112.purpose: Captures mass phishing that relies on a malicious file attachment as the payload delivery mechanism, distinguishing it from link-based and other mass phishing siblings.
scopeIncludes: Bulk email with a macro-enabled Office document, malicious PDF, or disguised executable attachment
Malicious archive (ZIP/ISO) attachments used to evade attachment scanning
scopeExcludes: Targeted attachment phishing aimed at a specific individual (ITID-11122)
The attachment being swapped into a previously legitimate/cloned message thread (ITID-11135)
ITID-11112.severity: Medium; escalates to High if any recipient opened the attachment and macros/executables ran.
ITID-11112.priority: P2 if execution is confirmed, otherwise P3.
ITID-11112.escalation: Escalate immediately to the SOC/IR team if telemetry shows the attachment executed on any endpoint.
indicators: Multiple users reporting the same attachment-bearing email
EDR alert for a spawned process from an Office application shortly after email delivery
vectors: Macro-enabled Office document requiring the user to enable content
Password-protected archive attachment (evading gateway scanning) containing an executable
rootCauses: Macro execution not blocked by policy on documents from the internet
Attachment sandboxing not covering password-protected archives
controls: Attachment sandboxing/detonation
Macro execution blocking policy for internet-sourced documents
EDR on endpoints
ITID-11112.detection: Attachment sandboxing and EDR process-lineage alerting provide strong technical coverage.
ITID-11112.response: Sandbox-detonate the attachment, isolate any endpoint where it executed, and purge the email from all mailboxes.
metrics: Count of malicious-attachment mass phishing emails blocked/reported per month
Number of endpoints with confirmed execution
ITID-11112.notes: Where a sibling report shows the same lure text but a link instead of an attachment, log it separately under ITID-11113 — payload type is the differentiator here.

playbook.name: Malicious Attachment Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for mass phishing delivering a weaponized attachment (macro document, protected archive, ISO/LNK dropper, or HTML smuggling).

steps.title: Collect and identify the attachment
steps.desc: Retrieve the attachment and confirm file type and hash.

steps.title: Quarantine and hash-block the attachment
steps.desc: Quarantine the attachment across the email environment and block its hash organization-wide.

steps.title: Isolate any endpoint where the attachment was opened
steps.desc: For any recipient who opened the attachment, isolate the endpoint pending EDR review.
steps.abort: If telemetry confirms the attachment was never opened, this step is not required — proceed to recovery.

steps.title: Restore or clear affected endpoints
steps.desc: Reimage any endpoint with confirmed execution; lift isolation on endpoints confirmed clean.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints returned to a verified-clean state.

steps.title: Review sandbox detection efficacy
steps.desc: If the attachment evaded sandbox scanning, file a detection-gap ticket with the sample details.

steps.title: Determine macro/script presence
steps.desc: Static analysis or sandbox detonation to confirm whether the attachment contains active macro or script content.
steps.outcome: Malicious/benign determination with a supporting hash and behavior summary.

steps.title: Identify all recipients
steps.desc: Message trace to determine every recipient of the campaign.

steps.title: Confirm whether macro/script executed
steps.desc: Review process lineage for Office or archive utilities spawning a script interpreter.

ITID-11113.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing email containing a link to a fake login page designed to capture usernames and passwords directly, without a real-time relay to the legitimate service.
ITID-11113.purpose: Captures mass phishing that drives recipients to a static credential-harvesting page, as distinct from attachment-based, AiTM, or QR-code delivery.
scopeIncludes: Bulk email linking to a static fake login page hosted on attacker infrastructure or a compromised legitimate site
Cases where a static credential form was found but no session-token relay/proxy behavior was observed
scopeExcludes: Kits that proxy the login in real time and capture session tokens/MFA (ITID-11114, Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kit Campaign)
Targeted link phishing aimed at a specific individual (ITID-11123)
Ongoing use of harvested credentials for account takeover, which rolls up under the relevant Unauthorized Access/Credential-Based Attacks ITID once compromise is confirmed
ITID-11113.severity: Medium; escalates to High if any recipient confirms credential submission.
ITID-11113.priority: P2 if submission is confirmed, otherwise P3.
ITID-11113.escalation: Escalate to IAM/SOC immediately upon confirmed credential submission to force a password reset and review account activity.
indicators: Multiple users reporting the same lure email with a login-page link
Web proxy logs showing employee visits to a newly registered lookalike domain
vectors: Lookalike domain hosting a cloned login form
Compromised legitimate website hosting a hidden phishing page
rootCauses: URL rewriting/sandboxing not catching a newly registered domain at time of delivery
Lack of phishing-resistant MFA allowing a bare password to be sufficient for access
controls: URL rewriting and time-of-click sandboxing
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring and takedown
ITID-11113.detection: URL rewriting logs and web proxy telemetry give good visibility into who clicked and whether the page was reached.
ITID-11113.response: Force password reset for any user who submitted credentials, review account sign-in logs, and request domain takedown.
metrics: Count of credential-harvesting mass phishing emails per month
Number of confirmed credential submissions
ITID-11113.notes: Scoped to exclude AiTM/session-relay kits (ITID-11114) since those carry materially different response steps (session revocation, not just password reset).

playbook.name: Malicious Link Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for mass phishing delivering a link to a static (non-proxying) credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Extract and defang the URL
steps.desc: Pull the malicious URL from the message and check proxy/web-gateway logs for hits.

steps.title: Block the destination domain network-wide
Contact users with confirmed clicks
steps.desc: Reach out directly to determine whether credentials were submitted on the page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status for every recipient who clicked.

steps.title: Verify no anomalous sign-in activity
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs for affected accounts for any unrecognized access.

steps.title: Review URL filtering efficacy
steps.desc: Assess whether the domain category should have been blocked proactively.

steps.title: Confirm the destination is a static credential-harvesting page
steps.desc: Visit the destination in an isolated analysis environment to confirm it is a static form, not a live reverse-proxy — if it relays a real MFA challenge, treat as ITID-11114 (AiTM) instead.
steps.abort: If the page relays a live authentication session, stop and switch to the AiTM playbook immediately.

steps.title: Identify recipients and click activity
steps.desc: Use proxy logs to determine which recipients clicked the link.

steps.title: Escalate confirmed credential submissions
steps.desc: If submission is confirmed, escalate to the Credential-Based Attacks track (ITID-12111), force a password reset, and revoke active sessions.
steps.abort: If no submission is confirmed, this step is not required.

ITID-11114.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing campaign using a reverse-proxy phishing kit (e.g. Evilginx-style) that transparently relays the victim's real credentials and MFA approval to the legitimate service while capturing the resulting session cookie for account takeover.
ITID-11114.purpose: Captures mass phishing delivered via an adversary-in-the-middle (reverse-proxy) kit that relays the real login flow and steals live session tokens, bypassing standard MFA.
scopeIncludes: Mass-distributed lure linking to a known or suspected AiTM/reverse-proxy phishing kit
Confirmed theft of a session cookie/token via a proxied login flow
scopeExcludes: Static credential-harvesting pages with no session relay (ITID-11113)
Targeted/individual AiTM campaigns (ITID-11124, ITID-11148)
Web-based phishing specifically for standalone MFA tokens outside a full AiTM relay (ITID-12610 family, Phishing for MFA Tokens)
Ongoing use of the stolen session token for account access, which rolls up under Unauthorized Access ITIDs once account takeover is confirmed
ITID-11114.severity: High — AiTM defeats standard OTP/push MFA, making this materially more severe than static credential phishing.
ITID-11114.priority: P1 upon confirmed session token theft, otherwise P2.
ITID-11114.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to revoke active sessions and refresh tokens for any affected account, not just reset the password.
indicators: Sign-in logs showing a successful MFA-satisfied login from an unfamiliar ASN/IP immediately after a phishing click
Reverse-proxy fingerprint (TLS/JA3, hosting pattern) matching known AiTM kits
vectors: Reverse-proxy phishing kit relaying a real identity-provider login page
Lookalike domain fronting the proxy
rootCauses: Standard OTP/push MFA in use instead of phishing-resistant MFA
Session tokens not bound to device/IP, allowing reuse from a different location
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Session/token binding and conditional access risk policies
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring
ITID-11114.detection: Identity provider sign-in risk signals and session-anomaly detection give strong coverage once the token is used.
ITID-11114.response: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for the affected account immediately, then force credential reset and review post-auth activity for lateral movement.
metrics: Count of confirmed AiTM session-token thefts per quarter
Median time from token theft to session revocation
ITID-11114.notes: Deliberately scoped as the initial-access/session-theft event only; anything the attacker does after taking over the session (mailbox rule abuse, data exfiltration) should be logged under the relevant Unauthorized Access or Data Breach ITID to avoid double-counting the same incident under two branches.

playbook.name: AiTM Phishing Kit Campaign Response
playbook.description: High-priority response playbook for mass phishing using a reverse-proxy kit capable of relaying live MFA and stealing session tokens. Materially different from static credential harvesting — a password reset alone does not remediate this.

steps.title: Confirm AiTM kit infrastructure
steps.desc: Correlate the destination domain against known AiTM kit fingerprints via threat intel.

steps.title: Block the destination domain immediately
Revoke the affected session/token
steps.desc: Force full re-authentication for the affected account. A password reset alone is not sufficient remediation.

steps.title: Confirm no anomalous access remains
steps.desc: Re-verify account access is clean before restoring normal use.

steps.title: Add kit infrastructure to threat-intel blocklist
steps.desc: Feed the confirmed kit fingerprint into the organization's threat-intel blocklist for earlier detection next time.

steps.title: Review identity provider sign-in logs
steps.desc: Check for any completed authentication (including MFA) against the flagged domain.
steps.outcome: List of accounts, if any, that completed authentication against the phishing kit.

steps.title: Escalate any confirmed MFA completion
steps.desc: Treat the resulting session as compromised immediately — do not wait for confirmed misuse before escalating.
steps.outcome: Incident response engaged for every account that completed authentication.

steps.title: Review the session's full activity window
steps.desc: Check sign-in and application-access logs for the session before revocation to scope any downstream access.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker activity during the live session established.

steps.title: Assess phishing-resistant MFA rollout
steps.desc: Evaluate prioritizing FIDO2/WebAuthn for affected users given the confirmed MFA-bypass technique.

ITID-11115.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing email or flyer containing a QR code that, when scanned (typically with a personal/unmanaged mobile device), directs the victim to a credential-harvesting or malware-delivery page.
ITID-11115.purpose: Captures mass phishing that delivers its malicious link via an embedded QR code rather than a clickable hyperlink, which evades link-scanning controls and shifts the click to an unmanaged mobile device.
scopeIncludes: Bulk email with an embedded QR code linking to a phishing page
Printed/physical flyers distributed broadly that use a QR code lure (when reported through the security channel)
scopeExcludes: Targeted QR code phishing aimed at a specific individual (ITID-11129)
QR codes used as a cross-channel bridge in a broader hybrid physical/digital attack (ITID-11915)
QR-code-based MFA enrollment phishing that targets an already-authenticated session (ITID-12617, MFA Bypass domain)
ITID-11115.severity: Medium; elevated because the scan typically occurs on an unmanaged personal device outside corporate security controls.
ITID-11115.priority: P2 if scanned/reported as successful, otherwise P3.
ITID-11115.escalation: Escalate if a corporate credential was entered after a scan, since the entry point (personal device) is outside standard endpoint telemetry.
indicators: Multiple users reporting the same QR-code-bearing email or flyer
Redirect-service logs showing a spike in scans of the embedded short-link
vectors: QR code embedded in an email image (evading text-based link scanning)
QR code printed on a physical poster/flyer placed in or near the workplace
rootCauses: Email security tooling not decoding and scanning QR code image content
No policy guidance discouraging corporate credential entry after a personal-device QR scan
controls: QR code decoding/scanning in the secure email gateway
User awareness training on QR code risks
Conditional access blocking sign-in from unmanaged devices
ITID-11115.detection: Limited — depends on gateway QR-decoding capability and user reporting; scans on personal devices are largely invisible to corporate telemetry.
ITID-11115.response: Decode and analyze the QR destination, block the domain, and check identity provider logs for any resulting sign-in attempt.
metrics: Count of QR code phishing reports per month
Percentage of email security tooling coverage with QR decoding enabled
ITID-11115.notes: Scoped to the mass/untargeted case; a QR code lure crafted for one specific individual should be logged under ITID-11129 instead to keep targeting-level reporting accurate.

playbook.name: QR Code Phishing (Quishing) Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for mass phishing delivering its lure as a QR code, typically pivoting to a personal or lightly-managed mobile device.

steps.title: Decode the QR code
steps.desc: Extract the destination URL from the reported QR code (email image, PDF, or physical lure).

steps.title: Block the destination domain network-wide
Follow the matching destination-type playbook
steps.desc: If the destination matches a known AiTM or credential-harvesting pattern, follow that ITID's own eradication steps for any confirmed interaction.

steps.title: Confirm no corporate credential use on the scanning device
Log the delivery channel
steps.desc: Record whether the lure was digital (email/PDF) or physical (printed) to inform awareness training focus.

steps.title: Reputation-check the destination and determine campaign type
steps.desc: Determine whether the destination is a static credential-harvesting page, an AiTM kit, or another pattern.
steps.abort: If the destination relays a live authentication session, switch to the AiTM playbook (ITID-11114).

steps.title: Check managed-device telemetry
steps.desc: Determine via MDM whether the code was scanned on a corporate-managed device.

ITID-11116.def: An untargeted, bulk-sent phishing email that impersonates a recognizable brand or online service — using its logo, tone, and typical notification format — to induce the recipient to click through, regardless of the specific payload mechanism used.
ITID-11116.purpose: Captures mass phishing whose primary lure is impersonation of a well-known brand or service (shipping carrier, streaming service, cloud provider) rather than a specific delivery mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Bulk phishing using convincing brand/service visual and textual impersonation as the primary social-engineering lever
Cases where brand impersonation is the defining characteristic even though the technical payload also fits another sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases where a fake software/browser update is the specific lure theme (ITID-11117)
Targeted brand-impersonation phishing built specifically around one individual (Targeted Spear Phishing branch, ITID-1112x)
Impersonation of a specific colleague or internal identity (Vishing Impersonation Attack branch covers the voice-channel equivalent, ITID-1121x)
ITID-11116.severity: Low-to-Medium; severity depends more on payload/interaction than on the impersonation theme itself.
ITID-11116.escalation: Escalate per the confirmed payload type (attachment, link, etc.) if interaction is confirmed.
indicators: Users reporting an unexpected notification from a service they don't use or an account they don't have
Brand-name lookalike domain registered recently
vectors: Spoofed shipping/delivery notification
Spoofed subscription renewal or payment-failure notice
rootCauses: Brand/domain-abuse monitoring not catching a newly registered lookalike domain quickly
Users not verifying sender domain against the real brand's known domains
controls: Brand/domain-abuse monitoring and takedown
SEG filtering
User awareness training
ITID-11116.detection: Relies on user reporting and brand-monitoring services; technical payload determines deeper telemetry coverage.
ITID-11116.response: Confirm the actual payload/mechanism used, handle per that mechanism's response steps, and submit the lookalike domain for takedown.
metrics: Count of brand-impersonation phishing reports per month by impersonated brand
ITID-11116.notes: This leaf tags the social-engineering theme (brand impersonation); the actual payload should still be checked against ITID-11112/11113/11114/11115 for response purposes where it clearly fits one of those.

playbook.name: Brand/Service Impersonation Phishing Triage
playbook.description: Triage playbook for mass phishing recognized first by its brand-impersonation lure theme, ahead of confirming the underlying payload mechanism.

steps.title: Identify the impersonated brand and lure theme
steps.desc: Determine which brand/service is impersonated and the lure angle (delivery notice, subscription renewal, account suspension, etc.).

steps.title: Block the sending domain/infrastructure
Reclassify into the matching payload-specific sibling ITID
steps.desc: Hand off to Attachment, Link, AiTM, QR, or Fake Update playbook once the payload mechanism is confirmed.
steps.abort: If the impersonation angle remains the most operationally useful classification, leave as-is and document why.

steps.title: Confirm no recipient interaction before closing
Track most-impersonated brands
steps.desc: Log the impersonated brand for trend reporting and targeted awareness training.

steps.title: Determine the underlying payload mechanism
steps.desc: Review message content for attachment, link, or QR code to identify the actual delivery vector.
steps.outcome: Payload mechanism identified for reclassification.

ITID-11117.def: An untargeted phishing email or web pop-up impersonating a software vendor or browser update notification, inducing the victim to download and run a malicious installer disguised as a legitimate update.
ITID-11117.purpose: Captures mass phishing specifically themed as a fake software or browser update prompt, a lure pattern strongly associated with drive-by malware delivery rather than credential harvesting.
scopeIncludes: Bulk email claiming an urgent browser/plugin/OS update is required, linking to a malicious installer
Fake update themes delivered via email as opposed to a compromised website pop-up (see ITID-11118 for the web-delivery variant)
scopeExcludes: Fake update pop-ups served via malicious ads or poisoned search results on a webpage (ITID-11118, Malvertising/Poisoned Search Result Phishing)
General brand impersonation lures with no update/installer theme (ITID-11116)
ITID-11117.severity: Medium-to-High — this lure pattern typically delivers executable malware directly rather than just harvesting credentials.
ITID-11117.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if installer execution is confirmed on any endpoint.
ITID-11117.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR upon any confirmed installer execution given the direct malware-delivery risk.
indicators: Users reporting an unsolicited update prompt received by email
EDR alert for an unsigned installer executed shortly after email delivery
vectors: Email impersonating a browser vendor with a link to a fake update installer
Disguised executable named to resemble a legitimate updater
rootCauses: Application control/allowlisting not blocking unsigned installers
Users accustomed to legitimate update prompts and not verifying source
controls: Application allowlisting/control
EDR on endpoints
SEG filtering
ITID-11117.detection: EDR execution telemetry gives strong coverage once the installer runs; email-stage detection depends on SEG heuristics.
ITID-11117.response: Isolate any endpoint where the installer ran, capture and analyze the payload, and block the distribution domain.
metrics: Count of fake-update phishing reports per month
Number of endpoints with confirmed installer execution
ITID-11117.notes: Scoped to the email-delivery variant of this lure theme; the same fake-update lure served via a compromised web page or ad is logged under ITID-11118 instead, since the response steps (browser/ad-network angle) differ.

playbook.name: Fake Software/Browser Update Phishing Response
playbook.description: High-priority response playbook for mass phishing that induces a victim to manually download and run a fake update or installer — a direct-execution lure with materially higher compromise likelihood than a passive click.

steps.title: Identify the source page/lure
steps.desc: Determine the web page or prompt that presented the fake update/CAPTCHA/verification lure.

steps.title: Block the source domain network-wide
Capture and analyze the downloaded artifact
steps.desc: Determine the malware family and capability of the executed payload.

steps.title: Restore or reimage confirmed-compromised endpoints
steps.desc: Reimage where compromise is confirmed; lift isolation once verified clean.

steps.title: Review local admin rights exposure
steps.desc: Assess whether affected users held local admin rights sufficient to install software.

steps.title: Review EDR for installer or script execution
steps.desc: Check any endpoint that visited the page for an unexpected installer download or clipboard-paste-and-run command execution.

steps.title: Isolate any endpoint with confirmed execution
steps.desc: Immediately isolate any endpoint where the fake installer or pasted command actually ran.
steps.abort: If no execution is confirmed, isolation is not required.

steps.title: Remove persistence and confirm clean state
steps.desc: Remove any established persistence mechanism and verify a clean state via EDR.

ITID-11118.def: A phishing or malware-delivery page reached when an employee clicks a malicious search-engine ad or a poisoned organic search result — commonly for common software downloads — rather than through an emailed lure.
ITID-11118.purpose: Captures mass phishing reached via malicious advertising or poisoned search-engine results rather than email, reflecting a fundamentally different delivery channel from the rest of this Type.
scopeIncludes: Employee reaching a phishing/malware page via a sponsored search ad
Employee reaching a phishing/malware page via an SEO-poisoned organic search result for a common software download
scopeExcludes: The same fake-update lure theme delivered by email (ITID-11117)
Any email-delivered lure regardless of theme (the other Mass Phishing Attacks leaves)
ITID-11118.severity: Medium-to-High, particularly for poisoned results targeting IT/admin tool downloads used by privileged users.
ITID-11118.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a privileged user's device is affected.
ITID-11118.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR immediately if the download executed, and to IT if the search terms suggest targeting of admin tooling.
indicators: Web proxy logs showing a click from a search results page to a newly registered domain
EDR alert for a downloaded installer immediately following browser search activity
vectors: Malicious sponsored search ad for a popular free tool
SEO-poisoned result ranking a malicious download page above the legitimate vendor site
rootCauses: Web filtering not blocking newly registered or low-reputation domains at time of visit
No policy directing users to a curated internal software catalog instead of open web search for downloads
controls: Web/DNS filtering with newly-registered-domain blocking
Application allowlisting
Internal curated software catalog
ITID-11118.detection: Web proxy and EDR telemetry give reasonable coverage; the search-ad/SEO stage itself is not directly monitored.
ITID-11118.response: Isolate any endpoint where the download executed, block the domain, and report the malicious ad/listing to the ad network or search engine.
metrics: Count of malvertising/SEO-poisoning incidents per quarter
Number of endpoints with confirmed malicious download execution
ITID-11118.notes: This is the only Mass Phishing Attacks leaf where email is not the delivery channel; kept distinct because response steps (ad-network reporting, web filtering) differ materially from email-based siblings.

playbook.name: Malvertising/Poisoned Search Result Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for phishing or malware delivery reached via a malicious advertisement or SEO-poisoned search result rather than a direct message — no email artifact exists to scan.

steps.title: Identify the malicious ad/search result and destination
steps.desc: Use web/proxy logs to identify the ad or search result and its destination.

steps.title: Block the destination domain/advertiser
Isolate endpoints with confirmed downloads
steps.desc: Isolate any endpoint with a confirmed download pending EDR review.

steps.title: Restore or reimage confirmed-compromised endpoints
steps.desc: Lift isolation for endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Report the malicious listing for takedown
steps.desc: Report the ad or search result to the hosting ad network or search engine.

steps.title: Determine payload type at the destination
steps.desc: Confirm whether the destination delivers a credential-harvesting page or a malware download.

steps.title: Identify all endpoints with traffic to the destination
Capture and analyze the downloaded artifact

ITID-11121.def: A phishing email crafted and sent to a specific, identifiable individual or small group — using personal or organizational detail to increase credibility — whose delivery mechanism has not yet been confirmed.
ITID-11121.purpose: Catch-all for a reported spear phishing attempt targeted at a specific individual or small group where the delivery mechanism has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported targeted phishing email before the mechanism is examined
scopeExcludes: Any case where the mechanism has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11122 through ITID-11129
Untargeted bulk phishing (Mass Phishing Attacks, ITID-1111x)
Targeting specifically a senior executive (Whaling Attacks, ITID-1114x)
ITID-11121.severity: Medium by default given the deliberate targeting; reassess once mechanism and any interaction are known.
ITID-11121.escalation: Escalate to the SOC promptly given that targeting implies a specific, motivated actor rather than opportunistic spam.
indicators: Email content referencing accurate, non-public details about the recipient or their role
A single employee reporting a uniquely tailored suspicious email with no matching reports from others
vectors: Personalized email referencing the target's role, project, or recent activity
rootCauses: Publicly available OSINT (LinkedIn, press releases, org charts) enabling credible personalization
controls: SEG filtering
User awareness training on targeted phishing
ITID-11121.detection: Limited — targeted, low-volume email is harder for bulk heuristics to catch; relies heavily on user reporting.
ITID-11121.response: Triage promptly to determine mechanism and reclassify; assess why this individual was targeted.
metrics: Count of unclassified targeted phishing reports pending reclassification
ITID-11121.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify once the delivery mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified Spear Phishing Triage
playbook.description: Short triage-to-reclassification playbook — confirms genuine individualized targeting and identifies the delivery mechanism before handing off to the matching sibling playbook.

steps.title: Confirm genuine individualized targeting
steps.desc: Check recipient count and message personalization to rule out a mass campaign.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message was crafted for one or a few specific individuals.

steps.title: Block sender/domain/infrastructure pending reclassification
Reclassify into the matching sibling ITID
steps.desc: Hand off to the specific sibling playbook once the delivery mechanism is confirmed.
steps.abort: If no sibling fits after full review, leave classified here and document why.

steps.title: Confirm no interaction occurred
Log the reclassification outcome and targeting rationale
steps.desc: Record the outcome for threat-intel tracking of targeted-attack attempts against this organization, regardless of technique.

steps.title: Check for a pattern of targeting
steps.desc: Determine whether other individuals with a similar role or access level were also targeted, suggesting a broader campaign against a role rather than one person.

steps.title: Identify the delivery mechanism
steps.desc: Review message content and headers for attachment, link, AiTM behavior, spoofing vs. compromise, or QR code.

ITID-11122.def: A phishing email sent to a specific individual, carrying a malicious attachment whose filename or content is tailored to reference that individual's role, project, or context.
ITID-11122.purpose: Captures spear phishing that uses a malicious attachment tailored to a specific individual, as opposed to a link-based or other targeted delivery mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Attachment referencing a real project name, contract, or internal document the target would plausibly expect
Malicious attachment sent as a targeted follow-up after OSINT research on the recipient
scopeExcludes: Untargeted mass-attachment phishing with no individual tailoring (ITID-11112)
The attachment being swapped into a hijacked or cloned prior legitimate thread (ITID-11135, Clone Phishing)
ITID-11122.severity: High — targeting plus a malware payload represents a materially elevated risk over generic mass phishing.
ITID-11122.priority: P1 if execution is confirmed, otherwise P2.
ITID-11122.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR; treat as a potentially motivated, targeted intrusion attempt rather than routine spam.
indicators: Attachment filename referencing a real, specific project or document the recipient would recognize
EDR alert for a spawned process from an Office application on the targeted user's device
vectors: Tailored document lure (e.g., a fake contract or invoice referencing a real vendor relationship)
rootCauses: Excessive publicly available detail about projects/vendors enabling credible tailoring
Macro execution not blocked by policy
controls: Attachment sandboxing/detonation
Macro execution blocking policy
EDR on endpoints
ITID-11122.detection: EDR and sandboxing give good coverage once the attachment is opened; the targeted email itself is hard to catch pre-delivery.
ITID-11122.response: Sandbox-detonate the attachment, isolate any endpoint where it executed, and investigate why this individual was specifically targeted.
metrics: Count of targeted attachment phishing incidents per quarter
Number of endpoints with confirmed execution
ITID-11122.notes: Where the same target receives a follow-up email reusing a real prior thread, log that as ITID-11135 (Clone Phishing) instead, since the attack surface (a hijacked legitimate conversation) differs from a cold targeted lure.

playbook.name: Malicious Attachment Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted attack delivering a tailored weaponized attachment, with added reconnaissance and repeat-targeting review beyond the mass-phishing equivalent.

steps.title: Collect and identify the attachment
steps.desc: Retrieve the attachment and confirm file type and hash.

steps.title: Quarantine and hash-block the attachment
Isolate any endpoint where the attachment was opened
steps.desc: Isolate pending EDR review.
steps.abort: If confirmed never opened, proceed to recovery.

steps.title: Restore or clear affected endpoints
Correlate with threat intel for attribution
steps.desc: A targeted, individually-crafted attachment implies a more capable/motivated actor — worth attribution effort beyond a mass campaign.

steps.title: Review the tailored context used in the lure
steps.desc: Identify what real information about the recipient's role/projects the attacker used — this scopes how the target was researched.

steps.title: Check for repeat targeting
steps.desc: Determine whether the same sender/theme targeted other individuals in a similar role.

steps.title: Confirm whether macro/script executed
Determine macro/script presence
steps.desc: Static analysis or sandbox detonation to confirm active content.

ITID-11123.def: A phishing email sent to a specific individual, containing a link to a fake login page tailored to the target's organization (e.g., a spoofed internal SSO portal), without real-time session-token relay.
ITID-11123.purpose: Captures spear phishing that drives a specific individual to a static credential-harvesting page tailored to their organization or role.
scopeIncludes: Link to a fake login page branded to match the target's actual internal SSO/portal
Targeted credential-harvesting lures referencing the recipient's specific application or vendor login
scopeExcludes: Real-time AiTM session-token relay against a targeted individual (ITID-11124)
Untargeted mass credential-harvesting phishing (ITID-11113)
ITID-11123.severity: High given the deliberate targeting; escalates further if the target holds privileged access.
ITID-11123.priority: P1 if the target holds privileged/admin access or submission is confirmed, otherwise P2.
ITID-11123.escalation: Escalate to IAM/SOC immediately upon confirmed submission, particularly for privileged accounts.
indicators: Link to a lookalike domain closely mimicking the organization's actual SSO branding
Web proxy log showing the targeted user visiting a newly registered lookalike domain
vectors: Spoofed internal SSO/portal login page tailored to the organization's real branding
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA on the targeted account
Brand/domain monitoring not catching a lookalike domain quickly enough
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring and takedown
URL rewriting/sandboxing
ITID-11123.detection: URL rewriting and web proxy telemetry provide good visibility once the link is clicked.
ITID-11123.response: Force password reset for the target, review sign-in logs for the account, and request domain takedown.
metrics: Count of targeted credential-harvesting incidents per quarter
Number involving privileged accounts
ITID-11123.notes: Deliberately excludes AiTM relay kits, logged separately under ITID-11124, since session-token theft requires a different response (session revocation) than a static credential harvest.

playbook.name: Malicious Link Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted attack delivering a tailored link to a static credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Extract and defang the URL
Block the destination domain network-wide
Contact the targeted individual directly
steps.desc: Determine whether credentials were submitted.

steps.title: Verify no anomalous sign-in activity
Correlate with threat intel for attribution
Confirm static (non-proxying) destination
steps.abort: If the page relays a live MFA challenge, switch to the AiTM spear phishing playbook immediately.

steps.title: Check for repeat targeting of similar roles
Escalate confirmed credential submissions
steps.desc: Escalate to the Credential-Based Attacks track, force password reset, revoke sessions.
steps.abort: If no submission confirmed, this step is not required.

steps.title: Review the tailored pretext used
steps.desc: Identify what real context the attacker referenced to make the lure credible to this specific recipient.

ITID-11124.def: A phishing attack against a specific individual using a reverse-proxy AiTM kit that relays the real login flow and steals the resulting session token, bypassing standard MFA for that targeted account.
ITID-11124.purpose: Captures spear phishing using an adversary-in-the-middle kit against a specifically targeted individual, distinguishing session-token theft from static credential harvesting.
scopeIncludes: Targeted lure linking to a known or suspected AiTM/reverse-proxy phishing kit against a specific individual
Confirmed theft of a session cookie/token for a specifically targeted account
scopeExcludes: Untargeted AiTM campaigns sent broadly (ITID-11114)
Static targeted credential harvesting with no session relay (ITID-11123)
The same technique used against a senior executive specifically (ITID-11148, Whaling)
ITID-11124.severity: High — combines deliberate targeting with an MFA-bypassing technique.
ITID-11124.priority: P1 upon confirmed session token theft.
ITID-11124.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to revoke active sessions and refresh tokens, not just reset the password.
indicators: Sign-in logs showing a successful MFA-satisfied login from an unfamiliar location immediately after the targeted user clicked a link
Reverse-proxy fingerprint matching known AiTM kits
vectors: Reverse-proxy phishing kit tailored with the target's organization branding
rootCauses: Standard OTP/push MFA in use instead of phishing-resistant MFA on a high-value account
Session tokens not bound to device/IP
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Session/token binding and conditional access risk policies
ITID-11124.detection: Identity provider sign-in risk and session-anomaly detection give strong coverage once the token is used.
ITID-11124.response: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for the targeted account immediately, then investigate for lateral movement.
metrics: Count of confirmed targeted AiTM session-token thefts per quarter
Median time from theft to session revocation
ITID-11124.notes: Scoped to the initial-access/session-theft event; post-compromise activity rolls up under the relevant Unauthorized Access ITID to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: AiTM Spear Phishing Kit Campaign Response
playbook.description: High-priority response playbook for a targeted AiTM campaign — a targeted AiTM attempt signals a more capable actor than the mass-phishing equivalent and warrants an explicit attribution step.

steps.title: Confirm AiTM kit infrastructure
Block the destination domain immediately
Revoke the affected session/token
steps.desc: Force full re-authentication; a password reset alone is not sufficient.

steps.title: Confirm no anomalous access remains
Engage threat intel for attribution
steps.desc: A targeted AiTM attempt is a real, actionable signal for identifying the threat actor behind it — feed the kit fingerprint and target profile to threat intel.

steps.title: Review identity provider sign-in logs
steps.outcome: List of accounts, if any, that completed authentication against the phishing kit.

steps.title: Escalate any confirmed MFA completion
steps.desc: Treat the resulting session as compromised immediately.

steps.title: Review the session's full activity window
steps.desc: Scope any downstream access before revocation.

steps.title: Assess phishing-resistant MFA for this individual/role
Assess the target's role for likely motive
steps.desc: A targeted AiTM attempt against a specific individual (exec, researcher, admin) suggests deliberate selection — note the role for threat-intel correlation.

ITID-11125.def: A targeted phishing email sent from an already-compromised legitimate email account belonging to a trusted colleague, partner, or vendor, leveraging that account's real trust relationship to reach a further target.
ITID-11125.purpose: Captures spear phishing sent from a genuinely compromised, trusted internal or partner account, distinguishing the phishing/further-compromise vector from downstream financial-fraud outcomes.
scopeIncludes: Phishing sent from a confirmed-compromised internal mailbox to other internal recipients (internal spearphishing / lateral spread)
Phishing sent from a confirmed-compromised partner/vendor mailbox to the organization
scopeExcludes: The same technique used to directly solicit a fraudulent wire transfer or payment, which is Business Email Compromise financial fraud (ITID-22411 through ITID-22415, and ITID-53111/53121/53131/53141 for the fraud-execution stage)
Spoofed sender identity with no actual account compromise (ITID-11126)
ITID-11125.severity: High — a compromised trusted account defeats sender-reputation-based defenses and often achieves high click-through.
ITID-11125.priority: P1, since this typically indicates an active, spreading compromise.
ITID-11125.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to contain the source account (reset, session revocation) in parallel with handling the phishing recipients.
indicators: Phishing email originating from a genuinely authenticated internal or partner mailbox (passes SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
Sign-in anomaly on the source account shortly before the phishing emails were sent
vectors: Compromised mailbox used to send phishing to the victim's own contact list or distribution groups
rootCauses: The source account's initial compromise (e.g., prior credential phishing) not detected before it was used to send further phishing
No outbound-mail anomaly detection on the source account
controls: Outbound mail anomaly detection
Phishing-resistant MFA
Prompt session revocation on detected account compromise
ITID-11125.detection: Outbound mail behavior analytics and recipient reports provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-11125.response: Contain the source account immediately (revoke sessions, reset credentials) and treat every downstream recipient as a potential secondary phishing case.
metrics: Count of compromised-account spear phishing incidents per quarter
Average number of downstream recipients per incident
ITID-11125.notes: Deliberately scoped to the phishing/further-compromise use of the hijacked account; if the same compromised account is instead used to directly request a fraudulent payment, log that under the Business Email Compromise ITIDs (ITID-22411 family) instead to avoid duplicating the incident across two branches.

playbook.name: Compromised Trusted-Account Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted attack sent from a real, previously-legitimate compromised account. The sending account/organization requires its own remediation, distinct from every other sibling in this branch.

steps.title: Confirm genuine account compromise, not spoofing
steps.desc: Header/authentication analysis (valid SPF/DKIM/DMARC from the real domain) to confirm this is a real account, not an impersonation.
steps.abort: If authentication fails, this is spoofing — switch to the Spoofed Sender Identity playbook instead.

steps.title: Disable and reset the compromised account if internal
steps.desc: Immediately disable credentials and revoke active sessions for an internal compromised account.
steps.abort: If the account is external/third-party, this step does not apply — proceed to vendor notification instead.

steps.title: Review the compromised account's full recent activity
steps.desc: Determine the scope of the campaign — what other recipients were targeted from this same account.

steps.title: Re-enable the account only after verified remediation
Review sender-authentication gaps
steps.desc: A legitimate, authenticated account bypasses most spoofing-focused controls — assess whether anomaly-based detection (unusual sending pattern/content) would have caught this.

steps.title: Determine whether the compromised account is internal or third-party
Notify the vendor's security team if external
steps.desc: Block further mail from the specific compromised account pending the vendor's own remediation.
steps.abort: If internal, this step does not apply.

steps.title: Determine the account's own root cause of compromise
steps.desc: If internal, link to the actual initial-access ITID responsible for the original compromise.
steps.abort: Not applicable for a third-party account outside this organization's own telemetry.

ITID-11126.def: A targeted phishing email that impersonates a trusted sender's identity through display-name spoofing or a lookalike sending domain, without the sender's actual mailbox having been compromised.
ITID-11126.purpose: Captures spear phishing where the sender identity is spoofed (display-name or lookalike domain) without any actual account compromise, distinguishing it from the genuinely-compromised-account leaf.
scopeIncludes: Display-name spoofing of a known colleague or executive with a different underlying email address
Lookalike/cousin domain used to impersonate a trusted sender
scopeExcludes: Phishing sent from a genuinely compromised trusted account (ITID-11125)
Display-name spoofing specifically executed as Business Email Compromise with no domain compromise (ITID-22412), which covers the financial-fraud-focused variant of this technique
ITID-11126.severity: Medium-High depending on the impersonated identity's authority.
ITID-11126.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the spoofed identity is a senior leader.
ITID-11126.escalation: Escalate if the recipient acted on the email (e.g., shared data, credentials) before verifying sender identity out-of-band.
indicators: Display name matches a known colleague but the underlying email address does not
DMARC/DKIM/SPF failure on an email purporting to be from an internal domain
vectors: Display-name spoofing exploiting mail clients that hide the full email address by default
Lookalike domain differing by a single character or TLD
rootCauses: DMARC not enforced at a reject/quarantine policy
Users not trained to verify the full sender address, not just the display name
controls: DMARC enforcement at reject/quarantine
External-sender banner tagging
User awareness training on sender verification
ITID-11126.detection: SEG sender-authentication checks (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) and external-sender banners provide good preventive coverage.
ITID-11126.response: Confirm no account compromise occurred, block the spoofed domain/display-name pattern, and verify whether the recipient acted on the email.
metrics: Count of spoofed-sender spear phishing incidents per quarter
DMARC enforcement coverage percentage
ITID-11126.notes: The key differentiator from ITID-11125 is confirmed absence of account compromise; if investigation later reveals the account actually was compromised, reclassify to ITID-11125.

playbook.name: Spoofed Sender Identity Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted attack impersonating a specific real identity without any genuine account compromise — centered on header/domain forensics rather than account remediation.

steps.title: Analyze message headers for spoofing indicators
steps.desc: Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC results and Reply-To mismatch to confirm spoofing rather than a genuine compromise.
steps.abort: If authentication passes for the real domain, this is a genuine compromise — switch to the Compromised Trusted-Account playbook instead.

steps.title: Block the spoofed sender pattern / lookalike domain
Determine spoofing method
steps.desc: Confirm whether this is simple display-name spoofing, a lookalike domain registration, or reply-chain hijacking of a real prior thread.

steps.title: Confirm no recipient acted on the spoofed message
Review DMARC enforcement posture
steps.desc: Assess whether stricter DMARC (reject/quarantine rather than none/monitor) would have blocked this specific spoof.

steps.title: Identify the specific identity being impersonated
Alert the impersonated individual
steps.desc: If the impersonated identity is internal, notify them directly that their identity is being spoofed.

steps.title: Report the lookalike domain for takedown

ITID-11127.def: A targeted phishing attack conducted across multiple messages over time — an initial benign or rapport-building message followed by a later message carrying the actual malicious link or attachment — designed to lower the target's guard before the payload arrives.
ITID-11127.purpose: Captures spear phishing conducted as a multi-message sequence that builds rapport or credibility before delivering the actual malicious payload, distinguishing patient social-engineering campaigns from single-shot lures.
scopeIncludes: A benign introductory email establishing context or trust, followed by a payload-bearing follow-up from the same persona
Multi-message sequences spanning days or weeks before payload delivery
scopeExcludes: A single-message lure with the payload present from the first contact (ITID-11122, ITID-11123, ITID-11124)

Warm-up conducted via a different channel (e.g., a social media DM building rapport) before an email payload, which should be logged under the relevant Social Media Exploitation Attacks ITID for the initial-contact stage and cross-referenced here for the email payload stage
ITID-11127.severity: High — the patience and structure involved typically indicate a more capable, motivated adversary.
ITID-11127.priority: P1 once the payload stage is identified, P2 during the warm-up stage alone.
ITID-11127.escalation: Escalate as soon as a warm-up pattern is recognized, even before a payload is delivered, given the likelihood of a following malicious message.
indicators: A benign email from an unfamiliar sender followed days later by a payload-bearing email from the same identity
Recipient reporting an unusually persistent or escalating conversation pattern from a new contact
vectors: Fake job recruiter or business-development contact building rapport before sending a malicious attachment
Multi-turn email exchange establishing legitimacy before a credential-harvesting link
rootCauses: No mechanism to correlate related messages from the same external sender/persona over time
Users not flagging early benign-seeming contact as suspicious
controls: SEG filtering with sender-history correlation
User awareness training on multi-stage social engineering
ITID-11127.detection: Weak — individual warm-up messages rarely trigger automated detection; relies on user suspicion and later payload-stage detection.
ITID-11127.response: Once identified, review the full message history with the sender persona and check whether the payload stage reached any other recipients.
metrics: Count of confirmed multi-stage spear phishing campaigns per quarter
Average number of messages before payload delivery
ITID-11127.notes: Log the case under this ITID once the multi-stage pattern is recognized, even if only the warm-up stage has occurred; do not wait for payload delivery to open the record.

playbook.name: Multi-Stage Warm-Up Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted attack pattern spanning two or more messages — an innocuous first contact followed by the real payload, requiring correlation across the full thread rather than treating either message in isolation.

steps.title: Identify the initial warm-up contact
steps.desc: Confirm the reported message is genuinely payload-free — no attachment, link, or credential request.

steps.title: Block sender/domain immediately
steps.desc: Block even if only the warm-up stage has been observed, pending the expected follow-up.

steps.title: Apply the matching payload-specific playbook
steps.desc: Once the follow-up stage's delivery mechanism is identified, hand off to that sibling's own eradication steps.

steps.title: Confirm the campaign did not progress past the warm-up stage
Log the warm-up pretext pattern
steps.desc: Record the rapport-building angle used for correlation with future campaigns against this or similar individuals.

steps.title: Search for a follow-up payload-bearing message
steps.desc: Check the same sender/thread for a subsequent message carrying the actual payload.

steps.title: Alert the targeted individual proactively
steps.desc: Warn them to expect and report a follow-up message rather than respond to it directly.

ITID-11128.def: A targeted phishing email inducing a specific individual to grant a malicious third-party application OAuth consent (e.g., mailbox read access) via a legitimate identity-provider consent prompt, rather than harvesting a password directly.
ITID-11128.purpose: Captures spear phishing whose goal is to obtain a malicious OAuth/application consent grant from a targeted individual, distinguishing the initial-access lure from downstream OAuth token abuse.
scopeIncludes: Targeted lure directing the victim to authorize a malicious OAuth application through a real identity-provider consent screen
Consent-phishing campaigns using a convincingly named app (e.g., mimicking a common productivity tool)
scopeExcludes: Ongoing abuse of an already-granted OAuth token for persistent mailbox/data access (ITID-33141 through ITID-33145, OAuth Token Abuse)
A rogue SAML/OAuth identity provider set up to intercept credentials directly (ITID-12915)
Standard credential-harvesting link phishing with no OAuth consent step (ITID-11123)
ITID-11128.severity: High — a granted OAuth consent can provide persistent, MFA-independent access that survives a password reset.
ITID-11128.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to revoke the application's consent grant and refresh tokens; a password reset alone does not remediate this.
indicators: Identity provider audit log showing a new third-party application consent grant shortly after a phishing email
Unfamiliar or newly registered application name requesting broad mailbox/data scopes
vectors: Phishing email linking to a real OAuth consent prompt for a malicious, convincingly branded application
rootCauses: User consent to third-party applications not restricted by admin policy
No review process for newly granted high-scope application consents
controls: Admin consent workflow restricting user self-service app consent
Regular review/revocation of high-scope OAuth grants
User awareness training on OAuth consent phishing
ITID-11128.detection: Identity provider consent-grant audit logs provide a strong, direct technical signal.
ITID-11128.response: Revoke the malicious application's consent grant and any issued tokens immediately, and audit for mailbox/data access during the grant window.
metrics: Count of confirmed malicious OAuth consent grants per quarter
Time from grant to revocation
ITID-11128.notes: Scoped to the initial phishing lure that obtains the consent grant; the attacker's subsequent use of that token for data access is a separate, ongoing incident logged under ITID-33141 through ITID-33145 to keep initial-access and post-access reporting distinct.

playbook.name: OAuth Consent Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted malicious app-consent grant. Remediation is scope-and-token revocation, not a password reset — the stolen access lives in the granted app permissions, not a credential.

steps.title: Identify the malicious OAuth app/consent request
steps.desc: Retrieve the app name, publisher, and requested scopes from the lure or from identity provider logs.

steps.title: Revoke the malicious application's access
steps.desc: Revoke organization-wide if granted, regardless of confirmed misuse yet.
steps.abort: If consent was never granted, this step is not required.

steps.title: Audit the granted app's activity during the consent window
steps.desc: Review mailbox, file, and calendar access the app's scope permitted while active.

steps.title: Confirm no anomalous access remains via the app's former scope
Review app-consent policy
steps.desc: Assess whether requiring admin consent for third-party app registrations would have blocked this.

steps.title: Check whether consent was actually granted
Block the app registration or delivery infrastructure

ITID-11129.def: A phishing message or physical lure sent to a specific individual containing a QR code — tailored with the target's context (e.g., referencing a real meeting or delivery) — that directs a scan to a credential-harvesting or malware page.
ITID-11129.purpose: Captures spear phishing delivered via a QR code tailored to a specific individual, distinguishing targeted quishing from the mass/untargeted variant.
scopeIncludes: QR code lure referencing a specific meeting, event, or document the target would recognize
Physical QR-code lure (e.g., a note left at the target's desk) targeting one individual
scopeExcludes: Untargeted, broadly distributed QR code phishing (ITID-11115)
QR code used as one step in a broader hybrid physical/digital attack chain (ITID-11915)
ITID-11129.severity: Medium-High given the targeting and the shift to an unmanaged personal device for the scan.
ITID-11129.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the target holds privileged access.
ITID-11129.escalation: Escalate if a corporate credential was entered after the scan, given the reduced endpoint telemetry on personal devices.
indicators: QR code lure content referencing accurate, specific detail about the target
Redirect-service log showing a single scan matching the timing of a targeted lure's delivery
vectors: QR code embedded in a personalized email or physical note referencing real context
rootCauses: Email security tooling not decoding QR image content for targeted, low-volume email
No policy guidance discouraging corporate credential entry after a personal-device QR scan
controls: QR code decoding/scanning in the secure email gateway
User awareness training on QR code risks
Conditional access blocking sign-in from unmanaged devices
ITID-11129.detection: Limited — low email volume evades bulk heuristics, and personal-device scans are largely invisible to corporate telemetry.
ITID-11129.response: Decode and analyze the QR destination, block the domain, and check identity provider logs for any resulting sign-in attempt on the targeted account.
metrics: Count of targeted QR code phishing incidents per quarter
ITID-11129.notes: Distinguished from ITID-11115 purely by targeting level; if a QR lure initially logged here turns out to have been sent broadly, reclassify to ITID-11115.

playbook.name: QR Code Spear Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a targeted QR-code lure, adding a targeting-confirmation step beyond the mass-phishing equivalent.

steps.title: Confirm the lure was addressed specifically to the target
steps.desc: Rule out a broad/mass send before treating this as genuinely targeted.

steps.title: Block the destination domain network-wide
Follow the matching destination-type playbook
steps.desc: If the destination matches AiTM or credential-harvesting, follow that playbook's eradication steps.

steps.title: Confirm no corporate credential use on the scanning device
Log the delivery channel and targeting rationale
Decode the QR code and reputation-check the destination
Check managed-device telemetry for the target's device

ITID-11131.def: A phishing message that closely replicates a real, previously seen legitimate email — reusing its formatting, branding, and often its actual prior content — with a malicious link or attachment substituted in, whose exact cloning mechanism is not yet known.
ITID-11131.purpose: Catch-all for a reported clone phishing incident where the specific cloning mechanism (intercepted mail, public template, reply-chain hijack, etc.) has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported clone phishing email before the source of the clone is determined
scopeExcludes: Any case where the cloning mechanism has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11132 through ITID-11139
A phishing lure with no genuine prior legitimate message being replicated (Mass or Targeted Phishing branches)
ITID-11131.severity: Medium by default; clone phishing generally carries higher credibility than cold phishing.
ITID-11131.escalation: Escalate promptly given clone phishing's typically higher success rate due to its borrowed legitimacy.
indicators: Recipient recognizing the email as resembling a real prior conversation or notification, but with a suspicious link/attachment
Email formatting matching a known legitimate sender's exact template
vectors: A replicated legitimate email format used as a wrapper for a malicious payload
rootCauses: Insufficient scrutiny given to messages that resemble familiar, previously seen communications
controls: SEG filtering
User awareness training on clone phishing
ITID-11131.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting until the specific cloning mechanism is identified.
ITID-11131.response: Triage promptly to determine the cloning mechanism and reclassify to the appropriate sibling leaf.
metrics: Count of unclassified clone phishing reports pending reclassification
ITID-11131.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify once the cloning mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified Clone Phishing Triage
playbook.description: Short triage-to-reclassification playbook — confirms a genuine clone and identifies the acquisition method before handing off to the matching sibling playbook.

steps.title: Confirm this is genuinely a clone
steps.desc: Compare against the real original email if available.

steps.title: Block sender/domain pending reclassification
Reclassify into the matching sibling ITID
steps.abort: If no sibling fits after full review, leave classified here and document why.

steps.title: Confirm no interaction occurred
Log the reclassification outcome
Identify how the clone was obtained/executed
steps.desc: Determine whether it came from a compromised thread, interception, or a public template.

ITID-11132.def: A phishing attack in which an attacker who has gained access to a mailbox (or a downstream copy of a thread) sends a malicious reply into a genuinely ongoing email conversation, relying on the thread's real history to appear legitimate to other participants.
ITID-11132.purpose: Captures clone phishing where an attacker hijacks an existing, ongoing legitimate email thread — requiring prior mailbox access — and inserts a malicious reply, as distinct from forging a fake support persona or intercepting mail in transit.
scopeIncludes: A malicious reply inserted into a real, ongoing email thread that other participants recognize
Cases requiring the attacker to have prior read/write access to at least one participant's mailbox or a synced copy of the thread
scopeExcludes: A fabricated customer-support persona inserted into a thread rather than a hijack of a genuine ongoing conversation (ITID-22331, Fake Customer Support Email Reply-Chain Impersonation)
Interception of a legitimate email in transit before delivery, then resending it with a swapped payload (ITID-11133)
The initial mailbox compromise itself, which is a separate Account Compromise incident this leaf's response should reference
ITID-11132.severity: High — reply-chain hijacks exploit genuine conversational trust and typically achieve high click-through among the other thread participants.
ITID-11132.priority: P1, since this indicates an active mailbox compromise being actively leveraged.
ITID-11132.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to contain the source mailbox in parallel with warning other thread participants.
indicators: A malicious reply appearing in a thread with correct prior history and formatting
Sign-in anomaly on the source mailbox around the time of the malicious reply
vectors: Attacker replies into a real thread from the compromised mailbox with a swapped-in malicious link or attachment
rootCauses: The originating mailbox compromise not detected before it was leveraged for reply-chain phishing
No outbound-mail anomaly detection flagging replies with newly added suspicious links
controls: Outbound mail anomaly detection
Prompt session revocation on detected account compromise
Phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-11132.detection: Outbound mail behavior analytics and recipient reports provide the primary detection surface; the hijack itself is hard to distinguish from a legitimate reply until payload analysis.
ITID-11132.response: Contain the source mailbox immediately and notify every other participant in the thread as a potential secondary target.
metrics: Count of confirmed reply-chain hijack incidents per quarter
Average number of other thread participants notified per incident
ITID-11132.notes: The differentiator from ITID-22331 is a genuinely pre-existing thread versus a fabricated support persona; the differentiator from ITID-11133 is that this requires mailbox access rather than in-transit interception.

playbook.name: Reply-Chain Hijack Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a hijacked real thread sent from a genuinely compromised mailbox — remediation centers on the compromised account itself, not just the message.

steps.title: Confirm the thread is real and the account is genuinely compromised
steps.desc: Check sender authentication headers against the real domain.
steps.abort: If authentication fails, this is spoofing, not a genuine compromise — switch to the Spoofed Sender Identity playbook.

steps.title: Disable and reset the compromised account if internal
steps.abort: If external/third-party, notify the vendor's security team instead.

steps.title: Review the compromised mailbox's full recent activity
steps.desc: Determine the true scope — every other real thread the attacker may have replied within.

steps.title: Re-enable the account only after verified remediation
Review anomaly detection for in-thread injection
Identify what changed versus the real prior thread content
Identify all recipients on the hijacked thread
Determine the account's own root cause of compromise
steps.abort: Not applicable for a third-party account outside this organization's own telemetry.

ITID-11133.def: A phishing attack in which a genuinely legitimate email is intercepted before reaching its intended recipient — via a compromised mail server, relay, or malicious forwarding/transport rule — and then resent to the recipient with a malicious link or attachment substituted in.
ITID-11133.purpose: Captures clone phishing where a legitimate email is intercepted in transit (e.g., via a compromised mail relay or forwarding rule) and resent with a malicious payload, distinguishing this from mailbox-hijack and template-based cloning.
scopeIncludes: Evidence of a malicious mail transport/forwarding rule or compromised relay used to intercept and modify a legitimate email before delivery
Delivery delay or duplication of a legitimate email consistent with in-transit interception
scopeExcludes: Reply-chain hijacking from a compromised mailbox with no in-transit interception (ITID-11132)
Cloning based on a publicly available template rather than an actual intercepted message (ITID-11134)
ITID-11133.severity: High — indicates a compromise at the mail infrastructure or transport-rule level, a materially more serious foothold than a single compromised mailbox.
ITID-11133.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR and mail infrastructure administrators to identify and remove the malicious transport/forwarding rule.
indicators: Discovery of an unauthorized mail forwarding or transport rule
Recipient receiving a legitimate-looking email later than expected, or the true sender confirming they never sent the received version
vectors: Malicious inbox forwarding rule created after a mailbox or admin-level compromise
Compromised on-premises mail relay or connector
rootCauses: Mail forwarding/transport rule changes not monitored or alerted on
Excessive administrative privilege over mail transport infrastructure
mitreTechniques: T1114.003 Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
controls: Mail forwarding/transport rule change monitoring and alerting
Restricted administrative access to mail transport configuration
ITID-11133.detection: Mail platform audit logs for forwarding/transport rule changes provide a strong, direct technical signal.
ITID-11133.response: Remove the malicious rule/relay configuration, audit for all messages affected during the window it was active, and notify all affected recipients.
metrics: Count of confirmed in-transit interception incidents per quarter
Number of messages affected per incident
ITID-11133.notes: This is the most infrastructure-serious of the Clone Phishing leaves; always cross-reference the mailbox/admin-account compromise that enabled the rule change as a related incident.

playbook.name: Intercepted-in-Transit Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a clone delivered via interception of real mail transport infrastructure — requires infrastructure-level remediation, not just a recipient-side response.

steps.title: Confirm the real original never arrived or arrived late/duplicated
Engage email infrastructure/IT to check for compromise
Remediate the compromised relay/gateway/DNS record
steps.abort: If no infrastructure compromise is confirmed, treat as a lower-confidence case and note the uncertainty explicitly.

steps.title: Confirm mail flow integrity is restored
Review mail transport security posture
steps.desc: DNSSEC, MTA-STS, and TLS enforcement.

steps.title: Identify the likely interception point
steps.desc: Mail relay, gateway, or DNS/MX manipulation.

steps.title: Block sender/domain of the cloned version
Determine if other emails were intercepted in the same window

ITID-11134.def: A phishing email that closely replicates a legitimate, publicly observable communication template — such as a standard vendor newsletter or system notification format — without any actual interception of a specific real message or mailbox compromise.
ITID-11134.purpose: Captures clone phishing built from a publicly available or previously leaked legitimate template (newsletters, standard notifications) rather than an actual intercepted or hijacked message.
scopeIncludes: Cloned newsletter or standard notification format built from publicly available examples
Recreation of a widely distributed template that was never specifically intercepted for this attack
scopeExcludes: Cloning based on an actual intercepted or hijacked specific message (ITID-11132, ITID-11133)
ITID-11134.severity: Low-to-Medium — carries the visual credibility of clone phishing but lacks the personalized trust signal of a genuinely hijacked thread.
ITID-11134.escalation: Escalate per the confirmed payload type if interaction is confirmed.
indicators: Multiple recipients reporting a near-identical templated email with no shared prior conversation
Email visually matching a public, widely distributed notification format
vectors: Recreated vendor password-reset or notification email template used as a wrapper for a malicious link
rootCauses: Users trusting familiar visual branding without verifying sender domain
controls: SEG filtering
User awareness training on template-based clone phishing
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring
ITID-11134.detection: Relies on SEG heuristics and user reporting; no infrastructure-compromise signal to detect since no interception occurred.
ITID-11134.response: Confirm the payload type, block the sending domain, and treat similarly to mass phishing for response purposes.
metrics: Count of public-template clone phishing reports per month
ITID-11134.notes: This is the clone phishing leaf closest in practice to mass phishing (ITID-11116, Brand/Service Impersonation Phishing); it is kept in this Type because the attack still clones an existing template's exact look rather than a generic brand theme.

playbook.name: Public Template Clone Phishing Triage
playbook.description: Triage playbook for a clone of a well-known vendor/SaaS template — identifies the swapped payload and hands off to the matching sibling playbook.

steps.title: Identify the cloned vendor/template
steps.desc: Compare against the real template to confirm the match.

steps.title: Block sender/domain
Hand off to the matching swap-type sibling playbook
Confirm no interaction before closing
Track most-cloned vendor templates
Determine the swapped malicious element
steps.desc: Confirm whether it is a link or attachment.

steps.title: Notify the impersonated vendor if identifiable

ITID-11135.def: A phishing email cloned from a real prior message in which the original legitimate attachment has been replaced with a malicious file, while the rest of the message content is preserved to maintain credibility.
ITID-11135.purpose: Captures clone phishing where a legitimate prior attachment is swapped for a malicious one, isolating the attachment-swap mechanism from the link-swap and site-cloning variants.
scopeIncludes: A previously legitimate attachment (invoice, report, etc.) replaced with a malicious version in a cloned message
Cases combined with reply-chain hijack or in-transit interception where the specific defining feature under review is the attachment swap
scopeExcludes: A malicious attachment sent cold with no genuine prior legitimate version being cloned (ITID-11122, Malicious Attachment Spear Phishing)
The link, rather than the attachment, being the swapped element (ITID-11136)
ITID-11135.severity: High — combines cloning's credibility with a direct malware payload.
ITID-11135.priority: P1 if execution is confirmed, otherwise P2.
ITID-11135.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR if telemetry shows the swapped attachment executed on any endpoint.
indicators: Recipient noting the attachment filename matches an expected document but the file hash/content does not match the known legitimate version
EDR alert for a spawned process following receipt of a resembling-legitimate document
vectors: Malicious macro-enabled document substituted for a legitimate invoice/report attachment in a cloned message
rootCauses: No integrity verification (hash comparison) of recurring attachment types from known senders
Macro execution not blocked by policy
controls: Attachment sandboxing/detonation
Macro execution blocking policy
EDR on endpoints
