ITID-11135.detection: Attachment sandboxing and EDR give strong coverage once opened; the swap itself is hard to detect pre-delivery without file-hash baselining.
ITID-11135.response: Sandbox-detonate the attachment, isolate any endpoint where it executed, and identify the source of the cloned original.
metrics: Count of attachment-swap clone phishing incidents per quarter
Number of endpoints with confirmed execution
ITID-11135.notes: Log the underlying cloning mechanism (reply-chain hijack ITID-11132, or in-transit interception ITID-11133) as the primary classification if that mechanism is confirmed; use this leaf when the attachment-swap is the most specific detail known.

playbook.name: Malicious Attachment Swap Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a clone phishing attack with a weaponized attachment swapped in for the real original.

steps.title: Retrieve the cloned attachment and compare against a real prior copy
steps.desc: If a real original is available, hash-compare to confirm the swap.

steps.title: Quarantine and hash-block the attachment
Isolate any endpoint where the attachment was opened
steps.abort: If confirmed never opened, proceed to recovery.

steps.title: Restore or clear affected endpoints
Review why the clone bypassed user suspicion
Confirm macro/script presence
Identify all recipients
Confirm whether macro/script executed

ITID-11136.def: A phishing email cloned from a real prior message in which the original legitimate hyperlink has been replaced with a malicious link, while the rest of the message content is preserved to maintain credibility.
ITID-11136.purpose: Captures clone phishing where a legitimate prior link is swapped for a malicious one, isolating the link-swap mechanism from the attachment-swap and site-cloning variants.
scopeIncludes: A previously legitimate link (document share, tracking link, etc.) replaced with a malicious link in a cloned message
Cases combined with reply-chain hijack or in-transit interception where the specific defining feature under review is the link swap
scopeExcludes: A malicious link sent cold with no genuine prior legitimate version being cloned (ITID-11123, Malicious Link Spear Phishing)
The attachment, rather than the link, being the swapped element (ITID-11135)
ITID-11136.severity: Medium-High depending on the destination the swapped link leads to.
ITID-11136.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credential submission or malware execution is confirmed.
ITID-11136.escalation: Escalate per the confirmed destination type (credential harvesting, malware) if interaction is confirmed.
indicators: Recipient noting the link destination domain does not match the expected legitimate service referenced in the cloned content
Web proxy log showing a click to a domain inconsistent with the message's ostensible source
vectors: Malicious link substituted for a legitimate document-share or tracking link in a cloned message
rootCauses: No integrity verification of expected link destinations in recurring message types
URL rewriting not flagging the swapped destination as suspicious at time of click
controls: URL rewriting and time-of-click sandboxing
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring
ITID-11136.detection: URL rewriting and web proxy telemetry give good visibility once the link is clicked.
ITID-11136.response: Analyze the swapped link's destination, block the domain, and identify the source of the cloned original.
metrics: Count of link-swap clone phishing incidents per quarter
ITID-11136.notes: Log the underlying cloning mechanism (reply-chain hijack ITID-11132, or in-transit interception ITID-11133) as the primary classification if that mechanism is confirmed; use this leaf when the link-swap is the most specific detail known.

playbook.name: Malicious Link Swap Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a clone phishing attack with a static credential-harvesting link swapped in for the real original.

steps.title: Extract the swapped URL and compare against the real original link
Block the destination domain network-wide
Contact users with confirmed clicks
Verify no anomalous sign-in activity
Review URL filtering efficacy
Confirm static (non-proxying) destination
steps.abort: If the page relays a live MFA challenge, switch to the AiTM Clone Phishing playbook.

steps.title: Identify recipients and click activity
Escalate confirmed credential submissions
steps.abort: If no submission confirmed, this step is not required.

ITID-11137.def: A phishing attack whose defining characteristic is a landing site that is a near-exact functional and visual replica of the legitimate destination it impersonates — including working secondary pages, correct branding, and realistic error handling — regardless of how the victim was directed to it.
ITID-11137.purpose: Captures clone phishing where the emphasis is the fidelity of the cloned destination website itself (a pixel-perfect replica), as distinct from a swapped link within an otherwise-cloned email.
scopeIncludes: A phishing site confirmed to closely replicate the legitimate site's full look, feel, and multi-page structure, not just a single login form
Cases where the site's fidelity itself is the notable/reportable characteristic (e.g., flagged by a user who almost entered real credentials before noticing a subtle discrepancy)
scopeExcludes: A simple single-page fake login form with no broader site cloning (ITID-11113, ITID-11123)
Real-time AiTM proxying of the actual legitimate site rather than a static clone (ITID-11114, ITID-11124, ITID-11138)
ITID-11137.severity: Medium-High given the elevated deception quality increases likelihood of successful credential submission.
ITID-11137.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if submission is confirmed.
ITID-11137.escalation: Escalate to IAM/SOC immediately upon confirmed credential submission.
indicators: User report noting the site looked identical to the real one but was reached via an unusual link
Web proxy/brand-monitoring detection of a domain hosting a structurally complete clone of the legitimate site
vectors: Fully cloned multi-page website hosted on a lookalike domain
rootCauses: Brand/domain-abuse monitoring not detecting a comprehensive site clone quickly
Lack of phishing-resistant MFA allowing a bare password to be sufficient for access
controls: Brand/domain-abuse monitoring and takedown
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
ITID-11137.detection: Brand-monitoring services and web proxy telemetry provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-11137.response: Force password reset for any user who submitted credentials and request urgent domain takedown given the site's deceptive quality.
metrics: Count of high-fidelity cloned-site incidents per quarter
ITID-11137.notes: The differentiator from the AiTM leaves is that this is a static clone with no real-time proxying of the legitimate service; if a relay/proxy behavior is discovered, reclassify to ITID-11138.

playbook.name: Cloned Destination Site Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a phishing attack whose destination is an exact clone of a real site, not just a generic fake login page.

steps.title: Compare the destination page against the real site
steps.desc: Confirm exact-clone status, not just a generic fake form.

steps.title: Block the destination domain network-wide
Contact users with confirmed visits
Verify no anomalous sign-in activity
Report the cloned domain for takedown
Identify the hosting domain/infrastructure
Identify recipients and click activity
Escalate confirmed submissions
steps.abort: If no submission confirmed, this step is not required.

ITID-11138.def: A phishing attack that clones a real prior message or thread to deliver a link into an AiTM reverse-proxy kit, which relays the real login flow and steals the resulting session token.
ITID-11138.purpose: Captures clone phishing combined with an adversary-in-the-middle relay, distinguishing session-token theft via a cloned message vector from static site cloning and from mass/targeted AiTM.
scopeIncludes: A cloned/hijacked message used as the delivery vector for an AiTM reverse-proxy link
Confirmed session-token theft where the initial lure was a clone phishing message
scopeExcludes: A cloned static site with no real-time relay (ITID-11137)
AiTM delivered via a cold mass or targeted lure with no cloning involved (ITID-11114, ITID-11124)
ITID-11138.severity: High — combines clone phishing's elevated credibility with an MFA-bypassing technique.
ITID-11138.priority: P1 upon confirmed session token theft.
ITID-11138.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to revoke active sessions and refresh tokens.
indicators: Sign-in logs showing a successful MFA-satisfied login immediately after a click on a cloned-message link
Reverse-proxy fingerprint matching known AiTM kits
vectors: Reply-chain hijack or intercepted message used to deliver an AiTM reverse-proxy link
rootCauses: Standard OTP/push MFA in use instead of phishing-resistant MFA
The originating clone/hijack compromise not detected before being leveraged for AiTM delivery
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Session/token binding and conditional access risk policies
Outbound mail anomaly detection
ITID-11138.detection: Identity provider sign-in risk and session-anomaly detection give strong coverage once the token is used.
ITID-11138.response: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens immediately and cross-reference the originating clone-phishing compromise.
metrics: Count of confirmed clone-phishing-delivered AiTM session thefts per quarter
ITID-11138.notes: Always log the originating clone/hijack mechanism (ITID-11132/11133) as a related incident, since remediation requires addressing both the delivery compromise and the session theft.

playbook.name: AiTM Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Highest-priority playbook in this branch — a clone's credibility combined with AiTM's MFA-bypass capability. Remediation is session/token revocation, not a password reset.

steps.title: Confirm AiTM kit infrastructure at the swapped destination
Block the destination domain immediately
Revoke the affected session/token
Confirm no anomalous access remains
Add kit infrastructure to threat-intel blocklist
Compare surrounding message content against a real prior original
steps.desc: Confirms the clone and how it was likely obtained.

steps.title: Escalate any confirmed MFA completion
Review the session's full activity window
Review identity provider sign-in logs

ITID-11139.def: A phishing message cloned from a real prior communication and sent to a broad distribution list or group alias — via a compromised list-management account or spoofed list address — rather than to a single hijacked thread's participants.
ITID-11139.purpose: Captures clone phishing distributed broadly via a compromised or spoofed distribution list/group alias, distinguishing mass-cloned-message delivery from a 1:1 reply-chain hijack or targeted swap.
scopeIncludes: A cloned message sent to an entire distribution list or group alias rather than to specific individual thread participants
Compromise of a distribution-list-management account used to send a cloned message broadly
scopeExcludes: A cloned reply sent within a specific 1:1 or small-group thread (ITID-11132)
Untargeted mass phishing with no genuine cloned prior message (Mass Phishing Attacks, ITID-1111x)
ITID-11139.severity: High given the potential blast radius of a single compromised distribution list reaching many recipients at once.
ITID-11139.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to contain the distribution-list-management account and to email administrators to halt further distribution if possible.
indicators: Many recipients on a shared distribution list reporting the identical cloned message near-simultaneously
Distribution list configuration change or send-as compromise around the time of the campaign
vectors: Compromised distribution-list owner/manager account used to send a cloned message to the full list
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls or monitoring on distribution-list management/send-as permissions
controls: Restricted and monitored distribution-list management permissions
Outbound mail volume anomaly detection
ITID-11139.detection: Outbound mail volume anomaly detection and simultaneous multi-recipient reporting provide strong signal.
ITID-11139.response: Contain the compromised distribution-list account immediately, recall/purge the message where possible, and notify all list members.
metrics: Count of confirmed distribution-list clone phishing incidents per quarter
Average number of recipients affected per incident
ITID-11139.notes: The differentiator from ITID-11132 is delivery breadth (a full distribution list versus specific thread participants); both may stem from the same underlying account compromise and can be cross-referenced.

playbook.name: Distribution List Clone Phishing Response
playbook.description: Response playbook for a cloned list-wide email resent to a real distribution list — the multi-recipient blast radius means the full list must be notified proactively, not just individual reporters.

steps.title: Confirm the clone matches a real prior list-wide send
Block sender/domain and notify the full list proactively
Follow the matching acquisition-method sibling's own eradication steps
Confirm no list member acted on the clone before closing
Review distribution list sender-access controls
Identify the full distribution list/group affected
Determine how the original list-wide email was obtained
steps.desc: Compromised member/owner account vs. interception.

ITID-11141.def: A phishing attack specifically directed at a senior executive, board member, or other high-value individual, whose specific technique (attachment, link, AiTM, personal-channel targeting, etc.) has not yet been confirmed.
ITID-11141.purpose: Catch-all for a reported phishing attack targeting a senior executive or other whaling-class target where the specific technique or angle has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported whaling attempt before the technique is examined
scopeExcludes: Any case where the technique has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11142 through ITID-11149
Spear phishing targeted at a non-executive individual (Targeted (Spear) Phishing Attacks, ITID-1112x)
ITID-11141.severity: High by default given the seniority of the target; reassess once technique and any interaction are known.
ITID-11141.escalation: Escalate immediately to the SOC and to executive protection/leadership given the target's seniority.
indicators: A phishing attempt specifically addressed to a named executive, board member, or their office
Email content referencing detail specific to the executive's role, schedule, or public profile
vectors: Personalized email referencing the executive's public role or recent public activity
rootCauses: Extensive public OSINT available on senior leadership (bios, press coverage, conference appearances)
controls: SEG filtering with executive-account priority handling
User awareness training tailored to executives and their support staff
ITID-11141.detection: Limited — low-volume, highly tailored email is hard for bulk heuristics to catch; relies heavily on reporting by the executive or their staff.
ITID-11141.response: Triage promptly to determine technique and reclassify; brief the executive and their assistant on the attempt.
metrics: Count of unclassified whaling reports pending reclassification
ITID-11141.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify once the technique is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Whaling Attack
playbook.description: For a phishing attack specifically targeting a senior executive whose specific technique has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Preserve the message and notify executive protection/security leadership immediately
steps.desc: Collect the email with full headers and immediately notify security leadership given the elevated risk of targeting an executive.
steps.guidance: Whaling incidents warrant expedited handling and direct leadership visibility given the potential business impact and the executive's typically broad access.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; security leadership notified.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for the executive's account if compromised.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for persistence and remediate
steps.desc: Review the executive's account for persistence and remediate any host compromise.
steps.outcome: Persistence confirmed and remediated.
steps.tool: Identity provider audit log / EDR console

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA and close monitoring
steps.desc: Restore access with fresh MFA enrollment and place the account under elevated, closely watched monitoring.
steps.outcome: Account restored; elevated monitoring active.

steps.title: Brief the executive and review executive-protection controls
steps.desc: Brief the executive directly on the attack and review whether current executive-protection controls (phishing-resistant MFA, dedicated monitoring) are adequate.
steps.outcome: Executive briefed; control adequacy reviewed.

steps.title: Determine what action the executive (or their staff) took
steps.desc: Confirm whether the executive or their assistant clicked, opened, or disclosed information.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss but still brief the executive given the targeting.

steps.title: Block the sender and check for related targeting of other executives
steps.desc: Block the sending infrastructure and check whether other executives received similar targeted attempts.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked; executive-wide targeting scope assessed.

ITID-11142.def: A phishing attack directed not at the executive directly but at their executive assistant or another delegate who holds proxy access to the executive's communications, calendar, or approval authority, exploiting that access as a softer entry point.
ITID-11142.purpose: Captures whaling that targets an executive's assistant or delegate as the entry point, exploiting their proxy access to the executive's calendar, inbox, or approvals.
scopeIncludes: Phishing targeting an executive assistant or delegate with proxy inbox/calendar access
Lures referencing the executive by name to add credibility while targeting the assistant's mailbox
scopeExcludes: Phishing sent directly to the executive's own primary account (ITID-11141 and other Whaling siblings)
Generic spear phishing targeting an assistant with no executive-proxy-access angle (Targeted Spear Phishing, ITID-1112x)
ITID-11142.severity: High — proxy access can grant equivalent reach into executive communications and approvals as compromising the executive directly.
ITID-11142.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC and brief the executive, given the assistant's proxy access.
indicators: Phishing addressed to an assistant referencing the executive's schedule or pending approvals
Sign-in anomaly on an assistant's account with delegate/proxy mailbox access
vectors: Email impersonating the executive requesting the assistant take an urgent action
rootCauses: Delegate/proxy access not scoped as tightly as the executive's own account protections (e.g., weaker MFA enforcement)
controls: Equivalent MFA/security controls applied to delegate/proxy accounts as to the executive account itself
User awareness training for executive support staff
ITID-11142.detection: Relies on reporting and standard email telemetry on the assistant's account.
ITID-11142.response: Treat any compromise of the assistant's account with the same urgency as an executive account compromise, given equivalent access.
metrics: Count of assistant/delegate-targeted whaling incidents per quarter
ITID-11142.notes: Scope decision: classified under Whaling Attacks (targeting proxy access to an executive) rather than generic Spear Phishing, since the assistant is targeted specifically because of their executive-proxy role.

playbook.name: Response: Executive Assistant / Delegate-Targeted Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack targeting an executive's assistant or delegate (who typically has mailbox/calendar delegate access or approval authority) rather than the executive directly, exploiting their access on the executive's behalf.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm the delegate's access scope
steps.desc: Collect the email with headers and document exactly what delegate access (mailbox, calendar, approval workflows, financial systems) the assistant holds for the executive.
steps.outcome: Message preserved and delegate access scope documented.

steps.title: Contain the assistant's account and halt any delegated action
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions for the assistant's account, and halt/reverse any transaction or disclosure made using delegate authority.
steps.outcome: Account secured; delegated action halted.

steps.title: Check both the assistant's and executive's accounts for persistence
steps.desc: Review both accounts for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants, since delegate access may extend to the executive's mailbox.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence on both accounts.

steps.title: Restore delegate access with re-verified identity
steps.desc: Restore the assistant's account and full delegate permissions once confirmed clean.
steps.outcome: Access and delegate permissions restored to normal, confirmed-clean operation.

steps.title: Document and brief assistants/delegates on verification protocols
steps.desc: Record findings and brief executive assistants org-wide on a verification protocol for high-value requests made in the executive's name.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted briefing delivered to assistant/delegate staff.

steps.title: Determine what action was taken using the delegate access
steps.desc: Confirm whether the assistant acted on the phishing request using their delegated authority (e.g. approved a payment, forwarded sensitive information, granted access).
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure, including any action taken on the executive's behalf.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Review and temporarily restrict delegate permissions pending investigation
steps.desc: Coordinate with the executive to temporarily restrict the scope of delegate access until the incident is resolved.
steps.outcome: Delegate access scoped down pending resolution.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods on both accounts.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on either account.

ITID-11143.def: A phishing attack directed at senior executives or board members using a lure themed as board governance, investor relations, or M&A-related communication, exploiting the sensitivity and urgency typical of that content.
ITID-11143.purpose: Captures whaling themed around board or investor communications, a lure pattern distinct from personal/travel-based or technique-based whaling siblings.
scopeIncludes: Lure impersonating board correspondence, investor communication, or confidential deal-related content
Phishing timed around known board meeting or earnings-related dates
scopeExcludes: Whaling with no board/investor thematic content (other Whaling siblings)
Legitimate insider-trading-adjacent misuse of real board information, which is not a phishing ITID
ITID-11143.severity: High — board/investor themes carry high urgency and confidentiality expectations that increase click-through likelihood.
ITID-11143.escalation: Escalate immediately given the potential for confidential, market-sensitive information exposure.
indicators: Phishing content referencing board meeting schedules, M&A activity, or investor calls
Timing correlated with known public board/earnings dates
vectors: Spoofed board-secretary or investor-relations email requesting urgent document review or approval
rootCauses: Board/investor meeting schedules or agendas being discoverable through public filings or prior leaks
controls: Dedicated secure channel for board/investor document sharing outside standard email
User awareness training for board members and executives
ITID-11143.detection: Relies heavily on reporting given the low volume and high tailoring of this lure type.
ITID-11143.response: Escalate to legal/compliance in parallel with SOC given the potential material/confidential information exposure.
metrics: Count of board/investor-themed whaling incidents per quarter
ITID-11143.notes: Coordinate with legal/compliance on any incident here given the potential for confidential or market-sensitive information exposure.

playbook.name: Response: Board / Investor Communication Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack impersonating or targeting board members or investors, often referencing confidential deal, governance, or financial matters to extract sensitive information or authorize fraudulent transactions.

steps.title: Preserve the message and engage Legal/General Counsel immediately
steps.desc: Collect the email with headers and immediately loop in Legal given the likely involvement of material non-public or governance-sensitive information.
steps.guidance: Board/investor-related incidents may carry disclosure or regulatory implications — Legal must be involved from the outset, not after the fact.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; Legal engaged.

steps.title: Halt any in-progress financial or information disclosure
steps.desc: If a wire transfer or information disclosure is in progress, immediately act to intercept or recall it, coordinating with Finance and the bank.
steps.outcome: In-progress disclosure/transfer halted or recalled.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review any compromised account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access and confirm financial/legal resolution
steps.desc: Restore any affected account access and follow up with Legal/Finance to confirm final resolution of any financial or disclosure exposure.
steps.outcome: Access restored; financial/legal resolution documented.

steps.title: Document and brief the board on verification protocols
steps.desc: Record findings with Legal's involvement and brief the board/investor relations team on an out-of-band verification protocol for sensitive requests.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; board-level briefing delivered.

steps.title: Determine what confidential information or authorization was requested and whether it was given
steps.desc: Establish exactly what was requested (deal details, financials, wire authorization) and whether the target complied.
steps.outcome: Confirmed request content and compliance status.
steps.abort: If no compliance occurred, downgrade to a near-miss but still notify Legal given the sensitivity.

steps.title: Contain any compromised account and verify with the real board member/investor
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions for any compromised account, and contact the real board member or investor through a known-good channel to confirm they did not send the message.
steps.outcome: Account contained; real individual confirmed uninvolved.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11144.def: A phishing attack directed at a senior executive's personal email address, personal phone/messaging app, or personal device, deliberately bypassing corporate email security controls that would apply to their work account.
ITID-11144.purpose: Captures whaling directed at an executive's personal device or personal (non-corporate) email/messaging account, a channel outside standard corporate email security controls.
scopeIncludes: Phishing sent to an executive's known personal email address or personal phone number
Lures referencing the executive's personal life or personal social media presence to increase credibility on a personal channel
scopeExcludes: Phishing sent to the executive's corporate email account (other Whaling siblings)
Voice-channel impersonation of a family member targeting an executive's personal life, which is a Vishing ITID (ITID-11217) rather than phishing
ITID-11144.severity: High — personal channels sit outside corporate visibility, making detection and response materially harder.
ITID-11144.escalation: Escalate immediately; coordinate with the executive directly since corporate tooling has no visibility into personal accounts/devices.
indicators: Executive self-reporting a suspicious message received on a personal email or phone number
Personal device enrolled in corporate MDM showing an anomalous app installation or configuration change
vectors: Phishing SMS or personal email referencing the executive's public persona or personal interests
rootCauses: No corporate security control coverage over personal accounts/devices used to conduct any business activity
Executive's personal contact details being discoverable through public/leaked sources
controls: Executive digital-footprint/OSINT monitoring service
Guidance and support extending basic security hygiene to executives' personal accounts/devices
ITID-11144.detection: Very limited — personal accounts and devices are outside standard corporate telemetry; relies entirely on self-reporting.
ITID-11144.response: Work directly with the executive to assess any personal account/device impact and advise on remediation outside standard corporate tooling.
metrics: Count of personal-channel whaling incidents self-reported per quarter
ITID-11144.notes: This leaf covers the phishing (text/email) channel to a personal account; the equivalent voice-call attack on an executive's personal/family life is scoped instead to ITID-11217 under Vishing to keep channel-based reporting clean.

playbook.name: Response: Personal Device / Personal Account Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack targeting an executive's personal device or personal email/social account (outside corporate control) as a route to corporate compromise, exploiting the weaker security controls typical of personal accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the personal account/device involved and its link to corporate access
steps.desc: Identify the specific personal account or device targeted and determine what corporate access it has (forwarded corporate email, VPN, SSO, MDM enrollment).
steps.guidance: Executives often forward corporate email to personal accounts or use personal devices for corporate access — establish this linkage precisely, as it determines corporate exposure.
steps.outcome: Personal account/device identified and its corporate access linkage documented.

steps.title: Revoke the personal account/device's corporate access immediately
steps.desc: Revoke VPN, SSO, or MDM-based corporate access tied to the personal account/device.
steps.outcome: Corporate access from the personal account/device revoked.

steps.title: Check corporate systems for any exposure from the personal-account compromise
steps.desc: Review corporate account/system logs for any anomalous activity correlated with the personal-account compromise window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of corporate-side exposure.

steps.title: Restore corporate access under tightened conditions
steps.desc: Restore corporate access from the personal device/account only once confirmed clean, and consider requiring a corporate-managed device going forward.
steps.outcome: Access restored under appropriately tightened conditions.

steps.title: Document and review the BYOD/personal-account policy for executives
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend a specific policy or technical control (e.g. mandatory corporate device for executives, restricted personal-device access) to reduce this exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy recommendation delivered to leadership.

steps.title: Determine compromise status and corporate exposure
steps.desc: Establish whether the personal account/device was compromised and, if so, what corporate systems/data it could reach.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise status and corporate exposure scope.
steps.abort: If no compromise occurred, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Assist the executive in securing the personal account/device directly
steps.desc: Advise or directly assist the executive (with their consent) in resetting the personal account's password, enabling MFA, and scanning/cleaning the personal device.
steps.guidance: Corporate IT typically cannot act unilaterally on a personal account — work with the executive's cooperation and consider engaging executive protection/concierge IT support if available.
steps.outcome: Personal account/device secured with the executive's cooperation.

steps.title: Remediate any confirmed corporate-side compromise
steps.desc: Remove any attacker-added persistence found in corporate systems as a result of the personal-account compromise.
steps.outcome: Corporate environment confirmed clean.

ITID-11145.def: A phishing attack against a senior executive timed to coincide with their known travel itinerary or a public event appearance, using publicly gathered (OSINT) detail about the trip or event to increase the lure's credibility and urgency.
ITID-11145.purpose: Captures whaling deliberately timed to an executive's known travel or public event appearance, using OSINT to increase the lure's plausibility and urgency.
scopeIncludes: Lure referencing the executive's specific known travel dates, destination, or conference appearance
Phishing timed to arrive during a period when the executive is known to be less reachable through normal channels (in transit, on stage)
scopeExcludes: Whaling with no travel/event-timing angle (other Whaling siblings)
General OSINT-informed vishing/financial fraud calls exploiting travel timing (ITID-11229, Reconnaissance-Informed Financial Fraud Call), which is the voice-channel equivalent
ITID-11145.severity: High — the timing exploits reduced verification opportunity while the executive is traveling.
ITID-11145.escalation: Escalate immediately; verify any urgent request through a pre-established out-of-band channel given reduced reachability during travel.
indicators: Lure content accurately referencing non-public or semi-public travel/event detail
Timing of the phishing attempt correlating precisely with a known trip or public appearance
vectors: Email impersonating a colleague requesting urgent action while the executive is 'traveling and unreachable'
rootCauses: Executive travel schedules or conference appearances being discoverable through public calendars, social media, or event listings
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Pre-established out-of-band verification procedure for urgent requests during executive travel
Executive digital-footprint/OSINT monitoring service
ITID-11145.detection: Relies heavily on reporting; the OSINT-gathering stage itself is not directly observable by the organization.
ITID-11145.response: Verify any related urgent request through the pre-established out-of-band channel before acting, regardless of apparent urgency.
metrics: Count of travel/event-timed whaling incidents per quarter
ITID-11145.notes: Scope decision: this leaf covers the email/phishing channel; the equivalent voice-call technique exploiting the same travel-timing OSINT is logged under ITID-11229 to keep channel-based reporting distinct.

playbook.name: Response: OSINT-Informed Travel/Event-Timed Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack timed to an executive's known travel or public event appearance (gleaned from public OSINT such as conference agendas, social posts, or press coverage), exploiting reduced availability/verification during travel.

steps.title: Confirm the OSINT source and timing correlation
steps.desc: Identify the public source (conference agenda, social media post, press release) that revealed the executive's travel/event timing, and confirm the phishing attempt's timing correlates with it.
steps.outcome: OSINT source and timing correlation documented.

steps.title: Contain any resulting exposure
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions or halt any financial/data action taken.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.

steps.title: Check for persistence and remediate
steps.desc: Review any affected account for persistence and remediate.
steps.outcome: Persistence confirmed and remediated.

steps.title: Restore access and reinforce travel-verification protocol
steps.desc: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA and confirm a travel-specific verification protocol (e.g. designated backup approver) is in place for future travel.
steps.outcome: Access restored; travel-verification protocol confirmed or established.

steps.title: Document and reduce public OSINT exposure of executive travel
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend reducing public/social visibility of executive travel plans ahead of time where feasible.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; OSINT exposure reduction recommendation delivered.

steps.title: Determine what action was taken given reduced availability
steps.desc: Confirm whether the executive or their team acted on the request, noting whether normal verification steps were skipped due to the executive being unreachable/traveling.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Reach the executive directly to confirm status and block the sender
steps.desc: Use a pre-established out-of-band channel to reach the traveling executive and confirm their actual status, and block the phishing sender.
steps.outcome: Executive status confirmed; sender blocked.

ITID-11146.def: A phishing email sent to a senior executive carrying a malicious attachment tailored to reference their role, organization, or a plausible business document they would expect to receive.
ITID-11146.purpose: Captures whaling that uses a malicious attachment as the payload, isolating the technical delivery mechanism from the audience/timing-based Whaling siblings.
scopeIncludes: Attachment referencing a real project, board matter, or executive-level document
Malicious attachment sent as a targeted follow-up after OSINT research on the executive
scopeExcludes: The equivalent technique used against a non-executive target (Targeted Spear Phishing, ITID-11122)

Attachment delivered via a cloned/hijacked prior thread targeting an executive (which should still be logged under the Clone Phishing branch, ITID-1113x, since the cloning mechanism is the more specific classification)
ITID-11146.severity: High — combines executive targeting with a direct malware payload.
ITID-11146.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR upon any confirmed execution given the executive's typical level of system access.
indicators: Attachment filename referencing a real, specific board or executive-level matter
EDR alert for a spawned process from an Office application on an executive's device
vectors: Tailored document lure referencing board materials, contracts, or executive-level reports
rootCauses: Executives often granted broader local admin or reduced application-control restrictions than standard users
Macro execution not blocked by policy
controls: Attachment sandboxing/detonation
Macro execution blocking policy
EDR on endpoints, with equivalent hardening applied to executive devices
ITID-11146.detection: EDR and sandboxing give good coverage once opened; the targeted email itself is hard to catch pre-delivery.
ITID-11146.response: Sandbox-detonate the attachment, isolate the executive's device if execution is confirmed, and treat as high-priority given typical executive access levels.
metrics: Count of attachment-based whaling incidents per quarter
Number involving confirmed execution
ITID-11146.notes: Where the same executive receives the attachment via a hijacked/cloned prior thread, log under the Clone Phishing branch (ITID-1113x) instead, since the cloning mechanism is the more specific and actionable classification.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Attachment Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack delivering malware via a malicious attachment specifically crafted for and sent to a senior executive.

steps.title: Preserve the attachment and notify security leadership immediately
steps.desc: Collect the attachment and email headers and notify security leadership given the elevated risk of executive targeting.
steps.outcome: Attachment preserved; leadership notified.

steps.title: Isolate the executive's device
steps.desc: Network-isolate the device if execution is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the attachment in a sandbox to determine malware family and capability, and assess for advanced/targeted-actor tooling.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore the device and place under close monitoring
steps.desc: Return the reimaged device to the executive and place associated accounts under close, elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; elevated monitoring active.

steps.title: Brief the executive and assess targeted-threat implications
steps.desc: Brief the executive directly and assess whether the malware/tooling indicates a sophisticated, potentially nation-state or organized threat actor requiring broader response.
steps.outcome: Executive briefed; threat-actor assessment completed and escalated if warranted.

steps.title: Confirm execution and payload behavior
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry for execution and any resulting process/network activity on the executive's device.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status and behavior.
steps.abort: If unexecuted, downgrade to a near-miss but still brief the executive.

steps.title: Block the sender and check for related executive targeting
steps.desc: Block the sending infrastructure and check whether other executives received similar attachments.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked; executive-wide targeting scope assessed.

steps.title: Remediate the device (reimage given the elevated risk)
steps.desc: Reimage the executive's device rather than clean-in-place, given the sensitivity of data typically on an executive endpoint.
steps.outcome: Device reimaged and confirmed clean.

ITID-11147.def: A phishing email sent to a senior executive containing a link to a fake login page tailored to the organization, designed to capture the executive's credentials directly without real-time session-token relay.
ITID-11147.purpose: Captures whaling that drives an executive to a static credential-harvesting page, isolating this technical mechanism from the audience/timing-based Whaling siblings.
scopeIncludes: Link to a fake login page branded to match the organization's actual internal SSO/portal, sent to an executive
Targeted credential-harvesting lures referencing an executive-specific application or approval system
scopeExcludes: Real-time AiTM session-token relay against an executive (ITID-11148)
The equivalent technique used against a non-executive target (Targeted Spear Phishing, ITID-11123)
ITID-11147.severity: High — executive accounts typically carry elevated approval authority and data access.
ITID-11147.escalation: Escalate to IAM/SOC immediately upon confirmed submission given the executive's access level.
indicators: Link to a lookalike domain closely mimicking the organization's actual SSO branding, sent to an executive
Web proxy log showing the executive visiting a newly registered lookalike domain
vectors: Spoofed internal SSO/portal login page tailored to the organization's real branding
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA on executive accounts specifically
Brand/domain monitoring not catching a lookalike domain quickly enough
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn), prioritized for executive accounts
Brand/domain-abuse monitoring and takedown
ITID-11147.detection: URL rewriting and web proxy telemetry provide good visibility once the link is clicked.
ITID-11147.response: Force password reset for the executive, review sign-in logs, and request domain takedown as a priority.
metrics: Count of executive credential-harvesting incidents per quarter
ITID-11147.notes: Deliberately excludes AiTM relay kits, logged separately under ITID-11148, since session-token theft requires a different response than a static credential harvest.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Link Whaling (Credential Harvesting)
playbook.description: For a whaling attack delivering a link to a fake login page crafted specifically to target a senior executive's credentials.

steps.title: Preserve the message and notify security leadership immediately
steps.desc: Collect the email with headers and link, and notify security leadership given the elevated risk.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; leadership notified.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all sessions immediately
steps.desc: Reset the executive's password and revoke all active sessions/tokens without delay given the account's typically broad access.
steps.outcome: Account secured against further use.

steps.title: Check for account persistence thoroughly
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, OAuth grants, and any delegate access changes.
steps.guidance: Executive accounts often have broad delegate permissions and financial approval authority — check these specifically, not just standard mailbox rules.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence and delegate-access tampering.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA and close monitoring
steps.desc: Have the executive set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device, then place the account under close monitoring.
steps.outcome: Account restored; elevated monitoring active.

steps.title: Brief the executive and prioritize phishing-resistant MFA
steps.desc: Brief the executive directly and prioritize rollout of phishing-resistant authentication for this account given the confirmed successful targeting.
steps.outcome: Executive briefed; authentication-hardening recommendation delivered.

steps.title: Confirm whether credentials were submitted
steps.desc: Check click-tracking and interview the executive/staff to confirm what was entered.
steps.outcome: Confirmed credential submission status.
steps.abort: If no credentials submitted, downgrade to a near-miss but still brief the executive.

steps.title: Block the harvesting site and check for related executive targeting
steps.desc: Block the harvesting domain and check whether other executives received similar targeted links.
steps.outcome: Site blocked; executive-wide targeting scope assessed.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods, and restore any tampered delegate permissions.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11148.def: A phishing attack against a senior executive using a reverse-proxy AiTM kit that relays the real login flow and steals the resulting session token, bypassing standard MFA for the executive's account.
ITID-11148.purpose: Captures whaling using an adversary-in-the-middle kit against a senior executive, distinguishing session-token theft from static credential harvesting.
scopeIncludes: Executive-targeted lure linking to a known or suspected AiTM/reverse-proxy phishing kit
Confirmed theft of a session cookie/token for an executive account
scopeExcludes: Static executive-targeted credential harvesting with no session relay (ITID-11147)
The same technique used against a non-executive individual (Targeted Spear Phishing, ITID-11124)
ITID-11148.severity: Critical — combines executive-level access with an MFA-bypassing technique.
ITID-11148.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to revoke active sessions and refresh tokens; treat as a potential precursor to broader compromise given the executive's access level.
indicators: Sign-in logs showing a successful MFA-satisfied login from an unfamiliar location immediately after the executive clicked a link
Reverse-proxy fingerprint matching known AiTM kits
vectors: Reverse-proxy phishing kit tailored with the organization's branding, targeted specifically at an executive
rootCauses: Standard OTP/push MFA in use instead of phishing-resistant MFA on the executive account
Session tokens not bound to device/IP
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn), prioritized for executive accounts
Session/token binding and conditional access risk policies
ITID-11148.detection: Identity provider sign-in risk and session-anomaly detection give strong coverage once the token is used.
ITID-11148.response: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for the executive account immediately, then investigate for lateral movement and data access during the exposure window.
metrics: Count of confirmed executive AiTM session-token thefts per quarter
Median time from theft to session revocation
ITID-11148.notes: Scoped to the initial-access/session-theft event; post-compromise activity rolls up under the relevant Unauthorized Access or Data Breach ITID to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: Response: AiTM Whaling Kit Campaign
playbook.description: For a whaling attack using an adversary-in-the-middle reverse-proxy phishing kit against a senior executive, capturing live session cookies to defeat MFA.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm AiTM technique
steps.desc: Collect the email and link, notify security leadership immediately, and confirm AiTM behavior via sign-in logs showing a successful authentication with MFA immediately following the interaction from an unfamiliar location.
steps.outcome: AiTM technique confirmed; leadership notified.

steps.title: Revoke all sessions and tokens immediately
steps.desc: Force a global session/token revocation for the executive's account without delay given its broad access.
steps.guidance: Password reset alone does not invalidate an already-stolen session cookie — explicit session/token revocation is mandatory.
steps.outcome: Stolen session invalidated.

steps.title: Check for attacker actions during the hijacked session, including financial systems
steps.desc: Review audit logs for mailbox rules, data access, OAuth consent, new MFA methods, and any access to financial/approval systems the executive can reach.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker actions documented, including any financial-system exposure.

steps.title: Restore access with new credentials and phishing-resistant MFA
steps.desc: Have the executive set a new password and enroll in phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkey) given the confirmed AiTM bypass of traditional MFA.
steps.outcome: Account restored with hardened, confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Brief the executive and leadership on the sophisticated threat
steps.desc: Brief the executive and security leadership on the AiTM technique and recommend organization-wide acceleration of phishing-resistant authentication given the demonstrated capability against a high-value target.
steps.outcome: Briefing delivered; organizational recommendation escalated to leadership.

steps.title: Identify stolen session token use and attacker actions
steps.desc: Review sign-in and activity logs for session replay and any subsequent attacker actions on the executive's account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed token theft and full scope of attacker activity.

steps.title: Block the proxy domain
steps.desc: Block the AiTM proxy domain at DNS/web proxy.
steps.outcome: Proxy domain blocked.

steps.title: Remove all attacker-established persistence
steps.desc: Remove any malicious inbox rule, revoke unauthorized OAuth grants, and remove attacker-registered MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

steps.title: Monitor closely for an extended window
steps.desc: Place the account under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days given the sophistication and targeting.
steps.outcome: No anomalous activity observed during the monitoring window.

ITID-11149.def: A phishing email sent from an already-compromised legitimate email account, directed at a senior executive and leveraging that account's real trust relationship with the executive to increase credibility.
ITID-11149.purpose: Captures whaling sent from a genuinely compromised, trusted account and directed at (or through) a senior executive, distinguishing the phishing/further-compromise vector from downstream financial-fraud outcomes.
scopeIncludes: Phishing sent from a confirmed-compromised internal or partner mailbox specifically to a senior executive
Cases where the trust relationship being exploited is between the compromised sender and the executive target
scopeExcludes: The same technique used to directly solicit a fraudulent wire transfer or payment from the executive, which is Business Email Compromise financial fraud (ITID-22411 through ITID-22415, and ITID-53111 for the fraud-execution stage)
The equivalent technique used against a non-executive target (Targeted Spear Phishing, ITID-11125)
ITID-11149.severity: Critical — a compromised trusted account defeats sender-reputation defenses and executive targets typically hold high-value access.
ITID-11149.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC to contain the source account in parallel with briefing and protecting the executive target.
indicators: Phishing email originating from a genuinely authenticated internal or partner mailbox, directed at an executive
Sign-in anomaly on the source account shortly before the phishing email was sent
vectors: Compromised mailbox of a known business partner or colleague used to send a targeted lure to the executive
rootCauses: The source account's initial compromise not detected before it was used to target the executive
No outbound-mail anomaly detection on the source account
controls: Outbound mail anomaly detection
Phishing-resistant MFA
Prompt session revocation on detected account compromise
ITID-11149.detection: Outbound mail behavior analytics and executive/staff reporting provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-11149.response: Contain the source account immediately and verify with the executive whether any action was taken on the email before confirming it was malicious.
metrics: Count of compromised-account whaling incidents per quarter
ITID-11149.notes: Deliberately scoped to the phishing/further-compromise use of the hijacked account targeting an executive; if the same compromised account is instead used to directly request a fraudulent payment from or impersonating the executive, log that under the Business Email Compromise ITIDs (ITID-22411 family / ITID-53111) instead to avoid duplicating the incident across two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Compromised Trusted-Account Whaling
playbook.description: For a whaling attack sent to a senior executive from a genuinely compromised trusted account (a colleague, board member, or known partner) rather than a spoofed identity.

steps.title: Confirm the sending account is genuinely compromised and notify leadership
steps.desc: Verify sender authentication results (SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass) confirming the source account is genuinely compromised, and notify security leadership immediately given executive targeting.
steps.outcome: Genuine compromise confirmed; leadership notified.
steps.abort: If authentication fails, this is spoofing, not compromise — redirect to the appropriate spoofed-sender whaling playbook.

steps.title: Contain the executive's exposure
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions or halt any financial/data action taken by the executive.
steps.outcome: Executive-side exposure contained.

steps.title: Check both accounts for persistence
steps.desc: Review the executive's account and (if applicable) the internal sending account for attacker-added persistence.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence on each account.

steps.title: Restore access for both accounts with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Restore the executive's and (if applicable) the internal sender's account access with fresh MFA enrollment.
steps.outcome: Both accounts restored to confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Document the trust-chain exploitation and consider board/partner vendor-risk review
steps.desc: Record findings and, if the compromised account belonged to a board member or external partner, raise this as a vendor/relationship-risk finding for follow-up.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; relationship-risk finding raised if applicable.

steps.title: Notify the compromised account's owner and determine executive's response
steps.desc: Alert the compromised account owner and confirm whether the executive acted on the message believing the sender was legitimate.
steps.outcome: Account owner notified; executive's action confirmed.
steps.abort: If the executive took no action, downgrade to a near-miss for the executive (compromised sender still requires action).

steps.title: If the compromised account is internal, contain it directly
steps.desc: If the compromised sending account belongs to your own organization, reset its credentials, revoke sessions, and isolate any associated host.
steps.outcome: Internal compromised account contained if applicable.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods on both accounts.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on either account.

ITID-11151.def: A phishing-style email sent as part of a verified, organizationally sanctioned security-awareness testing program, logged here before the specific outcome (passed, failed, sponsor type) is recorded.
ITID-11151.purpose: Catch-all for a logged, organizationally sanctioned phishing simulation event whose specific outcome or sponsor type has not yet been recorded.
scopeIncludes: Initial logging of a confirmed-sanctioned simulation event before outcome detail is available
scopeExcludes: Any case where sanctioning cannot be verified — log as ITID-11152 (Unverified Sponsorship Claim) instead until confirmed
Any case where the outcome is known — reclassify to ITID-11153 through ITID-11158
ITID-11151.severity: None/informational — this is a controlled internal exercise, not an attack.
ITID-11151.escalation: No security escalation required; escalate only to the awareness-training program owner for outcome tracking.
indicators: A phishing-style email matching a pre-registered simulation campaign identifier or sending domain
vectors: Simulated phishing email sent to general employee population via approved awareness platform
Simulated spear-phishing link targeting a broad, unclassified user group
rootCauses: Lack of scheduled baseline phishing awareness testing program
No prior simulation data to segment users by risk level
controls: Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11151.detection: Simulation platform reporting provides full visibility into delivery and interaction for sanctioned campaigns.
ITID-11151.response: Confirm sanctioning against the program's campaign registry and record the outcome once available.
metrics: Count of sanctioned simulation events logged per campaign
ITID-11151.notes: This branch tracks sanctioned internal exercises and must never be merged with real-attack phishing statistics; confirm sanctioning before logging here rather than under a real attack ITID.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Sponsored Phishing Simulation
playbook.description: For a reported phishing message that turns out to be an internal or vendor-sponsored phishing-awareness test, where the specific simulation sub-category has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the message matches an active simulation campaign
steps.desc: Check the security-awareness platform (or the sponsoring team) for an active campaign whose sender domain, subject, and timing match the reported message.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference sender IP/domain against the awareness platform's published sending infrastructure list.
steps.outcome: Match confirmed against a known, currently-active simulation campaign.
steps.abort: If no matching campaign is found, escalate immediately and reclassify as a suspected real phishing attack (see ITID-11152).

steps.title: Reassure the reporting user, if applicable
steps.desc: If the user submitted a ticket or contacted the SOC believing this was a real attack, confirm to them it was an authorized internal test and no further action is needed on their part.
steps.guidance: Do not reveal simulation status broadly if the campaign is still running against other users.
steps.outcome: Reporting user informed appropriately without disclosing the campaign to still-untested staff.

steps.title: Log the simulation outcome for the campaign record
steps.desc: Record the result in the awareness platform or campaign tracker so it rolls up into the overall campaign metrics.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded against the campaign.

steps.title: Note any process friction for future campaigns
steps.desc: Record whether the SOC intake process for this report was efficient, and flag any confusion (e.g. delayed sponsorship confirmation) for the next campaign planning cycle.
steps.outcome: Process note logged.

steps.title: Identify the reporting or targeted user and their action
steps.desc: Record which user(s) received the simulation and whether they clicked, submitted data, reported it, or took no action.
steps.outcome: User outcome recorded (no action / clicked / submitted / reported).

ITID-11152.def: A phishing-style email that claims or implies it is part of a sanctioned internal security test, but which does not match any registered campaign in the security awareness program and cannot be verified as legitimate — handled as a suspected genuine attack pending verification.
ITID-11152.purpose: Captures a reported phishing email claimed by the sender to be an authorized simulation, but whose sanctioning cannot be verified against the security awareness program's records — treated as a suspected real attack until confirmed.
scopeIncludes: Any phishing email claiming to be a 'test' or 'simulation' that does not match a registered campaign
Cases where sponsorship is claimed verbally or in-message but no record exists in the simulation platform
scopeExcludes: Any case where sanctioning is subsequently confirmed against the program registry — reclassify to ITID-11151 or the appropriate outcome leaf
A confirmed real attack with no simulation claim at all (the relevant Phishing Attacks ITID)
ITID-11152.severity: Medium-High — treat with the same rigor as a real attack until sanctioning is disproven or confirmed.
ITID-11152.escalation: Escalate to the SOC as a suspected real attack; escalate to the awareness-training program owner in parallel to check for an unregistered or miscommunicated legitimate test.
indicators: Phishing content explicitly claiming to be a security test with no matching registry entry
A vendor or internal team claiming after the fact to have sent a 'test' that was never approved through the standard process
vectors: Attacker impersonating a security-awareness vendor to discourage reporting of a real attack
rootCauses: Weak or informal approval process for internal phishing simulations enabling ambiguity
No central registry accessible to the SOC for verifying claimed simulation campaigns in real time
controls: Central simulation campaign registry accessible to the SOC for real-time verification
Formal written approval process for all internal phishing simulations
ITID-11152.detection: Relies on cross-referencing the SOC's verification checks against the simulation platform's campaign registry.
ITID-11152.response: Investigate exactly as a real attack until sanctioning is confirmed; do not stand down response purely on the basis of a claimed 'test'.
metrics: Count of unverified sponsorship claims investigated per quarter
Percentage resolved as genuine simulations vs. real attacks
ITID-11152.notes: This leaf exists specifically to prevent attackers from using a false 'this is just a test' claim to suppress a real incident response; always verify against the registry rather than trusting the claim.

playbook.name: Response: Unverified Sponsorship Claim (Suspected Real Attack)
playbook.description: For a phishing message where the sender or a downstream actor claims the message is a sanctioned internal or vendor phishing-awareness test, but no active sponsoring campaign can be confirmed. Treat as a genuine attack attempting to evade response by impersonating a simulation.

steps.title: Attempt to verify the sponsorship claim through the authorized channel only
steps.desc: Check the awareness platform and contact the internal security-awareness owner directly (not via any contact information provided in the suspect message) to confirm whether a legitimate campaign is running.
steps.guidance: Never use a phone number, email, or link supplied by the suspect message to perform this verification.
steps.outcome: Sponsorship claim confirmed false or unconfirmable.
steps.abort: If sponsorship is positively confirmed through the authorized channel, reclassify under ITID-11151 and stop this playbook.

steps.title: Block sender and malicious infrastructure across mail and web gateways
steps.desc: Add the sending domain/IP and any linked URLs to block lists.
steps.outcome: Further delivery and callback traffic blocked.

steps.title: Check for attacker-established persistence on affected accounts
steps.desc: Review for new mail rules, OAuth grants, forwarding rules, or MFA method changes on any account that submitted credentials.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected accounts with re-enrolled MFA and confirm clean state
steps.desc: Complete password reset, MFA re-enrollment from a clean device, and removal of any attacker artifacts before returning accounts to normal use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the false-sponsorship pretext and recommend a verification control
steps.desc: Record that the attacker impersonated a sanctioned simulation, and recommend a standard way for staff to verify simulation legitimacy through the authorized channel going forward.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a control recommendation.

steps.title: Preserve the original message and any attacker infrastructure indicators
steps.desc: Export the full message with headers, and capture any URLs, attachments, or phone numbers referenced.
steps.guidance: Export as .eml/.msg, not a forward.
steps.outcome: Original message and indicators preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Force credential reset for any user who submitted data
steps.desc: Immediately reset passwords and revoke active sessions for affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Determine scope of delivery and interaction
steps.desc: Identify all recipients of the message and which recipients clicked, submitted credentials, or executed attachments.
steps.outcome: Full recipient and interaction list established.

steps.title: Quarantine or remove the message from all mailboxes
steps.desc: Use mail gateway search-and-purge to remove the message from any mailbox it was delivered to but not yet opened.
steps.outcome: Message removed fleet-wide.

ITID-11153.def: A logged outcome of a sanctioned phishing simulation in which the targeted employee interacted with the simulated lure — clicking a link, opening an attachment, or submitting credentials into a simulated capture form.
ITID-11153.purpose: Captures the specific outcome of a sanctioned simulation where the recipient interacted with the lure (clicked, opened, or submitted credentials), used to drive individual and program-level training metrics.
scopeIncludes: Any interaction event captured by the simulation platform (click, open, credential submission) for a sanctioned campaign
scopeExcludes: The same interaction occurring in a real, non-sanctioned phishing attack (the relevant Phishing Attacks ITID)
The employee correctly reporting the simulation despite having initially clicked, which is instead a partial-pass nuance recorded within this same outcome for training purposes
ITID-11153.severity: None/informational from a security-risk standpoint — no real compromise occurred — but relevant to individual training-risk scoring.
ITID-11153.priority: P4/informational; routed to just-in-time training rather than incident response.
ITID-11153.escalation: No SOC escalation; route to the awareness-training program for automatic just-in-time coaching content delivery to the employee.
indicators: Simulation platform logging a click, open, or submission event tied to a specific employee
vectors: Simulated phishing email with embedded link clicked by user
Simulated phishing email attachment opened by user during sponsored campaign
rootCauses: Gaps in the employee's or population's phishing-recognition training
controls: Just-in-time training triggered automatically on simulation failure
Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11153.detection: Full visibility via the simulation platform's built-in tracking.
ITID-11153.response: Deliver automated just-in-time training to the employee; no containment action needed since no real payload was involved.
metrics: Organization-wide and per-department simulation failure rate
Click-to-submission conversion rate within simulations
ITID-11153.notes: A single individual accumulating repeated instances of this outcome should additionally be logged under ITID-11155 (Repeat Failure/At-Risk Employee Pattern) for trend-based coaching.

playbook.name: Response: Simulation Failed - User Interacted
playbook.description: For a confirmed sponsored phishing simulation where the targeted user clicked the link and/or submitted data into the simulated harvesting page.

steps.title: Confirm the campaign and the specific interaction recorded
steps.desc: Verify against the awareness platform that this user is a target of an active campaign and confirm exactly what interaction was logged (click only vs. data submission).
steps.outcome: Interaction type confirmed (click / submission).
steps.abort: If no matching campaign exists, escalate as a suspected real attack (ITID-11152).

steps.title: Trigger the automated just-in-time training module for the user
steps.desc: Confirm the awareness platform has enrolled the user in the immediate follow-up micro-training assigned to simulation failures.
steps.outcome: Training module assigned and delivered.

steps.title: Record the failure outcome against the user's training record
steps.desc: Log the click/submission event against the employee's awareness training history for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded in the employee training record.

steps.title: Feed the result into campaign-level effectiveness metrics
steps.desc: Record the failure against the campaign's overall click/submission rate to inform future scenario difficulty and targeting.
steps.outcome: Campaign metrics updated.

steps.title: Confirm no real credentials or sensitive data were entered
steps.desc: If the simulation landing page has a data-entry field, confirm the platform captured only simulated/test data and not the user's real password.
steps.guidance: Simulation platforms typically do not store real submitted values, but this should be confirmed per-vendor.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no real sensitive data was retained anywhere outside the awareness platform's controlled test.
steps.abort: If there is any doubt real credentials were entered into a non-test system, treat as ITID-11152.

ITID-11154.def: A logged outcome of a sanctioned phishing simulation in which the targeted employee correctly identified the email as suspicious and reported it through the proper channel (report-phishing button or mailbox) without clicking or submitting information.
ITID-11154.purpose: Captures the specific outcome of a sanctioned simulation where the recipient correctly identified and reported the lure without interacting with it, used for positive reinforcement metrics.
scopeIncludes: Correct use of the report-phishing button/mailbox in direct response to a simulation email
Reporting occurring before any interaction with the simulated lure
scopeExcludes: Reporting occurring after the employee had already clicked or submitted information (still logged as ITID-11153, though the reporting behavior itself can be noted as a positive secondary action)
Correct reporting of a real, non-sanctioned phishing attack (the relevant Phishing Attacks ITID)
ITID-11154.severity: None/informational — this is the desired positive outcome.
ITID-11154.escalation: No escalation required; may trigger positive-reinforcement recognition per the awareness program's design.
indicators: Simulation platform logging a report-button click with no prior interaction event for that employee
vectors: Simulated phishing email correctly identified and reported by user via report-phish button
rootCauses: N/A - control operating as intended; documented as positive outcome to confirm training efficacy
controls: Report-phishing button/mailbox integrated with the simulation platform
Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11154.detection: Full visibility via the simulation platform's built-in tracking.
ITID-11154.response: No action beyond program-level positive reinforcement/recognition where the program includes it.
metrics: Organization-wide simulation pass/report rate
Median time-to-report for successful reports
ITID-11154.notes: Tracked as the positive counterpart to ITID-11153; the two together give the full population-level simulation outcome picture.

playbook.name: Response: Simulation Passed - User Reported Correctly
playbook.description: For a confirmed sponsored phishing simulation where the targeted user correctly identified the message as suspicious and reported it through the proper channel without interacting with it.

steps.title: Confirm the report matches an active simulation campaign
steps.desc: Verify the reported message corresponds to a currently-running simulation campaign targeting this user.
steps.outcome: Match confirmed.
steps.abort: If no matching campaign exists, treat this as a genuine phishing report and route to standard phishing triage instead.

steps.title: Record the pass outcome and acknowledge the user
steps.desc: Log the correct-report outcome in the awareness platform and, where the program supports it, send the user positive automated acknowledgement.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded; user acknowledged.

steps.title: Feed the result into campaign-level effectiveness metrics
steps.desc: Record the pass against the campaign's overall report rate to help gauge program effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Campaign metrics updated.

steps.title: Confirm the user took no interaction prior to reporting
steps.desc: Check the platform log to confirm the report was submitted without a prior click or data-entry event.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean report with no interaction.

ITID-11155.def: A tracked pattern in which a specific employee fails (per ITID-11153) multiple sanctioned phishing simulations within a defined program window, indicating elevated individual phishing susceptibility requiring targeted intervention.
ITID-11155.purpose: Captures the trend-level pattern of an individual employee repeatedly failing sanctioned simulations, used to trigger targeted coaching or risk-based access review rather than tracking a single event.
scopeIncludes: An employee crossing the program-defined repeat-failure threshold (e.g., 3+ failures within 12 months)
Cross-referencing of multiple individual ITID-11153 events for the same employee
scopeExcludes: A single, first-time simulation failure (ITID-11153) that has not yet crossed the repeat threshold
ITID-11155.severity: Low from a direct security-incident standpoint, but Medium from an organizational-risk standpoint given the sustained pattern.
ITID-11155.priority: P3, routed to HR/manager-supported coaching rather than standard incident handling.
ITID-11155.escalation: Escalate to the employee's manager and the awareness-training program owner for a structured coaching conversation; consider a temporary access-risk review for employees with sensitive access.
indicators: Simulation platform trend report flagging an employee above the repeat-failure threshold
vectors: Repeated simulated phishing failures by the same individual across multiple sponsored campaigns
Pattern of clicking links or submitting credentials on successive simulation rounds
rootCauses: Insufficient individualized follow-up after prior single-instance failures
Role or workload factors reducing the employee's attention to email scrutiny
controls: Targeted, escalating coaching program for repeat failures
Manager notification workflow for at-risk employees
ITID-11155.detection: Full visibility via the simulation platform's longitudinal reporting.
ITID-11155.response: Deliver structured, escalating coaching (beyond automated just-in-time training) and loop in the employee's manager.
metrics: Count of employees crossing the repeat-failure threshold per quarter
Re-failure rate after targeted coaching
ITID-11155.notes: This is a derived/trend classification built from multiple ITID-11153 events, not a new type of simulation email itself.

playbook.name: Response: Repeat Failure / At-Risk Employee Pattern
playbook.description: For a confirmed sponsored phishing simulation failure by a user who has failed multiple prior simulations, indicating a persistent at-risk pattern requiring corrective, non-punitive coaching.

steps.title: Confirm the campaign match and pull the user's full simulation history
steps.desc: Verify this failure against the active campaign, then pull the user's historical simulation results to confirm a repeat-failure pattern.
steps.outcome: Repeat-failure pattern confirmed with dates and scenario types of prior failures.
steps.abort: If no matching campaign exists, escalate as a suspected real attack (ITID-11152).

steps.title: Enroll the user in a supplemental, coaching-focused training track
steps.desc: Assign the user to a more intensive, supportive training track beyond the standard just-in-time module, framed as skill-building rather than discipline.
steps.guidance: Coordinate tone and framing with the employee's manager or HR liaison as applicable per policy.
steps.outcome: User enrolled in supplemental training.

steps.title: Notify the user's manager per program policy, with a coaching framing
steps.desc: If the program's escalation policy calls for manager notification at this repeat-failure threshold, notify them with an emphasis on support and follow-up rather than penalty.
steps.outcome: Manager notified per policy, where applicable.

steps.title: Document the pattern and schedule a follow-up check
