steps.desc: Record the repeat-failure pattern, the coaching action taken, and schedule a check against the user's next simulation result to confirm improvement.
steps.outcome: Pattern documented with a follow-up checkpoint.

steps.title: Identify whether prior failures share a common lure type
steps.desc: Review whether the user repeatedly falls for the same category of pretext (e.g. urgency, authority impersonation) to target coaching effectively.
steps.outcome: Common failure pattern identified, if any.

ITID-11156.def: A sanctioned phishing simulation campaign executed through a third-party security-awareness vendor's platform (e.g., a commercial phishing-simulation-as-a-service provider) under a verified contract with the organization.
ITID-11156.purpose: Tags a sanctioned simulation as run through an external third-party vendor platform, distinguishing sponsor-type reporting from internally-run red team simulations.
scopeIncludes: Any sanctioned simulation delivered through a contracted external vendor's platform and registered in the program registry
scopeExcludes: Simulations run by the organization's own internal red team (ITID-11157)
ITID-11156.escalation: No security escalation; escalate only vendor operational issues to vendor management.
indicators: Simulation email sending infrastructure matching the contracted vendor's known ranges/domains
vectors: Simulated phishing campaign run and reported on behalf of the organization by a contracted third-party vendor
rootCauses: No internal coordination between security team and vendor-run simulation schedule
Vendor simulation results not integrated with internal risk register
controls: Vendor due-diligence and contract governance for the awareness platform
Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11156.detection: Full visibility via the vendor platform's reporting dashboard.
ITID-11156.response: Confirm the vendor's sending infrastructure is properly allowlisted to avoid the campaign being blocked or misreported as a real attack.
metrics: Count of vendor-sponsored simulation campaigns per year
ITID-11156.notes: Sponsor-type tag only; the actual per-employee outcome should still be logged under ITID-11153/ITID-11154.

playbook.name: Response: Third-Party Vendor-Sponsored Simulation
playbook.description: For a phishing message confirmed as originating from an authorized third-party vendor running a contracted phishing-awareness simulation on the organization's behalf.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor's authorization and current contract scope
steps.desc: Verify with the internal awareness-program owner that this vendor is currently under contract to run simulations, and confirm the message matches the vendor's registered sending infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Check the vendor's published sending domains/IPs against an internally maintained allowlist, not against information in the message itself.
steps.outcome: Vendor authorization and infrastructure match confirmed.
steps.abort: If the vendor relationship cannot be confirmed through internal records, escalate as a suspected real attack (ITID-11152).
steps.tool: Vendor management / awareness platform admin console

steps.title: Confirm the vendor's data-handling terms for any submitted data
steps.desc: Verify that any data captured by the vendor's simulation landing page is handled per the data-processing agreement and not retained beyond program need.
steps.outcome: Data handling confirmed compliant with contract terms.

steps.title: Log the simulation outcome for the campaign record
steps.desc: Record the result in the awareness platform or campaign tracker so it rolls up into the vendor's reporting.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded.

steps.title: Note any vendor coordination gaps for the next engagement
steps.desc: Record whether advance notice, sending-infrastructure disclosure, or scope communication from the vendor was adequate for smooth SOC triage.
steps.outcome: Vendor coordination note logged.

steps.title: Confirm the campaign scope matches the reported activity
steps.desc: Check that the targeted users, timing, and lure type fall within the scope the vendor was contracted to deliver.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope confirmed as in-bounds.
steps.abort: If activity falls outside the contracted scope, contact the vendor account owner to confirm before proceeding.

ITID-11157.def: A sanctioned phishing simulation campaign designed and executed by the organization's internal red team, intended as a population-wide security-awareness test rather than a stealth, narrowly-scoped intrusion exercise.
ITID-11157.purpose: Tags a sanctioned population-wide phishing simulation as run by the organization's internal red team, distinguishing broad awareness-testing activity from a scoped, stealth penetration-test engagement.
scopeIncludes: Internal-red-team-run campaigns registered as awareness-program simulations and reported through the same population-level metrics as vendor-run campaigns
scopeExcludes: A formally scoped red team engagement's technical credential-harvesting activity conducted as part of a broader, typically stealth, adversary-emulation exercise — logged instead under ITID-91121 (Simulated Credential Harvesting via Fake Login Page) in the dedicated Simulations and Testing Activities domain
ITID-11157.escalation: No security escalation; coordinate scheduling with the SOC to avoid confusion with a real incident.
indicators: Campaign registered in the awareness program registry as internal-red-team-sponsored
vectors: Simulated phishing/social-engineering campaign executed by internal red team as part of an authorized engagement
rootCauses: Gaps identified by red team in email filtering, user reporting behavior, or escalation workflow
controls: Formal rules-of-engagement/scoping document distinguishing awareness simulations from red team engagements
Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11157.detection: Full visibility via internal coordination with the red team's campaign registry.
ITID-11157.response: Confirm scoping intent up front: if the activity is part of a formally scoped, stealth red team engagement rather than a broad employee-population test, it belongs under ITID-91121 instead.
metrics: Count of internal-red-team-sponsored simulation campaigns per year
ITID-11157.notes: Scope decision: the rule for avoiding duplication with ITID-91121 is intent and audience — a broad, population-wide awareness test run by the red team belongs here; a stealth, narrowly-scoped adversary-emulation engagement belongs under ITID-91121 in the Simulations and Testing Activities domain.

playbook.name: Response: Internal Red Team-Sponsored Simulation
playbook.description: For a phishing message confirmed as originating from the organization's own internal red team under an approved rules-of-engagement (RoE) document, rather than a standard awareness-platform campaign.

steps.title: Confirm an active, signed rules-of-engagement covers this activity
steps.desc: Contact the red team lead directly (via a pre-established internal channel, not contact information in the message) to confirm a currently-authorized RoE covers this specific exercise, including target scope and time window.
steps.guidance: Do not rely solely on verbal confirmation; confirm against the signed RoE document.
steps.outcome: Active RoE confirmed covering this activity.
steps.abort: If no active RoE can be confirmed, escalate as a suspected real attack (ITID-11152) and pause any deconfliction assumptions.

steps.title: Apply any RoE-specified handling constraints
steps.desc: Follow any exercise-specific instructions in the RoE, such as not blocking red team infrastructure or not resetting a target account's credentials, so as not to invalidate the exercise.
steps.outcome: Handling aligned with RoE constraints.

steps.title: Log the interaction outcome for the exercise record
steps.desc: Record what occurred (detection timing, user interaction, SOC response actions) for inclusion in the red team's after-action report.
steps.outcome: Outcome logged for the exercise record.

steps.title: Contribute findings to the joint red team / SOC debrief
steps.desc: Record detection gaps or response-time observations to feed into the post-exercise purple-team debrief.
steps.outcome: Findings logged for debrief.

steps.title: Confirm SOC deconfliction status for this exercise
steps.desc: Verify whether the SOC was pre-briefed (white-carded) on this exercise or whether it is intentionally being run blind to test detection, per the RoE.
steps.outcome: Deconfliction status clarified so the SOC handles the event per the agreed exercise design.

ITID-11158.def: A sanctioned phishing simulation campaign that was misconfigured or technically flawed in its execution — for example, sent to the wrong distribution list, using an inappropriate or overly realistic template, or with broken click/reporting telemetry — requiring operational correction.
ITID-11158.purpose: Captures an operational error in a sanctioned simulation's execution (wrong template, wrong audience, broken tracking), used to correct the program rather than to score employee behavior.
scopeIncludes: Campaign sent to unintended recipients (e.g., contractors, external partners, or an incorrect internal list)
Template misconfiguration causing an inappropriate or overly convincing/harmful lure theme (e.g., referencing a sensitive real event)
Broken tracking preventing outcome data from being captured
scopeExcludes: A correctly executed campaign whose outcome is simply a high failure rate (ITID-11153 in aggregate) — that is a training-need signal, not a misconfiguration
ITID-11158.severity: Low from a security standpoint, but may carry reputational/employee-relations impact depending on the error.
ITID-11158.priority: P3, routed to the awareness-program owner for correction.
ITID-11158.escalation: Escalate to the program owner and, for externally-sent misconfigurations, to legal/communications given potential reputational exposure.
indicators: Recipient complaints referencing an inappropriate template theme or unexpected audience
Simulation platform showing zero tracked interactions consistent with a telemetry failure rather than universal success
vectors: Simulated phishing template misaligned with intended technique or audience, producing invalid campaign results
rootCauses: Inadequate pre-launch review of campaign audience/template configuration
Simulation platform integration issues affecting tracking accuracy
controls: Mandatory pre-launch review checklist for audience and template configuration
Security awareness phishing simulation program
ITID-11158.detection: Relies on recipient complaints and post-campaign data-quality review.
ITID-11158.response: Halt the campaign if still in progress, correct the configuration, and communicate as appropriate to affected recipients.
metrics: Count of misconfigured campaigns per year
Percentage of campaigns passing pre-launch review without incident
ITID-11158.notes: This leaf is about program execution quality, not employee behavior — do not use it to record a legitimately high failure rate.

playbook.name: Response: Simulation Technique Mismatch / Misconfigured Campaign
playbook.description: For a confirmed sponsored simulation where the delivered message does not match its intended template or configuration (e.g. wrong lure sent to wrong audience, broken landing-page link, incorrect branding), indicating a campaign configuration error rather than user behavior of interest.

steps.title: Confirm the campaign source and identify the specific mismatch
steps.desc: Verify the message against the awareness platform's intended campaign configuration and identify exactly what does not match (wrong template, wrong audience, broken link, incorrect sender branding, etc.).
steps.outcome: Specific misconfiguration identified.
steps.abort: If the message cannot be matched to any configured campaign at all, escalate as a suspected real attack (ITID-11152).

steps.title: Pause or correct the affected campaign
steps.desc: Pause the misconfigured campaign in the awareness platform to prevent further mis-delivery, and correct the configuration before any resend.
steps.outcome: Campaign paused or corrected.

steps.title: Exclude or flag affected results from campaign metrics
steps.desc: Mark results from the misconfigured send as invalid in the platform so they do not skew click/report-rate metrics or unfairly affect individual training records.
steps.outcome: Affected results flagged or excluded.

steps.title: Document the configuration error and recommend a pre-send validation step
steps.desc: Record the root cause of the misconfiguration and recommend a check (e.g. test-send review) to catch similar errors before future campaigns launch.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Determine the scope of users affected by the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Identify how many recipients received the mismatched or broken simulation, since results from this send should likely be excluded from normal reporting.
steps.outcome: Affected recipient scope established.

ITID-11211.def: An unsolicited phone call in which the caller falsely claims to represent a specific trusted identity (institution, colleague, or individual) in order to manipulate the recipient, whose specific impersonated identity has not yet been confirmed.
ITID-11211.purpose: Catch-all for a reported vishing call in which the caller impersonated some identity, where the specific impersonated identity has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported impersonation vishing call before the impersonated identity is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the impersonated identity has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11212 through ITID-11219
A cold-call tech support scam, which is tracked under a separate Tier-3/4 branch (Tech Support Scams, e.g. ITID-11521 through ITID-11528) rather than this Vishing Type
A call primarily focused on soliciting a payment rather than establishing a false identity as its defining feature (Financial Fraud Call, ITID-1122x)
ITID-11211.severity: Medium by default; reassess once impersonated identity and any resulting action are known.
ITID-11211.escalation: Escalate if the recipient disclosed sensitive information or took any requested action before the call was identified as fraudulent.
indicators: Employee reporting an unsolicited call claiming to be from a specific organization or person that could not be verified
Caller ID inconsistent with the claimed identity's known number
vectors: Unsolicited phone call using a false claimed identity to build trust before making a request
rootCauses: No standard callback-verification habit for unsolicited calls claiming a trusted identity
controls: Callback verification using an independently sourced phone number
User awareness training on vishing/impersonation calls
ITID-11211.detection: Relies entirely on employee reporting; phone calls carry no automated technical telemetry comparable to email.
ITID-11211.response: Triage promptly to determine the impersonated identity and reclassify; confirm whether the employee disclosed anything or took action.
metrics: Count of unclassified impersonation vishing reports pending reclassification
ITID-11211.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify once the impersonated identity is confirmed. Cold-call tech-support-themed vishing is deliberately out of scope for this Type and lives under the separate Tech Support Scams branch.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Impersonation Vishing Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated a person or entity to manipulate the target, not fitting a more specific vishing sub-category.

steps.title: Capture call details while fresh
steps.desc: Interview the target immediately and record the caller ID displayed, call time, duration, who/what was impersonated, and what was requested.
steps.outcome: Call details documented while memory is fresh.

steps.title: Contain any disclosed credentials or data
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were disclosed.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm any containment actions are complete.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the call pattern
steps.desc: Record the impersonation type and pattern for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether any information or access was disclosed
steps.desc: Establish whether the target shared credentials, personal/financial data, or performed any requested action during the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed, skip account containment and proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: Block the number and report to telephony provider
steps.desc: Block the caller number on the target's device/phone system and report it to the telephony provider's fraud/abuse channel.
steps.outcome: Number blocked and reported.

steps.title: Check call metadata for spoofing indicators
steps.desc: Review the displayed caller ID against known legitimate numbers for the impersonated entity, and check the telephony/PBX platform for call routing details if it came through corporate lines.
steps.outcome: Caller ID legitimacy assessed.

ITID-11212.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to represent the recipient's bank or another financial institution, typically citing suspicious account activity, in order to extract account credentials, card details, or authorization for a transaction.
ITID-11212.purpose: Captures vishing where the caller impersonates a bank or other financial institution, a common pretext used to obtain account credentials or authorize a fraudulent transaction.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to be from a bank's fraud department requesting account verification detail
Caller directing the victim to move funds to a 'safe account' under the guise of protecting them from fraud
scopeExcludes: The same pretext used specifically to coerce an immediate same-call payment, which is more precisely classified under Financial Fraud Call (ITID-11223) if payment coercion, rather than identity impersonation, is the dominant reportable feature
ITID-11212.severity: High — this pretext directly targets financial account access.
ITID-11212.priority: P1 if any account/card detail was disclosed, otherwise P2.
ITID-11212.escalation: Escalate immediately to the employee's actual bank/card issuer and to IAM if any corporate financial account credential was disclosed.
indicators: Caller referencing generic 'suspicious activity' without institution-specific verifiable detail
Caller creating urgency to bypass normal verification callback procedures
vectors: Caller ID spoofing to display the bank's real published number
Caller directing the victim to call a number provided during the call rather than the number on the back of their card
rootCauses: No organizational guidance for employees on verifying financial-institution calls via an independently sourced number
controls: User awareness training on bank-impersonation vishing
Callback verification using the number printed on the card/statement, never a number given during the call
ITID-11212.response: Advise the individual to contact their real bank directly using an independently sourced number and monitor the account for unauthorized activity.
metrics: Count of bank-impersonation vishing reports per quarter
ITID-11212.notes: Where the primary reportable event is a specific payment being coerced during the call rather than the identity claim itself, also consider logging under the relevant Financial Fraud Call leaf for the payment-coercion mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Bank / Financial Institution Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated a bank or financial institution, typically claiming suspicious activity on the target's account to extract credentials, card details, or OTP codes.

steps.title: Capture call details and the specific request made
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, impersonated institution, and exactly what was requested (card number, PIN, OTP, online banking login).
steps.outcome: Call details and request documented.

steps.title: Contact the real institution's fraud line immediately
steps.desc: Have the target (or finance/treasury, for a corporate account) call the institution directly using the number on the back of the card or official website, not any number provided by the caller, to freeze the account/card and flag the disclosure.
steps.guidance: Time-sensitive: act within minutes if possible, as fraudulent transfers following this pattern often happen quickly.
steps.outcome: Institution notified; account/card frozen or flagged.

steps.title: Verify no unauthorized transactions occurred
steps.desc: Review recent account activity/statements with the institution for unauthorized transactions.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized transactions, or fraud identified and disputed.

steps.title: Confirm account restored with monitoring
steps.desc: Confirm the account/card is usable again and, where applicable, under fraud monitoring by the institution.
steps.outcome: Account restored with monitoring active.

steps.title: Log the impersonation pattern
steps.desc: Record the impersonated institution and tactic for trend tracking and awareness content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether any financial or credential information was disclosed
steps.desc: Establish precisely what was disclosed and whether the target performed any action the caller requested (transfer, code read-out).
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed, proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: Reset online banking credentials if disclosed
steps.desc: Reset online/mobile banking credentials and revoke sessions if login details were disclosed.
steps.outcome: Online banking access secured.

steps.title: Determine whether this is a personal or corporate financial account
steps.desc: Establish account type to route containment appropriately.
steps.outcome: Account type established.

steps.title: Block the number and report it
steps.desc: Block the caller number and report it to the telephony provider's fraud channel and, where available, the real institution's fraud team (who often track spoofed-caller-ID campaigns against their brand).
steps.outcome: Number blocked and reported.

ITID-11213.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to represent a law enforcement agency, tax authority, or other government body, typically threatening legal consequence, arrest, or fines to compel the recipient to disclose information or make a payment.
ITID-11213.purpose: Captures vishing where the caller impersonates law enforcement or a government agency, a pretext that relies on fear of legal consequence to compel compliance.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to be from a police department, tax authority, or immigration/regulatory agency
Threats of arrest, warrant, or legal action used as the primary compliance lever
scopeExcludes: The same threat-of-consequence mechanism used primarily to coerce an immediate payment, which is more precisely classified under Threat-of-Consequence Payment Coercion Call (ITID-11228) if payment coercion is the dominant reportable feature
ITID-11213.severity: Medium-High given the psychological pressure this pretext exerts.
ITID-11213.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any sensitive personal or organizational information was disclosed.
ITID-11213.escalation: Escalate if the recipient disclosed personal identifying information or made any payment under duress.
indicators: Caller demanding immediate action to avoid arrest or legal consequence, refusing to allow time to verify
Caller requesting payment via untraceable methods (gift cards, wire transfer, cryptocurrency)
vectors: Caller ID spoofing to display a real government agency's published number
rootCauses: No organizational guidance reminding employees that legitimate government agencies do not demand immediate untraceable payment by phone
controls: User awareness training on government-impersonation vishing
Callback verification using an independently sourced agency number
ITID-11213.response: Advise the individual not to comply, verify independently with the claimed agency, and report the call to appropriate fraud-reporting channels.
metrics: Count of law-enforcement/government-impersonation vishing reports per quarter
ITID-11213.notes: Where payment coercion via threat is the dominant reportable feature rather than the identity claim itself, also consider cross-referencing ITID-11228.

playbook.name: Response: Law Enforcement / Government Agency Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated law enforcement or a government agency (tax authority, immigration, court), typically using threat of arrest or legal action to coerce payment or information disclosure.

steps.title: Capture call details and the specific threat/demand made
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, impersonated agency, badge/case numbers claimed, and the exact threat and demand (arrest warrant, deportation, fine, payment method demanded).
steps.guidance: A demand for payment via gift cards, wire transfer, or cryptocurrency is a strong indicator of fraud — genuine agencies do not collect fines this way.
steps.outcome: Call details and demand documented.

steps.title: If payment was made, advise on financial recovery steps
steps.desc: For wire transfers, advise contacting the bank immediately to attempt a recall; for gift cards, contact the issuer promptly; for cryptocurrency, contact the exchange used, though recovery is often not possible.
steps.outcome: Recovery attempt initiated where possible.

steps.title: Confirm the target understands no genuine action is pending and reassure them
steps.desc: Confirm with the target that no genuine legal action is pending; these calls are designed to induce panic, so explicit reassurance matters.
steps.outcome: Target reassured and understands the call was fraudulent.

steps.title: Log the impersonation pattern and reinforce awareness
steps.desc: Record the impersonated agency and tactic; reinforce in awareness content that government agencies do not demand immediate payment via gift cards or crypto over the phone.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Determine whether payment was made or information disclosed
steps.desc: Establish whether the target made any payment, provided personal/financial information, or complied with any instruction.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compliance status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed or paid, proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: If personal information was disclosed, advise identity-theft precautions
steps.desc: Advise the target to monitor credit reports and consider a fraud alert if sensitive personal information (SSN/national ID, date of birth) was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Target taking identity-protection steps.

steps.title: Verify independently whether any genuine matter exists
steps.desc: Advise the target to independently contact the real agency using an officially published number (never one provided by the caller) to confirm no genuine matter exists.
steps.outcome: Genuine matter ruled out via independent verification.

steps.title: Report the call to the real agency and relevant fraud reporting body
steps.desc: Report the impersonation to the real agency's fraud/impersonation reporting channel and to the national consumer fraud reporting body.
steps.outcome: Impersonation reported to appropriate authorities.

ITID-11214.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to represent a known vendor or supplier, using the existing business relationship to request updated payment details, sensitive account information, or system access.
ITID-11214.purpose: Captures vishing where the caller impersonates a known vendor or supplier representative, exploiting an existing business relationship to extract information or redirect payment.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to represent a real, known vendor requesting bank detail changes or account verification by phone
Caller impersonating vendor IT/support staff requesting remote access
scopeExcludes: The equivalent attack conducted via email rather than a phone call (BEC via Compromised Vendor/Third-Party Email Account, ITID-22414, or Impersonation via Compromised Real Vendor Account/Domain, ITID-22511)
Cold-call tech support scams with no genuine prior vendor relationship being impersonated (Tech Support Scams branch)
ITID-11214.severity: Medium-High — vendor relationships often carry established payment/access trust that can be abused directly.
ITID-11214.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment detail change or system access was granted.
ITID-11214.escalation: Escalate to finance/procurement immediately if any payment/banking detail change was requested, and to IT if system access was requested.
indicators: Caller requesting a change to bank account details for an existing vendor relationship by phone alone
Caller referencing accurate but not highly sensitive detail about an existing vendor contract
vectors: Caller impersonating a known vendor's accounts-receivable contact to request a banking-detail change
rootCauses: No dual-channel/dual-approval verification requirement for vendor payment-detail changes
controls: Dual-channel verification (callback to a known, independently sourced number) for any vendor payment-detail change
Vendor contact-detail registry maintained independently of inbound caller claims
ITID-11214.detection: Relies entirely on employee reporting and finance-process controls catching the change request.
ITID-11214.response: Verify any requested change through the vendor's known, independently sourced contact channel before acting, and reverse any change made under the pretext.
metrics: Count of vendor-impersonation vishing reports per quarter
Number resulting in an attempted or completed payment-detail change
ITID-11214.notes: Scope decision: this leaf covers the voice-channel version of vendor impersonation; the email-channel equivalent is logged under ITID-22414/ITID-22511 to keep channel-based reporting distinct even though the business impact is similar.

playbook.name: Response: Vendor / Supplier Representative Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated a known vendor or supplier representative, typically attempting to redirect payments, change banking details on file, or extract account access.

steps.title: Capture call details and the specific request made
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, impersonated vendor/representative name, and exactly what was requested (updated bank details, invoice payment, portal login).
steps.outcome: Call details and request documented.

steps.title: If payment details were changed, immediately revert and halt any pending payment
steps.desc: Notify accounts payable/finance immediately to revert any changed banking details and place a hold on any pending payment to the vendor until independently verified.
steps.outcome: Payment details reverted; pending payment held.

steps.title: Confirm vendor account records are accurate
steps.desc: Confirm with the real vendor that all payment and contact details on file are correct and unaltered.
steps.outcome: Vendor records confirmed accurate.

steps.title: Confirm normal vendor payment processing resumed
steps.desc: Confirm payments to the vendor are processing normally against verified correct details.
steps.outcome: Normal processing confirmed.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce vendor-change verification procedures
steps.desc: Record the incident; reinforce with accounts payable that any vendor banking-detail change must be verified via a known contact channel, never accepted based solely on an inbound call.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; procedure reinforced.

steps.title: Determine whether any action was taken or information disclosed
steps.desc: Establish whether the target updated vendor payment details, made a payment, or disclosed credentials/account information.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action/disclosure status.
steps.abort: If nothing was actioned or disclosed, proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: If a payment was already made to the fraudulent details, engage the bank immediately
steps.desc: Contact the bank to attempt a recall of the transfer as quickly as possible.
steps.outcome: Recall attempt initiated.

steps.title: Verify independently with the real vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor directly using a known, previously verified contact number (not one provided by the caller) to confirm whether the representative and request are genuine.
steps.guidance: This mirrors classic vendor-payment-redirection fraud; independent verification is the critical control.
steps.outcome: Genuine vendor request confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Contain any disclosed vendor portal credentials
steps.desc: Reset credentials and revoke sessions on any vendor portal account whose login was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Vendor portal access secured.

ITID-11215.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to be a specific, known internal colleague — often a superior or someone in another department — to induce the recipient to disclose information or take an action they would not for an unknown caller.
ITID-11215.purpose: Captures vishing where the caller impersonates a known internal colleague, exploiting internal familiarity and trust rather than an external institutional identity.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to be a specific named colleague, using a spoofed or unfamiliar number
Caller referencing accurate internal detail (org structure, project names) to support the impersonation
scopeExcludes: The caller specifically claiming to be from the internal security or fraud team referencing a prior breach (ITID-11219)
The caller spoofing a specific internal extension number as the primary technique rather than simply claiming a colleague's identity (Spoofed Internal Extension Financial Fraud Call, ITID-11227)
ITID-11215.severity: Medium-High depending on the seniority of the impersonated colleague and the nature of the request.
ITID-11215.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the impersonated identity is a senior leader or the request involves sensitive access/data.
ITID-11215.escalation: Escalate if the recipient took any action based on the call before independently verifying the colleague's identity.
indicators: Caller's voice or communication style inconsistent with the claimed colleague's known manner
Request for an action outside the claimed colleague's normal scope or process
vectors: Caller referencing internal detail plausibly gathered from social media, a prior breach, or public sources
rootCauses: No standard practice of verifying unusual internal requests through a secondary channel (chat, in-person)
controls: Secondary-channel verification practice for unusual internal requests
User awareness training on colleague-impersonation vishing
ITID-11215.response: Advise verification of any unusual request through a known secondary channel before acting, regardless of the caller's apparent identity.
metrics: Count of colleague-impersonation vishing reports per quarter
ITID-11215.notes: If the technique's defining feature is spoofing a specific internal extension number rather than simply claiming a colleague's name, log under ITID-11227 instead.

playbook.name: Response: Colleague Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated a real colleague (voice similarity, spoofed internal caller ID, or claimed identity) to extract information or request an action from the target.

steps.title: Capture call details and the specific request made
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, which colleague was impersonated, and what was requested.
steps.outcome: Call details and request documented.

steps.title: Contain any disclosed credentials or data
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were disclosed; assess data-loss scope if confidential information was shared.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm any containment actions are complete.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce out-of-band verification for unusual requests
steps.desc: Record the incident; reinforce that unusual requests, even appearing to come from a known colleague's number, should be verified via a separate channel (e.g. messaging them directly) before acting.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Confirm with the real colleague that they did not make the call
steps.desc: Contact the real colleague directly through a known channel to confirm they did not place the call.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed by the real colleague.
steps.abort: If the colleague confirms they did make the call, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Block the number and check for internal caller-ID spoofing
steps.desc: Block the number and, if it displayed as an internal extension, check the corporate telephony/PBX platform for how the spoofing occurred.
steps.outcome: Number blocked; spoofing mechanism understood if internal.

steps.title: Determine whether any information or access was disclosed
steps.desc: Establish whether the target shared credentials, data, or performed any requested action.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed, proceed to reporting only.

ITID-11216.def: A phone call in which the caller uses AI-generated synthetic audio that closely mimics the voice of a specific real, known individual (an executive, colleague, or family member), in order to impersonate them convincingly enough to defeat voice recognition as a trust signal.
ITID-11216.purpose: Captures vishing that uses AI-generated synthetic voice audio cloned from a real person's voice, isolating this real-time voice-channel deepfake technique from static synthetic-profile and video-based deepfake attacks elsewhere in the taxonomy.
scopeIncludes: A call using AI voice-cloning technology to mimic a known individual's voice in real time or via a pre-recorded synthetic clip
Cases where the target explicitly recognized the cloned voice as unusually convincing but ultimately artificial
scopeExcludes: A static AI-generated synthetic profile photo/bio used on social media with no voice component (ITID-11719, Fake Profiles branch)
A video-call deepfake combined with a physical follow-up meeting (ITID-11926, Cyber-Physical Social Engineering branch)
AI-generated deepfake content used in a public disinformation/misinformation campaign rather than a direct, individually targeted call (ITID-21226, ITID-23514)
ITID-11216.severity: High — voice cloning defeats one of the most commonly relied-upon informal identity-verification signals (recognizing a familiar voice).
ITID-11216.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC and, where an executive's voice was cloned, to executive protection/leadership.
indicators: Recipient reporting the voice sounded correct but the conversation content or context felt subtly wrong
Audio artifacts (unnatural pacing, flat affect, background inconsistency) noted on review of a recorded call
vectors: Publicly available audio/video of the impersonated individual (interviews, public speeches, social media) used to train a voice-cloning model
rootCauses: Reliance on voice recognition alone as an identity-verification method for sensitive requests
Extensive public audio/video availability of executives enabling high-quality voice cloning
controls: Out-of-band verification (a pre-agreed code phrase or secondary channel) for any sensitive request received by voice, regardless of apparent voice match
Executive digital-footprint/OSINT monitoring service
ITID-11216.detection: Very limited technically — no standard corporate telemetry detects a cloned voice in real time; relies on the recipient's own suspicion and post-call forensic audio analysis where a recording exists.
ITID-11216.response: Do not act on any sensitive request based on voice recognition alone; verify out-of-band before proceeding, and preserve any call recording for forensic analysis.
metrics: Count of confirmed or suspected AI voice-clone vishing incidents per quarter
ITID-11216.notes: Scope decision: deliberately narrowed to the real-time voice-call channel to avoid duplicating ITID-11719 (static synthetic profile) and ITID-11926 (video-call deepfake with physical follow-up), which sit in different Tier-3/4 branches with different response patterns.

playbook.name: Response: AI Voice Clone / Deepfake Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call using an AI-generated voice clone (deepfake audio) of a real, known individual — typically an executive or family member — to convincingly impersonate them and manipulate the target.

steps.title: Capture call details and what made the target suspicious despite the convincing voice
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, who was impersonated, what was requested, and any subtle audio artifacts or contextual inconsistencies that raised suspicion (odd pauses, generic background noise, urgency mismatched to the person's normal manner).
steps.guidance: Voice cloning is increasingly convincing, so document behavioral/contextual red flags rather than relying only on 'it sounded fake.'
steps.outcome: Call details and suspicion indicators documented.

steps.title: If funds were transferred, engage the bank immediately
steps.desc: Contact the bank without delay to attempt a recall of any wire transfer or payment made as a result of the call.
steps.guidance: AI voice-clone attacks are increasingly used for exactly this kind of urgent-transfer fraud; speed matters.
steps.outcome: Recall attempt initiated.

steps.title: Assess how the attacker obtained a voice sample for cloning
steps.desc: Consider likely sources of the impersonated person's voice sample (public video/social media, prior calls, voicemail greeting) to understand exposure.
steps.outcome: Likely voice-sample source identified where possible.

steps.title: Confirm resolution and reassure both the target and impersonated individual
steps.desc: Confirm any containment actions are complete and communicate the outcome to both the target and the impersonated individual.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed and communicated.

steps.title: Establish or reinforce a verification codeword/protocol for high-stakes voice requests
steps.desc: Recommend establishing a pre-agreed verification method (codeword, callback to a known number) for high-stakes requests from executives/family, given that voice alone is no longer reliable proof of identity; log the incident.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; verification protocol recommendation raised.

steps.title: Confirm with the real individual through an independent channel
steps.desc: Contact the real person directly via a known, separate channel (in person, a known number, video call) to confirm they did not make the call.
steps.guidance: Voice alone should never be treated as sufficient identity verification for high-stakes requests going forward.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed by the real individual.

steps.title: Contain any disclosed credentials or data
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were disclosed.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.

steps.title: Determine whether any information, access, or funds were disclosed/transferred
steps.desc: Establish exactly what the target did during or after the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure/transfer status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed or transferred, proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: Block the number and preserve any recording as evidence
steps.desc: Block the caller number; if a recording exists (voicemail or call recording), preserve it for forensic/legal purposes.
steps.outcome: Number blocked; recording preserved if available.

ITID-11217.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to be a family member of the recipient, typically claiming to be in an emergency (arrested, injured, in trouble) requiring an urgent, often untraceable payment.
ITID-11217.purpose: Captures vishing that impersonates a family member in a personal emergency, a pretext primarily relevant to an individual's personal life but tracked here when it involves an employee or executive and carries organizational risk implications.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to be a family member of an employee or executive, reported through the organization's security channel
Cases involving an executive where the personal-life targeting carries a plausible organizational risk dimension (e.g., timed to coincide with a business trip)
scopeExcludes: The equivalent AI voice-clone technique applied to this pretext, which should instead be logged under ITID-11216 given the more specific and materially different technical mechanism
Purely personal incidents with no organizational touchpoint or reporting through the security channel, which fall outside this taxonomy's scope entirely
ITID-11217.severity: Low from a direct organizational-security standpoint, but tracked given potential impact on employee wellbeing and, for executives, possible correlation with broader targeting.
ITID-11217.escalation: Escalate to executive protection if the target is a senior leader, particularly if timed around known travel.
indicators: Caller creating extreme urgency and emotional pressure, discouraging the recipient from calling the family member directly to verify
Request for payment via untraceable methods
vectors: Caller using publicly available family detail (names, relationships) gathered from social media
rootCauses: Family relationship detail being broadly discoverable through public social media presence
controls: Employee/executive awareness guidance on family-emergency vishing scams
Executive digital-footprint/OSINT monitoring service
ITID-11217.detection: Relies entirely on self-reporting through the security channel.
ITID-11217.response: Advise the individual to independently verify with the family member directly before taking any action or making any payment.
metrics: Count of family-emergency vishing reports per quarter
ITID-11217.notes: This leaf is scoped narrowly to cases reported through the organization's security channel with some organizational relevance; if AI voice cloning is used for this same pretext, reclassify to ITID-11216 instead.

playbook.name: Response: Family Member / Emergency Impersonation Call
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated a family member in a fabricated emergency (accident, arrest, medical crisis) to pressure the target into urgent payment, exploiting an employee's personal life.

steps.title: Support the target and capture call details
steps.desc: Approach the report with empathy, since the target may be distressed; record the caller ID, the claimed emergency, who was impersonated, and the payment demanded.
steps.guidance: This is primarily a personal-welfare matter that may have a minor corporate-resource touchpoint (e.g. if the call was received on a work device or the employee needs time/support).
steps.outcome: Target supported; call details documented.

steps.title: Advise on financial recovery steps if payment was made
steps.desc: For wire transfers, advise contacting the bank immediately; for gift cards, contact the issuer promptly, though recovery is often limited.
steps.outcome: Recovery attempt initiated where possible.

steps.title: Reassure the target and offer support resources
steps.desc: Confirm the target understands no genuine emergency occurred and point them to employee assistance resources given the emotional distress this scam is designed to cause.
steps.outcome: Target reassured and supported.

steps.title: Log the incident with appropriate confidentiality
steps.desc: Record corporate-relevant facts with discretion; consider including this scam pattern in general awareness content given how effective the urgency/panic tactic is.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm with the real family member independently
steps.desc: Advise the target to independently contact the real family member or another relative directly to confirm no genuine emergency exists.
steps.guidance: Advise the target not to call back any number the caller provided, and not to make any payment until independently verified.
steps.outcome: Genuine emergency ruled out via independent verification.

steps.title: Report the call to relevant fraud authorities
steps.desc: Advise the target to report the scam call to the national consumer fraud reporting body.
steps.outcome: Call reported.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made
steps.desc: Establish whether the target sent money (often via gift cards or wire transfer) before verification occurred.
steps.outcome: Confirmed payment status.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed to reporting/support only.

ITID-11218.def: A phone call in which the caller, posing as a trusted party (bank, IT support, etc.), induces the victim to read aloud a one-time passcode they just received, or to approve a live MFA push notification, so the attacker can complete an authentication in real time.
ITID-11218.purpose: Captures vishing that relays a real-time OTP or MFA push approval over a live phone call, isolating the voice-channel relay technique from web-based MFA token phishing and SMS-based OTP fatigue attacks elsewhere in the taxonomy.
scopeIncludes: Caller requesting the victim read out an OTP they just received via SMS/authenticator app during the call
Caller requesting the victim approve a push-notification MFA prompt while on the phone with the attacker
scopeExcludes: Web-based phishing for MFA tokens via a fake login page with no live voice-call relay (ITID-12610 through ITID-12619, Phishing for MFA Tokens branch)
Repeated automated SMS-based OTP fatigue attempts with no live voice-call component (ITID-11331 through ITID-11339, SMS OTP/MFA Fatigue Smishing)
MFA push-bombing via repeated automated prompts with no accompanying phone call (ITID-12621, ITID-12628, MFA Fatigue/Push Bombing branch)
ITID-11218.severity: High — this technique directly defeats real-time MFA, typically as the final step of an account-takeover attempt already in progress.
ITID-11218.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC; treat the associated account as compromised and revoke sessions regardless of whether the takeover is confirmed successful.
indicators: Employee reporting they were asked to read an OTP or approve an MFA prompt during an unsolicited call
Sign-in log showing a successful authentication immediately coincident with a reported vishing call to that user
vectors: Caller impersonating IT support or a bank fraud department, timed to coincide with an attacker-triggered authentication attempt
rootCauses: Standard OTP/push MFA reliant on user action rather than phishing-resistant methods
No organizational policy explicitly forbidding sharing OTPs or approving unexplained MFA prompts over the phone
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) not susceptible to voice relay
User awareness training explicitly prohibiting sharing OTPs or approving unexplained MFA prompts by phone
Number-matching MFA prompts to reduce blind approval
ITID-11218.detection: Identity provider sign-in logs give a strong technical signal correlating the call report with the authentication event.
ITID-11218.response: Revoke sessions and force credential reset for the targeted account immediately, and investigate for any resulting unauthorized access.
metrics: Count of confirmed OTP/MFA relay vishing incidents per quarter
Percentage of accounts on phishing-resistant MFA
detections: Identity provider sign-in correlation with reported vishing calls
ITID-11218.notes: Scope decision: this leaf is specifically the live voice-call relay mechanism; the web-based (ITID-12610 family) and SMS-based (ITID-11331 family) equivalents are tracked separately by channel to keep response-owner routing (SOC vs. telecom/SMS security) clean.

playbook.name: Response: Real-Time MFA/OTP Relay Vishing
playbook.description: For an active phone call in which an attacker, already holding valid credentials, is calling the target in real time to talk them through relaying a live MFA/OTP code — a fast-moving, live account-takeover-in-progress requiring urgent mid-call action.

steps.title: Treat as an active, live incident — do not wait for the call to end
steps.desc: If the SOC is contacted while the call is still in progress or has just ended, immediately confirm whether an OTP/MFA code was relayed to the caller.
steps.guidance: Speed is the entire point of this playbook — every minute matters while the attacker may still be attempting to use the code.
steps.outcome: Disclosure status confirmed within minutes.

steps.title: Lock the account immediately regardless of confirmed login status
steps.desc: Force an emergency password reset and revoke all sessions/tokens the moment a relayed code is confirmed — do not wait for full log confirmation, since the attacker may be authenticating as this step is being performed.
steps.guidance: This is the single highest-priority action in this playbook; execute it before completing full investigation.
steps.outcome: Account locked out before or immediately after attacker use.

steps.title: Remove any attacker-established persistence
steps.desc: Revoke any OAuth app grants, mailbox forwarding rules, or new MFA device enrollments created during the attacker's session if a successful login occurred.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed free of attacker persistence.

steps.title: Restore access with new credentials and re-enrolled MFA under heightened monitoring
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA on a verified device; place the account under short-term elevated SIEM monitoring.
steps.outcome: User has restored, confirmed-clean access under active monitoring.

steps.title: Document the full live-incident timeline and response speed
steps.desc: Record the exact timeline from initial report to containment to evaluate and improve response speed for future real-time relay attacks; this pattern warrants urgent, org-wide awareness given its speed and effectiveness.
steps.outcome: Timeline documented; urgent awareness reminder issued if part of a wider campaign.

steps.title: Check for a real-time or near-real-time authentication attempt
steps.desc: Immediately pull identity provider sign-in logs for the account in question to check for a login attempt matching the call window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attacker has authenticated.

steps.title: If a successful login is confirmed, immediately escalate to active intrusion response
steps.desc: Trigger the account-takeover/intrusion response process: check for mailbox rules, OAuth grants, active sessions on other services, and any data access or lateral movement performed during the session.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker access during the live session established and contained.

steps.title: Advise the target to end the call and not provide further information
steps.desc: If the call is still ongoing, instruct the target to hang up immediately and not answer follow-up calls from the same or related numbers.
steps.outcome: Call terminated; no further information disclosed.

steps.title: Block the caller number and report it
steps.desc: Block the number and report it to the telephony provider's fraud channel.
steps.outcome: Number blocked and reported.

ITID-11219.def: A phone call in which the caller falsely claims to be from the organization's own internal security, IT, or fraud team, asserting that the recipient's account or device has already been compromised in a prior incident, in order to induce urgent compliance with a request (password reset, remote access, information disclosure).
ITID-11219.purpose: Captures vishing where the caller impersonates the organization's own internal security or fraud team, using a fabricated prior-breach pretext to induce compliance — a distinctly higher-trust impersonation than a generic colleague or external institution.
scopeIncludes: Caller claiming to be internal security/IT following up on a supposed prior breach affecting the recipient
Caller requesting remote access, a password reset, or MFA approval under this pretext
scopeExcludes: A generic colleague impersonation with no security/fraud-team framing or breach pretext (ITID-11215)
A genuine internal security team member conducting legitimate incident response outreach — always verify identity before classifying a report here
ITID-11219.severity: High — this pretext specifically exploits the recipient's trust in the security function itself, which is uniquely damaging if successful.
ITID-11219.escalation: Escalate immediately to the real SOC/IAM team to both counter the pretext and check whether the claimed 'prior breach' has any factual basis.
indicators: Caller unable to be verified against the real security team's known staff or contact procedures
Caller creating urgency around a supposed active incident with no corroborating internal ticket or record
vectors: Caller ID spoofing to display an internal IT/security help-desk number
rootCauses: No standard, well-known process for employees to verify a claimed internal security contact (e.g., a published callback number or ticket-lookup step)
controls: Published, well-known callback verification procedure for any claimed internal security/IT contact
User awareness training explicitly covering this specific pretext
ITID-11219.detection: Relies entirely on employee reporting and cross-checking against real internal ticketing/incident records.
ITID-11219.response: Confirm with the real security team whether any legitimate outreach occurred, and treat any information already disclosed as potentially compromised.
metrics: Count of internal-security-impersonation vishing reports per quarter
ITID-11219.notes: Always cross-check against the real security team's ticketing system before dismissing a report as impersonation, in case it reveals a genuine breach the pretext is (coincidentally or not) referencing.

playbook.name: Response: Security/Fraud-Team Impersonation Call (Post-Breach Pretext)
playbook.description: For a reported phone call in which the caller impersonated the organization's own security or fraud team, using a post-breach pretext ('we detected suspicious activity on your account, we need to verify you') to extract credentials or MFA codes.

steps.title: Confirm with the real security/fraud team that no such call was made
steps.desc: Immediately check with the organization's actual security/fraud/IT team to confirm they did not place this call.
steps.guidance: This is a high-priority check since this pretext specifically exploits trust in the real security function.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the call was not from the legitimate team.
steps.abort: If the real team confirms it was a genuine call, redirect to the appropriate legitimate process.

steps.title: Immediately lock the account if credentials or an MFA code were disclosed
steps.desc: Force emergency password reset and full session/token revocation without delay.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Remove any attacker access or persistence
steps.desc: If remote access was granted or credentials used, conduct forensic review of the device/account for attacker actions and remove any installed remote-access tools, malware, or unauthorized changes.
steps.outcome: Device and account confirmed free of attacker access.
steps.abort: Escalate to full intrusion-response process if broader compromise is found.

steps.title: Restore access and device to service under monitoring
steps.desc: Restore account/device access with new credentials once confirmed clean, under short-term heightened monitoring.
steps.outcome: Access restored under active monitoring.

steps.title: Document the pretext and reinforce that the real security team never asks for credentials by phone
steps.desc: Record the full incident; urgently reinforce in awareness training that legitimate internal security/IT staff will never ask an employee to read out a password or MFA code, or to install remote-access software, over an inbound call.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; urgent awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Capture call details and exactly what was requested
steps.desc: Interview the target and record the caller ID, claimed pretext (which 'breach' or 'suspicious activity' was cited), and what was requested (password, MFA code, remote access).
steps.outcome: Call details and request documented.

steps.title: If remote access was granted, isolate the device immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect the device from the network and isolate it via EDR; treat as an active intrusion, not a routine phishing report.
steps.outcome: Device isolated pending forensic review.

steps.title: Determine whether credentials, MFA codes, or remote access were disclosed/granted
steps.desc: Establish precisely what the target disclosed or granted, including whether any remote-access tool was installed at the caller's direction.
steps.guidance: This pretext is sometimes paired with a request to install remote-access software — treat this as equivalent to a live intrusion if it occurred.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disclosure/access-grant status.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed or granted, proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: Block the caller number and alert other employees if part of a campaign
steps.desc: Block and report the number; if other employees received similar calls, send an urgent org-wide notice clarifying that the real security team will never ask for a password or MFA code over the phone.
steps.outcome: Number blocked; employees warned if campaign confirmed.

ITID-11221.def: An unsolicited phone call whose primary apparent goal is to induce the recipient to make a payment, disclose financial account detail, or authorize a financial transaction, whose specific mechanism (live-transfer, robocall funnel, threat-based coercion, etc.) has not yet been confirmed.
ITID-11221.purpose: Catch-all for a reported vishing call whose primary goal was extracting a financial payment or financial account access, where the specific mechanism has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage of a reported financial-fraud-themed vishing call before the mechanism is examined
scopeExcludes: Any case where the mechanism has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-11222 through ITID-11229
A call whose primary defining feature is establishing a false identity with no financial-payment goal yet apparent (Impersonation Attack, ITID-1121x)
ITID-11221.severity: Medium-High by default given the direct financial-loss potential; reassess once mechanism and outcome are known.
ITID-11221.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams if any payment was made or financial detail disclosed.
indicators: Employee reporting an unsolicited call requesting payment, banking detail, or a financial transaction authorization
vectors: Unsolicited phone call directly requesting a financial action
rootCauses: No standard verification process for unsolicited financial requests received by phone
controls: Dual-approval process for any payment or financial-detail change initiated by phone
User awareness training on financial fraud vishing
ITID-11221.response: Triage promptly to determine the mechanism and reclassify; confirm whether any payment was made or financial detail disclosed.
metrics: Count of unclassified financial fraud vishing reports pending reclassification
ITID-11221.notes: Intake/catch-all classification; reclassify once the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Financial Fraud Call
playbook.description: For a reported voice-based social-engineering call attempting to induce a fraudulent payment or disclosure of financial information, where the specific attack sub-pattern has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and capture full call details
steps.desc: Record the caller ID displayed, claimed identity, requested action, and a full account of what was said, as soon as possible after the call while details are fresh.
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form to avoid missing key details (time, number, claimed org/person, urgency tactics used).
steps.outcome: Structured call record captured.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold, referencing the transaction details.
steps.guidance: Time is critical for wire recalls; contact finance/treasury and the bank's fraud line in parallel.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update outbound-payment verification procedures if a control gap is identified
steps.desc: If the incident revealed a gap in callback/verification procedure for payment changes, update the finance team's standard verification checklist accordingly.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the call pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record the pretext used, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a wire/ACH transfer, purchased gift cards or crypto, or disclosed account/card details during or after the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the caller's claimed identity was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization or individual the caller claimed to represent, using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such call was authorized by them.
steps.guidance: Never use a callback number provided by the suspect caller.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity confirmed as fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11222.def: A financial fraud phone call in which the victim is transferred, mid-call, between multiple colluding fraudulent personas (e.g., a 'bank representative' who transfers to a 'fraud investigator' who transfers to 'law enforcement'), each reinforcing the pretext and increasing pressure to comply.
ITID-11222.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing conducted through a live, multi-party call transfer — passing the victim between colluding fraudulent personas — a mechanism distinct from a single caller's same-call coercion.
scopeIncludes: A single call session in which the victim is transferred between two or more distinct fraudulent personas
Multi-party relay used to simulate legitimacy through apparent institutional hand-off
scopeExcludes: A single caller maintaining one persona throughout the call (ITID-11223, ITID-11228)
ITID-11222.severity: High — the layered personas materially increase psychological pressure and perceived legitimacy.
ITID-11222.priority: P1 if any payment was made or in progress, otherwise P2.
ITID-11222.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams and, if a payment is in progress, attempt to halt it through the bank's own fraud channel.
indicators: Victim reporting being transferred multiple times within a single call session, each transfer reinforcing urgency
Call recording or victim account showing distinct personas with a consistent overall narrative
vectors: Coordinated multi-person call center operation running the layered-persona script
rootCauses: No organizational guidance on hanging up and independently re-initiating contact rather than trusting an in-call transfer
controls: Guidance to always hang up and independently re-initiate contact rather than trusting an in-call transfer
Dual-approval process for financial transactions initiated following a phone call
ITID-11222.response: Attempt to halt any in-progress payment through the legitimate bank's fraud channel, and advise the victim to independently verify with the real institution.
metrics: Count of multi-party call transfer fraud reports per quarter
ITID-11222.notes: This leaf is defined by the multi-persona transfer mechanism specifically; the impersonated identities involved (bank, law enforcement, etc.) can additionally be cross-referenced to the relevant Impersonation Attack leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Live Call Transfer Fraud (Multi-Party Relay)
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call where the victim was passed between multiple conspirators (e.g. an initial caller transfers to a fake 'supervisor', 'bank fraud department', or 'law enforcement officer') to build false legitimacy before requesting payment.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and reconstruct the full call chain
steps.desc: Record each leg of the call: who called first, who they were transferred to, the claimed role of each party, and what each party said or requested.
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form; ask specifically about any hold music, transfer announcements, or background office noise used to simulate a real call center.
steps.outcome: Full multi-party call chain documented.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.guidance: Time is critical for wire recalls; contact finance/treasury and the bank's fraud line in parallel.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update outbound-payment verification procedures if a control gap is identified
steps.desc: If the multi-party relay technique exploited a gap in payment-verification procedure (e.g. accepting a 'transferred' call as sufficient identity proof), update the finance team's checklist accordingly.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the relay pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record the multi-party pretext structure, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness training.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details at any point in the call chain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify each claimed identity in the call chain was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact each organization or role claimed (bank, law enforcement, internal department) using an already-known verified number to confirm none authorized the call.
steps.guidance: Never use a callback number provided during the suspect call.
steps.outcome: All claimed identities confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11223.def: A financial fraud phone call in which a single caller, maintaining one persona, creates urgency around a time-limited window to induce the victim to make an immediate payment before the call ends, without resorting to legal or personal threats.
ITID-11223.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing where a single caller uses time pressure alone (without threats or multi-party relay) to coerce an immediate payment within the same call.
scopeIncludes: Single-caller, single-persona urgency-based payment coercion within one call
Time-pressure tactics ('this offer/window expires when the call ends') as the primary lever
scopeExcludes: Coercion using explicit threats of legal or personal consequence (ITID-11228)
Coercion involving a multi-party call transfer between personas (ITID-11222)
ITID-11223.severity: Medium-High given the direct and immediate financial-loss potential.
ITID-11223.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment was made or is in progress.
ITID-11223.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams if a payment is in progress or was completed.
indicators: Caller insisting the payment or offer is only valid during the call
Caller discouraging the victim from hanging up to consult anyone else before paying
vectors: Caller using a time-limited discount, penalty-avoidance, or prize-claim pretext to force an immediate decision
rootCauses: No organizational guidance on treating any same-call payment demand as an automatic red flag
controls: Policy treating any same-call payment demand as an automatic red flag requiring independent verification before proceeding
User awareness training on urgency-based payment coercion
ITID-11223.response: Advise against making any payment during the call itself, regardless of the stated urgency, and verify independently first.
metrics: Count of same-call payment coercion reports per quarter
ITID-11223.notes: The differentiator from ITID-11228 is the absence of explicit threats — pure urgency versus urgency plus a stated consequence.

playbook.name: Response: Urgent Same-Call Payment Coercion
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call where the caller applied real-time pressure to have the recipient authorize or complete a payment before hanging up, exploiting urgency to bypass normal verification.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and capture the urgency tactics used
steps.desc: Record the caller ID, claimed identity, requested payment method, and the specific urgency/pressure language used (e.g. deadline threats, claims of an in-progress emergency).
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form.
steps.outcome: Structured call record captured including pressure tactics.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold, referencing exact transaction time.
steps.guidance: Same-call coercion cases are especially time-sensitive since the transfer may be only minutes old; escalate immediately.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update payment-authorization procedures to require a cooling-off/verification step
steps.desc: Update finance procedures to require independent verification before any payment is authorized under time pressure, regardless of claimed urgency.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the coercion pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record the specific urgency tactics used, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for staff awareness training.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether payment was completed during the call or after
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient completed a wire/ACH transfer, purchased gift cards or crypto, or read card/account details aloud during the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the caller's claimed identity was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization or individual the caller claimed to represent, using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such call was authorized.
steps.guidance: Never use a callback number provided by the suspect caller.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11224.def: A financial fraud phone call that begins as a pre-recorded automated robocall (often via an IVR-style menu) and, upon victim engagement (e.g., pressing a key to 'speak to a representative'), connects the victim to a live fraudulent agent to complete the scam.
ITID-11224.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing that begins as an automated robocall and funnels the victim to a live fraudulent agent, distinguishing the automated-to-live delivery chain from a purely live-caller-initiated attack.
scopeIncludes: An automated pre-recorded call that funnels an engaging victim to a live scam agent
IVR-style 'press 1 to dispute this charge' pretexts used as the initial automated hook
scopeExcludes: A vishing call that is entirely live-agent-initiated with no automated robocall stage (other Financial Fraud Call siblings)
A robocall used purely for reconnaissance/number validation with no live-agent funnel (not itself a financial fraud call until the funnel occurs)
ITID-11224.severity: Medium-High — the automated stage allows attackers to scale victim identification efficiently before investing live-agent time.
ITID-11224.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment was made or is in progress.
ITID-11224.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams if a payment is in progress or was completed.
indicators: Victim reporting an automated pre-recorded message followed by a live agent after pressing a key
High volume of similar automated calls reported across the organization in a short window
vectors: Mass automated robocall campaign designed to identify and funnel engaging victims to live agents
rootCauses: No organizational call-blocking/robocall-filtering technology deployed on corporate phone lines
controls: Robocall filtering/blocking technology on corporate phone lines
User awareness training on automated-to-live-agent fraud funnels
ITID-11224.detection: Telecom-level robocall filtering provides some preventive coverage; the live-agent stage relies on victim reporting.
ITID-11224.response: Report the automated call pattern to telecom/fraud-prevention channels and advise against engaging further once identified.
metrics: Count of robocall-to-live-agent fraud reports per quarter
ITID-11224.notes: The mass-automated-call volume seen with this mechanism can serve as an early warning signal for a broader coordinated campaign; correlate reports across the organization by call pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Automated Robocall-to-Live-Agent Funnel
playbook.description: For a financial fraud attempt that began as an automated robocall (e.g. a fake fraud alert or account-suspension message) prompting the recipient to press a number or call back, funneling them to a live scam agent.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and capture the automated message content and the live-agent interaction
steps.desc: Record the robocall's claimed source, the automated script content, the number reached after pressing through, and everything the live agent said or requested.
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form; ask if the recipient has a voicemail recording of the automated portion.
