steps.outcome: Full robocall-to-live-agent interaction documented.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update user guidance on handling automated financial alert calls
steps.desc: If applicable, update staff guidance to never call back numbers provided in an unsolicited automated financial alert, and instead use known verified contact numbers.
steps.outcome: Guidance reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the funnel pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record the robocall script pattern, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details to the live agent.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the claimed source of the automated alert was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization the robocall claimed to represent (e.g. the actual bank), using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such alert or account issue exists.
steps.guidance: Never use the callback number provided in the robocall itself.
steps.outcome: Claimed source confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11225.def: A financial fraud attack initiated by a voicemail message — often citing an urgent account or legal matter — that prompts the recipient to call back a provided number, at which point the victim is connected to a live fraudulent agent who initiates the scam.
ITID-11225.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing initiated by a voicemail lure that prompts the victim to call back a fraudulent number, distinguishing victim-initiated callback fraud from a direct inbound-call attack.
scopeIncludes: A voicemail lure prompting a callback to a fraudulent number
Cases where the victim, not the attacker, initiates the live call as a result of the voicemail
scopeExcludes: A direct inbound live call with no voicemail-callback stage (other Financial Fraud Call siblings)
ITID-11225.severity: Medium-High — victim-initiated callbacks can carry a false sense of security since the victim believes they are in control of initiating contact.
ITID-11225.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment was made or is in progress.
ITID-11225.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams if a payment is in progress or was completed.
indicators: Voicemail referencing an urgent account/legal matter with a callback number that does not match the claimed institution's published number
Victim reporting they called back a number left in a voicemail and reached a persuasive live agent
vectors: Pre-recorded voicemail dropped in bulk, relying on victim-initiated callback to establish the live scam
rootCauses: No organizational guidance to independently verify any callback number against the claimed institution's published contact detail before dialing
controls: Guidance to always verify a callback number against the institution's independently sourced published contact detail
User awareness training on voicemail-callback fraud
ITID-11225.response: Advise against calling the number left in the voicemail; verify independently with the real institution instead.
metrics: Count of voicemail-callback fraud reports per quarter
ITID-11225.notes: The victim-initiated nature of the callback is the key differentiator from other leaves in this Type, and is worth noting in incident write-ups since it affects how the psychological pressure operates.

playbook.name: Response: Voicemail-Initiated Callback Fraud
playbook.description: For a financial fraud attempt where the victim was left a voicemail (e.g. claiming an urgent account issue or unpaid invoice) prompting them to call back a number, connecting them to a scam agent.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and preserve the original voicemail
steps.desc: Record the voicemail's claimed source and requested action, preserve the audio recording if still available, and capture the callback number provided.
steps.guidance: Ask the recipient's voicemail system or provider whether the message can still be retrieved/exported.
steps.outcome: Voicemail content documented and audio preserved where possible.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized during the callback, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Block the callback number where feasible and update guidance
steps.desc: Add the fraudulent callback number to any available call-blocking list, and update staff guidance to verify voicemail claims through known channels before calling back.
steps.outcome: Number blocked where feasible; guidance updated.

steps.title: Document the voicemail pretext and outcome
steps.desc: Record the voicemail script pattern, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether the recipient called back and what occurred on that call
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient called the number back, what the live agent said or requested, and whether any payment or data was authorized or disclosed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of the callback interaction and any payment/disclosure.
steps.abort: If the recipient never called back, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the claimed source of the voicemail was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization the voicemail claimed to represent, using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such issue exists and the callback number is not theirs.
steps.guidance: Never use the callback number provided in the voicemail itself.
steps.outcome: Claimed source confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11226.def: A financial fraud phone call that is deliberately corroborated by a supporting email or SMS message — sent shortly before, during, or after the call — designed to lend the call additional credibility by appearing to independently confirm its claims.
ITID-11226.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing that is corroborated by a supporting email or text message, isolating this multi-channel credibility-boosting mechanism from a call operating in isolation.
scopeIncludes: A call whose claims are reinforced by a follow-up or concurrent email/SMS from a matching (spoofed) sender
Cases where the victim cites the supporting message as the reason they trusted the call
scopeExcludes: A call with no supporting email/SMS corroboration (other Financial Fraud Call siblings)
An email-based Business Email Compromise attack where a supporting phone call, if any, is only incidental rather than the multi-channel design's centerpiece (ITID-22411 through ITID-22415)
ITID-11226.severity: High — the multi-channel corroboration significantly increases perceived legitimacy and thus success likelihood.
ITID-11226.priority: P1 if any payment was made or in progress, otherwise P2.
ITID-11226.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams and preserve both the call detail and the corroborating message for the investigation.
indicators: Victim reporting they trusted the call because a matching email or text arrived around the same time
Corroborating message using a spoofed sender or lookalike domain matching the call's claimed identity
vectors: Coordinated phone call plus spoofed email/SMS sent from the same fraudulent operation
rootCauses: No organizational guidance that multi-channel corroboration does not itself prove legitimacy — each channel must be independently verified
controls: User awareness training explicitly covering multi-channel corroboration as a fraud technique, not a legitimacy signal
SEG/SMS filtering on the corroborating message channel
ITID-11226.detection: Partial — the email/SMS channel may be caught by standard filtering even where the call itself has no technical telemetry.
ITID-11226.response: Treat as a single coordinated incident; analyze both the call detail and the corroborating message, and block the message's sending infrastructure.
metrics: Count of multi-channel-corroborated fraud reports per quarter
detections: SEG/SMS filtering on the corroborating channel
ITID-11226.notes: Log the corroborating email/SMS as a related item under this same incident rather than opening a fully separate phishing case, since the two channels are part of one coordinated attack.

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Channel Financial Fraud Call (Call + Email/Text Corroboration)
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call reinforced by a corroborating email or text message (e.g. a fake invoice, a forged executive email, or an SMS confirming the caller's claimed identity) used to increase the victim's trust in the phone pretext.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and preserve all corroborating channels
steps.desc: Record the call details and separately preserve the corroborating email or text message (headers/full message for email, screenshot with sender number for text).
steps.guidance: Export the email as .eml/.msg, not a forward.
steps.outcome: Call record and corroborating message(s) preserved.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update outbound-payment verification procedures to require independent confirmation across channels
steps.desc: Update the finance team's procedure to require verification independent of any single channel, since cross-channel corroboration was used specifically to defeat single-channel checks.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the multi-channel pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record how the channels were combined, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details across any of the channels used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Block the corroborating email/text sender infrastructure
steps.desc: Add the sending domain/IP or phone number used for the corroborating message to block lists to prevent further delivery to other staff.
steps.outcome: Sender infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Verify the caller's and corroborating message's claimed identity were fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization or individual claimed across both channels, using an already-known verified number, to confirm neither the call nor the message was authorized.
steps.guidance: Never use contact information provided in either suspect channel.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity confirmed fabricated or unauthorized across both channels.

ITID-11227.def: A financial fraud phone call in which the caller spoofs the caller ID to display a specific known internal extension or phone number belonging to the organization, using that technical spoofing (rather than a claimed name alone) as the primary trust signal.
ITID-11227.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing where the caller spoofs a specific internal extension number as the primary credibility mechanism, isolating caller-ID-spoofing-of-internal-numbers from a generic colleague-identity claim.
scopeIncludes: Caller ID displaying a verified internal extension number that the recipient recognizes as belonging to a real internal line
Technical confirmation (e.g., from telecom/PBX logs) that the displayed number does not match the true originating call
scopeExcludes: A caller simply claiming to be a specific colleague by name with no confirmed number spoofing (ITID-11215, Colleague Impersonation Call)
ITID-11227.severity: High — successful caller ID spoofing of a verified internal number is a strong, hard-to-detect credibility signal.
ITID-11227.priority: P1 if a payment was made or in progress, otherwise P2.
ITID-11227.escalation: Escalate immediately to telecom/IT to investigate how internal extension spoofing was achieved (e.g., a PBX misconfiguration or compromise).
indicators: Recipient recognizing the displayed caller ID as a real internal extension, later confirmed via PBX logs not to match the true call origin
Financial request received from what appeared to be an internal number with no matching legitimate call record
vectors: Caller ID spoofing technique specifically targeting the organization's known internal numbering scheme
rootCauses: PBX/telecom system lacking caller ID authentication (e.g., STIR/SHAKEN) allowing internal number spoofing
controls: Caller ID authentication (STIR/SHAKEN) on the organization's telecom infrastructure
Policy that financial requests are never actioned on caller ID alone, internal or external
ITID-11227.detection: PBX/telecom call logs provide a strong technical signal once investigated, though real-time detection at the point of the call is limited.
ITID-11227.response: Investigate the telecom infrastructure for the spoofing vector and treat the request exactly as an external fraud attempt despite the internal-appearing caller ID.
metrics: Count of internal-extension-spoofing fraud reports per quarter
ITID-11227.notes: The differentiator from ITID-11215 is confirmed technical caller ID spoofing of a real internal number, not merely a claimed identity; if spoofing cannot be technically confirmed, classify under ITID-11215 instead.

playbook.name: Response: Spoofed Internal Extension Financial Fraud Call
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call where the caller ID displayed appeared to be a legitimate internal extension (e.g. impersonating an executive or the finance department), used to lend false internal credibility to a payment request.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and capture the displayed caller ID and requested action
steps.desc: Record the exact internal extension or name displayed, the claimed identity, and the requested payment action.
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form.
steps.outcome: Structured call record captured including the spoofed extension.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Update outbound-payment verification procedures to not rely on caller ID alone
steps.desc: Update the finance team's procedure to require independent out-of-band verification for payment requests regardless of how legitimate the displayed caller ID appears.
steps.outcome: Verification procedure reviewed and updated as needed.

steps.title: Document the spoofing technique and outcome
steps.desc: Record how the internal extension was spoofed (per the PBX log findings), financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Verify the internal extension spoofing via telephony/PBX log review
steps.desc: Review PBX/telephony call logs to determine whether the call actually originated from the claimed internal extension or was spoofed from an external trunk line, and identify the true originating source if possible.
steps.guidance: Check call detail records (CDRs) for trunk origin, SIP header anomalies, and correlate call timing against the internal extension's actual usage at that time.
steps.outcome: Spoofing confirmed via PBX logs, with true origin identified where possible.
steps.abort: If the call is confirmed to have genuinely originated from the internal extension, this is an internal actor incident, not vishing — escalate under the appropriate internal-threat playbook instead.

steps.title: Notify the impersonated employee and alert staff to the spoofing technique
steps.desc: Inform the employee whose extension/identity was spoofed, and issue a brief alert to relevant staff that caller ID for that extension cannot currently be trusted for payment requests.
steps.outcome: Impersonated employee notified; staff alerted.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details believing the call was internal.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

ITID-11228.def: A financial fraud phone call in which the caller explicitly threatens a specific negative consequence — arrest, service disconnection, legal action, or harm — if the victim does not make an immediate payment.
ITID-11228.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing that uses an explicit threat of legal, safety, or service-related consequence to coerce payment, isolating threat-based coercion from pure urgency-based coercion.
scopeIncludes: Explicit threats of arrest, lawsuit, deportation, or service cutoff used as the primary compliance lever
Threats combined with a specific payment demand within the same call
scopeExcludes: Coercion using time pressure alone with no explicit threat of consequence (ITID-11223)
The specific case of law-enforcement/government impersonation where identity impersonation, rather than the threat mechanism, is the dominant reportable feature (ITID-11213)
ITID-11228.severity: High — explicit threats materially increase psychological pressure and the risk of compliance.
ITID-11228.priority: P1 if a payment was made or in progress, otherwise P2.
ITID-11228.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams if a payment is in progress or was completed, and consider employee wellbeing support given the coercive nature of the threat.
indicators: Caller explicitly stating a specific negative consequence tied to non-payment
Caller refusing to allow the victim time to consult anyone else before the threatened consequence 'takes effect'
vectors: Caller combining a false authority claim with an explicit threat to maximize psychological pressure
rootCauses: No organizational guidance normalizing that legitimate entities do not threaten immediate consequence over the phone to compel payment
controls: User awareness training explicitly addressing threat-based payment coercion
Policy that no legitimate payment request is ever accepted under active threat during a single call
ITID-11228.response: Advise against making any payment under threat; verify independently and consider reporting the threat to appropriate authorities.
metrics: Count of threat-based payment coercion reports per quarter
ITID-11228.notes: The differentiator from ITID-11223 is the presence of an explicit threat rather than urgency alone; the differentiator from ITID-11213 is that here the coercion mechanism itself, not the impersonated identity, is the primary reportable and analytically relevant feature.

playbook.name: Response: Threat-of-Consequence Payment Coercion Call
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call where the caller used threats of negative consequence (e.g. legal action, arrest, termination of employment, service disconnection) to coerce the recipient into making a payment.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and capture the specific threats used
steps.desc: Record the caller ID, claimed identity, requested payment method, and the exact threat language used (e.g. claimed legal consequence, job/immigration/service-related threat).
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form; note the recipient's emotional state was likely a deliberate target of the tactic, and interview supportively.
steps.outcome: Structured call record captured including the specific threats made.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Offer the affected employee support and clarify no legitimate consequence exists
steps.desc: Follow up with the recipient to confirm the threat was fabricated and no real consequence is pending, given the coercive and potentially distressing nature of the call.
steps.outcome: Employee reassured; incident closed out with them directly.

steps.title: Document the coercion tactic and outcome
steps.desc: Record the specific threat pattern used, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for staff awareness training on high-pressure coercion tactics.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details under the threat.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the threatened consequence and caller's claimed identity were fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization the caller claimed to represent (e.g. actual court, tax authority, or employer HR), using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such action or requirement exists.
steps.guidance: Never use a callback number provided by the suspect caller.
steps.outcome: Claimed threat and identity confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

ITID-11229.def: A financial fraud phone call that incorporates specific, accurate detail about the target, their organization, or an executive's activity (schedule, travel, org structure) gathered through prior reconnaissance, used to substantially increase the call's credibility.
ITID-11229.purpose: Captures financial fraud vishing that is deliberately informed by prior reconnaissance (OSINT or otherwise) about the target or organization, isolating pre-call intelligence-gathering-driven attacks from generic, untailored fraud calls.
scopeIncludes: Calls referencing accurate, non-generic detail (a real project name, a real vendor relationship, a specific executive's travel) that indicates prior research
Calls following a related reconnaissance event (e.g., a prior data breach or a LinkedIn-sourced org chart) that can be connected to this call
scopeExcludes: A generic fraud call with no evidence of specific prior research (other Financial Fraud Call siblings)
The equivalent email-channel technique of OSINT-informed whaling timed to executive travel (ITID-11145), which is tracked separately by channel
ITID-11229.severity: High — the presence of accurate reconnaissance detail substantially increases both credibility and the sophistication implied of the threat actor.
ITID-11229.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/fraud teams and to threat intelligence to assess the source and extent of the reconnaissance used.
indicators: Caller referencing detail that would not be guessable without specific research (project codenames, exact reporting lines, precise travel dates)
Correlation with a known prior reconnaissance event (breach, OSINT campaign) targeting the same organization or individual
vectors: Caller leveraging OSINT gathered from social media, press coverage, or a prior data breach to tailor the call's pretext
rootCauses: Excessive organizational or personal detail publicly discoverable through social media, press, or job postings
A prior undetected reconnaissance or breach event providing the attacker with accurate internal detail
controls: Organizational OSINT/digital-footprint reduction guidance
Executive digital-footprint/OSINT monitoring service
Threat intelligence correlation with known reconnaissance/breach events
ITID-11229.detection: Relies on victim/employee reporting combined with threat-intelligence correlation to the source of the reconnaissance.
ITID-11229.response: Investigate the source of the reconnaissance detail used (public OSINT vs. a prior breach) in addition to standard fraud response steps.
metrics: Count of reconnaissance-informed fraud call reports per quarter
ITID-11229.notes: Scope decision: this leaf covers the voice-call channel specifically; the equivalent OSINT-timed whaling technique delivered by email is tracked under ITID-11145 to keep channel-based reporting distinct even where the underlying reconnaissance may be the same.

playbook.name: Response: Reconnaissance-Informed Financial Fraud Call
playbook.description: For a financial fraud call where the caller demonstrated specific knowledge of the organization, its personnel, or an in-progress transaction (e.g. correct vendor names, recent invoice amounts, an executive's travel schedule) gathered through prior reconnaissance, used to increase credibility.

steps.title: Interview the recipient and catalog every piece of specific knowledge the caller demonstrated
steps.desc: Record exactly what internal details the caller knew (names, amounts, schedules, org structure, ongoing deals) in addition to standard call details.
steps.guidance: Use a structured intake form; this level of detail is critical to tracing the reconnaissance source.
steps.outcome: Full call record captured with an itemized list of demonstrated insider knowledge.

steps.title: Contact the bank or payment processor immediately if a transfer occurred
steps.desc: If any payment was authorized, contact the receiving/sending bank or payment processor without delay to attempt a recall or hold.
steps.outcome: Bank/processor notified and recall attempt initiated, or confirmed no payment occurred.

steps.title: Reduce exposure of the information source identified during tracing
steps.desc: If the reconnaissance source was public over-exposure (e.g. oversharing on social media or public filings) or a compromised account, take the appropriate reduction action (guidance to staff, or account remediation if compromise is confirmed).
steps.outcome: Exposure reduced or remediation initiated as applicable.

steps.title: Document the reconnaissance-informed pattern and outcome
steps.desc: Record what information was used, its likely source, financial impact (if any), and recovery outcome for trend tracking and staff awareness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether any payment or financial data was actually initiated or disclosed
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient initiated a transfer, purchased gift cards/crypto, or disclosed account/card details, given the elevated credibility of this pretext.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether any payment or disclosure occurred.
steps.abort: If no payment was initiated and no data disclosed, this is a near-miss; proceed to lighter containment and documentation only.

steps.title: Verify the caller's claimed identity was fabricated
steps.desc: Independently contact the organization or individual the caller claimed to represent, using an already-known verified number, to confirm no such call was authorized.
steps.guidance: Never use a callback number provided by the suspect caller.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity confirmed fabricated or unauthorized.

steps.title: Trace the likely source of the reconnaissance information
steps.desc: Assess whether the demonstrated knowledge could plausibly have come from public sources (social media, press releases, public filings), a prior data breach, or a compromised internal account/mailbox, since the latter indicates a broader ongoing compromise.
steps.guidance: Check whether any of the specific details referenced appear only in internal, non-public systems.
steps.outcome: Likely reconnaissance source assessed (public OSINT vs. compromised internal source).
steps.abort: If internal-only information was used, escalate in parallel as a suspected account/mailbox compromise investigation.

ITID-11311.def: An SMS or SMS-like text message containing a link to a fake login/credential-capture page, logged before the specific lure theme (delivery, banking, carrier, toll, etc.) has been confirmed or where the lure does not clearly match a more specific sibling leaf.
ITID-11311.purpose: Catch-all for a smishing message containing a credential-harvesting link that does not yet match a more specific lure-themed leaf in this Tier-4 group.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the lure theme is confirmed
Credential-harvesting smishing using a generic, unbranded, or unclear pretext
scopeExcludes: A lure clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (package delivery, banking, toll/parking, carrier, login-verification, etc.)
Links that deliver malware rather than a credential-capture page (Malware Links group, ITID-11321 family)
Messages soliciting an OTP/MFA code rather than static login credentials (OTP/MFA Fatigue group, ITID-11331 family)
ITID-11311.severity: Medium; reassess once the lure theme and target are confirmed.
ITID-11311.escalation: Escalate to the anti-phishing/SOC queue; reclassify under a specific lure-themed leaf once identified.
indicators: User-reported suspicious text containing a link
Link resolving to a known phishing-kit domain or newly registered lookalike domain
vectors: SMS message with a shortened or brand-spoofed link to a fake login page
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available at time of report
Lack of automated URL categorization at intake
controls: Carrier/SMS spam filtering
Mobile threat defense URL reputation
User awareness training
ITID-11311.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting; carrier and mobile-threat-defense link-reputation feeds provide partial coverage.
ITID-11311.response: Document, block the URL/domain, and attempt reclassification under a specific lure-themed leaf.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-11311.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General SMS Credential Harvesting Link
playbook.description: For a reported SMS message containing a link to a credential-harvesting page that does not fit a more specific smishing sub-category.

steps.title: Preserve the SMS message and sender identifier
steps.desc: Have the reporting user screenshot the full message body, sender number/short code, and timestamp before deleting or blocking.
steps.guidance: Ask the user not to click the link again; forward the screenshot to the SOC mailbox or reporting tool.
steps.outcome: Message content, sender ID, and timestamp preserved in the case file.

steps.title: Contain any exposed corporate account
steps.desc: If credentials were entered on the page, force password reset and session/token revocation on any corporate account that used those credentials.
steps.guidance: Treat as a credential-theft incident; follow standard account-containment steps.
steps.outcome: Affected account(s) secured with new credentials and revoked sessions.

steps.title: Confirm no persistent compromise on the device
steps.desc: Check MDM for any unexpected app installs, profiles, or configuration changes on the reporting user's device.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean or issue identified for remediation.

steps.title: Restore account access and confirm normal use
steps.desc: Re-enable the affected account with new credentials and confirm the user can authenticate normally with MFA intact.
steps.outcome: User has restored, confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Log the campaign and update awareness materials if warranted
steps.desc: Record the lure theme, sender pattern, and landing-page domain in the case log; flag to security awareness training if it represents a new lure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness content updated if warranted.

steps.title: Check whether the link was opened or credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check mobile threat defense/MDM web-access logs for the device to confirm interaction with the link.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of whether the link was opened and whether any data was submitted.
steps.abort: If reported without any interaction, skip account containment and proceed directly to blocklisting.

steps.title: Block the malicious domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the phishing domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the originating number to the mobile carrier's smishing reporting channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked org-wide; number reported to carrier.

steps.title: Assess scope across the user base
steps.desc: Search mobile threat defense telemetry and other user reports for the same sender number, link, or landing-page domain.
steps.outcome: Scope of the campaign (isolated vs. broader) established.

ITID-11312.def: A smishing message impersonating a shipping carrier or retailer (USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, Amazon, etc.), claiming a delivery problem, redelivery fee, or customs charge, with a link to a fake login or payment-and-account page.
ITID-11312.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that uses a fake package-delivery/shipping-fee lure to drive a target to a credential-harvesting page.
scopeIncludes: Delivery/shipping-fee themed lure with a credential- or payment-detail-harvesting link
scopeExcludes: A delivery-lure message whose link installs malware/an app instead of harvesting credentials (Malware Links group, ITID-11321 family)
Other lure themes (banking, carrier, toll, etc. — see sibling leaves)
ITID-11312.severity: Medium; escalate if part of a large bulk campaign against many employees.
ITID-11312.priority: P3 default, P2 if a broad blast against the organization is confirmed.
ITID-11312.escalation: Escalate to SOC for domain blocking; notify affected users if corporate numbers are targeted at scale.
indicators: SMS spoofing a delivery brand with a link domain unrelated to the carrier's real domain
Urgency framing around a small redelivery/customs fee
vectors: Bulk/blast SMS with delivery-service branding and a shortened URL
rootCauses: Ease of brand impersonation in SMS with no sender verification
Users routinely expecting deliveries, lowering suspicion
controls: Brand-abuse/domain monitoring
SMS filtering
User awareness on delivery scams
ITID-11312.detection: Carrier SMS filtering and user reports; low technical visibility otherwise.
ITID-11312.response: Block the domain, alert affected users, and check for submitted credentials on corporate devices.
metrics: Count of delivery-lure smishing reports per month
ITID-11312.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves purely by lure theme (delivery/logistics branding).

playbook.name: Response: Package Delivery Notification Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS impersonating a courier or delivery service (missing address, failed delivery, customs fee) with a credential-harvesting or payment-detail link.

steps.title: Preserve the message and identify the spoofed carrier brand
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and note which courier/delivery brand is being impersonated and the sender number/short code.
steps.outcome: Message content, spoofed brand, and sender identifier preserved.

steps.title: If payment card details were entered, initiate card containment
steps.desc: Advise the user to contact their card issuer immediately to flag the card for fraud monitoring or reissue.
steps.guidance: This is a personal financial exposure; the SOC's role is to advise and document, not to act on the user's personal bank account.
steps.outcome: User has contacted card issuer; card flagged or reissued.

steps.title: Check for follow-on malware installation
steps.desc: Some delivery-smishing chains redirect to a fake tracking app install after the harvest page; verify via MDM whether any app was sideloaded.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean or malicious install identified.

steps.title: Confirm account and device are safe to use
steps.desc: Verify restored account access and device compliance status before closing the case.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Log the campaign and brand impersonated
steps.desc: Record the courier brand impersonated, lure pattern, and outcome for trend tracking and awareness content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Check whether the link was clicked and whether payment/personal details were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check MDM/mobile threat defense logs; delivery smishing commonly harvests payment card details rather than only account credentials.
steps.guidance: Ask specifically whether a card number, CVV, or address was submitted, not just a login.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of interaction and any data submitted.
steps.abort: If no interaction occurred, skip payment-related containment and proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: If corporate credentials were entered, contain the account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any corporate account whose credentials were entered on the linked page.
steps.outcome: Affected corporate account secured.

steps.title: Assess whether this matches a known active delivery-smishing campaign
steps.desc: Compare the sender number and link pattern against threat intel feeds and other user reports.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope and any known IOCs identified.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the number
steps.desc: Add the phishing domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the sender number to the carrier's smishing channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

ITID-11313.def: A smishing message impersonating a bank or financial institution, claiming fraud, a locked card, or suspicious activity, with a link to a fake bank login page.
ITID-11313.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that uses a fake bank/financial-account alert lure to drive a target to a credential-harvesting page.
scopeIncludes: Banking/financial-alert themed lure with a static credential-harvesting link
scopeExcludes: The equivalent lure delivered by live phone call (a distinct Vishing-branch ITID, not in this group)
OTP/MFA code solicitation tied to a bank account (OTP/MFA Fatigue group, ITID-11331 family) — this leaf covers static login-credential capture, not a code relay ask
ITID-11313.priority: P2 if bank-branded and corporate device involved; P3 otherwise.
ITID-11313.escalation: Escalate to SOC and, if a corporate device submitted credentials, initiate account-compromise response.
indicators: SMS spoofing a real bank's name/short code
Link domain mimicking the bank with subtle misspelling
vectors: Bulk smishing referencing generic 'suspicious activity' to cast a wide net across bank customers
rootCauses: Banks' legitimate use of SMS alerts normalizes clicking bank-branded texts
Lack of employee training on smishing specific to financial lures
controls: User awareness training
Mobile threat defense URL reputation
Personal-device credential-reuse monitoring where feasible
ITID-11313.detection: Minimal direct technical visibility unless the victim uses a corporate device; relies on user reporting.
ITID-11313.response: Block domain, advise victim to change reused passwords and contact their real bank.
metrics: Count of bank-lure smishing reports per month
ITID-11313.notes: Scoped to the SMS/link-based version specifically to avoid duplicating the live-call banking-fraud vishing ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy.

playbook.name: Response: Bank / Financial Account Alert Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS impersonating a bank or financial institution (suspicious transaction, account locked, verify identity) linking to a credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Preserve the message and identify the impersonated institution
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and record the impersonated bank/financial brand and sender number.
steps.outcome: Message content and impersonated brand preserved.

steps.title: If a corporate financial account or card was exposed, contain it immediately
steps.desc: Notify finance/treasury to freeze or flag the corporate account/card and contact the real institution's fraud line.
steps.guidance: Time-sensitive: financial-brand smishing is frequently followed by a live fraud attempt within hours.
steps.outcome: Corporate account/card frozen or flagged with the institution.

steps.title: Verify no follow-on fraudulent transactions occurred
steps.desc: Ask the user to check recent account activity/statements for unauthorized transactions in the days following the smishing attempt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized transactions, or fraud identified and reported to the institution.

steps.title: Confirm account restored and monitoring in place
steps.desc: Confirm the account is usable again and, if applicable, that the institution has placed a fraud monitoring flag.
steps.outcome: Account restored with monitoring active.

steps.title: Log the impersonated institution and lure pattern
steps.desc: Record findings for trend tracking; flag to awareness training if this is a new impersonation theme.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine if this targets a personal or corporate financial account
steps.desc: Interview the user to establish whether the impersonated account is personal banking or a corporate card/treasury account, and whether the link was clicked.
steps.outcome: Account type and interaction status confirmed.
steps.abort: If personal banking with no interaction, log and close after advising the user; no corporate containment needed.

steps.title: If credentials were entered, reset and revoke sessions on the affected online banking/identity account
steps.desc: Coordinate with the user (personal) or identity provider (corporate) to force a credential reset.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Check for a wider campaign against the same institution brand
steps.desc: Search for other reports referencing the same impersonated bank and sender pattern.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

steps.title: Block the phishing domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist; report the number to the carrier's smishing channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

ITID-11314.def: A smishing message claiming an unpaid toll or parking fine, threatening late fees or legal action, with a link to a fake payment portal that captures card details and/or account credentials.
ITID-11314.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that uses a fake toll-road or parking-violation payment demand to drive a target to a credential/card-harvesting page.
scopeIncludes: Toll/parking/government-payment themed lure with a payment-portal credential-harvesting link
scopeExcludes: Other government-agency impersonation lures not related to toll/parking payment (out of scope for this leaf)
ITID-11314.severity: Medium; primarily a personal-financial-fraud risk rather than corporate compromise.
ITID-11314.escalation: Escalate to SOC for domain blocking; advise affected employees to monitor card statements.
indicators: SMS referencing a toll authority or municipal parking system with a non-official domain
Small-dollar urgent payment demand
vectors: Mass smishing campaigns exploiting the ubiquity of toll/parking systems and E-ZPass-style branding
rootCauses: High plausibility of the lure given widespread toll-road usage
Lack of carrier-level filtering for this specific campaign pattern at time of send
controls: Mobile threat defense URL reputation
User awareness training
ITID-11314.detection: Almost entirely dependent on user reporting; no corporate system typically involved.
ITID-11314.response: Block domain and advise the individual to monitor for fraudulent card charges.
metrics: Count of toll/parking-lure smishing reports per month
ITID-11314.notes: Low corporate-risk lure theme, tracked primarily for awareness and volume trending.

playbook.name: Response: Toll Road / Parking Violation Payment Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS claiming an unpaid toll or parking violation with a link demanding payment and card details.

steps.title: Preserve the message and note the claimed toll authority/agency
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and record the impersonated toll or parking authority and sender number.
steps.outcome: Message content and impersonated agency preserved.

steps.title: If card details were entered, advise immediate card issuer contact
steps.desc: Advise the user to contact their card issuer to flag or reissue the card.
steps.outcome: User has contacted card issuer.

steps.title: Confirm no further fraudulent charges
steps.desc: Follow up with the user after a few days to confirm no unauthorized charges appeared on the card.
steps.outcome: No unauthorized charges confirmed, or fraud reported to issuer.

steps.title: Log the lure and note for awareness communications
steps.desc: Record the impersonated agency and pattern; this lure type spikes seasonally and is worth periodic awareness reminders.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Check whether payment details were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user to confirm whether the link was clicked and whether card details were submitted on the fake payment page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, skip payment containment and proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the number
steps.desc: Add the payment-harvesting domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the sender number to the carrier.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Compare sender number and link against other user reports and threat intel for known toll-smishing infrastructure.
steps.guidance: This lure type is commonly run as a mass campaign with rotating domains.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11315.def: A smishing message impersonating the target's mobile carrier, warning of an account suspension or billing issue, with a link to a fake carrier-account login page.
ITID-11315.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that uses a fake mobile-carrier account-suspension lure to drive a target to a credential-harvesting page for their carrier account.
scopeIncludes: Carrier-account-suspension themed lure with a static credential-harvesting link
scopeExcludes: A resulting SIM swap enabled by the harvested carrier credentials — tracked separately under the SIM Swapping ITID family (e.g., ITID-12641) once account takeover occurs; this leaf covers the initial credential-harvesting message only
ITID-11315.severity: Medium-High — carrier-account compromise is a known precursor to SIM swap and downstream account takeover.
ITID-11315.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if carrier-account credentials are confirmed submitted.
ITID-11315.escalation: Escalate immediately if credentials were submitted, given the SIM-swap precursor risk; coordinate with the individual's carrier if a corporate-linked number is involved.
indicators: SMS spoofing the carrier's real short code or brand name
Link domain resembling the carrier's portal
vectors: Carrier-branded smishing preceding a social-engineering-based SIM swap attempt
rootCauses: Carrier account credentials often reused or weakly protected
Lack of user awareness that carrier-account compromise enables SIM swap
controls: Carrier account PIN/passcode enforcement (organizational awareness)
Mobile threat defense URL reputation
User awareness training
ITID-11315.detection: Relies on user reporting; carrier-account login attempts are not visible to corporate telemetry.
ITID-11315.response: If credentials were submitted, treat as a SIM-swap precursor and advise the individual to contact their carrier to lock the account.
metrics: Count of carrier-lure smishing reports per month
Count with confirmed credential submission
ITID-11315.notes: Scoped to the credential-harvesting message itself; a completed SIM swap is a separate incident classified under the SIM Swapping ITID family (ITID-12641 and children) to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Mobile Carrier / Account Suspension Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS impersonating the user's mobile carrier, warning of account suspension or an unpaid bill, linking to a credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Preserve the message and identify the impersonated carrier
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and record the impersonated carrier brand and sender number.
steps.outcome: Message content and impersonated brand preserved.

steps.title: Lock down the carrier account if credentials were exposed
steps.desc: Have the user contact the carrier directly (via a verified number, not the SMS) to reset the carrier account password and add a port-out/SIM-change PIN if not already set.
steps.outcome: Carrier account secured with new credentials and port-out protection.

steps.title: Confirm carrier account and service restored to normal
steps.desc: Confirm the user has normal cellular service and carrier account access with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Service and account confirmed normal.

steps.title: Log the campaign and any SIM-swap linkage
steps.desc: Record findings, noting whether this was an isolated smishing attempt or part of a SIM-swap chain.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Check whether the carrier account credentials were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user; carrier account takeover can enable SIM-swap follow-on attacks, so treat any credential entry as high priority.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: If a SIM swap is confirmed, escalate as account takeover
steps.desc: Treat confirmed SIM swap as a separate, higher-severity incident: identify and reset any corporate accounts using this number for SMS-based MFA.
steps.outcome: Downstream accounts protected from SMS-MFA bypass.

steps.title: Check for related SIM-swap indicators
steps.desc: If carrier credentials were entered, check for unexpected loss of cellular signal, unrecognized SIM/eSIM changes, or carrier account notifications.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether a SIM swap has occurred alongside the credential harvest.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the phishing domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the number to the carrier's fraud/smishing channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

ITID-11316.def: A smishing message stating a verification code was sent or is needed, but whose link leads to a fake login page capturing username and password — no OTP/code is actually requested back from the victim.
ITID-11316.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that frames the malicious link itself as a 'verification code' notification, harvesting static login credentials rather than soliciting a real OTP.
scopeIncludes: 'Here is your verification link' or 'verify your account now' lures where the link itself is the attack vector, not a request for the victim to relay a code
scopeExcludes: Messages that ask the victim to reply with or relay an actual OTP/MFA code (OTP/MFA Fatigue group, ITID-11331 family) — that is a code-relay social-engineering ask, distinct from this leaf's static credential-harvesting page
ITID-11316.severity: Medium; treat as standard credential-harvesting risk.
ITID-11316.escalation: Escalate to SOC for domain blocking; check for corporate credential reuse if submitted.
indicators: SMS mentioning 'verification' with an embedded link (not a code to type back)
Link leads to a generic or brand-spoofed login form
vectors: Framing a phishing link as part of a routine verification/security process to lower suspicion
rootCauses: Users conditioned to click 'verify' links from legitimate services
No visual distinction between a genuine verification link and a spoofed one
controls: User awareness training
Mobile threat defense URL reputation
ITID-11316.detection: Relies on user reporting; link-reputation feeds provide partial coverage.
ITID-11316.response: Block domain and check for downstream credential reuse.
metrics: Count of fake-verification-link smishing reports per month
ITID-11316.notes: Deliberately scoped to the static-link variant to avoid duplicating the OTP/MFA Fatigue group, which covers messages that solicit an actual code from the victim.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Login Verification Code Link Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS containing a link that claims to let the recipient 'verify' or 'view' a login code, but actually leads to a credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Preserve the message and identify the spoofed service
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and record which service's login-verification flow is being spoofed and the sender number.
steps.outcome: Message content and spoofed service preserved.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions on the targeted account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session/refresh-token revocation on the spoofed account, regardless of whether entry is confirmed, if a correlating real login attempt was found.
steps.outcome: Account secured against the paired login attempt.

steps.title: Verify no persistent access was established
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected forwarding rules, OAuth grants, or new registered MFA devices added after the incident window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access with new MFA enrollment
steps.desc: Have the user re-enroll MFA and confirm normal account access.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access with fresh MFA.

steps.title: Log the campaign and pattern
steps.desc: Record the spoofed service and whether a correlating real login attempt was observed, for detection tuning.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Check whether the link was clicked and credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check MDM/mobile threat defense logs for interaction with the link.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction occurred, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the phishing domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the number to the carrier.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

steps.title: Correlate with any real authentication attempt around the same time
steps.desc: Check identity provider sign-in logs for a genuine login attempt on the spoofed service near the time the SMS was sent — this pattern is often paired with a real login attempt by the attacker.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether a corresponding real sign-in attempt exists.

ITID-11317.def: A smishing message using a shortened URL, homoglyph/lookalike domain, or open-redirect chain to disguise the true destination of a credential-harvesting link, logged when the obfuscation technique — used to evade carrier or URL filtering — is the primary point of interest, independent of or spanning multiple lure themes.
ITID-11317.purpose: Flags credential-harvesting smishing where the notable, classification-driving feature is the URL obfuscation/cloaking technique itself, rather than a specific lure theme.
scopeIncludes: Cases where a shortener, homoglyph domain, or redirect chain is the defining technical feature
Campaigns using obfuscation specifically noted as evading carrier-level URL filtering
scopeExcludes: Cases where the lure theme is clear and the obfuscation is incidental — classify under the specific lure leaf instead (ITID-11312 through ITID-11316, ITID-11318, ITID-11319)
ITID-11317.severity: Medium; elevated if the obfuscation technique indicates a sophisticated or evolving campaign.
ITID-11317.priority: P3 default, P2 if the technique is actively bypassing current filtering controls.
ITID-11317.escalation: Escalate to SOC/threat-intel for URL-pattern analysis and filter tuning.
indicators: Nested redirect chains observed in link analysis
Domain using unicode/homoglyph characters mimicking a trusted brand
vectors: URL shorteners masking the true destination
Open redirects on otherwise legitimate domains
rootCauses: URL filtering rules keyed to domain reputation rather than redirect-chain analysis
Gaps in homoglyph-domain detection
controls: URL/redirect-chain analysis at the gateway
Homoglyph-domain detection
Mobile threat defense URL reputation
ITID-11317.detection: Technical link-analysis tooling gives moderate coverage here, stronger than most sibling leaves in this group.
ITID-11317.response: Analyze the full redirect chain, block all hops, and feed indicators into filtering rules.
metrics: Count of obfuscation-technique smishing cases per quarter
Number of new evasion patterns identified
ITID-11317.notes: This is a technique-axis leaf, not a lure-theme leaf — used only when obfuscation itself is the notable classification driver, to avoid double-counting against the lure-themed siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Shortened / Obfuscated URL Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS credential-harvesting link that uses a URL shortener or other obfuscation technique to hide the true destination domain.

steps.title: Preserve the message and the shortened URL as-received
steps.desc: Screenshot the message capturing the exact shortened/obfuscated URL string and sender number.
steps.guidance: Do not click the link directly from a corporate device; use a sandboxed browser or URL-expansion tool.
steps.outcome: Shortened URL and sender preserved without direct interaction.

steps.title: If credentials were entered, contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any corporate account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and clean device state
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored and the device shows no signs of compromise.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Log the shortener/obfuscation technique used
steps.desc: Record the obfuscation method and resolved domain to help tune detection for similar future obfuscated links.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Resolve the shortened URL to its true destination
steps.desc: Use a URL-expansion/sandboxing tool or threat intel platform to safely resolve the shortener to the final landing-page domain.
steps.outcome: True destination domain identified.

steps.title: Block both the shortener redirect and the resolved destination domain
steps.desc: Add the resolved landing-page domain to the web/DNS blocklist; where feasible, also flag the specific short-link path since the shortener domain itself is likely legitimate infrastructure abused by many campaigns.
steps.guidance: Blocking the entire shortener domain (e.g. bit.ly) is usually too broad — block the specific resolved destination instead.
steps.outcome: Malicious destination blocked without over-blocking legitimate shortener traffic.

steps.title: Check whether the link was clicked and credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check MDM/mobile threat defense logs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Report the sender number
steps.desc: Report the originating number to the mobile carrier's smishing channel.
steps.outcome: Number reported.

ITID-11318.def: A credential-harvesting smishing message delivered through iMessage or RCS (Rich Communication Services), leveraging rich link previews, images, or interactive buttons — a delivery channel that often bypasses carrier-level plain-SMS filtering.
ITID-11318.purpose: Flags credential-harvesting smishing delivered via iMessage or RCS rich-media features rather than plain SMS.
scopeIncludes: Messages delivered via iMessage/RCS with rich-media formatting (link previews, embedded images, tappable buttons)
scopeExcludes: Plain-text SMS delivery of the same lure theme — classify under the relevant lure-themed leaf instead
ITID-11318.severity: Medium; elevated because rich-media formatting increases perceived legitimacy and often evades SMS-specific filtering.
ITID-11318.priority: P3 default, P2 if targeting iOS-heavy corporate device fleets at scale.
ITID-11318.escalation: Escalate to mobile device management/security team to assess whether iMessage/RCS filtering gaps need addressing.
indicators: Blue-bubble (iMessage) or RCS-formatted message with a rich link preview
Message not passing through standard carrier SMS filtering
vectors: Abuse of iMessage/RCS rich formatting to make a malicious link preview appear more trustworthy
rootCauses: SMS filtering controls not extended to iMessage/RCS channels
Rich previews obscuring the true destination URL
controls: MDM-enforced link-preview/URL filtering on managed devices
User awareness training on rich-media message risks
ITID-11318.detection: Weak — most carrier and gateway filtering is tuned for plain SMS, not iMessage/RCS.
ITID-11318.response: Report to MDM/mobile security team; treat filtering-gap findings as a control improvement item.
metrics: Count of iMessage/RCS-delivered smishing reports per quarter
ITID-11318.notes: Channel-axis leaf; distinguishes delivery protocol from lure theme.

playbook.name: Response: Rich-Media (iMessage/RCS) Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported smishing message delivered over a rich-media messaging channel (iMessage or RCS) rather than plain SMS, which can carry richer content and evade some SMS-focused filtering.

steps.title: Preserve the message and note the delivery channel
steps.desc: Screenshot the full message including any rich-media content (images, link previews, reply buttons) and confirm whether it arrived via iMessage or RCS rather than SMS/MMS.
steps.guidance: Rich-media channels can render link previews and quick-reply buttons that make the lure look more legitimate — note this in the report.
steps.outcome: Message content and channel type preserved.

steps.title: If credentials were entered, contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any corporate account whose credentials were entered on the linked page.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and clean device state
steps.desc: Confirm account restoration and that the device is not receiving further messages from the sender.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access; sender blocked.

steps.title: Log the channel gap and update filtering if needed
steps.desc: Record that this arrived via a rich-media channel and whether existing controls need extension to cover iMessage/RCS.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; filtering gap flagged to the mobile security team if applicable.

steps.title: Check whether the link was clicked or a quick-reply engaged
steps.desc: Interview the user; also check whether the user replied to the message, since replying can confirm the number is active and invite follow-up attacks.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status including any reply sent.
steps.abort: If no interaction occurred, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the sender and destination domain across available channels
steps.desc: Block the sender's Apple ID/number/RCS identity at the device level and add the destination domain to the web/DNS blocklist.
steps.outcome: Sender and domain blocked.

steps.title: Assess whether this bypassed existing SMS filtering controls
steps.desc: Check whether the organization's SMS/MMS filtering solution has visibility into iMessage/RCS traffic, and whether this message was flagged or missed.
steps.outcome: Gap in filtering coverage identified, if any.

steps.title: Report the sender to the platform
steps.desc: Report the message via the built-in 'Report Junk' function (iMessage) or the carrier's RCS abuse channel.
steps.outcome: Sender reported to the platform operator.

ITID-11319.def: A spear-smishing message crafted using organization-specific reconnaissance (the target's real name, internal tool branding, department context) impersonating the organization's own SSO or VPN login, aimed at harvesting corporate credentials for enterprise entry.
ITID-11319.purpose: Distinguishes targeted, recon-informed smishing against a specific employee's corporate SSO/VPN credentials from opportunistic consumer-lure smishing.
scopeIncludes: Messages referencing the target's real name, role, or internal system branding
Links mimicking the organization's actual SSO/VPN login page
scopeExcludes: Opportunistic, non-targeted consumer-brand lures (delivery, bank, toll, carrier — see sibling leaves)
The same targeted pretext delivered by phone call rather than text (a distinct Vishing-branch ITID)
ITID-11319.severity: High — direct enterprise credential targeting with confirmed reconnaissance.
ITID-11319.priority: P1, given the direct path to corporate account/network compromise.
ITID-11319.escalation: Escalate to SOC and IAM immediately; force credential reset and review SSO/VPN logs for the targeted account regardless of reported click-through.
indicators: SMS referencing the employee's real name/department
Link domain closely mimicking the organization's real SSO/VPN portal
vectors: Pre-attack reconnaissance (LinkedIn, breach data, org chart) informing a tailored spear-smishing message
rootCauses: Employee PII/role information available via public sources or prior breaches
SSO/VPN portal branding easily cloned
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/hardware keys) on SSO/VPN
Conditional access/impossible-travel detection
User awareness training on spear-smishing
ITID-11319.detection: Strong if phishing-resistant MFA is enforced; SSO/VPN authentication logs provide a real technical signal for anomalous logins following a reported click.
ITID-11319.response: Treat as a targeted intrusion attempt: reset credentials, review authentication logs, and hunt for follow-on activity regardless of confirmed submission.
metrics: Count of confirmed spear-smishing attempts per quarter
Time-to-credential-reset after a targeted attempt
ITID-11319.notes: Enterprise-targeted counterpart to the opportunistic lures in this group; distinguished by confirmed reconnaissance and a corporate authentication target.

playbook.name: Response: Reconnaissance-Informed Corporate SSO/VPN Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported smishing message that demonstrates prior reconnaissance — referencing the target's real employer, manager name, internal tool names, or SSO/VPN branding — to lend credibility to a credential-harvesting link.

steps.title: Preserve the message and catalogue what internal details it references
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and list every specific detail it uses (employer name, internal app/portal name, manager/colleague name, correct SSO branding) that suggests targeted reconnaissance.
steps.guidance: This detail catalogue is important for scoping how the attacker obtained the information.
steps.outcome: Message content and reconnaissance indicators documented.

steps.title: Immediately reset SSO/VPN credentials and revoke sessions for the targeted user
steps.desc: Force password reset, MFA re-enrollment, and full session/token revocation on the user's SSO account, regardless of confirmed entry, given the targeted nature of the attack.
steps.outcome: SSO/VPN account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent access was established via SSO/VPN
steps.desc: Review VPN connection logs, SSO application access, and any new device/MFA enrollments for signs the attacker gained real access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access, or further incident opened if found.
steps.abort: Escalate to full intrusion-response process if unauthorized access is confirmed.

steps.title: Confirm restored access with fresh MFA and monitor for follow-up attempts
steps.desc: Confirm the user has restored access and place the account under short-term heightened monitoring given the targeted nature of the attack.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access under monitoring.

steps.title: Document the reconnaissance vector and brief on targeted-smishing risk
steps.desc: Record the reconnaissance source and lure details; brief the security awareness team on targeted (spear-)smishing risk if this indicates deliberate targeting rather than a mass campaign.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted-attack pattern flagged for wider organizational awareness.

steps.title: Check whether the link was clicked and SSO/VPN credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check identity provider sign-in logs for any resulting authentication attempt against the real SSO/VPN service.
steps.guidance: Treat this as high-priority — targeted smishing against SSO/VPN often precedes a real intrusion attempt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status and any correlating real sign-in attempt.

steps.title: Block the phishing domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the destination domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the number to the carrier's fraud channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

steps.title: Determine how the attacker obtained the reconnaissance information
steps.desc: Check whether the referenced details (employer, manager, tool names) are exposed on LinkedIn, a recent data breach, a leaked directory, or a prior phishing/OSINT campaign against the organization.
steps.outcome: Likely source of the reconnaissance data identified where possible.

steps.title: Notify potentially co-targeted employees
steps.desc: If other employees appear to be part of the same targeted campaign, alert them directly with the specific lure details to watch for.
steps.outcome: Co-targeted employees warned before they act on the message.

steps.title: Check whether other employees were targeted with similarly tailored messages
steps.desc: Query other user reports and mobile threat defense telemetry for the same or similar targeted lure across the organization.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope against the organization established.

ITID-11321.def: An SMS or SMS-like text message containing a link intended to install malware on the recipient's mobile device, logged before the specific delivery mechanism (fake update, malicious profile, drive-by exploit, etc.) is confirmed.
ITID-11321.purpose: Catch-all for a smishing message containing a malware-delivery link that does not yet match a more specific leaf in this Tier-4 group.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the malware-delivery mechanism is confirmed
scopeExcludes: A mechanism clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
Links that harvest credentials rather than deliver malware (Credential Harvesting Links group, ITID-11311 family)
ITID-11321.severity: Medium-High; malware delivery carries greater device-compromise risk than credential harvesting alone.
ITID-11321.priority: P2 by default given malware risk.
ITID-11321.escalation: Escalate to SOC/mobile security immediately; reclassify once the delivery mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: User-reported suspicious text with a link prompting a download/install
vectors: SMS message with a link leading to a mobile malware payload
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available at time of report
controls: Mobile threat defense
User awareness training
ITID-11321.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting and mobile threat defense telemetry.
ITID-11321.response: Isolate/wipe the affected device if malware install is confirmed; reclassify under a specific leaf once the mechanism is known.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-11321.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General SMS Malware Link
playbook.description: For a reported SMS message containing a link that leads to malware download or installation, not fitting a more specific malware-smishing sub-category.

steps.title: Preserve the message and isolate the device from further action
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and sender number; instruct the user not to open the link again and to keep the device on hand for inspection.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; user instructed to avoid further interaction.

steps.title: Isolate the device from corporate resources if malware is suspected
steps.desc: Revoke the device's access to corporate email, VPN, and SSO via MDM/conditional access pending inspection.
steps.outcome: Device access to corporate systems suspended.

steps.title: Identify and remove any installed malicious app or profile
steps.desc: Remotely uninstall the malicious app/profile via MDM, or wipe the device if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed free of the malicious payload.

steps.title: Restore device access after confirming compliance
steps.desc: Re-enable corporate resource access once the device passes a fresh MDM compliance/health check.
steps.outcome: Device restored to normal, compliant status.

steps.title: Log the malware family and delivery pattern
steps.desc: Record the lure, sender pattern, and any identified malware family for future detection tuning.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the link was opened and whether anything was installed
steps.desc: Interview the user and check MDM for new app installs, configuration profiles, or permission grants since the message was received.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether malware installation occurred.
steps.abort: If the link was never opened, skip eradication and proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the malware-hosting domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the number to the carrier's smishing channel.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

steps.title: Assess campaign scope
steps.desc: Check mobile threat defense telemetry and other user reports for the same sender/link pattern.
steps.outcome: Scope of the campaign established.

ITID-11322.def: A smishing message claiming an app or OS update is required, linking to a malicious APK for the target to sideload outside the official app store.
ITID-11322.purpose: Distinguishes smishing that lures the target into sideloading a malicious Android APK disguised as a required app update.
scopeIncludes: Android-specific sideload lures framed as an 'update' or 'security patch'
scopeExcludes: iOS configuration-profile malware delivery (a distinct leaf, ITID-11323)
Fake security/antivirus app lures (a distinct leaf, ITID-11326) even if also APK-based — this leaf is scoped to the 'update required' pretext specifically
ITID-11322.severity: High — sideloaded APKs commonly carry banking trojans or spyware with broad device permissions.
ITID-11322.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if corporate device or corporate app data is at risk.
ITID-11322.escalation: Escalate to mobile security immediately; isolate/wipe the device if install is confirmed.
indicators: APK download prompt from a non-store URL
Device requesting 'install from unknown sources' permission following a smishing link
vectors: Fake update lure directing to a malicious APK hosted outside Google Play
rootCauses: Android's ability to sideload apps outside the official store
Lack of MDM policy blocking unknown-source installs on corporate devices
controls: MDM policy disabling installs from unknown sources
Mobile threat defense app-scanning
User awareness training
ITID-11322.detection: MDM/MTD tooling on managed devices provides meaningful coverage; unmanaged personal devices have minimal visibility.
ITID-11322.response: Isolate and wipe the affected device; review for lateral exposure if corporate apps/data were present.
metrics: Count of confirmed APK sideload smishing incidents per quarter
ITID-11322.notes: Scoped narrowly to the fake-update-driven sideload pretext to avoid overlap with the fake-security-app leaf (ITID-11326), which uses a different pretext.

playbook.name: Response: Fake App Update / Sideload APK Smishing
playbook.description: For a reported SMS urging the user to install an 'urgent app update' via a direct APK download or sideload link, bypassing the official app store.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm the device platform
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and record the sender number and target platform (this lure is primarily Android-focused, relying on sideloading).
steps.outcome: Message and platform context preserved.

steps.title: Isolate the device from corporate resources
steps.desc: Revoke the device's corporate email/VPN/SSO access via MDM/conditional access pending confirmation the sideloaded app is removed.
steps.outcome: Device access suspended.

steps.title: Remove the sideloaded app and revoke its granted permissions
steps.desc: Uninstall the malicious APK via MDM where possible; if it resists removal or has device-admin/accessibility privileges, wipe the device.
steps.guidance: Malicious sideloaded apps often request Accessibility Service or Device Admin rights to resist removal — check for these grants specifically.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed free of the malicious app and its elevated permissions.
steps.abort: If the app cannot be cleanly removed or has persisted elevated access, escalate to a full device wipe/reimage.

steps.title: Restore device access after compliance check
steps.desc: Re-enable corporate resource access once the device passes a fresh compliance check.
steps.outcome: Device restored to normal, compliant status.

steps.title: Log the fake update lure and APK source
steps.desc: Record the lure content, APK hosting domain, and any malware family identified for detection tuning and awareness content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the APK was downloaded and/or installed
steps.desc: Interview the user and check MDM for installation of an app outside the managed app catalogue, and whether 'install unknown apps' permission was enabled.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether sideload installation occurred.
steps.abort: If only downloaded but not installed, proceed to remove the downloaded file and skip full eradication steps.

steps.title: Block the APK-hosting domain and report the sender
steps.desc: Add the hosting domain to the web/DNS blocklist and report the number to the carrier.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; number reported.

steps.title: Re-disable installation from unknown sources
steps.desc: Confirm the 'install unknown apps' setting is reverted to disabled per policy after remediation.
steps.outcome: Sideloading permission reverted to policy default.

steps.title: Assess campaign scope
