ITID-11432.def: An attacker posing as an executive, contacting an employee via an interactive channel (text, chat, in-person) to urgently request the purchase of gift cards on the executive's behalf, with the gift card codes to be sent back to the attacker.
ITID-11432.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretexting request specifically asking the target to purchase gift cards, scoped to interactive channels rather than a scaled email campaign.
scopeIncludes: Interactive-channel requests specifically for gift card purchases attributed to an executive
scopeExcludes: The scaled, templated email version of this same scam (a distinct ITID under Financial Fraud/BEC, ITID-53141 Unclassified/General Gift Card Scam (BEC Context))
ITID-11432.severity: Medium — typically a lower per-incident dollar loss than wire fraud, but high volume/frequency.
ITID-11432.priority: P3 default, P2 if a purchase was already completed.
ITID-11432.escalation: Escalate to finance/fraud team; attempt to halt/cancel the purchase or gift card redemption if in progress.
indicators: Urgent, secrecy-framed request to purchase gift cards attributed to an executive via text/chat
Request to photograph and send the gift card codes directly
vectors: Impersonating an executive via text/chat to request an urgent, discreet gift card purchase
rootCauses: Employees' reluctance to question a request attributed to a senior executive
No policy explicitly stating executives never request gift card purchases via text/chat
controls: Explicit policy that executives never request gift card purchases informally
Out-of-band verification requirement for any executive purchase request
User awareness training
ITID-11432.detection: Relies entirely on human reporting and financial-loss discovery after the fact.
ITID-11432.response: Attempt to halt the purchase/redemption; report to the gift card issuer's fraud team if codes were already sent.
metrics: Count of executive gift-card pretext incidents per quarter
Dollar value lost/prevented
ITID-11432.notes: Deliberately scoped to the interactive-channel version to avoid duplicating ITID-53141, which covers the scaled email-based version of this same scam.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Gift Card Purchase Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive requested that an employee urgently purchase gift cards and send the codes, a classic business-email-compromise monetization pattern.

steps.title: Determine what was purchased and whether codes were sent
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee purchased any gift cards, the amount, retailer, and whether codes/photos of the cards were already sent to the requester.
steps.guidance: Time is critical — gift card codes can be redeemed within minutes of being sent.
steps.outcome: Clear picture of financial exposure and whether codes were disclosed.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly via a known phone number to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Report the loss to finance leadership and, if warranted, law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify finance of the financial loss and file a report with local law enforcement/relevant fraud reporting body if funds cannot be recovered.
steps.outcome: Loss documented and reported through appropriate channels.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further compliance is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee, reassuring them and confirming no further purchases should be made.
steps.guidance: Avoid a punitive tone — the goal is to encourage fast future reporting, not deter it.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps and supported.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce gift-card-request awareness training
steps.desc: Record the incident and issue a reminder that legitimate executives never request gift card purchases via email/text, particularly to finance/admin staff who commonly handle such requests.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Preserve the message and sender details
steps.desc: Retain the original email/text and note the sending address or phone number.
steps.outcome: Artifact preserved for analysis and reporting.

steps.title: If codes were already sent, contact the retailer(s) immediately to attempt a freeze
steps.desc: Call the gift card issuer's fraud line right away to report the codes and request they be frozen before redemption.
steps.guidance: Success depends heavily on speed — act within minutes, not hours.
steps.outcome: Retailer notified and freeze requested, if still possible.

ITID-11433.def: An attacker posing as an executive, requesting an employee handle an urgent personal errand or favor (beyond a specific gift card, document, or approval request) as a way to establish rapport and authority pressure before a further ask.
ITID-11433.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretexting request framed as a broad, urgent personal favor rather than a specific transaction type.
scopeIncludes: Broad, open-ended personal-favor requests attributed to an executive, not matching a more specific sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Requests specifically for gift cards (ITID-11432), documents (ITID-11434), approvals (ITID-11436), or travel arrangements (ITID-11437)
ITID-11433.severity: Medium — often a rapport-building precursor to a more damaging follow-on request.
ITID-11433.escalation: Escalate to SOC if the interaction continues or escalates to a more specific damaging request.
indicators: Unusual personal-favor request attributed to an executive via text/chat, inconsistent with the executive's normal communication pattern
vectors: Building rapport/authority through a low-stakes favor request before escalating to a more damaging ask
rootCauses: Employees' natural deference to a request attributed to a senior executive
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement for any unusual executive request
User awareness training
ITID-11433.response: Verify with the real executive through a known channel; monitor for escalation to a more specific damaging request.
metrics: Count of executive personal-favor pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11433.notes: Serves as the general/rapport-building leaf in this group; a request that develops into a more specific ask should be reclassified to the matching sibling leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Urgent Task/Personal Favor Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive requested an employee perform an urgent, out-of-the-ordinary personal favor (a purchase, a wire, contacting someone on their behalf) leveraging the pressure of appearing to help a superior.

steps.title: Determine the exact favor requested and whether it was performed
steps.desc: Establish what was asked and whether the employee carried out any part of it.
steps.outcome: Clear picture of the request and compliance status.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Assess any financial or informational loss
steps.desc: Determine whether money, information, or access was actually provided as part of the favor.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further compliance is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee, reassuring them without a punitive tone.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps and supported.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce out-of-band verification for unusual executive asks
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce that any unusual, urgent, off-process request purportedly from an executive should be verified before action, regardless of seniority pressure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with an awareness reminder.

steps.title: Preserve the message and sender details
steps.desc: Retain the original communication and note the sending address/number.
steps.outcome: Artifact preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Halt or reverse any action already taken
steps.desc: Stop or undo whatever step was in progress or completed based on the fraudulent request.
steps.outcome: No fraudulent action remains in effect.

ITID-11434.def: An attacker posing as an executive, requesting an employee urgently and confidentially send sensitive internal documents, financial reports, or data.
ITID-11434.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretexting request specifically for confidential documents or data.
scopeIncludes: Requests for confidential documents/reports/data attributed to an executive
scopeExcludes: Requests for banking/payment approval specifically (ITID-11436)
Vendor-impersonation data requests (a distinct group, ITID-11415)
ITID-11434.severity: High — successful compliance can result in significant sensitive-data exposure.
ITID-11434.escalation: Escalate to SOC and data owner immediately; assess scope of any data actually disclosed.
indicators: Urgent, confidentiality-framed document request attributed to an executive via an unusual channel
Request for data outside the employee's normal reporting line to that executive
vectors: Impersonating an executive to request sensitive documents under urgency and confidentiality framing
rootCauses: Employees' deference to a senior-executive request overriding normal data-handling caution
No out-of-band verification requirement for sensitive-document requests
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement for sensitive-document requests
Data loss prevention on outbound sensitive data
User awareness training
ITID-11434.detection: DLP tooling can flag unusual outbound sensitive-data transfers; the initial request is otherwise only visible via reporting.
ITID-11434.response: Verify with the real executive before sending; if data was already disclosed, assess exposure scope and notify data owners.
metrics: Count of executive confidential-document pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11434.notes: Scoped to executive-impersonation specifically, distinct from the vendor-impersonation data-request leaf (ITID-11415).

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Confidential Document Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive requested that an employee send a confidential document (financials, HR records, strategic plans, M&A materials) directly to them or a specified external address.

steps.title: Identify the document requested and its sensitivity
steps.desc: Determine exactly what document was requested and classify its sensitivity level.
steps.outcome: Requested document and sensitivity documented.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Escalate to legal/compliance given the document's sensitivity
steps.desc: Loop in legal/compliance to assess exposure, especially for M&A, financial, or HR data with regulatory or contractual implications.
steps.outcome: Legal/compliance informed and assessing next steps.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further compliance is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee without a punitive tone.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps and supported.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce confidential-document handling policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm staff know that confidential documents require verified identity and an approved channel before being sent, regardless of claimed seniority of the requester.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process/training recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the document was already sent and to where
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee sent the document and to what address.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether disclosure occurred.

steps.title: Attempt to recall or revoke access to the sent document
steps.desc: If sent as a link, revoke sharing access; if sent as an attachment, this cannot be recalled — document the exposure as final.
steps.outcome: Access curtailed where technically possible.
steps.tool: Cloud storage admin console / mail system

ITID-11435.def: An attacker posing as an executive or their assistant, manipulating calendar entries or meeting arrangements — inserting a fake call, redirecting a real one, or altering meeting details — to create an opportunity for a further social-engineering or fraud attempt.
ITID-11435.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretext that manipulates calendar or meeting logistics to create an opportunity for a further attack.
scopeIncludes: Calendar/meeting manipulation attributed to an executive or their assistant, used to set up a further attack
scopeExcludes: Direct financial or data requests with no calendar/meeting-manipulation component (other sibling leaves)
ITID-11435.severity: Medium — primarily a setup/enabling tactic rather than the damaging action itself.
ITID-11435.priority: P3 default, reassess based on the follow-on action it enables.
ITID-11435.escalation: Escalate to SOC and monitor for the follow-on request the manipulation was designed to enable.
indicators: Unexpected calendar change or meeting-detail alteration attributed to an executive or assistant, not corresponding to the real calendar system
Meeting redirected to an unfamiliar dial-in or platform
vectors: Manipulating meeting logistics to insert an attacker into a call or redirect a real interaction
rootCauses: Calendar/meeting-change requests not verified against the real executive's known scheduling process
controls: Verification requirement for calendar/meeting changes attributed to an executive
User awareness training
ITID-11435.detection: Relies entirely on human reporting; calendar system logs may show the change but not its intent.
ITID-11435.response: Verify with the real executive/assistant; monitor closely for the follow-on attack the manipulation was designed to enable.
metrics: Count of calendar/meeting-manipulation pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11435.notes: A setup/enabling-tactic leaf; the resulting damaging action, if it occurs, should be additionally classified under the matching sibling leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Meeting/Calendar Manipulation Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive contacted an employee (often an assistant) to manipulate a meeting or calendar entry — adding an unexpected attendee, redirecting a call, or rescheduling in a way that creates an opportunity for further social engineering or eavesdropping.

steps.title: Identify the specific calendar/meeting change requested
steps.desc: Determine what change was requested — attendee added, dial-in changed, meeting moved — and which meeting.
steps.outcome: Request details documented.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they requested the change.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Assess whether any information was exposed via the manipulated meeting
steps.desc: If the unauthorized attendee actually joined a meeting before the change was caught, determine what was discussed or shared.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented, or confirmed no exposure occurred.

steps.title: Notify meeting participants if the meeting was compromised
steps.desc: If an unauthorized party joined, inform legitimate participants so they are aware of what may have been overheard.
steps.outcome: Participants informed.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce calendar-change verification for assistants
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm executive assistants/schedulers know to verify unusual calendar-change requests through a trusted channel.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a training recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the change was already made
steps.desc: Check the calendar system for whether the change was applied.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of the calendar's current state.

steps.title: Revert the calendar change and remove any unauthorized attendee or dial-in
steps.desc: Undo the change and remove any added participant or altered dial-in/link.
steps.outcome: Calendar restored to its correct, verified state.

ITID-11436.def: An attacker posing as an executive, giving a fraudulent approval or sign-off — for a transaction, an access grant, a policy exception, or a document — to unblock a process that legitimately requires that executive's authorization, where the approval is not specifically a wire-transfer authorization.
ITID-11436.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretext requesting a fraudulent approval or sign-off to unblock a process, scoped beyond payment-specific wire fraud.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent approvals for access grants, policy exceptions, non-wire transactions, or documents attributed to an executive
scopeExcludes: The specific wire-transfer-authorization live-call script (a distinct ITID under a different domain, ITID-22431 Executive Impersonation Call Authorizing Urgent Wire Transfer)
ITID-11436.severity: Medium-High — depends on what the approval unblocks; can range from a minor policy exception to significant access exposure.
ITID-11436.priority: P2 default given the authorization-bypass implications.
ITID-11436.escalation: Escalate to SOC and the relevant process owner; halt the unblocked action pending independent verification.
indicators: Approval/sign-off attributed to an executive delivered outside the organization's real approval workflow
Approval requested urgently, with pressure not to seek secondary confirmation
vectors: Impersonating an executive to provide a fraudulent approval that bypasses a required authorization step
rootCauses: Approval workflows that accept an informal message as sufficient authorization
No secondary-verification requirement for executive approvals delivered outside the formal system
controls: Formal approval workflow requiring in-system authorization, not informal message approval
Secondary-verification requirement for high-impact approvals
User awareness training
ITID-11436.detection: Relies entirely on process controls; approval-workflow logs can show whether the formal system was actually used.
ITID-11436.response: Halt the unblocked action, verify with the real executive through a known channel, and review for process gaps.
metrics: Count of fraudulent executive approval pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11436.notes: Deliberately scoped to non-wire-transfer approvals to avoid duplicating ITID-22431, which covers the specific wire-transfer-authorization live-call scenario.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Approval/Sign-off Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive provided a fraudulent approval or sign-off for a payment, contract, expense, or other action that normally requires their authorization.

steps.title: Identify the action that was fraudulently approved and its value/impact
steps.desc: Determine exactly what was approved (payment amount, contract, expense) and its financial or operational impact.
steps.outcome: Approved action and impact documented.

steps.title: Halt the action immediately if not yet executed
steps.desc: Stop any pending payment run, contract execution, or expense processing tied to the fraudulent approval.
steps.outcome: Action halted before completion, if still possible.

steps.title: If the payment/action already executed, initiate recall/recovery immediately
steps.desc: Contact the bank for a payment recall, or legal for a contract already signed, and involve finance leadership and law enforcement as warranted.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical for financial recall attempts.
steps.outcome: Recovery process initiated where possible.

steps.title: Document the true approval status and correct any downstream records
steps.desc: Ensure ERP/contract records reflect the true, verified approval status.
steps.outcome: Records accurate and consistent with the verified facts.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce dual-control/verified-approval requirements
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether high-value approvals need dual control or a verified out-of-band confirmation step.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the approved action has been executed
steps.desc: Check whether the payment was sent, the contract signed, or the expense processed based on the fraudulent approval.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of execution status.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they gave the approval.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the approval did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, allow the action to proceed.

ITID-11437.def: An attacker posing as an executive who is (supposedly) traveling and hard to reach, requesting an employee make or change travel arrangements — or use that framing to justify other unusual, hard-to-verify requests made 'while I'm away'.
ITID-11437.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretext built around a travel-arrangement request, exploiting the 'unavailable while traveling' framing.
scopeIncludes: Travel-arrangement requests attributed to an executive
Use of the 'traveling/unavailable' framing to justify difficulty in real-time verification
scopeExcludes: Requests where travel is not part of the framing (other sibling leaves)
ITID-11437.severity: Medium — travel-arrangement fraud itself is typically lower-dollar, but the 'unavailable' framing often enables larger follow-on requests.
ITID-11437.priority: P3 default, escalate if it leads to a larger follow-on request.
ITID-11437.escalation: Escalate to SOC; verify travel status with the executive's assistant or through the real travel-booking system.
indicators: Travel-arrangement request attributed to an executive not corresponding to any real booking in the organization's travel system
Explicit framing that the executive is unreachable by normal means while traveling
vectors: Using a plausible 'traveling and unreachable' cover story to justify both the request and the difficulty of verifying it
rootCauses: No requirement to verify travel-related requests against the organization's real travel-management system
controls: Verification against the real corporate travel-management system
User awareness training
ITID-11437.detection: Relies entirely on human reporting; the real travel system can confirm or refute the claimed trip.
ITID-11437.response: Verify against the real travel-management system; treat as elevated risk if it leads to a further, harder-to-verify request.
metrics: Count of executive travel-pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11437.notes: Distinguished from other sibling leaves by the specific 'traveling and unreachable' framing used to justify the request and to suppress verification.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Travel Arrangement Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive requested urgent travel arrangements (flights, hotel, a booking payment) be made through an employee, often used to extract payment card details or push a fraudulent charge.

steps.title: Identify what was requested and whether payment details were shared
steps.desc: Determine what travel arrangement was requested and whether any payment card or account details were disclosed as part of it.
steps.outcome: Clear picture of the request and any disclosure.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, proceed through the normal corporate travel process.

steps.title: Review the card/account for any unauthorized charges
steps.desc: Check for any other charges made using the disclosed payment details.
steps.outcome: No unauthorized charges found, or charges identified and disputed.

steps.title: Rebook legitimate travel through the verified corporate travel process, if applicable
steps.desc: If genuine travel is needed, arrange it through the standard verified corporate travel channel.
steps.outcome: Legitimate travel arranged securely if applicable.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce travel-request verification policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm staff who arrange executive travel know to verify unusual or urgent requests through a trusted channel.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a training recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether a booking or payment was already made
steps.desc: Check whether the employee actually booked travel or processed a payment.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of financial exposure.

steps.title: Cancel any fraudulent booking and freeze/reissue any exposed payment card
steps.desc: Cancel bookings made under the false request and, if a corporate card number was disclosed, have finance freeze and reissue it.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent booking canceled; exposed card secured.

ITID-11438.def: An attacker posing as an executive, whose primary tactic is an explicit insistence on confidentiality or secrecy ('don't tell anyone', 'don't call me, I'll call you', 'keep this between us') used specifically to suppress the target's normal instinct to verify the request through another channel.
ITID-11438.purpose: Flags executive-impersonation pretexts where the notable, classification-driving feature is an explicit demand for secrecy that suppresses normal verification, cutting across the request content itself.
scopeIncludes: Cases where an explicit secrecy/no-verification demand is the dominant, classification-driving tactic, regardless of the underlying request content
scopeExcludes: Cases where secrecy framing is incidental and the request content is clear — classify under the specific request-type leaf instead
ITID-11438.severity: High — an explicit demand to avoid verification is one of the strongest indicators of social-engineering intent.
ITID-11438.priority: P2 default given the elevated-risk framing.
ITID-11438.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately; treat any 'don't verify this' instruction as a strong red flag requiring verification precisely because it was told not to.
indicators: Explicit instruction not to discuss the request with colleagues or to verify it through normal channels
Request framed as highly sensitive or confidential specifically to justify bypassing verification
vectors: Explicit secrecy demands designed to prevent the target from cross-checking the request
rootCauses: No mandatory policy stating that a request to avoid verification is itself grounds for verification
Employees' deference to confidentiality framing from a senior executive
controls: Explicit policy that a request to bypass verification must itself trigger verification
User awareness training on secrecy-based social engineering
ITID-11438.detection: Relies entirely on staff recognizing and reporting the secrecy-demand pattern; no technical detection surface.
ITID-11438.response: Verify the request through an independent channel regardless of the secrecy instruction; escalate to SOC.
metrics: Count of secrecy-demand-framed executive pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11438.notes: A tactic-axis leaf, used only when the secrecy/no-verification demand itself is the notable classification driver rather than a specific request type.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Confidentiality/Secrecy Demand Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive coupled a fraudulent request with an explicit demand for secrecy ('don't discuss this with anyone,' 'confidential deal, don't loop in finance') specifically to prevent the employee from seeking verification.

steps.title: Capture the request and the specific secrecy demand made
steps.desc: Record what was requested and exactly how the secrecy instruction was framed (e.g. legal reasons, deal confidentiality, personal privacy).
steps.guidance: An explicit instruction to bypass normal colleagues/approval is itself one of the strongest indicators of this fraud type — flag it prominently.
steps.outcome: Request and secrecy framing documented.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel — explicitly overriding the secrecy instruction
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they made the request; a genuine confidentiality need does not preclude verifying identity through a trusted channel.
steps.guidance: Make clear in security awareness material that verification is never the confidentiality breach the attacker claims it would be.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, respect any legitimate confidentiality requirements going forward through proper channels.

steps.title: Assess any financial or informational loss
steps.desc: Determine whether money, access, or information was disclosed as a result of complying under the secrecy instruction.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further compliance or secrecy is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee, explicitly reassuring them that raising it internally was correct despite the instruction to stay silent.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps and supported, without a punitive tone.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce that secrecy demands are a red flag, not a valid reason to skip verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and issue awareness material specifically calling out 'keep this confidential/don't tell anyone' instructions as a common fraud tactic requiring extra scrutiny, not compliance.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Determine whether any action was taken while under the secrecy instruction
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee complied with any part of the request without consulting others, as instructed.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether any compromise already occurred.

steps.title: Reverse or halt any action taken on the fraudulent request
steps.desc: If any step was completed, reverse or halt it immediately.
steps.outcome: No fraudulent action remains in effect.

ITID-11439.def: An attacker posing as an executive, claiming to be locked out or without access, asking an employee to share their own account credentials, badge access, or perform an action on the executive's behalf using the employee's own access.
ITID-11439.purpose: Distinguishes an executive-impersonation pretext specifically requesting the target share their own account access, credentials, or badge on the executive's behalf.
scopeIncludes: Requests for the employee to use or share their own access/credentials/badge 'on behalf of' the executive
scopeExcludes: Requests for vendor credential sharing (a distinct group, ITID-11412)
ITID-11439.severity: High — results in the employee's own access being directly used for an unauthorized purpose, complicating attribution.
ITID-11439.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if access/credentials were actually shared or used.
ITID-11439.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IAM immediately; reset the employee's credentials and review activity performed under their access.
indicators: Request for the employee to log in on the executive's behalf or physically badge someone in, attributed to a locked-out executive
Request made outside the executive's normal access-recovery process
vectors: Impersonating a locked-out executive to convince an employee to use their own access on the executive's behalf
rootCauses: No formal, verifiable account/access-recovery process for executives that avoids reliance on informal peer assistance
Employees' deference to a senior-executive request overriding standard access-sharing prohibitions
controls: Formal, verifiable executive access-recovery process not reliant on informal peer assistance
Explicit policy prohibiting credential/badge sharing under any circumstance
User awareness training
ITID-11439.detection: Access logs can show anomalous use of the employee's credentials/badge if the request was acted upon.
ITID-11439.response: Reset the employee's credentials, review all activity performed under their access during the relevant window, and treat as a potential account-compromise event.
metrics: Count of executive access-sharing pretext incidents per quarter
ITID-11439.notes: Scoped to executive-impersonation specifically; the vendor-impersonation credential-sharing equivalent is tracked under ITID-11412.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Access/Credential Sharing Request
playbook.description: For an incident where someone impersonating a senior executive requested that an employee share their own system access, login credentials, or grant the 'executive' temporary access to an account or system.

steps.title: Identify what access/credential was requested
steps.desc: Determine exactly what system access or credential was requested to be shared or granted.
steps.outcome: Requested access documented.

steps.title: Force a password reset and revoke any access granted
steps.desc: Reset the employee's credentials and revoke any access or permissions extended to the fraudulent requester, regardless of confirmation status, given the risk.
steps.outcome: Account secured and unauthorized access removed.

steps.title: Review account activity for unauthorized use
steps.desc: Check login and activity logs for the account for any use by an unauthorized party before access was revoked.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized use occurred, or unauthorized use identified and escalated as an account-compromise incident.

steps.title: Restore the employee's access with new credentials
steps.desc: Ensure the employee has working access restored securely.
steps.outcome: Employee access restored.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce that credentials/access are never shared, even with claimed executives
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce that legitimate access needs are provisioned through IAM, not by sharing personal credentials with anyone, including apparent leadership.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Determine whether access or credentials were already shared
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee disclosed a password, granted account access, or shared a session before recognizing the request as suspicious.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether compromise already occurred.

steps.title: Verify with the real executive through a separate, known channel
steps.desc: Contact the executive directly to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the request did not originate from the real executive.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, provision access through the standard verified process instead of credential sharing.

ITID-11511.def: An unsolicited offer of a reward, prize, gift, or benefit used as a pretext to get the target to click a link, share information, pay a fee, or take an action, without enough detail captured to classify it under a more specific incentive type.
ITID-11511.purpose: Catch-all for a fake incentive/reward pretext used to extract information, payment, or access that does not fit a more specific leaf under Fake Incentives.
scopeIncludes: Reports of an incentive-based lure logged before the specific incentive type is confirmed
Fake incentive pretexts that mix multiple incentive types (e.g., prize + loyalty points) with no single dominant type
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (prize notification, survey reward, free gift, etc.) once detail is available
Tech support-branded incentive offers, which belong under Tech Support Scams
ITID-11511.severity: Low-to-Medium by default; reassess once the specific incentive mechanism is known.
ITID-11511.priority: P3 by default, escalating if payment or credentials were actually surrendered.
ITID-11511.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassification once more detail is available; escalate immediately if any financial loss or credential disclosure occurred.
indicators: Unsolicited message offering a reward for an action
Urgency or a deadline attached to claiming the incentive
vectors: Email or message offering an unspecified reward in exchange for a click or a form submission
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
General susceptibility to reward-based social engineering
controls: Security awareness training on unsolicited reward offers
Email/link filtering
ITID-11511.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting; limited automated signal for a generic incentive lure.
ITID-11511.response: Document, attempt to reclassify against a more specific leaf, and advise the reporter not to act on the offer.
metrics: Count of incentive-pretext reports pending reclassification
ITID-11511.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the incentive type is known.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Incentive Offer
playbook.description: For a report of an employee being offered an incentive (prize, reward, discount, gift) in exchange for information or an action, where the specific type of incentive scam is not yet known.

steps.title: Capture the report details from the employee who was contacted
steps.desc: Record the contact channel, the offer made, what was requested in exchange, and any link/sender used.
steps.outcome: A documented account of the offer and request.

steps.title: Reset any credentials or information disclosed
steps.desc: If the employee entered a password, personal details, or corporate information, treat it as compromised and reset/rotate accordingly.
steps.outcome: Any disclosed credentials or information secured.

steps.title: Check for similar offers reaching other employees
steps.desc: Search mail/messaging logs for the same or similar offer sent to other staff.
steps.outcome: Scope of the campaign against the organization established.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further engagement is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the reporting employee.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue awareness reminder if broadly targeted
steps.desc: Record the incident and, if multiple employees were targeted, issue an organization-wide awareness note.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness action taken if warranted.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee engaged with the offer
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee clicked a link, provided information, or completed any requested action.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether any exposure occurred.

steps.title: Block the associated link/domain/sender where feasible
steps.desc: Add the offer's link, domain, or sender to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access to the malicious offer blocked for other employees.

ITID-11512.def: A message notifying the target that they have won a prize, lottery, or sweepstakes they never entered, requiring them to pay a fee, provide personal/financial details, or click a link to 'claim' the winnings.
ITID-11512.purpose: Captures the classic 'you've won' lure, where a fabricated prize or sweepstakes win is used to extract fees, personal data, or credentials.
scopeIncludes: Fake lottery/sweepstakes win notifications by any channel (email, SMS, call)
Requests for an upfront 'processing fee' or tax payment to release a fictitious prize
scopeExcludes: A prize/contest lure specifically delivered as a social media post or comment (see ITID-21244, Fake Giveaway/Contest Scam Link Post)
Fake reward tied to completing a survey (see ITID-11513)
ITID-11512.severity: Medium if a fee or financial detail was requested; High if payment was made.
ITID-11512.priority: P2 if any payment or financial information was disclosed, otherwise P3.
ITID-11512.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance teams immediately if a payment was made or financial account details were shared.
indicators: Notification of winning a prize/lottery the recipient never entered
Request for an upfront fee to release winnings
Urgency to respond within a short deadline
vectors: Mass unsolicited email or SMS claiming a prize win
Spoofed sweepstakes-brand sender identity
rootCauses: Lack of awareness that legitimate sweepstakes never require an upfront fee
No verification path publicized for confirming legitimate prize communications
controls: Security awareness training on prize/lottery scams
Financial-loss reporting channel
ITID-11512.detection: Relies mainly on user reporting; email gateway reputation filtering catches some mass campaigns.
ITID-11512.response: Advise the target not to pay or share details; report and block the sending domain/number where possible.
metrics: Count of prize/sweepstakes lures reported per quarter
Count resulting in financial loss
ITID-11512.notes: Scoped to direct prize/lottery win notifications; a prize lure delivered via a social media contest post is tracked separately under ITID-21244 to avoid double-counting the same pattern across two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Prize/Sweepstakes Win Notification
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee received a notification claiming they won a prize or sweepstakes they never entered, designed to lure them into providing personal/financial information or clicking a malicious link to 'claim' the prize.

steps.title: Capture the notification details and claimed prize
steps.desc: Record the channel, claimed prize, sponsor named, and any link or contact info provided to 'claim' it.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Reset any credentials or personal/financial information disclosed
steps.desc: If any information was entered on a claim form/site, treat as compromised and reset/rotate as applicable.
steps.outcome: Disclosed information/credentials secured.

steps.title: Check whether the notification was sent to multiple employees
steps.desc: Search mail logs for the same notification reaching other staff, indicating a mass campaign rather than a targeted one.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

steps.title: Advise the employee to monitor accounts if personal/financial data was shared
steps.desc: If personal or financial details were disclosed, advise the employee to monitor their own accounts/credit and report if company-issued payment instruments were involved.
steps.outcome: Employee aware of personal follow-up steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue a broad awareness reminder
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff that unsolicited prize notifications are a common phishing vector.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee interacted with the claim process
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee clicked the link, entered information, or made contact to claim the prize.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of engagement level.

steps.title: Block the claim link/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the link/domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

ITID-11513.def: A message offering a reward (cash, gift card, points) in exchange for completing a survey, where the survey itself is a pretext to harvest personal/financial data or redirect the target to a malicious site.
ITID-11513.purpose: Captures a fake 'complete this survey and get rewarded' lure used to harvest personal data or install malware.
scopeIncludes: Fake customer-satisfaction or brand surveys promising a reward on completion
Survey forms that harvest excessive personal/financial data beyond what a legitimate survey would need
scopeExcludes: Fake prize/sweepstakes win notifications with no survey component (see ITID-11512)
Fake loyalty program point offers (see ITID-11516)
ITID-11513.severity: Low-to-Medium; escalate if the survey collects payment card or credential data.
ITID-11513.priority: P3 by default, P2 if financial data was submitted.
ITID-11513.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance if payment data was disclosed via the fake survey form.
indicators: Unsolicited survey link promising a reward
Survey requesting payment card details to 'process' a reward
vectors: Email/SMS/social ad linking to a fake branded survey form
Spoofed retailer or brand survey invitation
rootCauses: Recipients unable to distinguish a legitimate market-research survey from a spoofed one
No published list of legitimate active surveys for major brands
mitreTechniques: T1598.003 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Link
controls: Security awareness training
URL/link reputation filtering
ITID-11513.detection: Relies mainly on user reporting; some coverage from web-filtering categorization of known fake-survey domains.
ITID-11513.response: Advise against submitting data; report and request domain takedown/blocking where the brand is impersonated.
metrics: Count of fake survey reward reports per quarter
ITID-11513.notes: Distinguished from prize/sweepstakes and loyalty-point offers by the survey-completion mechanism as the reward trigger.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Survey Reward Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee was offered a reward or payment for completing a survey that was actually a vehicle for harvesting personal/corporate information or credentials.

steps.title: Capture the survey link, claimed sponsor, and offered reward
steps.desc: Record the survey link/platform, who it claimed to be from, and what reward was offered.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Reset any credentials disclosed as part of the survey
steps.desc: If login credentials were requested/entered under the guise of 'verifying eligibility,' reset them immediately.
steps.outcome: Disclosed credentials secured.

steps.title: Assess whether corporate information was disclosed in survey answers
steps.desc: Review the survey questions and the employee's answers for any exposure of internal processes, org structure, or systems.
steps.outcome: Corporate information exposure assessed.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further engagement is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an awareness reminder about survey scams
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff to be cautious of unsolicited paid surveys, particularly those requesting login credentials.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Determine what information the employee provided in the survey
steps.desc: Establish what questions were answered and whether any personal, financial, or corporate information was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Disclosure scope established.

steps.title: Block the survey link/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the link/domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

ITID-11514.def: An unsolicited offer of a free product, gift, or sample requiring the target to pay a small shipping fee or provide personal/payment details to receive it.
ITID-11514.purpose: Captures a fake free-gift or product-sample offer used as bait to harvest shipping/personal/payment data.
scopeIncludes: Fake free product/sample offers requiring a 'shipping and handling' payment
Free-gift offers used to enroll the target in an undisclosed recurring subscription
scopeExcludes: Free software/service trial offers (see ITID-11519)
Fake charity donation match offers (see ITID-11517)
ITID-11514.severity: Low-to-Medium; escalate if recurring/undisclosed charges are confirmed.
ITID-11514.priority: P3 by default, P2 if card data was captured for a recurring charge scheme.
ITID-11514.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance if a card was charged beyond the disclosed shipping fee.
indicators: Offer of a free product for a small payment
Fine-print recurring subscription terms
vectors: Social media ad or email offering a free sample for a nominal fee
Fake brand giveaway landing page collecting card details
rootCauses: Ad-platform vetting gaps allowing fraudulent free-gift ads
Recipients not reading fine-print subscription terms
controls: Security awareness training
Corporate card monitoring for unrecognized recurring charges
ITID-11514.detection: Relies mainly on user/financial-institution reporting after a charge is noticed.
ITID-11514.response: Advise on disputing charges with the card issuer; document the offending domain/advertiser.
metrics: Count of free-gift/sample scam reports
Count resulting in recurring-charge fraud
ITID-11514.notes: Scoped to the free-product/sample pretext specifically; a general free-trial software offer is tracked separately under ITID-11519.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Free Gift/Product Sample Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee was offered a free gift or product sample requiring them to provide shipping/personal information, click a link, or install an app to 'claim' it, potentially exposing personal data or delivering malware.

steps.title: Capture the offer details and claimed sponsor
steps.desc: Record the channel, claimed product/brand, and what action was required to claim the gift.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint if anything was installed
steps.desc: Disconnect or isolate the device via EDR if an app or file was installed as part of the claim process.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated pending inspection.

steps.title: Scan the endpoint if anything was installed
steps.desc: Run a full malware scan and remediate if anything malicious is found.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean or fully remediated.

steps.title: Restore the endpoint to service if it was isolated
steps.desc: Return the cleaned endpoint to normal use once confirmed safe.
steps.outcome: Endpoint restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an awareness reminder about free-gift scams
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff that unsolicited free-gift offers requiring app installs or personal info are a common lure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Determine what the employee did in response
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee provided information, clicked a link, or installed anything.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of engagement level.

steps.title: Block the offer link/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the link/domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

ITID-11515.def: A message impersonating an internal HR/rewards program, notifying an employee of a recognition award or bonus and directing them to a fake portal to 'claim' it, harvesting credentials or banking details.
ITID-11515.purpose: Captures a fake internal employee-recognition or rewards-program message used to phish corporate credentials or payment data.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'employee of the month' or peer-recognition award notifications linking to a credential-harvesting portal
Fake internal bonus/award claim forms requesting banking details
scopeExcludes: Fake job referral bonus offers (see ITID-11518)
Fake loyalty program point offers aimed at customers rather than employees (see ITID-11516)
ITID-11515.severity: Medium-High given the internal/corporate targeting and credential-harvest risk.
ITID-11515.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if corporate SSO credentials were entered.
ITID-11515.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately if corporate credentials were submitted to the fake portal; escalate to HR to confirm no legitimate program matches the claim.
indicators: Unexpected recognition/award email referencing an internal program
Link to a portal outside known corporate domains requesting SSO credentials
vectors: Spoofed internal HR sender phishing for SSO credentials via a fake rewards portal
Fake bonus claim form requesting direct-deposit banking details
rootCauses: Employees unfamiliar with the organization's actual recognition program branding/domains
No published list of legitimate reward-program URLs
controls: SSO domain allow-listing/awareness
Email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) enforcement
Security awareness training
ITID-11515.detection: Email security gateway can flag look-alike domains impersonating HR; credential-entry attempts are visible in SSO logs if the target domain is known.
ITID-11515.response: Force password reset and review SSO logs immediately if credentials were entered; block the phishing domain.
metrics: Count of fake internal-reward phishing reports
Count resulting in credential submission
ITID-11515.notes: Distinguished from ITID-11518 (job referral bonus) by targeting an existing employee's recognition/rewards claim rather than a referral payout.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Employee Recognition/Rewards Program Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee received a message impersonating the company's internal recognition or rewards program, directing them to a fake portal to 'redeem' points — designed to harvest corporate login credentials.

steps.title: Capture the message details and the portal/link presented
steps.desc: Record the sender, the claimed rewards program name, and the link presented to redeem points.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Force a password reset if credentials were entered
steps.desc: Reset the employee's corporate credentials immediately if there is any chance they were entered on the fake portal.
steps.outcome: Account secured with a new credential.

steps.title: Review account activity for unauthorized access
steps.desc: Check login/activity logs for the account for any unauthorized use before the reset.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized use occurred, or use identified and escalated as an account-compromise incident.

steps.title: Restore the employee's access with a new credential
steps.desc: Ensure the employee has working access restored securely.
steps.outcome: Employee access restored.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an organization-wide awareness alert
steps.desc: Record the incident and alert all staff to the fake rewards-program phishing campaign, describing the exact lure used.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; organization-wide alert issued.

steps.title: Confirm whether the company has a genuine matching program
steps.desc: Check with HR/the actual program administrator whether this matches a real internal program and communication.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message is not a genuine internal communication.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Block the fake portal link/domain and report the phishing campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list and, where feasible, report the site for takedown.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

steps.title: Search for and remove the same phishing message from other mailboxes
steps.desc: Search organization-wide mail for the same message and remove it before other employees engage.
steps.outcome: Message removed from other mailboxes where found.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee entered credentials on the fake portal
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee attempted to log in with their corporate credentials on the linked site.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether credentials were disclosed.

ITID-11516.def: A message claiming the target's loyalty program points are expiring or can be redeemed for a discount, directing them to a fake login/redemption page that harvests account credentials or card data.
ITID-11516.purpose: Captures a fake loyalty-program points or discount offer used to harvest account credentials or payment data from customers/employees.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'your points are expiring' notifications linking to a spoofed loyalty-program login page
Fake discount-redemption pages requesting card details to 'unlock' a loyalty discount
scopeExcludes: Fake employee recognition/rewards claims (see ITID-11515)
Fake free-gift/sample offers (see ITID-11514)
ITID-11516.severity: Low-to-Medium; escalate if the loyalty account is linked to stored payment methods.
ITID-11516.priority: P3 by default, P2 if payment-linked account credentials were disclosed.
ITID-11516.escalation: Escalate to the brand's fraud team and advise credential reset if the loyalty account login was submitted.
indicators: Urgent 'points expiring' messaging
Look-alike domain for a known loyalty program
vectors: Spoofed loyalty-program email/SMS with a credential-harvesting link
Fake QR code on a printed flyer linking to a loyalty scam page
rootCauses: Point-expiry urgency exploited without user verification habits
No brand-published list of legitimate loyalty-program domains
controls: Web/URL reputation filtering
Security awareness training
ITID-11516.detection: Limited to user reporting and web-filtering categorization of the spoofed domain.
ITID-11516.response: Advise credential reset for the loyalty account; report the spoofed domain for takedown.
metrics: Count of fake loyalty-program lure reports per quarter
ITID-11516.notes: Scoped to loyalty-point/discount redemption pretexts specifically, distinct from generic free-gift or employee-reward pretexts.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Loyalty Program Points/Discount Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee received a message impersonating a retailer/airline/vendor loyalty program claiming points are expiring or a discount is available, directing them to a fake site to 'log in and redeem' — a common credential-harvesting or payment-card-skimming lure.

steps.title: Capture the message details and impersonated brand
steps.desc: Record the sender, the claimed loyalty program/brand, and the link presented.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Reset the affected account credential and notify the card issuer if payment details were entered
steps.desc: Reset the password on the affected account, and if a corporate card was entered, have finance freeze/reissue it.
steps.outcome: Account and any exposed payment instrument secured.

steps.title: Review the account/card for unauthorized use
steps.desc: Check for any unauthorized redemption, charge, or login on the affected account.
steps.outcome: No unauthorized use found, or use identified and disputed/reported.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further engagement is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an awareness reminder about loyalty-program phishing
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff to navigate directly to loyalty program sites rather than clicking emailed links, especially where corporate travel accounts are involved.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee entered credentials or payment details
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee logged in or entered payment card details on the linked site.
steps.guidance: Note whether this was a personal account or one linked to corporate travel/expense programs.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of what was disclosed and to which account type.

steps.title: Block the fake site link/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the link/domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

ITID-11517.def: A message claiming an employer, vendor, or public figure will 'match' the target's charitable donation, directing them to donate through a fraudulent portal that pockets the funds instead of forwarding them.
ITID-11517.purpose: Captures a fake charity donation-match offer used to redirect legitimate charitable giving to a fraudulent recipient.
scopeIncludes: Fake corporate donation-matching campaign notifications linking to a fraudulent donation portal
Impersonation of a known charity's matching-gift program
scopeExcludes: Fake free-gift/product sample offers (see ITID-11514)
General charity-impersonation fraud that makes no donation-match claim (tracked elsewhere under fraud/scam ITIDs outside this branch)
ITID-11517.severity: Medium; reputational and financial impact if employees/customers donate believing the organization is matching funds.
ITID-11517.priority: P2 given potential brand-reputation and financial-fraud impact.
ITID-11517.escalation: Escalate to legal/communications and finance if the organization's name is being used without authorization to solicit donations.
indicators: Donation-match claim referencing the organization's name without a corresponding real program
Payment portal outside known corporate/charity donation domains
vectors: Spoofed internal email announcing a fake donation-match drive
Fraudulent social media post citing a fake corporate match program
rootCauses: No centrally published, verifiable list of active corporate donation-match campaigns
Brand impersonation not proactively monitored
controls: Brand/domain monitoring for impersonation
Security awareness training
ITID-11517.detection: Relies on user/employee reporting and periodic brand-impersonation monitoring; limited automated technical signal.
ITID-11517.response: Issue a corrective notice confirming legitimate match-program details; request takedown of the fraudulent portal.
metrics: Count of fake donation-match reports
Count of confirmed brand-impersonation takedowns
ITID-11517.notes: Scoped specifically to the donation-matching pretext; broader charity-brand impersonation without a matching claim sits outside this ITID's scope.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Charity Donation Match Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee was targeted with a fake company charity-matching or donation-drive offer, directing them to donate/enter payment or personal information through a fraudulent site posing as an internal giving campaign.

steps.title: Capture the message details and claimed campaign
steps.desc: Record the sender, the claimed charity/matching campaign, and the link or payment method presented.
steps.outcome: Offer details documented.

steps.title: Advise the employee to contact their card issuer if payment was made
steps.desc: If the employee donated with a personal or corporate card, have them (or finance, for corporate cards) dispute the charge and monitor for further unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Card issuer notified and dispute initiated where applicable.

steps.title: Search for and remove the same message from other mailboxes
steps.desc: Search organization-wide mail for the same message and remove it before other employees engage.
steps.outcome: Message removed from other mailboxes where found.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further engagement is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an awareness reminder ahead of the next real giving campaign
steps.desc: Record the incident and, ahead of any genuine company giving campaign, pre-warn staff of the official channel it will use.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Confirm whether the company has a genuine matching campaign active
steps.desc: Check with HR/corporate social responsibility team whether this matches a real, currently active giving campaign.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message is not a genuine internal communication.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Block the fake campaign link/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the link/domain to the mail gateway/web filter block list.
steps.outcome: Further access blocked for other employees.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee donated or disclosed payment/personal information
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee made a donation or entered information on the fake site.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of any financial or information exposure.

ITID-11518.def: A message claiming the target is owed a referral bonus for a job candidate they referred, directing them to a fake HR portal to 'confirm' banking or identity details to receive payment.
ITID-11518.purpose: Captures a fake job-referral-bonus offer used to phish an employee's credentials or personal/banking data.
scopeIncludes: Fake referral-bonus payout confirmation emails linking to a spoofed HR/payroll portal
Requests for banking/tax-ID details to 'process' a fictitious referral payment
scopeExcludes: Fake employee recognition/rewards program offers unrelated to a referral (see ITID-11515)
Fake recruiter DM offering a job, not a referral bonus (see ITID-11724)
ITID-11518.severity: Medium-High given the direct request for banking/tax-ID data.
ITID-11518.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if banking details were submitted.
ITID-11518.escalation: Escalate to HR/payroll and finance immediately to confirm no legitimate referral payout matches the claim, and to flag any submitted banking details.
indicators: Referral bonus claim for a candidate the employee does not recall referring
Portal outside known payroll/HR domains requesting bank account details
vectors: Spoofed payroll/HR email requesting banking details to process a referral bonus
Fake internal portal harvesting SSO credentials under a referral-bonus pretext
rootCauses: Employees unfamiliar with the actual referral program's payout process/timing
No published verification path for referral bonus status
controls: Email authentication enforcement
Security awareness training
Payroll-change verification callback procedure
ITID-11518.detection: Email gateway can flag spoofed payroll domains; SSO logs show credential-entry attempts if the fake portal harvests SSO.
ITID-11518.response: Verify with HR/payroll before any payout action; force credential reset if SSO was entered on the fake portal.
metrics: Count of fake referral-bonus phishing reports
Count resulting in banking-detail disclosure
ITID-11518.notes: Distinguished from ITID-11515 by the specific referral-bonus payout pretext rather than a general recognition award.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Job Referral Bonus Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee was contacted with a fake offer to earn a referral bonus for providing candidate names, employee contacts, or personal information about coworkers, exploiting the legitimacy of real employee-referral programs.

steps.title: Capture the message details and what information was requested
steps.desc: Record the sender, the claimed referral program, and exactly what information (candidate names, coworker contacts, org details) was requested.
steps.outcome: Offer and requested data documented.

steps.title: Block the sender/domain where feasible
steps.desc: Add the sender/domain to the mail gateway block list.
steps.outcome: Further contact blocked for other employees.

steps.title: Notify any coworkers whose information was disclosed
steps.desc: If specific individuals' names or contact details were shared, inform them their information may have been exposed.
steps.outcome: Affected coworkers notified.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee that no further engagement is expected
steps.desc: Close the loop with the employee.
steps.outcome: Employee clear on next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and issue an awareness reminder about referral-bonus scams
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff that legitimate referral bonuses are processed through the HR system, not by emailing coworker details to an outside party.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Confirm whether this matches a genuine internal referral program
steps.desc: Check with HR/recruiting whether this matches a real, currently active referral program and communication.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message is not a genuine internal communication.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine what information the employee actually provided
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee shared any coworker names, contact details, or internal information in response.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of disclosure scope.

ITID-11519.def: An offer of a free trial for a software product or online service that requires payment-card registration and either bills the target without proper disclosure or delivers a malicious installer/app instead of the advertised product.
ITID-11519.purpose: Captures a fake free-trial offer for software or a service used to harvest payment card data or install malware under the guise of a legitimate trial.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'free trial, cancel anytime' offers that immediately or covertly charge the card provided
Free-trial sign-up pages used purely to harvest card data with no functioning product behind them
scopeExcludes: Cases where the trial sign-up itself is legitimate but the delivered installer is malicious (see ITID-11627, Fake Software Update/Installer Download, under Fake Downloads) — this ITID covers the payment/registration pretext, not the malicious file delivery mechanism
Fake free-gift/physical-product sample offers (see ITID-11514)
ITID-11519.severity: Low-to-Medium; escalate if recurring undisclosed charges are confirmed at scale.
ITID-11519.priority: P3 by default, P2 if a corporate card was used and charged fraudulently.
ITID-11519.escalation: Escalate to finance for corporate-card disputes; escalate to procurement/security if the 'trial' is for a business tool requesting broad account permissions.
indicators: Trial sign-up requiring full card details with vague cancellation terms
Unexpected recurring charge after a 'free trial' period
vectors: Fake SaaS/tool landing page advertised via search ads or social media
Trial sign-up form harvesting card data with no functioning backend service
rootCauses: Lack of scrutiny of unfamiliar SaaS vendors before card entry
No corporate policy requiring procurement review before trial sign-ups on company cards
controls: Corporate card monitoring for unrecognized recurring charges
Procurement review requirement for new SaaS trials
ITID-11519.detection: Relies mainly on card-issuer/finance monitoring after a charge is noticed; limited proactive technical signal.
ITID-11519.response: Assist with card dispute; flag the vendor for procurement/security review.
metrics: Count of fake free-trial billing-fraud reports per quarter
ITID-11519.notes: Scope decision: this ITID covers the payment-pretext/billing-fraud side of a fake trial offer; a malicious installer delivered under a fake update/trial pretext is classified under ITID-11627 in the Fake Downloads Type to avoid double-counting the same incident under two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Software/Service Free Trial Offer
playbook.description: For an incident where an employee was offered a free trial of a business tool/service requiring installation or account setup with corporate credentials, used as a lure to deliver malware or harvest credentials via a fake or malicious application.

steps.title: Identify the software/service offered and what was installed or entered
steps.desc: Determine the name of the trial software/service, and whether it was installed or corporate credentials were used to sign up.
steps.outcome: Offer and employee action documented.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint if the software was installed
steps.desc: Disconnect or isolate the device via EDR pending inspection.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated to prevent further compromise.

steps.title: Scan and remediate the endpoint
steps.desc: Run a full malware scan and remediate/reimage if anything malicious is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean or fully remediated.

steps.title: Restore the endpoint and account to normal service
steps.desc: Return the cleaned endpoint and reset account to normal use once confirmed safe.
steps.outcome: Endpoint and account restored.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce the approved-software request process
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff that new software/trials should be requested and vetted through IT/procurement, not installed directly from an unsolicited offer.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process/training recommendation.

steps.title: Check whether this is a known/approved tool via IT's software catalog
steps.desc: Check with IT/procurement whether this software is a recognized, vetted tool or entirely unknown.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the tool is legitimate and approved.
steps.abort: If confirmed as a legitimate, approved tool being trialed through proper channels, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Reset any corporate credentials used to sign up
steps.desc: If corporate email/credentials were used to register for the trial, reset the password and review OAuth/app permissions granted.
steps.guidance: Check for any OAuth grant to the third-party app that may need to be revoked, in addition to a password reset.
steps.outcome: Credentials secured; any excess OAuth access revoked.

steps.title: Review account activity for unauthorized access via the trial signup
steps.desc: Check logs for any unauthorized use of the account or data accessed by the trial application.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized use occurred, or use identified and escalated.

ITID-11521.def: An attacker posing as legitimate technical support convinces the target their device has a problem requiring paid assistance, remote access, or software installation, without enough detail captured to classify the initiation vector.
ITID-11521.purpose: Catch-all for a tech support scam that does not fit a more specific leaf under Tech Support Scams.
scopeIncludes: Tech support scam reports logged before the initiation mechanism (pop-up, cold call, remote session, etc.) is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the initiation vector is known
Internal IT/help-desk credential-verification pretexts (see ITID-11421, ITID-11428, under Pretexting)
ITID-11521.severity: Medium by default; reassess once the initiation vector and any access/payment granted are known.
ITID-11521.priority: P2 by default given the risk of remote-access compromise.
ITID-11521.escalation: Escalate immediately if remote access was granted or payment was made.
indicators: Report of an unsolicited tech support contact
Request for remote access or payment to 'fix' a device
vectors: Unsolicited tech support contact by unclear channel
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Security awareness training on tech support scams
ITID-11521.response: Document and attempt to reclassify against a more specific leaf.
metrics: Count of tech support scam reports pending reclassification
ITID-11521.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Distinct from ITID-11421/ITID-11428, which cover an attacker impersonating a company's own internal IT/help-desk to harvest employee credentials rather than a consumer-style unsolicited support scam.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Tech Support Scam
playbook.description: For a report of an employee being contacted by or contacting someone claiming to be tech support offering to fix a problem, where the specific initiation method (pop-up, cold call, refund claim, etc.) is not yet known.

steps.title: Capture the report details from the employee
steps.desc: Record how contact was initiated, what problem was claimed, and what the 'technician' asked the employee to do.
steps.outcome: A documented account of the scam interaction.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint if any access was granted or software installed
steps.desc: Disconnect or isolate the device via EDR pending inspection.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated to prevent further compromise.

steps.title: Scan and remediate the endpoint if compromise is suspected
steps.desc: Run a full malware scan and remediate/reimage if anything malicious is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean or fully remediated.

steps.title: Restore the endpoint to service once confirmed safe
steps.desc: Return the cleaned endpoint to normal use.
steps.outcome: Endpoint restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce that tech support is only ever employee-initiated through official channels
steps.desc: Record the incident and remind staff that legitimate tech support is reached by contacting the internal help desk, never through a pop-up or unsolicited call.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness note issued.

steps.title: Determine whether the employee granted access or ran anything
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee installed software, granted remote access, or provided information before recognizing it as a scam.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of whether any compromise occurred.

steps.title: Reset any credentials or payment details disclosed
steps.desc: If any credential or payment information was shared, reset/freeze it immediately.
steps.outcome: Disclosed credentials/payment details secured.

ITID-11522.def: A full-screen browser pop-up or scareware alert falsely claims the device is infected or locked and instructs the target to call a phone number for 'support', leading into a paid remediation or remote-access scam.
ITID-11522.purpose: Captures a tech support scam initiated by a fake browser pop-up or scareware alert falsely claiming the device is infected.
scopeIncludes: Fake antivirus/security alert pop-ups displaying a support phone number
Browser lock/scareware pages demanding a call to unlock the device
scopeExcludes: Scam initiated by an unsolicited inbound cold call with no pop-up (see ITID-11523)
Legitimate security software renewal notices later weaponized into a scam (see ITID-11529)
ITID-11522.severity: Medium; escalate if the target called the number and granted remote access.
ITID-11522.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if remote access or payment was granted.
ITID-11522.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the target's device was subsequently accessed remotely.
indicators: Full-screen browser alert with an urgent countdown and phone number
Browser tab impossible to close normally
vectors: Malvertising redirecting to a scareware page
Compromised legitimate website injecting a fake alert
rootCauses: Browser pop-up blocking/ad-blocking not enforced
Lack of awareness that OS/browser vendors never display a support phone number in an alert
controls: Browser pop-up/ad blocking
Web filtering for known scareware domains
Security awareness training
