ITID-11621.def: A target is lured into downloading a file advertised as one thing (software, media, a document) that is actually malicious, without enough detail captured to classify the specific content lure category.
ITID-11621.purpose: Catch-all for a fake-download baiting attempt that does not fit a more specific leaf under Fake Downloads.
scopeIncludes: Fake download reports logged before the content lure category is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the content lure category is known
ITID-11621.severity: Medium by default; reassess once the lure category and whether the file was executed are known.
ITID-11621.priority: P2 by default given the risk of malware execution.
ITID-11621.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the downloaded file was executed.
indicators: Report of a downloaded file from an unclear or untrusted source
vectors: Download from an untrusted site of unclear content category
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Security awareness training
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) monitoring
ITID-11621.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting and EDR execution alerting once the file is run.
ITID-11621.response: Document, quarantine the file, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count of fake download reports pending reclassification
ITID-11621.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Download
playbook.description: For a report of malware or unwanted software obtained via a deceptive download whose specific lure category has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Identify the download source and delivery URL
steps.desc: Collect the exact URL, site, or search result that led to the download, and the downloaded file itself.
steps.guidance: Check browser history and download manager entries rather than relying on user recall alone.
steps.outcome: Source URL and downloaded file(s) preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host if execution is confirmed or suspected.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload and identify malware family
steps.desc: Submit the file to sandbox analysis and/or AV/EDR detonation to determine malware type and capability.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability profile identified.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and place the host under elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and remind staff on safe download practices
steps.desc: Record the download source and malware type; reinforce guidance on downloading only from vetted, approved sources.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued if warranted.

steps.title: Determine if the file was executed
steps.desc: Check EDR process-creation telemetry to confirm whether the downloaded file was run, and if so what it spawned.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status and any child processes/network connections observed.
steps.abort: If the file was downloaded but never executed and can be deleted before opening, treat as a near-miss and skip to eradication of the file only.

steps.title: Block the source domain/URL
steps.desc: Add the download source to web/DNS blocklists to prevent further downloads org-wide.
steps.outcome: Source blocked at the web proxy/DNS layer.

steps.title: Remove the malware and verify eradication
steps.desc: Run EDR removal/quarantine, or reimage the host if the malware has rootkit or credential-theft capability.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean by rescan.

ITID-11622.def: A target downloads what is advertised as a cracked/pirated version of paid commercial software (e.g., a keygen or crack tool) from an untrusted site, which is actually malware or bundled with malware.
ITID-11622.purpose: Captures a fake download disguised as cracked or pirated commercial software.
scopeIncludes: Cracked/keygen downloads for paid commercial software (productivity suites, creative tools, etc.)
'Crack' or 'activation tool' executables bundled with malware
scopeExcludes: Fake game cheat/mod downloads (see ITID-11623)
Fake open-source package downloads (see ITID-11629)
ITID-11622.severity: Medium-High; users seeking cracked software often deliberately disable security controls, increasing compromise likelihood.
ITID-11622.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the crack tool was executed with elevated/administrator privileges.
ITID-11622.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the crack tool was executed.
indicators: Presence of a 'keygen' or 'crack' executable on an endpoint
Antivirus/security software disabled or excluded shortly before execution
vectors: Torrent/file-sharing site hosting a cracked-software installer bundled with malware
Forum post linking to a 'working crack' download
rootCauses: Use of unlicensed software on corporate devices
Security software exclusions added by the user to allow the crack tool to run
mitreTechniques: T1553.006 Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification
controls: Application allow-listing
Policy prohibiting unlicensed/pirated software
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) monitoring
ITID-11622.detection: EDR can detect execution of an unsigned crack/keygen binary and any subsequent malicious behavior.
ITID-11622.response: Quarantine and remove the software, scan the endpoint for additional payloads, and address the unlicensed-software policy violation.
metrics: Count of cracked-software malware incidents per quarter
ITID-11622.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11623 by targeting general commercial/productivity software rather than games specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Cracked/Pirated Software Fake Download
playbook.description: For malware delivered via a 'cracked' or pirated software installer/keygen downloaded from a torrent, warez, or piracy site.

steps.title: Identify the pirated title and download source
steps.desc: Determine which software/game was being pirated and the site/torrent used, and preserve the installer file.
steps.guidance: Cracked installers and keygens are one of the most common commodity-malware and infostealer delivery vectors; treat any hit as high-likelihood infostealer until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: Source and installer identified and preserved.

steps.title: Isolate the host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host immediately given the high likelihood of credential theft.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze payload and scope stolen data
steps.desc: Detonate the payload in sandbox to confirm malware family and identify what data classes it targets (browser stores, wallets, session tokens).
steps.outcome: Malware family confirmed and data-theft scope documented.

steps.title: Restore host with fresh credentials and monitor
steps.desc: Return the reimaged host to the user with newly issued credentials, and monitor associated accounts for anomalous activity.
steps.outcome: Host and accounts restored; monitoring active for 14+ days.

steps.title: Document and reinforce acceptable-use policy on unlicensed software
steps.desc: Record findings and reinforce the acceptable-use policy prohibiting installation of unlicensed/cracked software on corporate or work-connected devices.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy reminder issued.

steps.title: Confirm execution and check for infostealer indicators
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry for execution, and specifically look for browser-credential-store access, clipboard monitoring, or outbound connections to known stealer C2 patterns.
steps.guidance: Infostealers packaged with cracks commonly harvest saved browser passwords, cookies, and crypto-wallet files within seconds of execution.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status and infostealer behavior indicators (or absence thereof).

steps.title: Force credential reset on all accounts used on the host
steps.desc: Reset passwords and revoke sessions for all corporate accounts that were logged into the browser/OS on the affected host.
steps.guidance: Do not wait for confirmation of theft — assume compromise given the malware class.
steps.outcome: All potentially exposed credentials rotated and sessions revoked.

steps.title: Reimage the host
steps.desc: Reimage rather than clean-in-place given infostealers frequently deploy additional persistence and loader components.
steps.outcome: Host reimaged and returned to known-good baseline.

ITID-11623.def: A target downloads what is advertised as a video game cheat, mod, or trainer from an untrusted site or forum, which is actually malware or bundled with malware.
ITID-11623.purpose: Captures a fake download disguised as a video game cheat, mod, or trainer.
scopeIncludes: Game cheat/aimbot/trainer executables from untrusted sources
Game mod files bundled with malicious payloads
scopeExcludes: Cracked commercial productivity software (see ITID-11622)
Fake media/torrent downloads unrelated to gaming (see ITID-11624)
ITID-11623.severity: Medium; often targets personal rather than corporate devices, but is relevant where personal-device compromise leads to corporate credential reuse.
ITID-11623.priority: P3 on a personal device, escalating to P2 if the device also accesses corporate resources.
ITID-11623.escalation: Escalate to SOC if the affected device has been used to access corporate accounts or VPN.
indicators: Presence of a game cheat/trainer executable from an untrusted source
Malware detection correlated with a gaming-related download
vectors: Gaming forum or Discord server link to a 'undetected cheat' download
YouTube video description linking to a cheat/mod download
rootCauses: Use of personal devices with corporate account access and no endpoint protection
Gaming community trust exploited to bypass typical download suspicion
controls: Security awareness training
Conditional access restricting corporate resource access to managed devices
ITID-11623.detection: Limited on unmanaged personal devices; EDR provides signal only on managed endpoints.
ITID-11623.response: If the device has corporate access, force credential reset and review conditional-access logs for anomalous activity.
metrics: Count of game cheat/mod malware incidents affecting corporate-connected devices
ITID-11623.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11622 by the gaming-specific content lure (cheats, mods, trainers) rather than commercial productivity software.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Game Cheat/Mod Download
playbook.description: For malware delivered via a fake video game cheat, hack, trainer, or mod file, often distributed on gaming forums, Discord, or YouTube video descriptions.

steps.title: Identify the game, distribution channel, and file
steps.desc: Determine which game the cheat/mod claimed to target, where it was obtained (Discord, forum, YouTube description link), and preserve the file.
steps.guidance: Game cheats are a common vector for infostealers and RATs, especially on personal devices used for work (BYOD) or gaming during work hours on corporate hardware.
steps.outcome: Distribution channel and file identified and preserved.

steps.title: Isolate the device and revoke corporate access
steps.desc: Network-isolate a corporate device, or for a personal device, revoke its VPN/MDM/SSO session access immediately.
steps.outcome: Device isolated or its corporate access revoked.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the file in a sandbox to confirm malware family (commonly RAT or infostealer for this lure type).
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability confirmed.

steps.title: Restore access and monitor
steps.desc: Re-enable corporate access only after clean verification, and monitor the account for anomalous activity.
steps.outcome: Access restored; monitoring active for 14+ days.

steps.title: Document and review BYOD/personal-device access policy
steps.desc: Record findings and, if a personal device was involved, flag this to IT policy owners as input on BYOD conditional-access controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy input delivered if applicable.

steps.title: Determine if this is a personal or corporate device
steps.desc: Establish whether the infected device is corporate-managed or a personal/BYOD device that also accesses corporate resources.
steps.guidance: This changes remediation scope significantly — a personal device may require coordinating with the user rather than direct EDR action.
steps.outcome: Device ownership and corporate-resource access scope established.

steps.title: Reset credentials used on the device
steps.desc: Force a password/session reset for any corporate account accessed from the device.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and sessions revoked.

steps.title: Remediate the device
steps.desc: Reimage a corporate device, or advise/assist the user in fully cleaning or factory-resetting a personal device before restoring corporate access.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean before any corporate access is restored.

steps.title: Confirm execution and payload behavior
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry (corporate device) or interview/log review (personal device) for execution and RAT/stealer indicators.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution and behavior profile.

ITID-11624.def: A target downloads what is advertised as a media file (movie, TV episode, or music album) via a torrent or direct-download site, which is actually malware disguised with a media file extension or bundled codec/player installer.
ITID-11624.purpose: Captures a fake download disguised as a movie, TV show, or music torrent file.
scopeIncludes: Torrent downloads for movies/TV/music bundled with or disguised as malware
Fake 'required codec' or media-player installer prompts accompanying a torrent download
scopeExcludes: Game-related downloads (see ITID-11623)
Fake AI tool/model downloads (see ITID-11628)
ITID-11624.severity: Medium; typically targets personal devices, relevant where corporate credential/account exposure results.
ITID-11624.priority: P3 on a personal device, escalating to P2 if corporate resources were accessed from the affected device.
ITID-11624.escalation: Escalate to SOC if the affected device has corporate account or VPN access.
indicators: Fake 'codec required' installer prompt during media playback
Media file with an unexpected executable extension (e.g., .mp4.exe)
vectors: Torrent site hosting a malware-bundled media file
Fake streaming site prompting a 'player update' download
rootCauses: Use of personal/unmanaged devices for media piracy with corporate account access
File-extension visibility disabled, hiding the true executable nature of the file
controls: Security awareness training
Conditional access restricting corporate resource access to managed devices
ITID-11624.detection: Limited on unmanaged personal devices; EDR provides signal only on managed endpoints.
ITID-11624.response: If corporate access is implicated, force credential reset and review for anomalous account activity.
metrics: Count of media/torrent-related malware incidents affecting corporate-connected devices
ITID-11624.notes: Differentiated from other Fake Downloads siblings by the media/torrent-specific content lure.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Media/Movie/Music Torrent Download
playbook.description: For malware disguised as a movie, TV show, or music file distributed via torrent or streaming-piracy sites.

steps.title: Identify the torrent/site source and file
steps.desc: Determine the torrent client, tracker, or piracy site used, and preserve the downloaded file.
steps.guidance: Note whether the file has a double extension (e.g. Movie.mp4.exe) or an unusually small size for claimed media length — both are strong red flags.
steps.outcome: Source and file identified and preserved.

steps.title: Isolate the host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host if execution is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the file in a sandbox to determine malware family and capability.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the host for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and reinforce acceptable-use policy on P2P/piracy tools
steps.desc: Record findings and reinforce policy prohibiting torrent clients and piracy-site access on corporate devices/networks.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy reminder issued.

steps.title: Confirm whether the file was executed
steps.desc: Check EDR process telemetry for execution of the disguised file.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status.
steps.abort: If unexecuted and safely deleted, treat as a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the torrent client/site and disable P2P traffic if policy allows
steps.desc: Terminate any running torrent client process and block the associated tracker/site at the network layer.
steps.outcome: Torrent activity stopped and source blocked.

steps.title: Remove the malware or reimage
steps.desc: Run EDR removal or reimage if persistence/rootkit indicators are present.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

ITID-11625.def: A target downloads what is advertised as a free productivity tool or system utility (PDF converter, file compressor, cleanup tool) from search results or an ad, which is actually malware or a potentially unwanted program bundled with malware.
ITID-11625.purpose: Captures a fake download disguised as a free productivity tool or system utility.
scopeIncludes: Fake PDF converter, file compressor, registry cleaner, or similar utility downloads
Utility downloads bundled with adware, spyware, or a malicious payload
scopeExcludes: Fake software update/installer downloads impersonating a specific known vendor's update (see ITID-11627)
Fake AI tool/model downloads (see ITID-11628)
ITID-11625.severity: Medium; often affects corporate-managed devices directly since utilities are frequently sought for work tasks.
ITID-11625.priority: P2 given likelihood of corporate-device impact.
ITID-11625.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team if the utility was installed on a corporate-managed device.
indicators: Installation of an unrecognized 'free utility' from a non-approved source
Bundled adware/toolbar installed alongside the requested utility
vectors: Search-engine ad or poisoned result promoting a free utility download
Fake 'download' button on a utility-hosting site actually triggering a malicious file
rootCauses: No approved software catalog/self-service portal for common utility needs
Lack of application allow-listing on endpoints
controls: Application allow-listing
Approved software self-service catalog
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) monitoring
ITID-11625.detection: EDR can detect execution of an unsigned/unrecognized utility installer and any subsequent malicious behavior.
ITID-11625.response: Quarantine and remove the utility, scan for additional payloads, and direct the user to the approved software catalog.
metrics: Count of fake utility download incidents on managed devices per quarter
ITID-11625.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11627 by not impersonating a specific known vendor's official update — this is a generic/unbranded free-utility lure.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Productivity Tool/Utility Download
playbook.description: For malware disguised as a legitimate productivity tool, PDF converter, system optimizer, or other utility, typically found via search-engine results or ads.

steps.title: Identify the claimed tool and download source
steps.desc: Determine what utility the file claimed to be, where it was found (search result, ad, direct link), and preserve the installer.
steps.guidance: Compare the download domain against the tool's actual official domain — fake utility sites typically use lookalike domains or generic download-aggregator sites.
steps.outcome: Claimed tool identity and true source domain documented and compared to the legitimate vendor.

steps.title: Isolate the host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host if execution occurred, especially if elevated privileges were granted.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the installer in a sandbox to identify actual malware family bundled with or in place of the claimed utility.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the host for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and promote the approved software catalog
steps.desc: Record findings and remind staff to request tools through the approved software catalog/IT request process rather than searching for them directly.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Confirm execution and installation scope
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry for execution, and whether the installer requested elevated/admin privileges.
steps.guidance: Fake utility installers frequently request admin rights under the guise of installation — this is a key escalation point to check.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status and privilege level obtained.

steps.title: Block the fake vendor domain
steps.desc: Add the fake download site to web/DNS blocklists org-wide.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked.

steps.title: Remove the malware and check for admin-level persistence
steps.desc: Run EDR removal and specifically check for services, scheduled tasks, or registry run-keys installed with admin privileges.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean, including any admin-level persistence mechanisms.

ITID-11626.def: An attacker applies for an open position or otherwise reaches a recruiter/hiring manager, attaching or linking to a 'resume' or 'portfolio' file that is actually malware, exploiting the recipient's expectation of routine document review.
ITID-11626.purpose: Captures a fake download baiting recruiters or hiring managers with a malicious file disguised as a job applicant's resume.
scopeIncludes: Malicious resume/CV attachments or download links submitted through a job application channel
Malicious portfolio/work-sample download links submitted by a fake applicant
scopeExcludes: Resume-themed lures delivered as a standard email phishing attachment through the general email channel (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 ITID) rather than through an actual job-application/careers-site submission
Fake job offer DM scams targeting a job seeker rather than a recruiter (see ITID-11724)
ITID-11626.severity: Medium-High — recruiting staff routinely open unsolicited attachments as part of their job function, making this a reliably effective vector.
ITID-11626.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the file was opened/executed on a corporate-managed device.
ITID-11626.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the resume file was opened.
indicators: Resume/CV file with a double extension or macro-enabled document format submitted via an application channel
Application submitted with an implausible or inconsistent candidate profile
vectors: Malicious macro-enabled document submitted as a 'resume' via a careers site or email
Cloud-storage link to a 'portfolio' that actually delivers malware
rootCauses: No sandboxing/detonation of application-submitted attachments before recruiter access
Recruiting staff not included in standard phishing-attachment awareness training scope
controls: Attachment sandboxing/detonation for careers-site submissions
Application allow-listing
Security awareness training extended to recruiting staff
ITID-11626.detection: Email/attachment sandboxing can detonate and flag malicious resume attachments before they reach a recruiter's inbox.
ITID-11626.response: Quarantine the attachment, scan any device where it was opened, and notify the recruiting team of the pattern.
metrics: Count of malicious resume/application-attachment incidents per quarter
ITID-11626.notes: Scope decision: limited to attachments/links submitted through an actual job-application or careers-site channel targeting recruiting staff, to avoid overlapping with general resume-themed email phishing attachments tracked under the Phishing branch.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Job Application/Resume Attachment Download
playbook.description: For malware delivered as a fake resume, CV, or portfolio attachment sent to a recruiting/HR/hiring-manager mailbox as part of a fabricated job application.

steps.title: Preserve the application email and attachment
steps.desc: Collect the full email with headers and the attached file, and identify the mailbox(es) it was sent to.
steps.guidance: This vector frequently targets recruiting/HR mailboxes specifically because they are conditioned to open unsolicited attachments from strangers as part of normal job duties.
steps.outcome: Email and attachment preserved with full headers.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host where the attachment was opened and executed content.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the attachment in a sandbox to identify malware family (commonly macro-dropper or document-exploit delivering a RAT or loader).
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the host for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and brief recruiting/HR on safe attachment handling
steps.desc: Record findings and provide recruiting/HR staff with a safe-handling process (e.g. open attachments only in a sandboxed viewer or via the ATS) for unsolicited applications.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted briefing delivered to recruiting/HR.

steps.title: Search for the same campaign across other recruiting mailboxes
steps.desc: Search the mail gateway/SIEM for the same sender, attachment hash, or subject pattern across all HR/recruiting mailboxes and any public job-posting inbox.
steps.outcome: Full scope of mailboxes that received the campaign.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Use org-wide message purge to remove the attachment from all mailboxes that haven't opened it, and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged from remaining mailboxes; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the malware or reimage
steps.desc: Run EDR removal or reimage if persistence indicators are present.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

steps.title: Confirm whether the attachment was opened/executed
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry for the recipient's machine to confirm whether the attachment was opened and whether it executed macros or a payload.
steps.outcome: Confirmed open/execution status.

ITID-11627.def: A target is prompted (via a fake pop-up, spoofed email, or search result) to download what is presented as an official update or installer from a specific known software vendor, which is actually malware.
ITID-11627.purpose: Captures a fake download impersonating an official software update or installer from a specific known vendor.
scopeIncludes: Fake browser/OS update pop-ups prompting an installer download
Fake vendor-branded installer downloads impersonating a specific product (e.g., a fake 'Zoom update' or 'Adobe Reader update')
scopeExcludes: Generic/unbranded free-utility downloads not impersonating a specific vendor (see ITID-11625)

Billing/registration fraud for a fake free-trial offer where the delivered product may be legitimate (see ITID-11519, under Fake Incentives) — this ITID covers the malicious-installer delivery mechanism itself
ITID-11627.severity: Medium-High — vendor impersonation for a routine update is a highly effective and hard-to-distinguish lure.
ITID-11627.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the fake installer was executed.
ITID-11627.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the fake update/installer was executed.
indicators: Update prompt appearing outside the legitimate application's normal update mechanism
Installer downloaded from a domain not matching the vendor's official domain
vectors: Fake 'update required' browser pop-up
Spoofed vendor email prompting a manual installer download
Malvertising impersonating a vendor's download page
rootCauses: Users manually seeking updates outside the application's built-in updater
No enforced use of managed software deployment/patching for common applications
controls: Managed software deployment/patching to eliminate need for manual updates
Application allow-listing
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) monitoring
ITID-11627.detection: EDR can detect execution of an unsigned installer impersonating a known vendor; web filtering can flag known fake-update domains.
ITID-11627.response: Quarantine and remove the fake installer, scan for additional payloads, and direct users to only update software through the managed deployment channel.
metrics: Count of fake vendor-update installer incidents per quarter
detections: Web filtering known fake-update domain blocking
ITID-11627.notes: Scope decision: covers the malicious-installer delivery/execution mechanism specifically; a billing/registration-fraud free-trial pretext where the delivered product may be functionally legitimate is tracked separately under ITID-11519 to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Software Update/Installer Download
playbook.description: For malware delivered via a fake browser, OS, or application update prompt (e.g. a fake 'Chrome Update' or 'Flash Player' popup) prompting the user to download and run a malicious installer.

steps.title: Identify the fake update prompt and originating site
steps.desc: Determine which site or ad displayed the fake update prompt and preserve the downloaded installer.
steps.guidance: Fake update lures ('ClickFix'-style) frequently instruct the user to copy/paste a command into the Run dialog or terminal rather than executing a file directly — check for this pattern specifically.
steps.outcome: Originating site and delivery mechanism (file download vs. paste-and-run command) documented.

steps.title: Isolate the host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host given confirmed or suspected execution.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload/command
steps.desc: Determine what the executed installer or pasted command actually did (sandbox the file, or decode/analyze the command line).
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the host for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and brief staff on legitimate update mechanisms
steps.desc: Record findings and remind staff that software updates come through the managed patching system, never via browser popups or copy-pasted commands.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Confirm execution via file or command-line
steps.desc: Check EDR process-creation and command-line telemetry for execution of the installer or a manually pasted PowerShell/cmd command matching the lure pattern.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution vector and command/process details.

steps.title: Block the originating site/ad network
steps.desc: Add the fake-update site to web/DNS blocklists and report the malicious ad if delivered via an ad network.
steps.outcome: Site blocked; ad reported where applicable.

steps.title: Remove the malware or reimage
steps.desc: Run EDR removal or reimage if persistence/credential-theft indicators are present.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

ITID-11628.def: A target downloads what is advertised as an AI tool, model weights, or AI content-generation application (capitalizing on current AI trend interest) from an untrusted site, which is actually malware.
ITID-11628.purpose: Captures a fake download disguised as an AI tool, model, or AI-generated content generator.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'AI image/video generator' desktop application downloads
Fake AI model weight files or 'jailbreak' tool downloads bundled with malware
scopeExcludes: Fake open-source package/repository downloads not specifically AI-themed (see ITID-11629)
Malicious browser extensions or third-party plugins (tracked under supply-chain ITIDs outside this branch, e.g., ITID-62411)
ITID-11628.severity: Medium-High — high current interest in AI tools makes this an effective and fast-moving lure category.
ITID-11628.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if executed on a corporate-managed device.
ITID-11628.escalation: Escalate to SOC/endpoint team immediately if the fake AI tool was executed.
indicators: Download of an AI tool from an unofficial site rather than a recognized vendor/marketplace
AI tool requesting unusually broad system permissions during installation
vectors: Social media ad or influencer post promoting a 'free AI tool' download
Fake AI tool website closely mimicking a legitimate, well-known AI product
rootCauses: Rapid proliferation of AI tools outpacing vetting/awareness processes
No approved-AI-tools list published for staff
controls: Published approved-AI-tools list
Application allow-listing
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) monitoring
ITID-11628.detection: EDR can detect execution of an unsigned/unrecognized AI-tool installer and subsequent malicious behavior.
ITID-11628.response: Quarantine and remove the tool, scan for additional payloads, and direct users to the approved-AI-tools list.
metrics: Count of fake AI tool download incidents per quarter
ITID-11628.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11629 by the specific AI-tool/model theme of the lure rather than a general open-source package.

playbook.name: Response: Fake AI Tool/Model Download
playbook.description: For malware disguised as an AI application, chatbot client, or machine-learning model file distributed outside official/vetted repositories, capitalizing on current interest in AI tools.

steps.title: Identify the claimed AI tool and download source
steps.desc: Determine what tool/model the download claimed to be (e.g. a desktop client for a popular AI product, a 'local LLM' installer) and where it was obtained.
steps.guidance: This is an emerging, fast-evolving lure category — check whether the download source is an official vendor domain, verified repository, or an unofficial mirror/aggregator site.
steps.outcome: Claimed tool identity and true source documented.

steps.title: Isolate the host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host if execution is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Host isolated pending analysis.

steps.title: Analyze the payload
steps.desc: Detonate the file in a sandbox to identify actual malware family delivered under the AI-tool guise.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented.

steps.title: Restore host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the host for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Host restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and publish a vetted AI-tool guidance list
steps.desc: Record findings and, if not already published, provide staff a list of approved/vetted AI tools and official download sources to reduce future exposure to this lure category.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; guidance published or updated.

steps.title: Confirm execution and behavior
steps.desc: Check EDR telemetry for execution and any unusual network beaconing or credential-store access following execution.
steps.outcome: Confirmed execution status and behavior indicators.
steps.abort: If unexecuted, treat as a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the fake source and alert staff to the lure theme
steps.desc: Add the source to web/DNS blocklists and send a targeted alert if the tool name is trending internally (e.g. a specific AI product staff are actively asking about).
steps.outcome: Source blocked; targeted alert issued if warranted.

steps.title: Remove the malware or reimage
steps.desc: Run EDR removal or reimage if persistence indicators are present.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

ITID-11629.def: A developer is lured — via a forum post, fake GitHub repository, or search result — into manually cloning or downloading a package/repository presented as a legitimate open-source project, which actually contains malicious code.
ITID-11629.purpose: Captures a developer being socially engineered into manually downloading a fake open-source package or repository, as distinct from automated dependency-resolution supply-chain attacks.
scopeIncludes: Fake GitHub/GitLab repositories advertised via forum posts, social media, or search results as a legitimate open-source project
Manually downloaded 'utility' or 'library' code from an untrusted repository, socially engineered rather than pulled via a package manager
scopeExcludes: Automated dependency-confusion attacks where a malicious package is auto-resolved by a build/package manager (see ITID-61323, ITID-62321)
Typosquatted malicious packages published to a public registry and pulled automatically (see ITID-61321)
ITID-11629.severity: Medium-High given the potential for source-code or build-environment compromise.
ITID-11629.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the code was executed or integrated into a build.
ITID-11629.escalation: Escalate to SOC/engineering leadership immediately if the malicious code was executed or merged into a codebase.
indicators: Repository promoted via unsolicited forum/social posts rather than organic discovery
Repository with an inflated star count or fake positive reviews
Code containing obfuscated or unexpectedly network-calling functions
vectors: Fake repository promoted on developer forums (e.g., Stack Overflow, Reddit) as a solution to a common problem
Search-engine-optimized fake repository page mimicking a popular real project
rootCauses: No code-review/vetting step before manually incorporating third-party code
Developers trusting star counts/community signals without independent verification
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Mandatory code review for third-party/open-source code before integration
Software composition analysis (SCA) tooling
ITID-11629.detection: Software composition analysis and code-review processes provide a real technical signal if enforced before integration.
ITID-11629.response: Remove the code, audit the build environment for compromise, and review the CI/CD pipeline for any resulting persistence.
metrics: Count of malicious manually-sourced repository incidents per quarter
ITID-11629.notes: Scope decision: covers a developer being socially engineered into a manual, human-driven download of a fake repository; automated dependency-confusion and typosquatted-package attacks resolved without direct human deception are tracked separately under ITID-61321, ITID-61323, and ITID-62321 to avoid double-counting the same supply-chain risk under two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Open-Source Package/Repository Download
playbook.description: For malware delivered via a typosquatted or trojanized open-source package (npm, PyPI, etc.) or a fake GitHub repository pulled into a development environment or build pipeline.

steps.title: Identify the package/repository and where it was pulled into
steps.desc: Determine the exact package name, version, registry, or repository URL, and which developer machine, build server, or CI/CD pipeline pulled it in.
steps.guidance: Check package.json/requirements.txt/lockfiles and CI build logs for the exact dependency reference and installation timestamp.
steps.outcome: Package/repo identity and all locations it was installed to (dev machine, CI runner, build artifact) documented.

steps.title: Isolate affected developer machines and pause the CI/CD pipeline
steps.desc: Network-isolate any affected developer endpoint and pause/disable the CI/CD pipeline that pulled the package to prevent further builds from propagating it.
steps.outcome: Affected systems isolated; pipeline paused.

steps.title: Analyze the package payload and scope credential/secret exposure
steps.desc: Reverse the install script/payload to determine what it did — commonly exfiltrating environment variables, CI secrets, cloud credentials, or SSH keys.
steps.outcome: Full list of secrets/credentials potentially exposed to the malicious package.

steps.title: Restore clean pipeline and re-enable builds
steps.desc: Reimage affected developer machines if needed, restore the CI/CD pipeline from a known-clean state, and re-enable builds once verified clean.
steps.outcome: Pipeline restored to clean, verified state.

steps.title: Document and recommend dependency-supply-chain controls
steps.desc: Record the package, its behavior, and recommend controls such as dependency pinning, private registry mirroring/allowlisting, and install-script sandboxing.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete supply-chain control recommendation delivered to engineering leadership.

steps.title: Determine what the malicious package executed (install scripts, build-time hooks)
steps.desc: Review the package's install/postinstall scripts or build hooks and correlate with EDR/CI telemetry for what actually ran.
steps.guidance: Malicious packages commonly use install-time lifecycle scripts to run immediately upon `npm install`/`pip install`, before any application code executes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed what code executed and on which systems.

steps.title: Remove the malicious package from all manifests and caches
steps.desc: Purge the package from lockfiles, dependency caches, and any build artifacts or container images that included it.
steps.guidance: Check whether any built artifact containing the package was already deployed or published downstream.
steps.outcome: Malicious package removed from all manifests, caches, and artifacts.

steps.title: Rotate all exposed secrets and credentials
steps.desc: Rotate every credential, API key, and CI/CD secret the affected system had access to.
steps.guidance: Treat any secret available to the CI runner or developer machine environment as compromised, not just ones confirmed exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: All exposed secrets rotated and old values invalidated.

steps.title: Audit downstream artifacts for contamination
steps.desc: Check whether any build or release published before containment included the malicious package, and rebuild/republish clean versions as needed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean status of all downstream artifacts, or a remediation plan for contaminated ones.

ITID-11711.def: A fabricated social media profile created to deceive, without enough detail captured to classify the specific persona type it impersonates.
ITID-11711.purpose: Catch-all for a fake social media profile that does not fit a more specific leaf under Fake Profiles.
scopeIncludes: Fake profile reports logged before the impersonated persona type is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the persona type is known
ITID-11711.severity: Low-to-Medium by default; reassess once the persona type and target are known.
ITID-11711.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassification once more detail is available.
indicators: Report of a suspicious or unverified profile of unclear intent
vectors: Fake profile of unclear persona type
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Security awareness training
ITID-11711.response: Document and attempt to reclassify; report to the platform.
metrics: Count of fake profile reports pending reclassification
ITID-11711.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Social Media Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile impersonating an individual, brand, or entity connected to the organization, not fitting a more specific sub-category.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the fake profile
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile page, URL/handle, bio, posts, and any interactions before it can be altered or deleted.
steps.outcome: Fake profile evidence preserved with URL, handle, and timestamp.

steps.title: Warn any known contacted parties
steps.desc: If the fake profile has messaged employees, customers, or partners, warn them directly that the profile is not legitimate.
steps.outcome: Contacted parties warned before acting on the fake profile's requests.

steps.title: Track the report to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up on the report status until the platform removes or suspends the fake profile.
steps.guidance: Escalate through account manager/legal channels if the platform's standard report queue does not act within a reasonable timeframe.
steps.outcome: Fake profile removed or suspended.
steps.abort: If the platform does not act, escalate via legal/brand-protection channels or a paid trust & safety escalation path if available.

steps.title: Confirm removal and monitor for reappearance
steps.desc: Confirm the profile is down and set up monitoring for a re-created copycat profile.
steps.outcome: Profile confirmed removed; monitoring in place.

steps.title: Log the impersonation for pattern tracking
steps.desc: Record the profile details, platform, and resolution time for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine who or what is being impersonated and the intent
steps.desc: Establish whether the profile impersonates a real employee, executive, or the organization's brand, and assess apparent intent (scam, harassment, disinformation).
steps.outcome: Impersonation target and apparent intent documented.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation report
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation/fake-account report to the platform's trust and safety team, including evidence gathered.
steps.outcome: Report filed with the platform.

steps.title: Check whether the profile has contacted or scammed anyone
steps.desc: Check with the impersonated individual and search for reports of the fake profile messaging employees, customers, or the public.
steps.outcome: Scope of any resulting contact/harm established.

ITID-11712.def: A social media profile impersonating a recruiter or talent-acquisition professional, used to establish contact with job-seeking targets as a pretext for a later scam (fake job offer, data harvesting, or malware delivery).
ITID-11712.purpose: Captures a fake recruiter profile used to build trust with job-seeking targets before pivoting to a scam or data-harvesting objective.
scopeIncludes: Fake recruiter profiles on professional networking platforms contacting job seekers
Fake recruiter profiles impersonating a real employee at a known company
scopeExcludes: The actual fake job offer DM sent once contact is established (see ITID-11724, under Direct Messaging Scams) — this ITID covers the fabricated persona itself
Fake executive/colleague profiles not posing as a recruiter (see ITID-11713)
ITID-11712.severity: Medium; escalate if the profile impersonates a real named employee of the organization.
ITID-11712.priority: P2 if impersonating a real employee/brand, otherwise P3.
ITID-11712.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection/HR if the profile impersonates a real employee or uses the organization's name.
indicators: Recruiter profile with limited connection history or generic/stock photo
Profile claiming affiliation with the organization not present in official employee directories
vectors: Fake recruiter profile built specifically to target a known company's employees or job seekers
rootCauses: No monitoring for fake profiles impersonating recruiters using the organization's name
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Brand/impersonation monitoring on professional networking platforms
Security awareness training on verifying recruiter identity
ITID-11712.detection: Relies mainly on user/platform reporting and periodic brand-monitoring sweeps.
ITID-11712.response: Report the profile to the platform; notify affected employees/candidates if the organization's name was used.
metrics: Count of fake recruiter profile reports per quarter
ITID-11712.notes: Scope decision: this ITID covers the fabricated recruiter persona itself; the subsequent fake job offer message is tracked under ITID-11724 to avoid double-counting the same incident across two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Recruiter Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile posing as a recruiter, often used to lure targets into fake job interviews for credential/data harvesting, malware delivery, or advance-fee scams.

steps.title: Preserve the fake recruiter profile and any job posting/messages
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile, any job posting, and the full message thread with the target.
steps.outcome: Full evidence trail preserved.

steps.title: If any file was downloaded or link clicked, isolate the device
steps.desc: Revoke corporate access via MDM/conditional access pending inspection if the target is an employee who interacted with attacker-provided files or links.
steps.outcome: Device access suspended if applicable.

steps.title: Remove any malware from an affected device
steps.desc: If a malicious file was downloaded and run, remove it via MDM/EDR or wipe the device if removal cannot be confirmed reliable.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and profile takedown
steps.desc: Confirm the device/account is clean and follow up on the platform report status.
steps.outcome: Device restored; fake profile removed or takedown in progress.

steps.title: Warn other employees/candidates and log the pattern
steps.desc: If this appears to be a recurring recruiter-scam campaign targeting the organization's name, alert HR/talent acquisition and log the pattern for awareness content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; relevant teams alerted.

steps.title: Determine what the fake recruiter asked the target to do
steps.desc: Interview the targeted employee/candidate to establish whether they were asked to click a link, download a 'skills test' file, provide personal/financial details, or pay a fee.
steps.guidance: Fake recruiter scams frequently deliver malware disguised as a coding test or assessment tool.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the ask and any action taken by the target established.

steps.title: If personal/financial data was shared, advise the target on next steps
steps.desc: Advise the target to monitor for identity theft/fraud and, if payment was made, to contact their card issuer.
steps.outcome: Target informed and taking protective action.

steps.title: Check whether the fake profile is impersonating a real employee/recruiter or the organization's brand
steps.desc: Confirm whether the fake profile uses a real employee's name/photo or a fabricated identity claiming to recruit for the organization.
steps.outcome: Impersonation type confirmed.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation report
steps.desc: Report the fake recruiter profile to the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

ITID-11713.def: A social media profile impersonating a specific named executive or colleague from the target's own organization, used to build false trust for a subsequent request (financial, informational, or credential-related) directed at other employees.
ITID-11713.purpose: Captures a fake profile impersonating a specific known executive or colleague within the target's own organization.
scopeIncludes: Fake profiles using a real executive's or colleague's name and photo to connect with or message other employees
Duplicate/cloned profiles of a real internal employee used to solicit trust from their actual connections
scopeExcludes: Fake vendor/brand corporate profiles not impersonating a specific named individual (see ITID-11714)
A profile built entirely from a stolen real identity of someone outside the organization (see ITID-11718)
ITID-11713.severity: High — internal executive/colleague impersonation directly threatens the organization's own trust relationships.
ITID-11713.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if used to solicit a financial transaction or credentials from an employee.
ITID-11713.escalation: Escalate to SOC, executive protection, and legal immediately upon confirming impersonation of a named internal individual.
indicators: A duplicate profile using an existing employee's name and photo
Connection requests sent to the real employee's actual connections from the fake profile
vectors: Cloning a public LinkedIn profile's photo and details to create a duplicate impersonation account
Fake executive profile sending connection requests to direct reports
rootCauses: Executive/employee photos and details publicly accessible and easily cloned
No monitoring for duplicate profiles impersonating named employees
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Brand/impersonation monitoring for cloned employee profiles
Security awareness training on verifying unexpected internal contact via social media
ITID-11713.detection: Relies mainly on employee/platform reporting; some coverage from proactive brand-monitoring tools scanning for cloned executive profiles.
ITID-11713.response: Report and request platform takedown; notify affected employees and the impersonated individual directly.
metrics: Count of confirmed executive/colleague impersonation profile takedowns per quarter
ITID-11713.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11714 by impersonating a specific named individual internal to the organization rather than a generic vendor/brand identity.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive/Colleague Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile impersonating a real executive or colleague within the organization, often used to build trust before requesting money, gift cards, sensitive data, or credentials.

steps.title: Preserve the fake profile and message thread
steps.desc: Screenshot the fake profile and the complete conversation with the target, including any request made.
steps.outcome: Full evidence preserved.

steps.title: If money or gift cards were sent, immediately engage finance/fraud recovery
steps.desc: Contact the bank/payment provider to attempt a recall or freeze, and notify finance leadership immediately given the time-sensitivity of fraud recovery.
steps.outcome: Recovery attempt initiated with financial institution.

steps.title: Track the report to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up until the fake profile is removed; escalate via legal/brand-protection channels if needed.
steps.outcome: Fake profile removed.

steps.title: Confirm containment actions completed and profile removed
steps.desc: Confirm all affected accounts/finances are secured and the fake profile is down.
steps.outcome: Full recovery confirmed.

steps.title: Brief staff on executive-impersonation risk and log the incident
steps.desc: Log the incident and, if this reflects a broader pattern, brief staff (especially finance) that urgent requests via social media DM from 'executives' should always be verified through a separate known channel.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Confirm with the real impersonated executive/colleague that they did not send the messages
steps.desc: Directly verify with the real person through a known-good channel (not social media) that they did not create the profile or send the messages.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed by the real individual.

steps.title: If sensitive data or credentials were shared, contain accordingly
steps.desc: Force password reset/session revocation on any exposed account, and assess data-loss scope if confidential information was shared.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials/data contained.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and whether the target complied
steps.desc: Establish the exact ask (wire transfer, gift cards, credentials, confidential data) and whether the target acted on it.
steps.guidance: This mirrors a business email compromise / CEO fraud pattern conducted over social media instead of email.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the request and any compliance established.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation report
steps.desc: Report the fake profile to the platform's trust and safety team, ideally with the real executive/colleague's cooperation as the impersonated party.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

ITID-11714.def: A social media profile impersonating a known vendor's or brand's official corporate account (rather than a specific named individual), used to deceive customers, partners, or the public — often for phishing, fraud, or reputational harm.
ITID-11714.purpose: Captures a fake corporate profile impersonating a known vendor or brand (not a specific named individual) to deceive customers or partners.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'official' brand/company accounts on social media not verified as the legitimate corporate presence
Fake vendor corporate profiles used to solicit customer payments or credentials
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of a specific named executive or colleague (see ITID-11713)
Fake alumni/group affiliation profiles (see ITID-11717)
ITID-11714.severity: Medium-High given potential customer/partner financial harm and brand reputational damage.
ITID-11714.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if actively soliciting payments or credentials from customers.
ITID-11714.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection/legal and communications immediately upon discovering an active fake corporate account.
indicators: Duplicate or near-identical brand account with a slightly altered handle
Customer reports of contact from an unverified 'official' account
vectors: Fake customer-support account responding to public brand mentions with phishing links
Fake corporate account soliciting fraudulent payments from customers/partners
rootCauses: Brand's official accounts not consistently verified/badged across all platforms
No proactive monitoring for impersonating corporate accounts
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Brand/impersonation monitoring across platforms
Official account verification/badging on all major platforms
ITID-11714.detection: Relies mainly on customer/employee reporting and periodic brand-monitoring sweeps.
ITID-11714.response: Report and request platform takedown; issue a public notice if customers were actively targeted.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake corporate account takedowns per quarter
ITID-11714.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11713 by impersonating a corporate/brand identity generally, not a specific named individual.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Vendor/Brand Corporate Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile or page impersonating a vendor, supplier, or the organization's own corporate brand, often used to run scam customer 'support', fake promotions, or invoice fraud.

steps.title: Preserve the fake profile/page and any posts or messages
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile/page, its posts, and any DM interactions with customers or employees.
steps.outcome: Full evidence preserved.

steps.title: Issue a public warning if customers are being actively targeted
steps.desc: Post an official notice on verified organizational channels warning customers about the fake profile, if active scam engagement with the public is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Customers warned before acting on the fake profile's requests.

steps.title: Track the report to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up on the report status; escalate through legal/brand-protection or a verified-partner escalation channel if the platform's standard queue is slow.
steps.outcome: Fake profile/page removed.
steps.abort: If the platform does not act promptly and active customer harm continues, escalate to legal for a formal cease-and-desist / DMCA-style request where applicable.

steps.title: Confirm removal and monitor for copycats
steps.desc: Confirm the fake page is down and set up brand monitoring for reappearance.
steps.outcome: Profile removed; monitoring active.

steps.title: Log the incident and consider proactive brand-protection measures
steps.desc: Record the incident; if recurring, recommend proactive verified-account registration and brand monitoring subscriptions on the affected platform.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendation raised if warranted.

steps.title: Determine whether this impersonates a known vendor or the organization's own brand
steps.desc: Establish which entity is being impersonated and confirm with that entity (vendor security contact, or internal brand/marketing team) that the profile is not legitimate.
steps.outcome: Impersonation target confirmed.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation/brand infringement report
steps.desc: Submit a report to the platform's trust and safety or brand-protection reporting channel, including proof of brand ownership where required.
steps.outcome: Report filed with platform.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety / brand reporting portal

steps.title: Assess customer/public exposure
steps.desc: Check whether the fake profile has been actively engaging customers or the public with scam offers, fake support, or fraudulent invoices.
steps.outcome: Scope of public exposure established.

ITID-11715.def: A fabricated social media/dating profile used to build a long-term romantic relationship with a target, ultimately leveraging that emotional trust to solicit money, gifts, or sensitive information.
ITID-11715.purpose: Captures a fake profile built to establish a fabricated romantic relationship with a target for financial exploitation.
scopeIncludes: Fake dating/social media profiles used to build a romantic relationship over an extended period before requesting money
Profiles using stolen photos of an unrelated real person to construct a romantic persona
scopeExcludes: A fake profile using a specific stolen real identity where the primary objective is not romance (see ITID-11718)
A short-duration crypto/investment DM scam with no romantic relationship-building element (see ITID-11723)
ITID-11715.severity: Medium-High given the typically significant financial and psychological harm to individual victims.
ITID-11715.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the target is an employee being groomed for a subsequent insider-risk angle (e.g., pressured into internal fraud).
ITID-11715.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance support resources for the individual victim; escalate to insider-risk teams if the relationship appears aimed at manipulating an employee's access.
indicators: A relationship that has never involved an in-person or verified video meeting
Escalating requests for money framed as emergencies, travel costs, or investment opportunities
Reverse-image-search matches showing the profile photo belongs to an unrelated person
vectors: Fake dating-app or social media profile using stolen photos to build a long-term relationship
Persistent messaging cultivating emotional dependency before the first financial request
rootCauses: Lack of awareness of romance scam patterns among targeted demographics
No verification habit (video call, reverse image search) established before deepening trust
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Security awareness training on romance scam patterns
Financial institution alerts on unusual transfers to new/foreign recipients
ITID-11715.detection: Relies almost entirely on victim or bank reporting; minimal automated technical signal.
ITID-11715.response: Provide the victim with fraud-reporting resources; report the profile to the platform for takedown.
metrics: Count of romance scam profile reports per quarter
Total confirmed financial loss reported
ITID-11715.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11718 by the defining objective being a fabricated romantic relationship rather than general identity theft for other purposes.

playbook.name: Response: Romance Scam Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile running a romance scam against an employee, building a fabricated relationship to eventually solicit money, gift cards, or sensitive information.

steps.title: Support the employee in reporting with sensitivity
steps.desc: Handle the report discreetly and without judgment; romance scam victims often feel embarrassment, which can delay reporting and worsen loss.
steps.guidance: This is primarily a personal-welfare matter with a possible corporate-exposure component; approach supportively.
steps.outcome: Employee feels supported and willing to disclose full details.

steps.title: If corporate information or access was ever discussed, contain accordingly
steps.desc: If the employee shared any corporate credentials, confidential data, or system access details with the scammer, treat that portion as a credential/data-exposure incident and contain it.
steps.outcome: Any corporate exposure contained.

steps.title: Confirm any corporate exposure is resolved and offer continued support
steps.desc: Confirm corporate-side containment is complete; point the employee to any available employee assistance resources given the emotional impact.
steps.outcome: Corporate exposure resolved; employee supported.

steps.title: Log the incident with appropriate confidentiality
steps.desc: Record the corporate-relevant facts only, handling personal details with discretion; use anonymized patterns for awareness content if appropriate.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with appropriate confidentiality.

steps.title: Preserve the profile and conversation history
steps.desc: Screenshot the fake profile and, with the employee's consent, the relevant conversation history showing the relationship-building and any financial requests.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for reporting purposes.

steps.title: Advise the employee on financial fraud reporting
steps.desc: Direct the employee to report the financial loss to their bank/payment provider and to the relevant national fraud/romance-scam reporting authority.
steps.outcome: Employee has reported through appropriate personal-fraud channels.

steps.title: Determine financial loss and whether corporate resources/information were involved
steps.desc: Establish whether the employee sent personal money/gift cards, and separately whether any corporate device, account, or confidential information was ever discussed or exposed during the relationship.
steps.outcome: Personal financial loss and any corporate exposure both established.
steps.abort: If purely personal with zero corporate touchpoint, limit corporate involvement to supportive guidance and reporting assistance only.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation/scam report
steps.desc: Report the fake profile to the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

ITID-11716.def: A coordinated cluster of multiple fake ('sock puppet') social media profiles, operated by the same actor or group, working together to amplify a message, manufacture apparent consensus, or reinforce a single scam narrative across many apparent independent voices.
ITID-11716.purpose: Captures a coordinated network of multiple fake profiles operated together to amplify a single narrative or scam at scale.
scopeIncludes: Multiple fake profiles cross-commenting/liking/amplifying each other's content to manufacture credibility
A cluster of fake profiles used together to reinforce a single fraudulent narrative or investment scheme
scopeExcludes: A single standalone fake profile with no coordinated cluster (see ITID-11711 through ITID-11715, ITID-11717 through ITID-11719)
AI-generated deepfake misinformation campaigns operated for disinformation rather than a scam objective (see ITID-23514, under a different Type)
ITID-11716.severity: High — a coordinated multi-profile cluster indicates a resourced, organized operation with amplified reach and credibility.
ITID-11716.priority: P1 given the scale and organized nature of a confirmed sock puppet network.
ITID-11716.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection, legal, and platform trust-and-safety teams immediately upon confirming a coordinated cluster.
indicators: Multiple profiles created around the same time with overlapping connection graphs
Near-identical posting/commenting patterns and timing across profiles
Profiles engaging exclusively with each other's content
vectors: Network of fake accounts amplifying a fraudulent investment opportunity through fabricated testimonials
Coordinated cluster used to manufacture fake social proof for a scam product
rootCauses: No network-level analysis of coordinated inauthentic behavior applied to detected fake profiles
Platform-level detection of coordinated inauthentic behavior not integrated into internal brand-monitoring
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Coordinated inauthentic behavior detection/reporting to platform trust-and-safety
Brand/impersonation monitoring at network scale
ITID-11716.detection: Requires network-graph analysis across multiple accounts, typically only feasible via platform-level trust-and-safety tooling or specialized third-party monitoring.
ITID-11716.response: Report the full cluster to the platform's coordinated-inauthentic-behavior reporting channel rather than individual profiles one at a time.
metrics: Count of confirmed sock puppet network takedowns per year
Number of profiles removed per confirmed cluster
ITID-11716.notes: Differentiated from all other Fake Profiles siblings by requiring confirmed coordination across multiple profiles rather than a single standalone fake identity.

playbook.name: Response: Sock Puppet Network (Coordinated Fake Profile Cluster)
playbook.description: For a reported coordinated cluster of fake social media profiles (sock puppets) working together to target the organization or its people, e.g. to amplify disinformation, coordinate harassment, or run a layered social-engineering campaign.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the full identified cluster
steps.desc: Screenshot each identified profile, note handles/URLs, and document the connections between them (shared content, mutual follows/likes, coordinated timing, similar creation dates).
steps.guidance: Coordinated inauthentic behavior detection relies on documenting the pattern across accounts, not just one profile.
steps.outcome: Full cluster of related fake profiles documented with linking evidence.

steps.title: Support any directly targeted employees
steps.desc: If employees were directly harassed or targeted, provide support and advise them not to engage further with the accounts.
steps.outcome: Targeted employees supported and advised.

steps.title: Track the report and monitor for cluster reformation
steps.desc: Follow up on takedown status and monitor for the network reappearing under new handles, which is common with organized sock puppet operations.
steps.outcome: Cluster removed; monitoring in place for reformation.

steps.title: Confirm resolution and brief affected employees
steps.desc: Confirm the network is down or substantially disrupted and update any directly affected employees on the outcome.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed and communicated.

steps.title: Document the campaign pattern for ongoing monitoring
steps.desc: Record the full campaign structure, objective, and outcome; add identifying patterns to ongoing brand/threat monitoring watchlists.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; monitoring watchlist updated.

steps.title: Determine the campaign's objective and targets
steps.desc: Establish what the cluster is trying to achieve (disinformation amplification, coordinated harassment of specific individuals, a layered scam) and who/what is being targeted.
steps.outcome: Campaign objective and targets identified.

steps.title: File a coordinated inauthentic behavior report with the platform
steps.desc: Submit the full documented cluster to the platform's trust and safety team as coordinated inauthentic behavior, which is typically handled with more priority than a single fake profile report.
steps.outcome: Coordinated-behavior report filed, ideally reaching a specialized platform integrity team.

steps.title: Assess whether any real employees have been directly contacted or harmed
steps.desc: Check for direct engagement with employees (harassment, scam messages, targeted disinformation) versus general public-facing activity.
steps.outcome: Scope of direct impact on employees established.

steps.title: Consider legal/law enforcement notification for organized harassment or disinformation campaigns
steps.desc: For campaigns involving organized harassment, threats, or reputationally significant disinformation, loop in legal counsel and consider a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Legal/law enforcement engaged where warranted.

ITID-11717.def: A fabricated profile claiming membership in a group the target belongs to or values (a school alumni network, professional association, industry group, veteran's organization) to establish false in-group trust before pursuing a scam or data-harvesting objective.
ITID-11717.purpose: Captures a fake profile that claims a shared affiliation (alumni, professional group, community) with the target to build unearned trust.
scopeIncludes: Fake profiles claiming shared alumni/school affiliation to establish rapport
Fake profiles claiming membership in a professional association or industry group the target belongs to
scopeExcludes: Fake recruiter profiles (see ITID-11712)
Fake vendor/brand corporate profiles (see ITID-11714)
ITID-11717.severity: Medium; the in-group trust exploited here is typically weaker leverage than a direct executive/colleague or recruiter impersonation.
ITID-11717.escalation: Escalate for documentation; escalate further only if the profile is confirmed part of a broader coordinated scam.
indicators: Claimed affiliation that cannot be verified against actual membership/alumni records
Profile contacting multiple members of the same claimed group in a short window
vectors: Fake alumni profile reaching out to former classmates listed publicly on a school's alumni page
Fake industry-group member profile targeting attendees of a public conference list
rootCauses: Publicly available alumni/membership directories enabling easy targeting
No verification mechanism for claimed group affiliation on social platforms
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Security awareness training on verifying claimed shared affiliations before trusting a new contact
ITID-11717.response: Report the profile; advise the target to verify affiliation claims independently before engaging further.
metrics: Count of fake affiliation profile reports per quarter
ITID-11717.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11712/ITID-11713/ITID-11714 by the claimed-affiliation basis for trust rather than a professional or personal-relationship persona.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Alumni/Group Affiliation Profile
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile falsely claiming shared affiliation (alumni network, professional association, former colleague, shared employer history) to build trust with a target before a scam or data-harvesting attempt.

steps.title: Preserve the fake profile and conversation
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile including the claimed affiliation details and the message thread with the target.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Contain any exposed data or accounts
steps.desc: If the target shared credentials, confidential information, or made a payment, contain accordingly (credential reset, data-loss assessment, or fraud recovery contact).
steps.outcome: Any exposure contained.

steps.title: Track the report to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up until the profile is removed.
steps.outcome: Fake profile removed.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm any containment actions are complete and the fake profile is removed.
steps.outcome: Full resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the false-affiliation tactic
steps.desc: Record the specific trust-building tactic used for awareness content, since shared-affiliation claims are an effective and under-recognized pretext.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Verify the claimed affiliation against real records
steps.desc: Check whether the claimed shared history (alumni year, former role, association membership) matches any real record, or is entirely fabricated to build false rapport.
steps.outcome: Claimed affiliation confirmed false.
steps.abort: If the affiliation turns out to be genuine and this is a legitimate contact, close as a false positive.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation/fake-account report
steps.desc: Report the fake profile to the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Determine what the profile ultimately requested
steps.desc: Establish the end goal of the contact (data harvesting, investment scam, further introduction requests to widen the target's network) and whether the target complied.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the ask and any compliance established.

ITID-11718.def: A fake social media profile constructed using an actual real person's stolen name, photos, and biographical details — distinct from a wholly invented persona — used to deceive that real person's actual contacts or to commit fraud in their name.
ITID-11718.purpose: Captures a fake profile built using a real person's stolen identity (name, photos, biographical details) rather than a wholly fabricated persona.
scopeIncludes: A duplicate/cloned profile using a real, identifiable third party's actual name and stolen photos
Identity theft profiles used to defraud the impersonated real person's own contacts
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of a specific named internal executive/colleague (see ITID-11713, which covers internal-identity impersonation specifically)
AI-generated synthetic profiles with no real underlying stolen identity (see ITID-11719)
ITID-11718.severity: Medium-High given direct harm to the impersonated real individual's reputation as well as the deceived targets.
ITID-11718.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection/legal if the impersonated individual is an employee or notable public-facing representative of the organization.
indicators: A profile using a real, identifiable individual's photos and biographical details without their knowledge
The impersonated individual reporting they did not create the profile
vectors: Cloning a real person's public photos and bio to create a duplicate profile
Using a stolen identity to solicit money or information from the real person's actual social connections
rootCauses: Publicly accessible personal photos/details enabling easy identity cloning
No proactive monitoring for duplicate profiles using employees' real identities
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Brand/impersonation monitoring for cloned employee identities
Security awareness training on identity-theft profile red flags
ITID-11718.detection: Relies mainly on the impersonated individual's or their contacts' reporting.
ITID-11718.response: Report and request platform takedown; support the impersonated individual with a documented incident record for any resulting disputes.
metrics: Count of confirmed stolen-identity profile takedowns per quarter
