ITID-11718.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11713 by covering theft of any real individual's identity generally (not limited to an internal executive/colleague context) and from ITID-11719 by using an actual real person's stolen identity rather than a wholly synthetic AI-generated one.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Profile Using Stolen Real Identity
playbook.description: For a reported fake social media profile built using a real, stolen identity (a genuine private individual's actual name, photos, and personal details, used without their knowledge), distinct from impersonating a known executive/colleague.

steps.title: Preserve the fake profile as evidence
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile, its content, and any activity before it can be altered.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Notify the real identity owner if they are unaware
steps.desc: If the identity owner is an employee or known contact and unaware their identity is being used, notify them directly.
steps.outcome: Real identity owner informed.

steps.title: Track the report to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up until the fake profile is removed.
steps.outcome: Fake profile removed.

steps.title: Confirm removal and advise the identity owner on further protection
steps.desc: Confirm the profile is down; advise the real identity owner on setting up alerts/monitoring for future misuse of their identity.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed; identity owner advised.

steps.title: Log the incident
steps.desc: Record the incident and resolution time for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the real identity owner is an employee, customer, or unrelated third party
steps.desc: Establish who the stolen identity belongs to and their relationship (if any) to the organization.
steps.outcome: Real identity owner and relationship established.

steps.title: Warn any parties the fake profile has contacted
steps.desc: If the profile has been used to scam or contact others, warn those parties where identifiable.
steps.outcome: Contacted parties warned.

steps.title: Assess what the fake profile is being used for
steps.desc: Determine whether the stolen identity is being used to scam others, harass someone, or gain trust for a broader social-engineering campaign.
steps.outcome: Purpose of the fake profile established.

steps.title: File a platform impersonation report, ideally with the real identity owner's involvement
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report to the platform; identity-theft-based reports are often processed faster when the real individual co-files or verifies their identity.
steps.outcome: Report filed with platform.

ITID-11719.def: A fake social media profile using AI-generated (deepfake/synthetic) photos and often AI-generated biographical text, constructed as an entirely fabricated persona with no direct real-world individual whose identity was stolen.
ITID-11719.purpose: Captures a fake profile built using wholly AI-generated synthetic photos and/or biographical content, with no single real underlying stolen identity.
scopeIncludes: Profiles using AI-generated (e.g., GAN-produced) photos with no real matching individual
AI-generated biographical/backstory content used to make a synthetic persona appear authentic
scopeExcludes: A profile built using an actual real person's stolen photos/identity (see ITID-11718)
AI voice clone/deepfake impersonation calls, which occur via voice rather than a static social media profile (see ITID-11216, under Pretexting)
ITID-11719.severity: Medium-High — synthetic AI-generated identities are increasingly difficult to detect via reverse image search, raising the effectiveness of the resulting deception.
ITID-11719.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection if used at scale as part of a broader coordinated campaign (see ITID-11716).
indicators: Profile photo showing common AI-generation artifacts (asymmetric earrings, irregular background blending, unnatural texture)
No reverse-image-search match despite the photo appearing to be of a real person
vectors: AI-generated profile photo used to create a synthetic persona with no traceable real-world identity
AI-generated biography paired with a synthetic photo to construct an entirely fabricated professional persona
rootCauses: Reverse-image-search verification is ineffective against synthetic AI-generated photos, reducing a previously reliable detection method
Rapid accessibility of AI image-generation tools lowering the cost of creating a convincing fake persona
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Security awareness training on AI-generated image artifacts and detection limitations
Platform-level AI-generated content detection/labeling where available
ITID-11719.detection: Limited; traditional reverse-image-search verification does not work against synthetic photos, and dedicated AI-image-detection tooling is still maturing.
ITID-11719.response: Report the profile to the platform; treat lack of a reverse-image match as inconclusive rather than confirmation of legitimacy.
metrics: Count of confirmed AI-generated synthetic profile reports per quarter
ITID-11719.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11718 by the persona being wholly AI-synthesized with no single real underlying identity stolen.

playbook.name: Response: AI-Generated Synthetic Profile (Deepfake Photo/Bio)
playbook.description: For a reported social media profile using an entirely AI-generated identity — a synthetic (non-real-person) deepfake photo and fabricated bio — to build a false persona for scam, disinformation, or social-engineering purposes.

steps.title: Preserve the profile and flag indicators of AI generation
steps.desc: Screenshot the profile and note visual/behavioral indicators suggesting an AI-generated photo (artifacting around ears/hair/background, inconsistent details) and bio (generic or inconsistent life details).
steps.guidance: Note indicators as supporting evidence, not as the sole basis for the report — platforms still primarily act on behavioral/policy violations, not just 'this looks AI-generated.'
steps.outcome: Profile evidence and AI-generation indicators documented.

steps.title: Contain any exposure from a targeted employee/customer
steps.desc: If the profile scammed or obtained information from a target, contain accordingly (credential reset, fraud recovery contact, or data-loss assessment).
steps.outcome: Any exposure contained.

steps.title: Track the report and any related-profile cluster to takedown
steps.desc: Follow up on the report and any related profiles identified until removed.
steps.outcome: Profile(s) removed.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm the profile is down and any affected party's exposure is resolved.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the AI-generation indicators observed for detection tuning
steps.desc: Record the specific indicators observed for this synthetic profile to help train awareness content and any automated detection tooling in use.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine the profile's purpose and any target
steps.desc: Establish what the synthetic profile is being used for (romance/financial scam, fake reviews/endorsements, disinformation, building fake social proof) and who it has targeted.
steps.outcome: Purpose and targets established.

steps.title: File a platform report citing synthetic-media/fake-account policy
steps.desc: Report the profile, referencing the platform's synthetic media or inauthentic account policy in addition to general impersonation/scam categories.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Check for related synthetic profiles
steps.desc: AI-generated personas are often deployed in batches; check for similarly-styled profiles that may be part of the same operation.
steps.outcome: Related profiles identified if present.

ITID-11721.def: A scam conducted via a social media platform's direct messaging feature, without enough detail captured to classify the specific scam type or account status (fake vs. compromised).
ITID-11721.purpose: Catch-all for a direct-messaging scam that does not fit a more specific leaf under Direct Messaging Scams.
scopeIncludes: DM scam reports logged before the specific scam type or account status is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once detail is known
ITID-11721.severity: Low-to-Medium by default; reassess once the scam type and account status are known.
ITID-11721.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassification once more detail is available.
indicators: Report of an unsolicited or suspicious direct message of unclear scam type
vectors: Direct message of unclear scam type
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Security awareness training
metrics: Count of DM scam reports pending reclassification
ITID-11721.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported direct message scam on a social media platform that does not fit a more specific sub-category.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and sender profile
steps.desc: Screenshot the full message thread and the sender's profile before the user blocks or the sender deletes messages.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Contain any exposed account, data, or funds
steps.desc: Reset credentials, revoke sessions, or initiate fraud recovery as applicable based on what was shared.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm any containment actions are complete.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the scam pattern
steps.desc: Record the scam type and sender pattern for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine the scam type and what was requested
steps.desc: Interview the user to establish the scam pattern (payment request, link, credential harvest, etc.) and whether they acted on it.
steps.outcome: Scam type and interaction status confirmed.

steps.title: Block and report the sender
steps.desc: Block the sender at the platform level and file a scam report with the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked and reported.

steps.title: Assess scope across the organization
steps.desc: Check for other reports of DMs from the same sender or matching pattern.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11722.def: An attacker who has compromised a real person's social media account uses it to send scam direct messages to that account's real contacts, exploiting the target's existing trust in the account owner.
ITID-11722.purpose: Captures a DM scam sent from a genuinely compromised real account belonging to someone the target actually knows and trusts.
scopeIncludes: Scam messages sent from an account confirmed to belong to a real, known contact of the target, now under attacker control
Requests for money or gift cards sent from a compromised friend's/colleague's account
scopeExcludes: A scam sent from a wholly fake profile with no prior compromise (see ITID-11711 through ITID-11719, under Fake Profiles, or the other Direct Messaging Scams siblings)
Group chat/community infiltration where the attacker joins as a new participant rather than hijacking an existing member's account (see ITID-11726)
ITID-11722.severity: High — messages from a genuinely compromised known-contact account carry far higher trust and click-through/compliance likelihood than a fake profile.
ITID-11722.priority: P1 given both the account-compromise dimension and the elevated trust exploited.
ITID-11722.escalation: Escalate to the account owner immediately to begin account-recovery steps; escalate to SOC if the compromised account belongs to an employee using it for business purposes.
indicators: Message from a known contact with an uncharacteristic tone, urgency, or request
Account owner reports they did not send the message
vectors: Credential-stuffing or phishing compromise of the sender's account, then mass-messaging their contact list
Session-token theft enabling access without needing the sender's password
rootCauses: Lack of multi-factor authentication on the compromised account
Password reuse across platforms enabling credential-stuffing compromise
mitreTechniques: T1586.001 Compromise Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
Security awareness training on verifying out-of-character requests via a separate channel
ITID-11722.detection: Relies mainly on the account owner and contacts reporting; some platforms provide account-compromise alerts to the owner.
ITID-11722.response: Assist the account owner with password reset/MFA enablement and account recovery; warn their contacts not to act on messages sent during the compromise window.
metrics: Count of compromised-account DM scam incidents per quarter
ITID-11722.notes: Differentiated from every other Direct Messaging Scams sibling by requiring the sending account to be a genuinely compromised real account, not a fake or newly created one.

playbook.name: Response: Compromised Real Account DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM scam sent from a genuinely compromised, real account (a real friend or colleague's actual account, now controlled by an attacker), rather than a fake profile.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and note the account being used
steps.desc: Screenshot the message thread and confirm this is the real, known account of a friend/colleague, not a lookalike fake profile.
steps.guidance: Distinguishing a compromised real account from a fake profile matters — the real account owner needs to be warned and helped.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message came from a genuine but compromised account.

steps.title: Contain any exposure on the target's side
steps.desc: If the target shared money, credentials, or data, contain accordingly (fraud recovery contact, credential reset).
steps.outcome: Target-side exposure contained.

steps.title: Confirm the attacker no longer controls the account
steps.desc: Follow up with the real owner to confirm they have regained exclusive control, changed the password, and reviewed connected apps/sessions.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed recovered by the real owner.

steps.title: Confirm resolution on both sides
steps.desc: Confirm the target's exposure is resolved and the real account owner has regained control.
steps.outcome: Full resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the incident and remind users to verify unusual requests out-of-band
steps.desc: Record the pattern; reinforce that unusual requests from known contacts, even via their real account, should be verified through a separate channel before acting.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and whether the target complied
steps.desc: Establish the scam ask (money, gift cards, further personal data) and whether the target acted on it.
steps.outcome: Scope of the ask and compliance established.

steps.title: Advise the real account owner on account recovery
steps.desc: Point the compromised account owner to the platform's account-recovery process to regain control and remove the attacker.
steps.outcome: Account owner initiated recovery.

steps.title: Attempt to notify the real account owner through an out-of-band channel
steps.desc: Contact the real account owner via phone, email, or another platform to alert them their account is compromised — do not rely on the compromised account's own channel.
steps.outcome: Real account owner notified where reachable.

steps.title: Report the compromised account to the platform
steps.desc: File a compromised-account report with the platform's trust and safety team, distinct from a fake-profile report, since this speeds recovery for the real owner.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

ITID-11723.def: A direct message offering a fake cryptocurrency or investment giveaway, requiring the target to send funds (often crypto) first with the promise of a larger amount returned, which is never paid back.
ITID-11723.purpose: Captures a DM scam offering a fake cryptocurrency or investment giveaway requiring an upfront 'send to receive double back' payment.
scopeIncludes: 'Send X crypto, receive 2X back' giveaway DM scams
Fake investment 'guaranteed returns' pitches delivered via DM
scopeExcludes: A romance scam profile that later pivots to a crypto investment ask as part of a long-term relationship (see ITID-11715, under Fake Profiles) — this ITID covers a direct, short-duration investment pitch with no romantic relationship-building
Fake job offer DM scams (see ITID-11724)
ITID-11723.severity: Medium-High given typically immediate and often substantial financial loss.
ITID-11723.priority: P2, escalating to P1 once funds are confirmed sent.
ITID-11723.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance immediately upon confirming any funds were transferred.
indicators: Guaranteed-return or double-your-money investment claim
Request to send cryptocurrency to an unfamiliar wallet address first
vectors: DM impersonating a celebrity or known investor promoting a giveaway
Fake trading bot/investment platform screenshot used as fabricated social proof
rootCauses: Lack of awareness that legitimate giveaways never require sending funds first
Cryptocurrency transactions being irreversible, removing any recovery path once sent
controls: Security awareness training on crypto/investment giveaway scam patterns
Platform-level detection of known scam-wallet-address patterns where available
ITID-11723.detection: Relies mainly on victim reporting; blockchain analysis can sometimes trace funds but rarely enables recovery.
ITID-11723.response: Advise the target that cryptocurrency transactions are not reversible; report the profile and wallet address where possible.
metrics: Count of crypto/investment DM scam reports per quarter
Total confirmed financial loss reported
ITID-11723.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11715 (Romance Scam Profile) by the absence of a long-term relationship-building phase; this is a direct, transactional investment pitch.

playbook.name: Response: Crypto/Investment Giveaway DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM promising a cryptocurrency or investment giveaway/doubling scheme, typically requiring an upfront 'send crypto to receive more back' payment.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and sender profile
steps.desc: Screenshot the message thread, sender profile, and any linked wallet address or external site.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved including wallet address if provided.

steps.title: Advise immediate reporting to the exchange and financial fraud authorities
steps.desc: If funds were sent via a cryptocurrency exchange, advise the target to report to that exchange's fraud team immediately — some exchanges can freeze funds if reported quickly enough.
steps.guidance: Time is critical; funds moved through multiple wallets quickly become unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Exchange/fraud authority notified as quickly as possible.

steps.title: Confirm no further contact and document loss outcome
steps.desc: Confirm the target has blocked the sender and record whether any funds were recovered.
steps.outcome: Resolution documented, including financial loss if unrecovered.

steps.title: Log the scam pattern and wallet address for threat intel
steps.desc: Record the giveaway pattern and wallet address; contribute to threat intel/blocklist sharing where appropriate.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the target sent any funds
steps.desc: Interview the target to confirm whether cryptocurrency or fiat funds were sent, and the amount.
steps.guidance: Cryptocurrency transactions are generally irreversible — establish this quickly to set expectations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether funds were sent and the amount.
steps.abort: If no funds were sent, skip fraud-recovery containment and proceed to reporting only.

steps.title: Block and report the sender to the platform
steps.desc: Block the sender and file a scam report with the platform's trust and safety team, including the wallet address as evidence.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked and reported.

steps.title: Trace the destination wallet address if funds were sent
steps.desc: Record the destination wallet address and, where available, use blockchain analysis tooling or the exchange's fraud team to attempt tracing.
steps.outcome: Destination address documented for reporting purposes.

ITID-11724.def: A direct message offering the target an unsolicited job opportunity — often with unrealistically high pay for minimal work — used to harvest personal/banking data under the guise of onboarding, or to extract an upfront fee for 'equipment' or 'training'.
ITID-11724.purpose: Captures a fake job offer sent via direct message to a job seeker, used to harvest personal/financial data or extract upfront fees.
scopeIncludes: Unsolicited DM job offers requiring bank details for 'direct deposit setup' before any real hiring process
Fake job offers requiring the target to purchase equipment or pay a training fee upfront
scopeExcludes: A fake recruiter profile used to build trust before the offer is sent (see ITID-11712, under Fake Profiles) — this ITID covers the scam message/offer content itself
Fake job referral bonus offers targeting an existing employee rather than an external job seeker (see ITID-11518, under Fake Incentives)
ITID-11724.severity: Medium-High given the request for sensitive banking/personal data under a hiring pretext.
ITID-11724.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if banking details or an upfront payment were disclosed.
ITID-11724.escalation: Escalate to fraud/finance if the target disclosed banking details or made a payment.
indicators: Job offer with no interview process before requesting personal/banking data
Unrealistically high pay for minimal-effort work
Request for an upfront payment for equipment or training
vectors: Mass DM campaign targeting users who list themselves as 'open to work'
Fake job offer requiring the target to deposit a check and wire back a portion (money-mule recruitment)
rootCauses: Job seekers under financial pressure more susceptible to urgency and unrealistic pay claims
Lack of awareness that legitimate employers never request banking details before a formal offer
controls: Security awareness training on fake job offer red flags
ITID-11724.response: Advise the target not to share banking details or make payments; report the sending account.
metrics: Count of fake job offer DM scam reports per quarter
ITID-11724.notes: Scope decision: this ITID covers the fake job offer message content itself; the fabricated recruiter persona used to initiate contact is tracked under ITID-11712 to avoid double-counting the same incident across two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Job Offer DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM offering a fake job/gig opportunity, typically progressing to an upfront-fee request, fake check/overpayment scam, or credential/data harvesting under the guise of onboarding paperwork.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and any 'offer' documents
steps.desc: Screenshot the message thread and preserve any onboarding forms, fake checks, or documents sent.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Advise on financial containment if a fake check or payment was involved
steps.desc: If the target deposited a fake check or sent money/gift cards, advise them to contact their bank immediately and not to spend any related funds — fake check deposits typically bounce after several days, leaving the depositor liable.
steps.outcome: Target has contacted their bank; understands fake check risk.

steps.title: Confirm resolution and any recovered funds
steps.desc: Follow up to confirm containment steps were completed and document any financial loss.
steps.outcome: Resolution documented.

steps.title: Log the scam pattern and warn if impersonating the organization
steps.desc: Record the scam pattern; if the fake job offer impersonated the organization's own brand, alert HR/talent acquisition and brand protection.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; relevant teams alerted if applicable.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and how far the target progressed
steps.desc: Establish whether the target provided personal/banking details, deposited a fake check, sent money, or downloaded any file.
steps.outcome: Scope of the ask and target's actions established.

steps.title: If personal/financial data was submitted, advise identity-theft precautions
steps.desc: Advise the target to monitor credit reports and consider a fraud alert if sensitive personal or banking details were provided.
steps.outcome: Target taking identity-protection steps.

steps.title: Check whether the offer impersonates a real organization
steps.desc: If the fake job posting claims affiliation with a real company (potentially your own organization or a known brand), confirm with that entity's HR/security team.
steps.outcome: Impersonated organization identified and notified if applicable.

steps.title: Block and report the sender
steps.desc: Block the sender and file a scam report with the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked and reported.

ITID-11725.def: An attacker monitors public complaints or mentions of a brand and sends a DM posing as that brand's official customer support, directing the target to a phishing link or requesting account/payment details to 'resolve' the issue.
ITID-11725.purpose: Captures a fake customer support DM scam where an attacker poses as a brand's official support account to harvest credentials or payment data.
scopeIncludes: DM impersonating a brand's support account, sent in response to a public complaint about that brand
Fake support DM requesting account credentials or payment card details to process a refund
scopeExcludes: A fake vendor/brand corporate profile used as the persistent fake identity itself (see ITID-11714, under Fake Profiles) — this ITID covers the specific support-interaction scam message
Fake platform security alert credential harvest impersonating the social media platform itself rather than a brand using the platform (see ITID-11738)
ITID-11725.severity: Medium-High — this scam specifically targets customers already primed to trust a support response.
ITID-11725.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if payment or credential data was disclosed.
ITID-11725.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection/customer support teams to warn customers and to fraud/finance if payment data was disclosed.
indicators: Support DM received shortly after a public complaint, from an account not matching the brand's verified support handle
Support DM directing to a link outside the brand's known domains
vectors: Monitoring public brand mentions/complaints to identify targets actively expecting a support response
Fake support account using a near-identical handle to the real brand support account
rootCauses: Brand's official support handle not consistently verified/badged, making impersonation harder to distinguish
Customers unaware of the brand's actual support handle
controls: Verified/badged official support account
Published, clearly communicated list of the brand's legitimate support handles
ITID-11725.detection: Relies mainly on customer/employee reporting and periodic brand-monitoring sweeps for near-identical support handles.
ITID-11725.response: Report and request takedown of the fake support account; publicly clarify the brand's legitimate support handle.
metrics: Count of fake customer support DM scam reports per quarter
ITID-11725.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11738 (Fake Platform Security Alert Credential Harvest) by impersonating a brand's customer support specifically, not the social media platform's own security team.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Customer Support DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM from an account impersonating a platform's or brand's official customer support, typically responding to a public complaint to lure the user into a private conversation for credential or payment harvesting.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and the fake support account
steps.desc: Screenshot the message thread and the impersonating account's profile, noting how it mimics the real support account (name, badge, avatar).
steps.guidance: This scam typically targets users who recently posted a public complaint, watching for the opening to reach out.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: If credentials or payment details were shared, contain accordingly
steps.desc: Force password reset/session revocation on the affected account, or advise the target to contact their card issuer if payment details were shared.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.

steps.title: Confirm resolution
steps.desc: Confirm containment actions are complete.
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the pattern and remind users to verify support accounts
steps.desc: Record the pattern; add to awareness content that legitimate support will never DM first asking for a password or payment details.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Confirm this is not the real support account
steps.desc: Cross-check the account handle against the platform/brand's officially verified support account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed as an impersonating account.
steps.abort: If it is the genuine verified account, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Block and report the fake support account
steps.desc: Block the account and file an impersonation report with the platform's trust and safety team, specifically flagging it as fake customer support.
steps.outcome: Account blocked and reported.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and whether the target complied
steps.desc: Establish whether the target was asked for a password, payment card details, or to click a 'verification' link, and whether they complied.
steps.outcome: Scope of the ask and compliance established.

ITID-11726.def: An attacker joins a group chat, forum, or online community (often one with an established shared interest or trust, such as an investment or hobbyist group) as a new member, building credibility within the group before targeting individual members with a scam via direct message.
ITID-11726.purpose: Captures an attacker joining a group chat or online community as a new participant specifically to scam existing members from within.
scopeIncludes: An attacker joining an investment/trading group chat and building apparent credibility before privately DM-ing members with a scam
Infiltration of a hobbyist or support community to identify and privately target vulnerable members
scopeExcludes: A scam sent from a genuinely compromised existing member's account (see ITID-11722)
A single unsolicited DM with no prior group infiltration/credibility-building phase (see ITID-11721 or the relevant more specific sibling)
ITID-11726.severity: Medium-High — the group's existing trust context is exploited to lend credibility the attacker has not earned individually.
ITID-11726.escalation: Escalate to the group's moderators/administrators to remove the infiltrating account and warn other members.
indicators: A relatively new group member privately messaging multiple other members shortly after joining
Group members reporting a private DM scam attempt following interaction in the group
vectors: Joining an investment group chat, posting credible-seeming content publicly, then privately soliciting individual members
Infiltrating a support community to identify and privately target emotionally vulnerable members
rootCauses: Group moderation not screening new members or monitoring for a pattern of private outreach following group activity
Members conflating group-level trust with individual trustworthiness of any given member
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Group moderation/new-member vetting
Community guidance warning members not to trust unsolicited private DMs from fellow group members
ITID-11726.detection: Relies mainly on member/moderator reporting; some platforms provide moderation tooling to flag mass private-messaging behavior from a single account.
ITID-11726.response: Remove the infiltrating account, notify group members of the pattern, and report to the platform if mass-messaging behavior is confirmed.
metrics: Count of confirmed group infiltration scam reports per quarter
ITID-11726.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11722 by the attacker operating a new/infiltrating account rather than a hijacked existing member's account.

playbook.name: Response: Group Chat/Community Infiltration Scam
playbook.description: For a reported scam where an attacker infiltrates a group chat, community server, or forum the target trusts, posing as a genuine member before pivoting to a private DM scam.

steps.title: Preserve evidence from both the group and the resulting private DM
steps.desc: Screenshot the attacker's activity within the group/community (how they built credibility) and the subsequent private message where the scam occurred.
steps.outcome: Full context from group infiltration to private scam preserved.

steps.title: Alert the group/community moderators
steps.desc: Notify the moderators of the group/community so they can remove the attacker's account and warn other members.
steps.outcome: Moderators alerted and taking action.

steps.title: Confirm resolution across the group and the target
steps.desc: Confirm the attacker was removed from the group and any target-side exposure is resolved.
steps.outcome: Full resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the infiltration tactic and warn community members
steps.desc: Record the tactic and, where appropriate, ask moderators to remind members that group membership alone is not proof of trustworthiness for private requests.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; community warned.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and whether the target complied
steps.desc: Establish the scam ask and whether the target acted on it.
steps.outcome: Scope of the ask and compliance established.

steps.title: Contain any exposure on the target's side
steps.desc: If the target shared credentials, data, or funds, contain accordingly.
steps.outcome: Target-side exposure contained.

steps.title: Check whether other group/community members were targeted
steps.desc: Ask the group/community moderators whether other members received similar private messages from the same account.
steps.outcome: Scope across the community established.

steps.title: Block and report the attacker account to the platform
steps.desc: Block the account and file a scam report with the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Account blocked and reported.

ITID-11727.def: An attacker, via direct message, obtains or fabricates compromising images/video of the target (or claims to) and threatens to release them to the target's contacts or publicly unless a payment is made.
ITID-11727.purpose: Captures a sextortion scam conducted via direct message, where the attacker threatens to release compromising material unless paid.
scopeIncludes: DM-based extortion threatening release of real or fabricated compromising material
Extortion following a catfishing/romance approach that escalated to obtaining compromising material
scopeExcludes: A romance scam pursued purely for financial gain with no extortion/threat component (see ITID-11715, under Fake Profiles)
Video call deepfake combined with a physical follow-up, which is a different hybrid pattern entirely (see ITID-11926, under Cyber-Physical Social Engineering)
ITID-11727.severity: High — sextortion carries severe psychological harm risk to the victim in addition to financial loss.
ITID-11727.priority: P1 given the psychological-harm and safety risk to the victim.
ITID-11727.escalation: Escalate immediately to trained victim-support resources and, where the target is a minor or safety risk is indicated, to law enforcement.
indicators: Threat to release compromising material to the target's contact list unless paid
Rapid escalation from initial contact to a request for compromising material
vectors: Attacker posing as a romantic interest to obtain compromising material before threatening release
Fabricated/deepfake compromising material used without any material ever actually being obtained
rootCauses: Lack of awareness of sextortion patterns and available reporting resources
Victims deterred from reporting due to shame or fear of the material being released regardless
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Security awareness training on sextortion patterns and reporting resources
Access to trained victim-support and mental health resources
ITID-11727.detection: Relies entirely on victim reporting; no automated technical signal.
ITID-11727.response: Provide immediate access to victim-support resources; advise the target not to pay, to preserve all evidence, and to report to the platform and, where appropriate, law enforcement.
metrics: Count of sextortion reports per quarter
Count referred to law enforcement/victim-support resources
ITID-11727.notes: This is the highest-severity leaf in the Direct Messaging Scams group given the psychological-harm dimension distinct from purely financial DM scams.

playbook.name: Response: Sextortion DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM-based sextortion attempt, where an attacker (often after obtaining a compromising image/video or fabricating one) threatens to release it unless paid, targeting an employee.

steps.title: Handle the report with strict confidentiality and support
steps.desc: Receive the report discreetly, limit access to case details to those who strictly need to know, and reassure the employee they are not at fault.
steps.guidance: This is a sensitive personal-welfare matter first and a security incident second — prioritize the employee's wellbeing and privacy throughout.
steps.outcome: Employee feels safe disclosing full details; case access restricted.

steps.title: Advise on and support law enforcement reporting
steps.desc: Sextortion is a crime in most jurisdictions; support the employee in reporting to law enforcement and, where applicable, a specialized sextortion/child-exploitation reporting body if a minor is involved.
steps.guidance: If a minor is involved in any capacity, treat as a mandatory reporting matter and involve legal/law enforcement immediately.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement report filed with the employee's consent (or mandatorily if a minor is involved).

steps.title: Confirm no corporate systems or accounts were leveraged in the extortion
steps.desc: Confirm the attacker did not obtain the material via, or is not threatening exposure through, any corporate account or device.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no corporate-system involvement, or contained if found.

steps.title: Provide continued support and confirm the threat has stopped
steps.desc: Follow up with the employee, connect them to employee assistance/counseling resources, and monitor for renewed contact from the attacker.
steps.outcome: Employee supported; threat activity confirmed stopped or ongoing monitoring in place.

steps.title: Log the incident with strict confidentiality
steps.desc: Record only the facts necessary for organizational risk tracking, with strict access controls on the case record given its sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with appropriate confidentiality.

steps.title: Preserve evidence without further engaging the attacker
steps.desc: With the employee's consent, screenshot the threatening messages and attacker profile; advise the employee to stop responding to the attacker immediately.
steps.guidance: Do not pay, and do not continue negotiating — this typically escalates demands rather than resolving the situation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; further engagement with the attacker stopped.

steps.title: Report the attacker account and content to the platform
steps.desc: File an urgent report with the platform's trust and safety team; most major platforms have expedited handling for sextortion and non-consensual imagery.
steps.outcome: Account and content reported for priority handling.

steps.title: Determine whether any content has actually been shared and whether payment was made
steps.desc: Establish (sensitively) whether compromising content genuinely exists and was sent, whether it appears to be fabricated/deepfaked, and whether any payment was made.
steps.outcome: Facts of the situation established for appropriate response.

steps.title: Register content with a hash-matching takedown service if available
steps.desc: If compromising imagery exists, consider services (such as StopNCII) that create a content hash to help platforms proactively block re-uploads without the employee having to share the image itself.
steps.outcome: Content hash registered where the employee consents.

ITID-11728.def: A direct message falsely claims the target's account is at risk of suspension, has been flagged, or requires urgent 'verification'/'recovery' action, directing them to a phishing page that harvests their login credentials.
ITID-11728.purpose: Captures a DM scam falsely claiming the target's account requires urgent verification or recovery action, used to harvest credentials.
scopeIncludes: DM claiming an account will be suspended unless the target 'verifies' via an external link
DM posing as a 'recovery' step after a fabricated claim that the target's account was hacked
scopeExcludes: The broader, platform-wide fake 'account flagged/under review' campaign delivered via any channel (see ITID-11734, under Credential Harvesting Campaigns) — this ITID covers the specific instance delivered as a targeted DM
Fake verification badge credential harvest specifically offering a badge/checkmark rather than claiming an account risk (see ITID-11735)
ITID-11728.severity: Medium-High given the direct credential-harvesting objective.
ITID-11728.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were entered.
ITID-11728.escalation: Escalate to SOC if the account has any link to corporate use (e.g., an official corporate social media account).
indicators: DM urgently claiming account suspension/flagging with a link outside the platform's own domain
Link leading to a login page with a URL that does not match the actual platform
vectors: Mass DM campaign impersonating the platform's own automated account-security notifications
Fake 'recovery' link sent after a prior fake claim that the account was compromised
rootCauses: Lack of awareness that platforms rarely if ever DM account-security notices through direct message rather than in-app/email notifications
No published guidance on the platform's actual account-security notification channels
controls: Security awareness training on verifying account-security notices only through official in-app channels
Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
ITID-11728.detection: Relies mainly on user/platform reporting; some platforms provide in-app warnings for known phishing link domains.
ITID-11728.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; report the phishing link.
metrics: Count of fake verification/recovery DM scam reports per quarter
ITID-11728.notes: Scope decision: this ITID is for the DM-delivered instance specifically; the same pretext delivered as a broader multi-vector campaign is tracked under ITID-11734 to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Verification/Account Recovery DM Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM impersonating the platform itself, claiming the target's account is at risk and needs 'verification' or 'recovery' action, which actually harvests credentials or session tokens.

steps.title: Preserve the DM thread and confirm it did not come from the platform's official channel
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and confirm platform DMs from official accounts are distinguishable by verified badges/official handles; check whether this sender matches.
steps.guidance: Genuine platforms virtually never initiate account-verification requests via ordinary user-to-user DM.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the message is not from a legitimate platform channel.

steps.title: If credentials were entered, contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on the targeted social media/corporate account.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access was established
steps.desc: Check the account for unexpected connected apps, changed recovery details, or active sessions from unfamiliar devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials and normal access.
steps.outcome: User has confirmed-clean access.

steps.title: Log the campaign and clarify what legitimate verification looks like
steps.desc: Record findings; consider reminding users how genuine platform verification/recovery communications are actually delivered.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; user guidance clarified if warranted.

steps.title: Determine whether the target clicked any link or entered credentials
steps.desc: Interview the target and, where possible, check for any resulting login activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block and report the sender
steps.desc: Block the sender and file a phishing/impersonation report with the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked and reported.

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same fake verification lure.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11729.def: An attacker sends a QR code image or a shortened URL directly within a platform's direct messaging feature, leading the target to a credential-harvesting page or a malicious download, entirely within the messaging interaction.
ITID-11729.purpose: Captures a malicious QR code or link embedded directly within a direct message, without any separate cross-channel bridging step.
scopeIncludes: A QR code image sent as a DM attachment leading to a phishing or malware destination
A shortened/obfuscated URL sent within a DM leading to a phishing or malware destination
scopeExcludes: A QR code deliberately used to bridge from a different channel (print, screen-share, physical signage) into a mobile device as part of a broader hybrid campaign (see ITID-11915, under Multi-Channel Phishing)
QR code phishing delivered via email (see ITID-11115, ITID-11129)
ITID-11729.severity: Medium-High — a QR code within a DM is difficult for platform-level link-scanning to inspect, since the destination is embedded in an image rather than plain text.
ITID-11729.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were disclosed or malware was installed.
ITID-11729.escalation: Escalate to SOC if a corporate-connected device or account was affected.
indicators: DM containing a QR code image with no accompanying plain-text URL
Shortened URL within a DM with no context explaining its purpose
vectors: QR code image sent to evade platform text-based link scanning
Shortened URL disguising a phishing or malware destination
rootCauses: Platform link-scanning tools generally cannot inspect the destination encoded within an image-based QR code
Users conditioned to trust QR codes as inherently safe
controls: Security awareness training on scanning QR codes only from trusted, verified senders
Mobile device management (MDM) URL filtering on managed devices
ITID-11729.detection: Limited; platform-level automated link scanning generally cannot parse a QR code image's destination, making this evasive by design.
ITID-11729.response: Force credential reset if the destination was a login page and credentials were entered; scan the device if a download resulted.
metrics: Count of QR code/link-in-DM scam reports per quarter
detections: MDM URL filtering on managed devices
ITID-11729.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11915 by the QR code/link remaining entirely within the DM interaction, with no deliberate cross-channel/cross-device bridging step; a QR code used to move the target to an entirely different channel belongs under ITID-11915 instead.

playbook.name: Response: QR Code/Link-in-DM Malware or Credential Scam
playbook.description: For a reported DM containing a QR code image or shortened/obfuscated link that leads to malware installation or a credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Preserve the DM and the QR code/link without interacting with it directly
steps.desc: Screenshot the message; if analysis of the QR code or link is needed, use a sandboxed environment or URL-expansion tool rather than scanning/clicking from a live device.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved without further exposure.

steps.title: Isolate the device or contain the account depending on payload type
steps.desc: If malware was installed, isolate the device from corporate resources via MDM/conditional access; if credentials were entered, force a password reset and session revocation.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained appropriately for the payload type.

steps.title: Remove any installed malware
steps.desc: Uninstall the malicious payload via MDM/EDR or wipe the device if removal cannot be reliably confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and clean device state
steps.desc: Confirm the account and/or device are restored and clean before closing the case.
steps.outcome: Full resolution confirmed.

steps.title: Log the QR/link technique and payload
steps.desc: Record the delivery mechanism and payload identified for detection tuning and awareness content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Resolve the destination and determine what it delivers
steps.desc: Use a URL sandbox to resolve the QR code/link's true destination and determine whether it leads to malware or a credential-harvesting page.
steps.outcome: True destination and payload type identified.

steps.title: Block and report the sender
steps.desc: Block the sender and file a report with the platform's trust and safety team, including the resolved malicious destination.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked and reported.

steps.title: Determine whether the target scanned/clicked and what happened next
steps.desc: Interview the target and check MDM/EDR for any resulting app install, credential entry, or suspicious device behavior.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status and any resulting compromise.
steps.abort: If not scanned/clicked, proceed to blocklisting only.

ITID-11731.def: A campaign designed to harvest social media account credentials from targets, without enough detail captured to classify the specific pretext or mechanism used.
ITID-11731.purpose: Catch-all for a social media credential-harvesting campaign that does not fit a more specific leaf under Credential Harvesting Campaigns.
scopeIncludes: Credential-harvesting campaign reports logged before the specific pretext/mechanism is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the pretext/mechanism is known
ITID-11731.severity: Medium by default; reassess once the pretext and whether credentials were disclosed are known.
ITID-11731.priority: P2 by default given the credential-harvesting objective common to this Type.
ITID-11731.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately if credentials were disclosed.
indicators: Report of a suspected credential-harvesting attempt of unclear pretext
vectors: Credential-harvesting attempt of unclear pretext
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Security awareness training
Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
ITID-11731.detection: Relies primarily on user reporting pending classification.
ITID-11731.response: Document, force credential reset if disclosure occurred, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count of credential harvesting campaign reports pending reclassification
ITID-11731.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Social Media Credential Harvesting Campaign
playbook.description: For a reported social media credential-harvesting campaign that does not fit a more specific sub-category.

steps.title: Preserve the lure content and destination link
steps.desc: Screenshot the post/message/ad and record the destination link where credentials would be entered.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions, connected apps, or recovery-info changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the user has restored, confirmed-clean access.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the campaign
steps.desc: Record the lure and destination for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether credentials were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check identity provider logs for any correlating authentication activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If not interacted with, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the destination domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Assess campaign scope
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same lure or destination domain.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11732.def: A phishing page precisely mimicking a social media platform's real login page, designed to capture the username and password entered by a target who was directed there via any pretext.
ITID-11732.purpose: Captures the foundational technique of this Type — a straightforward fake login page mimicking a social media platform's real sign-in page.
scopeIncludes: A cloned/spoofed login page for any social media platform capturing entered credentials
Fake login pages distributed via link regardless of the delivery pretext, where the page itself (not the pretext) is the object of this ITID
scopeExcludes: Cases where the delivery pretext itself is the distinguishing/notable feature (fake flagged-account notice, fake verification badge offer, fake copyright notice, etc. — see ITID-11734 through ITID-11739)
OAuth/third-party app authorization harvesting, which does not use a spoofed login page at all (see ITID-11733)
ITID-11732.severity: High — a successful credential harvest on this leaf directly yields full account takeover.
ITID-11732.priority: P1 once credentials are confirmed entered.
ITID-11732.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately upon confirming credential entry; treat any linked corporate account as compromised.
indicators: Login page URL not matching the platform's actual domain
Page visually near-identical to the real login screen but hosted on an unrelated domain
vectors: Phishing link delivered via email, DM, or SMS leading to a cloned login page
Typosquatted domain closely resembling the platform's real domain
rootCauses: Lack of multi-factor authentication allowing a harvested password alone to grant account access
Users not checking the URL bar before entering credentials
controls: Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
Web/URL reputation filtering
Security awareness training on verifying login page URLs
ITID-11732.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains; SSO/platform login anomaly detection can flag credential use from an unusual location shortly after entry.
ITID-11732.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA immediately; report the phishing domain for takedown.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake login page credential harvests per quarter
ITID-11732.notes: Scope decision: this ITID is reserved for the generic spoofed-login-page technique where no other sibling's more specific pretext applies; siblings ITID-11734 through ITID-11739 each cover a login-page harvest distinguished by a specific delivery pretext.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Social Media Login Page
playbook.description: For a reported credential-harvesting page that closely mimics the real login page of a social media platform, typically reached via an ad, DM, or post.

steps.title: Preserve the fake login page and its URL
steps.desc: Screenshot the fake login page and record its exact URL, comparing it against the real platform's login domain.
steps.guidance: Use a sandboxed browser to view the page, not the corporate device directly.
steps.outcome: Fake page and URL preserved.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force password reset and full session/token revocation on the affected account, and re-enroll MFA on a verified device.
steps.outcome: Account secured with new credentials and fresh MFA.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions, connected third-party apps, or changed recovery details.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the user has restored, confirmed-clean access with new MFA.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the fake page and delivery vector
steps.desc: Record the URL, delivery vector, and takedown outcome for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine how the user reached the fake page and whether credentials were entered
steps.desc: Establish the delivery vector (ad, DM, search result, typosquat) and whether the user submitted their username/password.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector and interaction status confirmed.
steps.abort: If not interacted with, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the fake domain and report to the platform and hosting provider
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist; report both to the impersonated platform's trust and safety team and, where identifiable, the hosting provider/registrar for takedown.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked and reported for takedown.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Check whether MFA prevented full account takeover
steps.desc: If credentials were entered, check whether MFA was enabled on the account and whether an MFA challenge was also completed (indicating a real-time relay attack, not just static harvesting).
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether MFA blocked the attacker or was also bypassed.

ITID-11733.def: A target is lured (via a quiz, game, or utility app) into authorizing a malicious third-party application through the platform's legitimate OAuth consent flow, granting the attacker persistent API-level access to the target's account without ever capturing a password.
ITID-11733.purpose: Captures credential/data harvesting achieved via a malicious third-party app requesting OAuth authorization, rather than a spoofed login page.
scopeIncludes: Fake quiz/personality-test apps requesting broad OAuth permissions to a social media account
Malicious third-party apps retaining API access via an OAuth token after initial authorization
scopeExcludes: A spoofed login page directly capturing a username/password (see ITID-11732)
Spearphishing email specifically delivering an OAuth consent-phishing link outside the social media context (see ITID-11128, under a different Type)
Technical OAuth token abuse occurring post-compromise with no social-engineering consent step (see the ITID-331xx OAuth token abuse family)
ITID-11733.severity: High — OAuth-based access often persists independently of a password reset, making remediation materially harder than a standard credential harvest.
ITID-11733.priority: P1 once malicious app authorization is confirmed, given the persistence risk.
ITID-11733.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately; a password reset alone does not revoke OAuth app access, so explicit app-authorization revocation is required.
indicators: Unrecognized third-party app listed in the account's authorized-apps settings
Account activity (posts, messages) the owner did not perform, with no corresponding password change
vectors: Viral quiz/personality-test app requesting excessive OAuth scopes
Fake 'see who viewed your profile' app requiring authorization
rootCauses: Platform OAuth consent screens not clearly communicating the scope of access being granted
Users not periodically reviewing and revoking unused third-party app authorizations
controls: Periodic review and revocation of authorized third-party apps
Security awareness training on scrutinizing OAuth consent screens before authorizing
ITID-11733.detection: Platform-provided authorized-apps audit logs give a real technical signal once reviewed, though most users never proactively check this setting.
ITID-11733.response: Revoke the malicious app's authorization directly in account settings (a password reset alone is insufficient); review recent account activity for unauthorized actions.
metrics: Count of confirmed malicious OAuth app authorizations per quarter
detections: Authorized third-party app audit log review
ITID-11733.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11128 (email-delivered OAuth spear phishing) by occurring natively within the social media platform's own app ecosystem, and from the technical ITID-331xx OAuth abuse family by requiring an active social-engineering consent step rather than post-compromise technical token abuse.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Third-Party App/OAuth Authorization Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported incident where a malicious third-party application tricked a user into granting OAuth authorization to their social media account, giving the attacker persistent API-level access without needing the password.

steps.title: Identify the malicious app and the exact permissions granted
steps.desc: Have the user check their account's connected apps/authorized apps list and identify the suspicious app and the specific scopes it was granted (post on your behalf, read DMs, manage account, etc.).
steps.guidance: OAuth grants persist independently of a password change, which makes this distinct from a standard credential harvest.
steps.outcome: Malicious app and its exact granted scopes identified.

steps.title: Revoke the malicious app's OAuth authorization immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the app's access via the account's connected-apps settings — this is the critical containment step since a password reset alone does not remove OAuth-based access.
steps.outcome: Malicious app's access revoked.

steps.title: Undo any unauthorized changes made by the app
steps.desc: Remove any unauthorized posts, messages, or setting changes the app made while it had access.
steps.outcome: Account content/settings restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Confirm the account is clean and access fully revoked
steps.desc: Confirm no unauthorized app access remains and the account functions normally.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed clean.

steps.title: Log the app and educate on OAuth authorization risk
steps.desc: Record the malicious app's name and permissions requested; add to awareness content that granting app permissions can be as risky as sharing a password.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness content updated.

steps.title: Determine what the app has done with its access
steps.desc: Check the account's recent activity (posts made, messages sent, settings changed) for anything attributable to the malicious app's access.
steps.outcome: Scope of misuse established.

steps.title: Reset the account password as a precaution
steps.desc: Reset the password and review other connected apps for any additional unrecognized grants.
steps.outcome: Password reset; other connected apps reviewed.

steps.title: Assess whether other employees granted the same app access
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same malicious app to determine if this is an organization-wide campaign.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

steps.title: Report the malicious app to the platform
steps.desc: Report the app to the platform's developer/trust and safety team so it can be reviewed and potentially removed from the platform's app directory.
steps.outcome: Malicious app reported to the platform.

ITID-11734.def: A message falsely claiming the target's account has been flagged for a violation and is under review or pending suspension, directing them to a fake login page to 'appeal' or 'verify' their identity, harvesting their credentials.
ITID-11734.purpose: Captures a credential harvest delivered via a fake notice claiming the target's account has been flagged or is under review, pending suspension.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'your account has been flagged for suspicious activity' notices linking to a spoofed login page
Fake 'appeal your suspension' pages harvesting credentials
scopeExcludes: The same pretext delivered as a single targeted DM, where the DM channel itself is the object of the ITID (see ITID-11728, under Direct Messaging Scams)
Fake verification badge offers, which promise a benefit rather than threaten a penalty (see ITID-11735)
ITID-11734.severity: High — a suspension threat creates strong urgency, increasing the likelihood of a hasty, unverified credential submission.
ITID-11734.priority: P1 once credentials are confirmed entered.
ITID-11734.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately upon confirming credential entry.
indicators: Message threatening account suspension with a tight deadline
Link leading to a login page hosted outside the platform's actual domain
vectors: Mass email/DM campaign impersonating the platform's automated account-review notifications
Fake 'policy violation' notice referencing a vague or generic infraction
rootCauses: Users not verifying account-status notices through the platform's official in-app notification center
Suspension threats exploiting fear of losing access to an account with significant social/professional investment
controls: Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
Security awareness training on verifying account-status notices only via official in-app channels
ITID-11734.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake appeal page.
ITID-11734.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; report the phishing domain.
metrics: Count of confirmed flagged-account credential harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11734.notes: Scope decision: covers this pretext delivered broadly (email, in-app notification spoof, etc.); the identical pretext delivered specifically and only as a targeted DM is tracked under ITID-11728 to avoid double-counting the same incident across two branches.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Account Flagged/Under Review Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message falsely claiming the user's social media account has been flagged, reported, or is under review for a policy violation, pressuring them to 'appeal' via a credential-harvesting link.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm the account's real status
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and check the real account settings/notifications to confirm whether there is any genuine flag or review in progress.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; genuine account status confirmed.
steps.abort: If a genuine review is confirmed, redirect the user to the platform's real appeal process.

steps.title: If credentials were entered, contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions or connected apps.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the lure and clarify real appeal process communication
steps.desc: Record findings; clarify for users how the platform's genuine review/appeal notices actually look and arrive.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the link was clicked and credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user regarding interaction with the fake appeal link.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same fake 'account flagged' lure.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11735.def: A message offering the target a free or discounted official verification badge (checkmark) for their social media account, directing them to a fake login/application page that harvests their credentials or payment card data.
ITID-11735.purpose: Captures a credential harvest delivered via a fake offer of a verified/checkmark badge status.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'apply for verification' pages harvesting login credentials
Fake paid-verification offers harvesting payment card data alongside credentials
scopeExcludes: Fake flagged/under-review account notices, which threaten a penalty rather than offer a benefit (see ITID-11734)
Fake brand partnership/sponsorship offers unrelated to account verification status (see ITID-11737)
ITID-11735.severity: Medium-High given the dual credential and potential payment-data harvest.
ITID-11735.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials or payment data were disclosed.
ITID-11735.escalation: Escalate to SOC/fraud teams depending on whether credentials, payment data, or both were disclosed.
indicators: Unsolicited offer of a verification badge with no corresponding official application the target initiated
Application page requesting both login credentials and payment card details
vectors: Mass DM/email campaign offering verification to accounts with a large following
Fake 'verification review' page requesting login re-authentication mid-process
rootCauses: Desire for verification status among influencers/public-facing accounts exploited as a strong motivator
Lack of awareness of the platform's actual verification application process and official domain
controls: Security awareness training on the platform's actual official verification process
Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
ITID-11735.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake verification application page.
ITID-11735.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; dispute any resulting payment charge.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake verification badge credential harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11735.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11734 by offering a desirable benefit (verification status) rather than threatening a penalty (suspension) as the psychological lever.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Verification Badge Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message or ad offering a fake verification badge/checkmark, requiring the user to log in via a credential-harvesting page to 'apply' or 'claim' it.

steps.title: Preserve the lure and destination link
steps.desc: Screenshot the message/ad and record the destination link offering the fake verification badge.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions or connected apps.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the campaign
steps.desc: Record the lure and destination for trend tracking, noting it may correlate with real verification program announcements exploited by attackers.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether credentials were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user regarding interaction with the fake verification page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same fake verification lure, which are common around periods when platforms change their verification programs.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11736.def: A message falsely claiming the target has posted content violating copyright or community guidelines, directing them to a fake 'dispute' or 'appeal' login page to harvest their credentials.
ITID-11736.purpose: Captures a credential harvest delivered via a fake copyright or content-violation notice.
scopeIncludes: Fake DMCA/copyright-strike notices linking to a spoofed login page to 'dispute' the claim
Fake community-guidelines violation notices requiring login to 'review' the flagged content
scopeExcludes: Fake account-flagged/under-review notices unrelated to a specific content/copyright claim (see ITID-11734)
Fake brand partnership offers (see ITID-11737)
ITID-11736.severity: High — a copyright/content-violation threat is a strong urgency driver, particularly for accounts that monetize content.
ITID-11736.priority: P1 once credentials are confirmed entered.
ITID-11736.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately upon confirming credential entry, particularly for monetized/brand accounts.
indicators: Copyright/violation notice referencing content the account owner does not recall posting
Notice threatening immediate account termination with a tight response deadline
vectors: Mass campaign targeting content creators/monetized accounts with a fabricated copyright-strike notice
Fake 'appeal' page mimicking the platform's actual content-dispute process
rootCauses: Content creators particularly susceptible given the direct income impact of a real content-violation claim
Lack of awareness of the platform's actual copyright-dispute process and official domain
controls: Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
Security awareness training on verifying copyright/violation notices via the official in-app dispute process
ITID-11736.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake dispute page.
ITID-11736.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; verify any real content-violation claim through the official in-app process only.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake copyright notice credential harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11736.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11734 by the specific copyright/content-violation framing, which particularly targets monetized content-creator accounts.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Copyright/Content Violation Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message falsely claiming the user posted content that violates copyright or platform policy, threatening account suspension unless they log in via a credential-harvesting link to resolve it.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm the account's real status
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and check the real account for any genuine copyright/policy notice.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; genuine account status confirmed.
steps.abort: If a genuine copyright notice is confirmed, redirect the user to the platform's real dispute process.

steps.title: Contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions or connected apps.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the campaign, especially if the account manages a business page
steps.desc: Record findings; if the targeted account manages an organizational business page, flag to marketing/brand teams as a recurring targeted risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; relevant teams alerted if applicable.

steps.title: Determine whether the link was clicked and credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user regarding interaction with the fake link.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same fake copyright-strike lure, which is a well-known recurring campaign type targeting content creators and business accounts.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11737.def: A message offering the target a lucrative brand partnership or sponsorship deal, directing them to a fake login/application portal (often requiring re-authentication to 'confirm eligibility') that harvests their credentials.
ITID-11737.purpose: Captures a credential harvest delivered via a fake brand partnership or sponsorship offer targeting influencers/content creators.
scopeIncludes: Fake brand sponsorship/collaboration offers requiring login through an external portal
Fake 'brand ambassador program' applications harvesting credentials
scopeExcludes: Fake verification badge offers, which promise status rather than a paid partnership (see ITID-11735)
Fake customer support DM scams unrelated to a partnership offer (see ITID-11725, under Direct Messaging Scams)
ITID-11737.severity: Medium-High — content creators actively seeking monetization opportunities are a receptive target for this pretext.
ITID-11737.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were disclosed.
ITID-11737.escalation: Escalate to SOC/brand-protection if the offer impersonates a specific real brand.
indicators: Unsolicited high-value partnership offer with no prior brand relationship
Application portal requiring social media login credentials rather than a standard contact form
vectors: Mass DM/email campaign targeting accounts with a significant follower count offering a fabricated partnership
Fake brand-ambassador portal impersonating a real, well-known brand
rootCauses: Content creators' desire for monetization opportunities exploited as a strong motivator
