No published verification process for confirming legitimate brand partnership outreach
controls: Security awareness training on verifying partnership offers directly with the brand's official channels
Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
ITID-11737.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake partnership portal; brand-monitoring can flag impersonation of a specific real brand.
ITID-11737.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; verify any partnership offer directly with the brand before engaging.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake brand partnership credential harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11737.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11735 by offering a paid business partnership rather than free verification status as the lure.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Brand Partnership/Sponsorship Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message offering a fake brand partnership, sponsorship, or paid collaboration, requiring the target to log in via a credential-harvesting page to 'accept' the deal.

steps.title: Preserve the lure and destination link
steps.desc: Screenshot the message/offer and record the destination login link and the brand being impersonated.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Contain the affected account
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on any account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Affected account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions or connected apps.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the campaign, particularly for accounts with public reach
steps.desc: Record findings; this lure disproportionately targets accounts with follower reach used for marketing — flag to marketing/social media management teams if such an account was targeted.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; relevant teams alerted if applicable.

steps.title: Verify with the claimed brand whether the offer is genuine
steps.desc: Where feasible, check with the claimed sponsoring brand's official channels to confirm the offer is not genuine.
steps.outcome: Offer confirmed fraudulent.
steps.abort: If the offer turns out to be genuine, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Determine whether credentials were entered
steps.desc: Interview the user regarding interaction with the fake login page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status.
steps.abort: If no interaction, proceed to blocklisting only.

ITID-11738.def: A message impersonating the social media platform's own security team, falsely claiming unusual login activity or a security issue with the target's account, directing them to a fake login page to 'secure' their account.
ITID-11738.purpose: Captures a credential harvest delivered via a fake security alert impersonating the social media platform itself, rather than a brand using the platform.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'unusual login detected, verify your identity' notices impersonating the platform's own security team
Fake 'your password will expire, reset now' notices impersonating the platform
scopeExcludes: Fake customer support DM scams impersonating a brand that uses the platform, not the platform itself (see ITID-11725, under Direct Messaging Scams)
Fake account-flagged/under-review notices citing a policy violation rather than a security/login concern (see ITID-11734)
ITID-11738.severity: High — impersonating the platform's own security team directly exploits the target's instinct to trust and act quickly on a real security warning.
ITID-11738.priority: P1 once credentials are confirmed entered.
ITID-11738.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately upon confirming credential entry.
indicators: Security alert referencing a login location/device the target does not recognize, from a sender not matching the platform's verified notification channel
Password-reset link leading to a domain not matching the platform's actual domain
vectors: Mass email/DM campaign impersonating the platform's automated security-alert emails
Fake 'new login detected' notice designed to trigger an immediate, panicked click
rootCauses: Users unable to reliably distinguish the platform's real security-alert format/domain from a spoofed one
Lack of awareness that a real security alert should be verified via directly navigating to the platform, not clicking the alert's link
controls: Multi-factor authentication on social media accounts
Security awareness training on verifying security alerts by navigating directly to the platform rather than clicking embedded links
ITID-11738.detection: Web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake security-alert login page.
ITID-11738.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA if credentials were entered; report the phishing domain.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake platform security alert credential harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11738.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11725 by impersonating the social media platform's own security team/infrastructure, rather than a third-party brand's customer support that merely uses the platform.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Platform Security Alert Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message impersonating the platform's own security team, warning of a suspicious login or security issue and directing the user to a fake login page to 'secure' their account.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm no genuine platform alert exists
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and check the real account's security notifications for any genuine alert.
steps.outcome: Message preserved; genuine account status confirmed.
steps.abort: If a genuine alert is confirmed, redirect the user to the platform's real security center.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force password reset and full session/token revocation, especially given the increased likelihood of a paired real attack attempt.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Verify no persistent unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Review the account for unexpected sessions, connected apps, or recovery-info changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual attacker access.

steps.title: Confirm restored access with fresh MFA
steps.desc: Confirm the account is restored with new credentials and re-enrolled MFA.
steps.outcome: Access restored.

steps.title: Log the campaign and clarify legitimate alert format
steps.desc: Record findings; clarify for users what genuine platform security alerts look like and how they are actually delivered.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the link was clicked and credentials entered
steps.desc: Interview the user and check identity provider logs for any correlating real login attempt around the same time — this lure is often paired with an actual credential-stuffing attempt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status and any correlating real attempt.
steps.abort: If no interaction and no correlating attempt, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: Block the domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

steps.title: Check for a broader campaign
steps.desc: Check for other reports of the same fake security-alert lure.
steps.outcome: Campaign scope established.

ITID-11739.def: A message directed at the administrator of a social media group or business page, falsely claiming an admin-transfer or ownership-verification action is required, directing them to a fake login page that, once compromised, grants the attacker control of the group/page and its full audience.
ITID-11739.purpose: Captures a credential harvest targeting an administrator of a group or business page, aiming to seize control of the page/group itself rather than a personal account.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'confirm you want to transfer admin rights' notices targeting a page/group administrator
Fake 'verify page ownership' requests harvesting admin credentials to seize control of a business page
scopeExcludes: Credential harvests targeting an individual's personal account with no group/page administrative angle (see ITID-11732)
Group/community infiltration by joining as a new member, which does not involve targeting or compromising the existing administrator (see ITID-11726, under Direct Messaging Scams)
ITID-11739.severity: Critical for high-follower business pages — successful compromise grants the attacker control of the page's entire audience and reputation, with potential to run further scams at scale.
ITID-11739.priority: P1 given the amplified downstream impact of losing control of a page/group with an established audience.
ITID-11739.escalation: Escalate to brand-protection, communications, and SOC immediately upon confirming any admin credential disclosure for an official page/group.
indicators: Notice specifically referencing 'admin transfer' or 'ownership verification' rather than a generic personal-account alert
Admin reporting unexpected changes to page ownership/admin roster
vectors: Fake 'page ownership dispute' notice requiring the admin to log in to 'resolve' it
Fake collaboration request requiring temporary admin access that is never returned
rootCauses: Page/group admin roles not restricted via least-privilege or requiring multiple approvers for role changes
Lack of multi-factor authentication specifically enforced for accounts holding page/group admin rights
controls: Multi-factor authentication enforced for all page/group admin accounts
Multi-approver requirement for admin role changes on business pages
Security awareness training specifically for page/group administrators
ITID-11739.detection: Platform admin-activity logs can show role-change events; web filtering can flag known phishing-kit domains hosting the fake page.
ITID-11739.response: Force credential reset and enable MFA immediately; review the page's admin roster and activity log for unauthorized changes; contact platform support to reverse any unauthorized ownership transfer.
metrics: Count of confirmed admin-transfer credential harvest incidents per quarter
Count resulting in actual loss of page/group control
ITID-11739.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11732 by specifically targeting a group/page administrator to seize control of a shared, audience-bearing asset rather than a single personal account.

playbook.name: Response: Group/Page Admin Transfer Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For a reported message tricking a group or page administrator into logging into a fake page to 'confirm' or 'accept' an admin/ownership transfer, actually harvesting credentials to hijack control of the group/page.

steps.title: Preserve the message and confirm no genuine transfer was initiated
steps.desc: Screenshot the message and confirm with the group/page's actual admin team that no real ownership transfer was requested.
steps.outcome: Message confirmed illegitimate.
steps.abort: If a real transfer was intentionally initiated by another admin, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Reset the admin's credentials and revoke sessions immediately
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation on the targeted admin's personal account without delay.
steps.outcome: Admin account secured.

steps.title: Audit the page/group for unauthorized content or setting changes
steps.desc: Review recent posts, ads, and settings changes on the page/group for anything made during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Any unauthorized changes identified and reverted.

steps.title: Confirm the legitimate admin team has full, exclusive control restored
steps.desc: Confirm the admin list reflects only legitimate administrators and the personal account is secured with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Full control restored to legitimate admins.

steps.title: Log the incident and brief page/group admins on transfer-request risk
steps.desc: Record the incident; brief all admins of high-value pages/groups that transfer/ownership requests should always be verified directly within the platform's native admin interface, never via an external link.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; admin team briefed.

steps.title: Determine whether the admin entered credentials and check current admin/ownership status
steps.desc: Interview the target and immediately check the group/page's admin list for any unauthorized changes.
steps.guidance: This is time-critical — a hijacked page/group admin role can be used to lock out legitimate admins entirely.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interaction status and current admin list integrity.
steps.abort: If no interaction and admin list is unchanged, proceed to blocklisting only.

steps.title: If the page/group admin list was already altered, escalate for emergency recovery
steps.desc: If an unauthorized admin was added or the legitimate admin was removed, immediately use the platform's business/page-recovery escalation channel (often faster than standard consumer support for verified business pages) to reverse it.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized admin change reversed or recovery escalation initiated.

steps.title: Assess the value and reach of the targeted page/group
steps.desc: Determine the follower/member count and purpose of the targeted page/group to gauge business impact if hijacked (e.g. an official brand page vs. a small internal group).
steps.outcome: Business impact assessed.

steps.title: Block the fake login domain and report the campaign
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist and file a phishing/page-hijack report with the platform.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked; campaign reported.
steps.tool: DNS/web filter, platform trust & safety reporting portal

ITID-11811.def: An unauthorized person following an authorized person through a secured entry point without a specific pretext technique yet identified.
ITID-11811.purpose: Catch-all for a tailgating attempt reported as a social-engineering technique before enough detail is available to identify the specific pretext used.
scopeIncludes: Reports of tailgating logged before the pretext/method is known
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (courteous hold, hands-full, uniform, group, etc.)
Tailgating logged purely as a physical-access-control incident with no social-engineering pretext analysis (ITID-14111)
ITID-11811.severity: Low-to-Medium; reassess once the pretext is identified.
ITID-11811.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassify once more detail is available.
indicators: Access-control log showing one badge read followed by multiple people entering
vectors: Following an authorized person through a secured door
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Access-control door-position sensors
Employee security awareness training
ITID-11811.detection: Relies on human reporting or badge-vs-door-open count anomalies.
ITID-11811.response: Document and attempt to reclassify to the specific pretext used.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-11811.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Differentiated from ITID-14111, which is the physical-security-incident logging catch-all for tailgating with no social-engineering pretext analysis performed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Tailgating Attempt
playbook.description: For a reported or observed attempt by an unauthorized individual to follow an authorized employee through a badge-controlled entry point, where the specific method (door-holding, encumbrance, uniform, crowd, etc.) is not yet known.

steps.title: Capture the report details (who, where, when)
steps.desc: Record who reported the attempt, the exact door/entry point, and the approximate time.
steps.guidance: Get this from the reporting employee as soon as possible while memory is fresh; do not wait for a written statement before pulling footage.
steps.outcome: A time window and location narrow enough to search access logs and CCTV.

steps.title: Notify on-site security/facilities
steps.desc: Alert physical security staff so they can attempt to locate the individual while still on-site.
steps.outcome: Security is actively searching or has confirmed the individual has left.

steps.title: Trace areas the individual accessed while inside
steps.desc: Using the footage timeline, determine what areas the individual entered and whether anything was disturbed or removed.
steps.outcome: A confirmed list of areas/systems the individual had physical proximity to.

steps.title: Brief the employee who was followed or held the door
steps.desc: Speak with the employee involved, not punitively, to reinforce door policy and rule out coercion.
steps.outcome: Employee understands policy; coercion ruled out or escalated separately.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess control gaps
steps.desc: Record the entry point, time, and whether existing controls (turnstile, mantrap, guard presence) would have prevented the attempt.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; a physical-security improvement recommended if a real control gap is identified.

steps.title: Pull badge-reader logs and CCTV for the entry point and time window
steps.desc: Retrieve access-control logs and camera footage covering the door and time of the suspected attempt.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference a single badge scan against footage showing two or more people entering.
steps.outcome: Footage and log entries preserved covering the incident window.

steps.title: Challenge or escort the individual if located
steps.desc: Security locates the individual, verifies identity and purpose of visit, and escorts them to the lobby if unauthorized.
steps.guidance: Never have an unarmed employee personally confront the individual — this is a security/facilities responsibility.
steps.outcome: Individual verified as legitimate or removed from the premises.
steps.abort: If the individual becomes uncooperative or the situation escalates, involve law enforcement rather than continuing to engage directly.

steps.title: Classify the tailgating method observed
steps.desc: Determine which specific tailgating pattern occurred (door-holding, hands-full, uniform, crowd, etc.) to route to the appropriate follow-up handling.
steps.outcome: Incident reclassified under the correct specific ITID if a clear pattern emerges; otherwise handled under this general playbook.
steps.abort: If footage is inconclusive, document as unconfirmed and proceed only to awareness follow-up.

ITID-11812.def: An unauthorized person gains entry by an authorized employee courteously holding a secured door open for them, exploiting social norms around politeness rather than any disguise or story.
ITID-11812.purpose: Captures the most common tailgating pretext: an attacker relying on ordinary politeness, where an employee holds the door open for someone following behind.
scopeIncludes: An employee holding a door for a stranger without checking a badge
Elevator or vestibule courtesy-hold entries
scopeExcludes: Pretexts relying on encumbrance/hands-full staging (ITID-11813)
Pretexts relying on uniform/branding (ITID-11814)
ITID-11812.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the individual is later found in a restricted area.
ITID-11812.escalation: Escalate to physical security if the tailgater is later observed beyond common areas.
indicators: Single badge read followed by two or more entrants on CCTV
Employee self-report of having held the door
vectors: Approaching a door immediately behind a badge-in employee
rootCauses: No badge-verification culture; courtesy prioritized over security
controls: Anti-tailgating turnstiles/mantraps
Security awareness training on door-holding
ITID-11812.detection: CCTV review and badge-read-to-entrant-count mismatch provide a real technical signal.
ITID-11812.response: Review CCTV, identify the entrant, and reinforce badge-challenge training.
metrics: Count of courtesy-hold tailgating events per quarter
ITID-11812.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by pretext axis: this leaf is pure politeness/social-norm exploitation with no disguise or staged prop.

playbook.name: Response: Courteous Door-Hold Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an authorized employee, out of politeness, held a badge-controlled door open for an unauthorized individual who did not scan their own badge.

steps.title: Identify the door-holding employee and the individual let in
steps.desc: Establish who held the door and who entered without scanning, from the report or footage.
steps.outcome: Both parties identified or described.

steps.title: Notify security to locate the unescorted individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security so they can find and verify the individual who entered without a badge.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Check whether the individual accessed any non-public areas
steps.desc: Review the footage timeline for areas entered beyond the point of tailgating.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of physical access, if any, beyond the entry lobby.

steps.title: Coach the employee on door-holding policy
steps.desc: Speak with the employee about the risk of holding doors for unscanned individuals, framed as a reminder rather than discipline.
steps.guidance: Emphasize that politely asking a follower to badge in themselves is expected and not rude.
steps.outcome: Employee acknowledges the policy and understands the expected behavior going forward.

steps.title: Log the incident and consider a door-holding awareness reminder
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether a broader staff reminder (posters, email) on door-holding is warranted.
steps.outcome: Incident logged; awareness action taken if this is a recurring pattern at this entrance.

steps.title: Review badge logs against CCTV for the door in question
steps.desc: Confirm the badge count for the door does not match the number of people who entered during the window.
steps.guidance: A single valid scan followed by two entries on camera is the clearest signature of this pattern.
steps.outcome: Discrepancy between badge scans and physical entries confirmed.
steps.abort: If the footage shows only one person entering, close as a false report.

steps.title: Verify the individual's identity and purpose
steps.desc: Security checks the individual's ID and reason for being on-site; escort to lobby if no legitimate purpose is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Individual verified as a legitimate visitor who simply lacked an escort, or removed from premises.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11813.def: An unauthorized person gains entry by appearing to have their hands full — carrying boxes, bags, or equipment — prompting an authorized employee to open or hold the door for them.
ITID-11813.purpose: Captures a tailgating pretext where the attacker stages themselves as visibly encumbered (boxes, equipment, coffee trays) to make holding the door the obviously helpful thing to do.
scopeIncludes: Carrying staged props (boxes, trays, equipment cases) to appear burdened at a secured entry
scopeExcludes: Genuine delivery/courier personas with branded uniform or ID (ITID-11814, or the on-site impersonation leaves under ITID-11832)
ITID-11813.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if props conceal contraband or intrusion tools.
ITID-11813.escalation: Escalate if the individual is found carrying tools inconsistent with a delivery/courier context.
indicators: CCTV showing an entrant visibly overloaded with items at the point of entry
Employee report of assisting someone whose hands were full
vectors: Staging props at a secured entrance to solicit door-holding
rootCauses: Employees prioritizing helpfulness over badge verification
controls: Security awareness training
Reception/visitor escort policy for anyone without a visible badge
ITID-11813.detection: CCTV review of entry points; largely reliant on employee reporting otherwise.
ITID-11813.response: Review CCTV footage and reinforce that badge verification applies regardless of encumbrance.
metrics: Count of hands-full pretext tailgating events per quarter
ITID-11813.notes: Differentiated by pretext axis: staged physical encumbrance, distinct from uniform/branding-based pretexts (ITID-11814) and unstaged courtesy-hold (ITID-11812).

playbook.name: Response: Hands-Full/Encumbered Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual gained entry by appearing encumbered (carrying boxes, coffee, equipment) so an employee would hold or open the door for them rather than expect a badge scan.

steps.title: Confirm the encumbrance pretext used
steps.desc: From the report or footage, note what the individual was carrying and how it was used to justify not badging in.
steps.outcome: A description of the pretext and the individual.

steps.title: Notify security to locate the individual and their belongings
steps.desc: Alert physical security so the individual can be found and, if items were carried in, inspected before leaving the area.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Trace areas accessed and confirm nothing was left behind
steps.desc: Review footage for where the individual went and whether any carried item was placed or left in a facility area.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access and disposition of any carried items.

steps.title: Brief the employee who assisted
steps.desc: Remind the assisting employee that offering to badge someone in, rather than opening/holding the door, is the expected behavior even when someone appears burdened.
steps.outcome: Employee understands the expected alternative (badge the person in, or direct them to reception).

steps.title: Log the incident and note the pretext used
steps.desc: Record the specific encumbrance pretext for trend tracking, since this method is commonly reused across attempts.
steps.outcome: Incident logged with pretext detail for future awareness material.

steps.title: Pull CCTV for the door to confirm entry without a badge scan
steps.desc: Verify against badge logs that the individual entered without their own valid scan.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized entry event.

steps.title: Verify identity, purpose, and contents of carried items if present
steps.desc: Security confirms who the individual is, why they are on-site, and inspects any package or equipment they brought in if appropriate and safe to do so.
steps.guidance: Do not physically search a person or their belongings without proper authority — involve law enforcement if a search is warranted and the individual will not consent.
steps.outcome: Individual verified as legitimate or removed; any suspicious item flagged for further handling.
steps.abort: If the item is suspected hazardous or the individual refuses inspection and will not leave, treat as a security emergency and involve law enforcement/EOD as applicable.

ITID-11814.def: An unauthorized person gains entry by wearing a uniform, vest, or branded clothing/equipment associated with a trusted role (delivery, utility, contractor) to tailgate through a secured door.
ITID-11814.purpose: Captures a tailgating pretext where the attacker wears a uniform or displays branding to appear as a legitimate service provider, lowering an employee's guard enough to hold the door.
scopeIncludes: Wearing generic branded/uniformed attire while tailgating, without engaging in a full impersonation interaction
scopeExcludes: A full sustained impersonation persona involving conversation, fabricated credentials, or a specific role narrative (the on-site impersonation leaves, ITID-11832 through ITID-11839)
ITID-11814.priority: P2, given the deliberate use of visual trust cues.
ITID-11814.escalation: Escalate to physical security immediately; treat as a precursor to a more developed impersonation.
indicators: CCTV showing branded/uniformed attire inconsistent with any scheduled vendor visit
No corresponding entry in the vendor/visitor log
vectors: Wearing a hi-vis vest, courier jacket, or utility uniform to blend in at an entrance
rootCauses: No visitor log cross-check at point of entry; visual trust cues unverified
controls: Visitor/vendor pre-registration cross-check at entry
Security awareness training on verifying uniformed visitors
ITID-11814.detection: CCTV review cross-referenced against the vendor/visitor schedule provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11814.response: Cross-check CCTV against the visitor log and escalate any mismatch.
metrics: Count of uniformed-pretext tailgating events with no matching visitor-log entry
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11814.notes: Differentiated from the on-site impersonation leaves (ITID-11832-11839), which require a sustained persona and interaction; this leaf is limited to visual/uniform trust cues used only to get through the door.

playbook.name: Response: Uniformed/Branded Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual wearing a uniform, branded clothing, or displaying a fake company/vendor badge used the appearance of legitimacy to be waved through a controlled entry without scanning.

steps.title: Record what uniform/branding was presented and by whom it was observed
steps.desc: Capture the description of the uniform, logo, or credential displayed, and who let the individual through.
steps.outcome: A description sufficient to compare against known legitimate vendor/contractor uniforms.

steps.title: Notify security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security to find the individual and verify their credentials against the real vendor if claimed.
steps.guidance: Have security contact the actual vendor company directly (using a known number, not one provided by the individual) if identity is in question.
steps.outcome: Individual located and identity verified, or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Trace areas accessed and check for tampering
steps.desc: Review footage timeline to determine what areas were entered, particularly server rooms, comms closets, or restricted zones that a fake uniform could plausibly justify.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of physical access and no evidence of tampering, or tampering identified and escalated.

steps.title: Alert reception/security staff to the fake-uniform pattern observed
steps.desc: Circulate a description of the uniform/branding used so front-desk and security staff can recognize a repeat attempt.
steps.outcome: Front-line staff briefed on the specific pretext used.

steps.title: Log the incident and evaluate vendor-verification process
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether a stronger vendor pre-notification or ID-verification process would have prevented entry.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; process improvement recommended if a gap is identified.

steps.title: Verify against the legitimate vendor/contractor roster
steps.desc: Check whether any legitimate vendor matching that uniform/branding was scheduled to be on-site.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the individual matches a real, expected vendor visit or not.
steps.abort: If a legitimate scheduled vendor is confirmed and simply forgot to badge in, close as a policy reminder rather than a security incident.

steps.title: Escort the individual out if credentials cannot be verified
steps.desc: If the individual cannot produce verifiable identification or the claimed vendor denies sending them, escort them off the premises.
steps.outcome: Individual removed from the premises or confirmed legitimate.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

steps.title: Pull CCTV for the entry point
steps.desc: Retrieve footage to document the individual's appearance and entry.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved showing the individual and the uniform/branding used.

ITID-11815.def: An unauthorized person enters a secured facility by blending into a crowd or group (shift change, event, evacuation re-entry) where individual badge verification is not practically enforced.
ITID-11815.purpose: Captures a tailgating pretext that exploits crowding — following a large group through a door where individual verification breaks down.
scopeIncludes: Entering amid a shift-change crowd or large group without individual badge challenge
scopeExcludes: Deliberate exploitation of a fire drill/evacuation event specifically (ITID-14521, a fake-emergency pretext)
ITID-11815.priority: P3, escalating if occurring at a high-security facility.
ITID-11815.escalation: Escalate to physical security for review of crowd-entry procedures.
indicators: Entrant count on CCTV exceeding badge-read count during high-traffic periods
Unidentified individual observed in a shift-change crowd
vectors: Timing entry to coincide with shift changes or large group movement
rootCauses: Access-control process not designed to verify individuals within a crowd
controls: Turnstiles/mantraps enforcing one-badge-one-entrant
Increased security presence during shift changes
ITID-11815.detection: CCTV entrant-count vs. badge-read-count comparison during peak periods.
ITID-11815.response: Review CCTV for the relevant window and identify the unaccounted entrant.
metrics: Entrant-count vs. badge-read-count variance during peak periods
ITID-11815.notes: Differentiated by pretext axis: exploiting genuine crowd volume, not a staged emergency (see ITID-14521 for the fake-emergency variant).

playbook.name: Response: Group/Crowd Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an unauthorized individual entered a controlled door by blending into a group of authorized employees entering together, such that no single individual felt responsible for verifying the badge scan.

steps.title: Identify the group and approximate entry time
steps.desc: From the report, determine roughly which group of employees was entering and when.
steps.outcome: A narrowed time window and door for footage review.

steps.title: Notify security to locate the unaccounted individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security so they can search common areas for the individual.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Trace movement and areas accessed after entry
steps.desc: Review footage across cameras to follow the individual's path once inside.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access.

steps.title: Reinforce single-scan-per-entry expectation with staff at the affected door
steps.desc: Remind employees in the affected area that each person must scan their own badge even when entering as part of a group.
steps.outcome: Awareness reminder delivered to the relevant team or floor.

steps.title: Log the incident and evaluate the door's physical control
steps.desc: Record whether the door hardware (e.g. no turnstile/mantrap) makes group tailgating easy, and recommend a control upgrade if this is a recurring high-traffic entry point.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a control recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Reconcile badge scan count against people on camera
steps.desc: Compare the number of valid badge scans at the door against the number of individuals visible entering in that window.
steps.guidance: Group tailgating typically shows several valid scans followed by one or more extra unscanned entries within the door-open interval.
steps.outcome: Confirmed discrepancy and identification (or description) of the extra individual.
steps.abort: If counts reconcile, close as a false report.

steps.title: Verify identity and purpose
steps.desc: Security confirms who the individual is and why they are on-site; escort out if no legitimate purpose is established.
steps.outcome: Individual verified as legitimate or removed.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11816.def: An unauthorized person gains entry through a smoking-area door, loading dock, or other secondary entrance that employees prop open or use casually, bypassing the main reception/badge point entirely.
ITID-11816.purpose: Captures a tailgating pretext that targets informally-monitored secondary entrances, such as smoking areas or side/loading doors, rather than the main staffed entrance.
scopeIncludes: Entering through a propped smoking-area or side door used informally by staff
Loitering near a smoking area to slip in behind returning employees
scopeExcludes: Fire/emergency exit doors specifically propped for entry (ITID-14333)
ITID-11816.severity: Medium-High, given the entry point often bypasses reception entirely.
ITID-11816.escalation: Escalate to physical security and facilities to address the propped/unmonitored door.
indicators: Door-held-open sensor alert at a secondary entrance
Individual observed loitering near a smoking area then entering with staff
vectors: Waiting near a known smoking-break door for staff to return
rootCauses: Secondary doors lack badge readers or are habitually propped by staff for convenience
controls: Door-held-open alarms on secondary entrances
Policy prohibiting propping non-reception doors
ITID-11816.detection: Door-position sensor alerting provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11816.response: Investigate door-held-open alerts at secondary entrances and reinforce no-propping policy.
metrics: Count of door-held-open alerts at secondary entrances per month
ITID-11816.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14333, which covers fire/emergency exits specifically; this leaf covers informal secondary entrances such as smoking-break doors.

playbook.name: Response: Smoking Area/Side Door Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual gained entry through a side or rear door left propped open, or used unlabeled and unmonitored smoking-break access, bypassing the main badge-controlled entrance entirely.

steps.title: Identify the specific door and confirm it was propped or unmonitored
steps.desc: Locate the exact door used and determine whether it was propped open, had a defeated latch, or was simply unmonitored during a smoke break.
steps.guidance: Check for door-propped alarms in the access control system if the door is alarmed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed door and cause of the unmonitored access.

steps.title: Secure the door immediately
steps.desc: Close and confirm the door has latched/locked, and remove any object used to prop it.
steps.outcome: Door confirmed secured.

steps.title: Sweep the area adjacent to the door for tampering or left items
steps.desc: Physically inspect the immediate area for signs of tampering, unattended items, or removed property.
steps.outcome: Area cleared, or a finding escalated if tampering/removal is discovered.

steps.title: Brief staff who use this door for smoke breaks
steps.desc: Remind the relevant team that the door must not be propped and should always be allowed to latch behind them.
steps.outcome: Staff briefed and acknowledge the policy.

steps.title: Log the incident and recommend a physical/technical control fix
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend measures such as a door-propped alarm, camera installation, or a designated smoking area outside the secure perimeter.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete facilities recommendation.

steps.title: Pull CCTV for that door covering the relevant period
steps.desc: Retrieve footage, if a camera exists at this location, to document the individual and duration the door was left open.
steps.guidance: Side/smoking doors are frequently the least camera-covered entry points — note if no footage exists at all, as this is itself a finding.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available; absence of coverage documented as a gap.

steps.title: Notify security to search for the individual on-site
steps.desc: Alert physical security to locate and challenge the individual within the building.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed to have left.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11817.def: An individual follows an authorized employee out through a secured exit-only or badge-out door without their own exit being logged, typically used to leave undetected after gaining entry by other means or to probe exit-side control gaps.
ITID-11817.purpose: Captures the inverse tailgating pattern — an unauthorized person exiting behind a legitimate badge-out, used to establish a presence inside the facility first (e.g., via another entry method) then exit undetected, or to test exit-side controls.
scopeIncludes: Exiting a badge-controlled door immediately behind an authorized employee without badging out
scopeExcludes: The initial unauthorized entry method that got the individual inside in the first place (classify separately under the applicable entry-pretext leaf)
ITID-11817.priority: P3, escalating if paired with evidence of an unlogged entry.
ITID-11817.escalation: Escalate to physical security to reconcile badge-in vs. badge-out counts for the affected door.
indicators: Badge-out log showing fewer exits than CCTV-observed departures
Individual with no corresponding badge-in record observed exiting
vectors: Following an employee through an exit-only door to leave without a logged badge event
rootCauses: Exit doors not equipped with the same verification rigor as entry doors
controls: Badge-out enforcement on exit doors
CCTV coverage of exit points
ITID-11817.detection: Badge-in vs. badge-out reconciliation and CCTV provide a real technical signal.
ITID-11817.response: Reconcile badge logs against CCTV and investigate any unaccounted individual.
metrics: Badge-in vs. badge-out count variance per door per month
ITID-11817.notes: Scope decision: this leaf captures only the exit-side tailgating event itself; the entry method that got the individual inside is logged and classified under the relevant entry-pretext leaf to avoid double-counting the same incident.

playbook.name: Response: Reverse Tailgating (Following Someone Out)
playbook.description: For an incident where an unauthorized individual used an authorized employee's exit through a controlled door to slip inside as it opened outward, or an individual exited alongside an employee to avoid their own exit being logged (e.g. concealing removal of an item).

steps.title: Determine the direction and nature of the event
steps.desc: Clarify whether the concern is an outsider slipping in as an employee exited, or an individual exiting without their own badge-out being recorded (possibly while carrying something out).
steps.outcome: Event classified as an entry-via-exit-door concern, an unlogged-exit concern, or both.

steps.title: Notify security to search for any individual who entered via the exit door
steps.desc: If footage shows someone entering as the door opened outward, alert security to locate them inside the building.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed not present.

steps.title: Trace any unauthorized entrant's movement inside the facility
steps.desc: Review footage across cameras to follow the individual's path once inside, if applicable.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access, if any occurred.

steps.title: Remind staff to be aware of their surroundings when exiting controlled doors
steps.desc: Brief staff who use the affected exit that someone waiting outside can enter as the door opens for them to leave.
steps.outcome: Awareness reminder delivered.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess exit-side control gaps
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether the exit door needs an outbound reader, delayed-latch, or camera coverage to close this gap.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a control recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Pull CCTV and exit-door logs for the time window
steps.desc: Retrieve footage and any exit-side badge/motion logs for the door in question.
steps.guidance: Exit doors are frequently not equipped with outbound badge readers — note if this is the case, as it limits available log evidence.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained; exit logging capability at this door documented.

steps.title: If items were removed, halt the departing individual or flag for follow-up
steps.desc: If the concern involves an employee or visitor exiting with an item that should have been logged/checked out, contact them promptly to reconcile.
steps.outcome: Item accounted for, or an unauthorized removal confirmed and escalated as a separate loss/theft matter.

ITID-11818.def: An unauthorized vehicle follows an authorized vehicle through a gate, barrier arm, or car-park access point before it closes, bypassing vehicle-level credential checks.
ITID-11818.purpose: Captures tailgating at vehicle gates and barrier-arm entrances, a distinct control surface from pedestrian doors.
scopeIncludes: A vehicle following another through a barrier-arm or gate before closure
Pedestrian tailgating a vehicle through a vehicle gate
scopeExcludes: Pedestrian-door tailgating at building entrances (the other leaves in this Tier-4 group)
ITID-11818.severity: Medium-High, given the facility perimeter (not just a building) is breached.
ITID-11818.escalation: Escalate to physical security and site perimeter response immediately.
indicators: Gate/barrier sensor logging two vehicle transits for one credential read
CCTV showing close-following vehicles at a gate
vectors: Following an authorized vehicle closely through a gate before it closes
rootCauses: Barrier-arm timing/sensor configuration allows close-following vehicles through
controls: Anti-tailgating vehicle barrier design (single-vehicle capture)
License-plate recognition cross-checked against credential reads
ITID-11818.detection: Gate sensor and license-plate-recognition logs provide a real technical signal.
ITID-11818.response: Review gate logs and CCTV, dispatch perimeter security to intercept if the vehicle is still on-site.
metrics: Count of vehicle-gate credential-read-to-transit-count mismatches per month
sops: Perimeter and Vehicle Access Control SOP
detections: Gate sensor transit-count vs. credential-read mismatch alerting
ITID-11818.notes: Differentiated from the pedestrian-door leaves in this Tier-4 group by control surface: vehicle gates/barrier arms, not building doors.

playbook.name: Response: Vehicle Gate Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an unauthorized vehicle followed an authorized vehicle through a gate, barrier arm, or garage entrance controlled by a card/transponder reader, without presenting its own credential.

steps.title: Identify the gate, time, and vehicles involved
steps.desc: Determine which vehicle gate was involved, the approximate time, and if possible a description or plate of the following vehicle.
steps.outcome: A time window and location sufficient to pull gate camera footage.

steps.title: Notify security/patrol to intercept the vehicle on-site
steps.desc: Alert physical security or roving patrol to locate the vehicle in the parking structure/lot.
steps.outcome: Vehicle located and occupants approached, or confirmed to have already left via another exit.

steps.title: Check whether the vehicle or occupants accessed any building or secure area
steps.desc: Confirm via footage/badge logs whether occupants left the vehicle and entered any facility.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access, if any.

steps.title: Log the plate/description for the gate watch list, if applicable
steps.desc: Add the vehicle description or plate to a local security watch list to flag repeat attempts.
steps.outcome: Watch list updated where the facility maintains one.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess the gate's anti-tailgating control
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether the barrier's close timing, a vehicle-spacing sensor, or LPR coverage needs improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a facilities recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Pull gate camera/LPR footage and access logs
steps.desc: Retrieve license-plate-recognition footage or standard CCTV covering the gate, and cross-reference against the transponder/card log.
steps.outcome: A single valid credential scan followed by two vehicles passing the barrier confirms the pattern; ideally the second vehicle's plate is captured.
steps.abort: If only one vehicle is confirmed to have passed, close as a false report.

steps.title: Verify occupant identity and purpose
steps.desc: Security confirms who the occupants are and their reason for being on-site; direct to visitor registration or have them leave if no legitimate purpose.
steps.outcome: Vehicle/occupants verified as legitimate or asked to leave the property.
steps.abort: If uncooperative or the vehicle attempts to flee toward restricted areas, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11819.def: An unauthorized person tailgates into a facility during after-hours, overnight, or low-staff periods when fewer employees are present to notice or challenge an unfamiliar face.
ITID-11819.purpose: Captures tailgating that specifically exploits reduced staffing and vigilance during off-hours, nights, or weekends.
scopeIncludes: Tailgating events occurring outside normal business hours or during holiday/weekend low-staffing periods
scopeExcludes: Business-hours tailgating relying on a specific pretext technique (the other leaves in this Tier-4 group)
ITID-11819.severity: High, given reduced likelihood of live challenge or witness.
ITID-11819.escalation: Escalate to physical security and on-call incident response immediately; after-hours entries carry elevated risk of undetected dwell time.
indicators: Badge-read-to-entrant-count mismatch during off-hours windows
CCTV motion detected in areas with minimal expected after-hours activity
vectors: Timing entry to coincide with night shift, weekend, or holiday low-staffing periods
rootCauses: Reduced live security presence and slower alert response during off-hours
controls: After-hours CCTV monitoring with real-time alerting
Increased after-hours patrol frequency
ITID-11819.detection: After-hours motion/access-control alerting provides a real technical signal, though live response is slower.
ITID-11819.response: Treat any after-hours tailgating alert as high priority given reduced witness likelihood.
metrics: Count of after-hours tailgating events per quarter
Mean response time to after-hours access alerts
ITID-11819.notes: Differentiated by timing axis: after-hours/low-staff window, cutting across whatever pretext technique was used to gain entry.

playbook.name: Response: After-Hours/Low-Staff Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual exploited reduced staffing, an unmanned reception desk, or off-hours conditions to tailgate into the facility when fewer people were present to notice or challenge them.

steps.title: Confirm the after-hours window and door involved
steps.desc: Establish the exact time (outside normal business hours or during a low-staff period) and the entry point used.
steps.outcome: A confirmed after-hours time window and door.

steps.title: Notify on-call/night security immediately
steps.desc: Alert whatever security coverage is available after hours (guard, roving patrol, or remote monitoring center) to respond.
steps.guidance: After-hours response may take longer than daytime — treat this as higher urgency given reduced staff able to notice or intervene.
steps.outcome: Security dispatched to search for the individual.

steps.title: Full-building sweep of the individual's movement
steps.desc: Trace the individual across all available camera coverage to determine full scope of access before they left or were removed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access for the entire after-hours presence.

steps.title: Review with staff who work after-hours shifts
steps.desc: Brief any regular after-hours/shift staff on the incident and reinforce vigilance and door-security habits during low-staff periods.
steps.outcome: After-hours staff briefed.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess after-hours physical security posture
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether after-hours guard coverage, lighting, or camera monitoring needs strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a posture recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Pull CCTV and badge logs for the window
steps.desc: Retrieve footage and access logs; after-hours periods typically have fewer people to cross-reference against, so lean more heavily on camera evidence.
steps.outcome: Footage and logs obtained for the window.

steps.title: Lock down or verify occupancy of sensitive areas
steps.desc: Given reduced staff presence, confirm server rooms, executive offices, and other sensitive areas remain locked and check for anyone inside who should not be.
steps.outcome: Sensitive areas confirmed secure and unoccupied by unauthorized persons.

steps.title: Check for signs the individual waited or loitered near the entrance beforehand
steps.desc: Review a wider time window before the entry to see whether the individual was observed waiting for an employee to badge in during a quiet period.
steps.outcome: Established whether this was opportunistic or a deliberately timed attempt.

ITID-11821.def: An adversary searching a facility's discarded waste for useful information or materials, with the specific waste stream (paper, electronics, badges, recycling) not yet identified.
ITID-11821.purpose: Catch-all for a dumpster-diving reconnaissance report before the targeted waste stream is identified.
scopeIncludes: Reports of waste-bin searching logged before the material type is known
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (paper, electronic media, IT equipment, badges, recycling, off-site, event, vendor waste)
ITID-11821.severity: Low-to-Medium; reassess once the material searched is identified.
ITID-11821.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassify once more detail is available.
indicators: Report of an unknown individual searching outdoor waste receptacles
vectors: Searching unsecured waste bins for discarded materials
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Awareness training on secure disposal
ITID-11821.detection: Relies entirely on human reporting or CCTV coverage of waste areas.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-11821.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Dumpster Diving
playbook.description: For a report or observation of an unauthorized individual searching company waste receptacles for information or materials, where the specific target (paper, electronics, badges, etc.) is not yet known.

steps.title: Capture the report details (who, where, when)
steps.desc: Record who reported the activity, the exact waste location (dumpster, bin, loading dock), and the approximate time.
steps.outcome: A time window and location narrow enough to pull footage if available.

steps.title: Notify security/facilities to intervene if the individual is still present
steps.desc: Alert physical security so they can approach and identify the individual while still on-site.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Inventory what was disturbed or removed from the waste
steps.desc: Assess, from footage or a physical check, what materials appear to have been searched or taken.
steps.outcome: A list (even approximate) of what may have been exposed or removed.

steps.title: Notify affected teams if sensitive material may have been exposed
steps.desc: If the disturbed waste is traced to a specific department, inform them so they can assess downstream risk (e.g. reissue exposed identifiers).
steps.outcome: Relevant team notified and able to take follow-up action.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess disposal control gaps
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether current disposal practices (locked enclosures, shredding, escort of waste to pickup) are adequate.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a disposal-practice recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Pull CCTV covering the waste area, if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage of the dumpster/bin area for the reported time window.
steps.guidance: Waste areas are frequently outside primary camera coverage — note if no footage exists, as this is itself a finding.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available, or absence of coverage documented.

steps.title: Secure the waste area against further access
steps.desc: If the dumpster/bin enclosure is unlocked or accessible from public space, lock or restrict it pending review.
steps.outcome: Waste area access restricted.

steps.title: Classify what was being targeted, if determinable
steps.desc: Determine whether the activity targeted paper records, electronic media, IT equipment, badges, or general recycling, to route to the appropriate specific follow-up.
steps.outcome: Incident reclassified under a more specific ITID if a clear target emerges; otherwise handled under this general playbook.

ITID-11822.def: An adversary retrieves discarded paper documents (memos, org charts, printed emails, phone lists) from waste receptacles to gather intelligence for a later social-engineering attack.
ITID-11822.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting discarded paper records — the classic vector for org charts, memos, and internal documents useful for pretexting.
scopeIncludes: Retrieving discarded paper documents from waste or recycling bins for intelligence-gathering purposes
scopeExcludes: Reconstruction of shredded paper documents (ITID-14411, a distinct downstream exploitation technique)
Theft of documents directly from a desk or filing cabinet, not from waste (ITID-14231/14232)
ITID-11822.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if sensitive/confidential material is confirmed retrieved.
ITID-11822.escalation: Escalate to security if retrieved documents contain confidential or PII content.
indicators: Reports of unsecured paper waste found disturbed or missing
Individual observed removing paper from bins
vectors: Searching unsecured office paper waste for intact documents
rootCauses: Sensitive paper disposed of without shredding; waste bins left unsecured/accessible
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Mandatory shredding/secure disposal of sensitive paper
Locked recycling/waste receptacles
ITID-11822.detection: Relies mostly on physical observation/CCTV of waste areas.
ITID-11822.response: Assess what document types were exposed and notify affected data owners.
metrics: Count of confirmed paper-record dumpster-diving incidents per quarter
ITID-11822.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14411 (shredder reconstruction), which covers reassembly of already-shredded material; this leaf covers retrieval of intact, unshredded paper.

playbook.name: Response: Discarded Document/Paper Records Dumpster Diving
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual searched or removed discarded paper records (invoices, printouts, memos, org charts) from company waste that were not properly shredded prior to disposal.

steps.title: Identify what documents were exposed
steps.desc: Determine, from the report or a physical check of the bin, what categories of paper records were discarded unshredded and potentially accessed.
steps.guidance: Look for anything with names, account numbers, internal contact lists, or system details.
steps.outcome: A list of document types and their sensitivity level.

steps.title: Recover any documents still present
steps.desc: Physically retrieve and secure any remaining unshredded documents from the bin before they are collected by waste services.
steps.outcome: Remaining sensitive documents recovered and secured.

steps.title: Identify the source department and disposal failure point
steps.desc: Trace which team's waste this was and why it bypassed shredding (e.g. no shred bin nearby, overflow, policy not followed).
steps.outcome: Root cause of the improper disposal identified.

steps.title: Notify affected individuals or teams if PII/sensitive data was exposed
steps.desc: If the exposed documents contained personal or sensitive business data, notify the owning team/privacy office to determine if further notification obligations apply.
steps.outcome: Owning team/privacy office informed and assessing impact.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce clean-desk/shred-bin policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend a targeted reminder or additional shred bins for the source department.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete follow-up action.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the waste area if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage covering the bin location and reported time window.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available.

steps.title: Notify security if an individual was seen taking documents away
steps.desc: If someone was observed leaving with documents, alert security to attempt to identify or locate them.
steps.outcome: Security aware and attempting to locate the individual, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Ensure remaining backlog of similar waste is shredded
steps.desc: Check for and properly destroy any other unshredded paper waste from the same source.
steps.outcome: Backlog cleared and confirmed shredded.

ITID-11823.def: An adversary retrieves discarded electronic media (USB drives, external disks, backup tapes, optical media) from waste receptacles that may still hold recoverable data.
ITID-11823.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting discarded electronic storage media such as USB drives, backup tapes, or CDs/DVDs.
scopeIncludes: Retrieving discarded USB drives, disks, tapes, or optical media from waste
scopeExcludes: Discarded full IT equipment such as laptops/desktops/servers (ITID-11824)
Actual forensic data recovery performed on retrieved media (ITID-14421/14422, a downstream exploitation step)
ITID-11823.severity: Medium-High, given the potential for large volumes of data on small media.
ITID-11823.escalation: Escalate immediately if the media is known to have held sensitive data and was not verified wiped.
indicators: Inventory reconciliation showing missing decommissioned media
Media disposal records not matching destruction certificates
vectors: Searching e-waste or general waste bins for discarded storage media
rootCauses: No certified destruction process for small-form-factor media
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Certified media destruction/degaussing process
Chain-of-custody tracking for decommissioned media
ITID-11823.response: Determine what data the media held and initiate breach-assessment procedures if unencrypted.
metrics: Count of media items disposed without certified destruction record
ITID-11823.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14421/14422, which cover the act of recovering data from retrieved media, not the retrieval itself.

playbook.name: Response: Discarded Electronic Media Dumpster Diving
playbook.description: For an incident where discarded electronic storage media (USB drives, external disks, backup tapes, SD cards, CDs/DVDs) was found or removed from company waste without proper data destruction.

steps.title: Identify the media type and what data it may contain
steps.desc: Determine what kind of media was discarded and, if known, what data or systems it relates to.
steps.guidance: Check inventory/asset records if the media was tagged.
steps.outcome: Media type and likely data sensitivity established.

steps.title: Recover any remaining media from the waste stream
steps.desc: Physically retrieve any remaining unit(s) of the media before collection by waste services.
steps.outcome: Remaining media recovered and secured with IT/security.

steps.title: Determine whether the data on the media was ever properly wiped
steps.desc: Check IT asset disposal records to confirm whether the media underwent certified wiping/degaussing before disposal.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the media held live, recoverable data at time of exposure.

steps.title: Treat as a potential data exposure if wiping cannot be confirmed
steps.desc: If the media cannot be confirmed wiped and cannot be recovered, escalate to a data-loss/breach assessment.
steps.outcome: Privacy/security leadership informed and assessing exposure scope.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce certified media-destruction process
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm all electronic media disposal routes through certified destruction, not general waste.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; disposal process gap closed if identified.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the waste area if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage covering the bin location and reported time window.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available.

steps.title: Notify security if media was seen being removed by an individual
steps.desc: If someone was observed taking media away, alert security to attempt identification.
steps.outcome: Security aware and attempting to locate the individual, or confirmed departed.

ITID-11824.def: An adversary retrieves discarded IT equipment from waste or e-waste areas that may retain recoverable data or reusable components.
ITID-11824.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting discarded IT hardware (laptops, desktops, servers, networking gear) disposed of without proper data sanitization.
scopeIncludes: Retrieving discarded laptops, desktops, servers, or network equipment from waste/e-waste areas
scopeExcludes: Discarded small storage media such as USB drives or tapes (ITID-11823)
Theft of active/in-service IT equipment (ITID-14221/14222, hardware theft branch)
ITID-11824.severity: High, given full systems may retain complete disk images.
ITID-11824.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the device is confirmed to hold unencrypted sensitive data.
ITID-11824.escalation: Escalate immediately to data-breach assessment if device disposition/wipe status is unconfirmed.
indicators: Asset inventory showing decommissioned equipment unaccounted for at final disposal
E-waste vendor discrepancy between manifested and received units
vectors: Searching e-waste staging areas or loading docks for discarded equipment
rootCauses: Asset decommissioning process lacks verified data-wipe step before disposal
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Verified data-wipe prior to disposal
Secured e-waste staging with chain-of-custody
ITID-11824.detection: Relies on asset-disposal reconciliation and e-waste vendor manifests.
ITID-11824.response: Confirm wipe status of all discarded units and treat unconfirmed devices as a potential breach.
metrics: Count of decommissioned IT assets with unconfirmed wipe status
sops: IT Asset Decommissioning and Disposal SOP
ITID-11824.notes: Differentiated from the Hardware Theft branch (ITID-14221/14222), which covers theft of equipment still in active service, not discarded equipment.

playbook.name: Response: Discarded IT Equipment Dumpster Diving
playbook.description: For an incident where decommissioned IT equipment (laptops, desktops, servers, networking gear, printers) was found or removed from company waste without confirmed data wiping or asset disposition.

steps.title: Identify the equipment and its asset tag/serial number
steps.desc: Locate any asset tag, serial number, or identifying marks on the discarded equipment.
steps.outcome: Equipment identified against the IT asset inventory.

steps.title: Recover the equipment from the waste stream
steps.desc: Physically retrieve the equipment before collection by waste services and secure it with IT.
steps.outcome: Equipment recovered and in IT custody.

steps.title: Verify whether storage drives were wiped or physically destroyed prior to disposal
steps.desc: Check the asset's disposition record and, where possible, inspect or image the drive to confirm no recoverable data remains.
steps.outcome: Confirmed data-destruction status of the equipment.

steps.title: Treat as a potential data exposure if wiping cannot be confirmed
steps.desc: If drives cannot be confirmed wiped and the equipment was accessible to an outsider, escalate to a data-loss/breach assessment.
steps.outcome: Privacy/security leadership informed and assessing exposure scope.

steps.title: Log the incident and audit the IT asset disposal workflow
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm decommissioned equipment routes through the certified e-waste/ITAD vendor with wipe certificates, not general waste.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; disposal workflow gap closed if identified.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the waste area if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage covering the bin/loading dock location and reported time window.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available.

steps.title: Notify security if equipment was seen being removed by an individual
steps.desc: If someone was observed taking equipment away, alert security to attempt identification.
steps.outcome: Security aware and attempting to locate the individual, or confirmed departed.

ITID-11825.def: An adversary retrieves a discarded, deactivated, or improperly destroyed access badge or credential from waste to attempt reuse or cloning.
ITID-11825.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting discarded physical access badges or credentials that could be reused or cloned.
scopeIncludes: Retrieving a discarded physical badge or access card from waste receptacles
scopeExcludes: Fabrication of a new fake badge or cloning of an active badge (the Badge Forgery branch, ITID-14121-14123)
ITID-11825.severity: High, given a badge may still grant access if not properly deactivated.
ITID-11825.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the badge is confirmed still active.
ITID-11825.escalation: Escalate immediately to confirm the badge was deactivated in the access-control system.
indicators: Badge disposal not matching deactivation timestamp in access-control system
Recovered badge found active during audit
vectors: Searching waste for discarded badges before/without deactivation
rootCauses: Badge deactivation process not synchronized with physical disposal
controls: Immediate badge deactivation upon offboarding/replacement, prior to physical disposal
Secure badge destruction (shredding/cutting) process
ITID-11825.detection: Access-control deactivation logs cross-checked against disposal records.
ITID-11825.response: Immediately verify and force deactivation of any recovered badge.
metrics: Count of badges disposed prior to confirmed deactivation
ITID-11825.notes: Differentiated from the Badge Forgery branch, which covers fabricating or cloning a badge rather than reusing a discarded genuine one.

playbook.name: Response: Discarded Badge/Access Credential Dumpster Diving
playbook.description: For an incident where a physical access badge, key fob, visitor pass, or other physical credential was found or removed from company waste without being deactivated or destroyed.

steps.title: Identify the specific badge/credential and its assigned holder
steps.desc: Determine the badge ID, printed name, or barcode and look it up in the access control system.
steps.outcome: Badge identified and its current active/inactive status confirmed.

steps.title: Immediately deactivate the badge if still active
steps.desc: Revoke the badge's access rights in the access control system without delay, regardless of whether it was recovered.
steps.guidance: This is the single most important step — treat as urgent even before recovering the physical item.
steps.outcome: Badge access rights revoked.

steps.title: Check access logs for any use of the badge after disposal
steps.desc: Review the badge's usage history for any scans after the estimated disposal time, indicating misuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the badge was used by anyone other than its assigned holder after disposal.

steps.title: Issue a replacement badge to the affected employee if needed
steps.desc: If the badge belonged to a current employee, ensure they are issued a new one and understand why the old one was revoked.
steps.outcome: Employee has working access restored via a new badge.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce badge-destruction procedure at offboarding
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm the offboarding/badge-replacement process requires physical destruction or return, not disposal in general waste.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; process gap closed if identified.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the waste area if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage covering the bin location and reported time window.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available.

steps.title: Notify security if the badge or an individual holding it was seen being removed
steps.desc: If someone was observed taking the badge, alert security to attempt identification and recovery.
steps.outcome: Security aware and attempting to locate the individual/item, or confirmed departed.

ITID-11826.def: An adversary searches unsecured recycling bins — often positioned separately from general waste with lower physical security — for discarded sensitive materials.
ITID-11826.purpose: Captures reconnaissance conducted via unsecured recycling bins specifically, which are typically less monitored than general waste and often bypass shredding requirements.
scopeIncludes: Searching dedicated recycling receptacles (paper, cardboard, mixed recycling) distinct from general/secure waste streams
scopeExcludes: Searching general locked waste/shred bins (ITID-11822)
ITID-11826.escalation: Escalate to facilities to review recycling-stream security if a pattern is observed.
indicators: Recycling bins found disturbed or emptied outside collection schedule
Recyclable materials found containing unshredded sensitive documents
vectors: Searching outdoor or common-area recycling bins lacking locks/monitoring
rootCauses: Recycling program excluded from secure-disposal policy scope
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Extending secure-disposal (shred-before-recycle) policy to recycling streams
Locked recycling receptacles
ITID-11826.detection: Relies on physical inspection/CCTV of recycling areas.
ITID-11826.response: Audit what was placed in recycling and reinforce the shred-before-recycle policy.
metrics: Count of recycling-stream policy violations found in audits
ITID-11826.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11822 by disposal stream: unsecured recycling specifically, which often falls outside standard shred-bin policy coverage.

playbook.name: Response: Recycling Bin (Non-Secure Disposal) Reconnaissance
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual searched general/mixed recycling bins (as opposed to secure shred or e-waste bins) for company information, exploiting the fact that recycling is often handled with less physical security than general waste.

steps.title: Identify the recycling location and what was searched
steps.desc: Determine which recycling bin/area was involved and, if visible, what materials were disturbed.
steps.outcome: Location and approximate content exposed identified.

steps.title: Notify security/facilities if the individual is still present
steps.desc: Alert physical security to approach and identify the individual while on-site.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Identify what type of material typically ends up in this recycling stream
steps.desc: Survey what departments/floors feed this recycling point and whether sensitive paper or media is routinely (and incorrectly) placed there instead of secure disposal.
steps.outcome: Root cause of any policy gap in what goes to open recycling identified.

steps.title: Redirect sensitive-material streams to secure disposal
steps.desc: Ensure any paper/media currently misrouted to open recycling is redirected to shred bins or certified destruction.
steps.outcome: Sensitive material no longer routes through open recycling.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce recycling vs. secure-disposal guidance
steps.desc: Record the incident and issue guidance clarifying what belongs in open recycling versus secure shred/e-waste streams.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a clarified disposal guideline.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the recycling area if available
steps.desc: Retrieve footage covering the bin location and reported time window.
steps.guidance: Recycling areas are commonly outside camera coverage and in publicly accessible locations — note if no footage exists.
steps.outcome: Footage obtained where available, or gap documented.

steps.title: Secure or relocate the recycling receptacle if it is accessible from public space
steps.desc: If the recycling bin sits outside the secure perimeter or is easily accessible, move it inside or add a lock pending review.
steps.outcome: Recycling area access restricted.

ITID-11827.def: An adversary conducts reconnaissance at a third-party waste hauler, landfill, or recycling facility handling the organization's waste, beyond the organization's direct physical controls.
ITID-11827.purpose: Captures dumpster diving conducted at an off-site or third-party waste-management facility, outside the organization's own physical perimeter and monitoring.
scopeIncludes: Reconnaissance conducted at a contracted waste-management vendor's site or transfer facility
scopeExcludes: Reconnaissance conducted on the organization's own premises (the other Dumpster Diving leaves)
ITID-11827.severity: Medium, though harder for the organization to directly detect or control.
ITID-11827.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the waste vendor confirms a breach of contracted handling procedures.
ITID-11827.escalation: Escalate to vendor management/procurement to review the waste contractor's security controls.
indicators: Waste vendor report of tampering or unauthorized access at their facility
Chain-of-custody gap between pickup and destruction confirmation
vectors: Targeting a third-party waste facility's less-controlled environment instead of the source organization
rootCauses: Waste-vendor contract lacks security requirements or destruction verification
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Contractual security/chain-of-custody requirements for waste vendors
Certificate-of-destruction requirement from waste contractors
ITID-11827.detection: Relies on third-party vendor reporting; limited organizational visibility.
ITID-11827.response: Engage the waste vendor to investigate and confirm destruction chain-of-custody.
metrics: Count of waste-vendor chain-of-custody exceptions per year
ITID-11827.notes: Scope decision: limited to reconnaissance occurring at the third-party vendor's site, to avoid duplicating on-premises dumpster-diving leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Off-Site/Third-Party Waste Facility Reconnaissance
playbook.description: For an incident where company waste was searched after it left company premises — at a third-party waste hauler's transfer station, landfill, or recycling facility — indicating the exposure occurred outside the organization's direct physical control.
