steps.title: Confirm the report source and off-site location
steps.desc: Determine who reported the activity (often the waste vendor itself, law enforcement, or a third party) and at which facility it occurred.
steps.outcome: Report source and facility identified.

steps.title: Contact the waste vendor to secure the material and site
steps.desc: Request the vendor secure the affected load/area and, if the material is still present, prevent further access pending review.
steps.outcome: Vendor confirms the material is secured or already processed/destroyed.

steps.title: Assess what was exposed and to whom
steps.desc: Determine what categories of material were involved and whether the individual who accessed it is known (e.g. a scrapper, a journalist, a competitor).
steps.outcome: Exposure scope and, where known, the accessing party identified.

steps.title: Notify affected internal teams and, if warranted, privacy/legal
steps.desc: Inform the originating department and, for any sensitive data exposure, loop in privacy/legal for potential notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Relevant stakeholders informed and assessing downstream impact.

steps.title: Review the waste vendor's handling contract and chain-of-custody controls
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether the vendor contract needs stronger chain-of-custody, destruction-certificate, or site-security requirements.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; vendor contract/process improvement recommended if warranted.

steps.title: Identify which company waste stream/pickup this material came from
steps.desc: Work with the waste vendor to trace the load back to a pickup date, route, and originating building/department.
steps.outcome: Source pickup and originating location identified where possible.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot trace the load to a specific origin, document as an unattributed exposure and proceed to the vendor-contract review step.

ITID-11828.def: An adversary searches waste generated at a company event or conference (badges, handouts, printed presentations, sign-in sheets) discarded in venue receptacles outside normal office disposal controls.
ITID-11828.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting waste generated at a company-hosted conference, trade show booth, or off-site event, where handout materials and notes are discarded in a less-controlled environment.
scopeIncludes: Searching waste at or near a conference booth, event venue, or trade-show location associated with the organization
scopeExcludes: Standard office-based waste streams (the other Dumpster Diving leaves)
ITID-11828.escalation: Escalate to marketing/events and security if attendee PII or internal materials were discarded.
indicators: Event staff report of unattended discarded handouts/sign-in sheets
Missing post-event materials inventory
vectors: Searching venue waste bins after a conference or trade-show event
rootCauses: No secure-disposal process defined for event/conference materials
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Secure disposal/shredding requirement for event materials
Post-event materials inventory reconciliation
ITID-11828.detection: Relies on event-staff reporting; minimal technical detection.
ITID-11828.response: Reconcile discarded event materials and notify affected attendees if PII was exposed.
metrics: Count of events with a completed secure-disposal reconciliation
sops: Event and Conference Materials Handling SOP
ITID-11828.notes: Differentiated by venue/context: company-hosted or company-attended external events, not standard office premises.

playbook.name: Response: Post-Event/Conference Waste Reconnaissance
playbook.description: For an incident where waste generated at a company-hosted or company-attended event, conference booth, or trade show (handouts, badge printouts, notes, discarded promotional materials with contact/attendee data) was searched or collected by an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Identify the event, location, and what waste was generated
steps.desc: Determine which event the waste came from and what materials (attendee lists, lead-scan printouts, internal notes, presentation handouts) were likely discarded.
steps.outcome: Event and material types identified.

steps.title: Recover any remaining sensitive materials on-site
steps.desc: If still at the venue, retrieve and secure any remaining unshredded materials before venue cleanup/disposal.
steps.outcome: Remaining materials recovered where possible.
steps.abort: If the event has concluded and materials are no longer recoverable, proceed directly to impact assessment.

steps.title: Assess what attendee/lead or internal data may have been exposed
steps.desc: Determine what specific data (names, emails, phone numbers, internal notes) was in the discarded materials.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Notify affected attendees/leads if their data was exposed
steps.desc: If attendee or lead data was exposed, loop in marketing/privacy to determine if those individuals should be notified.
steps.outcome: Marketing/privacy informed and assessing notification need.

steps.title: Log the incident and update event/booth disposal procedures
steps.desc: Record the incident and add a requirement that event staff bring back or shred sensitive materials rather than discard on-site.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; event handling procedure updated.

steps.title: Determine venue vs. company responsibility for the waste
steps.desc: Establish whether the waste receptacle belonged to the company's booth/team or was managed by the venue, to know who can act on it.
steps.outcome: Responsible party for the receptacle identified.

steps.title: Notify venue security or event staff if the individual is still present
steps.desc: Alert venue security to identify or challenge the individual searching the waste.
steps.outcome: Individual identified/challenged by venue staff, or confirmed departed.

ITID-11829.def: An adversary searches waste generated by an on-site vendor, contractor, or managed-service crew (e.g., a maintenance or IT contractor's discarded work notes, device packaging, or access documentation) rather than the organization's own employee waste stream.
ITID-11829.purpose: Captures dumpster diving targeting waste generated by an on-site vendor or contractor, whose disposal practices may fall outside the organization's own secure-disposal policy.
scopeIncludes: Searching waste generated by a contractor/vendor crew working on-site (e.g., a discarded work order listing access codes)
scopeExcludes: Waste generated by the organization's own employees (the other Dumpster Diving leaves)
ITID-11829.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if vendor waste contains access credentials or facility layout information.
ITID-11829.escalation: Escalate to vendor management if a pattern of insecure vendor waste-handling is identified.
indicators: Vendor work materials found in general waste containing facility-sensitive information
Vendor crew observed discarding materials without following the organization's disposal policy
vectors: Searching waste left behind by a contractor crew at the end of a work shift
rootCauses: Vendor/contractor contracts do not extend the organization's secure-disposal requirements to their own materials
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Contractual requirement that vendor/contractor waste follow the organization's secure-disposal policy
Vendor work-area inspection at shift end
ITID-11829.detection: Relies on facilities/security spot-checks of vendor work areas.
ITID-11829.response: Review vendor contract terms and inspect the vendor's work area disposal practices.
metrics: Count of vendor work-area disposal policy violations found
ITID-11829.notes: Differentiated by waste source: contractor/vendor-generated waste specifically, not the organization's own employee waste stream.

playbook.name: Response: Vendor/Contractor Waste Stream Reconnaissance
playbook.description: For an incident where waste generated by or passed through a vendor or contractor working on company premises or systems (e.g. a print vendor, managed-service provider, cleaning contractor) was searched, exposing company information that transited outside direct company control.

steps.title: Identify the vendor/contractor and the waste stream involved
steps.desc: Determine which vendor's work generated the waste and what type of company information it may contain.
steps.outcome: Vendor and material type identified.

steps.title: Contact the vendor to halt and secure the waste stream
steps.desc: Notify the vendor's point of contact to immediately secure any remaining affected material and stop further disposal until reviewed.
steps.outcome: Vendor confirms the material is secured or already destroyed.

steps.title: Assess what company data was exposed through the vendor's process
steps.desc: Determine what specific company information was in the exposed waste and how sensitive it is.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Escalate to vendor management/procurement for contract review
steps.desc: Loop in the team that owns the vendor relationship to review the incident against the vendor's contractual data-handling obligations.
steps.outcome: Vendor manager informed and engaging the vendor on corrective action.

steps.title: Log the incident and reassess the vendor's disposal/security requirements
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend whether the vendor contract needs stronger disposal, chain-of-custody, or audit requirements — or whether the vendor relationship should be reconsidered.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a vendor-management recommendation.

steps.title: Confirm where in the process the exposure occurred
steps.desc: Establish whether the waste was exposed on company premises, at the vendor's facility, or in transit.
steps.outcome: Location/stage of exposure identified.

ITID-11831.def: An adversary physically presenting as someone they are not to gain facility access or cooperation, with the specific persona (delivery, maintenance, IT, cleaning, new-hire, auditor, interview candidate, emergency responder) not yet identified.
ITID-11831.purpose: Catch-all for a reported on-site impersonation attempt before the specific persona used is identified.
scopeIncludes: Reports of impersonation logged before the persona is known
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling persona ITID

The unclassified catch-all under the Physical Security Breaches / Social Engineering Attacks Tier-2 (ITID-14511), used for incidents logged purely as a physical-security event rather than a social-engineering pretext
ITID-11831.severity: Medium; reassess once the persona is identified.
ITID-11831.priority: P2 by default given the risk of escalation to further access.
ITID-11831.escalation: Escalate for documentation and reclassify once more detail is available.
indicators: Report of an unfamiliar individual claiming a role without verification
vectors: Presenting a fabricated role/identity to facility staff
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Visitor verification and escort policy
metrics: Count pending reclassification
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11831.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Differentiated from ITID-14511, which is used when no social-engineering pretext analysis was performed at all.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General On-Site Impersonation
playbook.description: For a report or observation of an individual on company premises falsely claiming a role or identity (vendor, staff, contractor, etc.) to gain access or cooperation, where the specific impersonated role is not yet known.

steps.title: Capture the report details (who, where, when, claimed identity)
steps.desc: Record who reported the impersonation, the location, time, and what role/identity the individual claimed.
steps.outcome: Enough detail to begin verification and pull footage.

steps.title: Notify security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security so they can find and verify the individual while on-site.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Trace areas accessed and information obtained
steps.desc: Determine what areas the individual entered and what information or cooperation they obtained from staff.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access and any information disclosed.

steps.title: Brief staff who interacted with the individual
steps.desc: Speak with any employees who cooperated with the individual to understand what was disclosed and reinforce verification habits.
steps.outcome: Staff briefed and aware of what occurred.

steps.title: Log the incident and assess identity-verification gaps
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether reception/staff verification procedures need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Verify the claimed identity against legitimate records
steps.desc: Check the claimed role against staff directory, vendor roster, or scheduled appointments to determine if it is genuine.
steps.guidance: Call the purported employer/company using a known number, not one the individual provided.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity confirmed as legitimate or confirmed false.
steps.abort: If the claimed identity checks out as legitimate, close as a false report.

steps.title: Escort the individual out if identity cannot be verified
steps.desc: If the individual cannot produce verifiable credentials matching the claimed identity, escort them off the premises.
steps.outcome: Individual removed from the premises or confirmed legitimate.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

steps.title: Pull CCTV covering the individual's presence
steps.desc: Retrieve footage documenting the individual's appearance, movements, and entry point.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11832.def: An adversary presents as delivery or courier personnel — using a branded uniform, packages, or handheld scanner props — to gain entry to a facility or reach a specific individual/area.
ITID-11832.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as a delivery driver or courier to gain physical access or hand off/receive an item under false pretenses.
scopeIncludes: Presenting as a package/courier delivery person to gain entry or reach a mailroom/reception area
scopeExcludes: Simply wearing courier-style branded clothing while tailgating without a sustained persona interaction (ITID-11814)
ITID-11832.escalation: Escalate to physical security and reception if no matching delivery is scheduled.
indicators: No matching entry in the delivery/courier log or scheduled shipment
Unfamiliar courier company or unmarked vehicle
vectors: Presenting fabricated packages or a false pickup/delivery request at reception
rootCauses: Reception does not verify deliveries against a pre-scheduled manifest
controls: Delivery pre-registration and manifest verification at reception
Mailroom/loading-dock as sole delivery drop point
ITID-11832.detection: Reception log cross-check against carrier manifests provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11832.response: Verify against the delivery manifest and detain/escort if unverifiable.
metrics: Count of unverified delivery-persona entries per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11832.notes: This on-site impersonation branch (Tier-3: Physical Social Engineering Attacks, Tier-2: Social Engineering) is scoped to the sustained delivery-persona interaction; brief uniform-based tailgating with no interaction is ITID-11814.

playbook.name: Response: Delivery/Courier Personnel Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as a delivery driver or courier to gain access to a controlled area, bypassing normal visitor verification because deliveries are often waved through quickly.

steps.title: Identify the claimed courier company and package details
steps.desc: Record which company the individual claimed to represent and what package/delivery was claimed.
steps.outcome: Claimed courier identity and delivery details recorded.

steps.title: Notify security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security to find and verify the individual, and to recover any package they may have left or claim not to have delivered.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Trace areas accessed beyond the loading dock/reception
steps.desc: Review footage to confirm whether the individual went beyond the expected delivery drop point.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access.

steps.title: Brief mailroom/reception staff on the pattern observed
steps.desc: Circulate a description of the individual and courier claim used so front-desk staff recognize a repeat attempt.
steps.outcome: Front-line staff briefed.

steps.title: Log the incident and evaluate delivery-verification process
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether delivery personnel should always be logged/escorted rather than waved through.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Verify against expected deliveries and the mailroom/reception log
steps.desc: Check whether a legitimate delivery from that courier was expected around that time.
steps.guidance: Contact the courier company directly via a known number if in doubt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether this was a legitimate expected delivery or not.
steps.abort: If a legitimate delivery is confirmed, close as a false report.

steps.title: Escort the individual out and inspect any item they carried in
steps.desc: If the individual cannot be verified as a legitimate courier, escort them out and, if safe and appropriate, inspect or isolate any item they brought.
steps.guidance: Do not physically handle a suspicious package yourself — involve security/law enforcement if a package is suspected hazardous.
steps.outcome: Individual removed; any suspicious item isolated and reported.
steps.abort: If a package is suspected hazardous, treat as a security emergency and involve law enforcement/EOD as applicable.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the entry point and delivery area
steps.desc: Retrieve footage of the individual's entry, uniform/vehicle, and movements.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11833.def: An adversary presents as a maintenance/facilities technician — carrying tools, a work order, or branded coveralls — to gain access to utility rooms, server closets, or restricted back-of-house areas.
ITID-11833.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as a maintenance or facilities technician to gain access to mechanical, electrical, or back-of-house areas.
scopeIncludes: Presenting a fabricated or unverified work order to gain access to mechanical/electrical/utility spaces
scopeExcludes: An IT/telecom-specific technician persona targeting network/server rooms (ITID-11835)
ITID-11833.severity: High, given access to utility and infrastructure areas.
ITID-11833.escalation: Escalate to facilities management to verify against the scheduled maintenance calendar.
indicators: No matching entry on the facilities work-order/maintenance schedule
Technician unable to name the correct facilities contact or building system
vectors: Presenting a forged or verbal-only work order at reception or to facilities staff
rootCauses: Facilities/maintenance visits not verified against a pre-scheduled work-order system
controls: Work-order pre-verification with facilities management
Escort requirement for maintenance access to restricted mechanical areas
ITID-11833.detection: Work-order schedule cross-check provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11833.response: Verify against the facilities work-order system before granting access.
metrics: Count of unverified maintenance-persona entries per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11833.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11835 by target area/persona focus: general building mechanical/electrical systems, not IT/telecom infrastructure.

playbook.name: Response: Maintenance/Facilities Technician Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as a maintenance or facilities technician (HVAC, plumbing, electrical) to gain access to restricted or back-of-house areas such as server rooms, comms closets, or utility spaces.

steps.title: Identify the claimed trade/company and work claimed to be performed
steps.desc: Record what trade the individual claimed, what company they said they were from, and what work they claimed to be doing.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity and work order details recorded.

steps.title: Notify security to locate and challenge the individual immediately
steps.desc: Given the elevated access facilities technicians are often granted (server rooms, comms closets), treat this as urgent and dispatch security without delay.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Inspect any restricted area (server room, comms closet, utility space) accessed
steps.desc: Physically inspect and, where applicable, have IT check for tampering with equipment, cabling, or added devices (e.g. rogue network taps).
steps.outcome: Area confirmed untampered, or tampering identified and escalated to IT security.

steps.title: Brief facilities and reception staff on the pattern observed
steps.desc: Circulate a description of the individual and claimed trade so staff recognize a repeat attempt.
steps.outcome: Facilities/front-line staff briefed.

steps.title: Log the incident and tighten escort requirements for unaccompanied trade access
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend that access to server rooms/comms closets by outside technicians always require an escort and pre-verified work order.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Verify against scheduled facilities work orders
steps.desc: Check with facilities management whether any maintenance work was actually scheduled matching this claim.
steps.guidance: Contact the claimed vendor directly via a known number if in doubt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether this matches a real scheduled work order.
steps.abort: If a legitimate scheduled work order is confirmed, close as a false report.

steps.title: Escort the individual out and secure any area they accessed
steps.desc: If identity cannot be verified, escort them out and lock down any restricted space they entered pending inspection.
steps.outcome: Individual removed; accessed restricted areas secured.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of entry and any restricted areas visited
steps.desc: Retrieve footage of the individual's entry, appearance, and movement toward sensitive areas.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11834.def: An adversary presents as cleaning/janitorial staff — often after hours — to gain broad, low-scrutiny access to offices, desks, and unattended workstations.
ITID-11834.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as cleaning or janitorial staff, a persona that plausibly grants after-hours, low-scrutiny access to nearly every area of a facility.
scopeIncludes: Presenting as janitorial/cleaning staff to gain after-hours or off-peak access to office areas
scopeExcludes: Genuine cleaning contractor personnel whose access is separately abused (covered under Access Abuse, ITID-14131-14133, if the individual is an authorized party misusing legitimate access)
ITID-11834.severity: High, given the persona's broad, low-scrutiny access footprint.
ITID-11834.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if occurring after hours with no other staff present.
ITID-11834.escalation: Escalate to physical security and facilities immediately, especially after hours.
indicators: Individual not on the contracted cleaning crew roster
Cleaning activity at desks/workstations inconsistent with the contracted scope
vectors: Presenting as cleaning staff to move freely through unattended offices after hours
rootCauses: Cleaning crew roster not verified nightly against the contracted vendor's staff list
controls: Nightly roster verification for contracted cleaning crews
After-hours CCTV monitoring of office areas
ITID-11834.detection: Roster cross-check and after-hours CCTV provide a real technical signal.
ITID-11834.response: Verify against the contracted cleaning crew roster and investigate any mismatch.
metrics: Count of cleaning-crew roster mismatches per month
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11834.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14131-14133 (Access Abuse), which covers a genuinely authorized individual misusing their own legitimate access, not an outsider impersonating the role.

playbook.name: Response: Cleaning/Janitorial Staff Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as cleaning/janitorial staff, exploiting the fact that such personnel typically work after-hours with broad, unaccompanied access to offices and desks.

steps.title: Identify the claimed cleaning company and shift
steps.desc: Record what cleaning company the individual claimed to represent and what shift/time they claimed to be working.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity and shift details recorded.

steps.title: Notify security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: Alert on-call/after-hours security to find and verify the individual.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed.

steps.title: Check desks/offices accessed for disturbed documents or devices
steps.desc: Working with affected employees, check whether any unlocked desks, papers, or unattended devices were disturbed or are missing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of physical access and no loss, or a loss identified and escalated.

steps.title: Remind employees of clean-desk policy for overnight hours
steps.desc: Reinforce that sensitive documents and devices should be secured before leaving for the day, given after-hours access by cleaning staff.
steps.outcome: Awareness reminder delivered to affected floor/team.

steps.title: Log the incident and review cleaning vendor access controls
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether the cleaning vendor's badge issuance, escort requirements, or after-hours monitoring need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a vendor-management recommendation.

steps.title: Verify against the contracted cleaning vendor's roster
steps.desc: Check with the contracted janitorial vendor whether this individual is a legitimate, currently employed staff member scheduled for that shift.
steps.guidance: Contact the vendor directly via a known number, not a number the individual provided.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the individual is a legitimate vendor employee.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as a false report but note if their badge/uniform was unclear.

steps.title: Escort the individual out if identity cannot be verified
steps.desc: If not confirmed as legitimate vendor staff, escort them off the premises.
steps.outcome: Individual removed or confirmed legitimate.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of entry and movement through office areas
steps.desc: Retrieve footage of the individual's entry, appearance, and which desks/offices they approached.
steps.guidance: After-hours cleaning shifts often coincide with reduced camera monitoring staff — flag this for review even if footage exists.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11835.def: An adversary presents as IT support or a telecom technician — citing a fabricated ticket or outage — to gain access to network infrastructure, server rooms, or an employee's workstation.
ITID-11835.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as an IT or telecom technician to gain physical access to network closets, server rooms, or end-user workstations.
scopeIncludes: Presenting a fabricated IT support ticket or telecom work order to gain access to network/server areas or workstations
scopeExcludes: A general maintenance/facilities technician persona not targeting IT infrastructure specifically (ITID-11833)
ITID-11835.severity: High, given direct access to network and server infrastructure.
ITID-11835.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if server-room or network-closet access is obtained.
ITID-11835.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately upon any unverified IT-persona access to infrastructure areas.
indicators: No matching ticket in the IT service-management system
Technician requesting direct physical access to server room without an escort
vectors: Citing a fabricated help-desk ticket or network outage to gain facilities/IT staff cooperation
rootCauses: IT support visits not verified against the IT service-management ticketing system
controls: Ticket verification against the IT service-management system before granting infrastructure access
Mandatory escort for server-room/network-closet access
ITID-11835.detection: IT ticketing system cross-check provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11835.response: Verify against the IT service-management system before granting any infrastructure access.
metrics: Count of unverified IT/telecom-persona access attempts per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11835.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11833 by target infrastructure: network/server/IT systems specifically, versus general building mechanical/electrical systems.

playbook.name: Response: IT/Telecom Technician Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as an IT or telecom technician on-site to gain physical access to workstations, network closets, or telecom equipment, often paired with a request to plug in a device or access a system directly.

steps.title: Identify the claimed company and stated work
steps.desc: Record what company/role the individual claimed and what work (cabling, equipment swap, line repair) they said they were performing.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity and work details recorded.

steps.title: Notify security and IT security to respond immediately
steps.desc: Given the potential for a physical device to be planted on the network, treat this as urgent and involve both physical security and IT security.
steps.outcome: Individual located and challenged, or confirmed departed; IT security aware.

steps.title: Inspect for rogue devices (implants, taps, unauthorized hardware)
steps.desc: Physically and, where possible, electronically inspect the affected equipment/network segment for any planted device.
steps.guidance: Check for anything plugged into ports, cabling, or peripherals that shouldn't be there.
steps.outcome: Rogue device found and removed, or area confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore isolated equipment to service once cleared
steps.desc: Reconnect and confirm normal operation of any equipment isolated during containment.
steps.outcome: Equipment restored to normal service.

steps.title: Log the incident and tighten escort/verification requirements for IT vendor access
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend that outside IT/telecom technicians always require a verified work order and internal escort.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Verify against IT/telecom vendor records and scheduled work
steps.desc: Check with the internal IT team and any contracted telecom/MSP vendor whether this work was actually scheduled and by whom.
steps.guidance: Contact the claimed vendor directly via a known number.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether this matches real scheduled work.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as a false report.
steps.tool: IT service management system / vendor management system

steps.title: Isolate any equipment the individual physically touched
steps.desc: Disconnect or isolate from the network any port, switch, or device the individual accessed, pending inspection.
steps.outcome: Potentially compromised equipment isolated.

steps.title: Review network logs for anomalous activity from the affected segment
steps.desc: Check SIEM/network logs around the incident time for unusual traffic, new device connections, or authentication attempts from the affected area.
steps.outcome: No anomalous activity found, or anomalies identified and escalated as a network intrusion.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of entry and any equipment areas accessed
steps.desc: Retrieve footage of the individual's entry, appearance, and any workstation/network closet interaction.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11836.def: An adversary presents as a new hire or newly onboarded contractor — claiming their badge/credentials are still being processed — to be escorted or granted temporary access by staff unfamiliar with the actual onboarding roster.
ITID-11836.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as a newly hired employee or contractor to exploit the onboarding process's inherent unfamiliarity and looser initial scrutiny.
scopeIncludes: Claiming new-hire status to obtain a temporary badge, escort, or provisional access
scopeExcludes: An interview-candidate persona used only to reach an interview location, not to obtain working access (ITID-11838)
ITID-11836.escalation: Escalate to HR and physical security to verify against the onboarding roster.
indicators: Individual not on the current-week onboarding/new-hire roster from HR
Requesting provisional access without a sponsoring manager present
vectors: Claiming new-hire status to bypass standard visitor verification
rootCauses: Reception/security not given a current daily new-hire roster from HR
controls: Daily new-hire roster shared with reception/security
Sponsoring-manager confirmation required for provisional access
ITID-11836.detection: HR onboarding-roster cross-check provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11836.response: Verify against the HR onboarding roster and require sponsoring-manager confirmation.
metrics: Count of unverified new-hire-persona entries per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11836.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11838 by objective: seeking working access/credentials as a purported employee, versus merely reaching an interview room as a candidate.

playbook.name: Response: New Employee/Contractor Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual claimed to be a newly hired employee or contractor to gain unescorted access, badge issuance, or system credentials before proper verification could occur.

steps.title: Identify the claimed name, role, and hiring manager/sponsor
steps.desc: Record the name, claimed role, department, and sponsoring manager the individual stated.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity details recorded.

steps.title: Halt any badge, credential, or account issuance in progress
steps.desc: If a badge or system account was being issued or was already issued based on the unverified claim, pause or revoke it immediately.
steps.outcome: No active badge/credential remains issued to an unverified individual.

steps.title: Determine what access, badge, or accounts were actually granted
steps.desc: Audit exactly what physical access and system accounts were provisioned before the impersonation was caught.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of any access granted.

steps.title: Brief HR/onboarding and facilities staff on the pattern observed
steps.desc: Share details with the teams who process new-hire access so they can recognize and prevent a repeat attempt.
steps.outcome: HR/facilities staff briefed.

steps.title: Log the incident and tighten new-hire verification before access provisioning
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend that badge/account issuance always require confirmed HR system verification before, not after, physical access is granted.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Verify against HR/onboarding records
steps.desc: Check with HR and the named sponsoring manager directly (not via contact info the individual provided) to confirm whether this hire is real and expected on this date.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the individual is a genuine new hire/contractor.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate but simply ahead of paperwork, resolve as an onboarding process delay rather than a security incident.

steps.title: Notify security to locate the individual if still on-site
steps.desc: If the individual cannot be verified, alert security to find and escort them out.
steps.outcome: Individual located and escorted out, or confirmed departed.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

steps.title: Revoke any granted access and disable accounts
steps.desc: Fully revoke any badge and disable any account created for the impersonated identity.
steps.outcome: All access revoked and confirmed.

ITID-11837.def: An adversary presents as an external auditor, compliance inspector, or regulatory official — invoking implied authority to compel cooperation and gain access to records or restricted areas.
ITID-11837.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as an auditor, compliance inspector, or regulator to leverage the authority of a compliance visit to gain access or extract information.
scopeIncludes: Presenting fabricated audit/inspection credentials to compel staff cooperation or access
scopeExcludes: A vendor/third-party support persona not invoking regulatory or audit authority (the other sibling personas in this Tier-4 group)
ITID-11837.severity: High, given the authority-based pretext often bypasses normal skepticism.
ITID-11837.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if financial or compliance records are accessed.
ITID-11837.escalation: Escalate to legal/compliance and physical security to verify the audit engagement is genuine.
indicators: No corresponding entry in the compliance/audit engagement calendar
Auditor unable to produce verifiable engagement documentation or firm contact
vectors: Invoking a claimed regulatory or audit mandate to pressure staff into granting access without verification
rootCauses: No process to verify an unannounced auditor against a known/expected engagement list
controls: Verification of any audit/inspection visit against legal/compliance's engagement calendar before granting access
Staff training on authority-based social-engineering pretexts
ITID-11837.detection: Compliance engagement-calendar cross-check provides a real technical signal.
ITID-11837.response: Verify with legal/compliance before granting any access based on an audit/inspector claim.
metrics: Count of unverified auditor-persona access attempts per year
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11837.notes: Differentiated from sibling personas by the authority-based pretext axis: invoking regulatory/audit authority specifically, distinct from service-role personas.

playbook.name: Response: Auditor/Inspector Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as a regulatory auditor, inspector, or compliance reviewer to gain access to records, facilities, or staff cooperation by invoking the authority and urgency typically associated with audits.

steps.title: Identify the claimed agency/firm and stated audit scope
steps.desc: Record what organization the individual claimed to represent, what audit/inspection they claimed authority for, and any documentation they presented.
steps.outcome: Claimed identity and audit scope recorded.

steps.title: Halt any document or system access being provided
steps.desc: Pause any records access, facility tours, or staff interviews being conducted based on the unverified claim.
steps.outcome: No further access or disclosure occurs pending verification.

steps.title: Determine what records or information were disclosed
steps.desc: Work with staff who interacted with the individual to establish exactly what documents, systems, or information were shown or handed over.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of disclosure.

steps.title: Loop in legal/compliance and, if warranted, notify affected data owners
steps.desc: Inform legal/compliance of the disclosure scope so they can assess regulatory or contractual notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/compliance informed and assessing next steps.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce audit-verification procedure
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm staff know to route any audit/inspection request through compliance for verification before granting access.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Verify with legal/compliance and the claimed agency directly
steps.desc: Contact internal legal/compliance to confirm whether an audit is genuinely scheduled, and independently verify the individual's credentials with the named agency/firm using a publicly known contact number.
steps.guidance: Never rely on contact information the individual themselves provides.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the audit and the individual's credentials are genuine.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, hand off to compliance for normal audit handling and close this playbook.

steps.title: Notify security to locate the individual if verification fails
steps.desc: If the claim cannot be verified, alert security to find and escort the individual out.
steps.outcome: Individual located and escorted out, or confirmed departed.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11838.def: An adversary presents as a scheduled interview candidate to gain a plausible, escorted entry into the facility, potentially deviating from the escort to reach unauthorized areas.
ITID-11838.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as a job interview candidate to gain a legitimate-seeming, escorted reason to be inside the facility.
scopeIncludes: Claiming a scheduled interview to gain entry, including deviating from an assigned escort once inside
scopeExcludes: Claiming new-hire status seeking ongoing working access/credentials (ITID-11836)
ITID-11838.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the individual is found away from the interview escort/location.
ITID-11838.escalation: Escalate to physical security if the individual deviates from the interview escort path.
indicators: No matching entry on the recruiting/interview schedule
Individual found in an area inconsistent with the interview location
vectors: Claiming a scheduled interview to obtain a visitor badge and building access
rootCauses: Interview visits not consistently verified against the recruiting calendar at reception
controls: Interview-schedule verification against the recruiting/ATS calendar at reception
Visitor badge restricted to interview-room floor/zone
ITID-11838.detection: Recruiting-calendar cross-check and zone-restricted badge access provide a real technical signal.
ITID-11838.response: Verify against the recruiting calendar and confirm the escort remained with the candidate throughout the visit.
metrics: Count of unverified interview-persona entries per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11838.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11836 by objective: a one-time escorted visit as a candidate, not an attempt to obtain ongoing employee-level access.

playbook.name: Response: Interview Candidate Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as a job interview candidate to gain a legitimate-seeming reason for on-site access, potentially to conduct reconnaissance of office layout, badge systems, or overheard conversations.

steps.title: Identify the claimed interview details
steps.desc: Record the name, role applied for, and interviewer/recruiter the individual claimed to be meeting.
steps.outcome: Claimed interview details recorded.

steps.title: Notify security/reception to hold the individual in the lobby pending verification
steps.desc: Do not allow the individual past reception into working areas until the interview claim is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Individual held in a public/controlled area pending verification.

steps.title: Check whether the individual gained any unescorted access before being stopped
steps.desc: Review footage/access logs to confirm the individual was contained to public/reception areas and did not wander unescorted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access, if any occurred.

steps.title: Brief reception/recruiting staff on the pattern observed
steps.desc: Share details with reception and recruiting so they recognize a repeat attempt and always confirm candidate visits before escort.
steps.outcome: Reception/recruiting staff briefed.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce candidate visit verification and escort policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm that interview candidates are always verified against the ATS/recruiter before being let past reception, and remain escorted throughout the visit.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Verify against the recruiting/ATS calendar
steps.desc: Check with the named recruiter/interviewer directly and the applicant tracking system to confirm a genuine interview was scheduled.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the interview is genuine and scheduled.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as a false report.

steps.title: Escort the individual out if the claim cannot be verified
steps.desc: If no matching interview exists, escort the individual off the premises.
steps.outcome: Individual removed or confirmed legitimate and properly escorted to the real interview.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, involve law enforcement.

ITID-11839.def: An adversary presents as a firefighter, paramedic, utility crew member, or other emergency responder — leveraging the urgency of the persona to be waved through access controls without verification.
ITID-11839.purpose: Captures an adversary posing as an emergency responder or utility worker to exploit the urgency and implied authority of an emergency-response persona to bypass normal access controls.
scopeIncludes: Presenting as an emergency responder or utility worker to bypass normal access verification during a claimed emergency
scopeExcludes: Staging a fake emergency event itself (fire drill, fake emergency vehicle) as the pretext mechanism (the Fake Emergency Services branch, ITID-14521/14522)
ITID-11839.severity: High, given staff are trained to yield to genuine emergency responders without question.
ITID-11839.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if no corresponding emergency was reported to local authorities.
ITID-11839.escalation: Escalate immediately and cross-check with local emergency services dispatch.
indicators: No corresponding call/dispatch record with local emergency services or the utility provider
Responder unable to produce agency/utility identification on request
vectors: Claiming an in-progress emergency to be waved past badge/reception controls
rootCauses: Staff trained to yield immediately to any emergency-responder claim without a verification step
controls: Dispatch/utility-provider verification call as part of emergency-access procedure where feasible
Security desk immediate notification protocol for any emergency-responder claim
ITID-11839.detection: Dispatch-record cross-check provides a real technical signal when time permits; largely reliant on staff judgment in true emergencies.
ITID-11839.response: Where safe and time permits, verify with dispatch/utility provider; otherwise document and reconcile after the fact.
metrics: Count of emergency-responder-persona access events reconciled against dispatch records
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-11839.notes: Differentiated from the Fake Emergency Services branch (ITID-14521/14522), which covers the adversary staging the emergency event itself; this leaf covers only the responder/worker persona used once an emergency (real or claimed) is already in play.

playbook.name: Response: Emergency Responder/Utility Worker Impersonation
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual posed as a firefighter, paramedic, police officer, or utility worker (power, water, gas) responding to a claimed emergency, exploiting the urgency of such claims to bypass normal access verification.

steps.title: Assess whether a genuine emergency is in progress
steps.desc: Immediately determine whether there is an actual emergency condition (fire alarm, utility outage, medical event) that would independently explain the responder's presence.
steps.guidance: If a real emergency is confirmed, prioritize life safety and normal emergency response over identity verification.
steps.outcome: Determined whether a genuine emergency condition exists.
steps.abort: If a genuine life-safety emergency is confirmed, follow standard emergency procedures first and revisit identity verification afterward.

steps.title: Notify security to discreetly verify and, if needed, challenge the individual
steps.desc: Alert physical security to approach the individual professionally, mindful that real emergency responders should not be obstructed if genuine.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with the identification/verification step before any direct challenge.
steps.outcome: Individual verified, or confirmed impersonator and handled accordingly.

steps.title: Trace areas accessed and any equipment/systems the individual interacted with
steps.desc: Review footage and access logs to determine full scope of access gained under the false pretext.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access.

steps.title: Brief security and reception staff on the pattern and correct verification steps
steps.desc: Ensure front-line staff know how to verify emergency responder/utility claims without obstructing genuine emergencies.
steps.outcome: Staff briefed with a clear verification procedure for future incidents.

steps.title: Log the incident and formalize the emergency-responder verification procedure
steps.desc: Record the incident and document a clear, fast verification procedure that balances not obstructing real emergencies against confirming legitimacy.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; procedure documented and shared with security/reception.

steps.title: Verify the individual's claimed agency/utility and credentials
steps.desc: If no independently confirmed emergency exists, contact the claimed agency or utility company directly via a known non-emergency number to verify dispatch.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on ID or a badge shown by the individual alone — verify via the issuing organization.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the individual was genuinely dispatched.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, cooperate normally and close this playbook.

steps.title: Escort the individual out if impersonation is confirmed
steps.desc: Once confirmed as an impersonator, escort them off the premises and contact actual law enforcement given the impersonation of a protected role.
steps.guidance: Impersonating an emergency responder or law enforcement officer is itself frequently a distinct criminal offense — involve real law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Individual removed and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of entry and movement
steps.desc: Retrieve footage documenting the individual's appearance, uniform/vehicle, and areas entered.
steps.outcome: Footage preserved for the incident window.

ITID-11911.def: A phishing campaign deliberately coordinated across two or more communication channels against the same target, without enough detail captured to classify which specific channels were combined.
ITID-11911.purpose: Catch-all for a multi-channel phishing campaign that does not fit a more specific leaf under Multi-Channel Phishing.
scopeIncludes: Multi-channel campaign reports logged before the specific channel combination is confirmed
scopeExcludes: A single-channel phishing/smishing/vishing/quishing attack (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 ITID)
Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the channel combination is known
ITID-11911.severity: Medium-High by default, since coordination across channels indicates a more resourced, deliberate campaign than a single-channel attempt.
ITID-11911.escalation: Escalate to SOC for cross-channel correlation once a second channel is confirmed.
indicators: Same target or theme contacted via more than one communication channel within a short window
vectors: Coordinated contact across an unconfirmed combination of channels
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Security awareness training on multi-channel phishing patterns
ITID-11911.detection: Requires cross-channel correlation (email, SMS, voice logs) that is often manual absent a unified reporting/triage tool.
ITID-11911.response: Document all channels involved and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count of multi-channel phishing reports pending reclassification
ITID-11911.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. The defining criterion for the whole Multi-Channel Phishing Type is coordinated use of two or more channels against the same target; a single-channel attempt belongs under the corresponding Phishing tier-4 ITID instead.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Multi-Channel Phishing Campaign
playbook.description: For a phishing attack that spans multiple communication channels (email, SMS, voice, social media) whose specific channel combination has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Map all channels used in the campaign
steps.desc: Interview the target(s) and review available logs to identify every channel the attacker used (email, SMS, call, social DM, etc.) and the sequence/timing.
steps.guidance: Multi-channel campaigns are often missed because each channel's owner (mail team, telecom, social media admin) sees only their piece — actively cross-check across teams.
steps.outcome: Full channel map and timeline of the campaign documented.

steps.title: Contain each compromised channel/account in parallel
steps.desc: For each channel where compromise occurred, apply the relevant containment (e.g. password reset for email, SIM/carrier lock for SMS-based compromise, account lock for social media).
steps.guidance: Coordinate containment across all owning teams simultaneously — a delay on one channel lets the attacker pivot back through it.
steps.outcome: All compromised channels/accounts contained.
steps.tool: Identity provider / carrier / social platform admin

steps.title: Check for persistence across all touched systems
steps.desc: Review each account/system the target interacted with for attacker-added persistence (forwarding rules, new MFA devices, OAuth grants, forwarding on mobile carrier account).
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence on each channel.

steps.title: Restore access across all channels with re-verified identity
steps.desc: Restore the user's access on each affected channel only after fresh identity verification and credential/MFA re-enrollment.
steps.outcome: Full access restored with confirmed clean state on every channel.

steps.title: Document the full attack chain across channels
steps.desc: Record the complete cross-channel sequence and identify which channel handoff was the weak point, feeding this into awareness training.
steps.outcome: Full attack chain documented and training material updated.

steps.title: Determine current compromise state
steps.desc: Establish whether the target took any action (clicked, called back, replied, submitted credentials/OTP) on any channel.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise state and which channel(s) led to it.
steps.abort: If no action was taken on any channel, downgrade to a reported near-miss and skip containment/eradication.

steps.title: Block attacker infrastructure across channels
steps.desc: Block the sending domain/email, phone number/SMS shortcode, and any social media accounts identified as part of the campaign.
steps.outcome: Attacker infrastructure blocked across all identified channels.
steps.tool: Mail gateway / SIEM / social platform admin

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Remove any malicious forwarding rules, unauthorized MFA methods, or OAuth grants found.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on any channel.

ITID-11912.def: An attacker sends a phishing email and a coordinated SMS text to the same target — often referencing each other or reinforcing the same pretext — to increase credibility and give the target a second path to the malicious link.
ITID-11912.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign that deliberately pairs an email lure with a follow-up or companion SMS message to the same target.
scopeIncludes: Phishing email followed by an SMS referencing the same pretext (e.g., 'check your email for an urgent notice')
SMS providing a shortened link that mirrors a phishing email sent to the same target
scopeExcludes: A standalone SMS phishing (smishing) attempt with no corresponding email (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 ITID)
Email + voice call combinations (see ITID-11913)
ITID-11912.severity: Medium-High — the second channel materially increases perceived legitimacy and click-through likelihood.
ITID-11912.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were entered on the linked page.
ITID-11912.escalation: Escalate to SOC for correlated email/SMS gateway analysis once both channels are confirmed.
indicators: Phishing email and SMS received within a short time window referencing the same theme
Matching or near-matching destination URL across both messages
vectors: Bulk phishing email campaign paired with an SMS blast using a leaked or scraped phone number list
rootCauses: Email and SMS security tooling operate in silos with no cross-channel correlation
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Email gateway filtering
SMS/carrier-level filtering
Security awareness training on cross-channel consistency checks
ITID-11912.detection: Requires correlating email gateway logs with SMS/carrier reporting; individually each channel has partial detection but the coordination itself is often only visible via manual analyst correlation.
ITID-11912.response: Block the shared destination URL/domain across both channels and treat as a single coordinated incident rather than two separate reports.
metrics: Count of confirmed email+SMS coordinated campaigns per quarter
detections: Email gateway and SMS filtering correlation
ITID-11912.notes: Defining criterion is the email+SMS channel pairing specifically; either channel alone is tracked under its own Phishing tier-4 ITID.

playbook.name: Response: Email + SMS Coordinated Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing campaign combining an email lure with a follow-up or preceding SMS (smishing) message reinforcing urgency or delivering a link/OTP request.

steps.title: Collect both the email and SMS message content
steps.desc: Preserve the full email with headers and the SMS content with sending number/shortcode.
steps.guidance: Check whether the SMS references the email (e.g. 'check your inbox') to confirm coordination rather than coincidence.
steps.outcome: Both messages preserved with metadata.
steps.tool: Mail gateway / mobile carrier or MDM logs

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke active sessions/tokens for the targeted account.
steps.outcome: Account secured against further use of any captured credentials.

steps.title: Check for attacker-established persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for new forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants created after the incident timestamp.
steps.guidance: If OTP was captured via SMS-linked MFA, specifically check for a newly registered MFA method.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has full, confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the coordination pattern
steps.desc: Record how the email and SMS reinforced each other, and add this multi-channel pattern as a specific example in awareness training.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness training updated with this specific pattern.

steps.title: Determine what action the target took and on which channel
steps.desc: Confirm whether the target clicked the email link, replied to the SMS, or entered credentials/OTP on a linked page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken on either channel, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the email sender/domain and SMS number, and purge the message
steps.desc: Block the sending infrastructure on both channels and purge the email from other mailboxes org-wide if part of a wider send.
steps.outcome: Both channels blocked; email purged where applicable.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, and remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11913.def: An attacker sends a phishing email and follows up (or precedes it) with a live phone call to the same target, using the call to build urgency, walk the target through the email, or verbally provide credentials/codes the email link requests.
ITID-11913.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign that pairs an email lure with a coordinated follow-up phone call to the same target.
scopeIncludes: Phishing email followed by a call urging the target to 'check your email' or act on it immediately
A call used to relay a one-time passcode or verification step tied to a phishing email link
scopeExcludes: Email + SMS coordinated phishing (see ITID-11912)
A standalone vishing call with no corresponding email (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 vishing ITID)
ITID-11913.severity: High — a live voice component significantly increases pressure and perceived legitimacy compared to email alone.
ITID-11913.priority: P1 if the call was used to relay an MFA/OTP code tied to the phishing link.
ITID-11913.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately if any credential or MFA code was disclosed during the call.
indicators: Phone call closely timed with a phishing email to the same target
Caller referencing specific content from the phishing email
vectors: Email phishing link paired with a live call pressuring the target to complete the action while on the phone
rootCauses: No unified reporting channel prompting staff to flag when a call and email are linked
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Email gateway filtering
Security awareness training on verifying unsolicited calls tied to an email
ITID-11913.detection: Email gateway logs provide signal on the email component; the voice component has no automated technical signal and relies on user reporting.
ITID-11913.response: Treat as a single coordinated incident; force credential/MFA reset if any code was disclosed during the call.
metrics: Count of confirmed email+voice coordinated campaigns per quarter
ITID-11913.notes: Defining criterion is the email+live-call pairing specifically, which is the highest-severity Multi-Channel Phishing combination given the real-time social-engineering pressure a live call adds.

playbook.name: Response: Email + Voice Call Coordinated Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing campaign combining a phishing email with a live or vished follow-up phone call (often impersonating IT support or a bank) to increase pressure and legitimacy.

steps.title: Preserve the email and capture call details
steps.desc: Preserve the email with headers and record all available call details — caller ID shown, claimed identity/organization, and what was said/requested.
steps.guidance: Interview the target promptly while call details are fresh; caller ID is often spoofed so treat it as an indicator, not proof of origin.
steps.outcome: Email preserved and call details documented.

steps.title: Terminate any remote-access session and isolate the host
steps.desc: If remote-access software was installed or a session granted, immediately terminate it and network-isolate the host.
steps.outcome: Remote session terminated; host isolated.

steps.title: Remove any remote-access tool and check for further payload
steps.desc: Uninstall any remote-access software installed during the call and scan the host for additional malware dropped during the session.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed free of remote-access tools and malware.

steps.title: Restore host and account access
steps.desc: Release network containment once the host is confirmed clean and restore account access with re-enrolled MFA.
steps.outcome: Host and account restored to normal, verified-clean operation.

steps.title: Document the vishing script and brief staff on IT-support verification
steps.desc: Record the pretext and script used on the call, and reinforce that IT support never asks for passwords/OTPs by phone and that staff should call back on a known internal number to verify.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued with the specific pretext used.

steps.title: Determine what information or access was given during the call
steps.desc: Establish exactly what the target disclosed or did during the call — password, OTP, remote access grant, or gift card/payment action.
steps.guidance: Vished calls following an email lure frequently pressure the target to install remote-access software — specifically ask about this.
steps.outcome: Confirmed record of what was disclosed or granted.
steps.abort: If nothing was disclosed and no remote access granted, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke active sessions for any account discussed or accessed during the call.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

ITID-11914.def: An attacker initiates contact via a social media platform (a connection request, DM, or comment) and follows up with a phishing email to the same target, using the social media contact to establish apparent legitimacy before the email lure.
ITID-11914.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign that pairs a social media contact (message, comment, or connection request) with a follow-up email to the same target.
scopeIncludes: A LinkedIn/social media connection or message followed by a phishing email referencing that contact
Social media profile research used to craft a highly targeted follow-up phishing email
scopeExcludes: A standalone direct-messaging scam confined entirely to the social media platform (see the Direct Messaging Scams Type, e.g., ITID-11721 through ITID-11729)
Multi-platform social media coordination with no email component (see ITID-11917)
ITID-11914.severity: Medium-High — social media pre-contact adds a credibility layer that increases the effectiveness of the subsequent email.
ITID-11914.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were disclosed.
ITID-11914.escalation: Escalate to SOC for correlated analysis once both the social contact and the email are confirmed linked.
indicators: Recent unsolicited social media connection/message followed shortly by a themed phishing email
Email referencing details only obtainable from the target's social media profile
vectors: Fake recruiter or business connection request used to warm up the target before an email phishing attempt
rootCauses: Oversharing of professional details on social media enabling highly tailored follow-up phishing
controls: Email gateway filtering
Security awareness training on cross-platform pretext consistency
ITID-11914.detection: Email gateway logs provide signal on the email component; the social media contact has no automated technical signal absent platform-level reporting.
ITID-11914.response: Treat as a single coordinated incident and review what profile information may have informed the pretext.
metrics: Count of confirmed social-media+email coordinated campaigns per quarter
ITID-11914.notes: Defining criterion is the social-media-to-email channel bridge; an attack confined entirely to the social platform belongs under Direct Messaging Scams instead.

playbook.name: Response: Social Media + Email Coordinated Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing campaign that begins with contact via a social media platform (DM, connection request, comment) and pivots to email to deliver the malicious link or attachment.

steps.title: Preserve the social media interaction and follow-up email
steps.desc: Screenshot/export the social media profile, message thread, and connection details, and preserve the follow-up email with headers.
steps.guidance: Note the social profile's creation date, connection count, and mutual connections — freshly created profiles with few connections are a strong indicator.
steps.outcome: Both the social interaction and email preserved with metadata.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if information was disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for any account whose credentials may have been disclosed.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has full, confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the social-to-email pivot pattern
steps.desc: Record how the social media contact built trust before pivoting to email, and add this as a specific example in awareness training.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness training updated.

steps.title: Determine what action the target took
steps.desc: Confirm whether the target clicked the email link, replied with information, or connected further with the fake profile.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Report and block the fake social profile, block the email sender
steps.desc: Report the fake profile to the social platform's trust and safety team and block the email sender/domain.
steps.outcome: Fake profile reported; email sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11915.def: An attacker embeds a QR code in one channel (a printed flyer, a screen during a video call, a physical notice) specifically to move the target from that channel onto their mobile device, where the actual phishing page or app-install prompt is delivered — with the channel bridge itself, not the destination content, being the differentiating feature.
ITID-11915.purpose: Captures a phishing attack that uses a QR code specifically as a deliberate bridge from one channel (print, physical signage, a screen) into another (mobile device/app), as the defining cross-channel mechanism.
scopeIncludes: A QR code deliberately used to move a target from a non-digital or different-device channel onto their mobile device as a distinct hop in a broader campaign
QR codes combined with another channel's messaging (e.g., an email referencing a QR code to scan for 'security verification')
scopeExcludes: A QR code embedded directly in a phishing email with no separate cross-channel bridge (see ITID-11115, QR Code Phishing (Quishing), and ITID-11129, QR Code Spear Phishing)
A QR code sent within a direct message on a social/messaging platform (see ITID-11729, QR Code/Link-in-DM Malware or Credential Scam)
ITID-11915.severity: Medium-High — moving the target to a mobile device often bypasses corporate email/web filtering entirely.
ITID-11915.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials or an app install resulted.
ITID-11915.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately given the likelihood of bypassing corporate network-layer controls on the mobile device.
indicators: QR code present in a non-email physical or screen-shared channel with no other means of following the link
Mobile device landing page requesting corporate SSO credentials
vectors: Fake QR code sticker placed over a legitimate one on physical signage
QR code displayed during a video call urging attendees to 'scan for the agenda/materials'
rootCauses: Corporate email/web filtering has no visibility into a URL only reached by scanning a QR code with a personal mobile device
Lack of awareness that a QR code can silently redirect to an entirely different device/network context
controls: Mobile device management (MDM) URL filtering
Security awareness training on verifying QR codes before scanning
ITID-11915.detection: Limited; corporate network/email filtering has no visibility once the target scans with a personal or off-network mobile device. MDM-enforced URL filtering provides partial coverage on managed devices.
ITID-11915.response: Document the physical/display location of the QR code, remove it, and force credential reset if a corporate login was entered on the destination page.
metrics: Count of confirmed QR cross-channel bridge phishing incidents per quarter
ITID-11915.notes: Scope decision: this ITID is reserved specifically for a QR code used to bridge between two distinct channels/devices as part of a broader hybrid campaign; a QR code embedded directly and solely within an email is ITID-11115/ITID-11129, and one sent within a DM is ITID-11729 — kept separate to avoid triple-counting the same QR-phishing pattern across three branches.

playbook.name: Response: QR Code Cross-Channel Bridge Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing attack where a QR code delivered on one channel (physical poster/flyer, email, printed document) bridges the victim to a mobile device for the actual credential harvest, deliberately evading mail/endpoint scanning.

steps.title: Locate and preserve the QR code source
steps.desc: Identify where the QR code was encountered (physical location, email, document) and preserve or photograph it along with surrounding context.
steps.guidance: QR bridging is specifically designed to move the victim from a monitored corporate device/network onto an unmonitored personal mobile device — note whether a personal or corporate phone was used to scan.
steps.outcome: QR code source and scanning device documented.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for any account whose credentials were entered.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check the mobile device and account for compromise indicators
steps.desc: If a corporate-managed mobile device was used, check MDM/EDR-for-mobile telemetry for any app installed or profile pushed via the QR flow; check the account for persistence.
steps.outcome: Confirmed device and account compromise status.
steps.tool: MDM console / Identity provider audit log

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has full, confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document and brief staff on QR-code risk and physical-space sweeps
steps.desc: Record the QR bridging technique and coordinate a facilities sweep for similar codes in common areas; add QR-specific guidance to awareness training.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; facilities sweep completed; training updated.

steps.title: Decode the QR code and determine the destination and action taken
steps.desc: Decode the QR code (in a sandboxed/isolated manner, not on a personal device) to identify the destination URL, and confirm what the target did after landing (credentials entered, app installed, payment made).
steps.outcome: Destination URL identified and target action confirmed.
steps.abort: If the code was never scanned or no destination reached, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Remove/cover physical QR codes and block the destination domain
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities to physically remove or cover any malicious QR posters/flyers, and block the destination domain at the network/DNS level.
steps.outcome: Physical QR codes removed; destination domain blocked.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed malicious app/profile or account persistence
steps.desc: Remove any malicious mobile app/configuration profile and any attacker-added account persistence found.
steps.outcome: Device and account confirmed clean.

ITID-11916.def: An attacker leaves a voicemail (often via a spoofed number, sometimes AI-generated) referencing an urgent matter and directing the target to check an email that follows, using the voicemail to prime the target to trust and act on the email.
ITID-11916.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign that pairs a fraudulent voicemail with a follow-up phishing email to the same target.
scopeIncludes: Voicemail directing the target to a follow-up phishing email
AI-generated or robocall voicemail referencing the same pretext as a subsequent email
scopeExcludes: Email + live voice call coordination (see ITID-11913)
A standalone voicemail scam with no follow-up email (tracked under the relevant vishing ITID)
ITID-11916.severity: Medium-High — a voicemail adds a sense of legitimacy and urgency ahead of the email lure.
ITID-11916.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were disclosed via the email link.
ITID-11916.escalation: Escalate to SOC for correlated analysis once both the voicemail and the email are confirmed linked.
indicators: Voicemail referencing an email the target should expect
Voicemail and email received within a short time window on the same theme
vectors: Robocall/voicemail campaign paired with a bulk phishing email blast
rootCauses: Voicemail systems lack the filtering rigor applied to email, allowing this priming step to go unchecked
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Email gateway filtering
Security awareness training on voicemail-primed phishing
ITID-11916.detection: Email gateway logs provide signal on the email component; the voicemail component has no automated technical signal and relies on user reporting.
ITID-11916.response: Treat as a single coordinated incident and preserve the voicemail recording for analysis where possible.
metrics: Count of confirmed voicemail+email coordinated campaigns per quarter
ITID-11916.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11913 by the voicemail (asynchronous, pre-recorded) channel rather than a live, interactive phone call.

playbook.name: Response: Voicemail + Email Coordinated Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing campaign combining a fake or spoofed voicemail (often referencing an urgent matter) with a follow-up email delivering the malicious link or attachment.

steps.title: Preserve the voicemail recording and follow-up email
steps.desc: Save the voicemail audio file and preserve the email with headers.
steps.guidance: Note whether the voicemail sounds synthetic/AI-generated — flag for deepfake voice analysis if the pretext involved impersonating a known individual.
steps.outcome: Voicemail and email preserved.
