steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for any account potentially compromised.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has full, confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the voicemail pretext and impersonation method
steps.desc: Record the pretext used and whether voice impersonation/spoofing was involved, feeding this into awareness training and, if deepfake voice is suspected, into executive-protection guidance.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness training updated.

steps.title: Determine what action the target took
steps.desc: Confirm whether the target clicked the email link, called back a number referenced in the voicemail, or disclosed information.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the email sender and flag the calling number
steps.desc: Block the email sender/domain and flag the originating phone number with telecom/PBX admin for blocking where possible.
steps.outcome: Email sender blocked; calling number flagged.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11917.def: An attacker contacts the same target through more than one social media platform (e.g., a LinkedIn message and an Instagram DM referencing each other, or a coordinated cross-platform impersonation), reinforcing the same pretext across platforms without involving email, SMS, or voice.
ITID-11917.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign coordinated across multiple distinct social media platforms against the same target, with no separate email/SMS/voice component.
scopeIncludes: The same fake persona or campaign contacting a target across two or more distinct social media platforms
Cross-platform reinforcement of the same phishing pretext (e.g., a fake brand account on both Instagram and Facebook contacting the same target)
scopeExcludes: Social media + email coordinated phishing (see ITID-11914)
A campaign confined to a single social media platform (tracked under Direct Messaging Scams or Fake Profiles)
ITID-11917.severity: Medium — cross-platform repetition of the same pretext increases perceived legitimacy relative to a single-platform contact.
ITID-11917.escalation: Escalate to the social media/brand-protection team to request coordinated takedown across all platforms involved.
indicators: Matching persona/branding contacting the same target across multiple platforms
Coordinated timing of messages across platforms
vectors: Sock puppet accounts operated across multiple platforms with consistent branding/persona
rootCauses: No cross-platform brand-impersonation monitoring in place
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Cross-platform brand/impersonation monitoring
Security awareness training
ITID-11917.detection: Relies mainly on user reporting and periodic brand-monitoring sweeps across platforms; individual platforms rarely correlate with each other automatically.
ITID-11917.response: Report each impersonating account to its respective platform and request coordinated takedown.
metrics: Count of confirmed multi-platform coordinated campaigns per quarter
ITID-11917.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11914 by remaining entirely within social media platforms with no email component; requires at least two distinct platforms to qualify.

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Platform Social Media Coordinated Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing/scam campaign coordinated across multiple social media platforms simultaneously (e.g. LinkedIn connection plus Instagram DM plus X mention) to increase apparent legitimacy and reach.

steps.title: Map all social platforms and profiles involved
steps.desc: Identify every platform and fake/compromised profile involved in the campaign, and preserve screenshots of each interaction.
steps.guidance: Check whether the same imagery, bio text, or writing style appears across platforms — confirms a coordinated single-actor campaign versus coincidental separate contacts.
steps.outcome: Full list of platforms and profiles documented with evidence.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for any account potentially compromised.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review any compromised corporate account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access and monitor for platform takedown confirmation
steps.desc: Restore any account access affected and confirm each reported fake profile is removed or track outstanding takedown requests.
steps.outcome: Access restored; takedown status tracked to completion.

steps.title: Document the coordinated multi-platform pattern
steps.desc: Record how the platforms reinforced each other's credibility, and add this pattern to awareness training and executive/high-profile staff guidance.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness training updated.

steps.title: Determine what action the target took
steps.desc: Confirm whether the target engaged (replied, clicked a link, disclosed information, sent funds) on any platform.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no engagement occurred, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Report and block every fake profile across all platforms
steps.desc: Report each identified fake/malicious profile to its respective platform's trust and safety team.
steps.outcome: All identified profiles reported for takedown.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11918.def: An attacker begins contact on one channel and, upon detecting resistance, filtering, or suspicion, deliberately switches to a different channel to continue the same pretext — the escalation/evasion behavior itself, rather than a fixed channel pairing, is the defining feature.
ITID-11918.purpose: Captures a phishing technique where the attacker deliberately switches communication channels mid-campaign specifically to evade detection or filtering on the original channel.
scopeIncludes: An attacker moving a conversation from a monitored/filtered channel (e.g., corporate email) to an unmonitored one (e.g., personal messaging app) upon suspicion of detection
A phishing attempt that explicitly instructs the target to 'continue this conversation on [another channel]' after initial contact
scopeExcludes: A fixed, pre-planned two-channel combination with no evasion-driven switch (see ITID-11912 through ITID-11916)
Cross-channel impersonation consistency attacks with no deliberate evasion motive (see ITID-11919)
ITID-11918.severity: High — the deliberate move to an unmonitored channel is itself a strong indicator of intentional evasion and sustained attacker engagement.
ITID-11918.priority: P1 once an evasion-driven channel switch is confirmed.
ITID-11918.escalation: Escalate to SOC immediately; the channel switch itself indicates the attacker is actively adapting to defenses.
indicators: Explicit request to move the conversation to a different platform or channel
Abandonment of a channel immediately after a filtering/blocking action, followed by contact via a new channel
vectors: Request to continue a support/business conversation over a personal messaging app instead of corporate email
Switch from email to SMS/voice after an email is quarantined or flagged
rootCauses: Monitoring/filtering exists on primary corporate channels but not on personal messaging apps used for work purposes
No policy prohibiting business conversations from moving to unmonitored personal channels
controls: Policy prohibiting business communications on unmonitored personal messaging apps
Security awareness training on channel-switch requests as a red flag
ITID-11918.detection: Limited once the attacker reaches an unmonitored personal channel; the initial-channel activity that preceded the switch may be visible in corporate logs.
ITID-11918.response: Treat any request to switch to an unmonitored channel as a red flag requiring verification before continuing the interaction.
metrics: Count of confirmed evasion-driven channel-switch incidents per quarter
ITID-11918.notes: Distinguishing axis is the deliberate, detection-driven motive behind the channel switch, not simply the use of multiple channels (which is common to the whole Multi-Channel Phishing Type).

playbook.name: Response: Escalating Channel-Switch Phishing
playbook.description: For a phishing attack that deliberately escalates through increasingly urgent/personal channels (e.g. email ignored, then SMS, then a phone call) to overcome target hesitation and manufacture urgency.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full escalation timeline
steps.desc: Interview the target and pull logs to build a timeline of each channel used, in order, with the escalating urgency/pressure tactics used at each step.
steps.guidance: The escalation pattern itself (channel switching specifically because earlier attempts were ignored) is a strong indicator of a deliberate, monitored campaign rather than automated mass phishing — treat with elevated priority.
steps.outcome: Complete chronological channel-escalation timeline documented.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions if disclosed
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke sessions for any account potentially compromised.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Check for account persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has full, confirmed-clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the escalation pattern and assess for targeted intent
steps.desc: Record the full escalation pattern and assess whether the level of persistence indicates the target was deliberately/individually selected, feeding into a targeted-threat assessment if so.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted-threat assessment triggered if warranted.

steps.title: Determine the point at which the target acted
steps.desc: Identify exactly which channel/step in the escalation caused the target to comply, and what was disclosed or done.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compliance point and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If the target never complied at any escalation step, downgrade to a near-miss and document the resistance as a positive finding.

steps.title: Block attacker infrastructure across all channels used
steps.desc: Block the email sender/domain, phone number, and any other channel identifiers used throughout the escalation.
steps.outcome: All identified attacker channels blocked.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11919.def: An attacker builds and maintains a consistent fake identity or persona (name, title, photo, backstory) across multiple channels (email signature, LinkedIn profile, voicemail greeting) so that a target who cross-checks the story across channels finds it corroborated, reinforcing trust rather than raising suspicion.
ITID-11919.purpose: Captures a phishing campaign where the attacker deliberately maintains a consistent fabricated identity/persona across multiple channels to make cross-checking the impersonation appear to confirm legitimacy.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated persona with matching details deliberately maintained across email, a social media profile, and/or a voicemail greeting to survive target verification attempts
Attacks specifically designed to defeat a target's instinct to 'verify by checking another channel'
scopeExcludes: A fixed two-channel delivery combination with no persona-consistency engineering (see ITID-11912 through ITID-11916)
Deliberate evasion-driven channel switching with no persona-consistency motive (see ITID-11918)
ITID-11919.severity: High — this technique is specifically engineered to defeat the standard verification advice of checking another channel, making it more effective against trained/aware targets.
ITID-11919.priority: P1 given the sophistication and specific intent to defeat standard verification practices.
ITID-11919.escalation: Escalate to SOC and brand-protection immediately; the existence of a consistent cross-channel persona suggests a well-resourced, planned campaign.
indicators: A fabricated persona's details (name, title, photo) matching consistently across multiple independently checked channels
A target reporting that they 'verified' the contact via another channel before falling for the pretext
vectors: Fake executive persona with a matching LinkedIn profile, email signature, and voicemail greeting built in advance of an attack
Sock puppet profile network reinforcing a single fabricated identity across platforms
rootCauses: Verification guidance tells staff to 'check another channel' without specifying independent, out-of-band verification (e.g., a known phone number, not one found via the same suspicious contact)
No centralized directory of verified executive contact details for staff to cross-check against
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Published, centrally verified directory of executive contact details for out-of-band verification
Security awareness training emphasizing independently-sourced verification, not attacker-provided channels
ITID-11919.detection: Relies heavily on brand-monitoring and user reporting; the persona-consistency itself is not something automated tooling readily detects.
ITID-11919.response: Treat any persona verified only through attacker-provided channels as unverified; require confirmation via an independently sourced contact method.
metrics: Count of confirmed persona-consistency cross-channel attacks per quarter
ITID-11919.notes: Distinguishing axis is the deliberate engineering of a consistent, verification-resistant persona across channels, which is a materially more sophisticated technique than simply using multiple channels for delivery.

playbook.name: Response: Cross-Channel Impersonation Consistency Attack
playbook.description: For a phishing attack where the attacker maintains a single consistent impersonated identity (name, role, photo, writing style) across multiple channels simultaneously to make the impersonation more convincing and harder to disprove on any one channel alone.

steps.title: Document the impersonated identity and every channel it appeared on
steps.desc: Record exactly who/what was impersonated (a real employee, executive, vendor contact) and collect evidence of the impersonation from every channel it appeared on.
steps.guidance: Verify the impersonation against the real individual/organization through a known-good channel — do not assume any single channel's version is more authoritative.
steps.outcome: Impersonated identity confirmed and full cross-channel evidence collected.

steps.title: Contain any compromised account and halt any in-progress transaction
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions for any compromised account, and if a financial transaction was initiated based on the impersonation, immediately contact finance/bank to attempt a hold or recall.
steps.guidance: Time is critical for financial recall requests — escalate to finance leadership immediately, do not wait for full investigation.
steps.outcome: Account secured; transaction hold/recall initiated if applicable.

steps.title: Check for account persistence and notify the impersonated individual
steps.desc: Review any compromised account for persistence, and notify the real impersonated individual/organization so they are aware their identity is being used maliciously.
steps.outcome: Persistence status confirmed; impersonated party notified.

steps.title: Restore access and confirm financial recovery status
steps.desc: Restore account access with re-enrolled MFA and follow up on any financial recall/hold to confirm final recovery status.
steps.outcome: Access restored; financial recovery status documented.

steps.title: Document the impersonation technique and recommend an out-of-band verification control
steps.desc: Record how the consistent cross-channel impersonation was constructed and recommend a specific out-of-band verification step (e.g. callback verification for financial/data requests) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete control recommendation delivered.

steps.title: Determine what action the target took across channels
steps.desc: Establish whether the target acted on the impersonation on any channel — money transfer, credential disclosure, data sharing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If no action taken, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Report and block the impersonating identity across every channel
steps.desc: Block/report the impersonating email address, phone number, and social profiles on every channel identified.
steps.outcome: Impersonating identity blocked/reported across all channels.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-11921.def: An attack deliberately combining a digital social-engineering component with a physical-world component against the same target or facility, without enough detail captured to classify the specific combination or sequencing.
ITID-11921.purpose: Catch-all for a hybrid cyber-physical social engineering attack that does not fit a more specific leaf under Cyber-Physical Social Engineering.
scopeIncludes: Cyber-physical attack reports logged before the specific digital/physical combination is confirmed
scopeExcludes: A purely physical attack with no digital component (tracked under Attacks Against Physical Security, e.g., ITID-11811 tailgating, ITID-14723/ITID-14724 physical reconnaissance)
A purely digital attack with no physical-world component (tracked under the relevant Phishing/Pretexting/Vishing ITID)
Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the combination is known
ITID-11921.severity: Medium-High by default, since a confirmed cyber-physical combination indicates a more resourced, targeted attack than either domain alone.
ITID-11921.escalation: Escalate to both SOC and physical security jointly once the digital and physical components are confirmed linked.
indicators: A digital contact (email, call, social media) and a physical-world event (facility visit, mailed item, in-person encounter) linked to the same target or pretext
vectors: Digital and physical components combined in an unconfirmed sequence
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
Physical security and SOC teams do not routinely correlate incidents with each other
controls: Joint physical security / SOC incident correlation process
ITID-11921.detection: Requires manual cross-team correlation between physical security logs (badge access, CCTV) and digital security logs (email, SSO); no single tool covers both.
ITID-11921.response: Document both components, notify both physical security and SOC, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count of cyber-physical attack reports pending reclassification
ITID-11921.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. The defining criterion for the whole Cyber-Physical Social Engineering Type is a confirmed, deliberate combination of digital and physical-world components; either alone belongs in a different branch of the taxonomy (Phishing/Pretexting/Vishing for pure digital, or Attacks Against Physical Security for pure physical).

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Cyber-Physical Social Engineering Attack
playbook.description: For an attack combining digital and physical social-engineering elements whose specific mechanism has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Establish the digital and physical elements involved
steps.desc: Interview the reporting party and reconstruct which parts of the attack occurred digitally and which occurred physically, and how they connected.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with both the SOC and physical security team from the outset — cyber-physical incidents are frequently mishandled when only one team is engaged.
steps.outcome: Full picture of digital and physical components documented.

steps.title: Contain the digital access vector
steps.desc: Reset credentials, revoke sessions, or isolate any host/account implicated.
steps.outcome: Digital vector contained.

steps.title: Check for persistence across both domains
steps.desc: Review digital systems for attacker persistence and physical areas for tampering (planted devices, altered access points).
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence in both domains.

steps.title: Restore normal digital and physical operations
steps.desc: Release containment and restore access once both domains are verified clean.
steps.outcome: Full operations restored.

steps.title: Document the cross-domain attack chain
steps.desc: Record how the digital and physical elements connected and recommend a joint cyber-physical control improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendation delivered to both security teams.

steps.title: Determine current exposure/compromise state
steps.desc: Establish what access, information, or physical area was actually compromised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of compromise.
steps.abort: If no access or information was actually obtained, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Contain the physical access vector
steps.desc: Coordinate with physical security to revoke badge access, change locks/codes, or increase monitoring of the affected physical area.
steps.outcome: Physical vector contained.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence or tampering
steps.desc: Remediate any digital persistence found and remove/replace any tampered physical equipment or access mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Both domains confirmed clean.

ITID-11922.def: An attacker uses digital means — social media reconnaissance, phishing for a badge photo or org chart, or a fake digital communication establishing a pretext — specifically to gather information or credentials used to carry out a later physical intrusion into a facility.
ITID-11922.purpose: Captures the case where digital reconnaissance or social engineering is used specifically to enable a subsequent physical intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Social media/OSINT reconnaissance of employee schedules, badge designs, or facility layouts later used to plan a physical intrusion
A phishing email harvesting a photo or document later used to fabricate a physical credential (e.g., a badge)
scopeExcludes: Purely digital reconnaissance with no confirmed follow-on physical intrusion attempt (tracked under the Reconnaissance ITIDs, e.g., ITID-52531/ITID-52532)
Physical access enabling a subsequent digital compromise, the reverse sequencing (see ITID-11923)
ITID-11922.severity: High — this represents deliberate premeditation and planning toward physical facility compromise.
ITID-11922.priority: P1 given the elevated risk of an imminent or realized physical intrusion.
ITID-11922.escalation: Escalate jointly to physical security and SOC immediately upon confirming digital reconnaissance was directed at facility intrusion planning.
indicators: Digital reconnaissance activity later corroborated by a physical intrusion attempt or fabricated credential
Phishing lure specifically requesting a badge photo, floor plan, or shift schedule
vectors: Fake HR/badge-reissue phishing email harvesting a photo used for a fabricated badge
Social media scraping of employee check-ins/photos revealing facility layout or badge design
rootCauses: Badge designs and facility layouts overexposed via employee social media posts
No policy restricting sharing of badge photos or facility interior images publicly
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Policy restricting employee sharing of badge/facility images
Physical badge design periodically refreshed to reduce cloning risk
ITID-11922.detection: Requires correlating a confirmed digital reconnaissance/phishing event with a subsequent physical security event (badge anomaly, unauthorized entry attempt) — a real but cross-team detection surface.
ITID-11922.response: Investigate the digital source of any information used in the physical intrusion; refresh compromised badge designs/credentials.
metrics: Count of confirmed digital-recon-to-physical-intrusion incidents per quarter
detections: Access-control/CCTV review correlated with digital reconnaissance findings
ITID-11922.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11923 by sequencing: digital reconnaissance/compromise occurring first, physical intrusion as the follow-on objective.

playbook.name: Response: Digital Recon Enabling Physical Intrusion
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary used digital reconnaissance (social media, org charts, leaked schedules, job postings) to enable a subsequent physical intrusion, such as impersonating an employee or contractor to gain building access.

steps.title: Identify the digital reconnaissance sources used
steps.desc: Determine what publicly or internally available information (org chart, employee photos, badge design, schedules, job postings revealing internal tools) the intruder appeared to leverage.
steps.guidance: Review the intruder's cover story/pretext for specificity — details that match real internal information indicate genuine reconnaissance rather than a generic attempt.
steps.outcome: Reconnaissance sources identified and documented.

steps.title: Revoke any access/credentials the intruder obtained
steps.desc: Revoke any visitor badge, temporary credential, or physical key issued to the intruder, and change any door/cabinet codes they may have observed.
steps.outcome: All obtained physical access revoked or invalidated.

steps.title: Sweep the accessed area for planted devices
steps.desc: Physically inspect any area the intruder accessed for planted network implants, rogue access points, or recording devices.
steps.outcome: Area confirmed clear or planted devices identified and removed.

steps.title: Restore normal access controls with improved verification
steps.desc: Reinstate normal facility access with an interim tightened visitor-verification step (e.g. mandatory sponsor confirmation call) until the root cause is addressed.
steps.outcome: Facility access restored with interim tightened control in place.

steps.title: Document the reconnaissance-to-intrusion chain and reduce public exposure
steps.desc: Record what publicly available information enabled the intrusion and recommend reducing exposure (e.g. limiting org-chart/schedule visibility, badge design changes) plus a physical-security process fix.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete exposure-reduction and process recommendations delivered.

steps.title: Establish the extent of physical access obtained
steps.desc: Review badge logs, visitor logs, and CCTV to determine exactly where the intruder went and what they accessed.
steps.outcome: Full physical access path and dwell time documented.

steps.title: Assess and contain digital exposure from the intrusion
steps.desc: Determine whether the intruder accessed any unattended workstation, network jack, or document, and isolate/contain accordingly.
steps.guidance: An intruder who gained physical proximity to a workstation may have plugged in a device or viewed a logged-in session — check EDR for anomalous activity during the intrusion window.
steps.outcome: Any digital exposure from the physical intrusion identified and contained.

steps.title: Remediate any digital compromise found
steps.desc: Remove any malware, unauthorized device, or account persistence identified from the intrusion.
steps.outcome: Digital environment confirmed clean.

ITID-11923.def: An attacker gains physical access to a facility (via tailgating, a fabricated visitor pretext, or an unlocked area) specifically in order to carry out a digital compromise — plugging into a network jack, accessing an unlocked workstation, or installing a rogue device — that would be harder to achieve remotely.
ITID-11923.purpose: Captures the case where an attacker gains physical access to a facility specifically to enable a subsequent digital compromise.
scopeIncludes: Physical facility access used to plug a rogue device into an internal network jack
An unattended, unlocked workstation accessed in person to install malware or exfiltrate data
scopeExcludes: Digital reconnaissance enabling a physical intrusion, the reverse sequencing (see ITID-11922)
A purely physical intrusion with no digital follow-on objective (tracked under Attacks Against Physical Security)
ITID-11923.severity: High — physical network access typically bypasses perimeter digital defenses entirely.
ITID-11923.priority: P1 given the likelihood of bypassing external network security controls.
ITID-11923.escalation: Escalate jointly to physical security and SOC immediately; treat the internal network as potentially compromised pending investigation.
indicators: Unrecognized device or MAC address appearing on the internal network shortly after a physical access anomaly
An unlocked/unattended workstation found to have been accessed by an unrecognized individual
vectors: Tailgating into a facility to plug a rogue device into an internal network jack
Fabricated vendor/contractor visit pretext used to gain unsupervised access to a workstation
rootCauses: Unused network jacks not disabled/port-secured
Insufficient visitor escort policy enforcement
Workstations not configured to auto-lock promptly when unattended
controls: 802.1X network access control on all jacks
Visitor escort policy enforcement
Workstation auto-lock policy
ITID-11923.detection: Network access control (NAC) and endpoint logs provide a real technical signal — an unrecognized device or unusual login on a workstation is detectable.
ITID-11923.response: Isolate any confirmed rogue device from the network immediately; review access-control/CCTV logs to identify the individual involved.
metrics: Count of confirmed physical-access-to-digital-compromise incidents per quarter
ITID-11923.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11922 by sequencing: physical access occurring first, digital compromise as the follow-on objective.

playbook.name: Response: Physical Access Enabling Digital Compromise
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary who gained physical access (as a visitor, tailgater, or via social engineering of reception/security) then used that access to compromise a digital system — e.g. plugging into a network port, accessing an unlocked workstation, or planting a rogue device.

steps.title: Establish how physical access was obtained and where the intruder went
steps.desc: Review badge/visitor logs and CCTV to reconstruct how the individual gained entry and their movement through the facility.
steps.outcome: Entry method and movement path documented.

steps.title: Isolate the affected system(s) and disable the used network port
steps.desc: Network-isolate any workstation accessed and disable the physical network port used, pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Affected system(s) isolated; network port disabled.

steps.title: Inspect for planted hardware and unauthorized software
steps.desc: Physically inspect the affected area/workstation for planted implants (rogue USB device, network tap) and scan the system for unauthorized software.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of planted hardware/software.

steps.title: Restore the system and re-enable the network port with monitoring
steps.desc: Release containment on the cleaned system and re-enable the network port with enhanced NAC monitoring.
steps.outcome: System and port restored with monitoring in place.

steps.title: Document and recommend physical access control hardening
steps.desc: Record how physical access translated into digital compromise and recommend controls such as 802.1X port authentication, workstation auto-lock enforcement, and visitor-escort policy tightening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete hardening recommendations delivered to facilities and IT.

steps.title: Identify what digital system(s) were touched
steps.desc: Determine which workstation, network port, or device the individual interacted with, using EDR telemetry and network access logs correlated to the intrusion timeframe.
steps.guidance: Check network access control (NAC) logs for any new/unrecognized device connecting to a wired port during the intrusion window.
steps.outcome: Specific system(s) touched identified.

steps.title: Revoke the intruder's physical access credentials
steps.desc: Deactivate any visitor badge or temporary credential used and flag the individual's identity (if known) to physical security.
steps.outcome: Physical access credential revoked.

steps.title: Remove any planted device or malware and reimage if needed
steps.desc: Remove any confirmed rogue hardware and reimage the affected workstation if compromise is confirmed.
steps.outcome: System confirmed clean and free of planted hardware.

ITID-11924.def: A fabricated physical letter or package is delivered to the target, directing them to a digital destination (a website, QR code, or phone number) to 'claim', 'verify', or 'track' something, using the physical delivery to lend credibility to the subsequent digital lure.
ITID-11924.purpose: Captures a fake physical mail or package delivery used specifically as the bridge to a digital phishing lure.
scopeIncludes: Fake delivery-notice letters directing the recipient to a phishing website or QR code to 'reschedule' or 'confirm' a delivery
Physical packages containing a note directing the recipient to a digital credential-harvesting or malware destination
scopeExcludes: A mailed USB drop device where the digital component is the device itself, not a separate destination (see ITID-11614, under Baiting Attacks)
A purely digital delivery-notice phishing email/SMS with no physical mail component (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 ITID)
ITID-11924.severity: Medium-High — the physical delivery channel lends significant credibility not achievable through email/SMS alone.
ITID-11924.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials or payment data were disclosed at the digital destination.
ITID-11924.escalation: Escalate to SOC once the digital destination is identified; escalate to mailroom/physical security to flag the delivery pattern.
indicators: Physical mail/package directing the recipient to a digital destination unaffiliated with any known legitimate sender
QR code or shortened URL printed on a physical notice
vectors: Fake courier 'delivery attempt' notice left at a residence or desk directing to a phishing site
Fake official-looking letter with a QR code claiming to require online action
rootCauses: No mailroom screening process flagging physical mail directing recipients to digital destinations
Recipients trusting physical mail more readily than email due to the perceived cost/effort of sending it
controls: Mailroom screening procedure for unsolicited physical mail directing to digital action
Web/URL reputation filtering
ITID-11924.detection: Web filtering can flag the digital destination once identified; the physical delivery itself has no automated technical signal.
ITID-11924.response: Preserve the physical item for analysis, block the digital destination, and force credential reset if data was disclosed.
metrics: Count of confirmed physical-mail-to-digital-lure incidents per quarter
ITID-11924.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11614 (mailed USB drop), where the physical item itself is the malicious payload rather than a bridge directing the recipient to a separate digital destination.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Physical Mail/Package Bridging to Digital Lure
playbook.description: For an attack using a fake physical mail piece or package (e.g. a fake delivery notice, fake invoice, or fake prize notification) that directs the recipient to a digital lure such as a phishing site or QR code.

steps.title: Preserve the physical mail/package and identify the digital bridge
steps.desc: Collect the mail piece/package and identify the specific digital call-to-action it contains (URL, QR code, phone number, email address).
steps.outcome: Physical item preserved and digital bridge mechanism identified.

steps.title: Contain any resulting digital compromise
steps.desc: Reset credentials/revoke sessions if credentials were disclosed, or isolate the host if malware was downloaded.
steps.outcome: Digital exposure contained.

steps.title: Analyze the digital payload if applicable
steps.desc: If malware was downloaded, detonate it in a sandbox to determine family and capability.
steps.outcome: Malware family and capability documented, or confirmed no payload beyond credential harvesting.

steps.title: Restore access/host and monitor
steps.desc: Release containment and monitor the affected host/account for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Restored to normal, verified-clean state; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and coordinate a mailroom screening improvement
steps.desc: Record the mail pretext and digital bridge used, and recommend a mailroom process improvement for flagging suspicious unsolicited mail.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; mailroom recommendation delivered.

steps.title: Determine whether the recipient followed the digital bridge
steps.desc: Confirm whether the recipient visited the URL/scanned the QR code and what happened next (credential entry, payment, malware download).
steps.outcome: Confirmed action taken and resulting exposure.
steps.abort: If the recipient did not follow the bridge, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the digital destination and alert mailroom/facilities
steps.desc: Block the destination URL/domain and alert mailroom/facilities staff to watch for similar mail pieces addressed to other staff.
steps.outcome: Destination blocked; mailroom alerted.

steps.title: Remediate the host or account fully
steps.desc: Remove any malware/persistence found, or complete the credential-rotation and session-revocation cycle.
steps.outcome: Host or account confirmed clean.

ITID-11925.def: An attacker who has established a digital impersonation (fake executive, vendor, or colleague identity) reinforces the pretext by physically showing up in person — at a facility, a meeting, or an event — matching the fabricated identity, to overcome any residual digital-verification skepticism.
ITID-11925.purpose: Captures the case where a digital impersonation attack is reinforced or 'confirmed' by an in-person physical appearance matching the fabricated identity.
scopeIncludes: An impersonator physically attending a facility or meeting in person to corroborate a prior digital impersonation
A fabricated vendor representative appearing in person after prior email/phone contact to complete a scam
scopeExcludes: Video call deepfake combined with a physical follow-up specifically involving synthetic video/audio (see ITID-11926)
Digital impersonation with no physical in-person component (tracked under the relevant Phishing/Vishing/Pretexting ITID)
ITID-11925.severity: High — an in-person appearance is a powerful trust-confirming action that can defeat digital-only verification skepticism.
ITID-11925.priority: P1 given the escalated commitment and sophistication implied by an in-person appearance.
ITID-11925.escalation: Escalate jointly to physical security and SOC immediately upon identifying an in-person appearance tied to a prior digital impersonation.
indicators: An individual physically present matching a previously digitally-established but unverified identity
Facility visit immediately following digital contact establishing a fabricated pretext
vectors: Fake vendor representative visiting in person after prior email contact to finalize a fraudulent transaction
Impersonator attending a scheduled meeting in person after establishing the pretext via email/LinkedIn
rootCauses: Visitor verification process does not cross-check identity against the organization the visitor claims digital affiliation with
Staff placing excessive trust in an in-person appearance as inherent proof of legitimacy
controls: Visitor identity verification against an independently confirmed appointment/vendor record
Physical security badge/visitor management procedure
ITID-11925.detection: Visitor management and CCTV logs provide a real technical signal for reconstructing the in-person appearance; the prior digital impersonation may be visible in email/call logs.
ITID-11925.response: Verify any in-person visitor's claimed affiliation independently before granting access or acting on their requests; review CCTV/visitor logs.
metrics: Count of confirmed digital-impersonation-with-physical-confirmation incidents per quarter
ITID-11925.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11926 by involving a real in-person physical appearance rather than a synthetic video/audio deepfake.

playbook.name: Response: Digital Impersonation Confirmed via Physical Presence
playbook.description: For an attack where a digital impersonation (fake caller, fake email sender) is reinforced or 'confirmed' by an accomplice's physical presence — e.g. a fraudulent caller claiming to be an on-site contractor while a second person physically presents at the facility posing as that contractor.

steps.title: Correlate the digital impersonation with the physical presence
steps.desc: Establish the timeline linking the digital contact (call/email) and the physical individual's appearance, confirming they are coordinated rather than coincidental.
steps.guidance: Check badge/visitor sign-in details against the claimed identity used in the digital contact for inconsistencies.
steps.outcome: Coordinated attack confirmed with full timeline.

steps.title: Revoke any physical access granted and escort the individual off-site if still present
steps.desc: Coordinate with physical security to revoke any granted access and, if the individual is still on-site, have them escorted out.
steps.outcome: Physical access revoked; individual removed from premises if applicable.

steps.title: Check for lingering access or planted items
steps.desc: Inspect any area the individual accessed for planted devices and review systems for any account/persistence changes made under the impersonation's instruction.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of lingering compromise.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with a verification step added
steps.desc: Resume normal operations, adding an interim requirement to verify contractor/vendor identity claims via a known-good callback before granting access or taking action.
steps.outcome: Operations restored with interim verification control in place.

steps.title: Document the coordinated impersonation and brief reception/security staff
steps.desc: Record the full digital-plus-physical impersonation technique and brief reception, security, and helpdesk staff on the specific verification failure that allowed it.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted briefing delivered to front-line staff.

steps.title: Determine what access or action was granted
steps.desc: Establish what the physical individual was granted access to, or what action staff took based on the digital contact's instructions.
steps.outcome: Confirmed access/action taken and its scope.
steps.abort: If access was correctly denied and no digital action was taken, document as a successfully resisted attempt.

steps.title: Contain any digital action taken based on the impersonation
steps.desc: Reverse or halt any digital action taken (e.g. a system change, data release, credential given) based on the caller's instructions.
steps.outcome: Digital action reversed or halted.

steps.title: Remediate any confirmed compromise
steps.desc: Remove any planted devices and reverse any unauthorized account/system change.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean.

ITID-11926.def: An attacker uses AI-generated deepfake video and/or audio to impersonate a known individual on a live video call, and follows up with a real-world physical action (a package delivery, an in-person meeting, a physical document) to reinforce the pretext established during the deepfake call.
ITID-11926.purpose: Captures a video call deepfake impersonation that is deliberately combined with a real-world physical follow-up action.
scopeIncludes: A deepfake video call establishing a pretext followed by a physical delivery, meeting, or document tied to the same scam
Deepfake video call impersonation where a physical action is required to complete the fraud (e.g., a courier pickup)
scopeExcludes: A standalone AI voice clone/deepfake impersonation call with no physical follow-up component (see ITID-11216, under Pretexting/Vishing)
A real in-person appearance with no deepfake/synthetic media component (see ITID-11925)
ITID-11926.severity: High — combining synthetic media with a physical-world action represents a highly sophisticated, well-resourced attack.
ITID-11926.priority: P1 given the sophistication and typically high-value target of this technique.
ITID-11926.escalation: Escalate to SOC, executive protection, and physical security immediately upon suspicion of a deepfake video call combined with any physical-world follow-up.
indicators: Video call artifacts consistent with deepfake generation (lip-sync mismatch, lighting inconsistency, audio latency)
A physical-world action (delivery, meeting, document) requested immediately following the video call
vectors: Deepfake video call impersonating an executive authorizing a transaction, followed by a courier pickup of funds or documents
Deepfake video call setting up a subsequent in-person meeting with an accomplice
rootCauses: No out-of-band verification procedure for high-value requests made on a video call, even when the caller appears visually authentic
Executive video/audio samples publicly available, enabling deepfake generation
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Out-of-band verification procedure for high-value requests regardless of video/audio authenticity
Executive protection awareness of deepfake risk
ITID-11926.detection: Limited automated technical signal for detecting the deepfake itself; the physical-world follow-up action may be visible in visitor/courier/CCTV logs.
ITID-11926.response: Halt any requested action pending independent out-of-band verification; preserve the video call recording for forensic analysis where available.
metrics: Count of confirmed deepfake-plus-physical-follow-up incidents per quarter
ITID-11926.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-11216 (a standalone deepfake vishing/video call with no physical follow-up), which stays under Pretexting; this ITID requires the additional confirmed physical-world component.

playbook.name: Response: Video Call Deepfake Combined with Physical Follow-up
playbook.description: For an attack using an AI-generated deepfake video/voice on a video call (impersonating an executive or trusted individual) followed by a physical follow-up action, such as a courier pickup or in-person meeting request, to complete the deception.

steps.title: Preserve the video call recording and identify deepfake indicators
steps.desc: Preserve any recording of the call and note specific technical anomalies (lip-sync mismatch, lighting inconsistency, unnatural blinking, audio artifacts) suggesting synthetic media.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on visual judgment alone — engage digital forensics or a deepfake-detection tool where available to formally assess the media.
steps.outcome: Call preserved and deepfake likelihood assessed.

steps.title: Halt any in-progress physical or financial handoff
steps.desc: If a courier pickup, cash transfer, or physical handoff is in progress or scheduled, immediately act to intercept or cancel it.
steps.guidance: Escalate to physical security and finance/legal simultaneously — this scenario often has a narrow window to prevent loss.
steps.outcome: Physical/financial handoff halted or intercepted.

steps.title: Trace and preserve the deepfake infrastructure used
steps.desc: Identify and preserve evidence of the video/voice call platform, calling identity, and any digital artifacts used to construct or deliver the deepfake for potential law enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and referral to law enforcement/legal considered.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with an interim executive-verification control
steps.desc: Resume operations, adding an interim requirement for out-of-band verification (a pre-agreed code phrase or callback) for any high-value request purportedly from an executive via video/voice call.
steps.outcome: Interim verification control in place.

steps.title: Document and brief executives and finance on deepfake risk
steps.desc: Record the deepfake technique and physical follow-up used, and brief executives, executive assistants, and finance staff specifically on this attack pattern and the verification control.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; targeted executive/finance briefing delivered.

steps.title: Establish the physical follow-up requested and whether it occurred
steps.desc: Determine what physical action was requested (courier pickup, cash handoff, in-person meeting) following the call, and whether it was carried out.
steps.outcome: Confirmed physical follow-up action and its outcome.
steps.abort: If the target did not act on the call, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Verify the real executive's status and alert them
steps.desc: Contact the actual impersonated executive/individual through a known-good channel to confirm they did not make the call and to alert them to the impersonation.
steps.outcome: Real individual confirmed uninvolved and made aware.

steps.title: Check for any digital system compromise tied to the call
steps.desc: Confirm whether any credentials, remote access, or data were also disclosed/granted during or after the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of digital compromise.

ITID-11927.def: An attacker socially engineers access to or control of a smart building system or IoT device (smart locks, badge readers, HVAC, cameras) — via a fake vendor support call, a phished management-portal credential, or a fake maintenance request — to produce a physical-world effect such as unlocking a door or disabling a camera.
ITID-11927.purpose: Captures social engineering directed at a smart building or IoT device to bridge digital manipulation into a physical-world effect.
scopeIncludes: Social engineering targeting facilities/building-management staff to gain smart-lock or badge-system access
Fake vendor maintenance calls seeking remote access to a building automation or IoT management portal
scopeExcludes: Purely technical exploitation of an IoT device vulnerability with no social-engineering component (tracked under the relevant technical ITID outside this branch)
Kiosk tampering via direct physical USB/peripheral access with no social-engineering pretext (see ITID-21633)
ITID-11927.severity: High — compromising a smart building system can directly enable physical intrusion or safety impact.
ITID-11927.priority: P1 given the potential for immediate physical access control or safety system compromise.
ITID-11927.escalation: Escalate jointly to physical security, facilities, and SOC immediately upon suspicion of smart-building/IoT social engineering.
indicators: Unsolicited contact posing as a building system/IoT vendor requesting portal access or credentials
Unexplained changes to badge/lock system configuration or camera status
vectors: Fake building-automation vendor support call requesting remote portal access
Phishing targeting facilities staff for smart-lock or camera-management system credentials
rootCauses: Facilities/building-management staff not included in standard security awareness training scope
Smart building systems administered with shared or unrotated credentials
controls: Security awareness training extended to facilities/building-management staff
Multi-factor authentication on building-management portals
Vendor callback verification procedure
ITID-11927.detection: Building-management system logs can show configuration changes and access attempts if logging is enabled and reviewed.
ITID-11927.response: Review building-management system logs for unauthorized changes; reset credentials and re-verify physical access-control configuration.
metrics: Count of confirmed smart-building/IoT social engineering incidents per quarter
ITID-11927.notes: Scope decision: requires a social-engineering vector (impersonation, pretext) targeting a human operator of the smart building/IoT system; a purely technical device exploit with no human deception belongs to a different, technical ITID branch.

playbook.name: Response: Smart Building/IoT Device Social Engineering
playbook.description: For an attack that socially engineers access to or manipulation of smart-building/IoT systems (badge readers, smart locks, cameras, building management systems) often by impersonating a vendor technician or facilities staff.

steps.title: Identify the targeted IoT/building system and the pretext used
steps.desc: Determine which system (badge reader, camera, HVAC/BMS, smart lock) was targeted and what pretext (vendor maintenance call, facilities request) was used to gain access.
steps.guidance: Verify any claimed vendor/technician against the actual scheduled maintenance record with facilities.
steps.outcome: Targeted system and pretext documented; legitimacy checked against maintenance records.

steps.title: Revoke any credentials or access given to the impersonator
steps.desc: Revoke any account, badge, or remote access credential provided to the impersonator on the IoT/BMS platform.
steps.outcome: Access revoked.

steps.title: Audit the system for unauthorized configuration or firmware changes
steps.desc: Compare current configuration/firmware against known-good baseline to identify any malicious changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Reconnect the system with monitoring and vendor verification process
steps.desc: Restore normal network connectivity for the system, with monitoring enabled, and implement a vendor-technician verification process for future maintenance requests.
steps.outcome: System restored; verification process in place.

steps.title: Document and recommend IoT/OT security hardening
steps.desc: Record the pretext and technical findings, and recommend hardening (credential rotation policy, network segmentation, vendor verification protocol) to facilities and OT/IT leadership.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; hardening recommendations delivered.

steps.title: Assess what was changed or accessed on the system
steps.desc: Review the building management system/IoT platform's logs for configuration changes, new device enrollments, or access-log tampering during the relevant window.
steps.guidance: IoT/BMS platforms often have weak or default credentials and limited logging — check vendor support logs as well if internal logging is insufficient.
steps.outcome: Confirmed changes or access made to the system.

steps.title: Isolate the affected IoT system from the broader network if compromise is suspected
steps.desc: Segment/isolate the affected building system from the corporate network to prevent lateral movement, coordinating with facilities and IT/OT teams.
steps.outcome: Affected system isolated pending verification.

steps.title: Restore the system to a known-good configuration
steps.desc: Revert any unauthorized changes and reset credentials on the affected IoT/BMS platform.
steps.outcome: System confirmed restored to known-good state.

ITID-11928.def: A fabricated physical sign or notice (e.g., a fake 'Wi-Fi password reset' or 'password expiring, click here' notice posted in a common area) directs employees or visitors to a digital credential-harvesting page or QR code, exploiting the apparent legitimacy of an on-site physical posting.
ITID-11928.purpose: Captures a fake physical sign or notice posted on-site specifically to bridge into a digital credential-harvesting destination.
scopeIncludes: Fake physical notices posted in break rooms, elevators, or near workstations directing to a credential-harvesting URL/QR code
Fake 'IT maintenance' or 'password reset' signage placed on-site
scopeExcludes: Fake physical mail/package delivery bridging to a digital lure (see ITID-11924)
A purely digital credential-harvesting phishing email/page with no physical signage component (tracked under the relevant Phishing tier-4 ITID)
ITID-11928.severity: High — on-site physical signage exploits the assumption that anything posted inside a secured facility is internally sanctioned.
ITID-11928.priority: P1 given the credential-harvesting objective combined with the implied requirement of some physical facility access to post the sign.
ITID-11928.escalation: Escalate jointly to physical security and SOC immediately upon discovering fake signage directing to a digital destination.
indicators: Signage referencing IT/security actions not corresponding to any actual internal communication
QR code or URL on a physical notice not matching known internal domains
vectors: Fake sign posted near an elevator or break room directing staff to 'reset your password' via a QR code
Fake notice placed on desks during an unsupervised facility visit
rootCauses: No process for verifying or removing unauthorized physical signage inside secured areas
Staff conditioned to comply with on-site IT instructions without independent verification
controls: Facility sweep procedure to identify and remove unauthorized signage
Web/URL reputation filtering
Security awareness training on verifying on-site IT communications
ITID-11928.detection: Web filtering can flag the digital destination once identified; the physical signage itself has no automated technical signal and relies on staff/facilities reporting.
ITID-11928.response: Remove the signage, block the digital destination, and force credential reset for any affected accounts.
metrics: Count of confirmed fake-signage-to-digital-harvest incidents per quarter
ITID-11928.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11924 by the on-site physical signage delivery mechanism, which implies the attacker gained some level of facility access to post it, rather than a mailed item sent from outside.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Physical Signage/Notice Bridging to Digital Credential Harvest
playbook.description: For an attack using fake physical signage or a posted notice (e.g. a fake IT notice at a printer or fake Wi-Fi instructions in a lobby) directing employees to a digital credential-harvesting site.

steps.title: Locate, preserve, and remove the fake signage
steps.desc: Photograph and remove the fake signage/notice, noting its exact posted location and any QR code or URL it contained.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with facilities to check nearby areas for additional copies of the same signage.
steps.outcome: Signage documented and removed; other locations checked.

steps.title: Reset credentials for anyone who submitted information
steps.desc: Force password resets and revoke sessions for every account whose credentials were entered on the fake site.
steps.outcome: All exposed accounts secured.

steps.title: Check affected accounts for persistence
steps.desc: Review each exposed account for attacker-added forwarding rules, MFA devices, or OAuth grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence per account.

steps.title: Restore access for all affected accounts
steps.desc: Have each affected user set a new password and re-enroll MFA from a known-clean device.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts restored to confirmed-clean, verified access.

steps.title: Document and issue guidance on verifying physical IT notices
steps.desc: Record the technique and remind staff that legitimate IT notices come through official channels, never unsolicited physical signage directing to external links.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Determine how many employees interacted with the digital destination
steps.desc: Check web proxy/DNS logs for hits to the destination URL and correlate with the timeframe the signage was posted, or interview known viewers.
steps.outcome: List of employees who visited the destination and what they entered.
steps.abort: If proxy logs show no hits, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Block the destination domain and review physical access controls for the posting area
steps.desc: Block the destination at the DNS/web proxy layer and review who had physical access to post signage in the affected area (badge/visitor logs, camera footage).
steps.outcome: Destination blocked; posting-area access reviewed.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any malicious inbox rule, revoke unrecognized OAuth grants, remove unrecognized MFA methods on each affected account.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on any account.

ITID-11929.def: An external attacker actively coordinates with a complicit or coerced insider, combining the insider's legitimate physical facility access with the external attacker's digital capabilities (credentials, malware, exfiltration infrastructure) to achieve a compromise neither could accomplish alone.
ITID-11929.purpose: Captures the most sophisticated Cyber-Physical Social Engineering pattern, where an external attacker actively coordinates with a complicit insider to combine physical and digital access.
scopeIncludes: A recruited or coerced insider granting physical facility/network access on behalf of an external attacker
Coordinated operations where an insider performs a physical action (plugging in a device, unlocking a door) at an external attacker's direction
scopeExcludes: An insider acting entirely alone with no external coordination (tracked under insider threat ITIDs outside this branch)
A purely external cyber-physical attack with no insider complicity (see ITID-11922 or ITID-11923)
ITID-11929.severity: Critical — insider-outsider coordination combines legitimate access with external attacker capability, representing one of the highest-severity social engineering patterns.
ITID-11929.priority: P1, always escalated given the combined insider-access and external-coordination risk.
ITID-11929.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC, physical security, HR, and legal given the insider-threat and potential criminal dimensions.
indicators: An employee's badge/network activity correlating with an otherwise unexplained external compromise
Evidence of external communication (financial payment, messaging) between an employee and an unknown external party preceding a security incident
vectors: An employee recruited via bribery or coercion to plug in a device or disable a control at an external attacker's direction
An insider granting a fabricated 'vendor' unsupervised physical access on behalf of an external attacker
rootCauses: Insider risk monitoring not correlated with physical access anomalies
No behavioral indicators program to flag employees at elevated insider-risk (financial distress, grievance, external contact patterns)
controls: Insider risk/behavioral monitoring program
Segregation of duties limiting any single insider's combined physical/digital access
Joint physical security and SOC incident correlation process
ITID-11929.detection: Requires correlating physical access-control/CCTV logs with digital security logs and, where available, insider-risk behavioral indicators — a genuine but resource-intensive cross-domain detection surface.
ITID-11929.response: Engage HR and legal alongside SOC and physical security; preserve all physical and digital evidence for a coordinated investigation.
metrics: Count of confirmed insider-outsider coordinated incidents per year
detections: Access-control/CCTV review correlated with digital logs
ITID-11929.notes: Scope decision: requires confirmed active coordination between an external attacker and a complicit/coerced insider; an insider acting entirely alone without external direction is out of scope and belongs under a dedicated insider threat ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy.

playbook.name: Response: Coordinated Insider-Outsider Physical-Digital Attack
playbook.description: For an attack involving collusion between an outside attacker and a complicit or coerced insider, combining the insider's legitimate physical/digital access with external attacker capability — the highest-severity cyber-physical scenario.

steps.title: Engage HR/legal and establish the scope discreetly
steps.desc: Immediately loop in HR, Legal, and senior security leadership given the insider-collusion element; begin scoping the insider's access and recent activity without alerting the individual.
steps.guidance: This category requires strict operational security — premature confrontation of a suspected insider can lead to evidence destruction or the individual fleeing/escalating; follow the org's insider-threat investigation protocol exactly.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; investigation scoped discreetly under insider-threat protocol.
steps.abort: If evidence does not support insider collusion after initial review, redirect to the appropriate non-insider incident type and disengage HR/Legal insider-threat track.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access simultaneously across all systems
steps.desc: Coordinate a simultaneous revocation of the insider's badge, network, application, and remote access to prevent tipping them off before all access is cut.
steps.guidance: Time this precisely with HR/Legal's planned action (e.g. suspension meeting) to avoid a window where the insider notices partial revocation and destroys evidence.
steps.outcome: All insider access revoked simultaneously.
steps.tool: Identity provider / Badge access system / EDR console

steps.title: Forensically preserve evidence for potential legal/law-enforcement action
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve all logs and communications before remediation, following chain-of-custody procedures suitable for legal proceedings.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal before any remediation that could destroy evidence needed for prosecution or termination proceedings.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved with documented chain of custody.

steps.title: Restore systems and reissue access under updated controls
steps.desc: Restore affected systems from clean state and reissue any legitimately needed access under refreshed credentials and tightened permissions.
steps.outcome: Systems restored; access reissued under hardened controls.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review with HR, Legal, and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the complete insider-outsider collusion chain, the effectiveness of the response, and recommend specific insider-threat detection and separation-of-duties improvements.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive after-action report delivered to leadership with concrete control recommendations.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full physical and digital access timeline for the insider
steps.desc: Pull badge logs, VPN/access logs, and EDR telemetry for the insider's account and correlate with the external attacker's activity to build a complete timeline.
steps.outcome: Complete correlated timeline of insider and external attacker actions.
steps.tool: Badge access system / SIEM / EDR console

steps.title: Contain the external attacker's infrastructure and any implanted access
steps.desc: Block any external attacker infrastructure identified and isolate any host/account showing signs of attacker-implanted access.
steps.outcome: External attacker access contained.

steps.title: Remove all attacker and insider-planted persistence
steps.desc: Remediate every system touched — remove malware, unauthorized accounts, backdoors, and any access the insider set up for the external party.
steps.outcome: All systems confirmed clean of attacker/insider-planted persistence.

steps.title: Determine full scope of data/system access and exfiltration
steps.desc: Identify everything the insider's access was used to reach, and whether any data was exfiltrated to the external party.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromised systems and any exfiltrated data documented.

ITID-12111.def: A phishing incident in which the victim was presented with a credential-harvesting page or form and is confirmed (via form-submission telemetry, attacker infrastructure logs, victim self-report, or observed anomalous login activity) to have entered valid credentials.
ITID-12111.purpose: Captures confirmed successful phishing-based credential theft where the target actually submitted credentials into an attacker-controlled form, distinguishing outcome-confirmed compromise from mere phishing exposure for severity/priority purposes.
scopeIncludes: Phishing email/link/page where the user is confirmed to have typed and submitted a working username/password
Credential harvesting confirmed via proxy logs, EDR browser telemetry, or attacker-side artifact recovery
User self-reports having entered credentials on a suspicious page
scopeExcludes: Phishing where the user clicked the link but did not submit credentials (see ITID-12112 and the target-specific leaves ITID-12113 to ITID-12119)
MFA/OTP relay or token phishing where the credential itself is a secondary artifact (ITID-12611 series)
Simulated/authorized phishing exercises (ITID-91121 series)
ITID-12111.severity: High - confirmed credential submission materially increases likelihood of account compromise versus mere exposure.
ITID-12111.priority: P1 if the account has elevated privilege or SSO scope; P2 otherwise, always higher than the unconfirmed-submission sibling.
ITID-12111.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/identity team for forced credential reset and session revocation; escalate to SOC for downstream login monitoring.
indicators: Outbound POST to known phishing-kit domain from user's browser session
Attacker panel logs showing captured username/password pair
User help-desk report of having entered credentials before realizing the site was fake
vectors: Credential-harvesting landing page mimicking a login portal
Adversary-in-the-middle phishing proxy (e.g. Evilginx-style kit)
rootCauses: Insufficient user awareness of URL/domain inspection
Lack of phishing-resistant authentication (FIDO2/passkeys)
mitreTechniques: T1598.003 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Link
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Secure email gateway URL rewriting/sandboxing
Forced password reset and session revocation workflow
ITID-12111.detection: Strong technical signal available: secure web gateway/proxy logs show POST requests to known-bad domains, EDR browser telemetry can flag form submission on flagged sites, and IAM correlates the credential event with subsequent anomalous logins (impossible travel, new device, new ASN).
ITID-12111.response: Immediately force password reset, revoke active sessions/tokens, and review authentication logs for the account for the 24-72 hours following submission.
metrics: Time from submission to credential reset
Count of confirmed credential submissions per month
Percentage resulting in confirmed account takeover
detections: Secure web gateway known-bad-domain POST alerting
ITID-12111.notes: This leaf is the confirmed-outcome escalation of the general phished-credential family (ITID-12112 through ITID-12119); it does not duplicate those leaves' target-system scoping and applies across any target-system type once submission is confirmed.

playbook.name: Standard Response: Phishing with Confirmed Credential Submission
playbook.description: Updated: for phishing campaigns where at least one recipient submitted credentials to the attacker-controlled page. Escalate to Incident if executive accounts affected.

steps.title: Confirm sender domain against known-bad indicators
steps.desc: Cross-reference the sending domain against threat intel feeds.
steps.guidance: Check the domain in the threat intel explorer first; if not present, pivot to WHOIS registration date and DNS history.
steps.outcome: Domain is confirmed malicious or benign with supporting evidence attached to the alert.
steps.abort: If the domain resolves to a known legitimate SaaS provider shared by multiple tenants, abort and downgrade to false positive review.

steps.title: Force password reset for every user who submitted credentials
steps.guidance: Use the identity provider's admin console to force reset, not a self-service email.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts require a new password before next login.

steps.title: Search mailbox for and remove any remaining copies of the phishing email
Confirm affected accounts show no further anomalous activity
steps.outcome: 72 hours of clean sign-in and mailbox activity logs.

steps.title: Document root cause and timeline
steps.guidance: Use the standard post-incident report template.
steps.outcome: A complete, reviewable writeup attached to the case.

steps.title: Identify every recipient of the campaign
steps.guidance: Query the mail gateway for all messages sharing the same sender/subject/attachment hash within a 24h window.
steps.outcome: Complete recipient list captured in the case.

steps.title: Revoke active sessions/tokens for affected accounts
steps.outcome: No active sessions remain for affected accounts.

steps.title: Check for and remove any mailbox forwarding rules the attacker may have added
steps.guidance: Attackers with valid creds commonly add a silent forwarding rule to maintain access after password reset.
steps.outcome: No unauthorized forwarding rules remain on any affected mailbox.

steps.title: Re-enable any accounts disabled during containment
Identify a real control gap and file a follow-up action item
steps.desc: Decide whether this was a detection gap, a training gap, or a technical control gap.
steps.guidance: Weigh the evidence gathered during identification/containment before assigning a category.
steps.outcome: A tracked action item exists with an owner and target date.
steps.abort: If no real gap is found (attacker was blocked entirely by existing controls), record that explicitly instead of forcing a finding.

steps.title: Confirm credential submission via proxy/EDR logs
steps.desc: Look for POST requests to the phishing domain from any recipient.
steps.guidance: Search proxy logs for outbound POST to the phishing domain; cross-check EDR for browser process activity at the same timestamp.
steps.outcome: List of accounts with confirmed credential submission, or confirmation that none occurred.
steps.abort: If no recipient clicked the link at all, abort remaining containment/eradication steps and close as contained-at-delivery.

steps.title: Block sender domain and URL at mail gateway and proxy
Escalate to Incident Commander if executive accounts affected
steps.desc: Executive accounts carry disproportionate blast radius.
steps.guidance: Page the on-call Incident Commander directly rather than waiting for the next standup.
steps.outcome: Incident Commander acknowledges and, if warranted, the case is promoted to a formal incident.
steps.abort: If no executive account is among the affected list, skip this step entirely.

ITID-12112.def: A phishing incident involving credential theft where the specific target system (SSO, VPN, cloud admin, email, SaaS, personal, or financial) has not yet been determined or does not fit a more specific sibling leaf.
ITID-12112.purpose: Catch-all for phished-credential incidents that do not yet identify which specific system or account type was targeted.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the targeted credential type is confirmed
Phishing credential theft against a system type not covered by a more specific sibling
scopeExcludes: Any case where the targeted credential type is known and matches ITID-12113 through ITID-12119
Confirmed submission cases better classified under ITID-12111 once outcome is established
ITID-12112.severity: Medium, pending reclassification once the target system is identified.
ITID-12112.escalation: Reclassify to a specific sibling leaf once the targeted system/account type is confirmed.
indicators: User report of a suspicious login page of unclear type
Phishing email flagged by filter with unclear credential target
vectors: Generic credential-harvesting phishing email or link
rootCauses: Insufficient triage detail captured at time of report
controls: Secure email gateway phishing detection
User phishing-report button
ITID-12112.detection: Same secure-email-gateway and proxy telemetry as the specific sibling leaves, pending finer classification of the target system.
ITID-12112.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific target-system leaf once confirmed; treat as potential credential exposure until ruled out.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-12112.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification within the Phished Credentials type, not a terminal one; reclassify as soon as target-system detail is known.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Phished Credential
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected phished-credential incident where the specific credential type/system has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message and identify the target system
steps.desc: Collect the original message and determine which system/account type the harvesting page was impersonating.
steps.outcome: Original message preserved; target system identified for reclassification if a more specific ITID applies.

steps.title: Reset the affected credential and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke active sessions for the affected account.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential invalidated.

steps.title: Check for persistence
steps.desc: Review the account for attacker-added forwarding rules, OAuth grants, or MFA enrollments.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access and monitor
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new credential and place the account under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Access restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and reclassify if applicable
steps.desc: Record findings and reclassify the incident to a specific phished-credential ITID if the target system is now known.
