steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm whether credentials were submitted
steps.desc: Interview the recipient and/or review harvesting-site logs to confirm submission.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status.
steps.abort: If no submission occurred, close as a near-miss/reported phish.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain and harvesting URL org-wide and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

ITID-12113.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for the organization's primary single sign-on or identity provider account (e.g. Okta, Azure AD/Entra ID, Ping, Google Workspace primary identity).
ITID-12113.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of the organization's corporate SSO/identity provider credential, the highest-blast-radius credential-theft target since it grants downstream access to federated applications.
scopeIncludes: Fake SSO/IdP login page phishing
Credential harvesting kit that mimics the corporate identity provider branding
scopeExcludes: Phishing for MFA/OTP codes tied to the SSO login, which is scoped to ITID-12611 series (MFA Token Phishing) not this leaf
Phished VPN-specific credential (ITID-12114)
Phished individual SaaS application credential not tied to SSO (ITID-12117)
ITID-12113.severity: Critical - SSO credential compromise cascades to every federated downstream application.
ITID-12113.priority: P1 always, regardless of confirmed submission status, given blast radius.
ITID-12113.escalation: Immediate escalation to IAM and SOC; treat as organization-wide exposure until scope is bounded.
indicators: Phishing kit domain closely resembling IdP login URL
Anomalous SSO login immediately following a flagged phishing click
vectors: Spoofed IdP login portal delivered via email or SMS
rootCauses: SSO not enforced with phishing-resistant MFA
Users not trained to verify IdP domain before entering credentials
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) on SSO
IdP anomalous-login risk scoring (impossible travel, new device)
ITID-12113.detection: IdP sign-in logs provide strong real-time telemetry: risk-based conditional access, impossible-travel detection, and new-device/new-IP login alerting.
ITID-12113.response: Force immediate SSO credential reset, revoke all active federated sessions, and audit downstream application access granted via that identity in the prior 30 days.
metrics: Count of SSO credential phishing incidents per quarter
Mean time to session revocation
ITID-12113.notes: Scoped to the password/credential itself, not the MFA step; MFA/OTP relay against this same login flow is ITID-12611 series in the MFA Bypass branch, kept separate to avoid duplicating that domain.

playbook.name: Response: Phished Corporate SSO/Identity Provider Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a corporate SSO/identity-provider credential, where compromise grants access across every federated application.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message and confirm the impersonated IdP
steps.desc: Collect the original message and confirm it was designed to impersonate the corporate SSO login page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed IdP-targeted phishing page and message preserved.

steps.title: Force password reset at the identity provider
steps.desc: Reset the account's password at the SSO/IdP layer immediately.
steps.outcome: IdP credential invalidated.

steps.title: Check for persistence across the IdP and connected apps
steps.desc: Review the IdP account and each connected application for attacker-added persistence (new MFA device, OAuth grant, delegated access).
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence across all connected systems.
steps.tool: Identity provider / connected app audit logs

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA and elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new password and re-enrolled MFA, and place the identity under elevated monitoring given the high blast radius.
steps.outcome: Access restored securely; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document as a high-severity finding
steps.desc: Record the incident with emphasis on SSO blast-radius risk and recommend phishing-resistant MFA (e.g. FIDO2) for high-value identities if not already in place.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and reviewed at appropriate severity.

steps.title: Confirm submission and enumerate downstream application exposure
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted, and enumerate every federated application the compromised identity has access to via SSO.
steps.guidance: This is the critical scoping step — treat the blast radius as every connected app until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission and full list of downstream application exposure.

steps.title: Revoke all SSO sessions and downstream application tokens
steps.desc: Terminate the SSO session and every downstream federated application session/token individually.
steps.guidance: Some federated apps cache a session independent of the IdP session lifetime — verify each is actually terminated, not just the IdP session.
steps.outcome: All access, including federated downstream sessions, terminated.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Remove any attacker-established persistence found across the IdP or downstream apps.
steps.outcome: No attacker foothold remains anywhere in the federated environment.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

ITID-12114.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a VPN client, remote desktop gateway, or other remote-access portal.
ITID-12114.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of a VPN or other remote-access credential, distinct from SSO/IdP theft because it targets network-layer remote access rather than federated application identity.
scopeIncludes: Fake VPN portal login page phishing
Harvested credential for remote-access gateway (e.g. Citrix, Cisco AnyConnect, Fortinet portal)
scopeExcludes: Phished SSO/IdP credential (ITID-12113)
Non-phishing VPN password spraying/brute force (ITID-12228, ITID-12316)
ITID-12114.severity: High - remote access credentials often bypass perimeter controls entirely.
ITID-12114.priority: P1 if VPN lacks MFA; P2 if MFA is enforced on the VPN.
ITID-12114.escalation: Escalate to network security team to disable the VPN account and review VPN connection logs immediately.
indicators: Fake VPN portal domain flagged by secure web gateway
VPN login from unrecognized IP shortly after a flagged phishing click
vectors: Spoofed VPN portal login page delivered via phishing email
rootCauses: VPN portal not enforcing MFA
Users unable to distinguish legitimate VPN domain
controls: MFA enforcement on VPN/remote access
VPN geo-velocity and new-device login alerting
ITID-12114.detection: VPN concentrator authentication logs provide concrete technical signal - new-device connections, geo-velocity anomalies, and failed-then-succeeded login patterns correlate directly with phishing timing.
ITID-12114.response: Disable the VPN account, force credential reset, and review VPN session logs for lateral movement or data access during any unauthorized session.
metrics: Count of VPN credential phishing incidents per quarter
Percentage of VPN accounts with MFA enforced
ITID-12114.notes: Scoped to phishing-sourced VPN credential theft specifically; non-phishing methods of obtaining the same VPN credential (spraying/brute force) are tracked under the Password Spraying and Brute Force types, not here.

playbook.name: Response: Phished VPN/Remote Access Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a VPN or remote-access credential, where compromise can grant network-level access.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message and confirm the impersonated VPN portal
steps.desc: Collect the original message and confirm the harvesting page impersonated the organization's VPN/remote-access login.
steps.outcome: Confirmed target and message preserved.

steps.title: Force password reset and terminate any active VPN session
steps.desc: Reset the credential and forcibly disconnect any active VPN session under the account.
steps.outcome: Credential invalidated; any live VPN session terminated.

steps.title: Investigate for internal lateral movement if VPN was accessed
steps.desc: If any VPN session occurred post-phishing, review internal network logs/EDR for lateral movement from that access point.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of internal compromise.

steps.title: Restore access with MFA enforced
steps.desc: Restore the user's VPN access with a new credential, confirming MFA is enforced for VPN authentication.
steps.outcome: Access restored with MFA confirmed active.

steps.title: Document and escalate as high-severity given network-access risk
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm VPN MFA coverage is adequate org-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and reviewed at appropriate severity.

steps.title: Confirm submission and check for VPN access already used
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted and check VPN gateway logs for any connection using the credential since the phishing timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and whether any VPN session has occurred.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

ITID-12115.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a cloud administrative console or infrastructure-management account (e.g. AWS/Azure/GCP root or admin console, on-prem hypervisor/domain admin portal).
ITID-12115.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of a cloud administrator or infrastructure-management credential, the highest-consequence target in this family given direct access to cloud control planes.
scopeIncludes: Fake cloud console login page phishing
Harvested credential for an account with cloud IAM administrative privilege
scopeExcludes: Phished credential for a standard (non-admin) cloud application account (ITID-12117)
Misuse of an already-compromised admin credential without a phishing origin (ITID-12412 series)
ITID-12115.severity: Critical - cloud admin compromise enables full infrastructure takeover, data exfiltration, and destruction.
ITID-12115.escalation: Immediate escalation to cloud platform/security engineering leadership; treat as active breach until scope is bounded.
indicators: Fake cloud console domain flagged by secure web gateway
Cloud audit log showing console login from unrecognized IP/device shortly after phishing click
vectors: Spoofed cloud provider login page targeting admin/root accounts
rootCauses: Cloud admin accounts not requiring hardware-key MFA
Root/admin credentials used for routine login rather than break-glass only
controls: Hardware-key MFA required for all cloud admin accounts
Break-glass account isolation with no routine phishing exposure
ITID-12115.detection: Cloud provider audit/control-plane logs (CloudTrail, Azure Activity Log, GCP Audit Logs) give precise, timestamped console-login and API-call telemetry correlating directly to the phishing event.
ITID-12115.response: Immediately disable/rotate the credential, revoke active cloud sessions/API keys, and audit all control-plane actions taken under that identity since the phishing event.
metrics: Count of cloud admin credential phishing incidents per year
Mean time to credential rotation and session revocation
ITID-12115.notes: Scoped to the phishing origin of the credential theft; the case where an already-obtained admin credential is subsequently misused belongs to ITID-12412 series (Misused Admin Credential) not this leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Phished Cloud Admin/Infrastructure Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a cloud administrator or infrastructure-management credential (e.g. cloud console, hypervisor, network device admin), carrying severe potential impact.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message and confirm the target's privilege level
steps.desc: Collect the original message and confirm the exact administrative scope of the account (e.g. cloud org owner, tenant admin, network admin).
steps.guidance: Treat this as a critical-severity incident from the outset given the potential blast radius.
steps.outcome: Confirmed privilege scope of the targeted account.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all active sessions/API keys
steps.desc: Immediately reset the credential and revoke all active console sessions, API keys, and access tokens tied to the account.
steps.guidance: Rotate any long-lived API keys/service credentials tied to this admin identity, not just the interactive login.
steps.outcome: All access under the account terminated.

steps.title: Audit infrastructure for unauthorized changes
steps.desc: Review cloud/infrastructure change logs since the phishing timestamp for any unauthorized resource creation, permission changes, or configuration modification.
steps.guidance: Look specifically for new admin accounts, new API keys, altered IAM policies, or new backdoor access paths.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of unauthorized infrastructure changes.

steps.title: Restore access with phishing-resistant MFA and elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Restore the admin's access with a new credential and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g. hardware key), and place the account and infrastructure under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Access restored securely; monitoring active.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review at critical severity
steps.desc: Document the full incident, notify leadership per policy, and confirm that privileged-access phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all admin identities.
steps.outcome: Post-incident review completed at appropriate severity.

steps.title: Confirm submission and check for any use of the credential since phishing
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted and review cloud/infrastructure audit logs for any activity under the account since the phishing timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and any post-phishing activity.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Revert unauthorized changes and remove persistence
steps.desc: Revert any unauthorized infrastructure changes and remove any attacker-added access mechanism.
steps.outcome: Infrastructure restored to a known-good state with no attacker foothold.

ITID-12116.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a corporate or personal email/webmail account.
ITID-12116.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of an email/webmail account credential, notable because compromised email is frequently used as a pivot for further account-recovery attacks.
scopeIncludes: Fake webmail login page phishing (e.g. spoofed Outlook Web Access/Gmail login)
Harvested credential for an email account used for business purposes
scopeExcludes: Phished SSO/IdP credential where email is one of several federated apps (ITID-12113)
OAuth token abuse against mailbox access without a password being phished (ITID-33142)
ITID-12116.severity: High - compromised email enables password-reset chains against other systems.
ITID-12116.priority: P1 if the mailbox has forwarding/delegate rules created; P2 otherwise.
ITID-12116.escalation: Escalate to IAM immediately to check for mailbox rule tampering, forwarding rules, and delegate access grants.
indicators: Fake webmail login domain flagged by secure web gateway
New inbox forwarding rule or delegate created shortly after phishing click
vectors: Spoofed webmail login page delivered via phishing email
rootCauses: Webmail account lacking MFA
No monitoring for new mailbox forwarding rules
mitreTechniques: T1114.003 Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
controls: MFA on webmail/email accounts
Alerting on new mailbox forwarding/delegate rule creation
ITID-12116.detection: Mailbox audit logs (e.g. Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log) provide concrete detection of new inbox rules, delegate grants, and anomalous mailbox access following the phishing event.
ITID-12116.response: Force password reset, remove any unauthorized forwarding/delegate rules, and review sent/received mail for the compromise window.
metrics: Count of email credential phishing incidents per quarter
Percentage with malicious mailbox rule created
ITID-12116.notes: Scoped to password-based mailbox credential theft; OAuth-token-based mailbox access abuse without a phished password is tracked separately under ITID-33142/33145.

playbook.name: Response: Phished Email/Webmail Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a corporate email/webmail credential, with the associated risk of mailbox takeover, internal spear-phishing, and business email compromise.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message
steps.desc: Collect the original message with headers intact from the affected mailbox.
steps.outcome: Original message preserved.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke mailbox sessions
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke all active mailbox sessions/tokens.
steps.outcome: Mailbox access terminated for the attacker.

steps.title: Check for mailbox persistence and outbound spear-phishing
steps.desc: Review the mailbox for attacker-added forwarding/inbox rules, and check sent items for any spear-phishing sent from the account to internal contacts.
steps.guidance: Business email compromise attacks often use a freshly compromised mailbox to target the victim's own contacts within minutes — check sent mail immediately.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence and outbound abuse.

steps.title: Restore mailbox access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new password and re-enrolled MFA.
steps.outcome: Access restored securely.

steps.title: Document root cause and delivery vector
steps.desc: Record the campaign details and recommend a control improvement (filtering rule, awareness point).
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm submission and check for mailbox activity since phishing
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted and review mailbox sign-in logs for activity since the phishing timestamp, including unfamiliar source locations/devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and any post-phishing mailbox activity.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message org-wide.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Remove persistence and notify recipients of any spear-phishing sent
steps.desc: Remove any malicious mail rule/OAuth grant, and notify any internal recipients who received a spear-phishing message sent from the compromised mailbox.
steps.outcome: No attacker foothold remains; internal recipients warned.

ITID-12117.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a standalone SaaS or third-party application account (e.g. a project-management tool, CRM, or vendor portal) not tied to the corporate identity provider.
ITID-12117.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of a SaaS or third-party application credential not federated through corporate SSO.
scopeIncludes: Fake SaaS application login page phishing
Harvested credential for a non-SSO-federated business application
scopeExcludes: Phished SSO/IdP credential (ITID-12113)
Credential stuffing/spraying against a SaaS portal using previously obtained credentials (ITID-12217, not phishing-sourced)
ITID-12117.severity: Medium-High depending on the data sensitivity of the SaaS application.
ITID-12117.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the application holds sensitive customer or financial data.
ITID-12117.escalation: Escalate to the application owner and IAM to disable the account and review activity logs.
indicators: Fake SaaS login domain flagged by secure web gateway
Anomalous login to the SaaS application shortly after phishing click
vectors: Spoofed SaaS application login page delivered via phishing email
rootCauses: SaaS application not integrated with corporate SSO/MFA
Shadow IT applications outside centralized identity governance
controls: SaaS application onboarding requiring SSO integration
CASB visibility into unsanctioned SaaS logins
ITID-12117.detection: Detection depends on the SaaS provider's own audit logging plus CASB visibility; less centralized than SSO-integrated apps but still a concrete technical signal where CASB/API log integration exists.
ITID-12117.response: Force password reset within the SaaS application, review account activity logs, and evaluate whether the application should be brought under SSO.
metrics: Count of non-SSO SaaS credential phishing incidents per quarter
Percentage of SaaS apps brought under SSO post-incident
ITID-12117.notes: Scoped to phishing-sourced theft of a standalone SaaS credential; non-phishing credential stuffing against the same portal type is tracked under ITID-12217.

playbook.name: Response: Phished SaaS/Third-Party Application Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a credential for a specific third-party SaaS application not federated through corporate SSO.

steps.title: Preserve the phishing message and identify the targeted SaaS application
steps.desc: Collect the original message and confirm which specific SaaS application's login page was impersonated.
steps.outcome: Confirmed target application and message preserved.

steps.title: Reset the credential within the SaaS platform
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke active sessions within the SaaS application's own admin console.
steps.outcome: Credential invalidated within the SaaS platform.

steps.title: Review the SaaS account for unauthorized data access or configuration changes
steps.desc: Check the SaaS platform's audit log (if available) for data accessed, exported, or configuration/permission changes made since the phishing timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any unauthorized activity within the platform.

steps.title: Restore access and consider SSO migration
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new credential, and evaluate migrating the application to corporate SSO to bring it under centralized MFA/monitoring.
steps.outcome: Access restored; migration considered.

steps.title: Document and update SaaS security inventory
steps.desc: Record the finding and update the organization's SaaS security posture tracking for this vendor.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm submission and check the SaaS platform's own logs
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted, and check the SaaS application's own authentication logs (via its admin console) for activity since the phishing timestamp.
steps.guidance: Access to detailed logs may require vendor support depending on the subscription tier.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and any post-phishing activity within the SaaS platform.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

ITID-12118.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a personal account (e.g. personal email, social media, personal cloud storage) but has confirmed or plausible corporate impact, typically via password reuse or stored corporate access on the same device.
ITID-12118.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of a personal (non-corporate) account credential that nonetheless creates corporate risk, such as through password reuse or personal-device access to work resources.
scopeIncludes: Personal account phishing where the victim also uses the same password for a corporate account
Personal device compromise via phished personal credential that also holds corporate app sessions
scopeExcludes: Purely personal-impact phishing with no plausible corporate nexus (out of ITID scope entirely)
Corporate account credential phishing (ITID-12113 through ITID-12117)
ITID-12118.severity: Medium, escalating to High if password reuse against a corporate account is confirmed.
ITID-12118.priority: P2 pending reuse confirmation; P1 if corporate account reuse is confirmed.
ITID-12118.escalation: Escalate to IAM to check for password reuse against corporate accounts using breach-monitoring/dark-web credential-check tooling.
indicators: Employee self-report of personal account phishing
Dark-web credential monitoring flags email address paired with a password matching corporate account pattern
vectors: Spoofed personal webmail or social media login page
rootCauses: Password reuse between personal and corporate accounts
No corporate breach-monitoring for employee personal emails
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Dark-web/breach credential monitoring for corporate identities
User education on password reuse risk
ITID-12118.detection: Limited direct technical telemetry on the personal-account side; corporate-side detection relies on breach-monitoring services and correlating exposed personal credentials against corporate password hashes/patterns.
ITID-12118.response: Check the exposed password against corporate account patterns; force corporate password reset if reuse is confirmed or suspected.
metrics: Count of personal-account phishing incidents with corporate nexus per quarter
sops: Employee Personal Account Breach Notification SOP
ITID-12118.notes: Scoped strictly to cases with a plausible or confirmed corporate nexus; purely personal-impact phishing incidents are not logged as an ITID at all.

playbook.name: Response: Phished Personal Account Credential with Corporate Impact
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a personal (non-corporate) account credential, where the resulting risk still impacts the organization (e.g. reused password on a corporate system, exposed personal email used for corporate password resets).

steps.title: Establish the corporate impact pathway
steps.desc: Determine specifically how the phished personal account creates corporate risk (e.g. it's used as the corporate account's recovery email, or the user has reused the same password on a corporate system).
steps.outcome: Confirmed corporate-impact pathway.

steps.title: Secure the corporate-side exposure
steps.desc: If a password was reused, force a reset on the corporate account; if the personal account is a recovery contact, temporarily remove it as a recovery option until secured.
steps.outcome: Corporate-side exposure closed.

steps.title: Advise the user to secure the personal account
steps.desc: Advise the user to reset the personal account's password and review it for unauthorized access, noting this falls outside direct organizational remediation authority.
steps.guidance: The SOC does not have authority to act directly on personal accounts — guidance only.
steps.outcome: User advised and personal account remediation left to them.

steps.title: Restore corporate access if it was affected
steps.desc: Restore any corporate access that was reset, with MFA confirmed active.
steps.outcome: Corporate access restored securely if applicable.

steps.title: Document and reinforce personal/corporate separation guidance
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend awareness messaging on not linking personal accounts to corporate recovery paths and avoiding password reuse.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Confirm submission and any corporate-side compromise
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted on the personal account, and check whether the corporate system reachable via that pathway shows any signs of compromise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and corporate-side compromise status.

ITID-12119.def: A phishing incident in which the credential harvested was for a corporate banking portal, payment platform, or financial services account.
ITID-12119.purpose: Captures phishing-based theft of a financial or banking portal credential belonging to the organization or an employee acting in a corporate financial capacity.
scopeIncludes: Fake corporate banking portal login page phishing
Harvested credential for a corporate payment/treasury platform account
scopeExcludes: Business email compromise used to redirect a wire transfer without credential theft (a social-engineering ITID elsewhere)
Personal banking credential phishing with no corporate nexus (out of ITID scope)
ITID-12119.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/treasury and the bank's fraud department to freeze the account and reverse any pending transactions.
indicators: Fake banking portal domain flagged by secure web gateway
Unauthorized transaction or login attempt on the corporate banking account shortly after phishing
vectors: Spoofed banking/payment platform login page delivered via phishing email
rootCauses: Banking portal not enforcing hardware-token MFA
Insufficient dual-control on financial transactions
controls: Hardware-token MFA on banking/treasury portals
Dual-control/approval workflow for outbound payments
ITID-12119.detection: Banking platform login and transaction logs, combined with the bank's own fraud-detection alerting, give a concrete, time-correlated signal against the phishing event.
ITID-12119.response: Freeze the account, contact the bank's fraud team, force credential reset, and review all transactions since the phishing event for reversal.
metrics: Count of banking credential phishing incidents per year
Dollar value of transactions frozen/reversed
ITID-12119.notes: Scoped to credential theft against a financial portal specifically; wire-fraud social engineering without credential theft is classified elsewhere.

playbook.name: Response: Phished Financial/Banking Portal Credential
playbook.description: For phishing that harvested a financial/banking portal credential belonging to an employee, with potential direct financial-fraud impact to the organization or the individual (e.g. corporate banking access, expense/payroll portal).

steps.title: Determine whether the account is personal or corporate financial access
steps.desc: Establish whether the phished credential is for a personal banking account or a corporate financial system (e.g. corporate banking portal, payroll/expense platform).
steps.guidance: This determines urgency and who must be engaged (finance/treasury team for corporate access).
steps.outcome: Confirmed account type and business criticality.

steps.title: Lock the financial account and notify the institution
steps.desc: If corporate financial access, immediately notify the bank/finance platform provider to freeze the account and lock further transactions; reset the credential.
steps.guidance: For a corporate banking portal, engage the finance/treasury team immediately — this is a joint SOC-and-finance response.
steps.outcome: Financial account locked; credential reset.

steps.title: Coordinate fraud reversal if a transaction occurred
steps.desc: Work with the financial institution/finance team to attempt reversal of any fraudulent transaction and file required fraud reports.
steps.outcome: Fraud reversal/reporting initiated where applicable.

steps.title: Restore access with strengthened verification
steps.desc: Restore access to the financial platform only after re-verification through the institution's strongest identity-verification path, with MFA confirmed active.
steps.outcome: Access restored securely.

steps.title: Document financial impact and notify required stakeholders
steps.desc: Document the full incident including any financial loss, and notify finance/legal/compliance stakeholders as required by policy.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and required notifications completed.

steps.title: Confirm submission and check for fraudulent transactions
steps.desc: Confirm what was submitted, and immediately check the financial platform for any unauthorized transaction or change (e.g. altered bank details, new payee) since the phishing timestamp.
steps.guidance: Speed matters — financial fraud following credential phishing often occurs within minutes to hours.
steps.outcome: Confirmed submission status and any fraudulent activity.

steps.title: Block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the sender domain/URL and purge remaining copies of the message.
steps.outcome: Domain/URL blocked; message purged.

ITID-12121.def: An incident involving suspected or confirmed keystroke-capture software or hardware where the specific mechanism (software, hardware, browser-based, kernel-level, RAT-embedded, mobile, cloud-session, or insider-installed) has not yet been identified.
ITID-12121.purpose: Catch-all for keylogging incidents where the specific keylogger delivery mechanism has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the keylogger delivery mechanism is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the mechanism is known and matches ITID-12122 through ITID-12129
ITID-12121.severity: High by default, pending reclassification, since keylogging implies broad credential exposure.
ITID-12121.escalation: Reclassify once the delivery mechanism is confirmed via forensic analysis.
indicators: EDR alert on suspicious input-hooking process of unclear type
User report of anomalous system behavior with unconfirmed cause
vectors: Unclear/unconfirmed at time of initial detection
rootCauses: Insufficient forensic detail captured at time of detection
controls: EDR behavioral detection of keystroke-hooking APIs
ITID-12121.detection: Same EDR/host telemetry as the specific sibling leaves, pending finer classification of the mechanism.
ITID-12121.response: Isolate the affected endpoint, perform forensic triage, and reclassify to a specific sibling leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12121.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification within Keylogging, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Keylogging Incident
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected keylogging incident where the specific mechanism (software, hardware, browser-based, etc.) has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Confirm the keylogging indicator
steps.desc: Review the triggering alert (EDR detection, user report of suspicious device behavior, unexplained account compromise) and gather initial context on the affected endpoint and user.
steps.outcome: Confirmed reasonable suspicion of keylogging, or ruled out.
steps.abort: If the alert is a known-benign EDR false positive with no corroborating evidence, close as false positive.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the device from the network via EDR to stop further capture/exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Remove the keylogging mechanism
steps.desc: Remove the identified keylogging component, or reimage the device if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the device and monitor affected accounts
steps.desc: Return the clean device to service and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document findings
steps.desc: Record the mechanism, exposure window, and remediation taken.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine the keylogging mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate the endpoint to determine whether the mechanism is software-based, hardware-based, browser-based, or something else, and reclassify to the specific ITID if identified.
steps.outcome: Mechanism identified and incident tagged accordingly.

steps.title: Reset credentials entered on the affected device
steps.desc: Force a password reset for all accounts the user is known to have accessed from the affected device during the suspected exposure window.
steps.outcome: Potentially captured credentials invalidated.

ITID-12122.def: A software keylogger installed on an endpoint via a malicious file, email attachment, or drive-by download, running in user-mode to capture keystrokes.
ITID-12122.purpose: Captures keystroke-capture malware delivered as a standalone software payload via typical malware delivery vectors (phishing attachment, drive-by download, trojanized installer).
scopeIncludes: User-mode software keylogger delivered via malicious attachment or download
Keylogger component bundled with commodity malware, delivered by a human-targeted vector
scopeExcludes: Kernel-level/rootkit keyloggers, which hook at a lower privilege level (ITID-12125)
RAT tools where keylogging is a secondary capability of a broader remote-access trojan (ITID-12126)
ITID-12122.severity: High - direct credential exposure for every application typed into on the affected endpoint.
ITID-12122.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if privileged-user endpoint.
ITID-12122.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR for endpoint isolation and full credential-reset scope determination.
indicators: EDR alert on process hooking SetWindowsHookEx or equivalent keyboard API
Unusual outbound traffic to exfiltrate captured keystroke logs
vectors: Malicious email attachment
Drive-by download from compromised website
rootCauses: Endpoint protection gap allowing initial malware execution
User executed an untrusted attachment
controls: EDR behavioral detection of keyboard-hooking APIs
Email attachment sandboxing
ITID-12122.detection: EDR provides strong host-level detection of known keyboard-hook API calls and the exfiltration channel used to send captured logs, giving concrete technical telemetry.
ITID-12122.response: Isolate the endpoint, force reset of every credential typed since likely infection date, and remove the malware via reimage.
metrics: Count of software keylogger incidents per quarter
Mean time to isolation
ITID-12122.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12125 (kernel-level) by privilege level, and from ITID-12126 (RAT) by keylogging being the primary rather than secondary capability of the malware.

playbook.name: Response: Software Keylogger via Malware Delivery
playbook.description: For a software keylogger delivered via a malicious attachment, drive-by download, or other malware infection vector.

steps.title: Confirm the malware and delivery vector
steps.desc: Use EDR to identify the specific malware family/sample and trace back the delivery vector (email attachment, malicious download, drive-by compromise).
steps.outcome: Confirmed malware identity and delivery vector.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the affected device from the network via EDR.
steps.outcome: Device isolated; further capture/exfiltration stopped.

steps.title: Remove the malware and verify persistence mechanisms are cleared
steps.desc: Remove the malware via EDR remediation and check for associated persistence (scheduled tasks, registry run keys, services); reimage if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean of the malware and its persistence.

steps.title: Restore and monitor
steps.desc: Return the clean device to service and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document infection chain and recommend control improvement
steps.desc: Record the full infection chain and recommend an improvement to the control that should have blocked delivery.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine exposure window and captured data scope
steps.desc: Establish how long the keylogger was active and what accounts/data were likely typed on the device during that window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure window and affected account scope.

steps.title: Reset all credentials typed during the exposure window
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for every account accessed from the device during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: All potentially captured credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Block the delivery infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the malicious sender domain/download source/C2 infrastructure identified during analysis.
steps.outcome: Delivery/C2 infrastructure blocked org-wide.

ITID-12123.def: A physical device inserted inline between a keyboard and computer, or embedded within a keyboard/peripheral, that records keystrokes for later retrieval or wireless exfiltration.
ITID-12123.purpose: Captures use of a physical hardware keylogging device (e.g. USB inline dongle, PS/2 adapter) requiring physical access to the target machine.
scopeIncludes: USB/PS2 inline hardware keylogger discovered attached to a workstation
Keyboard with an embedded keylogging chip
scopeExcludes: Software-based keyloggers requiring no physical access (ITID-12122, ITID-12124, ITID-12125)
ITID-12123.severity: High - implies physical access to the facility/device and targeted intent.
ITID-12123.priority: P1, given the physical-access and insider/on-site-attacker implications.
ITID-12123.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and SOC jointly; treat as a targeted, deliberate attack requiring facility access review.
indicators: Unexplained USB device found inline between keyboard and workstation
Physical security camera footage showing an unauthorized person accessing a workstation port
vectors: Physical insertion of an inline USB/PS2 hardware device during unattended access
rootCauses: Unrestricted physical access to workstations
No periodic physical inspection of exposed cabling/ports
controls: Periodic physical port/cable inspection
Port-lockdown/tamper-evident seals on workstation ports
ITID-12123.detection: Limited software telemetry since the device operates outside the OS; detection relies on physical inspection, asset audits, and correlating physical-access-control logs with the discovery timeframe.
ITID-12123.response: Remove the device, preserve it for forensic/chain-of-custody handling, force reset of all credentials typed at that workstation, and review facility access logs for the exposure window.
metrics: Count of hardware keylogger discoveries per year
ITID-12123.notes: This is the one leaf in the keylogging sibling group with a physical-access rather than software detection surface; coordinate with physical security ITIDs but log the credential-theft outcome here.

playbook.name: Response: Hardware Keylogger (Physical Device)
playbook.description: For a physical hardware keylogger discovered attached to a keyboard cable, USB port, or internally to a device, requiring physical investigation rather than purely digital response.

steps.title: Photograph and physically secure the device
steps.desc: Photograph the hardware keylogger in place before removal, then physically remove and securely retain it as evidence.
steps.guidance: Do not power-cycle or plug the device into another system to inspect it — treat as evidence and, if criminal activity is suspected, coordinate with physical security/legal before handling further.
steps.outcome: Device documented and secured as evidence.

steps.title: Reset all credentials typed on the affected keyboard during the exposure window
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for every account the user accessed on the affected device during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Potentially captured credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Investigate physical access to determine how the device was installed
steps.desc: Review facility access logs/CCTV/visitor logs to identify who had physical access to install the device.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security and, if warranted, law enforcement/legal given this indicates physical intrusion or an insider.
steps.outcome: Access investigation completed with findings or leads documented.

steps.title: Restore the workstation and monitor affected accounts
steps.desc: Return the workstation to service (hardware removed) and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Workstation restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and recommend physical-security control improvement
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend physical-security improvements (e.g. tamper-evident seals, restricted access to sensitive workstation areas, periodic physical inspection).
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendation tracked.

steps.title: Determine the exposure window
steps.desc: Establish, where possible (e.g. from facilities access logs, CCTV, or user report of a recent inspection), how long the device was likely in place.
steps.guidance: Physical placement is often the hardest part to date precisely — use the last known 'clean' inspection as the outer bound.
steps.outcome: Best-estimate exposure window established.

steps.title: Physically inspect nearby/similar devices
steps.desc: Check other devices in the same physical area (shared workstations, meeting-room terminals) for similar implants.
steps.guidance: Hardware keyloggers are sometimes installed on multiple machines in a single visit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of physical compromise limited to the one device, or additional devices found.

ITID-12124.def: A browser-based keylogger that captures keystrokes typed into web form fields via injected or malicious JavaScript running within the browser's rendering context.
ITID-12124.purpose: Captures keystroke capture executed via malicious JavaScript injected into or embedded within a webpage or browser extension, at the browser layer rather than the OS layer.
scopeIncludes: Malicious JavaScript injected into a compromised website capturing form-field keystrokes (web skimming-style)
Malicious browser extension capturing keystrokes at the DOM/input-event level
scopeExcludes: OS-level software keyloggers capturing all system keystrokes regardless of application (ITID-12122)
Credential injection into an already-rendered form by a malicious extension (ITID-12837, a different technique)
ITID-12124.severity: High if targeting a financial or credential-entry page; Medium otherwise.
ITID-12124.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment or credential-entry page is confirmed targeted.
ITID-12124.escalation: Escalate to web application security team to remove the malicious script/extension and to affected users for credential reset.
indicators: Unrecognized script tag or event listener injected into page source
Browser extension with excessive permissions requesting access to all input events
vectors: Compromised third-party JavaScript library/tag on the organization's website
Malicious browser extension installed from an unofficial or compromised store listing
rootCauses: Unvetted third-party scripts loaded on production pages
Lack of browser extension allowlisting policy
controls: Subresource Integrity (SRI) on third-party scripts
Browser extension allowlisting/enterprise policy
ITID-12124.detection: Content Security Policy violation reports, web application firewall/JS-integrity monitoring, and browser telemetry (managed extension inventories) provide concrete technical detection.
ITID-12124.response: Remove the malicious script or extension, force credential reset for affected users, and review page/extension change history to identify the injection point.
metrics: Count of browser-based keylogging incidents per quarter
ITID-12124.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12837 (Credential Injection via Malicious Browser Extension) by mechanism: this leaf captures keystrokes as typed, whereas ITID-12837 injects/manipulates already-stored credentials into a form.

playbook.name: Response: Browser-Based/JavaScript Keylogger
playbook.description: For a malicious script injected into a webpage (via a compromised site, malicious ad, or vulnerable third-party script) that captures keystrokes entered into that page's form fields.

steps.title: Identify the compromised/malicious page
steps.desc: Obtain the URL of the page where keylogging occurred and review its source for the injected JavaScript capturing keystroke events.
steps.guidance: Check whether the site itself is compromised (legitimate site serving malicious script) or is inherently malicious/phishing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed page and injected script identified.

steps.title: Block the malicious page/domain
steps.desc: Add the domain/URL to the web/DNS blocklist.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked org-wide.

steps.title: Notify the site owner if it's a legitimate third-party site
steps.desc: If the affected site belongs to a legitimate third party (vendor, partner) that was compromised, notify them so they can remediate the injection.
steps.outcome: Site owner notified where applicable.

steps.title: Monitor affected accounts
steps.desc: Place affected accounts under elevated monitoring for anomalous activity.
steps.outcome: Watchlist configured.

steps.title: Document finding
steps.desc: Record the technique, scope, and remediation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine affected users and data captured
steps.desc: Review proxy/DNS logs for which users visited the page during the compromise window, and determine what form fields (login, payment, personal data) were exposed to the script.
steps.outcome: List of affected users and scope of data exposure.

steps.title: Reset credentials for affected users
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for accounts entered on the compromised page.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

ITID-12125.def: A keylogger implemented as a kernel-mode driver or rootkit component that hooks keyboard input at a privilege level below standard EDR visibility.
ITID-12125.purpose: Captures keystroke capture implemented at the kernel driver or rootkit level, notable for its ability to evade user-mode security tooling.
scopeIncludes: Kernel driver keyboard filter installed by malware
Rootkit-embedded keystroke capture component
scopeExcludes: User-mode software keyloggers (ITID-12122)
ITID-12125.severity: Critical - kernel-level persistence implies both deep compromise and evasion of standard defenses.
ITID-12125.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR for full forensic investigation; assume broader compromise beyond keylogging alone.
indicators: Unsigned or anomalous kernel driver loaded
EDR/anti-rootkit tooling flags hidden process or hooked kernel keyboard filter
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability to load an unsigned kernel driver
Malware with a kernel-mode rootkit component
rootCauses: Driver signature enforcement not enabled/enforced
Endpoint lacking anti-rootkit/kernel-integrity monitoring
mitreTechniques: T1543.003 Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
controls: Driver signature enforcement (e.g. Windows HVCI)
Kernel-integrity/anti-rootkit monitoring
ITID-12125.detection: Requires specialized kernel-integrity and anti-rootkit tooling since standard user-mode EDR visibility can be evaded; offline forensic disk/memory imaging is often needed for confirmation.
ITID-12125.response: Isolate and reimage the endpoint from a known-good source (do not trust in-place remediation given rootkit persistence), and reset all credentials used on that host.
metrics: Count of kernel-level keylogger incidents per year
sops: Mandatory Reimage SOP for Kernel Compromise
ITID-12125.notes: Given the evasion capability, treat detection gaps as expected; do not rely on standard EDR alone to rule this out during triage.

playbook.name: Response: Kernel-Level/Rootkit Keylogger
playbook.description: For a keylogger operating with kernel-level privileges or rootkit stealth techniques, evading standard EDR/AV detection and requiring specialized forensic handling.

steps.title: Escalate for specialized forensic analysis
steps.desc: Given the stealth/kernel-level nature, escalate to a forensic specialist or incident-response retainer rather than relying solely on standard EDR triage, which may not fully detect the rootkit's scope.
steps.guidance: Kernel-level rootkits can also disable or blind EDR agents — do not trust the EDR's own assessment of the device as fully clean.
steps.outcome: Specialized forensic resource engaged.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint at the network layer
steps.desc: Physically or network-isolate the device rather than relying on host-based EDR isolation, which the rootkit may be able to evade.
steps.outcome: Device fully isolated at the network level.

steps.title: Reimage the device from bare metal
steps.desc: Given kernel-level compromise, do not attempt in-place removal — wipe and reimage the device from a known-good source.
steps.guidance: Kernel-level rootkits can survive standard OS reinstalls in some cases (e.g. firmware/bootkit persistence) — verify firmware integrity if that risk applies to this hardware class.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed rebuilt from a trusted baseline.

steps.title: Restore with enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Return the rebuilt device to service with enhanced EDR telemetry and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; enhanced monitoring active.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the full incident given its severity, including how the rootkit evaded standard detection, and recommend detection-capability improvements.
steps.outcome: Post-incident review completed.

steps.title: Determine exposure window and scope via offline/forensic imaging
steps.desc: Capture a forensic disk/memory image of the affected device for offline analysis to determine the rootkit's install date and full capability.
steps.guidance: Live analysis on a potentially rootkit-infected host is unreliable — offline imaging avoids the rootkit hiding artifacts from a running query.
steps.outcome: Forensic image captured; exposure window and capability confirmed.

steps.title: Reset all credentials associated with the device from a separate, trusted device
steps.desc: Reset every account accessed from the affected device, performed from a known-clean, separate device.
steps.outcome: All potentially captured credentials invalidated.

ITID-12126.def: A Remote Access Trojan installed on an endpoint that includes a keylogging module alongside broader remote-control capabilities (screen capture, file access, remote shell).
ITID-12126.purpose: Captures keystroke capture that is a secondary capability of a broader Remote Access Trojan (RAT), distinguishing this from standalone keylogger malware by the presence of full interactive remote-control capability.
scopeIncludes: RAT malware (e.g. njRAT, DarkComet-class tooling) confirmed with an active keylogging module
Keylogging observed as one of several data-collection features of a broader implant
scopeExcludes: Standalone keylogger malware with no remote-control capability (ITID-12122)
ITID-12126.severity: Critical - implies full remote control of the endpoint, not just credential exposure.
ITID-12126.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR; treat as full endpoint compromise requiring containment beyond credential reset alone.
indicators: EDR detection of known RAT family with keylogging module active
C2 beaconing pattern consistent with an interactive RAT
vectors: Phishing attachment delivering a RAT payload
Trojanized software download
rootCauses: Endpoint protection gap allowing RAT execution
Lack of egress filtering enabling C2 communication
controls: EDR RAT-family signature/behavioral detection
Egress filtering/C2 domain blocking
ITID-12126.detection: EDR and network detection together give strong signal: known RAT family detection plus C2 beaconing pattern analysis on network telemetry.
ITID-12126.response: Isolate the endpoint immediately, treat as full compromise (not just credential theft), reset all credentials used on the host, and hunt for lateral movement.
metrics: Count of RAT-with-keylogging incidents per quarter
Mean time to isolation
ITID-12126.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12122 by scope: this leaf applies when keylogging is one module of a broader interactive-control implant, not the malware's sole purpose.

playbook.name: Response: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) with Keylogging Capability
playbook.description: For a Remote Access Trojan providing an attacker interactive remote control of the device in addition to keystroke capture, representing a broader and more active compromise than keylogging alone.

steps.title: Confirm the RAT and assess for active attacker interaction
steps.desc: Identify the specific RAT family via EDR and review C2 communication logs to determine whether an attacker has been actively interacting with the device (not just passively collecting).
steps.guidance: Active RAT interaction changes urgency — treat as a live intrusion, not just a data-exposure incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed RAT identity and whether active attacker interaction occurred.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint immediately
steps.desc: Isolate the device from the network via EDR without delay to cut off the attacker's active access.
steps.outcome: Attacker's remote control severed.

steps.title: Reimage the device
steps.desc: Given active attacker control, reimage the device from a known-good baseline rather than attempting in-place removal.
steps.outcome: Device rebuilt from trusted baseline.

steps.title: Restore with enhanced monitoring and broaden the hunt
steps.desc: Return the rebuilt device to service and hunt across the environment for the same RAT indicators on other endpoints.
steps.outcome: Device restored; environment-wide hunt completed.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the full incident including attacker dwell time and actions taken, given the active-intrusion nature.
steps.outcome: Post-incident review completed.

steps.title: Determine full scope of attacker activity
steps.desc: Review what the attacker did via the RAT beyond keylogging — file access, screen capture, additional tool deployment, lateral movement attempts.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker activity documented.

steps.title: Reset all credentials and check for lateral movement
steps.desc: Reset credentials for all accounts accessed from the device and check whether the RAT was used to pivot to other systems.
steps.outcome: Credentials invalidated; lateral-movement scope confirmed.

steps.title: Block C2 infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the RAT's command-and-control domains/IPs at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: C2 infrastructure blocked org-wide.

ITID-12127.def: A malicious mobile application or exploit that captures keyboard input (including on-screen keyboard taps) on a smartphone or tablet.
ITID-12127.purpose: Captures keystroke/input capture malware targeting a mobile device (iOS/Android) rather than a desktop endpoint.
scopeIncludes: Malicious mobile app with input-capture/accessibility-service abuse for keylogging
Mobile malware capturing on-screen keyboard input via overlay or accessibility API abuse
scopeExcludes: Desktop/laptop keyloggers (ITID-12122 through ITID-12126)
SMS/smishing credential harvesting that does not involve keystroke capture (a separate phishing ITID branch)
ITID-12127.severity: High if the device has corporate app access (email, VPN, MDM-enrolled).
ITID-12127.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for MDM-enrolled corporate devices.
ITID-12127.escalation: Escalate to mobile device management (MDM) team to remotely wipe/quarantine the device and revoke app tokens.
indicators: MDM/MTD (mobile threat defense) alert flagging malicious app with accessibility-service abuse
Unusual battery/data usage pattern correlated with a sideloaded app
vectors: Sideloaded malicious application outside official app store vetting
Malicious app abusing Android Accessibility Service permissions
rootCauses: Device allows sideloading/unknown sources
No mobile threat defense (MTD) solution deployed
controls: Mobile threat defense (MTD) app scanning
MDM policy restricting sideloading and app permissions
ITID-12127.detection: MDM/MTD telemetry provides concrete technical detection of malicious app installation and abnormal accessibility-service permission usage.
ITID-12127.response: Remotely wipe or quarantine the device via MDM, force reset of credentials used on the device, and review app installation history.
metrics: Count of mobile keylogging incidents per quarter
ITID-12127.notes: Scoped to keystroke-capture mobile malware specifically, not general mobile phishing/smishing which is tracked under the phishing ITID branches.

playbook.name: Response: Mobile Device Keylogger
playbook.description: For a keylogging application or malicious profile installed on a mobile device (phone/tablet), corporate-managed or BYOD, capturing keystrokes or on-screen input.

steps.title: Identify the malicious app/profile and device management status
steps.desc: Determine the specific malicious app or configuration profile responsible, and whether the device is corporate-managed (MDM) or BYOD.
steps.guidance: Response authority and options differ significantly between MDM-managed and unmanaged personal devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious component and device management status.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the device's corporate access
steps.desc: Via MDM, restrict or revoke the device's access to corporate resources (email, VPN, apps) pending remediation.
steps.guidance: For unmanaged BYOD devices without MDM enrollment, revoke corporate app/session access at the identity-provider level instead.
steps.outcome: Device's corporate access restricted.

steps.title: Remove the malicious app/profile
steps.desc: Remove the malicious app/configuration profile via MDM, or guide the user to do so and factory-reset if MDM control is unavailable.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore corporate access
steps.desc: Restore the device's corporate access once confirmed clean, and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Access restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document and reinforce mobile security policy
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend reinforcement of mobile app-installation policy/awareness, particularly for BYOD devices.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine exposure window and accounts accessed
steps.desc: Establish how long the malicious component was present and which corporate accounts/apps were accessed on the device during that window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure window and affected account scope.

steps.title: Reset credentials accessed on the device
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for accounts accessed on the device during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Potentially captured credentials invalidated.

ITID-12128.def: A malicious or over-permissioned browser extension that captures keystrokes and/or session data specifically during interaction with cloud/SaaS applications.
ITID-12128.purpose: Captures keystroke or session-input capture performed via a malicious browser extension specifically targeting cloud/SaaS session activity, distinct from a general browser JavaScript keylogger by its persistence as an installed extension with broad tab access.
scopeIncludes: Browser extension with 'read and change all data on websites' permission confirmed capturing keystrokes on SaaS login/app pages
Extension-based capture of SaaS application session activity
scopeExcludes: One-off malicious JavaScript injected into a single compromised page (ITID-12124)
Extension-based credential injection into forms rather than capture of typed input (ITID-12837)
ITID-12128.severity: High - persistent extension access spans every SaaS session in that browser profile.
ITID-12128.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the extension has been active for an extended period across multiple SaaS applications.
ITID-12128.escalation: Escalate to IT/security to force-remove the extension fleet-wide via browser management policy and reset affected SaaS credentials.
indicators: Enterprise browser management console flags an extension with broad host permissions and no legitimate business justification
Unusual outbound traffic from the browser process correlated with extension activity
vectors: Malicious extension published on an official web store and later weaponized via an update
Extension installed via social engineering (fake productivity tool)
rootCauses: No enterprise browser extension allowlist/blocklist policy
Users granted local admin rights permitting arbitrary extension installation
controls: Enterprise browser extension allowlist policy
Browser management console extension inventory monitoring
ITID-12128.detection: Enterprise browser management (e.g. Chrome Browser Cloud Management, Entra-managed browser policies) gives a concrete inventory-based detection surface for over-permissioned extensions.
ITID-12128.response: Remove the extension fleet-wide, reset credentials for every SaaS application accessed during the extension's active period, and review SaaS access logs for anomalies.
metrics: Count of malicious extension incidents per quarter
Number of SaaS credentials reset per incident
ITID-12128.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12124 by persistence and scope: this leaf covers an installed extension with ongoing multi-session SaaS access, not a single injected-page script.

playbook.name: Response: Cloud/SaaS Session Keylogging via Browser Extension
playbook.description: For a malicious browser extension capturing keystrokes/input specifically within cloud/SaaS application sessions (e.g. capturing data entered into a CRM, cloud email, or collaboration tool).

steps.title: Identify the malicious extension and its fleet-wide footprint
steps.desc: Identify the extension via EDR/browser management console and determine how many managed browsers have it installed.
steps.outcome: Malicious extension identified and its fleet-wide install footprint determined.

steps.title: Force-remove the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Push a policy to block/remove the extension across all managed browsers.
steps.outcome: Extension removed from all affected endpoints.

steps.title: Add the extension to a permanent blocklist
steps.desc: Add the extension ID/publisher to the organization's permanent extension blocklist policy.
steps.outcome: Extension permanently blocked from installation.

steps.title: Review affected SaaS platforms for data exposure
steps.desc: Check each affected SaaS platform's own audit log for any data accessed or exported using the captured sessions/credentials.
steps.outcome: Downstream data-exposure risk assessed per platform.

steps.title: Document scope and recommend extension governance improvement
steps.desc: Record affected user count, data exposure, and recommend moving to an extension allowlist model if not already in place.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine which cloud/SaaS sessions were exposed
steps.desc: Based on the extension's permissions and observed behavior, determine which cloud/SaaS applications' data it had access to capture.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposed cloud/SaaS sessions documented.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and reset credentials for affected cloud/SaaS accounts
steps.desc: Force session revocation and password resets for every cloud/SaaS account used on a browser with the extension installed.
steps.outcome: Exposed sessions/credentials invalidated.

ITID-12129.def: A keylogger (hardware or software) installed by an individual with authorized access to the affected system or environment, for the purpose of surveilling another user's credentials or activity.
ITID-12129.purpose: Captures keylogging performed by an insider with authorized physical or logical access, distinguishing intentional internal deployment from external malware delivery for both response path and HR/legal handling.
scopeIncludes: Employee installing a keylogger on a shared or colleague's workstation
IT staff installing a keylogger beyond authorized monitoring scope
scopeExcludes: External attacker-delivered keyloggers (ITID-12122 through ITID-12127)
Authorized, disclosed employee-monitoring software operating within policy (not an incident)
ITID-12129.severity: High - implies both credential exposure and a trust/insider-threat dimension requiring HR involvement.
ITID-12129.priority: P1, given the insider-threat and potential legal/HR dimension.
ITID-12129.escalation: Escalate jointly to HR, Legal, and SOC; handle with insider-threat case-management procedures alongside technical remediation.
indicators: Keylogger software/hardware traced to an internal user account or physical access badge
Employee report of suspected surveillance by a colleague
vectors: Insider installing commercial/off-the-shelf monitoring software beyond policy scope
Insider physically installing a hardware keylogger on a colleague's device
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls preventing unauthorized software installation
No policy/technical control against unauthorized monitoring tools
controls: Application allowlisting preventing unauthorized monitoring software installation
HR/Legal insider-threat case management process
ITID-12129.detection: EDR software inventory and application-control logs can identify unauthorized monitoring tool installation and attribute it to the installing user account.
ITID-12129.response: Remove the keylogger, preserve evidence for HR/Legal, reset affected credentials, and manage the case through insider-threat procedures.
metrics: Count of insider-installed keylogger incidents per year
ITID-12129.notes: This leaf is differentiated from the rest of the Keylogging type purely by the internal/authorized-access origin of the actor, not by the technical mechanism used, which may match any of ITID-12122 through ITID-12125.

playbook.name: Response: Insider-Installed Keylogger
playbook.description: For a keylogger (software or hardware) deliberately installed by an insider — an employee or contractor — typically targeting a colleague's or executive's device, requiring coordination with HR/legal in addition to technical response.

steps.title: Confirm the keylogger and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Confirm the presence of the keylogger (software or hardware) on the target device and preserve forensic evidence (device image, physical device, install timestamps, associated logs) before any remediation actions that could destroy evidence.
steps.guidance: Given the likely HR/legal/disciplinary outcome, evidence handling and chain of custody matter more here than in a typical external-attacker incident — engage legal/HR before taking destructive action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with documented chain of custody.

steps.title: Reset credentials for the targeted victim
steps.desc: Force a password reset and session revocation for the targeted individual's accounts as a protective measure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with HR/legal so the reset does not tip off the suspected insider before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Victim's accounts secured.

steps.title: Remove the keylogging device/software
steps.desc: Once evidence is secured and HR/legal has authorized remediation, remove the keylogger from the affected device.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the victim's device and monitor
steps.desc: Return the clean device to service and place the victim's accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document the full case for the HR/legal record
steps.desc: Provide a complete technical timeline and evidence summary to HR/Legal for their disciplinary/legal process, and recommend any physical or access-control improvement to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Case documentation delivered to HR/Legal; control recommendation logged.

steps.title: Identify the installer and notify HR/legal
steps.desc: Determine, from install artifacts (timestamps, access logs, purchase records for hardware devices), who installed the keylogger, and escalate to HR and Legal immediately given the insider-threat nature.
steps.guidance: Do not confront the suspected individual directly — this is an HR/legal-led process from this point, with security providing technical support.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; suspected installer identified where possible.

steps.title: Restrict the suspected insider's access pending investigation
steps.desc: At HR/legal's direction, restrict or suspend the suspected individual's system access pending the outcome of the investigation.
steps.guidance: This step is directed by HR/Legal, not initiated unilaterally by the SOC.
steps.outcome: Suspected insider's access restricted per HR/legal direction.

ITID-12131.def: An incident involving malware confirmed or suspected of extracting stored credentials from an endpoint, where the specific target (browser passwords, memory, password manager vault, cached tokens, email client, Wi-Fi credentials, or commodity infostealer family) has not yet been identified.
ITID-12131.purpose: Catch-all for credential harvesting malware incidents where the specific data extracted or extraction method has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific credential-harvesting malware behavior is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific extraction target is known and matches ITID-12132 through ITID-12139
ITID-12131.escalation: Reclassify once forensic analysis confirms the specific extraction target/mechanism.
indicators: EDR alert on suspicious process accessing credential storage locations of unclear specificity
vectors: Unclear/unconfirmed at time of initial detection
rootCauses: Insufficient forensic detail captured at time of detection
controls: EDR behavioral detection of credential-store access
ITID-12131.detection: Same EDR/host telemetry as the specific sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12131.response: Isolate the affected endpoint, perform forensic triage, and reclassify once the extraction target is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12131.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification within Credential Harvesting Malware, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Credential Harvesting Malware Incident
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected credential-harvesting malware incident where the specific malware type/target has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Confirm the malware detection
steps.desc: Review the EDR/AV alert and gather initial context on the affected endpoint, user, and malware classification.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malware presence and initial classification.
steps.abort: If the alert is a confirmed EDR false positive, close as false positive.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the device from the network via EDR to stop further capture/exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Remove the malware
steps.desc: Remove the malware via EDR remediation, or reimage the device if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore and monitor
steps.desc: Return the clean device to service and place affected accounts under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Device restored; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document findings
steps.desc: Record the malware type, exposure scope, and remediation taken.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine the malware's specific capability and target
steps.desc: Identify what type of credential data the malware targets (browser-saved passwords, memory-resident credentials, password manager vaults, etc.) and reclassify to the specific ITID if identified.
steps.outcome: Malware capability identified and incident tagged accordingly.

steps.title: Reset credentials likely exposed on the device
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for accounts known to have stored credentials or active sessions on the device.
steps.outcome: Potentially captured credentials invalidated.

ITID-12132.def: Malware that reads and decrypts browser-stored credentials from the local password store (e.g. Chrome's Login Data SQLite database and associated DPAPI-protected encryption keys).
ITID-12132.purpose: Captures malware specifically designed to extract passwords stored in a browser's built-in password manager (e.g. Chrome/Edge/Firefox saved logins).
scopeIncludes: Malware targeting browser Login Data database and decryption keys
Extraction of autofill-saved passwords from a browser profile
scopeExcludes: Extraction from a dedicated third-party password manager application/vault (ITID-12134)
ITID-12132.severity: High - browser-saved passwords frequently include both personal and corporate credentials.
ITID-12132.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if corporate SSO credentials are confirmed among those extracted.
ITID-12132.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR for full credential-reset scoping across every site with a saved password on the affected browser profile.
indicators: EDR alert on process accessing browser Login Data file and DPAPI key material
Unusual read access to browser profile directory by an unrelated process
vectors: Commodity infostealer malware delivered via phishing or trojanized download
rootCauses: Reliance on browser-saved passwords instead of a managed password manager with additional protections
Endpoint protection gap allowing initial infostealer execution
mitreTechniques: T1555.003 Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
controls: EDR behavioral detection of browser credential-store access
Enterprise policy disabling browser password saving in favor of a managed vault
ITID-12132.detection: EDR provides strong host-level detection of processes accessing the browser's credential database file and associated OS key-protection APIs (e.g. DPAPI on Windows).
ITID-12132.response: Isolate the endpoint, force reset of every credential saved in the affected browser profile, and remove the malware.
metrics: Count of browser-password-extraction incidents per quarter
Average number of credentials reset per incident
ITID-12132.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12134 by the credential store targeted: this leaf is the browser's own built-in store, not a dedicated third-party password manager vault.

playbook.name: Response: Browser-Saved Password Extraction Malware
playbook.description: For malware specifically designed to extract passwords saved in browser credential stores (e.g. Chrome/Edge/Firefox saved-password databases).

steps.title: Confirm the malware and its browser-targeting capability
steps.desc: Identify the malware family via EDR and confirm it targets browser credential stores specifically.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malware identity and capability.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the device from the network via EDR.
steps.outcome: Device isolated; further exfiltration stopped.

steps.title: Remove the malware
steps.desc: Remove the malware via EDR remediation, or reimage if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Migrate the user to a managed password manager
steps.desc: Recommend the user move away from browser-native password storage to a managed, encrypted password manager.
steps.outcome: User transitioned to a more secure credential storage method.

steps.title: Document scope and recommend browser password-storage policy
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend an organizational policy/technical control discouraging browser-native password storage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Enumerate saved passwords likely exposed
