steps.desc: Determine the hashing algorithm and whether salting/work-factor tuning was in use (e.g., bcrypt/argon2 vs. unsalted MD5/SHA1).
steps.guidance: This determines how urgently accounts must be reset before offline cracking becomes practical.
steps.outcome: Understood cracking difficulty and urgency.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and contain the source of the hash exposure
steps.desc: Terminate active sessions for affected accounts and remediate the vulnerability or access path that allowed the hash dump to be exfiltrated in the first place.
steps.outcome: Sessions terminated; exfiltration path closed.

steps.title: Upgrade the hashing algorithm if found weak
steps.desc: If the exposed hashes used a weak or unsalted algorithm, migrate to a modern algorithm (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt) with appropriate work factor.
steps.outcome: Password storage upgraded to a strong, salted algorithm.

ITID-12313.def: Exhaustive password guessing performed directly against a live login endpoint, one interactive authentication attempt at a time, subject to whatever lockout or rate-limiting controls the endpoint enforces.
ITID-12313.purpose: Captures brute forcing performed online, interactively against a live authentication endpoint, where each guess is subject to potential lockout/rate-limiting detection.
scopeIncludes: Sequential/exhaustive guessing attempts against a single account's live login endpoint
scopeExcludes: Offline hash cracking with no live-endpoint interaction (ITID-12312)
Attempts using a curated wordlist rather than exhaustive sequential guessing (ITID-12321 series, Dictionary Attack)
ITID-12313.severity: Medium-High depending on whether lockout was triggered and whether MFA is present.
ITID-12313.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if lockout was not triggered or MFA is absent.
ITID-12313.escalation: Escalate to IAM if lockout policy failed to trigger as expected during the attack.
indicators: High volume of failed login attempts against a single account from a consistent source
Account lockout event triggered by rapid sequential guessing
vectors: Automated login-attempt tooling targeting a single account's live login form
rootCauses: Account lockout threshold set too high or not enforced
No rate limiting on the authentication endpoint
controls: Account lockout policy with appropriately tuned threshold
Progressive login-delay/rate limiting
ITID-12313.detection: Authentication logs provide direct, real-time technical signal via failed-login-count thresholds and lockout event correlation - a strong, concrete detection surface.
ITID-12313.response: Confirm lockout triggered as designed, investigate the source, and force reset if any successful login is found within the attempt sequence.
metrics: Count of online brute force incidents per quarter
Percentage where lockout triggered as designed
ITID-12313.notes: Differentiated from dictionary attack siblings by method: this leaf is exhaustive/sequential character-space guessing against a single account, not a curated-wordlist attempt.

playbook.name: Response: Online Interactive Brute Force
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary is submitting repeated login attempts directly against a live authentication endpoint (web login, VPN, RDP) in real time.

steps.title: Confirm the live attack is ongoing and quantify its rate
steps.desc: Pull the authentication log to confirm the attack is currently in progress and measure the attempt rate and target account(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed ongoing attack with rate and scope documented.

steps.title: Block the source IP(s) immediately
steps.desc: Block the attacking source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or WAF to stop the live attack.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic blocked.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm the login endpoint is protected against renewed attempts
steps.desc: Verify rate-limiting, CAPTCHA, or geo/IP-reputation filtering is active on the login endpoint going forward.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the endpoint is hardened against repeat attacks.

steps.title: Document the attack and recommend endpoint hardening
steps.desc: Record the attack pattern and recommend CAPTCHA, progressive delays, or IP-reputation filtering if not already in place.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any attempt has succeeded
steps.desc: Check whether any login attempt from the attacking source has succeeded.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack has resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Apply or verify account lockout/rate-limiting on the targeted account(s)
steps.desc: Ensure lockout or rate-limiting is actively applied to the targeted account(s) to stop further guessing even from new sources.
steps.outcome: Account protected against continued brute-force attempts.

steps.title: Force password reset for any account with a successful login
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12314.def: Offline password cracking performed using GPU-accelerated hardware or a distributed compute cluster, dramatically increasing the feasible keyspace and hash strength that can be attacked within a practical timeframe.
ITID-12314.purpose: Captures offline brute forcing performed at scale using GPU acceleration or a distributed cracking cluster, indicating a well-resourced attacker capable of cracking stronger hashes/longer passwords than a single commodity machine.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or attributed use of GPU/cluster cracking infrastructure against an exfiltrated hash set (e.g. via threat intelligence or cracked-password patterns exceeding single-machine feasibility)
scopeExcludes: Single-machine/CPU offline cracking (ITID-12312)
ITID-12314.severity: Critical - this level of resourcing indicates the attacker can feasibly crack even reasonably strong passwords and modern adaptive hashes.
ITID-12314.escalation: Escalate immediately; assume even complex passwords in the exfiltrated set are at meaningful risk and prioritize reset accordingly.
indicators: Cracked-password patterns recovered from threat intelligence exceeding what single-machine cracking could feasibly achieve within the observed timeframe
Attribution to a known threat actor group with documented cracking-cluster capability
vectors: Well-resourced criminal or state-sponsored actor operating dedicated GPU cracking infrastructure
rootCauses: Weak or insufficiently iterated hashing algorithm (e.g. unsalted MD5/SHA1) feasible even against high-end cracking hardware at scale
The underlying breach that exposed the hash set
controls: Strong adaptive/memory-hard hashing algorithm (Argon2/bcrypt/scrypt) resistant to GPU acceleration
Immediate mass credential reset upon confirmed hash exfiltration
ITID-12314.detection: As with all offline cracking, the process itself is not directly observable; detection relies on the upstream exfiltration event and downstream threat intelligence on the attacker's capability and cracked outputs.
ITID-12314.response: Force reset for the entire exfiltrated account population immediately and prioritize migrating any weak hashing algorithm to a memory-hard alternative.
metrics: Time from exfiltration to full reset
Percentage of accounts on a memory-hard hashing algorithm
ITID-12314.notes: This leaf's severity is driven by attacker resourcing/capability rather than a distinct detectable technical signature versus ITID-12312; the differentiator is confirmed or inferred scale of compute used.

playbook.name: Response: GPU/Distributed Cracking Cluster Brute Force
playbook.description: For an attack using GPU-accelerated hardware or a distributed cracking cluster/cloud rental to brute force stolen password hashes at very high speed, materially reducing the time-to-crack for even moderately strong passwords.

steps.title: Confirm the hash exposure and assess cracking speed implications
steps.desc: Determine which accounts' hashes were exposed and assess, given the hashing algorithm and known GPU/cluster cracking speeds, how quickly even complex passwords could be recovered.
steps.guidance: High-end GPU clusters can crack unsalted fast hashes (MD5/SHA1) at billions of attempts/second — treat exposure as urgent regardless of password complexity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed hash exposure with an urgency assessment based on cracking speed.

steps.title: Force password reset for every account whose hash was exposed, immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password for every affected account without delay, given the accelerated cracking timeline.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts have rotated credentials.

steps.title: Audit for use of any already-cracked password against the live system
steps.desc: Check authentication logs for any login using a plaintext password matching a hash from the dump.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether any cracked password has been used.

steps.title: Restore access with new credentials and enforce MFA
steps.desc: Confirm affected users have completed password resets and enforce MFA on affected accounts.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts restored with new credentials and MFA enforced.

steps.title: Document the exposure and prioritize hashing algorithm remediation
steps.desc: Record the exposure and cracking-speed risk, and prioritize the hashing-algorithm upgrade as a systemic fix rather than a one-time reset.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with root cause remediated or tracked to closure.

steps.title: Determine indicators the attack is using accelerated/distributed cracking
steps.desc: Look for evidence such as extremely rapid successful logins following a breach, or threat intel/dark-web chatter referencing this specific dump.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or reasonably assessed use of accelerated cracking infrastructure.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and close the exfiltration path
steps.desc: Terminate active sessions for affected accounts and remediate the access path that allowed the hash dump to be exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Sessions terminated; exfiltration path closed.

steps.title: Upgrade the hashing algorithm and work factor
steps.desc: Migrate to a memory-hard algorithm (argon2/bcrypt/scrypt) with a work factor tuned to resist GPU/ASIC acceleration.
steps.guidance: Memory-hard algorithms specifically neutralize the GPU-parallelism advantage exploited by this attack type.
steps.outcome: Password storage upgraded to resist accelerated cracking.

ITID-12315.def: Offline or online brute forcing constrained to a specific character-mask pattern (e.g. known minimum length, required character classes, or a known prefix/suffix convention) derived from knowledge of the organization's password policy, dramatically narrowing the effective keyspace versus a fully exhaustive attack.
ITID-12315.purpose: Captures brute forcing that uses a mask/pattern-constrained keyspace (e.g. known password-length and character-class rules derived from policy or prior intelligence) rather than a fully exhaustive search, indicating targeted attacker knowledge of the password policy.
scopeIncludes: Cracking/guessing attempts constrained to a mask matching the organization's documented password complexity policy
Attempts incorporating a known corporate password prefix/suffix convention
scopeExcludes: Fully exhaustive, unconstrained brute forcing (ITID-12312, ITID-12313)
ITID-12315.severity: High - mask-based targeting indicates prior reconnaissance of the password policy, giving a materially higher success probability per attempt than exhaustive guessing.
ITID-12315.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any accounts are confirmed compromised.
ITID-12315.escalation: Escalate to IAM/security policy team to review whether the published or inferable password policy itself is aiding attacker targeting.
indicators: Cracked-password recovery pattern consistent with a specific length/character-class mask
Guessing pattern in online logs consistent with the organization's known complexity rules rather than random guessing
vectors: Attacker reconnaissance of the organization's published password policy (e.g. from a password-reset page's stated requirements)
rootCauses: Password complexity requirements publicly documented or inferable, narrowing the attacker's effective keyspace
Weak hashing algorithm making a mask-constrained offline attack feasible
controls: Avoid publicly documenting specific password complexity rules where feasible
Strong adaptive hashing algorithm reducing feasibility of mask-based offline attacks
ITID-12315.detection: For the online variant, authentication logs showing a guessing pattern consistent with a known policy mask provide a concrete, attributable signal; the offline variant shares the same limited-observability profile as other offline cracking leaves.
ITID-12315.response: Review whether policy-derived mask targeting succeeded, force reset for any confirmed compromise, and consider whether the password policy itself needs adjustment.
metrics: Count of mask-based targeted attacks per year
ITID-12315.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12312/12313 by the constrained, policy-informed keyspace rather than a fully exhaustive search.

playbook.name: Response: Mask-Based Targeted Brute Force
playbook.description: For an attack using a mask-based cracking approach — targeting a known or assumed password pattern (e.g., a specific length, known suffix, or company-naming convention) rather than exhaustive or dictionary-based guessing.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the pattern being targeted
steps.desc: Review the failed-login pattern or exposed hash-cracking evidence to identify the specific mask/pattern the attacker appears to be targeting (e.g., 'CompanyName+season+year').
steps.guidance: A mask-based attack often indicates the attacker has specific knowledge of the organization's password conventions — investigate how they obtained that knowledge.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the targeted pattern identified.

steps.title: Force password reset for accounts matching the targeted pattern
steps.desc: Identify and reset passwords for any account likely to follow the identified pattern, prioritizing those confirmed compromised.
steps.outcome: At-risk accounts have rotated credentials.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm affected accounts are using compliant passwords
steps.desc: Verify all affected accounts have reset passwords that comply with the updated policy.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compliant, non-pattern passwords in use.

steps.title: Document the pattern and investigate how it was learned
steps.desc: Record the specific pattern targeted and investigate whether it was learned from a prior breach, public information, or insider knowledge.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with the knowledge-source investigated.

steps.title: Determine whether any account matching the pattern was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any account using a password matching the identified pattern was successfully accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any successful access.

steps.title: Block the source of the attack
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Enforce a password policy that prohibits the identified pattern
steps.desc: Update the password policy/blocklist to reject passwords matching the identified organizational naming convention going forward.
steps.outcome: Password policy updated to close this specific pattern gap.

ITID-12316.def: Exhaustive or automated password-guessing attempts against an SSH server or comparable remote-administration protocol endpoint (e.g. Telnet, WinRM).
ITID-12316.purpose: Captures brute forcing directed at SSH or another remote-administration protocol, a very common internet-facing target with mature, well-understood telemetry.
scopeIncludes: Repeated failed SSH login attempts against a server from a consistent or scanning source
Automated SSH brute-forcing tooling (e.g. Hydra-class tools) detected against an internet-facing host
scopeExcludes: RDP-specific brute forcing, tracked under its own dedicated ITID family (ITID-43331 through ITID-43334) given RDP's distinct prevalence and risk profile
Telnet-specific default/weak credential exploitation, tracked under ITID-43731/43732 in the network-device context
ITID-12316.severity: High - successful SSH compromise typically grants direct shell access to the underlying system.
ITID-12316.priority: P1 if the SSH service is internet-facing without key-based authentication; P2 if internal-only.
ITID-12316.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure/security engineering to enforce key-based authentication and disable password authentication on SSH.
indicators: fail2ban or equivalent tooling logs high-volume failed SSH attempts from a source or range
SSH server logs showing password-authentication attempts against a service where key-based auth should be exclusive
vectors: Internet-wide scanning tools identifying open SSH port 22 and launching automated password-guessing
rootCauses: SSH configured to allow password authentication instead of key-based authentication exclusively
SSH service exposed directly to the internet without a bastion/jump-host restriction
controls: Key-based SSH authentication with password authentication disabled
fail2ban/intrusion-prevention on SSH with automatic source blocking
Restricting SSH access to a bastion host/VPN
ITID-12316.detection: SSH server authentication logs and intrusion-prevention tooling (fail2ban, EDR network module) provide mature, well-established, concrete technical telemetry for this exact attack pattern.
ITID-12316.response: Block the source, disable password authentication in favor of key-based auth, and audit for any successful login during the attack window.
metrics: Count of SSH brute force incidents per quarter
Percentage of SSH services with password auth disabled
ITID-12316.notes: RDP-specific brute forcing has its own dedicated Tier-4/5 family elsewhere in the taxonomy (ITID-43331 through ITID-43334) and is excluded here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: SSH/Remote Administration Protocol Brute Force
playbook.description: For a brute-force attack targeting SSH, RDP, or another remote administration protocol directly, typically against internet-facing infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the targeted host(s)
steps.desc: Pull authentication logs from the targeted server(s)/protocol to confirm the brute-force pattern and identify every host being targeted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with full list of targeted hosts.

steps.title: Block the source IP(s) at the network edge
steps.desc: Block the attacking source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic blocked.

steps.title: Audit the compromised host for persistence
steps.desc: If a login succeeded, check the host for new users, SSH authorized_keys entries, cron jobs, or other persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence on the host.

steps.title: Confirm the host is clean and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm the host passes a clean-state check and restore normal remote administration access under the hardened configuration.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean and operating normally.

steps.title: Document the attack and recommend broader exposure remediation
steps.desc: Record the attack and, if other hosts share the same direct-internet-exposure pattern, open a remediation ticket to address them as well.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a fleet-wide remediation ticket if applicable.

steps.title: Determine whether any login succeeded
steps.desc: Check whether any attempt against the targeted host(s) resulted in a successful login.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Restrict remote administration access to a bastion/VPN if exposed directly to the internet
steps.desc: If the protocol is directly internet-facing, restrict it behind a bastion host or VPN and disable direct exposure.
steps.guidance: Direct internet exposure of SSH/RDP is itself a significant risk factor that should be corrected regardless of this specific incident.
steps.outcome: Remote administration access no longer directly internet-facing.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence and harden authentication
steps.desc: Remove any rogue account or key, and migrate to key-based authentication with password auth disabled if not already enforced.
steps.outcome: No attacker persistence remains; authentication hardened.

steps.title: Force password/key rotation for any account with a successful login
steps.desc: Rotate the password or SSH key and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12317.def: Exhaustive or automated password/API-key guessing attempts made directly against a backend API authentication endpoint.
ITID-12317.purpose: Captures brute forcing directed at an API authentication endpoint rather than a standard interactive login form.
scopeIncludes: Automated tooling submitting sequential/exhaustive authentication attempts directly to an API endpoint
scopeExcludes: Credential-stuffing-style attempts using known valid pairs against an API (ITID-12215, a distinct credential-stuffing technique rather than exhaustive guessing)
ITID-12317.severity: High - API endpoints frequently have weaker rate-limiting/lockout coverage than standard web login forms.
ITID-12317.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any account/API key is confirmed compromised.
ITID-12317.escalation: Escalate to API security/engineering to extend rate limiting and lockout policy to the affected endpoint.
indicators: Spike in failed authentication API calls from a consistent source with sequential/exhaustive guessing pattern
vectors: Automated tooling calling the authentication API endpoint directly
rootCauses: API authentication endpoint not covered by the same rate-limiting/lockout policy as the primary web login
controls: API gateway rate limiting and lockout policy parity with the web login form
ITID-12317.detection: API gateway logs provide concrete technical telemetry once instrumented to the same standard as the primary login form.
ITID-12317.response: Extend rate-limiting/lockout coverage to the API endpoint, block the identified source, and audit for successful authentications.
metrics: Count of API brute force incidents per quarter
ITID-12317.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12215 (API/Mobile Endpoint Credential Stuffing) by method: this leaf is exhaustive/sequential guessing, not use of known valid credential pairs.

playbook.name: Response: API Authentication Brute Force
playbook.description: For a brute-force attack targeting an API's authentication endpoint (API keys, OAuth client credentials, or token-based login), typically automated at high volume against a programmatic interface rather than a UI login form.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the targeted API endpoint
steps.desc: Pull API gateway/access logs to confirm the brute-force pattern and identify the specific endpoint and credential type targeted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with endpoint and credential type documented.

steps.title: Block the source and apply/verify API rate-limiting
steps.desc: Block the attacking source IP(s) at the API gateway/WAF and confirm rate-limiting is applied to the authentication endpoint.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; rate-limiting confirmed active.

steps.title: Audit for unauthorized API usage following the successful attempt
steps.desc: If a credential was compromised, review the API access log for calls made with it, looking for data access or state changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any unauthorized API activity.

steps.title: Restore normal API access under hardened credentials
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate integration/consumer has a working, rotated credential and normal API access is restored.
steps.outcome: Legitimate API access restored on rotated credentials.

steps.title: Document the attack and recommend stronger API authentication
steps.desc: Record the attack and recommend mutual TLS, OAuth with short-lived tokens, or stricter rate-limiting if the current authentication scheme proved too weak.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any credential was successfully validated
steps.desc: Check whether any attempt resulted in a valid API key/token being issued or accepted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized API access.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate any compromised API key/credential
steps.desc: Rotate the affected API key or client credential for any account/integration where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential rotated and old value invalidated.

steps.title: Remediate any unauthorized change made via the API
steps.desc: Reverse or remediate any data change made through unauthorized API calls.
steps.outcome: System state restored to pre-incident condition.

ITID-12318.def: Exhaustive guessing of a short numeric PIN code, exploiting the dramatically smaller keyspace compared to an alphanumeric password.
ITID-12318.purpose: Captures brute forcing of a short numeric PIN (e.g. device unlock PIN, banking PIN, voicemail PIN), a small keyspace attack distinct from full alphanumeric password brute forcing.
scopeIncludes: Brute forcing of a device unlock PIN
Brute forcing of a voicemail, banking, or account-recovery numeric PIN
scopeExcludes: WPS PIN brute forcing specifically, tracked under its own dedicated leaf (ITID-42122) given its distinct Wi-Fi-protocol-specific mechanism
ITID-12318.severity: High - the small keyspace of a numeric PIN makes exhaustive success highly likely absent a lockout control.
ITID-12318.priority: P1 if no lockout/rate-limiting exists on the PIN entry point; P2 if a lockout control is present.
ITID-12318.escalation: Escalate to the system owner to confirm/implement lockout after a small number of failed PIN attempts.
indicators: Rapid sequential PIN attempts against a device or account recovery flow
Lockout event triggered by exhaustive PIN guessing
vectors: Automated or manual sequential PIN guessing against a device unlock screen or IVR/voicemail system
rootCauses: No or insufficiently strict lockout policy on PIN-based authentication given its inherently small keyspace
controls: Strict lockout after a small number of failed PIN attempts (e.g. 3-5)
Progressive time-delay between PIN attempts
ITID-12318.detection: Device/system authentication logs and lockout event logs provide direct, concrete technical signal for this exact pattern.
ITID-12318.response: Confirm lockout triggered as designed, and force reset/reconfiguration of the PIN if any successful guess is suspected.
metrics: Count of PIN brute force incidents per quarter
Percentage of PIN-protected systems with lockout enforced
ITID-12318.notes: Wi-Fi WPS PIN brute forcing is a distinct, dedicated leaf (ITID-42122) and is excluded here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: PIN/Short-Numeric Brute Force
playbook.description: For a brute-force attack targeting a short numeric PIN (e.g., a 4-6 digit device unlock code, phone banking PIN, or physical access code), where the small keyspace makes exhaustive guessing practical.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the PIN-protected system targeted
steps.desc: Confirm the pattern of repeated PIN attempts and identify exactly which system/device/account the PIN protects.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the protected system identified.

steps.title: Lock the account/device and block the source if remote
steps.desc: Trigger a lockout on the PIN-protected system and, if the attack is remote, block the source IP.
steps.outcome: Further PIN attempts blocked.

steps.title: Audit for unauthorized activity if access was gained
steps.desc: If the PIN was successfully guessed, review what was accessed or changed using it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any unauthorized activity.

steps.title: Confirm normal access is restored under the new PIN
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate user/system has working access with the rotated PIN.
steps.outcome: Access restored under the new PIN.

steps.title: Document the attack and evaluate whether a longer credential is warranted
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether this system should move to a longer PIN, password, or additional factor given the demonstrated brute-forceability of a short numeric code.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the PIN was successfully guessed
steps.desc: Check whether any attempt resulted in successful access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Reset the PIN if compromised or as a precaution
steps.desc: Issue a new PIN, especially if the attempt succeeded or the small keyspace makes eventual success likely.
steps.outcome: PIN rotated to a new value.

steps.title: Enforce lockout-after-N-attempts if not already in place
steps.desc: Confirm or configure an attempt-count lockout policy on the PIN system, given the inherently small keyspace makes rate-limiting essential.
steps.guidance: A 4-digit PIN has only 10,000 possible values — lockout after a small number of attempts is the primary practical defense.
steps.outcome: Lockout policy confirmed or newly enforced.

ITID-12319.def: A brute force incident (any of ITID-12312 through ITID-12318) in which the guessing attack succeeded and access to the target account or system is confirmed.
ITID-12319.purpose: Captures confirmed successful brute force attack resulting in account/system access, distinguishing outcome-confirmed compromise from mere attack attempts for severity/priority purposes.
scopeIncludes: Any brute force method variant where a successful authentication and subsequent access is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Brute force attempts blocked, locked out, or otherwise unsuccessful (the specific method-based sibling leaves)
ITID-12319.severity: Critical - confirmed access, markedly higher than any attempt-only sibling leaf.
ITID-12319.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC for session revocation, credential reset, and full access audit.
indicators: Successful authentication following a confirmed brute force attempt pattern, followed by observed account/system activity
vectors: Any brute force vector where the guessed value happened to be correct and unprotected by MFA or lockout
rootCauses: No MFA on the affected account
Weak password or PIN chosen, or lockout policy failure
controls: MFA enforcement on all accounts
Forced password reset and session revocation workflow
ITID-12319.detection: Authentication success logs correlated with a preceding failed-attempt pattern, combined with post-login activity monitoring, provide a strong technical confirmation trail.
ITID-12319.response: Revoke sessions, force password/PIN reset, and conduct a full audit of actions taken during the compromise window.
metrics: Count of confirmed brute force compromises per quarter
Mean time to detection and containment
ITID-12319.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation applicable across any brute force method sibling leaf; it does not restate the method-specific scoping of ITID-12312 through ITID-12318.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Brute Force with Confirmed Access
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where a brute-force attack (of any technique) resulted in verified unauthorized access — the high-severity, post-compromise variant requiring full account/system-takeover response.

steps.title: Confirm and scope the successful access
steps.desc: Establish, from logs, that the brute-force attack succeeded, and determine the technique, account/system affected, and access timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed successful access with technique and timeline documented.

steps.title: Force credential reset and revoke sessions/tokens
steps.desc: Reset the compromised credential and invalidate all active sessions and tokens.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Remove all attacker persistence across affected accounts/systems
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, keys, accounts, or backdoors found across the full scope.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Restore access and validate with the user/owner
steps.desc: Restore access for all affected accounts/systems and confirm with the owner that access and data look correct.
steps.outcome: Verified-clean access restored.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full timeline, blast radius, and required control changes; report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine full extent of attacker activity post-access
steps.desc: Review all activity performed by the attacker during their access window: data accessed, files touched, systems reached, configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Complete activity timeline for the compromised access.

steps.title: Contain any downstream systems or accounts affected
steps.desc: Apply containment (credential reset, session revocation, isolation) to any secondary account or system identified in the blast-radius assessment.
steps.outcome: Blast radius fully contained.

steps.title: Close the underlying weakness that allowed the brute force to succeed
steps.desc: Enforce lockout/rate-limiting, MFA, or stronger credential requirements on the affected system.
steps.outcome: Underlying weakness remediated.

steps.title: Extended monitoring of all affected accounts/systems
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts/systems under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Assess blast radius to other accounts and systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker used this access to pivot to other accounts, shared resources, or connected systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact beyond the initial account/system.

ITID-12321.def: Password-guessing attempts using a curated wordlist of likely candidate passwords (as opposed to exhaustive brute forcing or precomputed rainbow tables), where the specific wordlist type (common list, org-specific, rule-based mutation, language-specific, hybrid, leaked list, trivial pattern) has not yet been identified.
ITID-12321.purpose: Catch-all for dictionary attack incidents where the specific wordlist type or method has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific wordlist type is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the wordlist type is known and matches ITID-12322 through ITID-12328
Exhaustive character-space brute forcing (ITID-12311 series)
ITID-12321.escalation: Reclassify once the specific wordlist/method is confirmed.
indicators: Guessing pattern consistent with a curated wordlist rather than exhaustive/sequential characters, of unclear specific list
vectors: Unclear/unconfirmed at time of initial detection
rootCauses: Insufficient triage detail captured at time of detection
controls: Banned-password-list enforcement
ITID-12321.detection: Authentication/cracking-attempt logs showing a wordlist-pattern give the same core signal as the specific sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12321.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific sibling leaf once the wordlist type is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12321.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification within Dictionary Attack, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: Baseline response for a detection or report of a password-guessing attack using a wordlist of likely candidate passwords rather than exhaustive brute force, where the specific wordlist type has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the dictionary-attack pattern from authentication logs
steps.desc: Pull the authentication log for the targeted account/system and confirm a pattern of failed attempts consistent with wordlist-based guessing (varied but recognizable words rather than sequential/random strings).
steps.outcome: Confirmed dictionary-attack pattern with supporting log evidence.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm a dictionary-resistant password policy is enforced
steps.desc: Verify the affected system rejects passwords found in common wordlists (a compromised-password check/blocklist).
steps.outcome: Confirmed dictionary/blocklist check is in place.

steps.title: Document the attack and recommend control improvements
steps.desc: Record the pattern observed and recommend a compromised-password blocklist or rate-limiting improvements if gaps were found.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine the wordlist type and source if identifiable
steps.desc: Classify whether the wordlist is a common-password list, org/industry-specific wordlist, rule-mutated, language-specific, hybrid, or a leaked-password list, and whether any account was compromised.
steps.guidance: Reclassify to the more specific ITID playbook once known and continue from there if one exists.
steps.outcome: Attack correctly classified by wordlist type.

steps.title: Force password reset on any account with a successful login
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where a dictionary-attack attempt succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.
steps.abort: If no account was successfully accessed, this step is not required.

steps.title: Determine whether any attempt succeeded
steps.desc: Check whether any of the dictionary-attack attempts resulted in a successful authentication.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

ITID-12322.def: Password-guessing attempts using a generic, publicly available list of the most common passwords, with no organization-specific or leaked-data targeting.
ITID-12322.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks using a generic, widely available common-password list (e.g. rockyou.txt-class lists).
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern matching a well-known generic common-password list
scopeExcludes: Organization/industry-specific wordlist attacks (ITID-12323)
Leaked-password-list attacks derived from an actual breach dataset (ITID-12327)
ITID-12322.severity: Medium - generic lists are the least targeted and typically have the lowest hit rate against a policy-enforced environment.
ITID-12322.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if any accounts are confirmed compromised (indicating weak password policy enforcement).
ITID-12322.escalation: Escalate to IAM if any hit is confirmed, since a generic common-password list hit indicates a significant password policy gap.
indicators: Attempted passwords matching entries from a well-known generic common-password list
vectors: Automated tooling loaded with a standard, publicly available common-password wordlist
rootCauses: Password policy not enforcing a banned-password-list check against common password compilations
controls: Banned-password-list check at password creation/reset time
ITID-12322.detection: Authentication logs showing common-list password attempts across accounts provide a clear, attributable technical signal.
ITID-12322.response: Block the source, force reset for any matching accounts, and confirm banned-password-list enforcement is active.
metrics: Count of common-list dictionary attack incidents per quarter
Percentage of accounts confirmed vulnerable to a common-list password
ITID-12322.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12323 by generality: this leaf covers non-targeted, publicly common passwords rather than organization-specific terminology.

playbook.name: Response: Common Password List Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack using a well-known list of the most common passwords globally (e.g., 'password123', 'qwerty', '123456') against a login endpoint.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify affected accounts
steps.desc: Pull the authentication log to confirm the pattern and identify which account(s) were targeted with common-password guesses.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with target account(s) identified.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Run a proactive audit for other accounts using common passwords
steps.desc: Run a compromised/common-password check against the full user base to proactively identify and force resets on other weak accounts before they're targeted.
steps.outcome: Other weak-password accounts identified and remediated proactively.

steps.title: Document the attack and enforce a minimum password complexity/blocklist policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and confirm or implement a policy rejecting top-common-password list entries at password creation/change time.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any account had a weak/common password matched
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account's actual password matched a common-list entry and was successfully accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12323.def: Password-guessing attempts using a custom wordlist built from organization-specific or industry-specific terminology (company name, products, jargon), indicating prior reconnaissance.
ITID-12323.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks using a wordlist curated from organization- or industry-specific terminology, indicating targeted reconnaissance.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern incorporating company name, branded products, or industry-specific terms
scopeExcludes: Generic common-password list attacks with no targeting (ITID-12322)

The equivalent targeted wordlist used specifically in a password spraying pattern (ITID-12227), a distinct many-usernames/few-passwords technique rather than dictionary cracking of a single account/hash
ITID-12323.severity: High - the targeted wordlist indicates prior reconnaissance and a materially higher hit rate.
ITID-12323.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any accounts are confirmed compromised.
ITID-12323.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence to assess likely reconnaissance/OSINT sources used to build the wordlist.
indicators: Attempted passwords incorporating company name, product names, or industry jargon
vectors: Manually curated or OSINT-derived organization-specific wordlist
rootCauses: Banned-password-list policy not extended to organization/industry-specific terms
controls: Organization-specific banned-password-list enforcement
ITID-12323.detection: Authentication/cracking-attempt logs showing organization-specific term patterns provide a clear, attributable technical signal.
ITID-12323.response: Block the source, extend the banned-password list, and force reset for matching accounts.
metrics: Count of org-specific dictionary attack incidents per quarter
ITID-12323.notes: Distinguished from ITID-12227 (the spraying-context equivalent) by the attack shape: this leaf is a single-account/hash dictionary attack, while ITID-12227 is a many-usernames/few-passwords spraying pattern; both may use similar wordlists without duplicating each other's classification.

playbook.name: Response: Organization/Industry-Specific Wordlist Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack using a wordlist custom-built around the target organization's name, products, terminology, or industry jargon, indicating deliberate reconnaissance rather than a generic list.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the organization-specific terms used
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern for evidence of organization-specific terms (company name, product names, internal jargon) being guessed.
steps.guidance: This is a strong signal of targeted reconnaissance against the organization specifically, not an opportunistic scan.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the specific org-related terms identified.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm affected accounts are compliant with the updated policy
steps.desc: Verify affected accounts have passwords that no longer contain the blocklisted terms.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compliant passwords in use.

steps.title: Document the targeted reconnaissance and consider broader threat assessment
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether the targeted nature of the wordlist suggests a more determined adversary warranting broader monitoring.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a threat-level assessment.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed using an organization-specific guess.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

steps.title: Blocklist the identified organization-specific terms in the password policy
steps.desc: Add the company name, product names, and identified jargon to the password blocklist so they cannot be chosen as passwords going forward.
steps.outcome: Password policy updated to reject the identified organization-specific terms.

ITID-12324.def: Password-guessing attempts using a wordlist processed through mutation/mangling rules (e.g. hashcat-style rule sets) that systematically apply common substitutions and appendages to base dictionary words to match typical complexity-policy patterns.
ITID-12324.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks that apply mutation rules (e.g. leetspeak substitution, appended digits/symbols, capitalization variants) to a base wordlist, expanding coverage against policy-driven complexity requirements.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern consistent with base-word-plus-mutation-rule application (e.g. 'password' to 'P@ssw0rd123!')
scopeExcludes: Unmutated dictionary word attempts (ITID-12322, ITID-12323)
Fully exhaustive brute forcing with no dictionary base (ITID-12311 series)
ITID-12324.severity: High - mutation rules specifically target the exact patterns users adopt to satisfy complexity policies, giving a high hit rate.
ITID-12324.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any accounts are confirmed compromised.
ITID-12324.escalation: Escalate to IAM/security policy team to evaluate password policy design, since complexity requirements alone are known to drive predictable mutation patterns.
indicators: Cracked or attempted passwords showing a recognizable base word with systematic substitution/appendage patterns
vectors: Automated cracking tooling applying standard mutation rule sets to a base dictionary
rootCauses: Password complexity policy driving predictable user mutation patterns (e.g. capital first letter, digit and symbol appended) without banned-pattern enforcement
controls: Banned-password-list enforcement that also screens common mutation patterns of banned base words
Move toward passphrase-based policy less susceptible to predictable mutation
ITID-12324.detection: For online attempts, authentication logs show the mutated-pattern guesses; for offline cracking, this shares the limited-observability profile of other offline cracking leaves, detected primarily via the upstream hash exfiltration.
ITID-12324.response: Force reset for confirmed matches, and consider policy changes reducing susceptibility to predictable mutation.
metrics: Count of rule-based mutation dictionary attack incidents per year
ITID-12324.notes: This leaf frequently surfaces a password-policy design weakness (complexity rules driving predictable mutations); remediation should be evaluated at the policy level.

playbook.name: Response: Rule-Based/Mutation Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack applying systematic mutation rules (character substitution like o→0, appended digits/symbols, capitalization changes) to a base wordlist, significantly expanding effective coverage beyond the base list.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the mutation patterns used
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern for evidence of systematic mutations (leetspeak substitutions, appended years/symbols) applied to recognizable base words.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with mutation pattern documented.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm the password policy resists simple character substitution
steps.desc: Verify the password-strength check normalizes common substitutions (e.g., treats 'P@ssw0rd' as equivalent to 'Password') when checking against blocklists.
steps.guidance: Many naive password-strength checks are fooled by simple leetspeak substitution — confirm this system's check is not.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the policy correctly resists mutation-based bypass of the blocklist.

steps.title: Document the mutation technique and recommend policy hardening
steps.desc: Record the specific mutation rules observed and recommend upgrading the password-strength checker if it does not normalize substitutions.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed via a mutated guess.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12325.def: Password-guessing attempts using a dictionary wordlist derived from a specific non-primary language, indicating either targeting of a specific regional user population or an attacker of a particular linguistic background.
ITID-12325.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks using a wordlist in a language other than the organization's primary operating language, relevant for multinational organizations or region-specific targeting.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern using words/phrases from a specific non-English or non-primary-operating-language dictionary relevant to the organization's regional footprint
scopeExcludes: Primary-language generic common-password attacks (ITID-12322)
ITID-12325.severity: Medium-High depending on whether the targeted regional user population is confirmed.
ITID-12325.priority: P2 if a specific regional office/user population is confirmed targeted.
ITID-12325.escalation: Escalate to the regional IT/security contact for the affected office/user population.
indicators: Attempted passwords consistent with a specific non-primary-language dictionary
Attack pattern correlated with accounts belonging to a specific regional office
vectors: Automated tooling loaded with a language-specific wordlist targeting a regional user population
rootCauses: Banned-password-list enforcement not extended to cover common password terms in all languages relevant to the organization's regional footprint
controls: Multi-language banned-password-list enforcement covering all regions of operation
ITID-12325.detection: Authentication logs showing language-specific term patterns, correlated with the targeted regional account population, provide a workable technical signal.
ITID-12325.response: Force reset for matching accounts and extend the banned-password list to cover the identified language.
metrics: Count of language-specific dictionary attack incidents per year
sops: Multi-Language Banned Password List Update SOP
ITID-12325.notes: Relevant primarily for multinational organizations; smaller single-region organizations may see limited incidence of this leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Language-Specific Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack using a wordlist built from a specific non-English language or region-specific vocabulary, suggesting the attacker has intelligence about the target population's likely language of password choice.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the language/region of the wordlist
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern for evidence of a specific non-English or regional wordlist being used.
steps.guidance: This can indicate the attacker specifically knows the target population's primary language, which may narrow the likely source of reconnaissance (e.g., a regional office's user list).
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the wordlist's language/region identified.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm the password blocklist covers the identified language's common terms
steps.desc: Verify the compromised-password/blocklist check includes common passwords in the identified language, not just English.
steps.outcome: Confirmed multi-language blocklist coverage.

steps.title: Document the attack and assess targeting rationale
steps.desc: Record the language/region observed and consider whether it indicates the specific business unit or region being targeted, informing broader monitoring.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a targeting assessment.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12326.def: Password-guessing attempts that combine a curated dictionary word/phrase base with an exhaustively brute-forced suffix or prefix (e.g. dictionary word plus an exhaustively tried 2-4 digit number), blending both technique families.
ITID-12326.purpose: Captures a hybrid attack combining a dictionary base with exhaustive brute-force character appendage, a common and effective real-world cracking strategy.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern showing a recognizable dictionary base combined with an exhaustively-varied numeric/character suffix
scopeExcludes: Pure dictionary attacks with a fixed mutation rule rather than an exhaustive appended range (ITID-12324)
Pure exhaustive brute forcing with no dictionary base (ITID-12311 series)
ITID-12326.severity: High - this hybrid approach is one of the most efficient and widely used real-world cracking strategies, giving it a high effective hit rate.
ITID-12326.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any accounts are confirmed compromised.
ITID-12326.escalation: Escalate to IAM/security policy team; this pattern effectively defeats simple 'word plus number' password conventions.
indicators: Cracked or attempted passwords showing a dictionary base with an exhaustively varied numeric suffix (e.g. testing every 4-digit combination after a base word)
vectors: Cracking tooling configured for combined dictionary-plus-brute-force ('hybrid') mode
rootCauses: Password policy allowing simple 'word plus short number' constructions to satisfy complexity requirements
controls: Passphrase-based policy or minimum-entropy scoring rather than simple complexity-class counting
ITID-12326.detection: Shares the online/offline detection profile of its component techniques: authentication logs for online attempts, upstream hash-exfiltration monitoring for offline cracking.
ITID-12326.response: Force reset for confirmed matches and evaluate moving to entropy-based password strength scoring.
metrics: Count of hybrid dictionary-brute-force incidents per year
ITID-12326.notes: This is the one dictionary-attack sibling explicitly blending both parent technique families; log it here rather than splitting across both Brute Force and Dictionary Attack types.

playbook.name: Response: Hybrid Dictionary + Brute Force Attack
playbook.description: For an attack combining dictionary-based word guessing with brute-force character appending/prepending (e.g., word + 2-4 digit brute-forced suffix), a common technique for defeating 'word plus number' password conventions.

steps.title: Confirm the hybrid pattern from the attempt log
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern for evidence of a base word combined with systematically varied appended/prepended characters.
steps.outcome: Confirmed hybrid attack pattern documented.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm rate-limiting is tuned to defeat hybrid attempt volume
steps.desc: Verify the lockout/rate-limiting threshold is low enough to stop a hybrid attack's larger effective guess space before completion.
steps.guidance: Hybrid attacks generate far more candidate guesses than a plain dictionary attack — confirm the lockout threshold accounts for this.
steps.outcome: Confirmed rate-limiting is effective against the larger hybrid guess space.

steps.title: Document the attack and reinforce guidance against 'word+number' passwords
steps.desc: Record the technique observed and issue awareness guidance discouraging predictable word-plus-number password patterns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12327.def: Password-guessing attempts using a wordlist compiled from an actual, identifiable leaked or breached password dataset (as opposed to a generic synthetic common-password compilation).
ITID-12327.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks using a wordlist derived directly from an actual leaked/breached password dataset, distinguishing real-world-sourced lists from generic or synthetic ones.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern matching a specific, identified leaked password dataset via threat intelligence
scopeExcludes: Generic, non-attributable common-password list attacks (ITID-12322)

Credential stuffing using breach-sourced username/password pairs directly against live accounts (ITID-12212), which is the live-login-attempt use of a breach list rather than offline/dictionary cracking of a separately-held hash
ITID-12327.severity: High - real-world leaked passwords reflect actual human password-choice behavior and have a materially higher hit rate than synthetic lists.
ITID-12327.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if any accounts are confirmed compromised.
ITID-12327.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence to identify the source breach and cross-reference against the organization's own account population.
indicators: Threat intelligence match between attempted/cracked passwords and a known published breach dataset
vectors: Automated cracking/guessing tooling loaded with a specific leaked password dataset
rootCauses: Widespread reuse of passwords that have previously appeared in third-party breaches
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Real-time breach-password screening at password creation (checking against known-leaked-password databases)
ITID-12327.detection: Threat intelligence feeds combined with authentication/cracking-attempt log correlation give a strong, specific technical signal tying the attack to a known dataset.
ITID-12327.response: Force reset for confirmed matches and implement real-time leaked-password screening at password creation/reset.
metrics: Count of leaked-password-list dictionary attack incidents per quarter
ITID-12327.notes: Differentiated from ITID-12212 (Breach Combolist-Sourced Credential Stuffing) by attack shape: this leaf covers dictionary-style cracking/guessing using leaked passwords as a wordlist, not live-account credential-stuffing using matched username/password pairs.

playbook.name: Response: Leaked Password List Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack using a wordlist compiled from a known public breach/leak collection (e.g., a combolist or breach compilation), against accounts that may reuse a previously-breached password.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the source breach compilation if possible
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern and, if threat intel is available, identify which known breach compilation the wordlist likely originates from.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the likely source compilation identified where possible.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Enable ongoing breach-password screening at password-change time
steps.desc: Configure the identity provider to reject new passwords found in known breach compilations going forward, if not already enabled.
steps.outcome: Ongoing breach-password screening enabled.

steps.title: Document the attack and reinforce password-reuse awareness
steps.desc: Record the incident and issue awareness guidance on avoiding password reuse across personal and corporate accounts.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised via password reuse
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed, indicating the user reused a password from the breached source.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access via reuse.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

steps.title: Run a proactive breach-password screen against the full user base
steps.desc: Check all account passwords against known breach compilations (e.g., via a Have I Been Pwned-style API) and force resets on any match.
steps.outcome: All accounts with breached passwords identified and reset proactively.

ITID-12328.def: Password-guessing attempts using extremely common, trivially guessable patterns that require minimal or no reconnaissance and succeed purely due to weak password hygiene.
ITID-12328.purpose: Captures dictionary attacks using trivially guessable patterns (e.g. '123456', 'qwerty', 'password', sequential keyboard patterns), the lowest-sophistication end of the dictionary attack spectrum.
scopeIncludes: Guessing pattern using top-of-list trivial passwords (sequential numbers, keyboard-walk patterns, the word 'password' itself)
scopeExcludes: Curated but non-trivial common-password-list attacks (ITID-12322)
ITID-12328.severity: Low-Medium in terms of attacker sophistication, but High in terms of policy-failure implication if a hit occurs.
ITID-12328.priority: P3 for the attempt; escalate to P1 if any hit is confirmed, since a hit here indicates a fundamental password policy enforcement failure.
ITID-12328.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM if any hit is confirmed - this represents the most basic possible password policy failure and warrants urgent review.
indicators: Attempted passwords matching the very top of any common-password frequency list
vectors: Trivial, unsophisticated guessing requiring no attacker investment
rootCauses: Password complexity/strength policy not enforced or not enforced consistently across all systems
controls: Mandatory minimum password strength/banned-trivial-password enforcement on every authentication system
ITID-12328.detection: Authentication logs showing trivial-pattern password attempts provide a clear, attributable technical signal.
ITID-12328.response: Force reset for any confirmed hit immediately and audit password policy enforcement across all systems, especially any that may have gaps.
metrics: Count of trivial-pattern dictionary attack incidents per quarter
Percentage resulting in a confirmed hit
ITID-12328.notes: A confirmed hit on this leaf should always trigger a broader password-policy-enforcement audit, since it indicates the most basic possible control gap.

playbook.name: Response: Trivial Pattern Dictionary Attack
playbook.description: For an attack targeting trivially predictable keyboard-pattern or sequential passwords (e.g., 'qwerty', '123456789', 'asdfgh'), a subset distinct from named common-password lists in that the pattern is generated rather than looked up.

steps.title: Confirm the attack and identify the trivial pattern used
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern for keyboard-walk or sequential-character guesses.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack with the specific trivial pattern documented.

steps.title: Block the source of the attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s)/ASN at the firewall or authentication gateway.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Audit for persistence on any compromised account
steps.desc: If any account was accessed, check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Confirm keyboard-pattern/sequential passwords are rejected by policy
steps.desc: Verify the password-strength check specifically rejects keyboard-walk and sequential-character patterns, which basic length/complexity rules often miss.
steps.guidance: A password like 'Qwerty123!' can pass naive complexity rules (upper, lower, digit, symbol) while remaining trivially guessable.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the policy rejects trivial patterns beyond basic complexity rules.

steps.title: Document the attack and recommend policy hardening if gaps found
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend upgrading the password-strength checker if it does not catch trivial patterns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any account was compromised
steps.desc: Check whether any targeted account was successfully accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack resulted in unauthorized access.

steps.title: Force password reset on any compromised account
steps.desc: Reset the password and revoke sessions for any account where the attack succeeded.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated for compromised accounts.

ITID-12329.def: A dictionary attack incident (any of ITID-12322 through ITID-12328) in which the guessing attack succeeded and access to the target account or system is confirmed.
ITID-12329.purpose: Captures confirmed successful dictionary attack resulting in account/system access, distinguishing outcome-confirmed compromise from mere attack attempts for severity/priority purposes.
scopeIncludes: Any dictionary attack wordlist-type variant where a successful authentication and subsequent access is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Dictionary attack attempts blocked, locked out, or otherwise unsuccessful (the specific wordlist-type sibling leaves)
ITID-12329.severity: Critical - confirmed access, markedly higher than any attempt-only sibling leaf.
ITID-12329.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/SOC for session revocation, credential reset, and full access audit.
indicators: Successful authentication following a confirmed dictionary-attack pattern, followed by observed account/system activity
vectors: Any dictionary attack vector where the guessed password happened to be correct and unprotected by MFA or lockout
rootCauses: No MFA on the affected account
Weak or common password chosen by the account holder
controls: MFA enforcement on all accounts
Forced password reset and session revocation workflow
ITID-12329.detection: Authentication success logs correlated with a preceding dictionary-attack pattern, combined with post-login activity monitoring, provide a strong technical confirmation trail.
ITID-12329.response: Revoke sessions, force password reset, and conduct a full audit of actions taken during the compromise window.
metrics: Count of confirmed dictionary attack compromises per quarter
Mean time to detection and containment
ITID-12329.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation applicable across any dictionary attack wordlist-type sibling leaf; it does not restate the wordlist-specific scoping of ITID-12322 through ITID-12328.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Dictionary Attack with Confirmed Access
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where a dictionary attack (of any wordlist type) resulted in verified unauthorized access — the high-severity, post-compromise variant requiring full account/system-takeover response.

steps.title: Confirm and scope the successful access
steps.desc: Establish, from logs, that the dictionary attack succeeded, and determine the wordlist type, account/system affected, and access timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed successful access with technique and timeline documented.

steps.title: Force credential reset and revoke sessions/tokens
steps.desc: Reset the compromised credential and invalidate all active sessions and tokens.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Remove all attacker persistence across affected accounts/systems
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, keys, accounts, or backdoors found across the full scope.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Restore access and validate with the user/owner
steps.desc: Restore access for all affected accounts/systems and confirm with the owner that access and data look correct.
steps.outcome: Verified-clean access restored.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full timeline, blast radius, and required control changes; report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine full extent of attacker activity post-access
steps.desc: Review all activity performed by the attacker during their access window: data accessed, files touched, systems reached, configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Complete activity timeline for the compromised access.

steps.title: Contain any downstream systems or accounts affected
steps.desc: Apply containment (credential reset, session revocation, isolation) to any secondary account or system identified in the blast-radius assessment.
steps.outcome: Blast radius fully contained.

steps.title: Run a proactive breach/dictionary-password screen and close the policy gap
steps.desc: Screen the full user base for other accounts vulnerable to the same wordlist type, and close the password-policy gap that allowed the weak password.
steps.outcome: Other at-risk accounts remediated; policy gap closed.

steps.title: Extended monitoring of all affected accounts/systems
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts/systems under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Assess blast radius to other accounts and systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker used this access to pivot to other accounts, shared resources, or connected systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact beyond the initial account/system.

ITID-12331.def: Use of a precomputed hash-to-plaintext lookup table to recover a password from a stolen hash without live per-guess computation, where the specific method (unsalted hash, legacy algorithm, custom table, cloud lookup service, LM hash downgrade, exfiltrated database, unpatched legacy system) has not yet been identified.
ITID-12331.purpose: Catch-all for rainbow table attack incidents where the specific hash type or method has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific rainbow table method is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the method is known and matches ITID-12332 through ITID-12338
Live-guessing brute force or dictionary attacks against a hash rather than precomputed-table lookup (ITID-12311 series, ITID-12321 series)
Reuse of a stolen hash directly for authentication without ever recovering the plaintext (Pass-the-Hash, ITID-12721 series, a distinct technique in a different Tier-4 type)
ITID-12331.severity: Medium-High, pending reclassification, since rainbow table feasibility already implies a weak hashing scheme.
ITID-12331.escalation: Reclassify once the specific hash/method is confirmed via forensic analysis.
indicators: Confirmed hash exfiltration where the hashing scheme is known to be vulnerable to precomputed table lookups
vectors: Unclear/unconfirmed at time of initial detection
rootCauses: Insufficient triage detail captured at time of detection
controls: Salted, adaptive hashing algorithm eliminating rainbow table feasibility
ITID-12331.detection: Same limited-observability profile as other offline cracking techniques, detected primarily via the upstream hash exfiltration, pending finer classification.
ITID-12331.response: Investigate and reclassify once the specific hash type/method is confirmed; treat the exfiltrated hash population as at-risk regardless.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12331.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification within Rainbow Table Attack, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Rainbow Table Attack
playbook.description: Baseline response for a detection or report of a precomputed hash-lookup (rainbow table) attack against stolen password hashes, where the specific hash weakness or source has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the hash exposure that enables the attack
steps.desc: Determine how the password hash(es) were exposed and identify which accounts are affected.
steps.guidance: Rainbow table attacks require the attacker to already have the hash — the exposure event itself is the root incident to scope first.
steps.outcome: Confirmed hash exposure with full account scope.

steps.title: Force password reset for every account whose hash was exposed
steps.desc: Reset the password for every affected account, since unsalted/weak hashes should be treated as effectively already cracked.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts have rotated credentials.

steps.title: Audit for use of any recovered password against the live system
steps.desc: Check authentication logs for use of any password recovered from the hash dump.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any unauthorized access.

steps.title: Restore access with new credentials and enforce MFA
steps.desc: Confirm affected users have completed password resets and enforce MFA on affected accounts.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts restored with new credentials and MFA enforced.

steps.title: Document the exposure and confirm hashing remediation across the estate
steps.desc: Record how the hash dump was obtained and check whether other systems in the estate share the same weak-hashing weakness.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; estate-wide hashing audit initiated if warranted.

steps.title: Determine the specific weakness that makes rainbow tables effective here
steps.desc: Classify whether the hashes are unsalted, use a legacy/weak algorithm, involve LM hash downgrade, come from an unpatched legacy system, or were looked up via a cloud rainbow table service.
steps.guidance: Reclassify to the more specific ITID playbook once known and continue from there if one exists.
steps.outcome: Attack correctly classified by underlying weakness.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and close the exfiltration path
steps.desc: Terminate active sessions for affected accounts and remediate the access path that allowed the hash dump to be exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Sessions terminated; exfiltration path closed.

steps.title: Upgrade hashing to a salted, memory-hard algorithm
steps.desc: Migrate password storage to a salted, memory-hard algorithm (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt), which defeats precomputed rainbow tables entirely.
