steps.outcome: Break-glass account confirmed dormant and monitored.

steps.title: Address the process gap and reinforce break-glass policy
steps.desc: If the use was unjustified, address it through the appropriate coaching/disciplinary process and reinforce the break-glass usage policy and mandatory post-use review requirement organization-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy reinforcement communicated.

steps.title: Determine whether a genuine emergency justified the use
steps.desc: Interview the individual and check for a corresponding incident/outage record to confirm whether a genuine emergency existed.
steps.guidance: Break-glass accounts should only be used when standard privileged access is unavailable — assess against that standard specifically.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether use was justified by a genuine emergency.

steps.title: Reverse any action found outside the legitimate emergency scope
steps.desc: Reverse or remediate any change made that exceeded the legitimate emergency need.
steps.outcome: Environment restored to appropriate state.

ITID-12419.def: Use of administrative credentials and access rights to pivot from an initially accessed system to additional systems within the environment, as a distinct technique from single-system data access or control tampering.
ITID-12419.purpose: Captures use of an administrative credential specifically to move laterally between systems.
scopeIncludes: Use of admin credentials to authenticate to multiple additional hosts/systems in sequence
Use of admin rights to establish remote sessions (RDP, PsExec, WinRM, SSH) to other systems
scopeExcludes: Single-system unauthorized data access with no pivot to additional systems (see ITID-12414)
Initial compromise of the admin credential itself (see ITID-12412)
ITID-12419.severity: Critical — lateral movement is a strong indicator of active, expanding compromise.
ITID-12419.escalation: Immediate escalation to incident response; contain by isolating affected hosts and revoking the credential across all systems.
indicators: Sequential admin authentications to multiple hosts within a short time window
Use of remote-execution tools (PsExec, WMI, WinRM) under an admin identity across systems
Admin credential used to authenticate to systems the account holder does not normally access
vectors: Pass-the-hash or pass-the-ticket using a captured admin credential/hash
Attacker using RDP/WinRM with a compromised admin account to pivot
rootCauses: Flat network/identity architecture allowing broad admin credential reuse across systems
No tiered administration model (no separation between workstation, server, and domain admin tiers)
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
controls: Tiered administration model (Microsoft/CISA privileged access model)
Lateral-movement detection via EDR and identity telemetry
ITID-12419.detection: EDR lateral-movement detection and identity-provider sequential-authentication correlation provide a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12419.response: Isolate all touched hosts, revoke and rotate the credential everywhere it is valid, and hunt for persistence mechanisms deployed during the pivot.
metrics: Mean time to detect lateral movement using admin credentials
Count of hosts touched per lateral-movement incident
ITID-12419.notes: Scoped to the lateral-movement technique specifically; the initial credential compromise and any single-system data access are tracked in ITID-12412 and ITID-12414.

playbook.name: Response: Admin Credential Used for Lateral Movement
playbook.description: For a high-severity incident where a compromised or misused administrative credential was used to pivot from an initial system to additional systems or accounts within the environment.

steps.title: Confirm the lateral movement path and escalate severity immediately
steps.desc: Trace the sequence of systems/accounts accessed using the admin credential, and escalate severity given the active spread beyond the initial foothold.
steps.outcome: Confirmed lateral movement path with severity escalated per policy.
steps.tool: SIEM / EDR / privileged access audit log

steps.title: Suspend the admin credential and revoke all sessions/tokens
steps.desc: Disable the credential immediately and terminate every active session and token associated with it.
steps.outcome: Credential access halted across all systems it reached.

steps.title: Remove attacker persistence from every affected system
steps.desc: Remove any rogue account, scheduled task, backdoor, or other persistence mechanism found on each affected system.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on any affected system.

steps.title: Restore systems from clean state and validate integrity
steps.desc: Restore each affected system from a known-clean backup or fully remediate in place, and validate system integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed clean and restored to production.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full lateral-movement timeline, blast radius, and required control changes (network segmentation, credential tiering, PAM adoption); report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine the full extent of systems and accounts reached
steps.desc: Enumerate every system and account the attacker/misuser reached via the lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Complete map of systems/accounts reached.

steps.title: Isolate every system reached via lateral movement
steps.desc: Isolate each system identified in the lateral-movement map from the network pending forensic review.
steps.outcome: All reached systems isolated.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials touched during the lateral movement
steps.desc: Rotate every credential (service accounts, other admin accounts, local admin passwords) that was accessed or could have been harvested during the lateral movement.
steps.outcome: All potentially-exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Extended monitoring across the full affected scope
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts and systems under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Determine the origin point and root cause of the credential's initial compromise or misuse
steps.desc: Trace back to how the admin credential was originally obtained or misused before the lateral movement began.
steps.outcome: Confirmed origin point and root cause.

ITID-12421.def: An incident involving abuse of a non-human service account, not yet matched to a more specific exploitation pattern.
ITID-12421.purpose: Catch-all for exploitation of a service account that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific service-account exploitation pattern is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Service Account Exploitation
ITID-12421.escalation: Escalate to IAM/platform engineering once the specific exploitation pattern is identified; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Service-account activity flagged by SIEM correlation rule without a clear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector involving a service account
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Service account inventory and ownership review
Least-privilege enforcement for non-interactive accounts
Automated credential rotation for service accounts
Monitoring for service account interactive logon
ITID-12421.detection: Same identity/SIEM telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12421.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12421.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Service Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For suspected misuse of a service account where the specific mode of exploitation has not yet been narrowed to a more specific category.

steps.title: Confirm the account is a service account and gather its baseline profile
steps.desc: Pull the account's registered purpose, owning system/application, expected source hosts, and expected schedule from the service-account inventory or CMDB.
steps.guidance: If the account is not in the inventory, that gap is itself a finding to capture.
steps.outcome: Documented baseline of expected behavior for the account.

steps.title: Rotate the service account credential
steps.desc: Reset the password, API key, or secret and propagate the new credential to legitimate consumers only.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the application owner to avoid an outage from the rotation.
steps.outcome: Old credential invalidated; legitimate consumers updated.

steps.title: Search for and remove any attacker-added access or persistence
steps.desc: Check for newly created accounts, added permissions, scheduled tasks, or API keys created using the compromised credential.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence, or removal, of attacker-added persistence.

steps.title: Validate restored automation and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate process using the account is functioning with the new credential and monitor for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Automation confirmed healthy; heightened monitoring active.

steps.title: Document root cause and update the service account inventory
steps.desc: Record how the credential was exposed or misused and correct any inventory/baseline gaps found during the response.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and inventory corrected.

steps.title: Distinguish legitimate automation from abuse
steps.desc: Compare the activity that triggered the alert against the account's baseline: source host/IP, logon type, time of activity, and actions taken.
steps.guidance: Interactive logon, human-typical timing, or unfamiliar source systems are strong abuse indicators for a service account.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether activity is consistent with automation or indicates human/attacker use.
steps.abort: If activity fully matches documented automation, close as a false positive and update the baseline if it was stale.

steps.title: Scope down permissions to only what is required
steps.desc: Review the account's current permission grants and remove anything not required for its documented purpose.
steps.outcome: Account holds least-privilege access only.

steps.title: Scope the extent of use of the credential
steps.desc: Identify every system, resource, and time window the account was used in during the suspected abuse period.
steps.outcome: Timeline and scope of credential use established.

ITID-12422.def: Compromise or misuse of a service account where the scope of resulting impact is enabled specifically by excessive/over-provisioned permissions relative to the account's functional need.
ITID-12422.purpose: Captures exploitation of a service account whose assigned permissions exceed what its function requires.
scopeIncludes: Service account with domain admin or equivalent rights used for a narrow, low-privilege function
Compromise where post-incident review confirms the account's permission scope was materially broader than required
scopeExcludes: Exploitation where the account's permissions were already appropriately scoped (see other siblings)
Human admin credential misuse (tracked under Misused Admin Credentials)
ITID-12422.severity: High — excessive permissions typically translate directly into a larger blast radius.
ITID-12422.escalation: Escalate to IAM to right-size permissions immediately upon detection, in parallel with standard IR containment.
indicators: Service account authenticating to or acting on resources outside its documented function
Permission audit reveals scope far exceeding the account's application requirements
vectors: Attacker pivoting through a compromised low-value application using its over-privileged service account to reach high-value assets
rootCauses: Service accounts provisioned with broad/admin-equivalent rights for convenience during initial setup, never right-sized
No least-privilege review process for service account entitlements
controls: Least-privilege entitlement review for service accounts
Just-in-time / scoped privilege elevation for automated processes
ITID-12422.detection: IAM entitlement analytics and UEBA flag service accounts acting outside their documented resource scope — a real, concrete signal.
ITID-12422.response: Contain the compromise, then permanently right-size the account's permissions before restoring service.
metrics: Count of over-privileged service accounts remediated per quarter
ITID-12422.notes: Differentiator is the excessive-permission root cause specifically, as distinct from credential-hygiene issues covered in ITID-12423.

playbook.name: Response: Service Account with Excessive Permissions Exploited
playbook.description: For exploitation of a service account whose assigned permissions substantially exceed what its function requires, enabling broader impact.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation and enumerate all granted permissions
steps.desc: Pull the account's full current permission set across all systems, not just the one where activity was flagged.
steps.guidance: Excessive-permission accounts are frequently over-provisioned across multiple systems, not just the affected one.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of the account's permission footprint.

steps.title: Rotate the credential
steps.desc: Reset the account's password/secret immediately to stop further use.
steps.outcome: Credential invalidated.

steps.title: Review and reverse actions taken via the excess permissions
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any changes made using the over-provisioned access (e.g. new accounts, modified configurations, exfiltrated data).
steps.outcome: Unauthorized changes reversed or documented for further action.

steps.title: Validate application function under reduced permissions
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate application/process still operates correctly after permissions were scoped down.
steps.outcome: Application confirmed functional under least privilege.
steps.abort: If functionality breaks, restore only the specific permission required and document why.

steps.title: Document why the account was over-provisioned and recommend a periodic entitlement review
steps.desc: Record the root cause of the excess permissions and propose a recurring review process for service account entitlements.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process recommendation.

steps.title: Determine which permissions were actually used maliciously
steps.desc: Correlate the account's activity logs against its full permission set to identify which excess permissions the attacker exercised.
steps.outcome: List of abused permissions and resulting impact.

steps.title: Strip permissions down to documented minimum requirement
steps.desc: Remove every permission not directly required by the account's documented function, not just the ones abused.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the application owner to confirm what is truly required before removing access.
steps.outcome: Account reduced to least-privilege access.

ITID-12423.def: Compromise or misuse of a service account where a long-lived, never-rotated static credential (password, API key, certificate) is the contributing factor enabling the exploitation.
ITID-12423.purpose: Captures exploitation of a service account whose credential has never been rotated.
scopeIncludes: Service account credential confirmed unchanged since initial provisioning, used in a confirmed compromise
Static API key/secret with no expiry or rotation history exploited by an attacker
scopeExcludes: Exploitation enabled by excessive permission scope rather than credential age (see ITID-12422)
Credentials exposed publicly, which is tracked under Credential Leakage regardless of rotation history
ITID-12423.severity: High — a stale, long-lived credential is both easier to have been previously compromised and harder to invalidate quickly.
ITID-12423.escalation: Escalate to platform/security engineering to force immediate rotation and implement automated rotation going forward.
indicators: Secret-management audit shows credential age exceeding rotation policy
Compromised credential confirmed to be the account's original, never-rotated secret
vectors: Long-lived API key harvested from an old, forgotten configuration or backup and reused by an attacker years later
rootCauses: No automated secret-rotation policy or tooling for service account credentials
Application architecture hardcodes secrets rather than retrieving them from a vault
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Automated credential rotation via a secrets manager
Secret-age monitoring and alerting
ITID-12423.detection: Secrets-manager audit logs and credential-age monitoring provide a concrete, real technical signal.
ITID-12423.response: Rotate the credential immediately and migrate the account to a vault-managed, automatically rotated secret.
metrics: Percentage of service account credentials rotated within policy window
Count of stale-credential exploitations per quarter
ITID-12423.notes: Differentiator is credential age/rotation hygiene, distinct from permission scope (ITID-12422).

playbook.name: Response: Service Account with Never-Rotated Credential Exploited
playbook.description: For exploitation of a service account whose credential had never been rotated since creation, increasing the window of exposure.

steps.title: Confirm credential age and rotation history
steps.desc: Pull the credential's creation date and rotation history from the secrets manager or identity provider.
steps.outcome: Confirmed credential age and rotation gap.

steps.title: Rotate the credential immediately
steps.desc: Generate and deploy a new credential, invalidating the old one everywhere it was used.
steps.outcome: Old credential invalidated across all consumers.

steps.title: Review activity across the credential's entire lifetime for prior undetected abuse
steps.desc: Given the long exposure window, extend log review further back than a typical incident to check for earlier undetected misuse.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of abuse across the credential's full lifetime.

steps.title: Enroll the account in an automated rotation schedule
steps.desc: Configure automatic periodic rotation for the credential going forward.
steps.outcome: Automated rotation schedule active.

steps.title: Document root cause and identify other never-rotated accounts
steps.desc: Record the finding and search the service account inventory for other credentials with no rotation history.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; related at-risk accounts identified for remediation.

steps.title: Assess likely exposure sources given the credential's age
steps.desc: Check whether the credential appears in known breach data, code repositories, log files, or configuration backups accumulated over its lifetime.
steps.guidance: A long-lived credential has more opportunity to have leaked through historical artifacts than a recently rotated one.
steps.outcome: Identified or ruled-out exposure source(s).

steps.title: Purge the old credential from any location it was exposed in
steps.desc: Remove the credential from code repositories, config backups, log files, or other locations identified during scoping.
steps.outcome: Credential no longer present in exposed locations.

ITID-12424.def: A service account, which by design should authenticate only programmatically/non-interactively, observed performing an interactive human logon (console, RDP, SSH shell) — a strong indicator of compromise or of a control gap enabling misuse.
ITID-12424.purpose: Captures a service account being used for interactive human logon, which is itself an anomaly signal.
scopeIncludes: Service account used to log into a desktop/server console session
Service account used to establish an interactive RDP or SSH session
scopeExcludes: Legitimate non-interactive/programmatic authentication by the service account (not an incident)
Service account misuse that remains non-interactive, e.g. API abuse (see other siblings)
ITID-12424.severity: High — interactive use of a service account is rarely legitimate and is a strong compromise indicator.
ITID-12424.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response; treat as probable account compromise pending investigation.
indicators: Interactive logon event type (Type 2/10 Windows logon, or interactive SSH session) recorded against a designated service account
Service account authenticating from an endpoint rather than its expected application server
vectors: Attacker who has obtained a service account credential using it to gain an interactive foothold
Insider abusing a service account for manual, unauthorized administrative tasks
rootCauses: No group policy / conditional access restriction denying interactive logon rights to service accounts
Service account credential known and used informally by staff for convenience
controls: "Deny interactive logon" group policy applied to all service accounts
Conditional access blocking interactive session types for designated service identities
ITID-12424.detection: Windows logon-type / SSH session-type telemetry in SIEM provides an unambiguous, real technical signal for this specific pattern.
ITID-12424.response: Treat as a likely compromise: rotate the credential, review the interactive session's activity, and enforce the deny-interactive-logon control.
metrics: Count of interactive-logon-by-service-account events detected per quarter
ITID-12424.notes: Differentiator is the logon-type anomaly itself, a distinct and highly reliable technical signal from the other siblings in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: Interactive Logon by Service Account
playbook.description: For a service account, which should only authenticate programmatically, observed performing an interactive (human-style) logon.

steps.title: Confirm the logon type and session details
steps.desc: Pull the logon event details including logon type, source host, and session duration.
steps.guidance: Interactive logon (console, RDP, or terminal session) by a service account is a strong abuse indicator on its own.
steps.outcome: Confirmed interactive logon with source and session details.

steps.title: Terminate the active session and rotate the credential
steps.desc: Kill any live session using the account and reset its credential.
steps.outcome: Session terminated; credential rotated.

steps.title: Investigate the host used for the interactive logon
steps.desc: Determine whether the source host itself is compromised, since an attacker typically needs an initial foothold to perform an interactive logon.
steps.outcome: Source host assessed as clean or compromised.

steps.title: Validate legitimate automation still functions post-restriction
steps.desc: Confirm the account's normal programmatic use is unaffected by the interactive-logon restriction.
steps.outcome: Automation confirmed functional.

steps.title: Document root cause and add interactive-logon monitoring for service accounts
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend a standing detection rule alerting on interactive logons by any service account.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with detection recommendation.

steps.title: Identify what was done during the interactive session
steps.desc: Review commands executed, files accessed, and processes launched during the session.
steps.outcome: Documented record of session activity.

steps.title: Disable interactive logon capability for the account
steps.desc: Apply a technical control (e.g. deny-interactive-logon group policy, disable console access) to prevent future interactive use.
steps.outcome: Account technically restricted to non-interactive use.

ITID-12425.def: A service account observed authenticating from, or acting on behalf of, a host/system other than its documented, expected source system — indicating either credential theft or unauthorized reuse.
ITID-12425.purpose: Captures a service account authenticating from a source system other than the one it is expected to run on.
scopeIncludes: Service account credential used from a host outside its documented application server inventory
Service account authentication source IP/hostname mismatch against its established baseline
scopeExcludes: Interactive human logon by a service account (see ITID-12424, a distinct anomaly type)
Authentication from an approved, documented secondary/failover host (not an incident)
ITID-12425.severity: High — source mismatch strongly suggests credential theft and reuse.
ITID-12425.escalation: Escalate immediately for credential rotation and investigation of the unexpected source host.
indicators: UEBA baseline deviation alert for service-account source host/IP
Service account credential used from an internet-facing or unmanaged host
vectors: Credential theft from the legitimate application server, reused by an attacker from a different host
Lateral movement using a harvested service-account credential against other systems
rootCauses: No source-host allow-listing/conditional access binding the credential to its expected system
Weak network segmentation allowing the credential to be replayed from anywhere
mitreTechniques: T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
controls: Source-host/IP allow-listing for service account authentication
UEBA baselining of service-account source telemetry
ITID-12425.detection: UEBA source-baseline deviation alerting provides a concrete, real technical signal specific to this pattern.
ITID-12425.response: Rotate the credential immediately, restrict authentication to the approved source host(s), and investigate the unexpected host for compromise.
metrics: Count of source-mismatch service-account authentications detected per quarter
ITID-12425.notes: Differentiator is authentication-source anomaly, distinct from the interactive-logon-type anomaly in ITID-12424.

playbook.name: Response: Service Account Used Outside Its Expected Source System
playbook.description: For a service account observed authenticating from a host or system other than its documented expected source.

steps.title: Confirm the account's documented expected source system(s)
steps.desc: Pull the account's registered expected source host(s)/IP range(s) from the service account inventory.
steps.outcome: Confirmed expected source baseline.

steps.title: Rotate the credential
steps.desc: Reset the account's password/secret to invalidate any copy in use on the unexpected source.
steps.outcome: Credential invalidated.

steps.title: Investigate the unexpected source system for compromise
steps.desc: Determine how the credential came to be used from that system and whether the system itself is compromised.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the mismatch determined; source system assessed.

steps.title: Validate legitimate automation from the approved source
steps.desc: Confirm the account continues to function correctly from its documented source system.
steps.outcome: Automation confirmed functional from approved source.

steps.title: Document root cause and update source baseline monitoring
steps.desc: Record the finding and confirm a detection rule exists for future source deviations.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with detection confirmed.

steps.title: Confirm the mismatch and identify the actual source
steps.desc: Verify the observed source host/IP against the baseline and identify what that unexpected source system is.
steps.outcome: Confirmed source mismatch and identity of the unexpected source system.
steps.abort: If the new source is a documented, recently-approved change (e.g. migration) not yet reflected in inventory, close as false positive and update inventory.

steps.title: Apply source restriction controls
steps.desc: Where supported, restrict the account's authentication to its approved source IP range or host allowlist.
steps.outcome: Account authentication technically restricted to approved sources.

ITID-12426.def: Compromise or misuse of a service account used by a continuous integration/continuous deployment pipeline (build agent, deployment automation, artifact registry) to gain unauthorized access to source code, secrets, or production deployment capability.
ITID-12426.purpose: Captures exploitation of a service account belonging specifically to a CI/CD pipeline.
scopeIncludes: CI/CD pipeline credential used to inject malicious code into a build or deployment artifact
CI/CD service account exploited to exfiltrate secrets stored in pipeline configuration/variables
scopeExcludes: Cloud IAM role/service-account exploitation not tied to a CI/CD pipeline specifically (see ITID-12427)
Third-party SaaS integration account exploitation (see ITID-12428)
ITID-12426.severity: Critical — CI/CD compromise can lead to a supply-chain-scale compromise of production systems.
ITID-12426.escalation: Immediate escalation to security engineering and DevOps leadership; treat as a potential supply-chain incident requiring build/artifact integrity review.
indicators: Unexpected modification to pipeline configuration or build scripts
Pipeline service account used to access repositories or environments outside its defined pipeline scope
Deployment triggered outside the normal commit-to-deploy workflow
vectors: Compromised pipeline secret (API token, deploy key) used to inject malicious code
Malicious pull request merged that alters pipeline configuration to exfiltrate secrets
rootCauses: Pipeline secrets stored in plaintext environment variables rather than a secrets manager
Pipeline service account granted broad write access to production deployment targets
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Secrets manager integration for all pipeline credentials
Pipeline configuration change review/approval gating
ITID-12426.detection: CI/CD platform audit logs and pipeline-configuration-change alerting provide a concrete, real technical signal.
ITID-12426.response: Freeze the pipeline, rotate all associated secrets, and conduct an integrity review of recently built/deployed artifacts.
metrics: Count of pipeline configuration-change anomalies detected per quarter
ITID-12426.notes: Scoped specifically to CI/CD pipeline identities to keep it distinct from general cloud IAM role exploitation (ITID-12427) and third-party integration accounts (ITID-12428).

playbook.name: Response: CI/CD Pipeline Service Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For exploitation of a service account used by a CI/CD pipeline, potentially enabling malicious code injection into build or deployment artifacts.

steps.title: Confirm the pipeline account and scope of its access
steps.desc: Identify the pipeline(s) the account serves and the repositories, artifact registries, and deployment targets it can reach.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of pipeline access.

steps.title: Rotate the pipeline secret and revoke exposed tokens
steps.desc: Rotate the service account credential/API token and revoke any other secrets stored alongside it in the CI/CD secret store.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with build/release owners to avoid breaking active deployments unexpectedly.
steps.outcome: Pipeline secrets rotated and old tokens revoked.

steps.title: Verify integrity of build artifacts and deployed code
steps.desc: Compare recent build artifacts and deployed versions against known-good source to confirm no malicious code was introduced.
steps.outcome: Artifacts confirmed clean, or contaminated artifacts identified for removal/redeployment.

steps.title: Re-enable the pipeline with the rotated secret and validate a clean build
steps.desc: Restore pipeline operation with new credentials and confirm a successful, clean build/deploy cycle.
steps.outcome: Pipeline restored and validated.

steps.title: Document root cause and recommend pipeline secret-hygiene improvements
steps.desc: Record how the pipeline credential was exposed and recommend controls such as short-lived tokens or stricter secret scoping.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement recommendation.

steps.title: Review build logs for unauthorized or anomalous pipeline runs
steps.desc: Examine recent build/deploy logs for runs not tied to legitimate commits, unexpected triggers, or unfamiliar job definitions.
steps.outcome: Identified any unauthorized or anomalous pipeline executions.

steps.title: Pause affected pipelines pending review
steps.desc: Temporarily disable or pause the affected pipeline(s) to prevent further unauthorized builds or deployments.
steps.outcome: Pipeline execution halted until cleared.

steps.title: Check for tampering with pipeline configuration or scripts
steps.desc: Review recent changes to pipeline definition files, build scripts, and deployment manifests for unauthorized modification.
steps.outcome: Confirmed integrity or identified tampering of pipeline configuration.

ITID-12427.def: Compromise or misuse of a cloud platform's native identity construct (AWS IAM role, Azure managed identity, GCP service account) rather than an application-layer service account, to gain unauthorized access to cloud resources.
ITID-12427.purpose: Captures exploitation of a cloud provider IAM service account or assumable role.
scopeIncludes: Compromised cloud IAM role/service-account key used to access or modify cloud resources
Privilege escalation via cloud IAM role-chaining/assumption abuse
scopeExcludes: CI/CD pipeline service accounts specifically (see ITID-12426)
Application-layer service accounts running on-premises or in a VM (see other siblings in this Type)
ITID-12427.severity: Critical — cloud IAM compromise can grant direct access to production infrastructure and data at scale.
ITID-12427.escalation: Immediate escalation to cloud security engineering; disable the credential/role and review CloudTrail/Activity Log for the full blast radius.
indicators: Unusual cloud API calls (e.g. CreateAccessKey, AssumeRole chains) from a service identity
Cloud resource access from an unexpected region/IP for a service account key
Privilege-escalation API call sequence matching known cloud IAM abuse patterns
vectors: Leaked cloud access key exploited for direct API access
Role-assumption chaining abused to escalate from a low-privilege to a high-privilege role
rootCauses: Cloud IAM roles granted overly broad policies (wildcard permissions)
Long-lived static access keys used instead of short-lived, federated credentials
mitreTechniques: T1550.001 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
controls: Cloud IAM least-privilege policy review
Short-lived/federated credentials in place of static cloud access keys
ITID-12427.detection: Cloud-native audit logs (CloudTrail, Azure Activity Log, GCP Audit Log) ingested into SIEM provide a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12427.response: Disable the compromised identity, review the full API call history for impact, and rotate/replace with short-lived credentials.
metrics: Count of cloud IAM anomaly detections per quarter
Percentage of cloud identities using short-lived vs. static credentials
detections: CloudTrail/Activity Log anomalous API call alerting
ITID-12427.notes: Scoped to cloud-native IAM constructs specifically, distinct from CI/CD pipeline identities (ITID-12426) even where a pipeline uses a cloud role, in which case classify under ITID-12426 if the pipeline context is the primary factor.

playbook.name: Response: Cloud IAM Service Account/Role Exploitation
playbook.description: For exploitation of a cloud IAM service account or assumable role, potentially enabling unauthorized access to cloud resources.

steps.title: Confirm the identity and enumerate its assigned roles/policies
steps.desc: Pull the service account or role's full set of attached IAM policies and any roles it is permitted to assume.
steps.outcome: Complete IAM permission footprint documented.

steps.title: Rotate or revoke the credential/access keys
steps.desc: Rotate the access key/secret or, for a role, revoke active sessions and update the trust policy to block further assumption.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated or role assumption blocked.

steps.title: Search for attacker-created cloud resources or persistence
steps.desc: Check for newly created IAM users/roles, access keys, storage buckets, compute instances, or lambda/function resources created under the identity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence, or removal, of attacker-created cloud resources.

steps.title: Validate legitimate cloud workloads and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate application/service using the identity functions correctly and enable heightened monitoring on the identity.
steps.outcome: Workload confirmed functional; monitoring active.

steps.title: Document root cause and recommend cloud IAM hardening
steps.desc: Record how the identity was exploited and recommend controls such as short-lived credentials or stricter role trust policies.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with hardening recommendation.

steps.title: Review cloud audit logs for actions taken under the identity
steps.desc: Examine cloud provider audit/activity logs for API calls made using the account or assumed role, focusing on unusual services, regions, or resource actions.
steps.outcome: Documented timeline of actions taken under the compromised identity.
steps.tool: Cloud audit log (e.g. CloudTrail, Activity Log, Cloud Audit Logs)

steps.title: Review and restrict the role via the cloud console
steps.desc: In the cloud IAM console, remove any attached policies granting access beyond the account's documented function, including inline policies and permission boundaries.
steps.outcome: Role/account reduced to least-privilege access.

ITID-12428.def: Compromise or misuse of a service account/API credential used to connect a third-party or vendor integration (SaaS app, monitoring tool, OAuth-connected app) to internal systems.
ITID-12428.purpose: Captures exploitation of a service account used to integrate a third-party SaaS or vendor system.
scopeIncludes: Compromised OAuth token or API key belonging to a third-party integration used to access internal data
Malicious/compromised third-party app abusing its granted integration scope
scopeExcludes: Cloud provider-native IAM role exploitation (see ITID-12427)
CI/CD pipeline accounts (see ITID-12426)
ITID-12428.severity: High, escalating to Critical if the integration has broad data-access scope.
ITID-12428.priority: P1 if broad scope confirmed, otherwise P2.
ITID-12428.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management and security engineering to revoke the integration and assess data exposure.
indicators: OAuth-connected app accessing data or performing actions beyond its documented integration scope
API traffic pattern from a third-party integration inconsistent with normal usage
vectors: Third-party vendor's own environment compromised, exposing the integration credential
Malicious OAuth app granted excessive consent by a user
rootCauses: No periodic review of third-party OAuth app grants and their scopes
Integration credentials granted broader scope than the integration's function requires
controls: Periodic third-party OAuth app/integration scope review
SaaS security posture management (SSPM) monitoring
ITID-12428.detection: SSPM/CASB tooling and API access logs for third-party integrations provide a concrete, real technical signal.
ITID-12428.response: Revoke the integration's access immediately, notify the vendor, and assess the scope of data potentially exposed.
metrics: Count of third-party integration anomalies detected per quarter
Count of over-scoped integrations remediated
ITID-12428.notes: Scoped to externally-owned integration credentials specifically, distinguishing it from internally-owned cloud IAM (ITID-12427) and CI/CD (ITID-12426) service accounts.

playbook.name: Response: Third-Party Integration Service Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For exploitation of a service account used by an external vendor or third-party integration to access internal systems.

steps.title: Confirm the integration and its documented data/access scope
steps.desc: Identify the third party the account belongs to, the integration's purpose, and the systems/data it is permitted to touch.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of the third-party integration.

steps.title: Rotate the integration credential/API key
steps.desc: Revoke and reissue the credential used by the integration, coordinating with the vendor to update their configuration.
steps.outcome: Old credential invalidated; vendor updated with new credential.

steps.title: Assess data exposure through the integration
steps.desc: Determine what data was accessible to or accessed through the integration during the suspected abuse window.
steps.outcome: Data exposure scope confirmed.

steps.title: Validate the integration functions correctly with new credentials
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor's integration operates normally after credential rotation and access scoping.
steps.outcome: Integration confirmed functional.

steps.title: Document root cause and review vendor access governance
steps.desc: Record the finding and evaluate whether the vendor's access agreement and review cadence need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with governance recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether activity originated from the vendor or an attacker
steps.desc: Compare the flagged activity's source and pattern against the integration's known behavior, and contact the vendor if needed to confirm whether the activity was theirs.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the vendor or an unauthorized party performed the activity.
steps.abort: If vendor confirms the activity as legitimate and expected, close as false positive.

steps.title: Restrict the integration to its minimum required access
steps.desc: Review and scope down the account's access to only the specific data/systems the integration requires.
steps.outcome: Integration reduced to least-privilege access.

ITID-12429.def: Compromise or misuse of a service account that has become orphaned — its original owning application, team, or business justification no longer exists or is untracked — leaving it unmonitored and typically over-privileged relative to any current need.
ITID-12429.purpose: Captures exploitation of a service account no longer associated with an active, known application or owner.
scopeIncludes: Service account with no identifiable current owner or application in the CMDB/IAM inventory, exploited by an attacker
Discovery, during investigation, that a compromised service account has been orphaned for an extended period
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a service account with a known, active owner (see other siblings in this Type)
Abandoned human user accounts (tracked under Abandoned Accounts)
ITID-12429.severity: High — an orphaned account is both unmonitored and typically has no one positioned to notice misuse quickly.
ITID-12429.escalation: Escalate to IAM to disable the account immediately pending ownership investigation; escalate to security if active exploitation is confirmed.
indicators: Service account with no matching entry in the current application/owner inventory
Service account activity with no corresponding active project or ticket for an extended period
vectors: Attacker discovering and reusing a forgotten, still-valid service account credential
Long-dormant service account reactivated for malicious use with no owner present to notice
rootCauses: No service account lifecycle/ownership tracking process
Decommissioned applications leaving their service accounts active
controls: Service account inventory and ownership recertification process
Automated disabling of accounts with no owner attestation
ITID-12429.detection: IAM governance tooling reconciling service accounts against an application/ownership inventory is the primary technical signal, supplemented by UEBA on dormant-account reactivation.
ITID-12429.response: Disable the account immediately, investigate any activity during the orphaned period, and determine whether it can be safely decommissioned.
metrics: Count of orphaned service accounts identified and remediated per quarter
ITID-12429.notes: Differentiator is the absence of a current owner/application, distinct from ITID-12429's siblings which assume an identifiable owner.

playbook.name: Response: Orphaned Service Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For exploitation of a service account whose owning team or original purpose can no longer be identified, leaving it unmonitored and unmanaged.

steps.title: Attempt to identify the account's original owner and purpose
steps.desc: Search inventory records, ticketing history, and configuration references to determine who created the account and what it was for.
steps.outcome: Owner/purpose identified, or confirmed genuinely unknown.

steps.title: Rotate the credential and disable non-essential access
steps.desc: Reset the credential and disable the account's access to any system where its use cannot be confirmed as still required.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; unconfirmed access disabled.

steps.title: Determine whether any live process still depends on the account
steps.desc: Check for active jobs, scripts, or integrations still calling the account before finalizing containment.
steps.outcome: Live dependencies identified or confirmed absent.
steps.abort: If a live dependency is found, engage its operator before fully disabling the account.

steps.title: Decommission the account or formally re-assign ownership
steps.desc: If no legitimate ongoing use is found, decommission the account; otherwise assign it a permanent, accountable owner in the inventory.
steps.outcome: Account decommissioned or formally re-owned.

steps.title: Document root cause and sweep for other orphaned accounts
steps.desc: Record the finding and search the environment for other service accounts lacking a confirmed owner.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; related orphaned accounts identified for remediation.

steps.title: Determine what the account currently has access to and how it has been used
steps.desc: Enumerate current permissions and review recent activity logs, since an orphaned account's actual footprint may differ from any outdated documentation.
steps.outcome: Current access and recent activity fully mapped.

steps.title: Assign temporary ownership for the duration of the investigation
steps.desc: Designate an interim owner (e.g. security or IT operations) to authorize any changes and answer questions about the account during response.
steps.outcome: Interim ownership assigned.

ITID-12431.def: An incident involving misuse of an account that should have been deprovisioned or disabled but remained active, not yet matched to a more specific abandonment pattern.
ITID-12431.purpose: Catch-all for exploitation of an abandoned account that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific abandonment pattern (departed employee, contractor, default, dormant, etc.) is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Abandoned Accounts
ITID-12431.escalation: Escalate to IAM once the specific abandonment pattern is identified; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Activity on an account flagged as stale/inactive by IAM lifecycle review, pattern unconfirmed
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector involving an abandoned account
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Joiner-mover-leaver account deprovisioning process
Periodic dormant/abandoned account review and disablement
Automated account lifecycle management tied to HR system
ITID-12431.detection: Same IAM lifecycle/UEBA telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12431.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12431.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Abandoned Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For a flagged account that appears to have been left active past its legitimate need, where the specific abandonment category has not yet been narrowed.

steps.title: Confirm the account should have been deprovisioned
steps.desc: Check HR/vendor/project records to establish whether the account's associated person, purpose, or engagement has ended.
steps.guidance: Most abandoned-account incidents are governance gaps, not active attacks — confirm the offboarding trigger before treating this as a compromise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed that the account should have been disabled and was not.
steps.abort: If the account's associated need is still active, close as false positive.
steps.tool: HR system / vendor records / project tracker

steps.title: Disable the account
steps.desc: Immediately disable sign-in for the account.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Review what the account accessed while dormant/abandoned
steps.desc: Determine what data or systems the account had access to during its abandonment period, whether or not it was actively misused.
steps.outcome: Documented access footprint during the abandonment period.

steps.title: Formally offboard the account
steps.desc: Complete full deprovisioning: remove group memberships, transfer or archive owned resources, and close out the account per the offboarding checklist.
steps.outcome: Account fully deprovisioned.

steps.title: Identify and fix the offboarding process gap that allowed the account to linger
steps.desc: Document why the account was not disabled on schedule and recommend a process or automation fix (e.g. HR-to-IAM feed trigger).
steps.guidance: Focus on the underlying lifecycle process, not just this one account.
steps.outcome: Root cause documented with a process improvement recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the account was actually used maliciously
steps.desc: Review the account's activity since the point it should have been disabled, looking for logons or actions inconsistent with dormancy.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the account was merely dormant or was actively misused.
steps.abort: If no activity occurred since the account became abandoned, treat as a governance-gap-only finding and skip to containment/eradication for cleanup only.

steps.title: Revoke active sessions and tokens
steps.desc: Terminate any active sessions, API tokens, or app passwords associated with the account.
steps.outcome: All active sessions/tokens revoked.

ITID-12432.def: Use of a former employee's still-active credential, following a failure of the offboarding process to disable or delete the account, by the former employee or by another party who obtained the credential.
ITID-12432.purpose: Captures exploitation of a departed employee's account that was never disabled at offboarding.
scopeIncludes: Former employee account used to log in after their termination/departure date
Third party using a still-active former-employee credential
scopeExcludes: Contractor/temporary worker accounts specifically (see ITID-12433)
Accounts disabled correctly but reactivated by an attacker (see ITID-12437)
ITID-12432.severity: High — represents both an access-control failure and potential malicious insider activity.
ITID-12432.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal if the former employee is confirmed to have accessed the account; escalate to IAM to audit the full offboarding pipeline.
indicators: Successful authentication on an account after its associated HR termination date
Account activity inconsistent with any current business need
vectors: HR-to-IAM deprovisioning workflow failure or delay
Former employee retaining and reusing personal knowledge of still-valid credentials
rootCauses: No automated, real-time HR-to-IAM deprovisioning integration
Manual offboarding checklist step missed or delayed
controls: Automated HR-to-IAM deprovisioning integration
Post-termination access audit within 24 hours
ITID-12432.detection: Correlating HR termination-date feeds against IAM authentication logs provides a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12432.response: Disable the account immediately, investigate all activity since the termination date, and audit the broader offboarding pipeline for similar gaps.
metrics: Mean time between termination date and account disablement
Count of post-termination logins detected per quarter
ITID-12432.notes: Scoped to full-time/permanent employee offboarding failures specifically, distinct from contractor engagements (ITID-12433).

playbook.name: Response: Departed Employee Account Never Disabled
playbook.description: For an employee's account that remained enabled after their termination or resignation date.

steps.title: Confirm the employee's departure date and offboarding record
steps.desc: Check HR records for the termination/last-day date and confirm whether an offboarding ticket was raised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed departure date and offboarding ticket status.
steps.abort: If HR shows the person as still active, close as false positive.

steps.title: Disable the account immediately
steps.desc: Disable sign-in for the account without delay.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Review post-departure access for malicious use, if any occurred
steps.desc: If activity was found after the departure date, determine what was accessed, changed, or exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Scope of any malicious post-departure activity confirmed.
steps.abort: If no post-departure activity occurred, skip to recovery.

steps.title: Complete full offboarding
steps.desc: Transfer or archive owned resources (mailbox, files, shared drives) and remove the account per the standard offboarding checklist.
steps.outcome: Offboarding completed.

steps.title: Fix the HR-to-IT offboarding trigger gap
steps.desc: Determine why the termination did not trigger account disablement and recommend closing that gap (e.g. automated HR feed, offboarding SLA).
steps.outcome: Root cause documented with a process fix recommended.

steps.title: Determine if the account was used after the departure date
steps.desc: Review logon and access history for activity occurring after the confirmed last-day.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether post-departure use occurred, and by whom if so.

steps.title: Revoke sessions, tokens, and remote access
steps.desc: Terminate active sessions, VPN access, and any issued API tokens or app passwords.
steps.outcome: All access channels revoked.

ITID-12433.def: Use of a contractor, vendor staff, or other temporary worker's still-active credential after their contract or engagement end date.
ITID-12433.purpose: Captures exploitation of a contractor or temporary worker's account left active past the end of their engagement.
scopeIncludes: Contractor account used to log in after the documented engagement end date
Third-party staffing agency worker's account left active past a contract renewal decision point
scopeExcludes: Permanent employee offboarding failures (see ITID-12432)
Third-party vendor integration service accounts (tracked under Service Account Exploitation)
ITID-12433.severity: High — contractor accounts are frequently under-tracked relative to full-time employee accounts.
ITID-12433.escalation: Escalate to procurement/vendor management and IAM to confirm engagement status and disable the account.
indicators: Successful authentication on a contractor account after the contract's documented end date
No corresponding active statement-of-work/engagement record for the account
vectors: Contract end-date not communicated to IAM by the sponsoring business unit
Contractor account provisioned outside the standard employee lifecycle process entirely
rootCauses: No formal contractor lifecycle tracking tied to contract/SOW end dates
Contractor accounts provisioned as standard employee accounts with no distinguishing expiry attribute
controls: Contractor account auto-expiry tied to SOW/contract end date
Vendor management-to-IAM engagement status integration
ITID-12433.detection: Correlating vendor/contract management system end dates against IAM authentication logs provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12433.response: Disable the account immediately, confirm current engagement status with vendor management, and audit account activity since the contract end date.
metrics: Count of contractor accounts active past documented contract end date
ITID-12433.notes: Scoped to contractor/temporary-worker human accounts specifically, distinct from employee offboarding (ITID-12432) and third-party service accounts (tracked under Service Account Exploitation).

playbook.name: Response: Contractor/Temporary Account Left Active Past Engagement
playbook.description: For a contractor or temporary-worker account that remained enabled after the end of the contracted engagement.

steps.title: Confirm the engagement end date
steps.desc: Check the contract, statement of work, or vendor management record for the documented engagement end date.
steps.outcome: Confirmed engagement end date.
steps.abort: If the engagement was extended and the account is still authorized, close as false positive and update records.

steps.title: Disable the account
steps.desc: Disable sign-in for the contractor account.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Review what the account accessed during the abandonment window
steps.desc: Determine what systems or data the account could reach after the engagement ended, and whether it was exercised.
steps.outcome: Access footprint during the abandonment window documented.

steps.title: Close out the contractor account and reclaim owned resources
steps.desc: Transfer any work product owned by the account and remove it per the contractor offboarding checklist.
steps.outcome: Account closed out.

steps.title: Fix the contractor lifecycle gap
steps.desc: Recommend tying contractor account expiry directly to the contract end date rather than relying on manual offboarding.
steps.outcome: Root cause documented with a process fix recommended.

steps.title: Determine if the account was used after the engagement ended
steps.desc: Review logon and access history for activity after the confirmed end date.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether post-engagement use occurred.

steps.title: Revoke any issued equipment and remote-access credentials
steps.desc: Revoke VPN access, badge access, and any hardware tokens issued for the engagement.
steps.outcome: All engagement-related access revoked.

ITID-12434.def: Use of an account originally created for testing or development purposes, which was never removed when the associated system moved to production, typically carrying weak or default credentials.
ITID-12434.purpose: Captures exploitation of a test or development account mistakenly left active in a production environment.
scopeIncludes: Test/dev account discovered active in a production system and exploited
Account with a known default or weak test credential exploited in production
scopeExcludes: Default/built-in vendor accounts shipped with a product (see ITID-12436)
Training/demo environment credential exposure (tracked under Accidental Disclosure)
ITID-12434.severity: High — test accounts frequently carry weak, well-known, or shared credentials.
ITID-12434.escalation: Escalate to application/platform engineering to remove the account and audit the production deployment/promotion process.
indicators: Account naming convention or metadata indicating test/dev origin, active and used in production
Weak or default password successfully used against a production system
vectors: Attacker discovering a leftover test account via credential stuffing or brute force due to its weak password
Test account with elevated debug privileges exploited for broader access
rootCauses: No environment-promotion checklist step to remove test/dev accounts before go-live
Test accounts provisioned with weak, shared, or default passwords
controls: Pre-production-promotion account audit/removal checklist
Password policy enforcement extended to test/dev-origin accounts
ITID-12434.detection: Account-naming/metadata review combined with authentication logs provides a concrete technical signal once the account inventory is known.
ITID-12434.response: Remove the account immediately, audit for other leftover test artifacts, and add a promotion-checklist control.
metrics: Count of test/dev accounts found active in production per audit cycle
ITID-12434.notes: Scoped to internally-created test/dev accounts specifically, distinct from vendor-shipped default accounts (ITID-12436).

playbook.name: Response: Test/Development Account Left in Production
playbook.description: For a test or development account, never intended for production use, discovered active in a production environment.

steps.title: Confirm the account's intended environment and current placement
steps.desc: Establish that the account was created for test/dev purposes and confirm it currently has production access or exists in the production environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the account is a test/dev account present in production.
steps.abort: If it was deliberately provisioned for production (e.g. renamed convention), close as false positive.

steps.title: Disable the account in production
steps.desc: Immediately disable the account's access to the production environment.
steps.outcome: Production access disabled.

steps.title: Assess whether the account's presence exposed production data to non-production use
steps.desc: Check whether the test account or associated test tooling pulled, cached, or exposed production data.
steps.outcome: Data exposure scope confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Remove the account from production entirely
steps.desc: Delete the test/dev account from the production environment rather than merely disabling it, unless a documented need for retention exists.
steps.outcome: Account removed from production.

steps.title: Recommend an environment-segregation control to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Document the finding and recommend a control such as environment-tagging enforcement or a deployment gate that blocks test accounts from reaching production.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine what production access the account holds and how it has been used
steps.desc: Review the account's production permissions and activity history to assess whether it was exercised, and by whom.
steps.guidance: Test accounts often carry weak or default credentials, making this a high-risk finding regardless of observed activity.
steps.outcome: Documented production access and usage history.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials that may be weak or shared
steps.desc: Reset the account's credential, since test accounts commonly use default or shared passwords.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated.

ITID-12435.def: Use of an account originating from an acquired, merged, or divested entity's identity environment that was never migrated, disabled, or reconciled into the current organization's IAM process.
ITID-12435.purpose: Captures exploitation of a legacy account carried over from a merger, acquisition, or divestiture that was never deprovisioned.
scopeIncludes: Account from an acquired company's legacy directory still active and exploited after integration
Account belonging to a divested business unit's former employee, never removed from the retained environment
scopeExcludes: Standard departed-employee offboarding failures within the current organization's own lifecycle (see ITID-12432)
ITID-12435.severity: High — M&A environments frequently have incomplete identity reconciliation and elevated legacy trust.
ITID-12435.escalation: Escalate to IAM and the M&A integration team to complete identity reconciliation for the affected legacy environment.
indicators: Account authenticating from a legacy/acquired-entity directory with no corresponding record in the current organization's HR system
Account activity discovered during a delayed post-acquisition IAM reconciliation audit
vectors: Former employee of the acquired entity retaining legacy access after the deal closes
Attacker exploiting an unreconciled trust relationship between the legacy and current directories
rootCauses: No formal identity reconciliation milestone in the M&A integration plan
Legacy directory trust relationship left in place indefinitely post-close
controls: M&A identity reconciliation and legacy-directory decommissioning milestone
Time-boxed trust relationship with automatic expiry for acquired-entity directories
ITID-12435.detection: Cross-referencing legacy directory authentication logs against the current HR/IAM system of record provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12435.response: Disable the account, complete the overdue identity reconciliation, and decommission or tightly scope the legacy trust relationship.
metrics: Count of unreconciled legacy accounts identified per integration audit
ITID-12435.notes: Scoped specifically to M&A-origin legacy accounts, distinct from standard employee/contractor offboarding failures.

playbook.name: Response: Merger/Acquisition Legacy Account Never Deprovisioned
playbook.description: For an account originating from a merged or acquired entity that was never migrated, disabled, or brought under current identity governance.

steps.title: Confirm the account's origin and current governance status
steps.desc: Trace the account back to the legacy/acquired entity and confirm it was never included in the post-merger identity consolidation or deprovisioning effort.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the account is a legacy artifact outside current governance.
steps.abort: If the account was deliberately retained under a documented exception, close as false positive.
steps.tool: Identity governance records / M&A integration documentation

steps.title: Disable the account
steps.desc: Disable sign-in for the legacy account across all systems it can reach.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Review whether the account was exploited to bridge into current-environment systems
steps.desc: Assess whether the legacy account provided a path into systems that are part of the current, post-merger environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any cross-environment exposure.

steps.title: Complete deprovisioning and reconcile against the identity governance system of record
steps.desc: Fully remove or archive the account and ensure it is reflected as closed in the current identity governance system.
steps.outcome: Account deprovisioned and governance records reconciled.

steps.title: Recommend completing the post-merger identity consolidation sweep
steps.desc: Document the gap and recommend a full sweep for other unconsolidated legacy accounts from the same merger/acquisition.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a consolidation sweep recommended.

steps.title: Determine what the account can currently access and whether it has been used
steps.desc: Review the account's current permissions (which may span legacy and current-environment systems) and its activity history.
steps.guidance: Legacy accounts often retain access that predates current access-review processes and may not appear in standard entitlement reviews.
steps.outcome: Documented access footprint and usage history.

steps.title: Revoke any residual access to legacy or bridged systems
steps.desc: Remove access to any legacy-entity systems still bridged into the current environment.
steps.outcome: All residual access revoked.

ITID-12436.def: Use of a vendor-provided default or built-in account (e.g. default admin, factory-set service account) that was never disabled, renamed, or had its default credential changed after deployment.
ITID-12436.purpose: Captures exploitation of a default or built-in account that a vendor product ships with and that was never disabled.
scopeIncludes: Default vendor admin account exploited using its well-known factory credential
Built-in service account shipped with an appliance/application, never disabled post-install
scopeExcludes: Internally-created test/dev accounts (see ITID-12434)
Service accounts created by internal teams for integration purposes (tracked under Service Account Exploitation)
ITID-12436.severity: High — default credentials are typically public knowledge and trivially exploitable.
ITID-12436.escalation: Escalate to the asset/system owner to immediately disable or re-credential the account; audit similar assets for the same gap.
indicators: Successful authentication using a known, published default/factory credential
Built-in account with no evidence of post-deployment credential change
vectors: Attacker using a publicly documented default credential against an internet-facing or internal appliance
Automated scanning tools identifying and exploiting default-credential devices at scale
rootCauses: No hardening/deployment checklist step to disable or re-credential default accounts
Asset deployed without following vendor security hardening guidance
controls: Deployment hardening checklist requiring default-credential change/disablement
Periodic default-credential scanning against asset inventory
ITID-12436.detection: Default-credential scanning tools and authentication logs against known default-account names provide a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12436.response: Disable or re-credential the account immediately and scan the broader asset inventory for the same exposure.
metrics: Count of assets found with active default credentials per audit cycle
ITID-12436.notes: Scoped to vendor-shipped default/built-in accounts specifically, distinct from internally-created test accounts (ITID-12434).

playbook.name: Response: Default/Built-In Account Never Disabled
playbook.description: For a default or built-in account (e.g. vendor-shipped admin account) that was never disabled or renamed after system deployment.

steps.title: Confirm the account is a default/built-in account and check its credential status
steps.desc: Identify the system/application the account belongs to and check whether its credential was ever changed from the vendor default.
steps.outcome: Confirmed default-account status and credential state.
steps.abort: If the account was already properly secured and this is a false alert, close as false positive.

steps.title: Disable or rename the account and rotate its credential
steps.desc: Disable the account if unneeded, or rename it and set a strong unique credential if it must remain in use.
steps.outcome: Account secured or disabled.

steps.title: Check for unauthorized changes made via the default account
steps.desc: Review configuration and access-control changes made under the account for anything unauthorized.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence, or identification, of unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Validate system function after securing the account
steps.desc: Confirm the system continues to operate correctly after the default account was disabled/secured.
steps.outcome: System confirmed functional.

steps.title: Add default-credential hardening to deployment standards
steps.desc: Document the finding and recommend that default-account hardening be a mandatory step in the system deployment/hardening checklist.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a deployment-standard recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the account has been used, and by whom
steps.desc: Review logon history for the account, distinguishing legitimate administrative use from unauthorized use.
steps.guidance: Default credentials are commonly known or easily guessed, so any successful external-facing use should be treated with high suspicion.
steps.outcome: Usage history and legitimacy of use determined.

steps.title: Restrict the account's access scope
steps.desc: If the account must remain active, scope its permissions down from default (often overly broad) to only what is required.
steps.outcome: Account access scoped to least privilege.

ITID-12437.def: An attacker reactivating, re-enabling, or restoring access to an account that had gone dormant/inactive (but was not necessarily a failure of the offboarding process), as a persistence or initial-access technique.
ITID-12437.purpose: Captures a dormant account that had been correctly disabled or inactive being reactivated by an attacker.
scopeIncludes: Attacker re-enabling a disabled account via administrative access
Attacker using an account that was inactive but never formally disabled, after a long idle period
scopeExcludes: Accounts that were never disabled due to an offboarding process failure (see ITID-12432, ITID-12433)
ITID-12437.severity: High — reactivation of a dormant account is a known persistence technique.
ITID-12437.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response; investigate how the reactivation was performed and by whom/what.
indicators: Account status change from disabled to enabled with no corresponding authorized request
First authentication on a previously dormant account after an extended idle period, from an anomalous source
vectors: Attacker with administrative access re-enabling a disabled account for stealthy persistent access
Attacker identifying and using a technically-enabled-but-long-idle account to blend in
rootCauses: No alerting on account status changes (disabled-to-enabled transitions)
No periodic disablement/removal of long-dormant accounts
controls: Real-time alerting on disabled-to-enabled account status changes
Automated disablement of accounts dormant beyond policy threshold
ITID-12437.detection: Directory service audit logs for account status changes provide a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12437.response: Disable the account again immediately, investigate the reactivation event and subsequent activity, and hunt for other persistence mechanisms.
metrics: Count of unauthorized account-reactivation events detected per quarter
ITID-12437.notes: Differentiator is attacker-driven reactivation as an active technique, distinct from passive offboarding-process failures in sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Dormant Account Reactivated by Attacker
playbook.description: For a previously dormant/abandoned account that has been confirmed reactivated and used by an attacker — a genuine active-compromise incident, not merely a governance gap.

steps.title: Confirm the account was dormant and identify the reactivation event
steps.desc: Establish the account's last legitimate activity date and pinpoint the specific logon or action that marks its reactivation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed dormancy period and the specific reactivation event.

steps.title: Disable the account and terminate all active sessions immediately
steps.desc: Disable sign-in and forcibly terminate any live sessions, tokens, or MFA methods associated with the account.
steps.outcome: Account disabled; all sessions and tokens revoked.

steps.title: Hunt for and remove attacker persistence established via the account
steps.desc: Search for new accounts, added permissions, scheduled tasks, mail rules, or MFA registrations created using the compromised account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed removal of all attacker-established persistence.

steps.title: Determine account disposition and restore securely if retained
steps.desc: Decide whether the account should be permanently decommissioned or, if a legitimate ongoing need exists, restored with a new credential and re-enrolled MFA under close monitoring.
steps.outcome: Account decommissioned, or securely restored with confirmed legitimate need.

steps.title: Document root cause and close the dormancy-monitoring gap
steps.desc: Record how the attacker discovered and reactivated the dormant account, and recommend detection for reactivation of long-dormant accounts going forward.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with detection recommendation.

steps.title: Confirm the reactivation was not performed by the legitimate owner
steps.desc: Attempt to contact the account's owner (if identifiable) and check for any legitimate business reason for reactivation; treat as compromised absent confirmation.
steps.guidance: Do not assume this is benign — dormant-account reactivation is a common attacker technique for establishing low-visibility access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized reactivation.
steps.abort: If the owner confirms legitimate reactivation through an approved process, close as false positive.

steps.title: Contain lateral movement from systems accessed via the account
steps.desc: Isolate or heighten monitoring on any hosts or systems the account accessed since reactivation, given the likelihood of further attacker footholds.
steps.outcome: Downstream systems contained or under heightened monitoring.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of attacker activity since reactivation
steps.desc: Trace all logons, access, and actions performed using the account since the reactivation event across all connected systems.
steps.outcome: Full timeline and scope of attacker activity established.

ITID-12438.def: An abandoned account whose retained access rights are themselves elevated or legacy in nature (former admin rights, deprecated system access), amplifying the impact of its exploitation beyond a standard abandoned standard-user account.
ITID-12438.purpose: Captures an abandoned account that retains elevated or legacy privileges disproportionate to any current need.
scopeIncludes: Abandoned account discovered to still hold administrative or elevated entitlements
Abandoned account retaining access to a legacy system no longer generally accessible to current staff
scopeExcludes: Abandoned standard-user accounts with no elevated entitlements (see other siblings, e.g. ITID-12432)
ITID-12438.severity: Critical — combines the abandonment exposure with a high-privilege blast radius.
ITID-12438.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM and security leadership given the elevated privilege combined with lack of ownership.
indicators: Access review identifies an abandoned account holding admin-group membership
Abandoned account with entitlements to a decommissioned or legacy system retained past its general deprecation
vectors: Attacker discovering and exploiting an abandoned account specifically because of its high privilege level
Insider exploiting a known-abandoned but still-privileged account for unauthorized access
rootCauses: Access recertification not extended to accounts already flagged as abandoned/dormant
No automatic privilege downgrade upon account inactivity threshold
controls: Automatic privilege downgrade or disablement on account inactivity threshold
Access recertification inclusive of dormant/abandoned accounts
ITID-12438.detection: IAM entitlement analytics cross-referenced with account activity/dormancy status provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12438.response: Disable the account immediately and audit for any activity during the period it held excess dormant privilege.
metrics: Count of abandoned accounts with elevated entitlements identified per audit cycle
ITID-12438.notes: Differentiator is the elevated-privilege dimension specifically, layered on top of the general abandonment pattern in sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Abandoned Account with Elevated/Legacy Permissions
