playbook.description: For an abandoned account that, in addition to being left active, retained elevated or legacy permissions no longer aligned with any current role.

steps.title: Confirm the account is abandoned and enumerate its elevated permissions
steps.desc: Confirm the account's associated need has ended and pull its full current permission set, noting any administrative or legacy-role grants.
steps.outcome: Confirmed abandonment and documented elevated-permission footprint.
steps.abort: If the associated need is still active, close as false positive.

steps.title: Disable the account
steps.desc: Disable sign-in for the account.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Review what the elevated access could have exposed
steps.desc: Determine the sensitivity of systems/data reachable through the elevated permissions and whether any were touched.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Formally offboard the account
steps.desc: Complete deprovisioning per the standard offboarding checklist.
steps.outcome: Account fully deprovisioned.

steps.title: Recommend a periodic review for elevated-permission accounts specifically
steps.desc: Document the finding and recommend that accounts holding elevated/administrative permissions receive more frequent access reviews than standard accounts.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a targeted review-cadence recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the elevated access was used during the abandonment period
steps.desc: Review activity logs for any use of the elevated permissions since the account became abandoned.
steps.guidance: Elevated permissions raise the potential impact even if the account was never actively misused.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether elevated access was exercised.

steps.title: Revoke the elevated/legacy permission grants
steps.desc: Remove the administrative or legacy-role permissions from the account, independent of the disable action, so the grant itself is cleaned up.
steps.outcome: Elevated permissions revoked.

ITID-12439.def: Exploitation of an identity/credential bound to a physical or virtual device/endpoint (machine account, IoT device certificate, decommissioned laptop's cached credential) that was never deprovisioned when the device left service.
ITID-12439.purpose: Captures exploitation of an abandoned device or endpoint identity rather than a human or service user account.
scopeIncludes: Decommissioned device's machine account/certificate still trusted by the domain and exploited
IoT/OT device credential left active after the device was physically retired
scopeExcludes: Human user or service account abandonment (see other siblings in this Type)
ITID-12439.severity: Medium-High, escalating if the device had privileged network trust (e.g. domain-joined machine account).
ITID-12439.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if privileged network trust is confirmed.
ITID-12439.escalation: Escalate to IT asset management and IAM to revoke the device's trust/certificate and confirm physical decommissioning status.
indicators: Authentication or network activity from a machine account/certificate tied to a device marked as retired in asset inventory
Device certificate used from an unexpected network location post-decommissioning
vectors: Attacker extracting a still-valid device certificate/credential from discarded hardware
Retired device's machine account reused for network access after resale or disposal without proper wipe
rootCauses: No asset-decommissioning step to revoke device certificates/machine account trust
Device disposal process lacking secure wipe and credential revocation verification
controls: Asset-decommissioning checklist requiring certificate/machine-account revocation
Certificate authority revocation list (CRL) enforcement
ITID-12439.detection: Correlating asset-management decommissioning records against network authentication/certificate-use logs provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12439.response: Revoke the device's certificate/machine account immediately and confirm the physical device has been securely disposed of or recovered.
metrics: Count of retired-device credentials found still active per audit cycle
ITID-12439.notes: Scoped to non-human device/endpoint identities specifically, distinct from human and service-account abandonment covered elsewhere in this taxonomy.

playbook.name: Response: Abandoned Device/Endpoint Account Exploitation
playbook.description: For a local or device-bound account on an endpoint that was retired, replaced, or otherwise abandoned without the account being disabled.

steps.title: Confirm the device's status and the account's abandonment
steps.desc: Check asset management records to confirm the device was retired, reimaged, or replaced, and that the account was not carried forward into decommissioning.
steps.outcome: Confirmed device status and account abandonment.
steps.abort: If the device is still in active service, close as false positive.

steps.title: Disable the local/device account
steps.desc: Disable the account, whether local to the device or its associated directory identity.
steps.outcome: Account disabled.

steps.title: Assess what the device/account accessed while abandoned
steps.desc: Review what network resources or data the device/account reached during the abandonment window.
steps.outcome: Access footprint during abandonment documented.

steps.title: Formally decommission the device and account
steps.desc: Complete the device decommissioning process, including wiping the endpoint and removing its associated identity records.
steps.outcome: Device and account fully decommissioned.

steps.title: Tie device decommissioning to account disablement in the asset lifecycle process
steps.desc: Document the gap and recommend that device retirement workflows automatically trigger associated account disablement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a process fix recommended.

steps.title: Determine how the account/device has been reached and used
steps.desc: Review network and logon activity for the account or device, including whether the device is still connecting to the network or the account is being used remotely.
steps.guidance: An abandoned endpoint that still connects to the network can be a foothold even without active malicious use.
steps.outcome: Usage and connectivity pattern documented.

steps.title: Block the device from the network
steps.desc: Remove or quarantine the device's network access (e.g. NAC quarantine, certificate revocation, MAC-based block).
steps.outcome: Device blocked from network access.

ITID-12511.def: An incident involving a credential discovered exposed to the public internet, not yet matched to a more specific exposure channel.
ITID-12511.purpose: Catch-all for a publicly exposed credential that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific public exposure channel is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Public Exposure
Deliberate posting/sale of credentials on dark web/criminal channels (tracked under Dark Web Listing)
ITID-12511.escalation: Escalate to security engineering once the specific exposure channel is confirmed; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Secret-scanning or attack-surface-monitoring alert of unclear specific channel
vectors: Exposure of unclear specific channel
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Secret-scanning across public-facing surfaces
ITID-12511.detection: Same secret-scanning/attack-surface-monitoring telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12511.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed; rotate the credential immediately regardless of classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12511.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Publicly Exposed Credential
playbook.description: General-purpose checklist for a credential discovered publicly exposed before the specific exposure channel has been confirmed.

steps.title: Confirm the credential is real, current, and belongs to the organization
steps.desc: Validate the discovered credential against the organization's account inventory to confirm it is genuine, active, and not a decoy/expired test value.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the credential is real and currently valid, or ruled out.
steps.abort: If the credential is fake, expired, or unrelated to the organization, close as false positive.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret regardless of exposure channel, as the first priority action.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Hand off to the matching specific exposure-channel playbook
steps.desc: Once the channel is confirmed, escalate to and follow the specific playbook for detailed takedown/remediation steps.
steps.outcome: Incident reassigned with all evidence carried forward.

steps.title: Confirm the exposure is removed/taken down and the new credential is functioning
steps.desc: Verify the exposed content has been removed where possible and normal account access functions with the new credential.
steps.outcome: Exposure remediated and normal access restored.

steps.title: Document findings and recommend a control improvement
steps.desc: Record how the credential was exposed and recommend a control such as secret scanning, DLP, or a rotation policy.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; improvement ticket opened where applicable.

steps.title: Determine the exposure channel
steps.desc: Establish exactly where and how the credential was exposed — code repository, cloud storage, paste site, search index, API response, config file, documentation, or vendor leak.
steps.guidance: This determines which specific playbook to hand off to.
steps.outcome: Exposure channel identified.

steps.title: Revoke active sessions/tokens for the affected account
steps.desc: Terminate any existing session or token tied to the account as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Sessions/tokens invalidated.

steps.title: Check for evidence the credential has already been used maliciously
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for the associated account for suspicious activity since the credential's likely exposure date.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the exposed credential has been abused.

ITID-12512.def: A credential (API key, password, token, private key) embedded directly in application source code that has been pushed to a publicly accessible repository (GitHub, GitLab, npm/PyPI package, etc.).
ITID-12512.purpose: Captures a credential hardcoded into source code committed to a public code repository.
scopeIncludes: Hardcoded secret found in a public GitHub/GitLab repository via secret scanning
Credential embedded in a published open-source package or its commit history
scopeExcludes: Credential exposed via a misconfigured cloud storage bucket rather than a code repo (see ITID-12513)
Credential exposed in public documentation/wiki rather than source code itself (see ITID-12518)
ITID-12512.severity: High — public repositories are actively and continuously scanned by attackers.
ITID-12512.escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering leadership for credential rotation and commit-history scrubbing.
indicators: Third-party or internal secret-scanning tool flags a match in a public repository
Vendor (e.g. cloud provider) proactive notification of a leaked API key found in public code
vectors: Developer commits a secret directly into code instead of using environment variables/a secrets manager
Secret left in commit history even after later removal from the current file version
rootCauses: No pre-commit secret-scanning hook enforced
No developer training on secrets management for source control
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Pre-commit and repository-level secret scanning (e.g. GitHub secret scanning, gitleaks)
Mandatory secrets-manager usage policy for application code
ITID-12512.detection: Secret-scanning tools (native GitHub/GitLab scanning plus third-party tools) provide a strong, concrete, automatable technical signal.
ITID-12512.response: Rotate the exposed credential immediately, purge it from commit history, and verify no unauthorized use occurred before rotation.
metrics: Mean time to rotate a secret after public-repo detection
Count of hardcoded-secret findings per quarter
ITID-12512.notes: Scoped to source-code/commit-history exposure specifically, distinct from documentation (ITID-12518) and cloud storage (ITID-12513) exposure channels.

playbook.name: Response: Hardcoded Credential in Public Code Repository
playbook.description: For a credential (API key, password, connection string) discovered hardcoded in source code pushed to a public repository (e.g. GitHub, GitLab).

steps.title: Confirm the credential and its exact location in the repository
steps.desc: Identify the specific file, commit, and line where the credential appears, and confirm the repository's public visibility.
steps.outcome: Exact location and public-visibility status confirmed.
steps.tool: GitHub/GitLab secret scanning alert or manual discovery

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Revoke and reissue the exposed API key/password/secret.
steps.guidance: Do this before or in parallel with repository cleanup — rotation is the actual fix; removing the file from the current commit does not un-expose a value already scraped.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Deploy secret scanning / pre-commit hooks to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Enable repository-level secret scanning (e.g. GitHub secret scanning/push protection) and recommend pre-commit hooks for the affected team.
steps.guidance: This is the durable fix — the incident will recur without a preventive control.
steps.outcome: Secret scanning enabled on the repository or organization-wide.

steps.title: Verify the application functions correctly with the rotated credential
steps.desc: Confirm the affected service/application operates normally using the new credential loaded via the proper mechanism.
steps.outcome: Application confirmed functioning normally.

steps.title: Document and audit other repositories for the same exposure pattern
steps.desc: Record the finding and run an organization-wide secret scan across other repositories to check for similar hardcoded credentials.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; org-wide scan completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Determine how long the credential has been publicly exposed
steps.desc: Check the commit history to establish when the credential was first pushed, since it may have been indexed/cloned/cached by third parties for that entire duration.
steps.guidance: Assume the credential was compromised for its entire public-exposure window, not just from when it was discovered — public repos are continuously scraped by automated bots.
steps.outcome: Exposure window established.

steps.title: Remove the credential from the repository
steps.desc: Remove the offending file/line from the current codebase and purge it from git history (e.g. via git filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner), then force-push.
steps.guidance: Removing only the latest commit is insufficient — the credential remains visible in history unless history is rewritten.
steps.outcome: Credential removed from current code and from git history.

steps.title: Move the credential to a proper secrets management solution
steps.desc: Migrate the application to load the credential from a secrets manager or environment variable rather than hardcoding it, as part of the fix.
steps.outcome: Application no longer hardcodes secrets in source.

steps.title: Check for evidence of malicious use
steps.desc: Review logs for the associated account/service for suspicious activity since the exposure window began.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the credential has been abused.

ITID-12513.def: A credential file, backup, or configuration containing secrets discovered in a cloud storage bucket (S3, Azure Blob, GCS) that was misconfigured for public/anonymous read access.
ITID-12513.purpose: Captures a credential exposed through a misconfigured, publicly accessible cloud storage bucket.
scopeIncludes: Configuration or backup file containing credentials found in a publicly readable S3/Blob/GCS bucket
Database backup with embedded connection strings exposed via a misconfigured bucket
scopeExcludes: Credential hardcoded in source code (see ITID-12512)
Credential exposed via a public API response (see ITID-12516)
ITID-12513.severity: High — bucket misconfigurations are actively scanned by both researchers and attackers.
ITID-12513.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security engineering to remediate bucket permissions and rotate any exposed credentials.
indicators: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) tool flags a publicly readable bucket containing sensitive files
External researcher/bug bounty report of an open bucket with credential content
vectors: Bucket ACL/policy misconfigured to allow public or authenticated-any-AWS-user read access
Backup or log export process writing to a bucket without appropriate access restriction
rootCauses: No CSPM/automated guardrail preventing public bucket configuration
No data-classification-based control over what may be written to cloud storage
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: CSPM continuous scanning for public bucket exposure
Bucket-level default-deny public access policy
ITID-12513.detection: CSPM tooling provides a strong, concrete, continuous technical signal for this exposure class.
ITID-12513.response: Remediate bucket permissions immediately, rotate all exposed credentials, and review access logs for evidence of prior unauthorized access.
metrics: Count of public bucket exposures detected per quarter
Mean time to remediate public bucket misconfiguration
ITID-12513.notes: Scoped to cloud storage misconfiguration specifically, distinct from source-code (ITID-12512) and API-response (ITID-12516) exposure channels.

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed via Misconfigured Cloud Storage
playbook.description: For a credential discovered exposed because a cloud storage bucket/container (e.g. S3, Azure Blob, GCS) was misconfigured for public/overly broad access.

steps.title: Confirm the bucket/container's public exposure and the credential's presence
steps.desc: Verify the storage resource's access configuration and confirm the specific object(s) containing the credential.
steps.outcome: Confirmed misconfiguration and credential location.

steps.title: Restrict the bucket/container access immediately
steps.desc: Correct the access policy to remove public/overly broad access, restoring least-privilege access.
steps.outcome: Storage resource no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Remove the credential file from cloud storage or replace with a reference to a secrets manager
steps.desc: Eliminate the practice of storing raw credentials in cloud storage objects; migrate to a proper secrets management solution.
steps.outcome: Credential no longer stored as a raw file in cloud storage.

steps.title: Verify no other objects in the bucket are similarly exposed
steps.desc: Audit the remainder of the bucket's contents for other sensitive files that may have been exposed by the same misconfiguration.
steps.outcome: Bucket contents confirmed reviewed; any other exposed sensitive data addressed.

steps.title: Document and audit other cloud storage resources for the same misconfiguration
steps.desc: Record the finding and run an organization-wide scan for other publicly accessible storage resources.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; org-wide scan completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Determine how long the bucket has been publicly accessible
steps.desc: Review the bucket's configuration change history to establish when public access was enabled.
steps.outcome: Exposure window established.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential
steps.desc: Revoke and reissue the exposed credential.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Deploy or tighten CSPM policies to prevent public storage misconfiguration
steps.desc: Implement or tune cloud security posture management rules to automatically detect and alert on/block publicly exposed storage resources.
steps.outcome: CSPM guardrail deployed or tightened.

steps.title: Check access logs for evidence of external access to the credential file
steps.desc: Review the bucket's access logs for requests to the specific object from outside the organization's known IP ranges.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether external parties accessed the file.

ITID-12514.def: A credential discovered posted on a public text-paste service (Pastebin and similar) or a public technical forum (Stack Overflow, Reddit, vendor support forum), typically pasted incidentally alongside troubleshooting content.
ITID-12514.purpose: Captures a credential posted, intentionally or accidentally, on a public paste site or forum.
scopeIncludes: Credential visible in a code snippet or log output pasted to a public paste site for troubleshooting
Credential included in a public forum question/answer post
scopeExcludes: Deliberate criminal listing/sale of credentials on breach forums (tracked under Dark Web Listing)
Credential exposed via search engine indexing of an otherwise-intended-private page (see ITID-12515)
ITID-12514.escalation: Escalate to security engineering for immediate credential rotation and takedown request to the hosting platform.
indicators: Attack-surface/dark-web monitoring service flags a match on a paste site or forum
Internal staff member reports having posted a credential-containing snippet publicly
vectors: Developer pastes a config file or log excerpt containing a live credential while seeking troubleshooting help
Support staff posts a credential-containing example in a public help forum thread
rootCauses: No developer/staff training on redacting secrets before public sharing
No monitoring of paste sites/forums for organizational credential leakage
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Continuous paste-site/forum monitoring for organizational secrets
Staff training on secret redaction before public posting
ITID-12514.detection: Third-party attack-surface/leak-monitoring services that continuously crawl paste sites and forums provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12514.response: Rotate the credential immediately, request takedown of the post where feasible, and reinforce redaction training.
metrics: Count of paste-site/forum credential exposures detected per quarter
ITID-12514.notes: Scoped to incidental public posting on paste/forum platforms, distinct from deliberate criminal-market listing (Dark Web Listing branch).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed in Public Paste Site/Forum Post
playbook.description: For a credential discovered posted on a public paste site (e.g. Pastebin) or forum, whether intentionally leaked or accidentally shared.

steps.title: Confirm the credential and capture the posting as evidence
steps.desc: Verify the credential is genuine and preserve a screenshot/archive of the post before it may be taken down or edited.
steps.outcome: Credential confirmed and post preserved as evidence.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Investigate how the credential ended up on the paste site
steps.desc: Determine the original source of the leak — was it scraped from another exposure (repo, config file), leaked by an insider, or obtained via a breach elsewhere.
steps.outcome: Root source of the leak identified where possible.

steps.title: Confirm normal access restored with the new credential
steps.desc: Verify the affected account/service functions normally with the rotated credential.
steps.outcome: Normal access confirmed restored.

steps.title: Document and expand dark web/paste site monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Record the finding and confirm ongoing monitoring coverage for the organization's credentials appearing on paste sites/forums.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; monitoring coverage confirmed or expanded.

steps.title: Determine the posting context and likely intent
steps.desc: Assess whether the post appears to be an intentional leak/dump, an accidental share (e.g. a debugging paste that included credentials), or part of a larger breach disclosure.
steps.outcome: Posting context and likely intent established.

steps.title: Submit a takedown request to the paste site/forum
steps.desc: Request removal of the post through the platform's abuse/takedown process.
steps.guidance: Takedown success varies by platform and is not guaranteed — treat rotation as the actual control, takedown as a secondary mitigation.
steps.outcome: Takedown request submitted.

steps.title: Remediate the root source if identified
steps.desc: If the paste originated from another exposure channel (e.g. a code repository or vendor breach), follow the corresponding specific playbook to close that root cause.
steps.outcome: Root source remediated where identified.
steps.abort: If no root source can be identified, document as an investigative gap.

steps.title: Check for evidence of malicious use since posting
steps.desc: Review authentication/service logs for suspicious activity since the post's likely creation date.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the credential has been abused.

ITID-12515.def: A credential discoverable via a standard web search engine (Google, Bing) because a page containing it — a misconfigured directory listing, an unindexed-by-intent but crawlable admin page, a cached document — was indexed.
ITID-12515.purpose: Captures a credential surfaced through general search engine indexing of a page not intended to be discoverable.
scopeIncludes: Credential found via a targeted Google dork/search query against organizational domains
Cached search-engine snapshot containing credentials from a page since removed but still indexed
scopeExcludes: Credential exposed via a misconfigured cloud storage bucket (see ITID-12513, even if that bucket is also search-indexed — classify by the underlying misconfiguration)
Credential exposed in a public API response (see ITID-12516)
ITID-12515.escalation: Escalate to web/security engineering to remove the page, rotate the credential, and request search engine cache removal.
indicators: Attack-surface monitoring flags a search-indexable page containing credential material
Internal security team's periodic Google-dork sweep against organizational domains returns a match
vectors: robots.txt or noindex directive missing/misconfigured on a sensitive page
Legacy page containing credentials left online and crawlable after its intended retirement
rootCauses: No periodic proactive search-engine exposure sweep of organizational domains
No consistent noindex/robots policy applied to internal-only web content
mitreTechniques: T1593.002 Search Open Websites/Domains: Search Engines
T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Periodic search-engine exposure sweep (Google dorking) of organizational domains
robots.txt/noindex enforcement for internal-only content
ITID-12515.detection: Periodic automated search-engine exposure sweeps and attack-surface-management tooling provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12515.response: Remove/restrict the page, rotate the credential, and submit a search engine cache-removal request.
metrics: Count of search-indexed credential exposures found per sweep cycle
ITID-12515.notes: Scoped to general search-engine discoverability as the exposure mechanism, distinct from the underlying misconfiguration classes covered by ITID-12513 (cloud storage) and ITID-12516 (API responses).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed via Search Engine Indexing
playbook.description: For a credential discovered exposed because a page or file containing it was crawled and indexed by a public search engine (Google dorking exposure).

steps.title: Confirm the indexed page/file and the credential's presence
steps.desc: Access the indexed URL (via cache if the live page has changed) to confirm the credential is genuinely present and readable.
steps.outcome: Confirmed indexed content and credential presence.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Submit a search engine removal request to expedite de-indexing
steps.desc: Use the search engine's URL removal tool (e.g. Google Search Console) to expedite removal of the cached content, since natural re-crawl can take time.
steps.outcome: Removal request submitted.

steps.title: Verify the content is no longer indexed and access is restricted
steps.desc: Confirm via search engine query and direct access test that the content is no longer publicly reachable.
steps.outcome: Confirmed content removed from index and access restricted.

steps.title: Document and run a broader search-exposure audit
steps.desc: Record the finding and run a broader dorking-style audit of the organization's public web presence for similar exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; broader audit completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Determine the underlying hosting location and how it became publicly crawlable
steps.desc: Identify the actual server/service hosting the file and why it was accessible to search engine crawlers (missing authentication, missing robots.txt exclusion, misconfigured web server).
steps.outcome: Hosting location and root exposure cause identified.
steps.tool: Web server logs / hosting configuration review

steps.title: Remove or restrict access to the underlying file/page
steps.desc: Delete the file, move it behind authentication, or otherwise restrict access at the hosting level.
steps.outcome: Underlying content no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Fix the root cause preventing future indexing of sensitive content
steps.desc: Implement proper access controls, robots.txt exclusions, and/or noindex meta tags on sensitive paths, and review the web server configuration that allowed the file to be publicly reachable in the first place.
steps.outcome: Root cause of public crawlability fixed.

steps.title: Estimate how long the content has been indexed and check for evidence of access
steps.desc: Use search engine cache date and web server access logs to estimate exposure duration and check for suspicious access to the file.
steps.outcome: Exposure window and access evidence established.
steps.tool: Search engine tools / web server logs

ITID-12516.def: A credential or secret exposed because a production or public-facing API returns it in a response body, error message, or verbose debug/stack-trace output.
ITID-12516.purpose: Captures a credential inadvertently returned in a public-facing API response or debug output.
scopeIncludes: API error response including a database connection string or internal API key in a stack trace
Verbose debug mode left enabled in production, exposing configuration secrets in responses
scopeExcludes: Credential exposed via a static configuration file rather than dynamic API/application output (see ITID-12517)
Credential exposed via cloud storage misconfiguration (see ITID-12513)
ITID-12516.severity: High — actively and trivially discoverable by automated scanning of the API surface.
ITID-12516.escalation: Escalate immediately to application engineering to disable debug output and rotate the exposed credential.
indicators: Automated API security scanning tool flags a credential/secret pattern in a response body
Bug bounty or researcher report of secrets in error responses
vectors: Debug/verbose error mode left enabled in a production deployment
Unhandled exception exposing internal configuration in the response payload
rootCauses: No environment-specific configuration hardening step disabling debug output for production
Inadequate exception handling that surfaces internal state to API consumers
mitreTechniques: T1552.005 Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Production deployment hardening disabling debug/verbose error output
Automated API security scanning (DAST) for secret leakage in responses
ITID-12516.detection: DAST/API security scanning tooling provides a concrete, automatable technical signal.
ITID-12516.response: Disable debug output immediately, rotate the exposed credential, and add regression testing to prevent recurrence.
metrics: Count of API/debug-output credential exposures detected per quarter
ITID-12516.notes: Scoped to dynamic application/API output specifically, distinct from static configuration files (ITID-12517).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed in Public API Response/Debug Output
playbook.description: For a credential discovered exposed because a public-facing API response or debug/error output inadvertently included it (e.g. a verbose error message, a debug endpoint, or an over-permissive API field).

steps.title: Confirm the exposure and reproduce the API call/condition that triggers it
steps.desc: Identify the specific endpoint, parameter, or error condition that causes the credential to appear in the response, and confirm it is reproducible.
steps.outcome: Exposure confirmed and reproduction steps documented.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret that was exposed in the response.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Fix the application to prevent credentials from appearing in API responses/error output
steps.desc: Work with the development team to sanitize error handling and API response serialization so sensitive fields are never included, and disable verbose debug output in production configuration.
steps.guidance: This is the definitive fix; treat as a required code and configuration change.
steps.outcome: Fix deployed and confirmed to no longer expose the credential.

steps.title: Verify the fix via the same reproduction steps used in identification
steps.desc: Attempt the same API call/error condition that previously exposed the credential and confirm it is no longer present in the response.
steps.outcome: Fix confirmed effective.

steps.title: Document and add a response-sanitization check to the secure development checklist
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend this check be added to the AppSec review checklist for future API development.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; AppSec checklist updated.

steps.title: Determine how long the endpoint/condition has existed in production
steps.desc: Review deployment history to establish when the vulnerable code was deployed to production.
steps.outcome: Exposure window established.

steps.title: Disable the vulnerable endpoint or debug mode as an emergency measure
steps.desc: If feasible, take the affected endpoint offline or disable debug/verbose error output in production immediately, pending a proper fix.
steps.outcome: Exposure condition no longer reachable.

steps.title: Review API access logs for evidence the exposing response was actually observed
steps.desc: Check API gateway logs for calls that would have triggered the exposing condition/response, and from what source.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the exposure was likely observed by an external party.

ITID-12517.def: A credential embedded in a static configuration file (.env, web.config, config.json, .git/config) that is directly web-accessible due to a deployment or web-server misconfiguration.
ITID-12517.purpose: Captures a credential left in a static configuration file that is publicly accessible.
scopeIncludes: Publicly fetchable .env or config file containing plaintext credentials on a production web server
Exposed .git directory allowing reconstruction of configuration history containing secrets
scopeExcludes: Credential dynamically returned in an API response (see ITID-12516)
Credential in a code repository's version-controlled source (see ITID-12512)
ITID-12517.severity: High — configuration files often contain multiple high-value secrets in one location.
ITID-12517.escalation: Escalate immediately to web/platform engineering to remove public access and rotate all secrets in the file.
indicators: Attack-surface scanning identifies a directly fetchable configuration file at a predictable path
Exposed .git directory discovered via automated scanning
vectors: Web server misconfiguration failing to block access to dotfiles/config directories
Deployment process copying configuration files into the public web root
rootCauses: No web-server hardening rule blocking access to configuration file extensions/paths
Deployment pipeline not separating configuration from publicly served content
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Web-server hardening rules blocking access to configuration file patterns
Deployment pipeline separation of secrets from public web root
ITID-12517.detection: Attack-surface-management scanning for common configuration file paths provides a concrete, automatable technical signal.
ITID-12517.response: Block public access immediately, rotate every credential the file contained, and audit for evidence of prior access.
metrics: Count of exposed configuration files detected per quarter
ITID-12517.notes: Scoped to static, deployed configuration files specifically, distinct from source-controlled code (ITID-12512) and dynamic API output (ITID-12516).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed in Public Configuration File
playbook.description: For a credential discovered exposed because a configuration file (e.g. .env, web.config, application.yml) was inadvertently made publicly accessible via the web server or deployment artifact.

steps.title: Confirm the configuration file is publicly accessible and contains the credential
steps.desc: Directly access the file's public URL to confirm exposure and catalogue every credential/secret it contains, not just the one initially reported.
steps.guidance: Configuration files frequently contain multiple secrets — treat this as a multi-credential exposure until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: File confirmed publicly accessible; full list of contained secrets catalogued.

steps.title: Restrict access to the configuration file immediately
steps.desc: Remove the file from the web-accessible directory or add a web server rule blocking access to it.
steps.outcome: File no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Fix the deployment/build process to exclude configuration files from the web-accessible directory
steps.desc: Correct the deployment pipeline or web server document root configuration so configuration files are never placed in a publicly servable location.
steps.outcome: Deployment process confirmed to exclude config files from public paths.

steps.title: Verify the fix and confirm the application functions with rotated credentials
steps.desc: Confirm the file is no longer accessible and the application operates normally with the new credentials.
steps.outcome: Fix verified; application functioning normally.

steps.title: Document and audit other deployments for the same exposure pattern
steps.desc: Record the finding and check other applications/deployments for the same configuration-file exposure pattern.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; sweep completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Determine how long the file has been publicly accessible
steps.desc: Review web server/deployment logs to establish when the file became reachable.
steps.outcome: Exposure window established.

steps.title: Rotate every credential/secret contained in the file
steps.desc: Reset every credential catalogued in identification, not just the originally reported one.
steps.outcome: All contained credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Migrate to a proper secrets management solution
steps.desc: Move secrets out of flat configuration files entirely in favor of a secrets manager or environment-injected values.
steps.outcome: Application no longer relies on a static file for secrets.

steps.title: Check for evidence of access and malicious use of any contained credential
steps.desc: Review web server access logs for requests to the file, and check authentication/service logs for each contained credential for suspicious activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed access evidence and whether any credential was abused.

ITID-12518.def: A credential included, typically as an oversight during authoring, in publicly published documentation such as a knowledge base article, API reference, README, or public wiki page.
ITID-12518.purpose: Captures a credential exposed through published, human-authored public documentation.
scopeIncludes: Sample/example credential in public API documentation that is actually a live, working credential
README or public wiki page containing an embedded live secret
scopeExcludes: Credential exposed in a code repository's source/commit history rather than authored documentation content (see ITID-12512)
Credential exposed via search engine indexing of an unintentionally crawlable page (see ITID-12515)
ITID-12518.escalation: Escalate to the documentation owner and security engineering for immediate redaction and credential rotation.
indicators: Secret-scanning tooling extended to documentation platforms flags a match
Reader/customer report of a working credential found in public documentation
vectors: Author copies a real configuration example into documentation without sanitizing the credential
Screenshot embedded in documentation reveals a live credential in the UI
rootCauses: No review process requiring sanitized/placeholder credentials in documentation examples
Documentation platform not included in the scope of secret-scanning tooling
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Secret-scanning extended to documentation/knowledge-base platforms
Documentation review checklist requiring placeholder credentials in examples
ITID-12518.detection: Secret-scanning tooling extended to cover documentation platforms provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12518.response: Redact the documentation immediately, rotate the credential, and confirm no unauthorized use occurred.
metrics: Count of documentation-based credential exposures detected per quarter
ITID-12518.notes: Scoped to authored documentation content specifically, distinct from source code (ITID-12512).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed via Public Documentation
playbook.description: For a credential discovered exposed because it was included as an example/placeholder in publicly published documentation (internal wiki made public, API docs, README, runbook) — often a real value mistakenly left in place of a sanitized example.

steps.title: Confirm the credential in the documentation is a real, live value rather than a sanitized example
steps.desc: Test or validate the credential against the associated system to confirm it is genuinely active rather than a placeholder/dummy value.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the credential is real and live, or ruled out as a benign placeholder.
steps.abort: If confirmed to be a properly sanitized dummy value, close as false positive.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Establish a documentation review practice to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Recommend a review step (peer review, automated secret scanning on documentation platforms where supported) before publishing operational documentation.
steps.outcome: Review practice recommended or implemented.

steps.title: Verify normal access restored with the new credential
steps.desc: Confirm the affected account/service functions normally with the rotated credential.
steps.outcome: Normal access confirmed restored.

steps.title: Document and audit other documentation for the same exposure pattern
steps.desc: Record the finding and review other internal/public documentation for similarly exposed real credentials used as examples.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; sweep completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Determine the documentation's publication scope and how long it has been public
steps.desc: Establish whether the documentation is fully public or has restricted-but-broad access, and how long it has been in its current state.
steps.outcome: Publication scope and exposure window established.

steps.title: Redact the credential from the documentation
steps.desc: Edit the documentation to remove or replace the real value with a properly sanitized placeholder, and check the platform's revision history for the same exposure.
steps.guidance: Like code repositories, many documentation platforms retain version history — the credential may remain visible in prior revisions unless those are also addressed.
steps.outcome: Documentation and its accessible revision history no longer expose the credential.

steps.title: Check for evidence of malicious use
steps.desc: Review authentication/service logs for suspicious activity since the exposure window began.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the credential has been abused.

ITID-12519.def: Organizational credentials (typically for a shared platform or integration) exposed because a third-party vendor suffered its own breach or public exposure incident, unrelated to any control failure within the organization itself.
ITID-12519.purpose: Captures organizational credentials exposed as a consequence of a third-party vendor's own, independent public leak.
scopeIncludes: Vendor's public breach disclosure confirming exposure of organizational account credentials it held
Vendor's own misconfigured infrastructure exposing customer credentials it stored
scopeExcludes: Organization's own control failure causing exposure (see other siblings in this Type)
Compromise of the organization's own service account used to integrate with the vendor (tracked under Service Account Exploitation)
ITID-12519.severity: High — response is largely reactive and dependent on vendor disclosure timeliness.
ITID-12519.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management and legal upon vendor breach notification; treat all credentials held by that vendor as compromised.
indicators: Vendor breach notification naming the organization as an affected customer
Dark-web/breach monitoring service correlating a leaked credential set to a known third-party vendor breach
vectors: Vendor's own systems compromised, exposing customer credential databases
Vendor's misconfigured storage/logging exposing customer secrets
rootCauses: Reliance on a vendor without independent verification of its security posture (inadequate vendor risk assessment)
No contractual requirement for prompt vendor breach notification
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Vendor risk assessment and breach-notification contractual requirements
Dark-web/breach monitoring covering known vendor relationships
ITID-12519.detection: Vendor breach notifications and dark-web monitoring correlated to known vendor relationships provide the primary, largely reactive signal here.
ITID-12519.response: Rotate all credentials associated with the affected vendor relationship immediately upon notification, regardless of confirmed misuse.
metrics: Mean time to rotate credentials following vendor breach notification
Count of vendor-breach-driven credential rotations per year
detections: Dark-web monitoring correlated to known vendor breaches
ITID-12519.notes: Scoped to leakage originating from the vendor's own environment/control failure, not the organization's; distinguishes root-cause attribution from other Public Exposure siblings which are internally caused.

playbook.name: Response: Credential Exposed via Third-Party Vendor's Own Public Leak
playbook.description: For a credential exposed not because of the organization's own error, but because a third-party vendor/partner publicly leaked data (their own repository, misconfigured storage, breach disclosure) that included the organization's credential.

steps.title: Confirm the credential belongs to the organization and validate it
steps.desc: Confirm the leaked credential is genuinely associated with the organization's account/integration with the vendor, and check whether it is still active.
steps.outcome: Confirmed ownership and current validity.
steps.abort: If the credential is stale/already rotated or unrelated, close as informational.

steps.title: Rotate the exposed credential on the organization's side immediately
steps.desc: Reset the password/API key/secret used for the vendor integration, regardless of whether the vendor has completed their own remediation.
steps.guidance: Do not wait on the vendor's timeline — the organization controls credential rotation on its own side of the integration.
steps.outcome: Exposed credential invalidated.

steps.title: Re-establish the vendor integration with the new credential
steps.desc: Confirm the integration functions correctly with the rotated credential.
steps.outcome: Integration confirmed functioning with new credential.

steps.title: Verify normal integration function and monitor for anomalies
steps.desc: Confirm the integration operates normally and monitor for any anomalous activity tied to the (now rotated) credential.
steps.outcome: Normal operation confirmed; no anomalies observed.

steps.title: Document the third-party exposure and update vendor risk records
steps.desc: Record the finding, the vendor's role, and update the organization's vendor risk assessment/tracking to reflect this incident.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; vendor risk record updated.

steps.title: Determine the vendor, the nature of their leak, and the exposure scope
steps.desc: Identify which vendor was responsible, how their leak occurred, and whether other organizations' credentials were also exposed (indicating a broader vendor incident).
steps.outcome: Vendor and leak details documented.

steps.title: Notify the vendor and request their incident details/remediation status
steps.desc: Formally notify the vendor of the finding and request details on their remediation, scope, and root cause.
steps.outcome: Vendor notified and engaged.

steps.title: Assess the vendor relationship given the incident
steps.desc: Review the vendor's security posture and incident response given this leak, and determine whether continued use warrants additional controls, contract review, or escalation to procurement/legal.
steps.outcome: Vendor risk assessment completed and documented.

steps.title: Check for evidence of malicious use of the credential
steps.desc: Review authentication/service logs for suspicious activity associated with the exposed credential.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the credential has been abused.

ITID-12521.def: An incident involving discovery of organizational credentials listed for criminal use on a dark web or underground channel, not yet matched to a more specific listing type.
ITID-12521.purpose: Catch-all for a dark web credential listing that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific listing channel/type (marketplace, breach forum, leak site, etc.) is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Dark Web Listing

Bulk stolen-data-for-sale listings tracked under the general data-breach/fraud domain (see ITID-51941 Unclassified / General Credentials Reuse Package Listing under Data-for-Sale Dark Web Dump Context) — this branch is scoped specifically to credentials intended for account/identity compromise, not general bulk data-dump monetization
ITID-12521.priority: P1 by default given active criminal marketing of the credential.
ITID-12521.escalation: Escalate to security engineering once the specific listing channel is confirmed; force credential rotation immediately regardless of classification.
indicators: Dark-web monitoring feed alert of unclear specific listing type
vectors: Listing of unclear specific channel
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Dark-web/underground-market credential monitoring
ITID-12521.detection: Same dark-web monitoring telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12521.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed; rotate the credential immediately.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12521.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Deliberately scoped away from ITID-51941 and the broader Data-for-Sale Dark Web Dump Context group, which cover general bulk data-breach monetization rather than identity/authentication-focused credential listings.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Dark Web Credential Listing
playbook.description: For a general credential listing discovered on a dark web forum, marketplace, or paste site that has not yet been categorized into a more specific listing type.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the listing
steps.desc: Take a full screenshot/HTML capture of the listing, the posting date, seller/poster handle, and forum/source URL before it can be edited or removed.
steps.guidance: Use the threat-intel platform's capture tooling rather than a manual browser screenshot where possible, to preserve metadata.
steps.outcome: Timestamped evidence of the listing preserved outside the source site.

steps.title: Force password reset on all implicated accounts
steps.desc: Immediately reset credentials for every account confirmed or reasonably suspected to be exposed.
steps.guidance: Prioritize privileged and externally-facing accounts first.
steps.outcome: All implicated accounts have new credentials; old credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Check for signs of account misuse prior to rotation
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs for the affected accounts for anomalous logins, new devices, or new forwarding rules dated before the reset.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the exposed credentials were used prior to containment.

steps.title: Confirm normal account operation and close monitoring window
steps.desc: Verify affected users can authenticate normally with new credentials and that no residual anomalous activity persists.
steps.guidance: Keep a short heightened-monitoring window (7-14 days) on the affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Accounts confirmed operating normally under new credentials.

steps.title: Document source, scope, and exposure pathway
steps.desc: Record where the listing originated, how the credentials likely leaked (if determinable), and any control gaps identified.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with recommended follow-up if a systemic leak source is suspected.

steps.title: Determine which credentials and accounts are exposed
steps.desc: Review any sample data, hashes, or free-form text in the listing to identify affected usernames, email addresses, and domains.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference exposed identifiers against the organization's directory to confirm they are real, current accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of specific accounts named or plausibly implicated by the listing.
steps.abort: If no organizational accounts can be confirmed, downgrade to a monitoring-only note.

steps.title: Enforce or verify MFA on affected accounts
steps.desc: Confirm MFA is enabled for each affected account and enroll any accounts found without it.
steps.outcome: MFA active on all affected accounts.

steps.title: Assess listing authenticity and scope
steps.desc: Determine whether the listing is a genuine new exposure, a re-post of previously known/remediated data, or a scam/fabricated listing intended to extort or mislead.
steps.guidance: Check credential age indicators, prior breach databases, and seller reputation on the forum.
steps.outcome: Listing classified as genuine-new, re-post of known data, or unverified/fabricated.

ITID-12522.def: Listing of organizational credentials or an authenticated foothold packaged and sold as "access-as-a-service" on a criminal marketplace, typically by an Initial Access Broker offering a specific, verified entry point rather than a raw credential list.
ITID-12522.purpose: Captures organizational access being sold as a discrete, ready-to-use service on a criminal marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Marketplace listing offering verified VPN/RDP/admin access to the organization for a set price
Listing explicitly advertising "access" rather than a bare credential or data dump
scopeExcludes: General Initial Access Broker profile/reputation activity not tied to a specific active listing (see ITID-12527)
Raw bulk credential dumps with no access packaging (see ITID-12523)
ITID-12522.severity: Critical — indicates a specific, likely-verified entry point is actively for sale.
ITID-12522.escalation: Immediate escalation to incident response; treat as an active precursor to intrusion and initiate full credential rotation plus threat hunting for the advertised access vector.
indicators: Dark-web monitoring feed match naming the organization with an access-for-sale listing
Listing description matching specific internal technology (VPN vendor, RDP, named admin panel) consistent with organizational infrastructure
vectors: Compromised VPN/RDP credential packaged and resold by an Initial Access Broker
Compromised admin panel access resold as a verified foothold
rootCauses: Externally facing remote-access service compromised and not yet detected internally
controls: Dark-web monitoring for access-as-a-service listings referencing the organization
Emergency credential rotation and remote-access session termination playbook
ITID-12522.detection: Dark-web monitoring services specializing in IAB/marketplace listings provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12522.response: Treat as an active, imminent intrusion threat: rotate all potentially affected credentials, terminate active remote-access sessions, and hunt for signs the access has already been used or resold.
metrics: Mean time from listing detection to full remediation
ITID-12522.notes: Differentiator vs. ITID-12527 is the presence of a specific active listing for sale, vs. general broker activity/reputation tracking.

playbook.name: Response: Credential Marketplace Listing (Access-as-a-Service)
playbook.description: For credentials advertised for sale on a dedicated dark web credential marketplace, typically sold individually or in small curated batches as a repeatable access-as-a-service offering.

steps.title: Capture the marketplace listing and pricing details
steps.desc: Preserve the listing including price, described access level, sample data, and any buyer reviews or transaction history for the seller.
steps.guidance: Buyer reviews on marketplace listings can indicate whether the access has already sold.
steps.outcome: Listing preserved with commercial details intact.

steps.title: Force credential rotation on every advertised account
steps.desc: Reset credentials for all accounts matching the advertised access, treating a 'sold' status as evidence of likely active compromise.
steps.guidance: Escalate priority if the listing indicates a completed sale.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated for all matching accounts.

steps.title: Hunt for evidence of buyer access or persistence
steps.desc: Review authentication logs, VPN logs, and endpoint telemetry for the affected accounts for signs a buyer already used the access.
steps.guidance: Pay particular attention to logins from unfamiliar geographies or ASNs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of unauthorized access.

steps.title: Restore verified-clean access and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm affected users can authenticate normally and maintain heightened monitoring on the accounts for an extended window.
steps.guidance: Given the commercial nature of the listing, extend monitoring to 30 days.
steps.outcome: Accounts restored and under active monitoring.

steps.title: Document the marketplace source and access pathway
steps.desc: Record the marketplace, price point, advertised access, and any identified root cause of the exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and shared with threat intel team for ongoing monitoring of the seller.

steps.title: Identify the specific accounts and access level advertised
steps.desc: Determine which credentials, systems, or access level (VPN, email, admin panel, etc.) the marketplace listing claims to provide.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against directory and asset inventory.
steps.outcome: Confirmed accounts/systems matching the advertised access.
steps.abort: If no organizational match can be confirmed, downgrade to monitoring-only.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and review active sessions
steps.desc: Enroll MFA where missing and revoke all active sessions/tokens for affected accounts.
steps.outcome: MFA enforced and all prior sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Check whether the listing shows signs of a completed sale
steps.desc: Review listing status, comments, or escrow indicators for evidence the access has already been purchased.
steps.outcome: Determined whether the listing is still active-for-sale or marked sold.

ITID-12523.def: Discovery of organizational credentials as part of a large-scale, typically third-party-origin bulk credential dump posted to a breach/hacking forum, distinct from a curated, targeted listing.
ITID-12523.purpose: Captures organizational credentials appearing within a large, bulk credential dump posted to a breach forum.
scopeIncludes: Organizational domain email addresses/passwords found within a mega-breach combolist posted to a forum
Bulk dump containing organizational credentials as a small subset of a much larger, unrelated-source dataset
scopeExcludes: Curated, packaged access-for-sale listings (see ITID-12522)
Targeted, employee-specific credential bundles (see ITID-12529)
ITID-12523.severity: Medium-High — credentials here are often stale/reused-password-sourced rather than from a direct organizational breach.
ITID-12523.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials are confirmed still valid.
ITID-12523.escalation: Escalate to IAM to force password reset for affected accounts and verify no active reuse.
indicators: Breach-monitoring service match against a known, named bulk dump/combolist
Multiple organizational accounts appearing together within the same forum-posted dataset
vectors: Password reuse across a third-party breached site later aggregated into a bulk dump
Historical, unrelated third-party breach whose credentials happen to include organizational email addresses
rootCauses: Employees reusing corporate credentials/email addresses on external, lower-security third-party sites
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Breach-forum/combolist monitoring for organizational domain matches
Mandatory password reset and MFA enforcement upon credential-stuffing exposure
ITID-12523.detection: Breach-monitoring services matching organizational domains against known dump sources provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12523.response: Force password reset for all confirmed affected accounts and verify MFA enrollment before re-enabling access.
metrics: Count of organizational credentials found in bulk dumps per quarter
ITID-12523.notes: Differentiator is the bulk, largely third-party-sourced nature of the dump vs. targeted employee-specific bundles (ITID-12529) or curated access listings (ITID-12522).

playbook.name: Response: Breach Forum Bulk Credential Dump Listing
playbook.description: For organizational credentials found within a large bulk credential dump posted to a breach forum, typically aggregated from an unrelated third-party breach rather than a direct compromise.

steps.title: Preserve the dump listing and obtain a sample
steps.desc: Capture the forum post details and, where safely obtainable through the threat-intel provider, a sample of the dump content relevant to the organization's domains.
steps.guidance: Do not download the raw dump directly from the forum; use the threat-intel vendor's sanitized feed where available.
steps.outcome: Listing and relevant sample preserved.

steps.title: Force password reset for confirmed current accounts
steps.desc: Reset credentials for every account confirmed as current and matching the dump.
steps.guidance: Prioritize accounts where the dump's plaintext or cracked password still matches or resembles the account's current password.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated for all matched current accounts.

steps.title: Check for password reuse across other systems
steps.desc: Determine whether affected users reused the exposed password on other organizational systems and rotate those as well.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with app owners for systems outside central identity provider.
steps.outcome: Password reuse identified and remediated across all in-scope systems.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and notify affected users
steps.desc: Verify affected users can authenticate and provide brief guidance on password hygiene and reuse.
steps.outcome: Users restored to normal access with reuse guidance delivered.

steps.title: Log dump source and reuse findings
steps.desc: Record the originating breach, number of matched accounts, and any password-reuse patterns identified for future control improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Extract and validate organizational credentials from the dump
steps.desc: Filter the dump for the organization's email domains and validate matched accounts against the directory.
steps.guidance: Bulk dumps often include stale or already-changed passwords; check credential age where timestamps are available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of current, valid organizational accounts present in the dump.
steps.abort: If no current accounts match, log as informational only.

steps.title: Enforce MFA on matched accounts
steps.desc: Confirm or enroll MFA on all matched accounts.
steps.outcome: MFA active on all matched accounts.

steps.title: Determine likely source of the underlying breach
steps.desc: Identify which third-party breach the dump originated from, if disclosed, to assess whether it is a known/already-notified event or a new exposure.
steps.outcome: Source breach identified or confirmed unknown.

ITID-12524.def: Discovery of organizational credentials within data published (or threatened for publication) on a ransomware group's dedicated leak site, typically as part of double-extortion following a ransomware incident.
ITID-12524.purpose: Captures organizational credentials exposed specifically via a ransomware group's data-leak site.
scopeIncludes: Credentials found within data samples or full dumps posted to a ransomware group's leak site
Threatened publication of credential-containing data as ransomware extortion leverage
scopeExcludes: Credential exposure unrelated to a ransomware/extortion event (see other siblings in this Type)
ITID-12524.severity: Critical — directly tied to a confirmed or highly probable ransomware compromise.
ITID-12524.escalation: Immediate escalation to the active ransomware incident response effort; this is not a standalone incident but a symptom of a broader compromise requiring full IR engagement.
indicators: Ransomware group leak-site posting naming the organization
Sample data published containing organizational credential material as extortion proof-of-access
vectors: Ransomware actor exfiltrating credential stores (password managers, hash dumps, config files) prior to encryption
Double-extortion publication of stolen data including credentials
rootCauses: Underlying ransomware intrusion root cause (tracked in the corresponding ransomware incident record, not duplicated here)
controls: Leak-site monitoring integrated with ransomware incident response
Full credential rotation as part of ransomware IR containment
ITID-12524.detection: Dedicated ransomware leak-site monitoring services provide a real, concrete technical signal, typically surfaced already during active IR.
ITID-12524.response: Coordinate with the active ransomware incident response team; rotate all potentially exposed credentials as part of the broader containment and recovery effort.
metrics: Count of confirmed leak-site credential exposures per ransomware incident
ITID-12524.notes: This leaf documents the credential-leakage consequence of a ransomware event specifically; the intrusion itself is scoped and root-caused under the separate ransomware/malware ITID branch to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Group Leak Site Credential Exposure
playbook.description: For organizational credentials found published or referenced on a ransomware group's extortion/leak site, typically as proof of compromise or as part of a data-leak package during a double-extortion campaign.

steps.title: Preserve the leak site listing and any published sample data
steps.desc: Capture the ransomware group's listing, victim page, claimed data volume, and any sample credential files published.
steps.guidance: Engage legal/incident response leadership immediately given the likely severity of a ransomware-linked exposure.
steps.outcome: Listing and sample data preserved.

steps.title: Force organization-wide credential rotation for all exposed accounts
steps.desc: Reset credentials for every account identified in the leak, treating this as a confirmed-compromise scenario.
steps.guidance: Given ransomware context, also consider broader precautionary rotation of privileged accounts.
steps.outcome: All exposed and privileged credentials rotated.

steps.title: Hunt for ransomware precursor activity and persistence
steps.desc: Search endpoint and network telemetry for indicators associated with the identified ransomware group's known tactics.
steps.guidance: Engage the broader ransomware incident response playbook if active intrusion indicators are found.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of active ransomware precursor activity.

steps.title: Restore verified-clean access under close monitoring
steps.desc: Restore affected accounts and systems only after confirming no persistence remains, with extended heightened monitoring.
steps.outcome: Accounts and systems restored under active monitoring.

steps.title: Document exposure, notify stakeholders, and record findings
steps.desc: Record the ransomware group, exposure scope, and coordinate any required legal/regulatory notification with leadership.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and stakeholders notified per policy.

steps.title: Determine whether this reflects an active or prior known intrusion
steps.desc: Cross-reference the leak site claim against any known active incident or prior ransomware event to determine if this is a new intrusion or disclosure tied to a previously contained event.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the incident commander for any related active ransomware case.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this listing is linked to a known, active incident.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and isolate affected systems if intrusion is active
steps.desc: Enforce MFA on all exposed accounts and coordinate with the network team to isolate any systems suspected of active compromise.
steps.outcome: MFA enforced; any actively compromised systems isolated.

steps.title: Identify all credentials and systems referenced in the leak
steps.desc: Catalog every account, system, and credential type referenced in the published or sampled data.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of exposed credentials and affected systems.

ITID-12525.def: Discovery of organizational credentials posted, sold, or shared within a Telegram channel/group or other encrypted-messaging-based criminal marketplace, a channel increasingly favored over traditional forums.
ITID-12525.purpose: Captures organizational credentials shared or sold via a Telegram channel or other encrypted messaging platform.
scopeIncludes: Credentials posted in a monitored Telegram channel known for credential trading
Automated "logs" bot output (e.g. stealer-log distribution channels) containing organizational credentials
scopeExcludes: Traditional web-based breach forum listings (see ITID-12523)
Combolist aggregator sites (see ITID-12526)
ITID-12525.severity: High — Telegram-based distribution is often faster and less indexed than traditional forums, increasing risk of missed detection.
ITID-12525.escalation: Escalate to IAM for immediate credential rotation and to threat intelligence for channel/actor tracking.
indicators: Dark-web/messaging-platform monitoring service flags an organizational domain match in a Telegram channel
Stealer-log distribution channel post containing organizational endpoint/credential data
vectors: Infostealer malware harvesting browser-saved credentials, exfiltrated and distributed via Telegram "logs" channels
Direct criminal-to-criminal credential trading within closed Telegram groups
rootCauses: Endpoint infected with infostealer malware harvesting locally stored browser credentials
mitreTechniques: T1555.003 Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
controls: Telegram/encrypted-channel monitoring for organizational domain matches
Endpoint anti-malware/EDR to prevent infostealer infection
ITID-12525.detection: Specialized dark-web/messaging-platform monitoring services covering Telegram provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12525.response: Rotate the exposed credentials immediately and investigate the source endpoint for infostealer infection.
metrics: Count of Telegram-sourced credential exposures per quarter
ITID-12525.notes: Scoped to the Telegram/encrypted-channel distribution mechanism specifically, distinct from web forums (ITID-12523) and aggregator sites (ITID-12526).

playbook.name: Response: Telegram/Encrypted Channel Credential Listing
playbook.description: For organizational credentials shared or offered within a Telegram channel or other encrypted messaging platform used for illicit credential trading.

steps.title: Capture the channel post and channel metadata
steps.desc: Preserve the message content, channel name/ID, subscriber count, and posting timestamp before it can be deleted.
steps.guidance: Messages on these channels are frequently deleted quickly; capture promptly through the threat-intel monitoring tool.
steps.outcome: Channel post preserved with metadata.

steps.title: Force credential rotation for affected accounts
steps.desc: Reset credentials for all confirmed affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated.

steps.title: Check for evidence of use prior to rotation
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs for anomalous activity on affected accounts predating containment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of prior misuse.

steps.title: Confirm restored access
steps.desc: Verify affected users can authenticate normally with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Access confirmed restored.

steps.title: Document channel source and continue monitoring
steps.desc: Record the channel identity and add it to ongoing threat-intel monitoring for repeat postings.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and channel added to watchlist.

steps.title: Identify affected credentials from the shared content
steps.desc: Review any attached file, screenshot, or text for specific accounts and cross-reference against the directory.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of affected accounts.
steps.abort: If no organizational accounts can be confirmed, downgrade to monitoring-only.

steps.title: Enforce MFA on affected accounts
steps.desc: Confirm or enroll MFA for every affected account.
steps.outcome: MFA active on affected accounts.

steps.title: Assess channel's reach and repost risk
steps.desc: Determine subscriber count and whether the channel is known to feed into broader marketplaces, to gauge how quickly exposure may spread.
steps.outcome: Reach and repost risk assessed.

ITID-12526.def: Discovery of organizational credentials indexed on a purpose-built combolist aggregator platform that compiles and makes searchable credentials from many prior breaches, distinct from a single dump posting.
ITID-12526.purpose: Captures organizational credentials appearing on a searchable combolist aggregator site.
scopeIncludes: Organizational domain match returned by querying a known combolist aggregator/search service
Credential set confirmed to be sourced from multiple historical breaches, aggregated and re-indexed
scopeExcludes: A single, discrete bulk dump posting to a forum (see ITID-12523)
Telegram-based distribution (see ITID-12525)
ITID-12526.severity: Medium — aggregator-listed credentials are typically older and more likely already rotated, but confirmation is still required.
ITID-12526.escalation: Escalate to IAM to verify current validity and force rotation if the credential is still live.
indicators: Aggregator-monitoring/breach-checking service returns an organizational domain match
vectors: Prior, already-known breach's credentials re-indexed by an aggregator alongside newer breach data, extending its usable shelf life for attackers
Aggregator combining organizational credentials from multiple unrelated historical breaches into one searchable record
rootCauses: Password reuse across multiple external services over time, compounding exposure as more breaches are aggregated
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Periodic querying of known combolist aggregators for organizational domain exposure
Mandatory unique-password policy reducing aggregation impact
ITID-12526.detection: Periodic automated querying of aggregator platforms/APIs provides a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12526.response: Verify current credential validity; rotate if still live, and document as low-incremental-risk if already superseded by prior rotation.
metrics: Count of organizational credentials found on aggregator platforms per quarter
ITID-12526.notes: Differentiator is the aggregation/re-indexing mechanism itself, distinct from a single fresh dump posting (ITID-12523).

playbook.name: Response: Combolist Aggregator Listing
playbook.description: For organizational credentials appearing within a large automated combolist (username:password pairs) aggregated from many unrelated sources and circulated for use in credential-stuffing attacks.

steps.title: Preserve the combolist reference and obtain matched entries
steps.desc: Capture the combolist name/source and, through the threat-intel feed, extract any entries matching organizational domains.
steps.guidance: Combolists are typically massive; rely on automated matching rather than manual review.
steps.outcome: Matched entries for the organization's domains preserved.

steps.title: Force password reset on confirmed current accounts
steps.desc: Reset credentials for all confirmed current accounts appearing in the combolist.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated for matched current accounts.

steps.title: Review login telemetry for stuffing attempts
steps.desc: Check authentication logs for failed or successful login attempts consistent with automated credential-stuffing using the combolist.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of active stuffing attempts.

steps.title: Confirm restored access and monitor login patterns
steps.desc: Verify affected users can authenticate normally and maintain monitoring for continued stuffing attempts against rotated accounts.
