steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence or unauthorized access
steps.desc: Remediate any findings from the persistence audit.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access remains.

ITID-12615.def: An adversary phishes a victim into revealing one or more single-use MFA backup/recovery codes, then uses a code to authenticate without needing the primary MFA factor.
ITID-12615.purpose: Captures phishing specifically aimed at harvesting MFA backup/recovery codes, which bypass the primary factor entirely once obtained.
scopeIncludes: Fake account-recovery or security-review pages requesting backup codes
Pretexts framed as 'verify your backup codes are still valid'
scopeExcludes: Phishing for a live TOTP/push/hardware-token response (other leaves in this Type)
ITID-12615.severity: High — a backup code is a full authentication bypass and often has a long validity window.
ITID-12615.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
ITID-12615.escalation: Escalate and invalidate all remaining backup codes for the account immediately upon confirmation.
indicators: Phishing page requesting entry of backup/recovery codes
Authentication using a backup code shortly after a phishing report
vectors: Fake account-security or recovery-verification phishing page
rootCauses: Backup codes generated once and never rotated
Users unaware backup codes are as sensitive as passwords
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rollout for high-value accounts
Number-matching / context-rich push approval prompts
AiTM-aware conditional access (token binding, IP/device continuity checks)
User security awareness training on real-time credential relay phishing
ITID-12615.detection: Strong technical signal: IdP logs surface impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins immediately following a phishing click, reverse-proxy/AiTM kits leave detectable TLS and referrer fingerprints, and session tokens issued through a phishing relay show anomalous issuance velocity compared to genuine logins.
ITID-12615.response: Force sign-out and reset credentials plus MFA re-enrollment for the targeted user immediately on confirmation; hunt for reuse of any session token or code captured during the phishing window; block the phishing infrastructure at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of MFA phishing attempts detected per month
Median time from click to credential reset
Percentage of targeted users on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-12615.notes: Scoped to the backup/recovery-code factor specifically; distinguishing axis for this Type is the specific factor targeted.

playbook.name: Response: Backup/Recovery Code Phishing
playbook.description: For an attack where a user was phished into disclosing one or more static MFA backup/recovery codes, which — unlike TOTP or push — remain valid until manually invalidated.

steps.title: Confirm which backup codes were disclosed
steps.desc: Interview the user and determine whether one code or the full backup code set was disclosed or photographed/screenshotted.
steps.guidance: Backup codes are typically issued as a batch of 8-10 single-use codes — assume the whole set is compromised unless the user can confirm otherwise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of code disclosure.

steps.title: Invalidate all existing backup codes immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the entire backup code set for the account, since static codes remain valid indefinitely until manually rotated.
steps.guidance: This is the single most time-sensitive step — unlike TOTP/push, these codes do not expire on their own.
steps.outcome: All previously issued backup codes are no longer valid.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for new MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added if the codes were used successfully.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Issue a fresh backup code set and store guidance
steps.desc: Generate a new set of backup codes and advise the user on secure storage (password manager, not a photo or unsecured note).
steps.outcome: New backup codes issued; user briefed on secure storage.

steps.title: Document disclosure vector and reinforce backup code handling
steps.desc: Record how the codes were phished and issue guidance on treating backup codes as equivalent to a password.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder issued.

steps.title: Check for use of the disclosed codes
steps.desc: Review identity provider logs for any authentication event using a backup/recovery code on this account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the codes have already been used by an attacker.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the account password and terminate all active sessions.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any rogue MFA method, rule, or grant found.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-12616.def: An adversary social-engineers a victim into completing a biometric confirmation step on the victim's own device to approve an authentication request the adversary initiated.
ITID-12616.purpose: Captures social engineering that induces a victim to approve a biometric authentication prompt (e.g. a mobile authenticator's Face/Touch ID confirmation step) on the victim's own device.
scopeIncludes: Pretexts convincing a victim to unlock/confirm an authenticator app's biometric prompt for an adversary-initiated request
scopeExcludes: Push-notification approval phishing that does not involve a biometric confirmation step (ITID-12613)
ITID-12616.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
indicators: User report of being asked to 'just confirm on your phone' for an unfamiliar request
Sign-in immediately following a biometric-confirmed approval
vectors: Phone or chat pretext instructing the victim to complete a biometric confirmation
rootCauses: No context shown to the user about what the biometric confirmation is authorizing
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rollout for high-value accounts
Number-matching / context-rich push approval prompts
AiTM-aware conditional access (token binding, IP/device continuity checks)
User security awareness training on real-time credential relay phishing
ITID-12616.detection: Strong technical signal: IdP logs surface impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins immediately following a phishing click, reverse-proxy/AiTM kits leave detectable TLS and referrer fingerprints, and session tokens issued through a phishing relay show anomalous issuance velocity compared to genuine logins.
ITID-12616.response: Force sign-out and reset credentials plus MFA re-enrollment for the targeted user immediately on confirmation; hunt for reuse of any session token or code captured during the phishing window; block the phishing infrastructure at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of MFA phishing attempts detected per month
Median time from click to credential reset
Percentage of targeted users on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-12616.notes: Distinguishing axis: the confirmation mechanism is device-local biometric approval rather than a typed code or a simple push tap.

playbook.name: Response: Biometric Prompt Social Engineering
playbook.description: For an incident where a user was socially engineered into unlocking a device or approving an authentication prompt using their own biometric (fingerprint/face) at an attacker's request or under a deceptive pretext.

steps.title: Confirm the circumstances of the biometric approval
steps.desc: Interview the user to establish what pretext was used (e.g., handed device to a 'colleague', coerced during a fake support call) and what was approved.
steps.guidance: Distinguish a genuine social-engineering approval from a stolen/unlocked device scenario, which should be handled as device theft instead.
steps.outcome: Confirmed pretext and scope of what was approved.
steps.abort: If the device was physically stolen rather than voluntarily unlocked, escalate as lost/stolen device instead of pursuing this playbook.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on affected accounts
steps.desc: Reset credentials and terminate active sessions for any account accessed via the approved biometric prompt.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for unauthorized actions taken during the approval window
steps.desc: Review logs for any transaction, data access, or configuration change made in the window the attacker had access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any unauthorized action taken.

steps.title: Restore normal access and re-enroll biometrics if the device was reset
steps.desc: Return the device to the user and re-enroll biometric/MFA methods if the device was wiped.
steps.outcome: User has verified-clean device and access restored.

steps.title: Document the social-engineering pretext and brief the user/team
steps.desc: Record the pretext used to coach the user into approving, and share a targeted awareness point about not unlocking devices or approving prompts for others, including under authority pressure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; awareness reminder delivered.

steps.title: Determine what access the biometric approval granted
steps.desc: Identify whether the biometric unlocked the device itself, approved an MFA push, or authorized a specific transaction/app action.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of the access or action the attacker obtained.
steps.tool: Device management console / identity provider logs

steps.title: Remotely lock or wipe the device if still in attacker possession
steps.desc: If the device is not back in the legitimate user's control, issue a remote lock or wipe via MDM.
steps.outcome: Device secured or wiped remotely.
steps.abort: If the device has already been returned and verified clean, skip this step.

steps.title: Reverse or remediate any unauthorized actions found
steps.desc: Undo or remediate any change, transaction, or access grant made during the incident.
steps.outcome: System state restored to pre-incident condition.

ITID-12617.def: An adversary presents a victim with a QR code (in person, via phishing email, or via a compromised display) that, when scanned during an MFA enrollment flow, registers an attacker-controlled device or authenticator as a valid second factor on the victim's account.
ITID-12617.purpose: Captures attacks where a victim is tricked into scanning an attacker's QR code to enroll the attacker's own device as a trusted MFA method on the victim's account.
scopeIncludes: Malicious QR codes injected into an MFA enrollment or re-registration flow
'Quishing' emails linking to a fake enrollment page with a QR code
scopeExcludes: Help-desk impersonation used as the delivery pretext for a reset request (ITID-11424, tracked separately as a social-engineering pretext ITID)
QR codes used purely for phishing a login page rather than an MFA enrollment step
ITID-12617.severity: High — successful enrollment gives the adversary a durable, self-service authentication method on the account.
ITID-12617.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
ITID-12617.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke the newly enrolled authenticator and audit all MFA methods on the account.
indicators: New MFA method enrolled shortly after a QR-code interaction
Enrollment from a device/IP inconsistent with the user's normal pattern
vectors: Quishing email or physical QR-code substitution used to hijack an enrollment flow
rootCauses: MFA enrollment/re-registration flow lacking step-up verification
No alerting on new-authenticator enrollment events
mitreTechniques: T1556.006 Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rollout for high-value accounts
Number-matching / context-rich push approval prompts
AiTM-aware conditional access (token binding, IP/device continuity checks)
User security awareness training on real-time credential relay phishing
ITID-12617.detection: Strong technical signal: IdP logs surface impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins immediately following a phishing click, reverse-proxy/AiTM kits leave detectable TLS and referrer fingerprints, and session tokens issued through a phishing relay show anomalous issuance velocity compared to genuine logins.
ITID-12617.response: Force sign-out and reset credentials plus MFA re-enrollment for the targeted user immediately on confirmation; hunt for reuse of any session token or code captured during the phishing window; block the phishing infrastructure at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of MFA phishing attempts detected per month
Median time from click to credential reset
Percentage of targeted users on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-12617.notes: Scope decision: the help-desk-impersonation delivery mechanism for a credential/MFA reset is tracked separately at ITID-11424; this leaf is scoped to the technical enrollment-hijack outcome via QR code regardless of pretext.

playbook.name: Response: QR-Code-Based MFA Enrollment Phishing
playbook.description: For an attack where a user was tricked into scanning a malicious QR code that enrolled an attacker-controlled authenticator app instance as a trusted MFA method on their account, rather than simply harvesting a credential.

steps.title: Confirm the QR code's actual function
steps.desc: Obtain the QR code image or its decoded target and determine whether it was a legitimate MFA-enrollment QR redirected to an attacker session, or a link-based phishing QR (quishing) leading to a credential page.
steps.guidance: MFA-enrollment QR abuse typically works by an attacker starting their own enrollment flow and presenting the resulting QR to the victim to scan — confirm which direction the enrollment went.
steps.outcome: Confirmed mechanism: MFA method enrolled to attacker's authenticator, or credentials harvested via a linked page.

steps.title: Remove the attacker-enrolled MFA method immediately
steps.desc: Delete the rogue authenticator/device enrollment from the account.
steps.guidance: This is the priority containment action — until removed, the attacker retains standing authentication capability on the account.
steps.outcome: Rogue MFA method removed; only legitimate methods remain.

steps.title: Audit for further attacker activity using the rogue MFA method
steps.desc: Review authentication and access logs for any activity that occurred using the attacker-controlled MFA method before it was removed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any access or activity by the attacker.

steps.title: Re-enroll the user's legitimate MFA method under verified conditions
steps.desc: Have the user re-enroll their authenticator app in person or via a verified secure channel.
steps.outcome: User has a confirmed-legitimate MFA method restored.

steps.title: Document the enrollment-abuse technique and consider enrollment safeguards
steps.desc: Record how the QR enrollment trick worked and recommend controls such as enrollment approval workflows or restricting self-service MFA enrollment to managed devices.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Enumerate all MFA methods currently registered on the account
steps.desc: List every MFA method enrolled on the account and identify which one(s) were added around the phishing timestamp.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of legitimate vs. attacker-added MFA methods.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the account password and terminate all active sessions and tokens.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Remediate any downstream access or changes found
steps.desc: Reverse or remediate any change made by the attacker during their access window.
steps.outcome: System state restored to pre-incident condition.

ITID-12618.def: An adversary uses an AiTM reverse-proxy phishing kit to sit between the victim and the legitimate identity provider, transparently relaying credentials and whichever MFA factor the victim completes, then capturing the resulting authenticated session token/cookie.
ITID-12618.purpose: Captures full adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) reverse-proxy phishing that transparently relays an entire authentication session — password, MFA prompt, and resulting session token — in one continuous flow.
scopeIncludes: Reverse-proxy phishing kits (e.g. Evilginx-style) that relay a full multi-factor login flow
Chained capture of password + any MFA factor + session token in a single phishing session
scopeExcludes: Phishing for a single isolated factor with no full-session relay/token theft (other leaves in this Type)
Post-authentication session-token theft via malware or physical device access unrelated to phishing (Session Hijacking Type, ITID-12921-12929)
ITID-12618.severity: Critical — full session token theft is equivalent to compromise even after the user changes their password.
ITID-12618.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke all active sessions/tokens for the account in addition to password and MFA reset.
indicators: TLS certificate/domain anomalies consistent with a reverse-proxy phishing kit
Session token reuse from an IP/device inconsistent with the original login
vectors: AiTM reverse-proxy phishing infrastructure chaining credential and MFA capture
rootCauses: No token-binding or conditional-access continuity check between authentication and session use
Phishable MFA factors in use for high-value accounts
mitreTechniques: T1556.006 Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rollout for high-value accounts
Number-matching / context-rich push approval prompts
AiTM-aware conditional access (token binding, IP/device continuity checks)
User security awareness training on real-time credential relay phishing
ITID-12618.detection: Strong technical signal: IdP logs surface impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins immediately following a phishing click, reverse-proxy/AiTM kits leave detectable TLS and referrer fingerprints, and session tokens issued through a phishing relay show anomalous issuance velocity compared to genuine logins.
ITID-12618.response: Force sign-out and reset credentials plus MFA re-enrollment for the targeted user immediately on confirmation; hunt for reuse of any session token or code captured during the phishing window; block the phishing infrastructure at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of MFA phishing attempts detected per month
Median time from click to credential reset
Percentage of targeted users on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-12618.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from the Session Hijacking Type (ITID-12921-12929) by requiring the token theft to occur as part of a live phishing relay of the login itself, not post-login theft via malware or device access.

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Factor Chained Phishing
playbook.description: For a sophisticated adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing kit attack that chained the harvest of password, MFA code/push approval, and session cookie in a single real-time relay flow.

steps.title: Confirm the chained nature of the attack
steps.desc: Review the phishing page/kit and user account of the interaction to confirm password, MFA response, and session token were all relayed through an attacker-controlled proxy.
steps.guidance: Look for hallmark AiTM indicators: a reverse-proxy phishing page mirroring the real login flow, and a session established immediately after user interaction.
steps.outcome: Confirmed AiTM chained phishing rather than a single-factor harvest.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all sessions and tokens
steps.desc: Reset the account password and invalidate every active session, refresh token, and app password immediately.
steps.guidance: Session/token revocation is the critical step here — password reset alone does not kill an already-stolen session cookie.
steps.outcome: Password rotated; all sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence and lateral movement
steps.desc: Review the account for new forwarding rules, OAuth grants, privilege changes, and check for any lateral movement into other systems using the stolen session.
steps.outcome: Confirmed full scope of persistence and lateral movement.
steps.tool: SIEM / EDR / identity provider audit log

steps.title: Restore access on a phishing-resistant MFA method
steps.desc: Restore the user's access and migrate them to a phishing-resistant method (FIDO2/passkey) that is not vulnerable to AiTM relay.
steps.guidance: TOTP and push are both relayable by AiTM kits; only token-binding methods like FIDO2 close this gap.
steps.outcome: User restored with a phishing-resistant authentication method where available.

steps.title: Document the AiTM technique and drive conditional access hardening
steps.desc: Record the kit's behavior and push for conditional access controls (token binding, device compliance, phishing-resistant MFA mandate) as a systemic fix.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete follow-up action assigned to the identity/security engineering team.

steps.title: Determine full scope of session and account compromise
steps.desc: Review identity provider logs for the session created via the relay, and check what that session accessed.
steps.guidance: Session tokens obtained via AiTM bypass MFA entirely on reuse — treat this as full account compromise until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of what the attacker accessed using the stolen session.

steps.title: Re-enroll all MFA methods on the account
steps.desc: Remove and re-register every MFA method on the account, since the attacker may have added their own during the session.
steps.outcome: Only verified-legitimate MFA methods remain.

steps.title: Remove all confirmed persistence and remediate downstream access
steps.desc: Remove any rogue rule, grant, or foothold identified, and remediate any downstream system accessed.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Monitor the account for an extended observation window
steps.desc: Flag the account for elevated monitoring for at least 30 days given the severity of a full session compromise.
steps.outcome: No anomalous activity observed during the monitoring window.

steps.title: Block the AiTM phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the phishing/relay domain at the web proxy and mail gateway, and purge the message org-wide.
steps.outcome: Infrastructure blocked; message purged.

ITID-12619.def: A confirmed instance of MFA token phishing (any factor) in which the captured code, approval, or session token was successfully used by the adversary to authenticate to the target account.
ITID-12619.purpose: Escalation leaf for confirmed successful MFA token phishing where the adversary is verified to have used the captured factor to bypass MFA and authenticate.
scopeIncludes: Any sibling phishing leaf in this Type where downstream unauthorized authentication is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Phishing attempts where no successful authentication is confirmed (respective attempt-stage sibling leaves)
ITID-12619.severity: Critical — confirmed account compromise, markedly higher than the corresponding attempt-stage siblings.
ITID-12619.escalation: Immediate incident response activation: credential reset, MFA re-enrollment, session revocation, and compromise-scope investigation.
indicators: Confirmed unauthorized sign-in immediately following a phishing interaction
Post-authentication adversary activity (mailbox rules, data access, lateral movement)
vectors: Any MFA token phishing vector in this Type that reached successful use
rootCauses: Reliance on phishable MFA factors for high-value accounts
Absence of conditional-access controls that would have blocked the resulting session
mitreTechniques: T1556.006 Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rollout for high-value accounts
Number-matching / context-rich push approval prompts
AiTM-aware conditional access (token binding, IP/device continuity checks)
User security awareness training on real-time credential relay phishing
ITID-12619.detection: Strong technical signal: IdP logs surface impossible-travel and new-device sign-ins immediately following a phishing click, reverse-proxy/AiTM kits leave detectable TLS and referrer fingerprints, and session tokens issued through a phishing relay show anomalous issuance velocity compared to genuine logins.
ITID-12619.response: Force sign-out and reset credentials plus MFA re-enrollment for the targeted user immediately on confirmation; hunt for reuse of any session token or code captured during the phishing window; block the phishing infrastructure at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of MFA phishing attempts detected per month
Median time from click to credential reset
Percentage of targeted users on phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-12619.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation of the phishing attempt leaves above it; severity and priority are set markedly higher than the technique-description siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Successful MFA Token Phishing with Confirmed Bypass
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where MFA-targeted phishing (of any factor type) resulted in verified attacker access to the account — the high-severity, post-compromise variant of the MFA phishing family requiring full account-takeover response.

steps.title: Confirm and scope the successful bypass
steps.desc: Establish, from logs and user interview, that the attacker successfully authenticated using the phished factor, and determine which factor and technique were used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed successful bypass with technique and timeline documented.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all sessions and tokens
steps.desc: Reset the password and invalidate every active session, refresh token, and app password on the account immediately.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; all sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Remove all attacker persistence across affected accounts
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, OAuth grants, and any created accounts or backdoors found across the full scope.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Restore access on phishing-resistant MFA and validate with the user
steps.desc: Restore access for all affected users, migrating to a phishing-resistant MFA method where available, and confirm with each user that access and data look correct.
steps.outcome: Verified-clean access restored for all affected users.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full timeline, blast radius, and required control changes (phishing-resistant MFA rollout, conditional access, detection gaps); report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine full extent of attacker activity post-authentication
steps.desc: Review all activity performed by the attacker during their access window: data accessed, emails sent, files touched, systems reached.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a full account-takeover investigation, not a phishing near-miss.
steps.outcome: Complete activity timeline for the compromised session.

steps.title: Suspend the account if active attacker activity is ongoing
steps.desc: If the investigation begins while the attacker session may still be active, temporarily disable the account pending containment.
steps.outcome: Account access halted; no further attacker action possible.

steps.title: Re-enroll MFA on all affected accounts
steps.desc: Remove and re-register MFA methods on every account confirmed or suspected compromised.
steps.outcome: Only verified-legitimate MFA methods remain on all affected accounts.

steps.title: Extended monitoring of all affected accounts
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Assess blast radius to other accounts and systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker used this account to pivot to other accounts, shared drives, or connected systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact beyond the initial account.

steps.title: Contain any downstream systems or accounts affected
steps.desc: Apply containment (credential reset, session revocation, isolation) to any secondary account or system identified in the blast-radius assessment.
steps.outcome: Blast radius fully contained.

ITID-12621.def: An incident of repeated MFA push prompting intended to fatigue a user into approval, not clearly matching a more specific leaf under this Type.
ITID-12621.purpose: Catch-all for MFA fatigue/push-bombing reports not yet matching a more specific pattern.
scopeIncludes: Reports of repeated unsolicited MFA prompts where the specific pattern (timing, targeting, automation, scope) is not yet determined
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the pattern is known
ITID-12621.severity: Medium by default; reassess once pattern is confirmed.
ITID-12621.priority: P3 pending reclassification, P2 if privileged account.
ITID-12621.escalation: Reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: User report of repeated unexplained MFA prompts
vectors: Repeated authentication attempts against a valid, previously compromised password
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12621.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12621.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12621.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General MFA Fatigue Attack
playbook.description: Baseline response for a report of repeated, unsolicited MFA push notifications aimed at wearing down a user into approving an attacker-initiated login, where the specific pattern has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the fatigue pattern with the user
steps.desc: Interview the reporting user to confirm they received multiple unsolicited push prompts and determine whether any were approved.
steps.guidance: Capture approximate count, time span, and whether the user approved any prompt, even accidentally.
steps.outcome: Confirmed pattern of unsolicited pushes and whether any was approved.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the account password and terminate any active sessions, regardless of whether a push was approved.
steps.guidance: Repeated bombing implies the attacker already has the password — treat it as compromised.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for a successful approval or bypass
steps.desc: Confirm from the log whether any push was actually approved, and if so, review resulting account activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the bombing succeeded and, if so, the scope of resulting activity.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Have the user set a new password and re-enroll MFA.
steps.outcome: User has clean, verified access restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend push-approval hardening
steps.desc: Record the pattern observed and recommend number-matching, rate-limiting, or geo-velocity checks on push challenges if not already enabled.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Pull the full push notification log for the account
steps.desc: Retrieve the identity provider's MFA challenge log for the account covering the reported window.
steps.outcome: Complete timeline of push challenges, denials, and approvals for the account.

steps.title: Block the source of the bombing attempts
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP/ASN at the identity provider's conditional access policy or firewall.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further authentication attempts.

steps.title: Determine the source of the login attempts triggering the pushes
steps.desc: Identify the source IP(s), ASN, and device fingerprint generating the authentication attempts.
steps.outcome: Source infrastructure of the bombing attempts identified.

ITID-12622.def: An adversary with a valid password repeatedly triggers MFA push prompts in rapid succession, relying on the sheer volume to wear down the victim into approving one.
ITID-12622.purpose: Captures the classic high-volume push-bombing pattern: rapid, repeated MFA prompts sent in quick succession until the victim approves out of annoyance.
scopeIncludes: Sustained high-frequency push prompting within a short window with no other distinguishing feature
scopeExcludes: Prompts specifically timed for off-hours (ITID-12623)
Prompts paired with a live phone call (ITID-12624)
ITID-12622.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
ITID-12622.escalation: Escalate immediately on any approval; investigate as password compromise regardless of approval outcome.
indicators: 10+ push prompts within a short window
User denies multiple prompts before one is approved or the sequence stops
vectors: Scripted repeated authentication attempts against a compromised password
rootCauses: Compromised password with no rate limit on MFA prompt generation
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12622.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12622.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12622.notes: Baseline volume-based pattern; other siblings differentiate by timing, targeting, automation, or account type.

playbook.name: Response: Push Notification Bombing (Volume-Based Fatigue)
playbook.description: For a high-volume push-bombing attack where an attacker rapidly triggered a large number of authentication prompts in an attempt to wear the user into approving one by sheer volume, without an accompanying social-engineering call.

steps.title: Quantify the volume and rate of push challenges
steps.desc: Pull the exact count and interval of push prompts sent to the user's device from the identity provider log.
steps.guidance: A high rate (many prompts within minutes) is a strong signal of automated/scripted bombing versus opportunistic retries.
steps.outcome: Confirmed volume and rate pattern documented.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the password and terminate all active sessions regardless of approval outcome.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass and resulting activity
steps.desc: If any prompt was approved, review the resulting session's activity in full.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any attacker activity.

steps.title: Restore access and re-enable push once safe
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new password, and re-enable push MFA once number-matching or rate-limiting is confirmed in place.
steps.outcome: User has clean access restored under hardened push settings.

steps.title: Document the bombing pattern and push for number-matching enforcement
steps.desc: Record the volume/rate pattern observed and, if not already enforced org-wide, recommend mandatory number-matching and challenge rate-limiting.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a policy recommendation to the identity team.

steps.title: Determine whether any prompt was approved
steps.desc: Check the log and interview the user to establish whether fatigue led to an accidental approval.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval status.

steps.title: Block the source IP/infrastructure generating the bombing
steps.desc: Block the source IP(s) or ASN at the conditional access policy or network edge.
steps.outcome: Bombing source blocked.

steps.title: Temporarily pause push as an approved MFA method for the account
steps.desc: Disable push notifications as a login option for the affected account pending investigation, leaving other factors active.
steps.outcome: Push approval no longer possible for this account until re-enabled.

ITID-12623.def: An adversary sends repeated MFA push prompts during off-hours, exploiting reduced user alertness to increase the odds of an accidental approval.
ITID-12623.purpose: Captures push bombing deliberately timed for nights, early mornings, or weekends when a groggy user is more likely to approve without full attention.
scopeIncludes: Push prompts concentrated outside normal business hours for the target user's time zone
scopeExcludes: Daytime high-volume bombing with no off-hours timing element (ITID-12622)
ITID-12623.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
indicators: Push prompts clustered between local midnight and 6am
User reports being woken by repeated notifications
vectors: Off-hours scripted authentication attempts timed to target time zone
rootCauses: No time-of-day risk scoring in conditional access for MFA challenges
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12623.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12623.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12623.notes: Differentiating axis from sibling leaves: timing (off-hours) rather than volume, targeting, or automation.

playbook.name: Response: Off-Hours Push Bombing
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack timed to strike outside the user's normal working hours, exploiting drowsiness or reduced vigilance to increase the chance of an accidental approval.

steps.title: Confirm the off-hours timing and pattern
steps.desc: Pull the push challenge log and confirm the timestamps fall well outside the user's normal working pattern (e.g., late night, early morning).
steps.guidance: Off-hours timing is itself a strong indicator of malicious intent rather than a legitimate user's own mistyped login.
steps.outcome: Confirmed off-hours timing pattern documented.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the password and terminate active sessions immediately.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass and resulting activity
steps.desc: If a prompt was approved, review resulting session activity in full, especially any activity that itself occurred off-hours.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any attacker activity.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new password and re-enrolled MFA method.
steps.outcome: User has clean access restored.

steps.title: Document the timing pattern and recommend anomalous-hours alerting
steps.desc: Record the off-hours pattern and recommend SIEM alerting on push challenges outside a user's normal working-hours baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a detection improvement recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether the user was asleep/unavailable and whether any push was approved
steps.desc: Interview the user about their state at the time (e.g., asleep, phone on nightstand) and confirm whether any prompt was approved, possibly unknowingly.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval status and user context.

steps.title: Block the source and consider time-based conditional access
steps.desc: Block the source IP/ASN, and if supported, apply a conditional access rule requiring additional verification for logins outside the user's normal hours/geography.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; time-based risk policy considered or applied.

ITID-12624.def: An adversary triggers MFA push prompts and simultaneously places a live phone call impersonating IT support or security, instructing the victim to approve the prompt to 'resolve an issue.'
ITID-12624.purpose: Captures push bombing combined with a live phone call impersonating IT/security to talk the victim into approving, blending a technical and social-engineering vector.
scopeIncludes: Push bombing paired with a concurrent live phone call pretext
scopeExcludes: Push bombing with no accompanying live call (ITID-12622)
Pure voice-channel OTP relay with no push component (ITID-11218, vishing)
ITID-12624.severity: Critical — the live call materially raises approval likelihood.
ITID-12624.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as active social-engineering attack requiring user and help-desk awareness alert.
indicators: Push prompt approval correlated with an inbound call from an unrecognized/spoofed number
User report of a caller instructing them to approve a prompt
vectors: Combined technical push generation and live vishing call
rootCauses: No caller-ID verification culture for IT/security calls
Users not trained that legitimate IT never asks to approve an unexplained prompt
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12624.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12624.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12624.notes: Scope decision: this leaf requires the push-generation mechanism to be present; a vishing call alone that only relays a spoken OTP with no push involved is ITID-11218 under the Vishing Attacks branch.

playbook.name: Response: Push Bombing Combined with Live Call
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack paired with a live phone call from an attacker impersonating IT/helpdesk, pressuring the user in real time to approve one of the flooding prompts.

steps.title: Capture details of the impersonation call
steps.desc: Interview the user for the caller's claimed identity, phone number (including any spoofed caller ID), script used, and what they were asked to do.
steps.guidance: This detail supports both the technical investigation and any subsequent internal awareness communication or reporting to telecom/law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Documented record of the impersonation pretext and caller details.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the password and terminate all active sessions immediately.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass and check for a broader vishing campaign
steps.desc: Review resulting session activity if a prompt was approved, and check whether other users received similar calls (this is frequently a coordinated campaign against multiple staff).
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of attacker activity and whether the campaign targeted others.

steps.title: Restore access with re-enrolled MFA
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a new password and re-enrolled MFA method.
steps.outcome: User has clean access restored.

steps.title: Alert the workforce to the vishing pretext used
steps.desc: Issue an organization-wide alert describing the specific caller pretext and script observed, and reinforce that IT/helpdesk will never ask staff to approve a push they did not initiate.
steps.outcome: Awareness alert distributed; finding logged.

steps.title: Pull the push challenge log and confirm any approval tied to the call
steps.desc: Correlate the timing of the call with the push challenge log to confirm whether the user approved a prompt during or after the call.
steps.outcome: Confirmed correlation between the call and any approval.

steps.title: Block the source of the bombing and flag the calling number
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP/ASN, and record the calling number for telecom/fraud reporting and for correlation against other victims.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; calling number logged for cross-referencing.

steps.title: Remove any attacker persistence if the bypass succeeded
steps.desc: Remove any rogue MFA enrollment, forwarding rule, or OAuth grant added during a successful bypass.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-12625.def: An adversary directs repeated MFA push prompts at an account holding elevated/administrative privileges to fatigue that specific user into approval.
ITID-12625.purpose: Captures push bombing specifically targeting privileged or administrative accounts, warranting materially higher severity due to blast radius.
scopeIncludes: Push bombing where the targeted account is confirmed to hold domain admin, cloud admin, or other privileged entitlements
scopeExcludes: Push bombing against standard user accounts (ITID-12622)
ITID-12625.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC and privileged access management team.
indicators: Push bombing pattern where the target's role/group membership is administrative
vectors: Targeted scripted authentication attempts against a known privileged account's compromised password
rootCauses: Privileged accounts not enrolled on phishing-resistant MFA
No additional step-up/PAM check for privileged authentication
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12625.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12625.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12625.notes: Differentiating axis: target scope (privileged account) rather than volume or timing.

playbook.name: Response: Push Bombing Targeting Privileged/Admin Accounts
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack directed specifically at a privileged or administrative account, where a successful bypass carries materially higher impact than a standard user account.

steps.title: Confirm the account's privilege level and immediately escalate severity
steps.desc: Confirm the targeted account's administrative scope (e.g., domain admin, cloud admin, SaaS super-admin) and escalate the incident severity accordingly.
steps.guidance: Treat any bombing against a privileged account as high severity from the outset, regardless of whether a prompt was approved.
steps.outcome: Incident severity escalated and appropriate stakeholders notified per policy.

steps.title: Suspend the privileged account pending investigation
steps.desc: Temporarily disable the admin account rather than only resetting the password, given the severity of a potential bypass.
steps.outcome: Account access halted immediately.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass and review all privileged actions taken
steps.desc: If a prompt was approved, conduct a full review of every privileged action taken during the session (config changes, new accounts, permission grants, log deletions).
steps.guidance: An attacker with admin access will often try to create persistence or disable logging quickly — check both.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of any privileged actions taken by the attacker.

steps.title: Restore privileged access on a phishing-resistant, tightly monitored basis
steps.desc: Restore the account with a new password, phishing-resistant MFA where available, and place it under enhanced monitoring.
steps.outcome: Admin access restored on hardened, monitored terms.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review and mandate stronger controls for privileged accounts
steps.desc: Document the incident and require phishing-resistant MFA and number-matching for all privileged/admin accounts if not already mandatory.
steps.outcome: Formal review completed with control changes assigned to identity/security engineering.

steps.title: Pull the push challenge log and determine approval status
steps.desc: Retrieve the full challenge log and confirm whether any prompt was approved.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval status and timeline.

steps.title: Revoke all sessions and any standing elevated-access grants
steps.desc: Terminate all sessions and review/revoke any just-in-time or standing privileged access grants tied to the account.
steps.outcome: All sessions and elevated grants terminated.

steps.title: Reverse all unauthorized privileged actions and remove persistence
steps.desc: Undo any unauthorized configuration change, delete any rogue account, and remove any persistence mechanism found.
steps.outcome: Environment restored to pre-incident state with no attacker-controlled access remaining.

steps.title: Block the source of the bombing
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP/ASN at the identity provider risk policy or firewall.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

ITID-12626.def: An adversary uses automated scripts or tooling to generate MFA push prompts at machine-consistent intervals, often as part of a broader credential-stuffing or account-takeover toolkit.
ITID-12626.purpose: Captures push bombing carried out by automated tooling/scripts rather than manual, human-paced attempts, typically identifiable by machine-precision timing.
scopeIncludes: Push prompt sequences with statistically uniform, machine-generated timing intervals
scopeExcludes: Manually paced, human-timed push bombing (ITID-12622)
ITID-12626.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
ITID-12626.escalation: Escalate immediately; correlate with any concurrent credential-stuffing activity against the same account.
indicators: Push prompts at uniform sub-minute intervals inconsistent with human retry behavior
Source IP associated with known automation/attack infrastructure
vectors: Automated account-takeover toolkit chaining credential stuffing with MFA prompt generation
rootCauses: No bot/automation detection on the authentication endpoint
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12626.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12626.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12626.notes: Differentiating axis: automation signature in prompt timing/source rather than manual pacing.

playbook.name: Response: Automated/Scripted Push Bombing
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack driven by automated tooling/scripting rather than manual attempts, typically producing very high-frequency, machine-paced challenge patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the automated pattern from challenge timing
steps.desc: Analyze the push challenge log's inter-arrival timing; highly regular, sub-second-to-second intervals indicate scripted/automated generation rather than manual retries.
steps.outcome: Confirmed automated pattern with supporting timing evidence.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions
steps.desc: Reset the password and terminate all active sessions immediately.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass on any targeted account
steps.desc: Review whether any account in the campaign had a prompt approved, and if so, the resulting activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any successful bypass across the campaign.

steps.title: Restore access for all affected accounts
steps.desc: Restore access for every affected account with new passwords and re-enrolled MFA.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts restored to clean, verified access.

steps.title: Document the campaign and recommend anti-automation controls
steps.desc: Record the campaign's scope and technique and recommend CAPTCHA, rate-limiting, or bot-detection controls on the authentication endpoint if gaps are identified.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Identify the source infrastructure and any credential-stuffing correlation
steps.desc: Determine the source IP(s)/ASN and check whether this account appeared in a broader credential-stuffing or password-spray campaign, since automated bombing often follows automated credential validation.
steps.outcome: Source identified and correlated with any wider campaign.

steps.title: Block the source infrastructure and rate-limit authentication attempts
steps.desc: Block the source IP(s)/ASN and apply or verify rate-limiting/lockout thresholds on repeated authentication attempts.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; rate-limiting confirmed in place.

steps.title: Check other accounts for the same automated pattern
steps.desc: Search the identity provider log across all accounts for the same source infrastructure or timing signature to catch other targeted accounts.
steps.outcome: Full list of accounts targeted by the same automated campaign.

ITID-12627.def: An adversary triggers MFA push prompts across several accounts or MFA-enrolled devices linked to the same identity, increasing the chance one is approved.
ITID-12627.purpose: Captures push bombing that spreads across multiple linked accounts or enrolled devices belonging to the same user, rather than a single account/device.
