scopeExcludes: Push bombing confined to a single account/device (ITID-12622)
ITID-12627.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts.
ITID-12627.escalation: Escalate immediately; reset and re-enroll MFA across all affected linked accounts/devices.
indicators: Correlated push prompts across multiple accounts/devices for the same identity within a short window
vectors: Credential reuse across linked accounts enabling multi-account targeting
rootCauses: Shared/reused credentials across linked accounts
No cross-account correlation in MFA anomaly detection
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12627.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12627.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12627.notes: Differentiating axis: scope spans multiple linked accounts/devices rather than a single target.

playbook.name: Response: Push Bombing Across Multiple Linked Accounts/Devices
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack that spans several accounts or devices linked to the same user (e.g., personal and corporate identity, multiple enrolled devices), increasing the chance of an accidental approval on any single surface.

steps.title: Enumerate all linked accounts and devices affected
steps.desc: Identify every account and enrolled device belonging to the user that received push challenges during the incident window.
steps.guidance: Check both corporate and any federated/linked personal identities if SSO spans them.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of accounts and devices targeted.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on every affected account
steps.desc: Reset credentials and terminate sessions for every linked account identified, not just the one that showed an approval.
steps.outcome: All affected accounts have rotated credentials and terminated sessions.

steps.title: Audit each affected account for a successful bypass
steps.desc: Review each linked account individually for evidence of a successful approval and resulting activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact per account.

steps.title: Restore access across all affected accounts
steps.desc: Restore access with new passwords and re-enrolled MFA for every affected account.
steps.outcome: All accounts restored to clean, verified access.

steps.title: Document the cross-account pattern and review identity-linking exposure
steps.desc: Record which accounts/devices were linked and how, and assess whether that linkage unnecessarily expands the attack surface.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with an identity-architecture recommendation if warranted.

steps.title: Determine which surface, if any, had a prompt approved
steps.desc: Cross-reference challenge logs across all identified accounts/devices to determine whether any single one had an approval.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval status across all surfaces.

steps.title: Block the source across all affected identity boundaries
steps.desc: Block the source IP/ASN at every identity provider or conditional access boundary involved.
steps.outcome: Source blocked across all relevant systems.

steps.title: Remove any persistence found on any affected account
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants from any account where a bypass succeeded.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains on any account.

ITID-12628.def: An adversary triggers MFA push prompts against a shared or break-glass account, where approval may reach any of several monitoring personnel or an on-call rotation rather than one dedicated user.
ITID-12628.purpose: Captures push bombing against shared or break-glass emergency-access accounts, which typically lack an individual user to fatigue and carry outsized organizational risk if bypassed.
scopeIncludes: Push bombing targeting accounts explicitly designated as shared, service, or break-glass/emergency-access
scopeExcludes: Push bombing against a standard individually-owned account (ITID-12622)
ITID-12628.severity: Critical — break-glass accounts typically hold global/emergency privileges.
ITID-12628.escalation: Escalate immediately to identity/PAM team; break-glass account compromise requires organization-wide access review.
indicators: Push bombing pattern against an account flagged as break-glass/shared in the identity directory
vectors: Targeting of a known emergency-access account whose credentials may be less closely held
rootCauses: Break-glass account credentials not stored/rotated with sufficient rigor
Break-glass account not exempted from standard push MFA in favor of hardware-key-only access
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12628.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12628.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12628.notes: Differentiating axis: account category (shared/break-glass) rather than an individually assigned account.

playbook.name: Response: Push Bombing Against Shared/Break-Glass Account MFA
playbook.description: For a push-bombing attack targeting a shared service account or emergency break-glass account's MFA, where responsibility and accountability for approval are less clear-cut than for an individually-owned account.

steps.title: Identify all individuals with knowledge of or access to the shared/break-glass credential
steps.desc: Pull the list of everyone with legitimate access to the account's credential and MFA device.
steps.guidance: Shared account custody records or a password vault's access log are the starting point.
steps.outcome: Complete list of individuals with legitimate access.

steps.title: Suspend the account and rotate the credential via the PAM/vault workflow
steps.desc: Disable the account and rotate its credential following the organization's break-glass/shared-account emergency rotation procedure.
steps.guidance: Shared and break-glass accounts often require a documented, witnessed rotation process — follow it rather than an ad hoc reset.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated per formal procedure; account access halted pending investigation.

steps.title: Audit for a successful bypass and review all actions taken under the shared identity
steps.desc: If a prompt was approved, review every action taken during that session — attribution is harder with shared accounts, so cross-reference with device/location data.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any attacker activity, with best-effort attribution.

steps.title: Restore the account under the vault's normal checkout process
steps.desc: Return the account to normal availability through the PAM checkout workflow with fresh MFA enrollment.
steps.outcome: Account restored to normal, governed availability.

steps.title: Review whether this account should remain shared and reinforce break-glass procedures
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether the account's shared nature increases risk enough to warrant individual accountability controls (e.g., PAM check-out logging, reduced custodian list).
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a governance recommendation.

steps.title: Determine whether any prompt was approved and by whom
steps.desc: Review the push challenge log and interview each individual with access to determine whether any of them approved a prompt, intentionally or accidentally.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval status and, if approved, by which custodian.

steps.title: Block the source of the bombing
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP/ASN at the identity provider or network edge.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further attempts.

steps.title: Remove any persistence and re-issue the credential to authorized custodians only
steps.desc: Remove any rogue enrollment or grant found, and re-issue the rotated credential only to verified, currently-authorized custodians.
steps.outcome: No attacker access remains; credential access list re-validated.

ITID-12629.def: A confirmed instance of push-bombing MFA fatigue in which the target ultimately approved a fraudulent prompt, granting the adversary an authenticated session.
ITID-12629.purpose: Escalation leaf for confirmed successful push bombing where the victim approved a fraudulent prompt and the adversary obtained an authenticated session.
scopeIncludes: Any sibling push-bombing leaf in this Type where the approval and resulting unauthorized session are confirmed
scopeExcludes: Push bombing attempts where no approval is confirmed (respective attempt-stage sibling leaves)
ITID-12629.severity: Critical — confirmed account compromise, markedly higher than the attempt-stage siblings.
ITID-12629.escalation: Immediate incident response: force sign-out, credential reset, MFA re-enrollment, and scope-of-compromise investigation.
indicators: Confirmed approval event followed by unauthorized sign-in and post-authentication activity
vectors: Any push-bombing vector in this Type that reached a confirmed approval
rootCauses: Absence of number-matching or rate limiting that would have blocked the fraudulent approval
controls: Number-matching push approval (no simple accept/deny tap)
Push-request rate limiting and automatic lockout after N consecutive denials
Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged/break-glass accounts
Real-time alerting on repeated MFA denials followed by an approval
ITID-12629.detection: Well-instrumented: IdP/MFA provider logs show the exact sequence and timing of push requests and responses, making rapid-fire prompts and off-hours bursts straightforward to detect and correlate with the eventual accept event.
ITID-12629.response: Contact the user directly to confirm intent before treating any approval as legitimate; on confirmed accidental/coerced approval, force sign-out, reset credentials, and re-enroll MFA immediately.
metrics: Count of push-bombing incidents per month
Median number of denied prompts before user reports
Percentage of accounts on number-matching MFA
ITID-12629.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation of the push-bombing attempt leaves above it.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Push Bombing with Confirmed Approval
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where push-bombing succeeded — the user approved an attacker-initiated authentication prompt — requiring full account-takeover response rather than a near-miss handling.

steps.title: Confirm the approval and establish the resulting session's scope
steps.desc: Confirm from logs and user interview that a push was approved, and identify the resulting session's source IP, device, and duration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed approval with full session detail.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all sessions and tokens
steps.desc: Reset the password and invalidate every active session, refresh token, and app password on the account.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; all sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Remove all attacker persistence across affected accounts
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, forwarding rules, OAuth grants, and any created accounts or backdoors found across the full scope.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Restore access with number-matching enforced and validate with the user
steps.desc: Restore access for all affected users, enforce number-matching on push if not already active, and confirm with each user that access and data look correct.
steps.outcome: Verified-clean access restored under hardened push settings.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full timeline, blast radius, and required control changes (number-matching, rate-limiting, phishing-resistant MFA); report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine full extent of attacker activity during the session
steps.desc: Review all activity performed during the attacker's session: data accessed, emails sent, files touched, systems reached, configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Complete activity timeline for the compromised session.

steps.title: Contain any downstream accounts or systems affected
steps.desc: Apply containment (credential reset, session revocation, isolation) to any secondary account or system identified in the blast-radius assessment.
steps.outcome: Blast radius fully contained.

steps.title: Re-enroll MFA on all affected accounts
steps.desc: Remove and re-register MFA methods on every account confirmed or suspected compromised.
steps.outcome: Only verified-legitimate MFA methods remain.

steps.title: Extended monitoring of all affected accounts
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Assess blast radius to other accounts and systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker pivoted from this account to other accounts, shared drives, or connected systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact beyond the initial account.

ITID-12631.def: An incident of an adversary presenting a device as trusted/compliant when it is not, not clearly matching a more specific leaf under this Type.
ITID-12631.purpose: Catch-all for device-impersonation reports not yet matching a more specific technique.
scopeIncludes: Reports of unauthorized access via device-trust spoofing where the specific technique is not yet determined
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the technique is known
ITID-12631.severity: Medium by default; reassess once technique is confirmed.
ITID-12631.priority: P3 pending reclassification, P2 if privileged account/device.
ITID-12631.escalation: Reclassify once the specific device-impersonation technique is clarified.
indicators: Conditional-access anomaly of unclear specific cause tied to device trust
vectors: Activity of unclear specific device-spoofing vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12631.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12631.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12631.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Device Impersonation
playbook.description: Baseline response for a detection or report of an attacker presenting a device to an identity system as if it were a trusted/enrolled endpoint, where the specific spoofing technique has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the device-trust anomaly
steps.desc: Review the alert or report describing the device claiming trusted status and confirm it does not match a known, currently-enrolled device for the user.
steps.guidance: Compare device ID, certificate serial, and compliance attestation against the MDM/device inventory record.
steps.outcome: Confirmed mismatch between claimed and actual enrolled device.
steps.abort: If the device matches a legitimate, recently re-imaged or re-enrolled endpoint, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Revoke the impersonating device's trust and sessions
steps.desc: Remove the device's trusted/compliant status and terminate any sessions established through it.
steps.outcome: Device trust revoked; sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for new device enrollments, MFA methods, or OAuth grants added during the impersonation window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Re-enroll the user's legitimate device and restore access
steps.desc: Verify and re-enroll the user's genuine device, and restore normal account access.
steps.outcome: User has verified-clean device and access restored.

steps.title: Document the technique and evaluate device-trust control gaps
steps.desc: Record how the device impersonation was achieved and recommend hardening (e.g., stronger device attestation, certificate pinning) if a systemic gap is identified.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine the specific impersonation technique
steps.desc: Classify whether the technique used was fingerprint/user-agent spoofing, certificate/token theft, jailbreak masquerading, emulation, hardware ID cloning, cookie theft, or a man-in-the-browser technique.
steps.guidance: Reclassify to the more specific ITID playbook once the technique is known and continue from there if one exists.
steps.outcome: Attack correctly classified by technique.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke tokens on the affected account
steps.desc: Reset the account password and revoke any tokens issued during the impersonated session.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and tokens revoked.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any rogue device enrollment, MFA method, or grant found.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

steps.title: Determine what access the impersonated device obtained
steps.desc: Review authentication and conditional access logs for what the impersonating device was granted access to.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access obtained via the impersonated device.

ITID-12632.def: An adversary manipulates browser/device fingerprinting signals (User-Agent, screen metrics, installed fonts, etc.) to make an untrusted device appear to a service as a device the victim has previously used.
ITID-12632.purpose: Captures spoofing of a device's fingerprint or User-Agent string to make an unmanaged/untrusted device appear as a previously-recognized, trusted one.
scopeIncludes: User-Agent spoofing, fingerprint replay, or fingerprint-randomization-defeat techniques used to bypass device-recognition checks
scopeExcludes: Theft of an actual trusted-device cookie/token (ITID-12637)
Certificate-based device trust theft (ITID-12633)
ITID-12632.escalation: Escalate if paired with a successful sign-in bypassing device-recognition-based step-up.
indicators: Device fingerprint inconsistent with claimed device history
User-Agent string anomalies or known spoofing tool signatures
vectors: Browser automation/fingerprint-spoofing tooling used against login flows
rootCauses: Device recognition relying solely on client-supplied, spoofable signals
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12632.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12632.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12632.notes: Differentiating axis: the spoofed signal is software-level fingerprint/UA data rather than a stolen cryptographic credential.

playbook.name: Response: Spoofed Device Fingerprint/User-Agent Impersonation
playbook.description: For an attack where the adversary manipulated browser/client fingerprint attributes (user-agent string, screen resolution, installed fonts, etc.) to make a foreign device appear to match a previously trusted device profile.

steps.title: Confirm the fingerprint mismatch indicators
steps.desc: Review the risk/anomaly detection alert for the specific fingerprint attributes that triggered suspicion despite a matching device profile claim.
steps.guidance: Look for subtle inconsistencies risk engines flag even when the high-level fingerprint matches, e.g., IP geolocation inconsistent with claimed device history.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fingerprint spoofing indicators documented.
steps.abort: If the anomaly is explained by a legitimate browser/OS update changing the fingerprint, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Terminate the session and force password reset
steps.desc: Kill the active session and reset the account password.
steps.outcome: Session terminated and credential rotated.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for new MFA methods, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added during the session.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access and re-baseline the user's device profile
steps.desc: Restore user access and re-establish a clean device-trust baseline from a verified endpoint.
steps.outcome: User restored to access with a verified-clean device baseline.

steps.title: Document the spoofing technique and recommend attestation hardening
steps.desc: Record the specific fingerprint attributes spoofed and recommend moving trust decisions toward hardware-backed attestation rather than client-reported fingerprints.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine what access was granted based on the spoofed fingerprint
steps.desc: Review conditional access and application logs for what the session accessed after being granted trusted-device status.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access obtained.

steps.title: Block the source IP and strengthen device-trust evaluation
steps.desc: Block the source IP/ASN and, if the platform supports it, enable stronger device signals (hardware-backed attestation, managed-device certificates) rather than relying on browser fingerprint alone.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; device-trust evaluation strengthened.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any rogue MFA method, rule, or grant found.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-12633.def: An adversary exfiltrates a device's enrollment certificate or hardware-bound authentication token and replays it from adversary-controlled infrastructure to be recognized as the legitimate trusted device.
ITID-12633.purpose: Captures theft and reuse of a genuine device certificate or hardware-bound token to impersonate a trusted, enrolled device.
scopeIncludes: Theft of a device management (MDM/Intune-style) enrollment certificate
Extraction and replay of a hardware-bound device authentication token
scopeExcludes: Fingerprint/User-Agent spoofing with no genuine credential theft (ITID-12632)
ITID-12633.severity: High — a stolen certificate is a durable, high-fidelity trust credential.
ITID-12633.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke the certificate at the CA/MDM and force re-enrollment.
indicators: Same device certificate presented from two geographically inconsistent locations
Certificate use from a device that fails other compliance checks
vectors: Malware or physical access used to extract a device certificate/private key
rootCauses: Device certificates not stored in hardware-backed secure enclave/TPM
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12633.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12633.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12633.notes: Differentiating axis: theft of a genuine cryptographic device-trust credential rather than a spoofed software signal.

playbook.name: Response: Stolen Device Certificate/Token Impersonation
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary exfiltrated and reused a legitimate device's authentication certificate or device-bound token to impersonate that trusted endpoint from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

steps.title: Identify the specific certificate/token used and its origin device
steps.desc: Determine which certificate or device-bound token was presented and trace it back to the legitimate device it was issued to.
steps.outcome: Confirmed identity of the stolen certificate/token and its rightful device.

steps.title: Revoke the stolen certificate/token immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the specific certificate via the CA/PKI or invalidate the device-bound token at the identity provider.
steps.guidance: Revocation, not just session termination, is required since a certificate/token can be reused to establish new sessions.
steps.outcome: Certificate/token revoked and no longer usable.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence and reissue a new certificate/token
steps.desc: Check for attacker persistence on any account accessed, then reissue a fresh certificate/device-bound token to the legitimate device.
steps.outcome: No attacker persistence remains; legitimate device has a fresh credential.

steps.title: Restore access with the reissued device credential
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate device operates normally with its new certificate/token and restore full access.
steps.outcome: Device and account access restored on verified-clean credentials.

steps.title: Review certificate/token issuance and storage security
steps.desc: Document the exfiltration vector and recommend hardening of certificate storage (e.g., TPM/secure enclave binding) if the theft resulted from inadequate protection.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine how the certificate/token was likely exfiltrated
steps.desc: Investigate the legitimate device for signs of compromise (malware, unauthorized access) that could explain how its certificate/token was extracted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or ruled-out compromise of the origin device.

steps.title: Isolate the origin device if it shows signs of compromise
steps.desc: If the origin device is found compromised, isolate it from the network pending forensic review.
steps.outcome: Compromised device isolated.
steps.abort: If the origin device shows no compromise, this may be a supply-chain or storage-side leak — investigate the certificate issuance/storage process instead.

steps.title: Remediate the compromised origin device if applicable
steps.desc: Re-image or remediate the origin device if it was found compromised, before reissuing its certificate.
steps.outcome: Origin device confirmed clean before receiving new credentials.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on any account accessed via the stolen credential
steps.desc: Reset credentials and terminate sessions for any account accessed using the impersonated device identity.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and sessions terminated.

ITID-12634.def: An adversary or malware on a rooted/jailbroken device uses root-cloaking tooling to defeat compliance attestation, causing the device to be granted trust it does not qualify for under device-compliance policy.
ITID-12634.purpose: Captures a rooted or jailbroken device that hides its modified state to pass compliance/attestation checks and be treated as a trusted, policy-compliant device.
scopeIncludes: Root/jailbreak-cloaking tools (e.g. Magisk Hide-style) defeating MDM/attestation checks
Compliant-status reported by a device confirmed post-incident to be rooted/jailbroken
scopeExcludes: Emulator/virtual-device impersonation (ITID-12635), a distinct evasion mechanism
ITID-12634.severity: High — root/jailbreak defeats the security assumptions the compliance policy relies on.
ITID-12634.escalation: Escalate immediately; quarantine the device from corporate resources and force re-attestation.
indicators: Post-incident forensic confirmation of root/jailbreak despite a 'compliant' MDM status
Attestation API responses inconsistent with device telemetry
vectors: Root-cloaking apps/modules installed to defeat compliance checks
rootCauses: Attestation relying on OS-reported signals rather than hardware-rooted attestation (e.g. Play Integrity/DeviceCheck hardware tier)
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12634.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12634.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12634.notes: Differentiating axis: the device is physically real but its compliance state is misrepresented, distinct from emulated/virtual devices.

playbook.name: Response: Rooted/Jailbroken Device Masquerading as Compliant
playbook.description: For an incident where a rooted or jailbroken mobile device evaded compliance checks and was granted access as if it met the organization's device-security policy.

steps.title: Confirm the root/jailbreak status and how it evaded detection
steps.desc: Confirm the device's actual root/jailbreak state and determine what technique (e.g., root-hiding tools) allowed it to pass the compliance check.
steps.outcome: Confirmed root/jailbreak status and evasion technique.

steps.title: Revoke the device's access and mark it non-compliant
steps.desc: Remove the device's conditional access trust and flag it as non-compliant in MDM.
steps.outcome: Device access revoked and correctly flagged.

steps.title: Assess whether organizational data was accessed or cached on the device
steps.desc: Determine whether corporate email, files, or app data were synced to or cached on the compromised-trust device.
steps.guidance: A rooted device with app data access represents a materially higher data-exposure risk than a normal unauthorized-login scenario.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any data present on the device.

steps.title: Restore access only after the device (or a replacement) passes compliance
steps.desc: Do not restore access until the user enrolls a genuinely compliant device.
steps.outcome: Access restored only on a verified-compliant device.

steps.title: Close the compliance-check evasion gap
steps.desc: Document the specific evasion technique and work with the MDM vendor/team to close the detection gap (e.g., updated root-detection signatures).
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a remediation ticket against the MDM/endpoint team.

steps.title: Determine what access the device obtained while marked compliant
steps.desc: Review conditional access and application logs for what the non-compliant device accessed while it was incorrectly treated as compliant.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access obtained under the false compliance status.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on the associated account
steps.desc: Reset the account password and terminate active sessions established from the device.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated and sessions terminated.

steps.title: Remote-wipe corporate data from the device if enrolled under MDM management
steps.desc: Issue a selective or full wipe of corporate data/apps from the device.
steps.outcome: Corporate data removed from the non-compliant device.
steps.abort: If the device is personally owned (BYOD) and cannot be wiped, revoke its access instead and notify the user to remove corporate apps manually.

ITID-12635.def: An adversary runs an emulator or virtual device instance configured with spoofed hardware identifiers to be accepted by device-trust checks as a genuine physical device.
ITID-12635.purpose: Captures use of an emulator or virtual machine configured to mimic a legitimate mobile/desktop device in order to pass device-based trust checks.
scopeIncludes: Android/iOS emulators configured with spoofed IMEI/serial/build fingerprints
Virtual machine instances used to defeat device-based conditional access
scopeExcludes: A genuine physical device that has been rooted/jailbroken (ITID-12634)
ITID-12635.escalation: Escalate immediately; block the associated device identifiers and investigate the account for broader compromise.
indicators: Device telemetry consistent with known emulator signatures (timing, sensor absence, virtualized hardware IDs)
Sign-in from a device identifier with no corresponding physical procurement record
vectors: Commodity or custom emulator/farm tooling used for automated account-takeover at scale
rootCauses: Device trust checks not validating against emulator-detection signals
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12635.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12635.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12635.notes: Differentiating axis: no physical device exists at all, versus a real device whose compliance state is misrepresented.

playbook.name: Response: Emulator/Virtual Device Impersonation
playbook.description: For an attack where an emulator or virtualized device was used to present itself as a physical mobile or desktop endpoint in order to pass device-based access controls.

steps.title: Confirm emulator/virtualization indicators
steps.desc: Review the session's device telemetry (hardware IDs, sensor data absence, virtualization artifacts) for indicators of an emulator rather than physical hardware.
steps.guidance: Common indicators include generic/default hardware identifiers, absence of expected sensor data, and known emulator signature strings.
steps.outcome: Confirmed use of an emulator/virtual device.
steps.abort: If the session is explained by a legitimate corporate virtual desktop (VDI), close as a false positive.

steps.title: Terminate the session and force password reset
steps.desc: Kill the active session and reset the account password.
steps.outcome: Session terminated and credential rotated.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for new MFA methods, device enrollments, or OAuth grants added during the session.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access from a verified physical device
steps.desc: Restore user access, confirming the reconnecting device is a genuine, attested physical endpoint.
steps.outcome: User restored to access on a verified-genuine device.

steps.title: Document the emulation technique and evaluate app attestation coverage
steps.desc: Record the emulator signature observed and assess whether app/device attestation coverage should be expanded to close this gap.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine what access was obtained via the emulated device
steps.desc: Review conditional access and application logs for what the emulated session accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access obtained.

steps.title: Block the source IP and tighten conditional access against emulation
steps.desc: Block the source IP/ASN, and if supported, enable app-level attestation (e.g., Play Integrity, DeviceCheck) that specifically flags emulated environments.
steps.outcome: Source blocked; emulator-detection attestation enabled where available.
steps.tool: Identity provider risk policy / app attestation service

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence
steps.desc: Delete any rogue MFA method, device enrollment, or grant found.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-12636.def: An adversary programs adversary-controlled hardware with the cloned hardware identifiers of a victim's legitimate enrolled device, so that identifier-based trust checks cannot distinguish the two.
ITID-12636.purpose: Captures cloning of a device's hardware identifiers (IMEI, MAC address, serial number) onto adversary-controlled hardware to impersonate a specific enrolled device.
scopeIncludes: IMEI/MAC/serial-number cloning onto physical adversary hardware
scopeExcludes: Software-only fingerprint/User-Agent spoofing with no hardware-identifier cloning (ITID-12632)
Emulated/virtual devices with no physical cloned hardware (ITID-12635)
ITID-12636.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke trust bound to the cloned identifier and issue a new identifier to the legitimate device.
indicators: Same hardware identifier observed active from two physically inconsistent locations simultaneously
Carrier/network anomaly reports of duplicate device identifiers
vectors: Physical access to a device sufficient to extract and reprogram identifiers onto cloned hardware
rootCauses: Trust decisions relying solely on a static hardware identifier with no additional cryptographic binding
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12636.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12636.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12636.notes: Differentiating axis: identifier cloning onto real, separate physical hardware — the most physically involved variant among the device-impersonation siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Cloned Device Identity (Hardware Identifier Spoofing)
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary cloned a legitimate device's hardware identifiers (IMEI, MAC address, serial number, or similar) onto attacker-controlled hardware to impersonate a trusted endpoint.

steps.title: Confirm the cloned identifier and identify the legitimate device it was cloned from
steps.desc: Determine which hardware identifier was duplicated and trace it back to the legitimate device record.
steps.guidance: Look for two simultaneous or overlapping sessions claiming the same hardware identifier from different locations/networks — a strong cloning indicator.
steps.outcome: Confirmed cloned identifier and its legitimate source device.

steps.title: Revoke trust for the cloned identifier and terminate its sessions
steps.desc: Remove the hardware identifier's trusted status and kill any active sessions tied to it.
steps.outcome: Cloned identifier's trust revoked; sessions terminated.

steps.title: Re-provision the legitimate device with a fresh, non-guessable identifier where possible
steps.desc: Work with the endpoint/network team to reissue or re-bind the legitimate device's identity to prevent further cloning.
steps.guidance: Some identifiers (e.g., IMEI) cannot be changed — in that case, layer additional attestation (certificate-based NAC) on top instead.
steps.outcome: Legitimate device's trust re-established on a hardened basis.

steps.title: Restore access for the legitimate device and user
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate device and user regain normal access under the re-hardened identity.
steps.outcome: Legitimate device and user access restored.

steps.title: Document the cloning technique and evaluate identifier-based trust reliance
steps.desc: Record how the identifier was captured/cloned and recommend reducing reliance on static hardware identifiers alone for trust decisions.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Determine what access the cloned device obtained
steps.desc: Review conditional access, network access control (NAC), and application logs for what the cloned-identity device accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of access obtained via the cloned identity.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke tokens on any account accessed
steps.desc: Reset credentials and revoke tokens for any account accessed via the cloned device identity.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and tokens revoked.

steps.title: Audit for and remove attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for and remove any new MFA method, account, or rule added during the cloned-device access window.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains.

ITID-12637.def: An adversary steals a persistent 'trusted device' cookie or token (issued after a prior successful MFA challenge) and replays it to skip MFA on subsequent logins as if from the original trusted device.
ITID-12637.purpose: Captures theft of a browser or app 'remember this device' cookie/token that grants an adversary the trusted-device exemption from re-authentication or MFA.
scopeIncludes: Theft of 'remember this device'/device-trust cookies via malware, browser data theft, or endpoint compromise
Replay of a stolen device-trust token from a different device/browser
scopeExcludes: General web session-token theft unrelated to a device-trust exemption (Session Hijacking Type, ITID-12921-12929)
ITID-12637.severity: High — directly skips the MFA challenge entirely.
ITID-12637.escalation: Escalate immediately; invalidate all trusted-device tokens for the account and require re-authentication with MFA everywhere.
indicators: Trusted-device cookie/token used from a browser/device fingerprint inconsistent with its original issuance
Sign-in with no MFA challenge from an unrecognized IP
vectors: Infostealer malware harvesting browser cookies/local storage
Endpoint compromise exfiltrating device-trust tokens
rootCauses: Device-trust tokens with excessively long validity and no re-binding to device fingerprint
mitreTechniques: T1550.004 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12637.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12637.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12637.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from the general Session Hijacking Type (ITID-12921-12929) by requiring the stolen artifact to specifically be an MFA-exempting device-trust token, not an ordinary logged-in session.

playbook.name: Response: Trusted-Device Cookie/Token Theft
playbook.description: For an attack where an adversary stole a 'remember this device' cookie or trusted-device token (via malware, session hijacking, or browser data theft) and reused it to skip MFA on future logins.

steps.title: Confirm the trusted-device cookie/token was reused from an unfamiliar context
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for a login that skipped MFA via a trusted-device cookie/token, from a source (IP, browser, location) inconsistent with the legitimate device's history.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous reuse of the trusted-device credential.

steps.title: Revoke the trusted-device token/cookie and terminate the session
steps.desc: Invalidate the specific trusted-device token at the identity provider and kill the active session.
steps.outcome: Token revoked; session terminated.

steps.title: Audit for attacker persistence
steps.desc: Check for new MFA methods, forwarding rules, or OAuth grants added during the session established via the stolen token.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore access and require fresh MFA/device trust re-establishment
steps.desc: Restore the user's access with a fresh password and require the trusted-device relationship to be re-established from a confirmed-clean device.
steps.outcome: User has clean access and a fresh device-trust relationship.

steps.title: Document the theft vector and reconsider trusted-device cookie lifetime
steps.desc: Record how the token was stolen and evaluate whether trusted-device 'remember me' duration should be shortened or require periodic re-verification.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete policy recommendation.

steps.title: Determine the likely theft vector
steps.desc: Investigate the legitimate device for malware or browser-data-stealing activity (infostealer) that could explain the cookie/token theft.
steps.guidance: Trusted-device cookies are a common infostealer malware target — check EDR alerts and browser artifact access on the legitimate device.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or ruled-out malware compromise as the theft vector.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke all sessions/tokens on the account
steps.desc: Reset the account password and invalidate all sessions and tokens, not just the stolen one.
steps.outcome: Credential rotated; all sessions and tokens terminated.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence and clean the malware source device
steps.desc: Delete any rogue MFA method, rule, or grant, and complete malware removal/re-imaging of the source device if it was infected.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains; source device clean.

steps.title: Isolate and remediate the legitimate device if malware is confirmed
steps.desc: Isolate the infected device from the network and begin malware remediation.
steps.outcome: Compromised device contained pending remediation.

ITID-12638.def: Malware resident in the victim's browser on their own trusted device intercepts and manipulates the authentication flow in real time (injecting requests, altering responses) to extend or abuse the device's existing trust without the device itself being spoofed.
ITID-12638.purpose: Captures man-in-the-browser malware that manipulates a legitimate, already-trusted device's browser session in real time to bypass device-trust checks from within the trusted device itself.
scopeIncludes: Browser-resident malware/extensions that manipulate live authentication traffic on a genuinely trusted device
scopeExcludes: Device fingerprint/identifier spoofing from a separate adversary-controlled device (other leaves in this Type)
ITID-12638.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat the endpoint as compromised and remediate before trusting further authentication from it.
indicators: Malicious browser extension or injected script detected on an otherwise-trusted device
Authentication traffic anomalies originating from a device that itself passes compliance checks
vectors: Malicious browser extensions
Banking-trojan-style man-in-the-browser malware
rootCauses: Lack of endpoint detection for malicious browser extensions
Browser session integrity not independently verified beyond device compliance status
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12638.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12638.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12638.notes: Differentiating axis: the device itself is genuinely trusted and unspoofed; the abuse happens through malware manipulating the session from inside that trust boundary.

playbook.name: Response: Man-in-the-Browser Device Trust Bypass
playbook.description: For an attack where browser-resident malware (a man-in-the-browser trojan or malicious extension) manipulated an authenticated session or its device-trust signals from within the legitimate user's own trusted browser.

steps.title: Confirm the anomalous activity originated from within a legitimately trusted session
steps.desc: Review the anomaly (unexpected transaction, configuration change, or data access) and confirm it occurred from the user's own trusted device/session rather than an external login.
steps.guidance: This is the key distinguishing feature from other device-impersonation ITIDs — the device trust is genuine, but the browser session itself is compromised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the anomaly originated from within the legitimate trusted session.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the device from the network to stop further manipulation.
steps.outcome: Device isolated pending remediation.

steps.title: Remove the malicious browser component and verify no other persistence
steps.desc: Remove the malicious extension/trojan and scan the endpoint for other malware persistence.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean of the malicious component and any related persistence.

steps.title: Restore the device and re-verify account access
steps.desc: Re-image or fully clear the endpoint if warranted, and restore the user's normal account access with fresh credentials.
steps.outcome: User has a verified-clean device and account access restored.

steps.title: Document the MitB technique and review browser/extension controls
steps.desc: Record the malware family and delivery vector, and recommend browser extension allow-listing or endpoint controls to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete control recommendation.

steps.title: Identify the malicious browser component
steps.desc: Work with the endpoint team to identify the malicious extension, plugin, or trojan present in the browser.
steps.guidance: Check installed extensions, unexpected proxy/certificate settings, and EDR alerts for known MitB malware families.
steps.outcome: Malicious browser component identified.

steps.title: Terminate affected sessions and force password reset
steps.desc: Kill any active sessions from the device and reset passwords for accounts accessed through the compromised browser.
steps.outcome: Sessions terminated and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Reverse any unauthorized transactions or changes made through the manipulated session
steps.desc: Identify and reverse any transaction, data change, or configuration modification made by the malware while masquerading as the user.
steps.outcome: Affected systems restored to pre-incident state.

ITID-12639.def: A confirmed instance of device impersonation (any technique) in which the adversary successfully bypassed device-trust/compliance checks and authenticated as the impersonated device.
ITID-12639.purpose: Escalation leaf for confirmed successful device impersonation where the adversary obtained an authenticated session by bypassing device-trust checks.
scopeIncludes: Any sibling device-impersonation leaf in this Type where downstream unauthorized authentication is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Device-impersonation attempts where no successful bypass is confirmed (respective attempt-stage sibling leaves)
ITID-12639.severity: Critical — confirmed account/device-trust compromise, markedly higher than attempt-stage siblings.
ITID-12639.escalation: Immediate incident response: revoke device trust, reset credentials, and investigate scope of access gained.
indicators: Confirmed unauthorized authentication via a bypassed device-trust check followed by post-authentication activity
vectors: Any device-impersonation vector in this Type that reached successful use
rootCauses: Device trust granted based on spoofable or stolen signals with no compensating hardware-backed attestation
mitreTechniques: T1550.004 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
controls: Device compliance/attestation enforcement (managed-device conditional access)
Certificate-based device trust with hardware-backed key storage
Continuous device-risk scoring (jailbreak/root detection, emulator detection)
Session/cookie binding to device fingerprint with anomaly alerting
ITID-12639.detection: Moderate-to-strong: device-attestation and MDM telemetry flag jailbroken/rooted or emulated devices directly, and conditional-access logs surface device-fingerprint or certificate mismatches when an impersonated device attempts to reuse trust it was never granted.
ITID-12639.response: Revoke the device's trust/certificate and any session tied to it immediately; force re-enrollment through an attested, compliant device before restoring access.
metrics: Count of device-impersonation incidents per month
Percentage of devices enrolled with hardware-backed attestation
Mean time to revoke an impersonated device's trust
ITID-12639.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation of the device-impersonation attempt leaves above it.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Device Impersonation with Confirmed Bypass
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where device impersonation (of any technique) resulted in verified attacker access — the high-severity, post-compromise variant of the device impersonation family requiring full account-takeover response.

steps.title: Confirm and scope the successful impersonation
steps.desc: Establish, from logs and investigation, that the impersonated device successfully bypassed device-trust controls and gained access, and determine which technique was used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed successful bypass with technique and timeline documented.

steps.title: Revoke device trust, sessions, and force password reset
steps.desc: Revoke the impersonated device's trust status, terminate all sessions/tokens, and reset the affected account's password.
steps.outcome: Device trust revoked; sessions terminated; credential rotated.

steps.title: Remove all attacker persistence across affected accounts and devices
steps.desc: Remove rogue MFA enrollments, device enrollments, forwarding rules, OAuth grants, and any created accounts or backdoors found across the full scope.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access mechanism remains anywhere in scope.

steps.title: Restore access and validate with the user
steps.desc: Restore access for all affected users and confirm with each that access and data look correct.
steps.outcome: Verified-clean access restored for all affected users.

steps.title: Conduct a formal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document root cause, full timeline, blast radius, and required control changes (device attestation, certificate hardening, conditional access); report to relevant stakeholders per incident severity policy.
steps.outcome: Formal after-action report completed with assigned remediation owners.

steps.title: Determine full extent of attacker activity post-access
steps.desc: Review all activity performed by the attacker during their access window: data accessed, emails sent, files touched, systems reached.
steps.outcome: Complete activity timeline for the compromised session.

steps.title: Contain any downstream systems or accounts affected
steps.desc: Apply containment (credential reset, session revocation, isolation) to any secondary account or system identified in the blast-radius assessment.
steps.outcome: Blast radius fully contained.

steps.title: Re-establish device trust and MFA on legitimate bases
steps.desc: Re-enroll the user's legitimate device and MFA methods from a verified-clean state.
steps.outcome: Only verified-legitimate device and MFA methods remain.

steps.title: Extended monitoring of all affected accounts and devices
steps.desc: Place all affected accounts and devices under elevated monitoring for at least 30 days.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous activity observed during the window.

steps.title: Assess blast radius to other accounts and systems
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker used the impersonated device's access to pivot to other accounts, shared drives, or connected systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of impact beyond the initial account/device.

ITID-12641.def: An incident of an adversary hijacking a victim's phone number to intercept SMS/voice-based MFA, not clearly matching a more specific leaf under this Type.
ITID-12641.purpose: Catch-all for SIM-swap reports not yet matching a more specific mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Reports of a suspected SIM swap where the specific mechanism (carrier social engineering, insider, self-service portal, eSIM, porting, physical theft) is not yet determined
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is known
Downstream digital-wallet fraud enabled by a SIM swap (ITID-53712, tracked as a financial-fraud outcome)
ITID-12641.severity: Medium by default; reassess once mechanism and downstream impact are confirmed.
ITID-12641.priority: P3 pending reclassification, P2 if privileged/high-value account tied to the number.
ITID-12641.escalation: Reclassify once the specific mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Sudden, unexplained loss of cellular service on the victim's device
vectors: Activity of unclear specific SIM-swap vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Migration away from SMS/voice as an MFA factor for high-value accounts toward app-based or hardware MFA
Carrier account PIN/passcode and port-freeze enrollment
Step-up verification for any SIM-swap-adjacent event (new device sign-in shortly after a carrier change)
Real-time carrier port/SIM-change notification monitoring where available
ITID-12641.detection: Partial and largely dependent on carrier and telecom-adjacent telemetry outside direct enterprise control: sudden loss of cellular service on the victim's phone, a carrier port/SIM-change notification, or a cluster of SMS-based MFA resets immediately following a reported service outage are the primary internal signals.
ITID-12641.response: On any indicator, immediately disable SMS/voice as an MFA factor for the affected account, force a credential reset, and coordinate with the user to re-secure the carrier account.
metrics: Count of SIM-swap-related incidents per quarter
Percentage of high-value accounts still using SMS/voice as an MFA factor
Mean time to disable SMS MFA after a suspected swap
detections: SMS-based MFA reset correlated with reported service loss
New-device sign-in shortly after phone-number-based MFA reset
ITID-12641.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General SIM Swap Attack
playbook.description: Baseline response for a report or detection of a user's phone number being fraudulently transferred to an attacker-controlled SIM/device, where the specific method used has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm loss of cellular service as reported by the user
steps.desc: Confirm with the user that their phone unexpectedly lost signal/service, a classic first indicator of a completed SIM swap.
steps.guidance: Ask when service was lost and whether they received any unexpected 'SIM change' or 'porting' confirmation texts/emails beforehand.
steps.outcome: Confirmed timeline of service loss and any precursor notifications.

steps.title: Initiate carrier SIM/port reversal
steps.desc: Work with the carrier to reverse the unauthorized swap/port and restore the number to the legitimate SIM/device.
steps.outcome: Number restored to the legitimate device.

steps.title: Audit each at-risk account for attacker access or persistence
steps.desc: Review each account for evidence of attacker login or persistence during the window the number was under attacker control.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any account compromise.

steps.title: Confirm carrier account security is hardened and restore normal use
steps.desc: Add a carrier PIN/passcode and port-lock to the account, and confirm the user's normal phone service is fully restored.
steps.outcome: Phone service restored with hardened carrier account controls.

steps.title: Document the swap method and reinforce moving away from SMS MFA
steps.desc: Record how the swap was executed and recommend that all users/accounts relying on SMS-based MFA migrate to app-based or hardware authentication.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with a concrete policy recommendation.

steps.title: Contact the carrier to confirm and get the swap timeline
steps.desc: Contact the mobile carrier's fraud team directly to confirm the SIM/port change and obtain the exact timestamp and method used to authorize it.
steps.guidance: Use the carrier's dedicated fraud line, not general support, for faster escalation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed swap timestamp and authorization method from the carrier.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on every account tied to the number
steps.desc: Reset passwords and terminate active sessions on every account identified as using the number for MFA/recovery.
steps.guidance: Do this even before number restoration is confirmed, since the attacker may already be using the number.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and sessions terminated across all at-risk accounts.

steps.title: Remove any confirmed persistence and move affected accounts off SMS-based MFA
steps.desc: Remove any rogue access mechanism found, and migrate affected accounts to an app-based or hardware MFA method not tied to the phone number.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access remains; accounts hardened against future SIM-based attacks.

steps.title: Identify every account tied to the phone number for SMS/voice MFA or recovery
steps.desc: Enumerate all accounts (personal and corporate) that use this phone number for SMS-based MFA, voice-call verification, or password recovery.
steps.guidance: This defines the full blast radius — any of these accounts could now be targeted using the stolen number.
steps.outcome: Complete list of accounts at risk via this phone number.

ITID-12642.def: An adversary contacts the victim's mobile carrier, impersonating the victim using gathered PII, and convinces a support representative to port the victim's number onto a SIM the adversary controls.
ITID-12642.purpose: Captures the classic pattern of an adversary social-engineering a mobile carrier's customer support representative into transferring the victim's number to an attacker-controlled SIM.
scopeIncludes: Phone/chat social engineering of carrier support staff to execute a SIM swap
scopeExcludes: Swaps facilitated by a complicit carrier insider (ITID-12643)
Swaps executed through a self-service online portal (ITID-12644)
ITID-12642.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-value accounts.
ITID-12642.escalation: Escalate immediately; coordinate with the carrier's fraud team to reverse the port and disable SMS MFA.
indicators: Carrier confirms a support-desk-initiated SIM change consistent with social engineering
Sudden loss of service followed by MFA-driven account changes
vectors: Pretexting carrier support with victim PII obtained from breaches or OSINT
rootCauses: Weak carrier identity-verification procedures for SIM changes
controls: Migration away from SMS/voice as an MFA factor for high-value accounts toward app-based or hardware MFA
Carrier account PIN/passcode and port-freeze enrollment
Step-up verification for any SIM-swap-adjacent event (new device sign-in shortly after a carrier change)
Real-time carrier port/SIM-change notification monitoring where available
ITID-12642.detection: Partial and largely dependent on carrier and telecom-adjacent telemetry outside direct enterprise control: sudden loss of cellular service on the victim's phone, a carrier port/SIM-change notification, or a cluster of SMS-based MFA resets immediately following a reported service outage are the primary internal signals.
ITID-12642.response: On any indicator, immediately disable SMS/voice as an MFA factor for the affected account, force a credential reset, and coordinate with the user to re-secure the carrier account.
metrics: Count of SIM-swap-related incidents per quarter
Percentage of high-value accounts still using SMS/voice as an MFA factor
Mean time to disable SMS MFA after a suspected swap
detections: SMS-based MFA reset correlated with reported service loss
New-device sign-in shortly after phone-number-based MFA reset
ITID-12642.notes: Differentiating axis: the swap is executed through legitimate carrier support channels via social engineering, distinct from insider assistance or self-service abuse.

playbook.name: Response: Social Engineering-Based Carrier SIM Swap
playbook.description: For a SIM swap achieved by an attacker directly deceiving carrier customer support staff (impersonating the victim, providing plausible-sounding PII) into transferring the number to a new SIM.

steps.title: Confirm the swap and gather the carrier's call/interaction record
steps.desc: Contact the carrier fraud team to confirm the swap and request the recording/transcript or notes of the support interaction that authorized it.
steps.guidance: This record is critical evidence for both remediation and any law-enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Carrier interaction record obtained describing what the attacker presented to authorize the swap.

steps.title: Reverse the swap and lock the carrier account
steps.desc: Work with the carrier to restore the number and apply an account lock/enhanced verification requirement for any future changes.
steps.outcome: Number restored; carrier account locked against further unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Audit each at-risk account for compromise
steps.desc: Review each account for evidence of attacker access during the swap window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any account compromise.

steps.title: Add a carrier PIN and restore normal service
steps.desc: Set a carrier account PIN/passcode required for any future account changes, and confirm phone service restoration.
steps.outcome: Phone service restored with a hardened carrier account.

steps.title: Report the social-engineering technique and consider a carrier complaint/regulatory report
steps.desc: Document the social-engineering script used against the carrier, and consider filing a complaint with the carrier and, if warranted, a regulatory or law-enforcement report given the identity-theft dimension.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; external reporting completed where applicable.

steps.title: Assess what PII the attacker used and its likely source
steps.desc: Identify what personal information (SSN, DOB, address, previous bills) the attacker presented, and assess whether it suggests a prior data breach or targeted OSINT gathering against this specific user.
steps.outcome: Understanding of the PII source informing whether other systems/accounts need review.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on every account tied to the number
steps.desc: Reset passwords and terminate sessions on all identified at-risk accounts.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and sessions terminated across all at-risk accounts.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence and migrate off SMS-based MFA
steps.desc: Remove any rogue access mechanism found, and move affected accounts to app-based or hardware MFA.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access remains; accounts hardened.

steps.title: Identify all accounts tied to the phone number
steps.desc: Enumerate all accounts using this phone number for SMS MFA, voice verification, or recovery.
steps.outcome: Complete list of at-risk accounts.

ITID-12643.def: An adversary pays or coerces a carrier employee to directly execute an unauthorized SIM swap on the victim's number, bypassing normal identity-verification procedures entirely.
ITID-12643.purpose: Captures SIM swaps carried out with the direct, willing assistance of a corrupted or bribed carrier employee.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected carrier-employee complicity in executing a SIM swap
scopeExcludes: Swaps achieved purely through external social engineering of support staff with no complicity (ITID-12642)
ITID-12643.severity: Critical — insider complicity bypasses every external control.
ITID-12643.escalation: Escalate immediately to carrier fraud/security team; this typically requires law-enforcement coordination.
indicators: Carrier internal audit trail showing account access by an employee with no legitimate service ticket
Pattern of swaps traced to a single carrier employee across multiple victims
vectors: Bribery or coercion of carrier retail/support staff
rootCauses: Insufficient carrier-side auditing/dual-control on SIM-swap actions performed by staff

Carrier account PIN/passcode and port-freeze enrollment
Step-up verification for any SIM-swap-adjacent event (new device sign-in shortly after a carrier change)

playbook.name: Response: Insider-Assisted Carrier SIM Swap
playbook.description: For a SIM swap where investigation indicates a carrier employee (or contractor) directly and improperly authorized the transfer, bypassing normal verification, rather than being deceived by social engineering.

steps.title: Confirm the swap and request the carrier's internal authorization record
steps.desc: Contact the carrier's fraud/security team and specifically request the internal record of which employee authorized the change and by what process.
steps.guidance: Insider involvement is often only surfaced when the carrier's own fraud investigation finds no normal verification was actually performed.
steps.outcome: Carrier internal authorization record obtained.

steps.title: Reverse the swap and escalate the case with the carrier's fraud/legal team
steps.desc: Work with the carrier to restore the number and formally escalate the insider-fraud finding to their fraud and legal teams for their own internal action.
steps.outcome: Number restored; carrier formally engaged on the insider-fraud angle.

steps.title: Audit each at-risk account for compromise
steps.desc: Review each account for evidence of attacker access during the swap window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any account compromise.

steps.title: Add carrier account protections and restore service
steps.desc: Add a carrier PIN and port-lock, and confirm phone service restoration.
steps.outcome: Phone service restored with hardened carrier account controls.

steps.title: Document and formally report the insider-fraud finding
steps.desc: Record the full finding and file a formal report with the carrier and, given the insider dimension, consider a law-enforcement report; brief legal/compliance stakeholders given the potential systemic risk if the insider affected other customers.
steps.outcome: Formal report filed; internal stakeholders briefed.

steps.title: Assess indicators of insider involvement
steps.desc: Review the carrier's findings for indicators such as bypassed verification steps, unusual account access patterns by staff, or connections between the employee and known fraud rings.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or reasonably suspected insider involvement documented.
steps.abort: If the carrier's investigation attributes the swap to social engineering rather than insider action, redirect to the social-engineering carrier swap playbook.

steps.title: Force password reset and revoke sessions on every account tied to the number
steps.desc: Reset passwords and terminate sessions on all identified at-risk accounts.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and sessions terminated across all at-risk accounts.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence and migrate off SMS-based MFA
steps.desc: Remove any rogue access mechanism found, and move affected accounts to app-based or hardware MFA.
steps.outcome: No attacker-controlled access remains; accounts hardened.

steps.title: Identify all accounts tied to the phone number
steps.desc: Enumerate all accounts using this phone number for SMS MFA, voice verification, or recovery.
steps.outcome: Complete list of at-risk accounts.

ITID-12644.def: An adversary logs into the victim's carrier self-service account (using stolen credentials or a weak account-recovery flow) and initiates a SIM swap or eSIM transfer directly through the automated portal.

scopeExcludes: Swaps requiring live interaction with carrier support staff (ITID-12642, ITID-12643)

ITID-12644.escalation: Escalate immediately; determine whether the carrier account credentials were reused from a known breach.

No support-ticket record corresponding to the swap

Password reuse between the carrier account and previously breached credentials

Carrier account PIN/passcode and port-freeze enrollment
Step-up verification for any SIM-swap-adjacent event (new device sign-in shortly after a carrier change)
Real-time carrier port/SIM-change notification monitoring where available

Mean time to disable SMS MFA after a suspected swap
detections: SMS-based MFA reset correlated with reported service loss
New-device sign-in shortly after phone-number-based MFA reset
ITID-12644.notes: Differentiating axis: fully automated, self-service execution path with no human carrier interaction.

playbook.name: Response: Online/Self-Service Portal SIM Swap
playbook.description: For a SIM swap performed entirely through the carrier's self-service web/app portal, typically using a stolen or guessed portal password rather than any interaction with carrier staff.

steps.title: Confirm the swap occurred via the self-service portal
steps.desc: Contact the carrier to confirm the change was made through the online/app portal and obtain the login timestamp, source IP, and authentication method used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed portal-based swap with login details.

steps.title: Reverse the swap and reset the carrier portal password
steps.desc: Work with the carrier to restore the number and immediately reset the carrier portal account password.
steps.outcome: Number restored; carrier portal credential rotated.

steps.title: Audit each at-risk account for compromise
steps.desc: Review each account for evidence of attacker access during the swap window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any account compromise.

steps.title: Enable MFA on the carrier portal account and restore service
steps.desc: Enable MFA (not SMS-based) on the carrier portal account itself if supported, add a port-lock, and confirm phone service restoration.
steps.outcome: Carrier portal hardened; phone service restored.

steps.title: Document the credential-reuse vector and reinforce unique-password hygiene
steps.desc: Record how the carrier password was obtained and issue guidance on avoiding password reuse across the carrier account and other services.

steps.title: Determine how the carrier portal credential was obtained
steps.desc: Assess whether the carrier account password was reused from a breached site, phished, or guessed, by checking breach-monitoring data and interviewing the user about password reuse.
