steps.title: Determine what the attacker did with the impersonated token
steps.desc: Review what actions were taken using the newly elevated privilege (e.g. SYSTEM-level command execution).
steps.outcome: Actions taken with elevated privilege documented.

steps.title: Harden against unauthorized named pipe creation/impersonation
steps.desc: Review application allowlisting, EDR behavioral rules, and where feasible restrict SeImpersonatePrivilege on standard user accounts to reduce this attack surface.
steps.outcome: Hardening applied or ticketed.

ITID-12743.def: An adversary injects malicious code into a running higher-privileged process and calls token-manipulation APIs (e.g. OpenProcessToken, DuplicateToken) from within that process's context to steal and reuse its token.
ITID-12743.purpose: Captures token impersonation carried out by injecting code into a higher-privileged process and stealing its token from within.
scopeIncludes: Process injection specifically used as the vector to reach and duplicate a target process's token
scopeExcludes: Named-pipe-based impersonation with no process injection (ITID-12742)
ITID-12743.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the target process runs as SYSTEM/domain-privileged.
ITID-12743.escalation: Escalate immediately; isolate the host and terminate the injected process.
indicators: EDR alert on code injection into a privileged process followed by a token-duplication API call
vectors: DLL injection, process hollowing, or reflective injection into a privileged process
rootCauses: Insufficient process-integrity protections allowing injection into privileged processes
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12743.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12743.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12743.notes: Differentiating axis: the specific technique is process injection as the path to token theft.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation via Process Injection
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack where the attacker injected code into a higher-privileged process and stole/reused its access token to operate with that process's privilege.

steps.title: Confirm process injection into a higher-privileged process
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry for code injection indicators (e.g. CreateRemoteThread, unusual memory allocation) targeting a higher-privileged process.
steps.outcome: Confirmed injection event with source and target process identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint where the injection occurred.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild the endpoint
steps.desc: Reimage the endpoint given the depth of compromise implied by successful process injection into a privileged process.
steps.outcome: Endpoint reimaged from a known-clean source.

steps.title: Verify the rebuilt endpoint is clean before return to service
steps.desc: Confirm the endpoint is clean before returning it to the user.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean.

steps.title: Document the technique and confirm detection/prevention coverage
steps.desc: Record the finding and confirm exploit-protection/ASR rule coverage across the fleet.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; coverage confirmed or ticketed.

steps.title: Identify the target process and its privilege level
steps.desc: Determine which process was injected into and the privilege/token it held.
steps.outcome: Target process and privilege level identified.

steps.title: Terminate the injected/malicious process
steps.desc: Kill the compromised process and any processes it spawned with elevated privilege.
steps.guidance: Killing the legitimately-running-but-injected process may disrupt a business service — coordinate with the system owner if it's a critical service.
steps.outcome: Malicious activity terminated.

steps.title: Investigate initial access and injection technique used
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained the initial foothold and which specific injection technique was used, to inform detection tuning.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector and technique documented.

steps.title: Determine what actions were taken using the stolen token
steps.desc: Review activity performed by the injected code operating with the target process's elevated token.
steps.outcome: Actions documented.

steps.title: Enable/verify exploit protection and attack surface reduction rules
steps.desc: Confirm endpoint protection features that block common injection techniques (e.g. ASR rules, exploit protection) are enabled fleet-wide.
steps.outcome: Protections confirmed enabled or gap ticketed.

ITID-12744.def: An adversary uses any token-impersonation technique to elevate their session from a standard/service-account privilege level to full SYSTEM privilege on the local host.
ITID-12744.purpose: Captures token impersonation used specifically to escalate a session to SYSTEM-level privilege on the local host, the most common objective of this technique.
scopeIncludes: Any token-impersonation mechanism where the confirmed outcome is local SYSTEM-level privilege
scopeExcludes: Token impersonation used for lateral movement to a remote host rather than local privilege escalation (ITID-12745)
ITID-12744.severity: Critical — SYSTEM privilege grants full local control including credential-dumping capability.
ITID-12744.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat the host as fully compromised at the highest local privilege level.
indicators: Process token lineage showing an escalation from a standard/service account to SYSTEM
vectors: Any token-impersonation technique culminating in local SYSTEM elevation
rootCauses: Standard/service accounts holding SeImpersonatePrivilege unnecessarily
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12744.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12744.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12744.notes: Differentiating axis: the confirmed objective/outcome (local SYSTEM privilege escalation) rather than the specific mechanism used to get there.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation for SYSTEM-Level Privilege Escalation
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack whose specific and confirmed outcome was full SYSTEM-level privilege escalation on the endpoint, regardless of the specific technique used.

steps.title: Confirm SYSTEM-level privilege was achieved
steps.desc: Confirm via EDR telemetry that a process operated with the SYSTEM token following the impersonation activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed SYSTEM-level access achieved.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint given the severity of confirmed SYSTEM-level compromise.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild the endpoint from a known-clean image
steps.desc: Reimage the endpoint — do not attempt in-place remediation given confirmed SYSTEM-level compromise.
steps.outcome: Endpoint rebuilt from a known-clean source.

steps.title: Extended monitoring given the severity of SYSTEM-level compromise
steps.desc: Apply elevated monitoring on the rebuilt endpoint and any account whose credentials may have been exposed, for an extended period.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed during the monitoring window.

steps.title: Full incident report given confirmed local privilege escalation to SYSTEM
steps.desc: Document the complete attack chain and response; brief leadership given the severity of full local system compromise.
steps.outcome: Full report completed.

steps.title: Determine the specific technique used to reach SYSTEM
steps.desc: Establish the specific mechanism (named pipe impersonation, process injection, rogue service, SeImpersonatePrivilege abuse) that led to SYSTEM privilege.
steps.outcome: Technique identified.

steps.title: Check for and contain any credential theft enabled by SYSTEM access
steps.desc: Since SYSTEM privilege enables LSASS/SAM access, check whether the attacker used it to dump credentials and, if so, follow the appropriate PtH/PtT containment steps in parallel.
steps.outcome: Any resulting credential theft identified and contained.

steps.title: Reset any credentials confirmed or suspected harvested via the SYSTEM-level access
steps.desc: Rotate passwords for any account whose credentials may have been accessible from the compromised endpoint at SYSTEM level.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Catalogue everything done at SYSTEM level
steps.desc: Given SYSTEM privilege grants essentially unrestricted local access, thoroughly catalogue every action taken — file access, registry changes, new accounts, credential dumping, persistence.
steps.guidance: SYSTEM-level compromise should be treated as a full local compromise — assume the attacker could access anything on the machine.
steps.outcome: Complete catalogue of SYSTEM-level actions.

steps.title: Investigate initial access and close the escalation path
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained the initial foothold and remediate the specific escalation technique's root cause.
steps.outcome: Initial access and escalation path closed.

ITID-12745.def: An adversary uses a stolen/impersonated token to authenticate to and act on a remote host, extending token-impersonation privilege escalation into network lateral movement.
ITID-12745.purpose: Captures token impersonation used to pivot to a remote host, extending the technique beyond local privilege escalation into lateral movement.
scopeIncludes: Use of an impersonated token to establish sessions or execute actions on a remote system
scopeExcludes: Token impersonation confined to local privilege escalation with no remote pivot (ITID-12744)
ITID-12745.severity: Critical — extends compromise beyond the originally-compromised host.
ITID-12745.escalation: Escalate immediately; isolate both the source and target hosts and scope the full lateral-movement chain.
indicators: Remote authentication/action immediately following a local token-impersonation event on the source host
vectors: Impersonated token combined with remote service creation or WMI/PsExec-style execution
rootCauses: Impersonated tokens carrying network-authentication rights not scoped to the local host only
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12745.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12745.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12745.notes: Differentiating axis: scope extends to a remote host, distinguishing this from the local-privilege-escalation sibling.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation for Remote Lateral Movement
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack where the elevated/impersonated token was used to authenticate to and move laterally onto other systems on the network (e.g. via the impersonated token's network credentials).

steps.title: Confirm the impersonated token was used for remote/network access
steps.desc: Correlate the local token impersonation event with subsequent remote authentication activity using the impersonated account's identity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed remote use of the impersonated token.

steps.title: Isolate every system in the lateral movement path
steps.desc: Network-isolate the originating endpoint and every system subsequently accessed.
steps.outcome: All affected systems isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild every affected system
steps.desc: Reimage the originating endpoint and any subsequently accessed systems where compromise is confirmed or suspected.
steps.outcome: Affected systems rebuilt from known-clean sources.

steps.title: Verify all affected systems are clean before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Confirm every system in the lateral movement path is clean before closing.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Full incident report with lateral movement analysis
steps.desc: Document the complete attack chain from local privilege escalation through lateral movement, and response; assess notification obligations given multi-system impact.
steps.outcome: Full report completed; notification obligations assessed if required.

steps.title: Map the lateral movement path
steps.desc: Trace every system the attacker accessed using the impersonated token's network identity.
steps.outcome: Full lateral movement path mapped.

steps.title: Reset the impersonated account's credentials
steps.desc: Rotate the password for the account whose token was impersonated, invalidating its network-level access.
steps.outcome: Impersonated account's credentials rotated.

steps.title: Investigate initial access and the local privilege escalation technique used
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained the initial foothold and the specific token impersonation technique used to enable lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Initial access and technique documented.

steps.title: Identify the impersonated account and its network privileges
steps.desc: Determine which account's token was impersonated and what network-level access/privileges it holds.
steps.outcome: Impersonated account and its network access scope identified.

steps.title: Review and reduce standing network-level privilege of the impersonated account
steps.desc: Assess whether the impersonated account held more network access than necessary and reduce standing privilege where possible.
steps.outcome: Account privilege reviewed and minimized where appropriate.

ITID-12746.def: An adversary with sufficient privilege creates a new Windows service configured to run as SYSTEM (or another privileged account), starts it, and captures the resulting privileged token from the spawned service process.
ITID-12746.purpose: Captures token impersonation achieved by creating a rogue Windows service configured to run as SYSTEM, then capturing that service's token upon execution.
scopeIncludes: Rogue service creation specifically as the vector to obtain a privileged token
scopeExcludes: Token theft via named-pipe impersonation or process injection with no service creation involved (ITID-12742, ITID-12743)
ITID-12746.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for SYSTEM-level outcomes.
ITID-12746.escalation: Escalate immediately; identify and remove the rogue service and isolate the host.
indicators: New service creation event immediately followed by privilege escalation on the same host
Service binary path pointing to an unusual/temporary location
vectors: Service-creation-based local privilege-escalation exploit chains
rootCauses: Excessive service-creation rights (SeCreateServicePrivilege/service-control-manager permissions) granted to non-admin accounts
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12746.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12746.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12746.notes: Differentiating axis: the specific technique is rogue service creation as the token-capture vector.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation via Rogue Service Creation
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack where the attacker created a new Windows service configured to run as SYSTEM (or another privileged account), then triggered it to obtain and use its elevated token.

steps.title: Confirm rogue service creation
steps.desc: Review Windows security logs (Event ID 4697/7045) for a newly created service, especially one configured with an unusual binary path or run-as account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed rogue service creation event with service name, binary path, and configured account identified.

steps.title: Stop and disable the rogue service
steps.desc: Stop the rogue service immediately and set it to disabled to prevent it from starting again (including on reboot).
steps.outcome: Rogue service stopped and disabled.

steps.title: Remove the rogue service and its binary
steps.desc: Delete the rogue service registration and the malicious binary/script it pointed to.
steps.guidance: Given the level of access implied, consider a full rebuild if additional persistence is suspected.
steps.outcome: Rogue service and binary removed.

steps.title: Verify no rogue services remain before return to service
steps.desc: Audit the endpoint's full service list against a known-good baseline to confirm no other rogue services exist.
steps.outcome: Service list confirmed clean.

steps.title: Document and reinforce service-creation privilege restrictions
steps.desc: Record the finding and evaluate whether service-creation rights are appropriately restricted fleet-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; privilege review completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Identify who created the service and how they obtained the necessary privilege
steps.desc: Determine the account/process that created the service and how it obtained the local privilege (e.g. SeCreateServicePrivilege or existing local admin rights) required to do so.
steps.outcome: Creating account and privilege source identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint where the rogue service was created.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild the endpoint if broader compromise is suspected
steps.desc: Reimage the endpoint if the investigation finds evidence of additional persistence or compromise beyond the single rogue service.
steps.outcome: Endpoint rebuilt if warranted, or confirmed limited to the single removed service.
steps.abort: If the rogue service was isolated with no other compromise indicators, in-place remediation may suffice.

steps.title: Determine what the rogue service did once started
steps.desc: Review what actions the rogue service performed while running with its elevated privilege.
steps.outcome: Actions documented.

steps.title: Investigate how the attacker obtained service-creation privilege
steps.desc: Determine the root cause — over-provisioned local admin rights, exploited vulnerability, or another escalation path — and remediate.
steps.outcome: Root cause identified and closed.

ITID-12747.def: An adversary exploits an account holding SeImpersonatePrivilege (commonly granted to IIS/SQL/service accounts by default) using a known local privilege-escalation exploit chain to obtain a SYSTEM-level token.
ITID-12747.purpose: Captures token impersonation exploiting SeImpersonatePrivilege specifically via known exploit chains (e.g. Potato-family exploits), the most common and well-documented root-cause pattern for this Type.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of SeImpersonatePrivilege via documented exploit techniques/tooling (e.g. Potato-family exploits) regardless of the specific downstream mechanism
scopeExcludes: Token impersonation via a privilege other than SeImpersonatePrivilege, or where SeImpersonatePrivilege exploitation is not the identified root cause
ITID-12747.severity: Critical — this is the most common and highest-yield real-world token-impersonation exploit pattern.
ITID-12747.escalation: Escalate immediately; audit all service accounts for unnecessary SeImpersonatePrivilege assignment as part of remediation.
indicators: EDR detection of a known Potato-family exploit tool signature
Service account observed obtaining SYSTEM privilege shortly after suspicious network/COM activity
vectors: Potato-family and related SeImpersonatePrivilege exploit tooling
rootCauses: Default SeImpersonatePrivilege grant to IIS/SQL/service accounts not reviewed or restricted
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12747.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12747.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12747.notes: Differentiating axis: root-cause framing (the specific privilege exploited) rather than the downstream mechanism — this is the leaf to use when SeImpersonatePrivilege abuse is the defining fact of the incident.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation Exploiting SeImpersonatePrivilege
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack that specifically exploited the SeImpersonatePrivilege (commonly assigned to service accounts) to escalate to SYSTEM, e.g. via a Potato-family exploitation technique.

steps.title: Confirm SeImpersonatePrivilege exploitation
steps.desc: Review EDR/process telemetry for known Potato-family or similar SeImpersonatePrivilege exploitation tool signatures and behavior patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation of SeImpersonatePrivilege with the specific technique identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint where the exploitation occurred.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild the endpoint given SYSTEM-level compromise
steps.desc: Reimage the endpoint, since this technique typically results in full SYSTEM privilege.
steps.outcome: Endpoint reimaged from a known-clean source.

steps.title: Verify the rebuilt endpoint and patched application are clean before return to service
steps.desc: Confirm the endpoint is clean and the vulnerability is patched before restoring the service to production.
steps.outcome: Endpoint and application confirmed clean and patched.

steps.title: Document the technique and audit other services for the same exposure
steps.desc: Record the finding and check whether other services in the environment share the same vulnerable-application-plus-SeImpersonatePrivilege exposure pattern.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; sweep completed or ticketed.

steps.title: Identify the service account that held SeImpersonatePrivilege
steps.desc: Determine which account/service context the attacker's process was running under prior to escalation — this privilege is typically granted by default to service accounts.
steps.outcome: Originating service account identified.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious process and any SYSTEM-level processes it spawned
steps.desc: Kill the exploiting process and any elevated processes it created.
steps.outcome: Malicious activity terminated.

steps.title: Patch or remediate the underlying application vulnerability that gave initial code execution
steps.desc: Address the root-cause vulnerability (e.g. vulnerable web application, deserialization flaw) that allowed the attacker to execute code under the service account in the first place.
steps.outcome: Underlying vulnerability patched or mitigated.

steps.title: Determine how the attacker gained code execution in that service context
steps.desc: Establish the initial access vector that allowed the attacker to execute code as the service account in the first place (e.g. a vulnerable web application running under that service identity).
steps.outcome: Initial access vector identified.

steps.title: Review and minimize SeImpersonatePrivilege assignment where feasible
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the affected service genuinely requires SeImpersonatePrivilege, and apply mitigations (e.g. running under a lower-privileged virtual/managed service account, or applying vendor-recommended Potato-family mitigations) where feasible.
steps.guidance: Removing this privilege entirely often breaks legitimate service functionality — apply mitigations rather than blanket removal unless confirmed safe.
steps.outcome: Mitigation applied or documented as not feasible with compensating controls noted.

ITID-12748.def: An incident where token impersonation was identified specifically through detection of anomalous parent-child process token lineage (e.g. a low-privilege process's descendant unexpectedly running with a higher-privilege token).
ITID-12748.purpose: Captures token impersonation first identified through anomalous process-token-lineage detection logic, representing the primary technical detection pathway for this technique.
scopeIncludes: Cases where the detection trigger itself was a process-token-lineage anomaly rule
scopeExcludes: Token-impersonation incidents detected through other means (e.g. a specific exploit-tool signature as the primary trigger) with no token-lineage anomaly involved
ITID-12748.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for SYSTEM-level outcomes.
ITID-12748.escalation: Escalate promptly upon detection; correlate with the source process for technique-specific evidence.
indicators: EDR alert specifically keyed on a child process token privilege level inconsistent with its parent process
vectors: Any token-impersonation technique that happens to trip the token-lineage anomaly detector
rootCauses: Detection logic tuned to the environment's expected process/token-lineage baseline
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12748.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12748.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12748.notes: Differentiating axis: classified by detection pathway (token-lineage anomaly) rather than by the specific impersonation mechanism used.

playbook.name: Response: Token Impersonation Detected via Anomalous Process Token Lineage
playbook.description: For a token impersonation attack where the primary detection signal was an anomalous process token lineage (a process operating with a token/integrity level inconsistent with its parent process chain) flagged by automated detection.

steps.title: Validate the detection finding against raw process lineage data
steps.desc: Pull the raw process creation/token telemetry to confirm the flagged process genuinely operates with a token inconsistent with its parent chain, ruling out a detection-rule false positive.
steps.guidance: Check for legitimate elevation patterns (e.g. UAC, a signed installer performing expected elevation) before treating as malicious.
steps.outcome: Confirmed genuine anomaly, or closed as tuning/false-positive.
steps.abort: If explained by legitimate elevation behavior, close as false positive and tune the detection rule.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint where the anomaly was detected.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Remediate per the identified specific technique
steps.desc: Once the specific technique is confirmed, follow the corresponding specific playbook for full eradication.
steps.outcome: Underlying technique remediated per the specific playbook.

steps.title: Confirm no further lineage anomalies for the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Monitor the endpoint for a defined window to confirm no recurrence.
steps.outcome: No further anomalous lineage activity observed.

steps.title: Document the detection success and reinforce process-lineage monitoring
steps.desc: Record what worked in catching this via lineage-anomaly detection and consider expanding similar detection coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; detection coverage reviewed.

steps.title: Determine the specific impersonation technique behind the lineage anomaly
steps.desc: Investigate the process and its context to determine which specific technique (named pipe, injection, rogue service, SeImpersonatePrivilege) produced the anomalous lineage.
steps.outcome: Specific technique identified.

steps.title: Terminate the flagged process
steps.desc: Kill the process operating with the anomalous token.
steps.outcome: Malicious activity terminated.

steps.title: Tune and preserve the detection rule that caught this event
steps.desc: Review the process-lineage detection logic and confirm it remains sensitive to this pattern for future detections.
steps.outcome: Detection rule confirmed effective and preserved.

steps.title: Determine what actions were taken with the inconsistent token
steps.desc: Review activity performed by the process while operating with the anomalous privilege level.
steps.outcome: Actions documented.

ITID-12749.def: A confirmed instance of token impersonation (any mechanism) in which the adversary is verified to have successfully escalated privilege and acted with the impersonated token's authority.
ITID-12749.purpose: Escalation leaf for confirmed token impersonation attacks where the adversary is verified to have achieved privilege escalation using the impersonated token.
scopeIncludes: Any sibling token-impersonation leaf in this Type where confirmed privilege escalation is verified
scopeExcludes: Token impersonation attempts with no confirmed successful privilege escalation (respective attempt-stage sibling leaves)
ITID-12749.severity: Critical — confirmed privilege escalation, markedly higher than the attempt-stage siblings.
ITID-12749.escalation: Immediate incident response: isolate the host, terminate the impersonating process, and audit all actions taken under the impersonated token.
indicators: Confirmed unauthorized privileged actions taken under an impersonated token's identity
vectors: Any token-impersonation vector in this Type that reached confirmed privilege escalation
rootCauses: Excessive impersonation-related privilege assignment combined with insufficient EDR coverage enabling successful escalation
controls: Least-privilege assignment of SeImpersonatePrivilege/SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege to only the accounts/services that require it
EDR behavioral detection for token-duplication and impersonation API call chains
Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules limiting credential-theft/token-abuse tooling
Service-account hardening (no interactive logon, restricted token scope)
ITID-12749.detection: Well-instrumented via EDR: token-manipulation API calls (DuplicateToken/ImpersonateLoggedOnUser-style sequences), anomalous parent-child process token lineage (a low-privilege process spawning a SYSTEM-token child), and named-pipe creation immediately followed by privilege escalation are all reliable detection points on modern endpoint telemetry.
ITID-12749.response: Isolate the affected host immediately, terminate the impersonating process, and audit for any actions taken under the impersonated token's identity before remediation.
metrics: Count of token-impersonation incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with EDR token-manipulation detection enabled
Mean time to isolate a host after a token-impersonation alert
ITID-12749.notes: This is the confirmed-outcome escalation of the token-impersonation leaves above it.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Token Impersonation with Confirmed Privilege Escalation
playbook.description: For a confirmed case where a token impersonation attack (any mechanism) resulted in demonstrated privilege escalation and the attacker used the elevated access.

steps.title: Confirm and catalogue every action taken with the escalated privilege
steps.desc: Build a complete, timestamped list of every action the attacker performed after achieving privilege escalation.
steps.guidance: Treat this as an active intrusion investigation.
steps.outcome: Complete action log documented.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint(s) immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate the originating endpoint and any system reached via subsequent lateral movement.
steps.outcome: All affected systems isolated.

steps.title: Rebuild all affected endpoints from known-clean images
steps.desc: Reimage every endpoint confirmed compromised given the depth of access privilege escalation typically provides.
steps.outcome: All affected endpoints rebuilt.

steps.title: Verify all affected systems are clean before restoring normal access
steps.desc: Confirm every affected system is clean before closing.
steps.outcome: All affected systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Full incident report with impact and notification assessment
steps.desc: Document the complete attack chain, impact, and response; assess breach notification obligations given confirmed privilege escalation and unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Full report completed; notification obligations assessed and actioned if required.

steps.title: Determine the specific token impersonation mechanism used
steps.desc: Establish the specific vector (named pipe, process injection, rogue service, SeImpersonatePrivilege exploitation) to identify the matching specific playbook.
steps.outcome: Mechanism identified.

steps.title: Terminate all attacker processes and sessions
steps.desc: Kill every process and session tied to the attacker's escalated access.
steps.outcome: Attacker no longer has active access.

steps.title: Remediate the specific mechanism and initial access vector
steps.desc: Follow the applicable specific playbook to close the underlying escalation technique, and remediate the initial access vector that gave the attacker their starting foothold.
steps.outcome: Underlying mechanism and initial access both remediated.

steps.title: Assess system impact and lateral movement
steps.desc: Determine what was accessed/modified on the local system and whether the attacker pivoted to other systems.
steps.outcome: Full impact scope established.

steps.title: Reset credentials for any account confirmed exposed via the escalated access
steps.desc: Rotate passwords for any account whose credentials may have been accessible via the SYSTEM/elevated-level access gained.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials rotated.

ITID-12811.def: An incident involving an attempt to determine which usernames/accounts exist in a system, not yet matched to a more specific enumeration technique.
ITID-12811.purpose: Catch-all for an account enumeration attempt that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific enumeration technique is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Account Enumeration

Network/service/asset enumeration in the reconnaissance domain (see ITID-42324 Unclassified / General Service Enumeration and siblings) — this branch is scoped strictly to enumeration of authentication-system identities (usernames/accounts) via login-adjacent flows, not infrastructure or service discovery
ITID-12811.escalation: Escalate to application security once the specific technique is confirmed; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Authentication system alert of unclear specific enumeration technique
vectors: Enumeration attempt of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Generic account-response messaging
ITID-12811.detection: Same authentication-system telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12811.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12811.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Scope is deliberately kept distinct from the reconnaissance-domain's network/service enumeration leaves (e.g. ITID-42324), which cover infrastructure discovery rather than authentication-identity enumeration.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Account Enumeration Attempt
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected account-enumeration attempt where the specific technique has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Confirm enumeration signal in logs
steps.desc: Review web/application access logs and WAF/SIEM alerts for the source IP(s) and request pattern that triggered the alert.
steps.guidance: Look for a high ratio of failed/varied username attempts against login, registration, or password-reset endpoints from a small number of sources.
steps.outcome: Confirmed log evidence of systematic account-probing behaviour, or determination that the alert is benign (e.g. a single mistyped login).
steps.abort: If the volume is consistent with normal user error and there is no repeated pattern, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Rate-limit or block the source
steps.desc: Apply IP/ASN-based rate limiting or a temporary block at the WAF/edge for the offending source(s).
steps.guidance: Prefer rate-limiting over a hard block if the source is a shared NAT/proxy range to avoid collateral impact on legitimate users.
steps.outcome: Enumeration traffic from the source is throttled or blocked.

steps.title: Harden the enumerable surface
steps.desc: File a remediation ticket to make login/registration/reset responses indistinguishable for valid vs invalid identities (uniform messages, timing, status codes).
steps.guidance: This is a design fix, not something the SOC can remediate directly — route to the application owner.
steps.outcome: Ticket opened with the application team to close the enumeration vector.

steps.title: Monitor for follow-on attacks
steps.desc: Add a watchlist/alert for credential-stuffing or password-spraying activity against the identities harvested in this incident.
steps.guidance: Enumeration is almost always a precursor step, not the end goal.
steps.outcome: Detection rule in place for follow-on activity against the exposed identity list.

steps.title: Document findings and remediation status
steps.desc: Record the technique, scope, and status of the application-hardening ticket in the case file.
steps.outcome: Case closed with a clear record and open remediation tracked to completion.

steps.title: Characterise the technique used
steps.desc: Determine which enumeration vector was used (error-message differential, timing, endpoint response codes, etc.) so the incident can be reclassified to the correct specific ITID if applicable.
steps.guidance: Compare response bodies, status codes, and timing for valid vs invalid usernames tested by the source.
steps.outcome: Technique identified and incident tagged accordingly.

steps.title: Alert owners of high-value probed accounts
steps.desc: Notify the owners of any privileged or high-value accounts found in the probed list to increase their vigilance.
steps.outcome: Affected users aware and advised to watch for follow-on phishing or credential-stuffing attempts.

steps.title: Determine scope of targeted usernames
steps.desc: Extract the list of usernames/emails probed to see whether they correlate to a known list (e.g. leaked breach data, employee directory, executives).
steps.guidance: A list matching internal naming conventions suggests reconnaissance ahead of a targeted attack, not random scanning.
steps.outcome: List of probed identities and an assessment of targeting intent.

ITID-12812.def: Enumeration of valid usernames/accounts by exploiting a login form that returns different error messages for "account not found" versus "incorrect password", allowing an attacker to distinguish valid from invalid accounts without ever guessing a password.
ITID-12812.purpose: Captures username enumeration achieved via differences in the login form's error message.
scopeIncludes: Login form returning "user not found" vs. "incorrect password" as distinct messages
Automated testing/scanning of a login endpoint to catalog error-message differences
scopeExcludes: Enumeration via response timing rather than message content (see ITID-12813)
Enumeration via the password reset flow specifically (see ITID-12814)
ITID-12812.severity: Low-Medium — a precursor to credential stuffing/targeted attacks rather than a compromise itself.
ITID-12812.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if paired with subsequent targeted login attempts.
ITID-12812.escalation: Escalate to application engineering to standardize error messaging; escalate to security if paired with a targeted follow-on attack.
indicators: WAF/application log showing scripted requests testing many usernames against the login endpoint
Distinct, cataloged error-message variants returned across test usernames
vectors: Automated scripted testing of a username list against the login form to catalog message differences
rootCauses: Login form not designed with a generic, identical error message for both invalid-username and invalid-password cases
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Generic, identical authentication error messaging regardless of failure reason
Rate limiting on login endpoint requests
ITID-12812.detection: WAF/application log analysis for scripted, sequential username-testing patterns provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12812.response: Standardize the error message and monitor for follow-on targeted login attempts against confirmed valid usernames.
metrics: Count of enumeration-pattern requests detected per quarter
ITID-12812.notes: Scoped specifically to the login-form error-message vector, distinct from timing-based (ITID-12813) and password-reset-flow (ITID-12814) enumeration.

playbook.name: Response: Login Error Message Differential Enumeration
playbook.description: For enumeration where an attacker distinguishes valid from invalid accounts by differences in login error messages.

steps.title: Confirm the message differential exists
steps.desc: Reproduce the login flow with a known-valid and a known-invalid username to confirm the application actually returns different error text/codes.
steps.guidance: Check both the visible UI message and the underlying HTTP status/response body — differentials are sometimes only in the API layer.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence (or absence) of a distinguishable error differential.
steps.abort: If no differential can be reproduced, the alert may be based on stale behaviour — close as unconfirmed and note the finding.

steps.title: Rate-limit the login endpoint
steps.desc: Apply or tighten rate limiting on the login endpoint for the offending source(s).
steps.outcome: Enumeration traffic throttled.

steps.title: Unify the error response
steps.desc: File a ticket for the application team to return an identical generic message and status code for both valid and invalid usernames.
steps.guidance: Also confirm response timing is normalised — a fixed message with a timing gap still leaks information (see timing-based enumeration).
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened describing the exact differential to fix.

steps.title: Verify fix once deployed
steps.desc: Re-test the login flow after the application fix ships to confirm the differential is gone.
steps.outcome: Valid and invalid usernames now return indistinguishable responses.

steps.title: Document the vulnerability and fix timeline
steps.desc: Record the specific differential found and how long remediation took, for use in future secure-coding guidance.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and referenced in secure development guidelines.

steps.title: Correlate probing traffic to the flow
steps.desc: Search access logs for repeated login attempts against many distinct usernames from the same source in a short window.
steps.outcome: List of source IPs and volume of usernames tested.

ITID-12813.def: Enumeration of valid usernames/accounts by measuring statistically significant differences in server response latency between requests for valid vs. invalid accounts (e.g. because a valid-account lookup triggers an extra password-hash comparison).
ITID-12813.purpose: Captures username enumeration achieved by measuring differences in server response time.
scopeIncludes: Statistical timing analysis of login/authentication endpoint responses across many requests
Automated tooling specifically designed to exploit timing side-channels in an authentication flow
scopeExcludes: Enumeration via visible error-message differences (see ITID-12812)
Enumeration via API response code/structure rather than timing (see ITID-12816)
ITID-12813.escalation: Escalate to application engineering to implement constant-time authentication comparison logic.
indicators: High-volume, statistically patterned requests against the authentication endpoint consistent with timing-analysis tooling
Security testing/pentest finding confirming a timing side-channel
vectors: Automated timing-attack tooling submitting repeated requests per candidate username to build a statistical distribution
rootCauses: Authentication logic not implemented with constant-time comparison, causing measurable latency difference based on account existence
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Constant-time authentication comparison logic
Rate limiting/anomaly detection on high-volume repeated requests per source
ITID-12813.detection: Requires statistical/behavioral analysis of request volume and timing patterns in WAF/application logs — a real but more subtle technical signal than message-based enumeration.
ITID-12813.response: Remediate the timing side-channel in authentication logic and monitor for the high-volume request pattern characteristic of this technique.
metrics: Count of high-volume timing-pattern authentication requests detected per quarter
ITID-12813.notes: Scoped specifically to the timing side-channel vector, distinct from message-based (ITID-12812) and structural (ITID-12816) enumeration.

playbook.name: Response: Response Timing-Based Enumeration
playbook.description: For enumeration where an attacker infers account validity from response-time differences (e.g. password hashing only occurring for valid usernames).

steps.title: Confirm the timing differential
steps.desc: Measure response latency for known-valid vs known-invalid usernames across several samples.
steps.guidance: Timing attacks require statistical confirmation — a single measurement is not sufficient; take a batch of samples for each case.
steps.outcome: Confirmed measurable and consistent timing gap, or ruled out.
steps.abort: If timing is within normal network jitter with no consistent gap, close as unconfirmed.

steps.title: Rate-limit and add response-time jitter
steps.desc: Apply rate limiting at the edge and, if supported, enable a WAF/gateway feature to add randomised delay to auth responses as a stopgap.
steps.guidance: Jitter is a temporary mitigation, not a permanent fix.
steps.outcome: Enumeration throughput reduced and timing signal degraded.

steps.title: Fix the underlying timing asymmetry
steps.desc: File a ticket for the application team to perform constant-time authentication checks (e.g. always hash/compare even for non-existent usernames).
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened with the specific code path identified.

steps.title: Re-measure after fix
steps.desc: Re-run timing measurements after the fix ships to confirm the gap is closed.
steps.outcome: No statistically significant timing difference remains.

steps.title: Document and share as a secure-coding example
steps.desc: Record the finding as a reference example for constant-time comparison requirements in development standards.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; development guidance updated.

steps.title: Identify the source and volume of probing
steps.desc: Search logs for a high volume of sequential/scripted login attempts consistent with timing measurement (often single-threaded, evenly spaced requests).
steps.outcome: Source IP(s) and request pattern identified.

ITID-12814.def: Enumeration of valid usernames/accounts by exploiting a password reset flow that reveals, through message, timing, or behavioral difference, whether a submitted identifier corresponds to an existing account.
ITID-12814.purpose: Captures username enumeration achieved through the password reset/forgot-password flow specifically.
scopeIncludes: "If an account exists, a reset email has been sent" message inconsistently applied (revealing account existence through other cues)
Password reset flow behaving differently (redirect, delay, follow-up field) for existing vs. non-existing accounts
scopeExcludes: Enumeration via the standard login form's error messaging (see ITID-12812)
Enumeration via the account registration flow (see ITID-12815)
ITID-12814.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if paired with a subsequent targeted attack on confirmed accounts.
ITID-12814.escalation: Escalate to application engineering to standardize the reset flow's response regardless of account existence.
indicators: Automated scripted requests submitted to the password reset endpoint across many candidate identifiers
Confirmed inconsistency in reset-flow response/behavior across test accounts during security testing
vectors: Automated scripted testing of the password reset endpoint to catalog account-existence signals
rootCauses: Password reset flow not designed to return an identical response regardless of whether the submitted identifier matches an account
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Standardized, identical password-reset response regardless of account existence
Rate limiting on password reset endpoint requests
ITID-12814.detection: WAF/application log analysis for scripted, sequential requests against the reset endpoint provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12814.response: Standardize the reset flow response and monitor for follow-on targeted attacks against confirmed accounts.
metrics: Count of enumeration-pattern requests against the reset endpoint per quarter
ITID-12814.notes: Scoped specifically to the password reset flow as the enumeration surface, distinct from the login form (ITID-12812) and registration flow (ITID-12815).

playbook.name: Response: Password Reset Flow Enumeration
playbook.description: For enumeration via the password-reset ('forgot password') flow, where the response reveals whether a submitted identity has an account.

steps.title: Confirm the reset flow leaks account existence
steps.desc: Submit the reset form with a known-valid and known-invalid identity and compare the response message, page behaviour, and email/SMS side effects.
steps.guidance: Check for differences like 'email sent' vs 'no account found', or a visible delay only on valid accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leak vector identified, or ruled out.

steps.title: Rate-limit the reset endpoint
steps.desc: Apply or tighten rate limiting on the password-reset endpoint.
steps.outcome: Reset-flow probing throttled.

steps.title: Fix the reset flow to a uniform response
steps.desc: File a ticket for the application team to return an identical message ('if an account exists, an email has been sent') regardless of account existence, with consistent timing.
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened.

steps.title: Verify fix once deployed
steps.desc: Re-test the reset flow after the fix to confirm uniform responses.
steps.outcome: No distinguishable difference between valid and invalid identity submissions.

steps.title: Document finding and fix timeline
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability and remediation for the case file and secure-coding reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Identify scope of probed identities
steps.desc: Review reset-flow logs for the volume and list of identities submitted from the source(s) in question.
steps.outcome: List of probed identities and source IPs.

steps.title: Alert owners of exposed high-value accounts
steps.desc: Notify owners of any privileged accounts confirmed present in the probed list.
steps.outcome: Affected users aware and advised to watch for follow-on attacks.

ITID-12815.def: Enumeration of already-registered accounts by exploiting a sign-up flow that reveals whether a submitted email/username is already in use (e.g. "this email is already registered" messaging).
ITID-12815.purpose: Captures username/email enumeration achieved through the account registration/sign-up flow.
scopeIncludes: Registration flow returning an explicit "account already exists" message
Registration flow behaving differently in timing or subsequent-step routing for already-registered identifiers
scopeExcludes: Enumeration via the password reset flow (see ITID-12814)
Enumeration via the login form (see ITID-12812)
ITID-12815.escalation: Escalate to application engineering to redesign the registration flow's account-existence handling.
indicators: Automated scripted requests submitted to the registration endpoint across many candidate email addresses
Security testing finding confirming account-existence disclosure via registration response
vectors: Automated scripted testing of the sign-up endpoint to catalog which email addresses are already registered
rootCauses: Registration flow designed with direct user-facing feedback on account-existence for usability, without considering the enumeration trade-off
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Registration flow redesigned to defer account-existence disclosure (e.g. always "check your email" messaging with the actual notification differing server-side)
Rate limiting on registration endpoint requests
ITID-12815.detection: WAF/application log analysis for scripted, sequential requests against the registration endpoint provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12815.response: Redesign the registration flow's messaging and monitor for follow-on targeted use of confirmed valid accounts.
metrics: Count of enumeration-pattern requests against the registration endpoint per quarter
ITID-12815.notes: Scoped specifically to the sign-up flow as the enumeration surface, distinct from login (ITID-12812) and password reset (ITID-12814) flows.

playbook.name: Response: Account Registration Flow Enumeration
playbook.description: For enumeration via the account-registration ('sign up') flow, where an 'email already registered' style response reveals existing accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the registration flow leaks account existence
steps.desc: Attempt registration with a known-existing and a known-non-existing identity and compare the response.
steps.guidance: Look for messages like 'account already exists' that directly confirm an identity is registered.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leak vector identified, or ruled out.

steps.title: Rate-limit the registration endpoint
steps.desc: Apply or tighten rate limiting and add CAPTCHA/bot-detection to the registration endpoint.
steps.outcome: Registration-flow probing throttled.

steps.title: Fix the registration flow response
steps.desc: File a ticket for the application team to use an out-of-band confirmation model (always show 'check your email to complete registration') instead of an immediate existence-revealing response.
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened.

steps.title: Verify fix once deployed
steps.desc: Re-test the registration flow after the fix ships.
steps.outcome: No distinguishable difference for existing vs non-existing identities.

steps.title: Document finding
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability and remediation status.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Identify scope of probed identities
steps.desc: Review registration-flow logs for the identities and volume submitted by the source(s).
steps.outcome: List of probed identities and source IPs.

ITID-12816.def: Enumeration of valid accounts by exploiting an API endpoint (rather than a rendered web form) that returns a different HTTP status code, response schema, or field set depending on whether the queried identifier corresponds to an existing account.
ITID-12816.purpose: Captures username enumeration achieved through differences in an API's HTTP status code or response structure.
scopeIncludes: API returning HTTP 404 for a non-existent user vs. 401/403 for an existing one on the same endpoint
API response including additional fields (e.g. account creation date) only when the account exists
scopeExcludes: Enumeration via a rendered login form's visible error message (see ITID-12812)
Enumeration via a third-party SSO provider's own response behavior (see ITID-12818)
ITID-12816.escalation: Escalate to API/application engineering to standardize response status codes and schemas regardless of account existence.
indicators: Automated scripted API requests testing many identifiers and cataloging status-code/schema differences
API security testing finding confirming structural enumeration
vectors: Automated scripted testing of an API endpoint to build a map of account existence via status code or schema variance
rootCauses: API designed without consideration for information disclosure via differential status codes/response structure
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Standardized API response status codes/schema regardless of account existence
API rate limiting and anomaly detection
ITID-12816.detection: API gateway/WAF logging of status-code distribution per source and endpoint provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12816.response: Standardize the API's response behavior and monitor for follow-on targeted use of confirmed accounts.
metrics: Count of API enumeration-pattern requests detected per quarter
ITID-12816.notes: Scoped specifically to API-layer status code/schema variance, distinct from rendered-form error messaging (ITID-12812) and third-party SSO response behavior (ITID-12818).

playbook.name: Response: API Response Code/Structure Enumeration
playbook.description: For enumeration via a backend API that returns different HTTP status codes or JSON response structures for valid vs invalid identities.

steps.title: Confirm the API differential
steps.desc: Call the identified API endpoint(s) with valid and invalid identities and compare status codes, response shape, and field presence.
steps.guidance: Check for differences such as a 200 vs 404, or a present-vs-absent field like 'userId' in the payload.
steps.outcome: Confirmed differential vector identified.

steps.title: Rate-limit and restrict the API endpoint
steps.desc: Apply rate limiting, and if the endpoint should not be public, restrict access (auth requirement, network ACL).
steps.outcome: Enumeration traffic blocked or throttled.

steps.title: Fix the API response structure
steps.desc: File a ticket for the API owner to standardise responses so no field/status/shape differs based on identity existence.
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened with the exact endpoint and differential documented.

steps.title: Verify fix once deployed
steps.desc: Re-test the API after remediation to confirm uniform responses.
steps.outcome: No distinguishable response differential remains.

steps.title: Document finding and API inventory gap
steps.desc: Record the finding, and if the endpoint was undocumented/unmanaged, flag a gap in the API inventory process.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; API inventory updated if needed.

steps.title: Identify scope of probing and exposed API
steps.desc: Review API gateway logs for the source(s), endpoint, and volume of enumeration requests.
steps.guidance: Pay attention to whether this is a public-facing API vs an internal/mobile-only endpoint that was not meant to be externally reachable.
steps.outcome: Source IPs, endpoint, and scope of exposure documented.

ITID-12817.def: An enumeration campaign characterized primarily by its scale and automation (bulk/scripted requests against an authentication-adjacent endpoint), where the volume and automated tooling itself is the notable characteristic, potentially combining multiple techniques.
ITID-12817.purpose: Captures the operational/volume dimension of enumeration — large-scale, scripted, automated requests — regardless of which specific technical vector is exploited.
scopeIncludes: High-volume automated enumeration campaign observed spanning multiple techniques (error message, timing, API structure) in combination
Enumeration traffic sourced from a known scanning/enumeration tool or botnet infrastructure
scopeExcludes: A single, low-volume enumeration technique clearly attributable to one of the specific-vector siblings (ITID-12812 through ITID-12816, ITID-12818)
ITID-12817.severity: Medium — scale increases both the likelihood of successful account discovery and downstream targeted attack risk.
ITID-12817.escalation: Escalate to security operations for source IP/infrastructure blocking and to application engineering if the campaign reveals a previously unaddressed enumeration vector.
indicators: Sustained high-volume request pattern against authentication-adjacent endpoints from one or more sources
Traffic signature matching known enumeration/credential-testing tooling (e.g. specific user-agent or request-pattern fingerprints)
vectors: Botnet or distributed scripted infrastructure conducting large-scale enumeration ahead of a credential-stuffing campaign
rootCauses: Insufficient rate limiting/bot-management controls on authentication-adjacent endpoints
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Bot-management/WAF rate limiting on authentication-adjacent endpoints
IP reputation-based blocking for known enumeration/scanning infrastructure
ITID-12817.detection: Bot-management and WAF volumetric/behavioral analytics provide a strong, concrete technical signal for this scale-driven pattern.
ITID-12817.response: Block the source infrastructure and monitor for a follow-on targeted or credential-stuffing campaign against discovered accounts.
metrics: Volume of automated enumeration requests blocked per quarter
ITID-12817.notes: Differentiator is scale/automation as the defining characteristic, cutting across the specific-vector siblings rather than duplicating them.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk/Automated Enumeration via Scripted Requests
playbook.description: For large-scale, scripted/automated enumeration sweeping many identities against one or more endpoints, identified primarily by volume and request automation signatures.

steps.title: Confirm automation signatures
steps.desc: Review request headers, user-agent, TLS fingerprint, and request cadence for indicators of scripted/tooled traffic (e.g. missing browser headers, uniform timing, known tool user-agents).
steps.outcome: Confirmed automated tooling behind the traffic.

steps.title: Block the source infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the source IP(s)/ASN or enable bot-mitigation/CAPTCHA challenge for the affected endpoints.
steps.guidance: If distributed across many IPs, use bot-management/fingerprinting rather than simple IP blocks.
steps.outcome: Automated traffic blocked or challenged.

steps.title: Deploy sustained anti-automation controls
steps.desc: File a ticket to add persistent bot-detection/CAPTCHA and stricter rate limiting to the swept endpoint(s), rather than a one-off block.
steps.outcome: Durable anti-automation control in place.

steps.title: Monitor for renewed sweeps
steps.desc: Watch for the same tooling signature or infrastructure returning under a different source range.
steps.outcome: Detection in place for recurrence.

steps.title: Document campaign and control gaps
steps.desc: Record scope, tooling signature, and the anti-automation control deployed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine full scope and target list
steps.desc: Extract the complete list of identities probed and the endpoint(s) targeted across the campaign duration.
steps.guidance: Check whether the list matches a known breach combolist or internal naming convention to assess intent.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the sweep documented.

steps.title: Notify owners of high-value probed accounts
steps.desc: Alert owners of privileged accounts found in the scope list.
steps.outcome: Affected users aware.

ITID-12818.def: Enumeration of valid accounts by exploiting differential behavior in a third-party identity provider or SSO flow (e.g. "redirecting to your organization's login" only for known domains, or a federated provider revealing account existence during the handoff).
ITID-12818.purpose: Captures username enumeration achieved by observing a third-party SSO or federated login provider's own response behavior.
scopeIncludes: SSO "discover my organization" flow revealing whether an email domain/account is provisioned
Federated login handoff exposing account-existence signals distinct from the relying application's own logic
scopeExcludes: Enumeration entirely within the organization's own login form/API (see ITID-12812, ITID-12816)
ITID-12818.escalation: Escalate to identity engineering to review SSO/federation flow behavior with the identity provider vendor.
indicators: Automated scripted requests against the SSO discovery/federation endpoint testing many identifiers
Security testing finding confirming enumeration via the federation handoff
vectors: Automated scripted testing of an SSO "enter your email" discovery step to catalog which domains/accounts are provisioned
rootCauses: SSO/federation flow implemented by the identity provider or relying application without considering enumeration risk in the discovery step
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: SSO discovery flow reviewed and hardened against differential response behavior
Rate limiting on the SSO discovery endpoint
ITID-12818.detection: Identity provider and application-side logs correlated for the SSO discovery step provide a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12818.response: Work with the identity provider/vendor to harden the discovery flow; monitor for follow-on targeted attacks.
metrics: Count of SSO discovery enumeration-pattern requests detected per quarter
ITID-12818.notes: Scoped specifically to the third-party/federated identity provider surface, distinct from the organization's own first-party login/API surfaces covered by sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Enumeration via Third-Party Login/SSO Provider Response
playbook.description: For enumeration where an attacker uses a federated login or 'Sign in with X' flow's response behaviour to determine whether an identity has a linked account.

steps.title: Confirm the SSO/federated flow differential
steps.desc: Test the 'Sign in with' flow with a linked and an unlinked identity and compare the redirect behaviour, error message, or account-linking prompt.
steps.guidance: This often occurs at the account-linking step rather than the identity provider itself — check what your own application does after the IdP returns control.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leak vector identified.

steps.title: Rate-limit the affected flow
steps.desc: Apply rate limiting to the SSO callback/account-linking endpoint.
steps.outcome: Probing throttled.

steps.title: Fix the differential or escalate to vendor
steps.desc: File an internal remediation ticket, or open a support case with the identity provider, depending on where the leak originates.
steps.outcome: Ticket opened with the responsible party.

steps.title: Verify fix once deployed
steps.desc: Re-test the flow after remediation.
steps.outcome: No distinguishable differential remains.

steps.title: Document finding
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability, responsible party, and resolution.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the leak is in your app or the IdP
steps.desc: Establish whether the differential originates in your application's account-linking logic or in the third-party identity provider's own response.
steps.guidance: If it's the IdP's issue, remediation may require a vendor ticket rather than an internal code fix.
steps.outcome: Responsible party identified.

ITID-12819.def: Confirmed correlation between a prior account enumeration event and a subsequent targeted attack (credential stuffing, password spraying, phishing) specifically directed at the accounts confirmed to exist through that enumeration.
ITID-12819.purpose: Captures the case where enumeration has been confirmed to directly feed a subsequent, targeted attack against the discovered accounts.
scopeIncludes: Targeted login attempts observed against the specific set of usernames previously confirmed via enumeration
Phishing campaign targeting the specific email addresses confirmed to exist via a prior enumeration event
scopeExcludes: Enumeration activity with no confirmed downstream targeted attack (tracked under the relevant technique-specific sibling)
ITID-12819.severity: High — confirms the enumeration has translated into active exploitation risk.
ITID-12819.escalation: Immediate escalation to incident response; treat the confirmed-existing accounts as an active, elevated-risk target set requiring proactive protection (forced MFA, monitoring).
indicators: Login attempts or phishing targeting correlated by timestamp and target list to a prior enumeration event
Threat intelligence or internal correlation confirming the same source infrastructure conducted both the enumeration and the follow-on attack
vectors: Enumeration used to build a validated target list, followed by credential stuffing or spray attacks against only the confirmed-valid accounts
Enumeration used to build a validated target list for a subsequent spear-phishing campaign
rootCauses: Underlying enumeration vector not remediated in time to prevent its use in the follow-on attack (root-caused under the originating enumeration sibling ITID)
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Proactive forced MFA/step-up authentication for accounts confirmed exposed via enumeration
Correlation rule linking enumeration and subsequent authentication-attack telemetry
ITID-12819.detection: SIEM correlation linking enumeration-phase and attack-phase telemetry by target-list overlap and timing provides a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12819.response: Proactively protect the confirmed target-account set (forced MFA, password reset, heightened monitoring) and treat the correlated attack as a single elevated-priority incident.
metrics: Count of enumeration-to-attack correlations confirmed per quarter
ITID-12819.notes: This leaf documents the confirmed-correlation/downstream-impact case specifically; the enumeration technique itself is root-caused under its specific sibling ITID.

playbook.name: Response: Enumeration Feeding a Downstream Targeted Attack
playbook.description: For confirmed enumeration where evidence shows the harvested identity list was subsequently used to launch a targeted attack (phishing, credential stuffing, spraying) against the same population.

steps.title: Correlate enumeration output to the downstream attack
steps.desc: Compare the list of identities probed during enumeration against the target list of the follow-on attack (phishing send list, credential-stuffing usernames, etc.).
steps.guidance: Look for timing proximity and overlapping source infrastructure between the two campaigns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed link between enumeration and the downstream attack, with full scope of both.

steps.title: Contain the downstream attack per its own type
steps.desc: Trigger the appropriate response (credential stuffing, phishing, or spraying playbook) for the follow-on attack against the affected accounts.
steps.guidance: This incident should be cross-referenced to the downstream attack's own case; do not duplicate containment steps here.
steps.outcome: Downstream attack contained under its own playbook.

steps.title: Close the enumeration vector
steps.desc: File a remediation ticket to close the specific enumeration vector that supplied the target list.
steps.outcome: Ticket opened with the application team.

steps.title: Monitor the affected population
steps.desc: Add elevated monitoring for the full list of enumerated identities for renewed attack activity.
steps.outcome: Watchlist in place.

steps.title: Document the full attack chain
steps.desc: Record the enumeration-to-attack chain as a case study, including how the correlation was made, for use in detection-rule tuning.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; detection rule created to correlate enumeration spikes with follow-on attack alerts.

steps.title: Establish full incident scope
steps.desc: Determine total accounts targeted, any confirmed compromises from the downstream attack, and the timeline from enumeration to attack.
steps.outcome: Complete timeline and impact assessment.

steps.title: Block the shared enumeration/attack infrastructure
steps.desc: Block source IPs/infrastructure common to both the enumeration and downstream phases.
steps.outcome: Shared attacker infrastructure blocked.

ITID-12821.def: An incident involving exploitation of an account lockout mechanism, not yet matched to a more specific exploitation pattern.
ITID-12821.purpose: Catch-all for account lockout exploitation that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific lockout exploitation pattern is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Account Lockout Exploitation
ITID-12821.escalation: Escalate to application security once the specific pattern is confirmed; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Authentication system alert of unclear specific lockout-related pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector involving account lockout
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Account lockout policy monitoring
ITID-12821.detection: Same authentication-system telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12821.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12821.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Account Lockout Exploitation
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected account-lockout exploitation incident where the specific technique has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Confirm abnormal lockout activity
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for accounts that have locked out, the source(s) of the failed attempts, and the rate of lockouts across the environment.
steps.guidance: Compare against baseline lockout volume — a spike in a short window from few sources is the key signal.
steps.outcome: Confirmed abnormal lockout pattern, or ruled out as ordinary user error.
steps.abort: If lockouts are isolated, low-volume, and consistent with normal forgotten-password behaviour, close as false positive.

steps.title: Block or throttle the source
steps.desc: Rate-limit or block the source IP(s)/infrastructure generating the failed login attempts.
steps.outcome: Further lockout-inducing traffic stopped.

steps.title: Review lockout policy for gaps
steps.desc: Assess whether the lockout threshold/policy itself needs adjustment to reduce future exploitability while balancing usability.
steps.outcome: Policy reviewed and adjusted or confirmed adequate.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
