steps.desc: Watch the affected accounts and source infrastructure for renewed activity.
steps.outcome: No further abnormal lockout activity observed.

steps.title: Document findings and policy changes
steps.desc: Record the technique, impact, and any lockout-policy changes made.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Characterise the exploitation technique
steps.desc: Determine whether this is a DoS-style mass lockout, threshold probing, targeted privileged-account lockout, or a lockout-triggered social-engineering angle, and reclassify if a more specific ITID applies.
steps.outcome: Technique identified and incident tagged accordingly.

steps.title: Unlock affected legitimate users
steps.desc: Identify and unlock accounts belonging to legitimate users impacted by the incident, verifying identity through an out-of-band channel before unlocking.
steps.guidance: Never unlock on the basis of an inbound call alone — verify against known contact details or a second factor.
steps.outcome: Legitimate users restored to service; no accounts unlocked without identity verification.

ITID-12822.def: An attacker intentionally submitting repeated failed login attempts against a target account specifically to trigger the lockout policy and deny the legitimate user access, rather than as a byproduct of a credential-guessing attempt.
ITID-12822.purpose: Captures deliberate triggering of account lockouts as a denial-of-service technique against one or more users.
scopeIncludes: Repeated failed logins against a single known-valid username with no evidence of password-guessing variety, consistent with a deliberate lockout intent
User self-report of being unexpectedly locked out coinciding with a burst of failed attempts they did not make
scopeExcludes: Failed logins as a byproduct of a credential-stuffing/brute-force attempt genuinely seeking to guess the password (tracked under Account Enumeration or brute-force related ITIDs)
Lockout-threshold probing/testing without denying an actual user (see ITID-12823)
ITID-12822.severity: Medium — primarily an availability/business-disruption impact rather than a compromise.
ITID-12822.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if targeting a business-critical or privileged account.
ITID-12822.escalation: Escalate to security operations to block the source and unlock the affected account after identity verification.
indicators: Burst of failed login attempts against one username with low variation, immediately triggering lockout
Multiple user reports of unexpected lockout without having attempted to log in
vectors: Attacker repeatedly submitting a known-invalid password against a target's known username purely to trigger lockout
Automated tooling scripted to lock out large numbers of accounts to disrupt business operations
rootCauses: Lockout policy triggered purely by failed-attempt count with no source-based or behavioral differentiation
controls: Source-IP-based or risk-based lockout thresholds rather than flat per-account thresholds
Account lockout alerting distinguishing likely-malicious lockout patterns
ITID-12822.detection: SIEM analysis of failed-login patterns (low password variation, single-account focus, burst timing) provides a real, concrete technical signal distinguishing this from genuine brute-force.
ITID-12822.response: Unlock the affected account after identity verification and block the source of the malicious attempts.
metrics: Count of confirmed malicious lockout-DoS events per quarter
ITID-12822.notes: Differentiator is malicious intent to deny access (low password variation, single target) vs. genuine credential-guessing attempts.

playbook.name: Response: Denial-of-Service via Deliberate Lockout Triggering
playbook.description: For an attacker deliberately submitting bad credentials against known usernames purely to trigger account lockouts and deny legitimate users access.

steps.title: Confirm intent is denial-of-service, not credential guessing
steps.desc: Review the failed-attempt pattern — a DoS lockout attack typically uses a small number of wrong-password attempts per account across a wide swath of known usernames, rather than many guesses per account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed pattern consistent with deliberate lockout DoS.

steps.title: Block the source infrastructure
steps.desc: Block or rate-limit the source IP(s)/ASN generating the lockout-inducing attempts at the edge/WAF.
steps.outcome: Further lockout attempts stopped.

steps.title: Unlock verified legitimate accounts
steps.desc: Bulk-unlock the confirmed list of legitimately affected accounts once the source is blocked, verifying via IAM audit that no unauthorized unlock requests are mixed in.
steps.outcome: Legitimate users restored to access.

steps.title: Consider adaptive lockout controls
steps.desc: Evaluate enabling smarter lockout logic (e.g. IP-based throttling before account-based lockout, CAPTCHA challenge) to reduce future DoS exploitability.
steps.outcome: Decision made and, if applicable, ticket opened for IAM configuration change.

steps.title: Document business impact and recommend policy change
steps.desc: Record scope of disruption, response time, and recommended lockout-policy improvements.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with recommendation tracked.

steps.title: Determine scope of locked-out accounts
steps.desc: Produce the full list of accounts locked out as a result of this activity, including business-critical or customer-facing accounts.
steps.outcome: Complete impact list with business criticality noted.

steps.title: Notify business stakeholders of service impact
steps.desc: Inform affected business units/support teams of the scope of impacted accounts so they can manage user inquiries.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed and prepared for increased support volume.

ITID-12823.def: An attacker deliberately submitting a controlled, small number of failed attempts against one or more accounts to determine the exact number of attempts, time window, or reset behavior of the lockout policy, as reconnaissance for a subsequent attack designed to stay just under the threshold.
ITID-12823.purpose: Captures an attacker probing the authentication system to determine the exact lockout threshold and policy behavior.
scopeIncludes: Controlled, incrementing failed-attempt testing against a test or throwaway account to map the lockout threshold
Systematic testing of lockout reset timing (how long until the counter resets)
scopeExcludes: Actual lockout-triggering denial-of-service intent against a real target (see ITID-12822)
Successful low-and-slow attack that has moved beyond probing into full exploitation (see ITID-12826, ITID-12827)
ITID-12823.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if paired with a subsequent low-and-slow attack.
ITID-12823.escalation: Escalate to security operations to monitor for a follow-on low-and-slow credential attack once the threshold is believed to be mapped.
indicators: Small, controlled batches of failed attempts against an account with pauses consistent with threshold-testing behavior
Repeated distinct failed-attempt-count patterns from the same source against a test or sacrificial account
vectors: Attacker testing failed-attempt counts against their own or a throwaway account before conducting a full attack against target accounts
rootCauses: Lockout policy behavior not obscured (predictable/documented threshold and reset window)
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Randomized/less-predictable lockout threshold and reset window behavior
Behavioral monitoring for threshold-probing patterns
ITID-12823.detection: SIEM pattern analysis for controlled, incrementing failed-attempt batches provides a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12823.response: Monitor the source for escalation into a full low-and-slow attack and consider proactively tightening detection thresholds.
metrics: Count of threshold-probing patterns detected per quarter
ITID-12823.notes: Differentiator is reconnaissance/mapping intent, distinct from denial-of-service intent (ITID-12822) and full exploitation (ITID-12826, ITID-12827).

playbook.name: Response: Lockout Threshold Probing
playbook.description: For an attacker deliberately testing the exact number of failed attempts allowed before lockout, typically as reconnaissance ahead of a low-and-slow credential attack.

steps.title: Confirm threshold-probing pattern
steps.desc: Review logs for a small number of failed attempts per account (below the lockout threshold), repeated methodically across a set of accounts.
steps.guidance: This is distinct from a DoS attempt — the attacker deliberately stays under the threshold rather than triggering lockouts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed probing pattern.

steps.title: Block the source
steps.desc: Block or rate-limit the source IP(s) conducting the probing.
steps.outcome: Probing traffic stopped.

steps.title: Flag accounts for elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Place the probed account list on a watchlist for a follow-on low-and-slow credential attack.
steps.outcome: Watchlist/alert configured.

steps.title: Monitor for the anticipated follow-on attack
steps.desc: Track the watchlisted accounts for renewed low-volume authentication attempts over the following weeks.
steps.outcome: Follow-on attack detected early if it occurs, or no further activity observed.

steps.title: Document as reconnaissance precursor
steps.desc: Record the probing pattern as a precursor indicator for future detection-rule tuning.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; detection rule refined if applicable.

steps.title: Identify the probed account list
steps.desc: Extract the accounts targeted to assess whether this is reconnaissance ahead of a targeted low-and-slow attack.
steps.outcome: List of probed accounts and correlation to any prior enumeration activity.

ITID-12824.def: A deliberate account-lockout denial-of-service attack (per ITID-12822's general pattern) where the target is specifically a privileged, administrative, or otherwise business-critical account, elevating the business impact and threat intent.
ITID-12824.purpose: Captures deliberate lockout denial-of-service specifically targeting a privileged or otherwise high-value account.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate lockout triggering against a named administrator, executive, or on-call/critical-role account
Lockout DoS timed to coincide with a critical business event (e.g. incident response, financial close) to maximize disruption
scopeExcludes: Deliberate lockout DoS against a standard, non-privileged user account (see ITID-12822)
ITID-12824.severity: High — targets an account whose unavailability has outsized business or security impact.
ITID-12824.escalation: Immediate escalation to security operations and the affected individual's leadership; verify identity and unlock urgently.
indicators: Lockout-triggering burst specifically against a known privileged/administrative account identifier
Lockout timing correlated with a sensitive business event or the account holder's known critical responsibilities
vectors: Attacker locking out a security or IT administrator's account to delay incident response during a broader attack
Attacker locking out an executive account ahead of a time-sensitive business action
rootCauses: No differentiated, higher-scrutiny lockout/alerting policy for privileged and business-critical accounts
controls: Elevated, real-time alerting on lockout events for privileged/critical accounts
Expedited emergency unlock/break-glass process for privileged accounts
ITID-12824.detection: SIEM alerting tuned specifically for lockout events against the privileged-account watchlist provides a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12824.response: Treat as a potential precursor to or component of a broader attack (e.g. delaying IR response); unlock urgently after identity verification and investigate for concurrent malicious activity.
metrics: Count of privileged-account lockout DoS events per quarter
Mean time to restore access to a locked-out privileged account
ITID-12824.notes: Differentiator vs. ITID-12822 is the privileged/critical nature of the specific target, warranting a higher default priority.

playbook.name: Response: Targeted Privileged Account Lockout DoS
playbook.description: For a deliberate attack that locks out specific privileged/administrative accounts to disrupt incident response, change control, or critical operations.

steps.title: Confirm targeting of privileged accounts
steps.desc: Confirm the locked-out accounts are privileged/admin accounts and review the timing against any concurrent suspicious activity (this technique is often used to hinder defenders during a broader intrusion).
steps.guidance: Treat this as a potential diversion — check for other concurrent alerts before assuming this is the whole incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed privileged-account targeting and assessment of whether it correlates with a broader active intrusion.

steps.title: Invoke break-glass access if needed
steps.desc: If critical operations are blocked, use the organization's documented break-glass/emergency-access procedure to restore privileged capability.
steps.guidance: Break-glass use must be logged and reviewed post-incident per policy.
steps.outcome: Critical privileged capability restored via an audited emergency path.
steps.abort: If no break-glass procedure exists, escalate immediately to IT leadership.

steps.title: Verify accounts unlocked with strong identity check
steps.desc: Unlock affected privileged accounts only after strong identity verification (manager confirmation plus a second factor), given the elevated risk of social-engineering follow-up.
steps.outcome: Privileged accounts restored with no unauthorized unlocks.

steps.title: Investigate for concurrent intrusion activity
steps.desc: Broaden the investigation to check for any concurrent unauthorized activity that the lockout may have been used to mask or hinder response to.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of a related broader intrusion.

steps.title: Document and review break-glass process
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether the break-glass process performed adequately under pressure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; break-glass process improvements identified if needed.

steps.title: Assess operational impact
steps.desc: Determine what critical functions (change approval, incident response, break-glass access) are impaired by the lockout.
steps.outcome: Impact to critical operations documented.

steps.title: Block the source infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the source(s) generating the failed privileged-account login attempts.
steps.outcome: Further lockout attempts stopped.

ITID-12825.def: An attacker triggering or falsely claiming an account lockout, then contacting the help desk/support channel posing as the legitimate user to obtain an unauthorized unlock or password reset, exploiting the help desk's identity-verification gap.
ITID-12825.purpose: Captures a social-engineering attack where an attacker exploits a lockout event (real or falsely claimed) by calling the help desk to obtain a fraudulent unlock or reset.
scopeIncludes: Attacker calling the help desk claiming lockout and successfully socially engineering an unlock/reset with insufficient identity verification
Attacker triggering a real lockout specifically to create a pretext for a follow-up fraudulent support call
scopeExcludes: A genuine, correctly verified lockout/unlock support interaction (not an incident)
Self-service unlock portal abuse not involving a human help desk interaction (see ITID-12828)
ITID-12825.severity: High — a successful social-engineering unlock/reset directly grants the attacker account access.
ITID-12825.escalation: Immediate escalation to security and help desk management; treat as a confirmed account compromise pending verification.
indicators: Help desk ticket/call log showing an unlock or reset granted with weak or bypassed identity verification
Unlock/reset immediately followed by anomalous account activity
vectors: Vishing (voice phishing) call to the help desk impersonating the account holder to request an unlock/reset
Pretexting using publicly available personal information to pass weak identity-verification questions
rootCauses: Help desk identity-verification process relying on easily obtainable information (e.g. employee ID, date of birth)
No callback-to-verified-number or manager-attestation step for high-risk unlock/reset requests
controls: Strengthened help desk identity verification (callback to verified number, video verification, manager attestation) for unlock/reset requests
Help desk staff training on social-engineering/vishing recognition
ITID-12825.detection: Help desk call/ticket recording review and post-unlock account-activity monitoring provide the primary, real technical and process signal.
ITID-12825.response: Immediately lock the account again pending verified re-authentication, review the help desk interaction, and retrain/adjust the verification process.
metrics: Count of confirmed fraudulent unlock/reset events per quarter
ITID-12825.notes: Scoped to the human help-desk social-engineering vector specifically, distinct from self-service portal abuse (ITID-12828).

playbook.name: Response: Lockout-Triggered Fake Support Call Exploitation
playbook.description: For an attack combining deliberate account lockout with a follow-up social-engineering call to the helpdesk impersonating the locked-out user to obtain a fraudulent unlock or password reset.

steps.title: Confirm the lockout-to-social-engineering chain
steps.desc: Correlate the account lockout event with a subsequent helpdesk contact requesting unlock/reset, and review the helpdesk interaction for identity-verification failures.
steps.guidance: Check call/ticket logs, caller ID vs registered contact number, and whether standard verification steps were followed or bypassed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or ruled-out social-engineering attempt tied to the lockout.

steps.title: Lock the account pending verified re-identification
steps.desc: If a fraudulent unlock/reset succeeded, immediately re-lock the account and force a password reset through a verified channel.
steps.outcome: Account secured against the impersonator.

steps.title: Restore access with strengthened verification
steps.desc: Restore the legitimate user's access only through the organization's strongest identity-verification path (e.g. in-person or manager-vouched).
steps.outcome: Legitimate user access restored securely.

steps.title: Retrain or coach the helpdesk agent involved
steps.desc: Review the interaction with the helpdesk agent and reinforce identity-verification procedure.
steps.outcome: Coaching completed; procedure gap addressed.

steps.title: Document and strengthen helpdesk verification policy
steps.desc: Record the full attack chain and recommend a policy improvement (e.g. mandatory callback to a registered number, out-of-band manager approval for privileged unlocks).
steps.outcome: Finding logged; policy recommendation tracked to completion.

steps.title: Determine whether the fraudulent unlock succeeded
steps.desc: Establish whether the helpdesk actually performed an unlock/reset for the impersonator, and if so, whether the account was subsequently accessed by an unauthorized party.
steps.outcome: Confirmed status: attempt only, or successful account takeover.

steps.title: Revoke sessions established by the impersonator
steps.desc: If the account was accessed, revoke all active sessions/tokens issued since the fraudulent unlock.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized sessions terminated.

ITID-12826.def: A credential attack (brute force, password spraying, credential stuffing) designed to stay under the lockout threshold by distributing failed attempts across a large number of distinct source IPs, such that no single IP or short time window triggers detection or lockout.
ITID-12826.purpose: Captures an attacker evading lockout thresholds by distributing failed login attempts across many source IP addresses.
scopeIncludes: Failed login attempts against a target account or account set originating from a large, distributed pool of IPs (e.g. via botnet or residential proxy network)
Attack pattern specifically engineered to keep per-IP or per-window attempt counts below alerting/lockout thresholds
scopeExcludes: Lockout threshold probing without an active distributed attack underway (see ITID-12823)
A single-source, high-volume attack that does trigger lockout as intended by policy (not this specific evasion pattern)
ITID-12826.severity: High — represents a sophisticated, evasion-aware credential attack likely to succeed against IP-based rate limiting alone.
ITID-12826.escalation: Immediate escalation to security operations; this pattern indicates a capable, persistent adversary requiring broader monitoring beyond simple IP blocking.
indicators: Low per-IP failed-attempt counts aggregating to a high total against the same account/account set across many distinct source IPs
Source IPs consistent with known residential proxy/botnet infrastructure
vectors: Residential proxy network or botnet used to distribute credential-stuffing/spraying attempts
Automated tooling explicitly designed to rotate source IPs to evade rate limiting
rootCauses: Lockout/rate-limiting policy based solely on per-IP thresholds with no per-account or global velocity correlation
controls: Per-account and global velocity-based detection independent of per-IP rate limiting
Device fingerprinting and behavioral analytics to detect distributed attack patterns
ITID-12826.detection: UEBA/behavioral analytics correlating per-account attempt velocity across distributed sources provides a real, concrete technical signal beyond simple IP-based rate limiting.
ITID-12826.response: Enforce account-level protective actions (forced MFA, temporary step-up authentication) independent of IP blocking, and investigate for successful compromise.
metrics: Count of distributed-source credential attacks detected per quarter
ITID-12826.notes: Differentiator is the deliberate distribution across sources to evade lockout, a distinct evasion technique from simple threshold probing (ITID-12823) or exploiting a policy gap (ITID-12827).

playbook.name: Response: Lockout Bypass via Distributed Source IPs
playbook.description: For an attacker distributing failed login attempts across many source IPs to stay under a per-IP or aggregate threshold and avoid triggering account lockout while still attempting many passwords.

steps.title: Confirm distributed low-volume-per-source pattern
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for many distinct source IPs each submitting a small number of attempts against the same account(s), collectively exceeding what a single-source lockout policy would catch.
steps.guidance: This typically indicates botnet or proxy infrastructure; check ASN diversity and any shared user-agent/TLS fingerprint across sources.
steps.outcome: Confirmed distributed lockout-evasion pattern.

steps.title: Enable aggregate/account-based rate limiting
steps.desc: Shift or supplement lockout logic to trigger on aggregate failed attempts per account regardless of source IP, rather than per-IP thresholds alone.
steps.guidance: This is the direct fix for this evasion technique — coordinate with IAM/identity platform owner if it requires a configuration change.
steps.outcome: Account-based throttling active, closing the per-IP evasion gap.

steps.title: Reset credentials for any compromised accounts
steps.desc: If any account was confirmed compromised, force a password reset and session revocation for that account.
steps.outcome: Compromised accounts secured.

steps.title: Enforce MFA on targeted accounts
steps.desc: Require or verify MFA enrollment on all targeted accounts to reduce risk from any successful password guess.
steps.outcome: MFA enforced on all targeted accounts.

steps.title: Document lockout-policy gap and fix
steps.desc: Record the evasion technique and the account-based throttling change made to close it.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Identify targeted accounts and any successful logins
steps.desc: Determine which accounts were targeted and check for any successful authentication among the attempts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of targeted accounts and whether any were compromised.

steps.title: Block identifiable distributed infrastructure
steps.desc: Block known botnet/proxy ranges identified in the source list where feasible.
steps.outcome: Portion of distributed infrastructure blocked.

ITID-12827.def: Successful credential attack enabled by an actual defect or inconsistency in how the lockout policy is implemented — such as a policy that applies to one authentication endpoint but not another for the same account, or a counter that does not reset/apply correctly — as distinct from evading a correctly functioning policy via distributed sources.
ITID-12827.purpose: Captures exploitation of a genuine gap or inconsistency in the lockout policy's design, rather than evasion of a properly designed policy.
scopeIncludes: Lockout policy enforced on the primary web login but not on a legacy API, mobile, or protocol endpoint (e.g. legacy IMAP/SMTP) sharing the same credential store
Lockout counter reset logic flaw allowing effectively unlimited attempts
scopeExcludes: Evasion of a correctly functioning lockout policy via distributed source IPs (see ITID-12826)
Reconnaissance-only threshold probing (see ITID-12823)
ITID-12827.severity: High — indicates a systemic control gap rather than a sophisticated attacker technique, often exploitable at scale.
ITID-12827.escalation: Immediate escalation to application/identity engineering to close the policy gap across all authentication surfaces.
indicators: Successful high-volume credential attack against an authentication endpoint known not to enforce the standard lockout policy
Post-incident review confirming the lockout counter did not function/reset as designed
vectors: Attacker targeting a legacy protocol endpoint (e.g. legacy mail protocols, an older API version) that shares credentials with the main application but lacks equivalent lockout enforcement
rootCauses: Lockout policy implemented inconsistently across authentication surfaces sharing the same identity store
Legacy or deprecated authentication endpoints not decommissioned or brought into policy parity
controls: Consistent lockout policy enforcement across all authentication surfaces sharing an identity store
Decommissioning or hardening of legacy authentication endpoints
ITID-12827.detection: Cross-endpoint authentication log correlation reveals the policy gap being actively exploited — a concrete, real technical signal once cross-surface visibility exists.
ITID-12827.response: Close the policy gap immediately across all affected endpoints and audit for accounts compromised via the gap while it existed.
metrics: Count of authentication surfaces found with inconsistent lockout enforcement per audit cycle
sops: Authentication Surface Lockout Policy Parity SOP
ITID-12827.notes: Differentiator is a genuine implementation/policy defect as root cause, distinct from an attacker's evasion technique against a correctly functioning policy (ITID-12826).

playbook.name: Response: Lockout Policy Gap Exploitation
playbook.description: For an attacker exploiting a specific configuration gap or inconsistency in the lockout policy (e.g. a legacy protocol endpoint not covered by the lockout rule, or differing thresholds across systems).

steps.title: Identify the specific policy gap exploited
steps.desc: Determine exactly which endpoint, protocol, or system is not enforcing the same lockout threshold as the primary authentication path, and confirm attempts are concentrated there.
steps.guidance: Common gaps: legacy IMAP/POP/SMTP auth, an API that bypasses the web lockout logic, or a federated system with its own separate policy.
steps.outcome: Specific gap identified and confirmed as the exploited vector.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the gapped access path
steps.desc: If the gapped endpoint/protocol is not business-critical, disable it; otherwise apply an equivalent lockout/rate-limit control directly to it as an interim measure.
steps.outcome: Gap closed or mitigated.

steps.title: Align lockout policy across all authentication paths
steps.desc: File a ticket to bring the identified system/protocol under the same lockout policy as the primary path on a permanent basis.
steps.outcome: Consistent lockout enforcement across all authentication surfaces.

steps.title: Verify no accounts were compromised via the gap
steps.desc: Check whether any successful authentication occurred through the gapped path during the exploitation window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no compromise, or compromised accounts identified for remediation.

steps.title: Document the gap and audit for similar inconsistencies
steps.desc: Record the specific gap and recommend an audit of all authentication endpoints for similar policy inconsistencies.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; audit initiated.

steps.title: Determine scope of accounts targeted through the gap
steps.desc: Extract the accounts and volume of attempts made through the gapped path.
steps.outcome: Scope documented.

ITID-12828.def: Exploitation of an automated, self-service account unlock/reset portal (e.g. security-question-based unlock, SMS/email-based unlock) where weaknesses in the portal's own automated verification logic allow an attacker to unlock or reset an account without human interaction.
ITID-12828.purpose: Captures abuse of a self-service account unlock portal itself, as distinct from a human help-desk social-engineering interaction.
scopeIncludes: Attacker guessing or researching security-question answers to pass an automated self-service unlock flow
Automated unlock portal vulnerable to SIM-swap-enabled SMS interception or email-account takeover as the verification factor
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent unlock obtained via a human help-desk phone/chat interaction (see ITID-12825)
ITID-12828.severity: High — grants the attacker direct, unsupervised account access if successful.
ITID-12828.escalation: Immediate escalation to identity engineering to strengthen the self-service portal's verification factors.
indicators: Successful self-service unlock/reset immediately followed by anomalous account activity
Security-question or knowledge-based-authentication answers submitted that correlate with publicly available OSINT about the account holder
vectors: Attacker researching an account holder's public social media/OSINT to answer security questions
SIM-swap attack enabling interception of an SMS-based unlock code
rootCauses: Self-service unlock relying on weak knowledge-based authentication (easily researchable security questions) as the sole factor
SMS as the sole out-of-band factor for unlock, vulnerable to SIM-swap
controls: Strengthened self-service unlock verification (avoid knowledge-based questions alone; prefer app-based or hardware MFA over SMS)
Post-unlock anomalous-activity monitoring
ITID-12828.detection: Self-service portal audit logs combined with post-unlock UEBA monitoring provide a concrete technical signal.
ITID-12828.response: Lock the account again pending verified re-authentication, strengthen the portal's verification factors, and investigate for compromise.
metrics: Count of self-service unlock portal abuse events confirmed per quarter
ITID-12828.notes: Scoped to the automated self-service portal specifically, distinct from the human help-desk social-engineering vector (ITID-12825).

playbook.name: Response: Self-Service Unlock Portal Abuse
playbook.description: For an attacker abusing the self-service account-unlock portal (e.g. weak security questions, SMS/email interception, or automation) to unlock and take over an account without helpdesk involvement.

steps.title: Confirm abuse of the self-service unlock flow
steps.desc: Review self-service portal logs for the unlock attempt(s), the verification method used (security questions, SMS/email code), and whether it succeeded.
steps.outcome: Confirmed method of abuse and outcome.

steps.title: Lock the account and revoke sessions if compromised
steps.desc: If the unlock led to unauthorized access, re-lock the account and revoke all active sessions/tokens.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

steps.title: Reset weak verification factors
steps.desc: Reset the account's security questions/recovery contact details and force a password reset through a verified channel.
steps.outcome: Weak verification factors replaced; account restored securely.

steps.title: Assess and harden the self-service unlock method
steps.desc: File a ticket to strengthen the verification factor exploited (e.g. replace security questions with MFA-based unlock, or add anomaly detection to the self-service flow).
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened with the specific weakness documented.

steps.title: Document and review self-service portal security posture
steps.desc: Record the abuse method and recommend a broader review of the self-service unlock portal's security controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; review scheduled if warranted.

steps.title: Determine if the account was subsequently accessed
steps.desc: Check whether a successful self-service unlock was followed by an actual login and, if so, from what source/device.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise status.

ITID-12829.def: A confirmed case where exploitation of the lockout mechanism (via any of the technique-specific siblings in this Type) directly resulted in a further confirmed security outcome — unauthorized account access, a successful denial-of-service with measurable business impact, or a confirmed fraudulent unlock leading to compromise.
ITID-12829.purpose: Captures the confirmed-successful outcome of a lockout-related attack — where the lockout mechanism's exploitation directly enabled a further, confirmed compromise.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed unauthorized account access following a fraudulent unlock or self-service portal exploitation
Confirmed, measurable business disruption from a lockout denial-of-service attack (e.g. missed SLA, blocked critical operation)
scopeExcludes: Attempted but unsuccessful lockout exploitation with no confirmed further impact (tracked under the relevant technique-specific sibling)
ITID-12829.severity: Critical — represents confirmed realized impact rather than an attempted or contained exploitation.
ITID-12829.escalation: Immediate escalation to full incident response; treat as a confirmed compromise or confirmed business-impacting availability incident.
indicators: Confirmed anomalous account activity immediately following a lockout-related exploitation event
Documented business/operational impact directly attributable to a lockout denial-of-service
vectors: Any of the sibling techniques in this Type (fraudulent help-desk unlock, self-service portal abuse, distributed evasion, policy-gap exploitation) culminating in a confirmed compromise or measurable disruption
rootCauses: Underlying technique-specific root cause (root-caused under the originating sibling ITID, not duplicated here)
controls: Full incident response activation for confirmed lockout-enabled compromise
Post-incident review feeding back into the specific technique's control gap
ITID-12829.detection: Combines the technique-specific detection from the originating sibling with confirmed post-event impact evidence (account activity logs, business-impact reporting).
ITID-12829.response: Full incident response: contain, investigate scope of compromise/impact, remediate the originating technique's control gap, and report business impact.
metrics: Count of confirmed lockout-enabled compromises/impacts per year
ITID-12829.notes: This leaf documents confirmed realized outcomes specifically; the enabling technique is root-caused under its specific sibling ITID (ITID-12822 through ITID-12828) to avoid duplicating root-cause detail.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Lockout-Enabled Attack
playbook.description: For a confirmed incident where account-lockout manipulation (DoS, threshold evasion, or self-service/helpdesk abuse) directly enabled a successful account takeover or other confirmed compromise.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and reconstruct the attack chain
steps.desc: Establish the full sequence from the lockout manipulation technique used through to the confirmed unauthorized access, and identify the account(s) and systems affected.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a confirmed account-takeover incident — prioritize accordingly.
steps.outcome: Complete, documented attack chain and confirmed scope of compromise.

steps.title: Lock the account and revoke all sessions/tokens
steps.desc: Immediately disable the compromised account and revoke every active session, API token, and OAuth grant.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Check for persistence established during access
steps.desc: Review the account and any downstream systems reached for attacker-added persistence (forwarding rules, new credentials, OAuth grants, scheduled tasks).
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore account with strengthened verification and monitoring
steps.desc: Restore legitimate access through verified channels, enforce MFA if not already present, and place the account under elevated monitoring for 30 days.
steps.outcome: Account restored securely with monitoring in place.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the full chain, notify affected stakeholders as required by policy, and drive the lockout-policy fix to completion.
steps.outcome: Post-incident review completed; remediation tracked to closure.

steps.title: Determine what the attacker did with access
steps.desc: Review activity logs for the compromised account since the point of takeover to identify data accessed, actions taken, or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker activity documented.

steps.title: Block the attacker infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the source IP(s)/infrastructure used in both the lockout-manipulation phase and the subsequent access.
steps.outcome: Attacker infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Remove confirmed persistence and close the lockout vector
steps.desc: Remove any attacker-established persistence, and remediate the specific lockout-manipulation vector used (per the relevant technique-specific playbook).
steps.outcome: No attacker foothold remains; the exploited lockout mechanism is fixed.

ITID-12831.def: An incident involving injection of credentials or authentication material into an application flow through an unintended technical mechanism, not yet matched to a more specific injection technique.
ITID-12831.purpose: Catch-all for credential injection that does not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific injection technique is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Credential Injection
ITID-12831.escalation: Escalate to application security once the specific technique is confirmed; reclassify accordingly.
indicators: Application security alert of unclear specific injection technique
vectors: Injection attempt of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Input validation and authentication-flow integrity monitoring
ITID-12831.detection: Same application-security telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-12831.response: Investigate and reclassify to a specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-12831.notes: Intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Credential Injection
playbook.description: General triage playbook for a suspected credential-injection incident (input directly manipulating or bypassing an authentication mechanism) where the specific technique has not yet been identified.

steps.title: Confirm the injection alert
steps.desc: Review the WAF/application alert and associated request payload to confirm it contains injection syntax targeting an authentication field.
steps.guidance: Look at the raw request body/headers for SQL/LDAP metacharacters, script tags, or malformed session tokens submitted at a login/auth endpoint.
steps.outcome: Confirmed injection attempt, or ruled out as benign.
steps.abort: If the payload is clearly a WAF false positive (e.g. a legitimate special character in a password), close as false positive.

steps.title: Block the source
steps.desc: Block or rate-limit the source IP(s) at the WAF/edge.
steps.outcome: Further injection attempts blocked.

steps.title: Escalate the vulnerable endpoint for remediation
steps.desc: File a ticket with the application team identifying the exact endpoint and payload type for input-validation/parameterization fixes.
steps.outcome: Remediation ticket opened.

steps.title: Verify no unauthorized access resulted
steps.desc: If injection succeeded, follow the account-takeover recovery steps (reset credentials, revoke sessions) for any affected account.
steps.outcome: Any compromised account secured.

steps.title: Document finding
steps.desc: Record the technique, endpoint, and remediation status.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the injection succeeded
steps.desc: Check application/auth logs for whether the injected request resulted in a successful authentication or an error.
steps.outcome: Confirmed success or failure of the injection attempt.

ITID-12832.def: Malware installed on the victim's endpoint that hooks into the browser to intercept, modify, or inject content into an authenticated session in real time — capturing credentials as entered, or injecting fraudulent form fields/transactions into a legitimate, already-authenticated session.
ITID-12832.purpose: Captures credential/transaction manipulation performed by malware operating within the victim's own browser session (Man-in-the-Browser).
scopeIncludes: Browser-hooking malware (e.g. banking trojan) intercepting credentials as typed into a legitimate login form
Malware injecting additional form fields (e.g. requesting extra authentication data) into a legitimate site's rendered page
scopeExcludes: Malicious browser extension performing the injection (see ITID-12837, a distinct delivery mechanism)
Credential harvesting via a phishing site rather than manipulation of a legitimate session (tracked under phishing-related ITIDs)
ITID-12832.severity: Critical — occurs within a genuine, already-authenticated session and can bypass many session-based defenses.
ITID-12832.escalation: Immediate escalation to incident response for endpoint remediation and account credential/session rotation.
indicators: EDR detection of known Man-in-the-Browser malware family behavior/hooking APIs
Anomalous DOM modification or injected form fields detected by client-side integrity monitoring
vectors: Banking trojan or similar malware family hooking browser APIs to intercept form submissions
Malware injecting a fraudulent request (e.g. for an additional OTP) into a legitimate banking/application page
rootCauses: Endpoint lacking adequate anti-malware/EDR coverage allowing the browser-hooking malware to persist
No client-side integrity/tamper monitoring for high-value authentication pages
controls: EDR detection/blocking of known browser-hooking malware families
Client-side integrity monitoring for authentication and transaction pages
ITID-12832.detection: EDR malware-family detection and client-side page-integrity monitoring provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12832.response: Remediate the infected endpoint, rotate all credentials entered during the infection period, and review for fraudulent transactions.
metrics: Count of Man-in-the-Browser detections per quarter
ITID-12832.notes: Scoped to malware operating directly within the browser process itself, distinct from a malicious browser extension (ITID-12837), a related but architecturally distinct delivery mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Man-in-the-Browser Credential Injection
playbook.description: For malware or a malicious browser component that injects transactions or credential-capture fields into a legitimate session in the victim's browser (man-in-the-browser).

steps.title: Confirm MitB indicators on the endpoint
steps.desc: Investigate the reporting user's endpoint for a banking-trojan/MitB family (e.g. injected form fields, unexpected transaction confirmation prompts) via EDR telemetry.
steps.guidance: MitB frequently targets banking/finance portals with injected extra fields (SSN, card PIN) not part of the legitimate page.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence of MitB malware/component, or ruled out.

steps.title: Isolate the infected endpoint
steps.desc: Isolate the affected device from the network via EDR to stop further injection/exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Remove the malware and reimage if needed
steps.desc: Remove the MitB component via EDR remediation, or reimage the device if clean removal cannot be confirmed.
steps.guidance: Browser-injecting malware often persists via a malicious extension or hooked browser process — full reimage is the safest path when in doubt.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Coordinate fraud reversal if a transaction occurred
steps.desc: If a fraudulent transaction was submitted, work with the affected financial institution/payment provider to attempt reversal.
steps.outcome: Fraud reversal initiated where applicable.

steps.title: Document infection vector and financial impact
steps.desc: Record how the malware was delivered, data exposed, and any financial impact for the case record.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine what was captured or manipulated
steps.desc: Establish what credential/transaction data the injected content captured or altered, and whether any fraudulent transaction was submitted.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the targeted service (e.g. bank/payment provider) if a transaction may have been manipulated.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of data exposure and any fraudulent transaction.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and reset affected credentials
steps.desc: Force a password reset and session revocation for any account whose credentials were exposed through the injected fields.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

ITID-12833.def: Abuse of a browser's or password manager's automatic form-filling behavior — typically via hidden or off-screen form fields injected by a malicious or compromised page — to trick the autofill mechanism into revealing stored credentials to an attacker-controlled field.
ITID-12833.purpose: Captures exploitation of browser autofill or password manager auto-fill behavior to harvest credentials without user awareness.
scopeIncludes: Malicious page containing hidden form fields exploiting password-manager autofill heuristics to exfiltrate stored credentials
Phishing page cloned to trigger legitimate-site autofill matching, harvesting credentials silently
scopeExcludes: Man-in-the-Browser malware directly hooking the browser process (see ITID-12832)
Credential injection via a malicious browser extension with direct DOM/API access (see ITID-12837)
ITID-12833.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if confirmed against privileged accounts.
ITID-12833.escalation: Escalate to security engineering and end-user awareness teams; force credential rotation for confirmed-affected users.
indicators: Security research/threat intelligence identifying a phishing kit using autofill-exploitation techniques targeting the organization's domain
Endpoint/browser telemetry showing autofill triggered on a non-legitimate domain matching the organization's saved credential
vectors: Phishing page designed to closely match the legitimate domain's autofill-matching heuristics
Hidden iframe or off-screen field technique to trigger autofill without user awareness
rootCauses: Password manager/browser autofill heuristics not strict enough about domain matching
No user training on verifying domain authenticity before allowing autofill to proceed
mitreTechniques: T1555.003 Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
controls: Browser/password-manager domain-matching hardening settings
Phishing-resistant MFA reducing the value of a harvested password alone
ITID-12833.detection: Endpoint/browser security telemetry and threat-intelligence tracking of phishing kits using this technique provide a concrete, real signal.
ITID-12833.response: Rotate credentials for confirmed-affected users and reinforce phishing-resistant MFA to limit impact of any harvested password.
metrics: Count of autofill-exploitation-based credential harvesting events confirmed per quarter
ITID-12833.notes: Scoped to exploitation of the autofill mechanism specifically, distinct from browser-hooking malware (ITID-12832) and malicious extensions (ITID-12837).

playbook.name: Response: Autofill/Password Manager Field Injection Exploitation
playbook.description: For an attacker abusing hidden or off-screen form fields on a malicious/compromised page to trick a browser autofill or password manager into disclosing saved credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious page and technique
steps.desc: Obtain and analyze the reported page's source for hidden/invisible input fields designed to capture autofilled credentials.
steps.guidance: Check for off-screen positioning, zero-opacity fields, or fields outside the visible form matching common credential field names.
steps.outcome: Confirmed technique and page identified.

steps.title: Block the malicious domain
steps.desc: Add the domain to the web/DNS blocklist.
steps.outcome: Domain blocked org-wide.

steps.title: Advise on autofill hardening
steps.desc: Issue guidance/policy recommendation to disable browser-native autofill for credentials in favor of a managed password manager with domain-matching, which is not fooled by hidden off-screen fields.
steps.outcome: Recommendation delivered to security awareness/endpoint teams.

steps.title: Monitor affected accounts
steps.desc: Place affected accounts under elevated monitoring for anomalous login activity.
steps.outcome: Watchlist configured.

steps.title: Document finding and awareness gap
steps.desc: Record the technique and recommend awareness content on autofill risks.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Identify affected users and accounts
steps.desc: Determine who visited the page with autofill enabled and whether credentials were likely disclosed.
steps.guidance: Check web proxy/DNS logs for visits to the malicious domain from managed devices.
steps.outcome: List of potentially affected users.

steps.title: Reset credentials for confirmed-affected accounts
steps.desc: Force a password reset and session revocation for any account confirmed or suspected to have been autofilled on the malicious page.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

ITID-12834.def: Exploitation of a SQL injection vulnerability in an authentication mechanism, where crafted input into a login field manipulates the underlying database query to bypass authentication (e.g. always returning a valid user record) without knowing a valid credential.
ITID-12834.purpose: Captures authentication bypass achieved by injecting SQL syntax into a login form or authentication query.
scopeIncludes: Classic SQL injection authentication bypass payload (e.g. tautology-based) submitted to a login form field
Blind or time-based SQL injection used to iteratively bypass or extract credential data from the authentication query
scopeExcludes: LDAP injection targeting a directory-based authentication backend (see ITID-12835)
API parameter/header injection not involving SQL syntax (see ITID-12838)
ITID-12834.severity: Critical — a successful SQL injection authentication bypass grants direct, often unrestricted account access.
ITID-12834.escalation: Immediate escalation to application security engineering; treat as a critical application vulnerability requiring emergency patching in addition to incident response.
indicators: WAF alert on SQL injection payload patterns submitted to authentication endpoints
Successful authentication bypass confirmed via application/database audit logs correlating with an anomalous query pattern
vectors: Unsanitized login field input concatenated directly into a SQL query string
Legacy authentication code not using parameterized queries/prepared statements
rootCauses: Authentication query construction using string concatenation instead of parameterized queries
No input validation/WAF coverage on authentication endpoints
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements mandatory for all authentication logic
WAF SQL injection detection and blocking on authentication endpoints
ITID-12834.detection: WAF SQL-injection signature/heuristic detection combined with application and database audit logs provides a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12834.response: Patch the vulnerable authentication code immediately (parameterized queries), rotate credentials for potentially affected accounts, and audit for prior successful exploitation.
metrics: Count of SQL injection authentication-bypass attempts blocked per quarter
Mean time to patch a confirmed SQL injection vulnerability in authentication code
ITID-12834.notes: Scoped to SQL-backed authentication systems specifically, distinct from LDAP-backed systems (ITID-12835).

playbook.name: Response: SQL Injection-Based Authentication Bypass
playbook.description: For an attacker using SQL injection syntax in a login field to bypass authentication logic directly against the backend database.

steps.title: Confirm the SQLi payload and target endpoint
steps.desc: Review the WAF/application logs for the exact injection payload submitted and the login endpoint targeted.
steps.guidance: Classic indicators include payloads like ' OR '1'='1 in username/password fields.
steps.outcome: Confirmed payload and endpoint.

steps.title: Block the source and consider temporary endpoint lockdown
steps.desc: Block the source IP at the WAF; if the vulnerability is actively exploitable and unpatched, consider taking the affected login endpoint offline or behind additional authentication until patched.
steps.guidance: Weigh business impact of downtime against continued exposure — escalate this decision to the application/service owner.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation stopped.

steps.title: Patch the vulnerable query as an emergency fix
steps.desc: Escalate to the application team to deploy parameterized queries/prepared statements for the affected authentication logic as an emergency patch.
steps.guidance: This is a critical-severity code vulnerability — treat as an emergency change, not routine backlog.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable query parameterized and deployed.

steps.title: Verify the fix and re-test
steps.desc: Re-test the endpoint with the original and variant payloads after the patch deploys.
steps.outcome: Bypass no longer possible.

steps.title: Document as a critical finding and drive SDLC improvement
steps.desc: Record full details and recommend secure-coding training/SAST gate improvements to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and shared with the application security program.

steps.title: Determine whether the bypass succeeded
steps.desc: Check whether the injected request resulted in an authenticated session, and if so, as which account/role.
steps.guidance: This is a critical determination — a successful SQLi auth bypass can grant unintended privilege levels depending on query logic.
steps.outcome: Confirmed success/failure and, if successful, the resulting access level.

steps.title: Revoke any session established via the bypass
steps.desc: If a session was created via the bypass, revoke it immediately.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized session terminated.

steps.title: Scan for similar vulnerable patterns elsewhere
steps.desc: Request a broader code/DAST scan for the same unsafe query-construction pattern across other endpoints.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of the vulnerability class across the application.

ITID-12835.def: Exploitation of an LDAP injection vulnerability in an authentication mechanism backed by a directory service (Active Directory, OpenLDAP), where crafted input manipulates the LDAP search filter to bypass authentication or return unintended directory objects.
ITID-12835.purpose: Captures authentication bypass achieved by injecting LDAP filter syntax into a directory-based authentication query.
scopeIncludes: Crafted login input manipulating an LDAP filter to bypass a directory-backed login (e.g. wildcard/tautology injection)
LDAP injection used to enumerate directory objects/attributes as part of an authentication-adjacent attack
scopeExcludes: SQL injection targeting a relational-database-backed authentication system (see ITID-12834)

LDAP injection used purely for object/attribute enumeration outside an authentication-bypass context (tracked under the reconnaissance-domain ITID-43722 LDAP Injection for Unauthorized Object/Attribute Enumeration)
ITID-12835.severity: Critical — directory services frequently back an organization's core identity infrastructure.
ITID-12835.escalation: Immediate escalation to identity/application security engineering; treat as a critical vulnerability requiring emergency patching.
indicators: WAF/application alert on LDAP injection payload patterns submitted to authentication endpoints
Directory service audit log showing an anomalous search filter pattern correlated with an authentication bypass
vectors: Unsanitized login field input concatenated directly into an LDAP search filter string
Legacy or custom-built authentication code not using an LDAP library's safe filter-escaping functions
rootCauses: Authentication query construction using unsanitized string concatenation into the LDAP filter
No input validation/WAF coverage on directory-backed authentication endpoints
controls: Proper LDAP filter escaping/sanitization in all authentication code
WAF LDAP injection detection and blocking on authentication endpoints
ITID-12835.detection: WAF LDAP-injection signature detection combined with directory service audit logs provides a strong, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12835.response: Patch the vulnerable authentication code immediately (proper filter escaping), rotate credentials for potentially affected accounts, and audit directory logs for prior exploitation.
metrics: Count of LDAP injection authentication-bypass attempts blocked per quarter
ITID-12835.notes: This branch is scoped to LDAP injection used specifically for authentication bypass; pure directory object/attribute enumeration without an authentication-bypass component is tracked separately under the reconnaissance domain's ITID-43722 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: LDAP Injection-Based Authentication Bypass
playbook.description: For an attacker using LDAP injection syntax in a login field to manipulate directory-service authentication logic and bypass login.

steps.title: Confirm the LDAP injection payload and target
steps.desc: Review WAF/application logs for LDAP filter metacharacters (e.g. *, (, ), &, |) submitted in authentication fields, and identify the affected login endpoint/directory integration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed payload and affected system.

steps.title: Block the source
steps.desc: Block the source IP at the WAF/edge.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation stopped.

steps.title: Fix the LDAP query construction
steps.desc: Escalate to the application team to properly escape/sanitize LDAP filter input as an emergency patch.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable query fixed and deployed.

steps.title: Verify fix and re-test
steps.desc: Re-test the endpoint with the original and variant payloads after the patch.
steps.outcome: Bypass no longer possible.

steps.title: Document as a critical finding
steps.desc: Record details and recommend secure-coding guidance for directory-integration code.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the bypass succeeded
steps.desc: Check directory/application logs for whether the injected filter resulted in an authenticated session, and against which account.
steps.outcome: Confirmed success/failure and resulting access level.

steps.title: Revoke any session established via the bypass
steps.desc: If a session resulted, revoke it immediately.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized session terminated.

ITID-12836.def: Injection or replay of a stolen, predicted, or forged session token/cookie into a request to impersonate an already-authenticated user, bypassing the login step entirely rather than manipulating the credential-submission process itself.
ITID-12836.purpose: Captures unauthorized use of a session identifier or cookie to impersonate an authenticated user without ever presenting a credential.
scopeIncludes: Stolen session cookie (via malware, network interception, or XSS) replayed by an attacker to hijack an active session
Session token predicted or forged due to weak session-ID generation
scopeExcludes: Credential interception at the point of entry via browser-hooking malware (see ITID-12832)
Man-in-the-Browser manipulation of an active session's page content (see ITID-12832) as distinct from pure token replay
ITID-12836.severity: Critical — grants immediate authenticated access without needing any credential at all.
ITID-12836.escalation: Immediate escalation to incident response for session invalidation across all active tokens and investigation of the theft/prediction vector.
indicators: Same session token used from two geographically inconsistent locations/devices in immediate succession
Session ID pattern showing predictability/weak entropy in security testing
vectors: Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability used to exfiltrate a session cookie
Network-level interception of an unencrypted session cookie (e.g. over an insecure Wi-Fi network)
Weak session-ID generation algorithm allowing prediction/brute-forcing of valid tokens
rootCauses: Session cookies not marked Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite
Weak, predictable session-token generation algorithm
Unpatched XSS vulnerability allowing cookie exfiltration
controls: Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes enforced on all session tokens
Cryptographically strong, unpredictable session-token generation
XSS prevention (output encoding, Content Security Policy)
ITID-12836.detection: UEBA impossible-travel/concurrent-session detection and session-ID entropy testing provide a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12836.response: Invalidate the hijacked session and all related tokens immediately, force re-authentication, and remediate the underlying theft/prediction vector (e.g. patch the XSS vulnerability).
metrics: Count of confirmed session hijacking events per quarter
ITID-12836.notes: Scoped to session-token-level compromise specifically, distinct from credential-entry-point manipulation (ITID-12832, ITID-12833).

playbook.name: Response: Session/Cookie Injection
playbook.description: For an attacker injecting or fixating a session identifier/cookie value to hijack or force a victim into a known, attacker-controlled session (session fixation/injection).

steps.title: Confirm the injected/fixated session identifier
steps.desc: Review application logs for a session ID that was set prior to authentication (session fixation) or a cookie value manipulated in transit/via XSS.
steps.guidance: Check whether the application accepts an attacker-supplied session ID rather than always generating a new one on login.
steps.outcome: Confirmed technique and affected session(s).

steps.title: Invalidate the affected session(s)
steps.desc: Force-expire the specific session ID(s) involved immediately.
steps.outcome: Attacker's session access terminated.

steps.title: Fix session-management logic
steps.desc: Escalate to the application team to regenerate session IDs on privilege change/login and reject client-supplied session identifiers, as an emergency fix if actively exploitable.
steps.outcome: Session fixation vulnerability closed.

steps.title: Verify fix and re-test
steps.desc: Confirm the application now always issues a fresh session ID at authentication.
steps.outcome: Fixation no longer possible.

steps.title: Document finding
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability class and remediation for secure-coding reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine which account/session was compromised
steps.desc: Identify the victim account tied to the hijacked/fixated session and what access the attacker obtained.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of compromise.

steps.title: Reset credentials for the affected account
steps.desc: Force a password reset for the victim account as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Account secured.

ITID-12837.def: A browser extension, installed by the user (maliciously disguised or later compromised via a supply-chain update), that uses its granted browser API permissions to intercept form input, read/modify page content, or exfiltrate credentials/session tokens.
ITID-12837.purpose: Captures credential interception or injection performed via a malicious or compromised browser extension.
scopeIncludes: Malicious browser extension harvesting credentials entered into any visited login form via its content-script permissions
Legitimate extension compromised via a supply-chain attack (malicious update) later used to harvest credentials
scopeExcludes: Malware hooking the browser process directly without an extension (see ITID-12832)
Autofill-mechanism exploitation not involving an extension (see ITID-12833)
ITID-12837.severity: High — extensions often have broad, standing access to all visited pages' content.
ITID-12837.escalation: Escalate immediately to endpoint security to remove the extension fleet-wide and rotate credentials for affected users.
indicators: Browser extension management/CASB tooling flags an extension with excessive permissions or known-malicious reputation
Threat intelligence report naming a specific extension/publisher as compromised or malicious
vectors: Malicious extension distributed via an official web store disguised as a legitimate utility
Legitimate extension's update mechanism compromised (supply-chain attack) to push malicious code to existing installs
rootCauses: No enterprise browser extension allow-listing/governance policy
Users permitted to install extensions from official stores without security review
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Enterprise browser extension allow-listing/governance policy
Browser management tooling to detect and remove unauthorized/malicious extensions fleet-wide
ITID-12837.detection: Enterprise browser management/CASB tooling providing extension inventory and reputation scoring gives a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12837.response: Remove the malicious extension fleet-wide immediately and rotate credentials for all users who had it installed during the compromise window.
metrics: Count of malicious/high-risk extensions identified and removed per quarter
ITID-12837.notes: Scoped to the browser-extension delivery mechanism specifically, distinct from process-level browser-hooking malware (ITID-12832).

playbook.name: Response: Credential Injection via Malicious Browser Extension
playbook.description: For a malicious or compromised browser extension that injects content into login forms or intercepts/injects credentials as the user authenticates.

steps.title: Identify the malicious extension
steps.desc: Investigate the reporting user's browser for installed extensions, cross-referencing against known-malicious extension IDs or unusual permission grants (e.g. 'read and change all data on websites').
steps.guidance: Check EDR/browser management console for extension inventory across the fleet, not just the one reporting user.
steps.outcome: Malicious extension identified and its fleet-wide install footprint determined.

steps.title: Force-remove the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Push a policy to block/remove the extension across all managed browsers.
steps.outcome: Extension removed from all affected endpoints.

steps.title: Add the extension to a permanent blocklist
steps.desc: Add the extension ID/publisher to the organization's permanent extension blocklist policy.
steps.outcome: Extension permanently blocked from installation.

steps.title: Review extension allowlisting policy
steps.desc: Assess whether moving to an extension allowlist model would reduce future risk.
steps.outcome: Policy recommendation made.

steps.title: Document scope and remediation
steps.desc: Record affected user count, data exposure, and the extension governance improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Determine what was captured
steps.desc: Assess what credentials/sessions the extension had access to inject into or exfiltrate from, based on its permissions and observed behavior.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure documented.

steps.title: Reset credentials for all affected users
steps.desc: Force password resets and session revocation for every account used on a browser with the extension installed.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated across all affected users.

ITID-12838.def: Manipulation of API request parameters, headers, or object identifiers (e.g. a trusted internal header, a role/permission parameter, an IDOR-style user-ID parameter) to bypass or subvert the authentication or authorization check on an API endpoint, without exploiting SQL/LDAP injection specifically.
ITID-12838.purpose: Captures authentication bypass achieved by manipulating API request parameters or headers rather than the credential fields themselves.
scopeIncludes: Manipulation of a client-supplied header the backend incorrectly trusts as an authentication signal (e.g. X-User-Role, X-Internal-Request)
Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)-style parameter tampering to assume another user's authenticated context
scopeExcludes: SQL injection-based authentication bypass (see ITID-12834)
LDAP injection-based authentication bypass (see ITID-12835)
ITID-12838.severity: High — often grants direct impersonation or privilege escalation with minimal attacker sophistication required.
ITID-12838.escalation: Immediate escalation to application security engineering to patch the parameter/header trust flaw.
indicators: API security testing/DAST finding confirming a trusted-header or IDOR-style bypass
Anomalous API request patterns showing systematic parameter/ID manipulation (e.g. sequential user-ID iteration)
vectors: Client-supplied header naively trusted by the backend as an internal/authenticated signal
Sequential or predictable object-ID parameters allowing an authenticated but low-privilege user to access another user's data/session context
rootCauses: Backend authorization logic relying on client-controllable input (headers, parameters) rather than server-side session state
No object-level authorization check (broken object-level authorization) on API endpoints
controls: Server-side authorization checks independent of client-controllable headers/parameters
API security testing (DAST/SAST) specifically covering broken object-level authorization
ITID-12838.detection: API gateway/WAF anomaly detection for parameter tampering patterns (sequential IDs, unexpected header values) provides a real, concrete technical signal.
ITID-12838.response: Patch the authorization logic immediately, audit for prior unauthorized access enabled by the flaw, and notify affected users if data was exposed.
metrics: Count of parameter/header-based bypass attempts blocked per quarter
ITID-12838.notes: Scoped to parameter/header manipulation as the technique, distinct from SQL (ITID-12834) and LDAP (ITID-12835) injection.

playbook.name: Response: API Parameter/Header Injection for Authentication Bypass
playbook.description: For an attacker manipulating API request parameters or headers (e.g. a trusted internal header, JWT claim, or role parameter) to bypass authentication or escalate privilege.

steps.title: Confirm the manipulated parameter/header
steps.desc: Review API gateway/application logs for the specific header or parameter manipulated (e.g. X-User-Role, an unverified JWT claim, an IDOR-style user-id parameter) and the endpoint targeted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vector and affected endpoint.

steps.title: Block the source and/or the vulnerable endpoint
steps.desc: Block the source IP at the API gateway/WAF; if actively exploitable and severe, temporarily disable the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation stopped.

steps.title: Fix server-side authorization enforcement
steps.desc: Escalate to the API team to enforce authorization checks server-side rather than trusting client-supplied headers/parameters, as an emergency fix.
steps.guidance: The core fix is: never trust client-supplied identity/role data without independent server-side verification.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable authorization logic fixed and deployed.

steps.title: Verify fix and re-test
steps.desc: Re-test the endpoint with the original manipulated parameter/header after the fix.
steps.outcome: Bypass no longer possible.

steps.title: Document as a critical finding
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend an API security review for similar trust-boundary issues across other endpoints.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; broader API review initiated.

steps.title: Determine the access level obtained
steps.desc: Establish exactly what access or data the manipulated request granted the attacker.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of unauthorized access.

steps.title: Revoke any tokens/sessions obtained
steps.desc: Invalidate any API tokens or sessions established via the bypass.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access terminated.

ITID-12839.def: A confirmed case where a credential injection technique (via any of the technique-specific siblings in this Type) directly resulted in confirmed unauthorized authenticated access, as distinct from a blocked or unsuccessful attempt.
ITID-12839.purpose: Captures the confirmed-successful outcome of a credential injection attack — where the technique directly resulted in a confirmed authentication bypass.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed unauthorized account access or session establishment following a successful injection technique
Post-incident forensic confirmation that an injection attempt bypassed authentication and reached authenticated functionality
scopeExcludes: Blocked or unsuccessful injection attempts with no confirmed authentication bypass (tracked under the relevant technique-specific sibling)
ITID-12839.severity: Critical — represents confirmed realized impact rather than an attempted or blocked exploitation.
ITID-12839.escalation: Immediate escalation to full incident response; treat as a confirmed compromise requiring scope assessment across all data/functionality reachable from the bypassed authentication point.
indicators: Confirmed anomalous authenticated activity immediately following an injection attempt of any technique
Forensic log analysis confirming the injection payload succeeded in bypassing the authentication check
vectors: Any of the sibling techniques in this Type (SQL injection, LDAP injection, session hijacking, parameter/header manipulation, browser-based injection) culminating in confirmed unauthorized access
rootCauses: Underlying technique-specific root cause (root-caused under the originating sibling ITID, not duplicated here)
controls: Full incident response activation for confirmed injection-based compromise
Post-incident review feeding back into the specific technique's control gap and emergency patching
ITID-12839.detection: Combines the technique-specific detection from the originating sibling with confirmed post-bypass activity evidence in application and identity logs.
ITID-12839.response: Full incident response: contain, assess the scope of unauthorized access, patch the originating vulnerability on an emergency basis, and notify affected parties as required.
metrics: Count of confirmed credential injection compromises per year
ITID-12839.notes: This leaf documents confirmed realized outcomes specifically; the enabling technique is root-caused under its specific sibling ITID (ITID-12832 through ITID-12838) to avoid duplicating root-cause detail.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Credential Injection Attack with Confirmed Bypass
playbook.description: For a confirmed incident where a credential-injection technique successfully bypassed authentication and resulted in unauthorized access, regardless of the specific injection method used.

steps.title: Confirm the bypass and reconstruct the attack chain
steps.desc: Establish exactly which injection technique was used, the endpoint/system affected, and the account/role the attacker obtained.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against the technique-specific ITID (SQLi, LDAP, session, API parameter, etc.) for detailed context if not already classified.
steps.outcome: Complete, documented attack chain.

steps.title: Revoke all access obtained and block the source
steps.desc: Terminate every session/token obtained via the bypass and block the attacker's source infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Check for persistence established during access
steps.desc: Review the compromised account and any downstream systems for attacker-added persistence.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected accounts with verification and monitoring
steps.desc: Reset credentials for affected accounts through verified channels and place them under elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Accounts restored securely with monitoring in place.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the full chain, notify stakeholders per policy, and confirm the vulnerability fix is verified in production.
steps.outcome: Post-incident review completed and remediation confirmed.

steps.title: Determine what the attacker did with access
steps.desc: Review activity logs for the compromised account/session since the point of bypass to identify data accessed, actions taken, or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker activity documented.

steps.title: Contain the vulnerable system if still exploitable
steps.desc: If the injection vulnerability is not yet patched, take the affected endpoint offline or restrict access until an emergency fix is deployed.
steps.guidance: Escalate this decision to the application/service owner given business impact.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable system contained pending patch.

steps.title: Deploy the emergency patch and remove persistence
steps.desc: Deploy the fix for the specific injection vulnerability and remove any confirmed attacker-established persistence.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability closed; no attacker foothold remains.

ITID-12911.def: An incident involving a rogue or spoofed authentication system used to trick a human into authenticating against attacker-controlled infrastructure, not yet matched to a more specific leaf (e.g. evil-twin Wi-Fi, rogue DHCP/DNS, rogue IdP, rogue VPN gateway, captive portal, or a compromised legitimate system).
ITID-12911.purpose: Catch-all for cases that do not fit the more specific Rogue Authentication System leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to identify which infrastructure was spoofed
Reports of a suspected rogue authentication prompt where the underlying vector has not yet been confirmed
