steps.abort: If on a personal, non-managed device/account, remote remediation typically isn't possible — proceed to Legal for external options.

steps.title: Assess and notify affected employees if required
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy/HR to determine breach-notification obligations to the affected employees, given this is internal personal data.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and, if applicable, executed.

steps.title: Document the case and review HR-system access controls
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and assess whether HRIS access needs tighter least-privilege controls, DLP, or audit logging.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off; control improvement recommended if a gap is identified.

steps.title: Loop in HR leadership and Legal before proceeding further
steps.desc: Given the sensitivity of HR data and possible involvement of HR-system credentials, escalate to senior HR leadership (not just the individual's direct manager) and Legal.
steps.guidance: Handle with heightened discretion — this case involves the personal data of many other employees.
steps.outcome: Senior HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict HR-system access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the individual's access to HRIS and related systems.
steps.outcome: Further access prevented.

ITID-13114.def: A trusted insider's deliberate, unauthorized copying or removal of organizational data not clearly matching a more specific Data Theft leaf.
ITID-13114.purpose: Catch-all for malicious insider data theft that does not clearly fit the customer-data, IP, or HR-record leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific data class is confirmed
Theft of internal data not fitting customer/IP/HR categories (e.g. internal strategy documents, vendor contracts)
scopeExcludes: Theft clearly matching ITID-13111 (customer PII/financial), ITID-13112 (IP/trade secrets), or ITID-13113 (HR records)
ITID-13114.severity: High; reassess and reclassify once the specific data class is confirmed.
ITID-13114.priority: P1 by default given the malicious-insider context, pending reclassification.
ITID-13114.escalation: Escalate to legal and HR for investigation; reclassify to a more specific leaf once the data class is confirmed.
indicators: Anomalous data access/export by an insider with unclear data classification
vectors: Direct export or copying of data using legitimate access
rootCauses: Insufficient data classification to immediately determine the specific category stolen
controls: Data classification program
DLP and export monitoring
ITID-13114.detection: Same general DLP/audit-log telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-13114.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once the data class is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-13114.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Data Theft
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected insider data-theft incident not yet classified into a more specific category.

steps.title: Confirm the scope of data accessed and exported
steps.desc: Review DLP, database access logs, and file-server audit logs for the individual's account to establish what was accessed, copied, or transmitted.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal before broadly reviewing an employee's activity; scope the review to what is necessary.
steps.outcome: Documented, timestamped record of what data was accessed and where it went.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Image the employee's device and preserve relevant logs before any account action is taken, per this org's evidence-handling procedure.
steps.guidance: Do not tip off the employee before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved and logged.

steps.title: Determine if exfiltrated data is recoverable or revocable
steps.desc: Assess whether remote wipe, shared-link revocation, or cloud-storage takedown is possible for the destination of the stolen data.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether remote remediation is possible and executed where feasible.
steps.abort: If data left on a personal device or third-party service, remote remediation typically isn't possible — proceed to Legal for external options.

steps.title: Assess and execute any required breach notification
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to determine whether regulatory or customer notification obligations apply.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed on the required timeline.

steps.title: Document the case and review access-control gaps
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and assess whether tighter DLP rules, access reviews, or monitoring would have caught this earlier.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity and classification of the data involved
steps.desc: Determine whether the accessed data is regulated, trade-secret, or customer PII, which drives notification and legal obligations later.
steps.outcome: Data classification and potential regulatory exposure documented.

steps.title: Restrict account access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict access to sensitive systems, timed per HR/Legal guidance rather than immediately by default.
steps.guidance: Premature restriction can tip off the subject and cause evidence destruction; coordinate timing carefully.
steps.outcome: Further data access prevented at the agreed time.

steps.title: Loop in HR and Legal before proceeding further
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal that a suspected insider data-theft investigation is underway and request direction on scope and pace.
steps.guidance: SOC should not act unilaterally beyond initial evidence preservation.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and providing direction on next steps.

ITID-13121.def: A trusted insider's deliberate, unauthorized destructive action against IT systems, applications, or infrastructure — deleting data, disabling services, or planting destructive logic — motivated by grievance, retaliation, or personal gain.
ITID-13121.purpose: Captures a malicious insider deliberately damaging or disrupting IT systems or infrastructure, distinguishing insider-perpetrated sabotage from the same act by an external actor.
scopeIncludes: Deleting production data or backups with malicious intent
Disabling or misconfiguring security controls to cause an outage
Planting a logic bomb or destructive script triggered on a future condition
scopeExcludes: The same act performed by an external, unattributed actor (ITID-14611 series, Sabotage of Facilities — physical; or the relevant cyber-sabotage ITID elsewhere) — this leaf requires the actor to be a trusted insider
Insider sabotage of physical equipment/facilities specifically (ITID-13122)
Insider theft of data without a destructive/disruptive act (ITID-13111-13114)
ITID-13121.severity: High to Critical, depending on blast radius — an insider with legitimate access can cause damage far exceeding what an external attacker without that access could achieve as quickly.
ITID-13121.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT leadership, security, and HR; treat as an active incident requiring immediate access suspension.
indicators: Unexplained mass deletion of data or backups
Configuration changes disabling security controls with no change-ticket justification
Destructive script or scheduled task discovered with no legitimate business purpose
Sabotage timed shortly after a disciplinary action or before a known termination
vectors: Direct deletion/modification using legitimate administrative access
Planting a logic bomb or scheduled destructive task
Disabling backups or monitoring before the destructive act
rootCauses: Excessive standing administrative privilege with no just-in-time elevation
No change-control review for destructive/high-impact actions
No behavioral monitoring for privileged-account anomalies
controls: Just-in-time/least-privilege administrative access
Immutable/offline backups
Change-control review for destructive actions
Privileged-account behavioral monitoring
ITID-13121.detection: Backup-integrity monitoring, privileged-account activity logging, and change-control audit trails provide real technical signal here.
ITID-13121.response: Suspend the insider's access immediately, activate incident response and recovery from immutable backups, and preserve all activity logs for investigation.
metrics: Count of confirmed insider sabotage incidents per year
Recovery time from insider-caused outage
ITID-13121.notes: The differentiator from any externally-attributed sabotage elsewhere in the taxonomy is purely actor identity — a trusted insider using legitimate access, not a technique difference.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Sabotage of IT Systems/Infrastructure
playbook.description: An insider has intentionally disrupted, disabled, or damaged IT systems or infrastructure, such as deleting production data, disabling backups, or planting logic bombs.

steps.title: Identify the affected systems and the nature of the damage
steps.desc: Determine which systems were disrupted, what was deleted or altered, and whether the damage is ongoing (e.g., a scheduled logic bomb).
steps.guidance: Treat as a live incident — sabotage may recur on a timer.
steps.outcome: Scope of affected systems and damage type documented.

steps.title: Revoke privileged access immediately
steps.desc: Disable the individual's privileged/admin credentials across all systems to stop further damage, including any scheduled or dormant malicious code.
steps.guidance: Check for secondary/backdoor accounts the individual may have created.
steps.outcome: All privileged access for the individual revoked.

steps.title: Remove malicious changes and restore integrity
steps.desc: Remove any planted scripts, unauthorized changes, or malicious code, restoring configurations to a known-good baseline.
steps.outcome: Systems restored to a verified clean state.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and data from backup
steps.desc: Restore deleted or corrupted data and systems from verified clean backups, validating integrity before returning to production.
steps.outcome: Systems and data restored and validated.
steps.abort: If backups were also sabotaged, escalate to disaster-recovery procedures.

steps.title: Review privileged access controls and change-management gaps
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether separation-of-duties, change approval, or backup-integrity controls need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Trace the actions to the responsible account and timeline
steps.desc: Correlate admin/privileged account activity, change logs, and access times to identify who performed the sabotage and when.
steps.outcome: Responsible account and action timeline identified.

steps.title: Search for additional logic bombs, scheduled tasks, or backdoors
steps.desc: Review scheduled tasks, cron jobs, scripts, and recently modified system configs for additional planted malicious logic.
steps.outcome: No further latent sabotage mechanisms remain active.

steps.title: Loop in HR, Legal, and IT leadership immediately
steps.desc: Given active system damage, escalate immediately rather than waiting for full scoping.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal/leadership aware and directing next steps.

ITID-13122.def: A trusted insider's deliberate, unauthorized physical damage to organizational equipment, machinery, or facilities, motivated by grievance, retaliation, or personal gain.
ITID-13122.purpose: Captures a malicious insider deliberately damaging physical equipment or facilities, distinguishing insider-perpetrated physical sabotage from the same act by an external actor.
scopeIncludes: Deliberately damaging servers, network hardware, or other equipment
Physically disabling facility systems (HVAC, power, physical security hardware) with intent to harm the organization
Vandalism of company property by an employee/contractor
scopeExcludes: The same act performed by an external, unattributed actor (ITID-14611-14616, Sabotage of Facilities)
Insider sabotage of IT systems/infrastructure (ITID-13121)
ITID-13122.severity: Medium to High, depending on the criticality of the damaged equipment/facility.
ITID-13122.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, facilities, and HR; treat as an active incident requiring immediate access/badge suspension.
indicators: Physical damage to equipment discovered with no accidental explanation
Witness report of deliberate damage by an employee/contractor
Timing coinciding with a disciplinary action or known termination
vectors: Direct physical damage using legitimate facility access
Sabotage disguised as accidental damage or normal wear
rootCauses: No physical access review tied to disciplinary status
Insufficient camera coverage of equipment/critical facility areas
No process to revoke facility access promptly upon a disciplinary event
controls: Prompt facility-access revocation on disciplinary action
Camera coverage of critical equipment areas
Physical security incident reporting culture
ITID-13122.detection: Relies primarily on physical discovery and camera footage review — no network/endpoint telemetry applies to purely physical damage.
ITID-13122.response: Document the damage, preserve camera footage, suspend the individual's facility access, and coordinate with HR/legal on personnel action.
metrics: Count of confirmed insider physical sabotage incidents per year
ITID-13122.notes: No real MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — ATT&CK's Enterprise matrix covers cyber technique, not physical property damage; left empty rather than forcing a fit.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Sabotage of Physical Equipment or Facilities
playbook.description: An insider has intentionally damaged physical equipment, hardware, or facility infrastructure.

steps.title: Assess the physical damage and affected equipment/facilities
steps.desc: Work with facilities/physical security to document what equipment or infrastructure was damaged and the operational impact.
steps.outcome: Damage scope and operational impact documented.

steps.title: Restrict the individual's physical and system access
steps.desc: Suspend badge access and relevant system credentials per HR/Legal direction to prevent further damage.
steps.outcome: Further physical access prevented at the agreed time.

steps.title: Repair or replace damaged equipment
steps.desc: Coordinate repair, replacement, or vendor service for the damaged equipment or facility component.
steps.outcome: Equipment/facility restored to operational condition.

steps.title: Validate restored operations and file any insurance/police reports as required
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems/operations are functioning normally; involve law enforcement if warranted by Legal.
steps.outcome: Operations restored; required reports filed.

steps.title: Review physical security controls and access provisioning
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether badge-access scoping, monitoring, or facility controls need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Review badge access and CCTV to identify the responsible individual
steps.desc: Correlate badge-access logs and camera footage with the time of damage to identify who was present.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security; involve Legal before reviewing footage broadly.
steps.outcome: Responsible individual identified or narrowed down.

steps.title: Secure and document the damaged area/equipment as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the scene, photograph damage, and safeguard equipment for potential investigation or insurance claims.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved with chain of custody.

steps.title: Loop in HR, Legal, and Physical Security leadership
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal; physical sabotage may also warrant a facilities/safety risk assessment.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal/Physical Security aware and directing next steps.

ITID-13123.def: A trusted insider's deliberate sabotage — of IT systems, data, or physical equipment — carried out in the period immediately surrounding their resignation, termination, or notice of termination.
ITID-13123.purpose: Captures insider sabotage specifically timed to coincide with the insider's own departure or termination, a distinct risk window warranting its own tracking regardless of whether the sabotage itself is IT- or physically-focused.
scopeIncludes: Sabotage discovered to have occurred in the days/weeks around a resignation or termination
Destructive actions taken during a notice period before departure
Sabotage triggered to execute after the insider's departure (e.g. a time-delayed logic bomb)
scopeExcludes: Insider sabotage with no clear connection to departure timing (ITID-13121, ITID-13122)
ITID-13123.severity: High to Critical — departure-timed sabotage often targets maximum disruption specifically because the actor expects no further consequence.
ITID-13123.escalation: Escalate immediately; this pattern should also trigger a broader review of the departing employee's full access footprint for other planted risks.
indicators: Destructive activity within days of a resignation/termination notice
Access retained or used after the effective termination date
Time-delayed destructive logic discovered post-departure
vectors: Sabotage carried out during the notice period while access is still active
Time-delayed logic bomb set to trigger after departure
Access retained through an offboarding gap
rootCauses: No immediate access revocation upon resignation/termination notice
No elevated monitoring of departing employees during their notice period
Offboarding process gaps allowing residual access
controls: Immediate or accelerated access revocation on resignation/termination notice
Elevated monitoring of departing-employee activity
Offboarding checklist audit
ITID-13123.detection: Correlating HR departure events with privileged-account activity logs provides real, actionable technical signal here.
ITID-13123.response: Treat any departing-employee anomalous activity as high-priority; review the full access footprint of the departing individual for other planted risks.
metrics: Count of departure-timed sabotage incidents per year
Time from resignation/termination notice to access revocation
ITID-13123.notes: This leaf is organized around timing (departure window), not target type — it can co-occur with either ITID-13121 (IT) or ITID-13122 (physical); use this leaf when departure timing is the salient, reportable fact.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Sabotage Timed to Departure/Termination
playbook.description: An insider has sabotaged systems, data, or equipment timed around their resignation or termination, potentially including pre-planted actions set to trigger after departure.

steps.title: Determine the individual's departure timeline and access status
steps.desc: Establish resignation/termination date, notice period, and current access status to understand the window of risk.
steps.outcome: Departure timeline and access status documented.

steps.title: Immediately revoke all access if not already offboarded
steps.desc: Disable all accounts, VPN, and physical access for the individual without delay, including any accounts discovered outside standard offboarding.
steps.guidance: Check for accounts created outside the standard identity system.
steps.outcome: All access for the individual revoked.

steps.title: Remove malicious changes and validate system integrity
steps.desc: Remove any planted code or unauthorized changes and validate affected systems are in a known-good state.
steps.outcome: Systems verified clean.

steps.title: Restore any affected data or systems from backup
steps.desc: Restore any damaged data/systems from verified clean backups and validate integrity.
steps.outcome: Systems and data restored and validated.

steps.title: Review offboarding process and timing of access revocation
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether offboarding procedures need same-day access revocation, exit interviews, or heightened monitoring for departing staff.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with offboarding process improvements assigned.

steps.title: Review activity in the pre-departure window for anomalies
steps.desc: Audit access logs, data exports, and system changes made by the individual in the weeks leading up to and following their departure notice.
steps.guidance: Pay particular attention to scheduled tasks or delayed-trigger scripts.
steps.outcome: Anomalous pre-departure activity identified or ruled out.

steps.title: Search for delayed-trigger sabotage mechanisms
steps.desc: Review scheduled tasks, automation, service accounts, and code changes for time-delayed or trigger-based malicious logic left behind.
steps.outcome: No latent sabotage mechanisms remain active.

steps.title: Loop in HR and Legal immediately
steps.desc: Departure-timed sabotage is high risk; escalate immediately for coordinated response, especially if the individual retains any access.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

ITID-13124.def: A trusted insider's deliberate, unauthorized destructive or disruptive act not clearly matching a more specific Sabotage leaf.
ITID-13124.purpose: Catch-all for malicious insider sabotage that does not clearly fit the IT-systems, physical-equipment, or departure-timed leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific target (IT vs. physical) or timing pattern is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Sabotage clearly matching ITID-13121 (IT systems), ITID-13122 (physical equipment/facilities), or ITID-13123 (departure-timed)
ITID-13124.severity: High; reassess and reclassify once more detail is available.
ITID-13124.priority: P1 by default given the malicious-insider context, pending reclassification.
ITID-13124.escalation: Escalate immediately; reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
indicators: Report of insider-caused disruption with unclear target or timing
vectors: Destructive or disruptive action using legitimate access
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection to determine target/timing
controls: Insider-threat monitoring program
ITID-13124.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-13124.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-13124.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Sabotage
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected insider sabotage incident not yet classified into a more specific category (IT systems, physical, or departure-timed).

steps.title: Determine what was sabotaged and the current operational impact
steps.desc: Establish whether the sabotage affected IT systems, physical equipment, or both, and assess ongoing operational impact.
steps.outcome: Scope and impact of the sabotage documented.

steps.title: Restrict the individual's access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict system and physical access, timed per HR/Legal guidance to prevent further damage.
steps.outcome: Further sabotage prevented.

steps.title: Remove or repair the sabotage impact
steps.desc: Remove malicious changes/code or repair damaged equipment as applicable.
steps.outcome: Sabotage impact remediated.

steps.title: Validate restored systems/operations
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems or equipment are functioning normally before returning to standard operations.
steps.outcome: Operations confirmed restored.

steps.title: Document the case and review relevant controls
steps.desc: Record the timeline and assess whether access controls, monitoring, or physical security need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off.

steps.title: Identify the responsible individual and their access
steps.desc: Correlate logs, badge access, or witness reports to identify the responsible individual and what access/privileges they hold.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal before broadly reviewing an employee's activity.
steps.outcome: Responsible individual identified with documented access level.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Preserve logs, images, or physical evidence of the sabotage before remediation begins.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved.

steps.title: Loop in HR and Legal before proceeding further
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal that a suspected insider sabotage investigation is underway.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and providing direction.

ITID-13131.def: A trusted insider's deliberate, unauthorized sharing of their own valid account credentials with another person, granting that person access they should not have.
ITID-13131.purpose: Captures a malicious insider voluntarily sharing their own legitimate credentials with an unauthorized party for self-motivated reasons, as opposed to being paid or coerced by an external attacker.
scopeIncludes: Sharing login credentials with a friend, family member, or unauthorized colleague
Sharing credentials to let a terminated coworker retain informal access
Sharing credentials as a convenience or favor, with malicious insider intent to bypass access controls
scopeExcludes: Sharing credentials with an external attacker in exchange for payment (ITID-13511, Collusion — Collaboration with External Attackers)
Casual/negligent credential sharing with no malicious intent (this taxonomy's Negligent Insider branch covers accidental exposure, not deliberate sharing)
ITID-13131.severity: Medium to High, depending on the scope of access shared.
ITID-13131.escalation: Escalate to HR and security for investigation and access review upon discovery.
indicators: Login activity for one account from two clearly distinct, geographically inconsistent locations/devices with no travel explanation
A terminated or unauthorized individual observed performing actions attributable to an active employee's account
vectors: Direct sharing of username/password
Sharing an authenticated session or device
rootCauses: No monitoring for concurrent/anomalous session patterns on a single account
Weak organizational culture around credential-sharing norms
No individual accountability enforcement for shared-looking account activity
controls: Concurrent-session/anomalous-location alerting
Credential-sharing policy and awareness training
MFA tied to a registered individual device
ITID-13131.detection: Anomalous concurrent-session and impossible-travel alerting provides real technical signal here.
ITID-13131.response: Reset the shared credential, investigate the scope of unauthorized access granted, and take personnel action.
metrics: Count of confirmed malicious credential-sharing incidents per year
ITID-13131.notes: Written as a general definition of this Tier-4 concept since it is the lone Tier-5 child — no sibling to differentiate against. The real distinguishing line is against ITID-13511: payment/collusion with an external attacker escalates this from an insider-risk leaf to a Collusion-branch leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Credential Sharing (Malicious Context)
playbook.description: An insider has intentionally shared their credentials with an unauthorized party for malicious purposes.

steps.title: Confirm credential sharing and identify who received access
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for concurrent/anomalous logins, and interview evidence (e.g., reported by a colleague) to determine who the credentials were shared with and why.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal before broadly reviewing an employee's activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed sharing event with details on the unauthorized party and access granted.

steps.title: Reset the shared credentials and revoke active sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and terminate all active sessions for the compromised account immediately.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access via the shared credential terminated.

steps.title: Verify no persistent access was established by the unauthorized party
steps.desc: Check for new accounts, added MFA devices, forwarding rules, or other persistence created during the unauthorized access window.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Assess and notify affected parties if required
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to determine notification obligations if sensitive data was exposed.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed on the required timeline.

steps.title: Document the case and reinforce credential-sharing policy
steps.desc: Record the timeline and assess whether MFA, conditional access, or training gaps contributed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off.

steps.title: Determine what the unauthorized party accessed or did with the credentials
steps.desc: Review activity logs tied to the shared account for the period of unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Scope of unauthorized activity documented.

steps.title: Restrict the insider's broader access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the individual's access to sensitive systems pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized use prevented.

steps.title: Loop in HR and Legal before proceeding further
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal given the intentional and policy-violating nature of the sharing.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and providing direction.

ITID-13141.def: A trusted insider's sustained, deliberate collection and exfiltration of sensitive organizational information over time, typically directed or sponsored by an external party (a competitor, foreign government, or organized group) rather than a single opportunistic theft.
ITID-13141.purpose: Captures a malicious insider conducting sustained espionage — collecting and exfiltrating sensitive information on an ongoing basis, typically on behalf of an external sponsor — as distinct from a one-time, self-motivated data theft.
scopeIncludes: An insider recruited or directed by an external sponsor to systematically collect and exfiltrate information over an extended period
An insider maintaining an ongoing covert relationship with an external party to supply information
scopeExcludes: A one-time, self-motivated theft of source code/trade secrets with no external sponsor (ITID-13112)
A one-time theft of customer PII/financial records (ITID-13111)
Espionage conducted by a non-insider external actor (a separate espionage-domain ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy) — this leaf requires the actor to be a trusted insider
ITID-13141.severity: Critical — sustained, sponsored espionage represents the most severe insider-threat pattern, with potential national-security or major competitive implications.
ITID-13141.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and, where a foreign sponsor or national-security nexus is suspected, appropriate law enforcement/counterintelligence channels.
indicators: Pattern of repeated, low-and-slow data access/exfiltration over an extended period rather than a single bulk event
Unexplained foreign travel, contacts, or financial activity correlated with data access patterns
Long-term access retention or role-seeking behavior inconsistent with the individual's stated career interests
vectors: Recurring small-scale exfiltration timed to avoid volume-based DLP thresholds
Covert communication channels with an external handler
Deliberate pursuit of roles/access granting broader collection opportunity
rootCauses: No behavioral baseline sensitive to low-and-slow, sustained collection patterns (as opposed to single bulk-export detection)
Insufficient counterintelligence awareness/training for personnel in sensitive roles
No periodic re-vetting of personnel in high-sensitivity positions
controls: UEBA tuned for low-and-slow collection patterns, not just bulk-export thresholds
Periodic re-vetting for sensitive-role personnel
Counterintelligence awareness training
ITID-13141.detection: Requires longer-baseline UEBA specifically tuned to detect sustained, low-volume patterns — standard bulk-export DLP alerting is largely blind to this pattern by design.
ITID-13141.response: Engage legal and, where warranted, law enforcement/counterintelligence resources before taking overt action, to avoid tipping off a sponsored actor prematurely.
metrics: Count of confirmed insider espionage cases per year (expected to be rare)
Coverage of sensitive roles under low-and-slow behavioral monitoring
ITID-13141.notes: Written as a general definition of this Tier-4 concept since it is the lone Tier-5 child. The key differentiator from ITID-13111/13112 is sustained, externally-directed collection versus a single opportunistic theft — investigate any suspected case for a pattern, not just an event.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Espionage (Malicious Context)
playbook.description: An insider is suspected of acting on behalf of a competitor, foreign entity, or other third party to steal sensitive information, potentially warranting law enforcement or counterintelligence involvement.

steps.title: Confirm indicators of espionage activity
steps.desc: Review access to sensitive/strategic data, unusual contact patterns, travel, or data staging behavior consistent with espionage rather than opportunistic theft.
steps.guidance: Handle with extreme discretion; limit knowledge to a minimal need-to-know group.
steps.outcome: Documented indicators supporting or ruling out an espionage hypothesis.

steps.title: Restrict access to the most sensitive assets first, timed per Legal/law-enforcement guidance
steps.desc: Coordinate carefully-timed restriction of access to the most sensitive systems/data, balancing containment against evidentiary/investigative needs.
steps.guidance: Timing is typically dictated by Legal or law enforcement, not the SOC.
steps.outcome: Access to critical sensitive assets restricted at the agreed time.

steps.title: Fully revoke access and secure all affected systems
steps.desc: Once directed by Legal/law enforcement, fully revoke the individual's access and secure any exposed systems or data.
steps.outcome: Access fully revoked and systems secured.

steps.title: Assess broader exposure and notify affected stakeholders as directed
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine the scope of exposed sensitive/strategic information and any required notifications.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope assessed and notifications executed as directed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case at an appropriate classification level and review data-protection controls for sensitive/strategic assets.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with Legal/leadership sign-off; controls improvements assigned.

steps.title: Preserve evidence covertly without alerting the subject
steps.desc: Begin covert log and evidence preservation while avoiding any action that would tip off the individual.
steps.guidance: Overt containment too early can destroy evidence needed for prosecution or counterintelligence action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved without alerting the subject.

steps.title: Preserve full chain of custody for all collected evidence
steps.desc: Ensure all evidence collection follows a chain of custody suitable for potential criminal proceedings.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership; consider law enforcement/counterintelligence referral
steps.desc: Given the severity and potential national-security or highly-sensitive commercial implications, escalate to Legal and leadership at once; Legal should assess referral to law enforcement or counterintelligence authorities.
steps.guidance: Do not contact external authorities directly without Legal's coordination.
steps.outcome: Leadership and Legal engaged; referral decision documented.

ITID-13211.def: An employee's or contractor's unintentional exposure of sensitive organizational data — through misdirected communication, misconfiguration, or careless handling — with no malicious intent.
ITID-13211.purpose: Captures a negligent (non-malicious) insider's accidental exposure of sensitive data, as distinct from any deliberate theft or sabotage elsewhere in this domain.
scopeIncludes: Sending sensitive data to the wrong recipient by mistake
Misconfiguring a sharing setting causing broader-than-intended access
Leaving sensitive information visible/accessible through carelessness (e.g. an unlocked screen, a publicly-shared document link)
scopeExcludes: Deliberate, malicious data theft (ITID-13111-13114)
Deliberate policy violations (ITID-13221-13224) — this leaf is for an honest mistake, not a known rule broken
ITID-13211.severity: Low to Medium, scaling with the sensitivity and scope of the exposed data.
ITID-13211.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for high-sensitivity data or broad exposure.
ITID-13211.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal if regulated data (PII, financial, health) is involved, to assess notification obligations.
indicators: Self-reported mistake by the employee
Recipient or third party reporting receipt of misdirected sensitive information
Discovery via DLP of an unintended broad-sharing configuration
vectors: Autocomplete-driven wrong-recipient email/message
Overly permissive sharing link or folder setting
Unattended device or document in a non-secure area
rootCauses: No DLP outbound-content scanning for sensitive data
No default-to-restrictive sharing settings
Insufficient data-handling training
controls: Outbound DLP scanning with recipient-verification prompts
Default-restrictive sharing settings
Data-handling awareness training
ITID-13211.detection: DLP outbound-content scanning and sharing-configuration monitoring provide real technical signal here.
ITID-13211.response: Attempt to recall/revoke the exposed data where possible, assess actual exposure scope, and notify affected parties/regulators if thresholds are met.
metrics: Count of accidental exposure incidents per quarter
Percentage caught by DLP before external delivery
ITID-13211.notes: Written as a general definition of this Tier-4 concept since it is the lone Tier-5 child. No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is a non-adversarial human-error event, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Accidental Data Exposure (Negligent Insider Context)
playbook.description: An employee has unintentionally exposed sensitive data through error, such as misconfigured sharing settings, misdirected email, or an accidental public upload. This is a corrective, non-punitive response.

steps.title: Identify what data was exposed and to whom
steps.desc: Determine the exact data exposed, the exposure mechanism (e.g., misdirected email, public share link, open storage bucket), and who could have accessed it.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of the exposure.

steps.title: Revoke sharing and restrict further access immediately
steps.desc: Disable the public link, correct sharing permissions, or recall the misdirected communication as soon as identified.
steps.guidance: Act quickly — this is a corrective action, not a disciplinary one.
steps.outcome: Exposure vector closed.

steps.title: Confirm no copies remain outside authorized locations
steps.desc: Verify whether the exposed data was cached, indexed by search engines, or downloaded by third parties, and pursue takedown if needed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual unauthorized copies remain, or takedown initiated.

steps.title: Assess notification obligations with Legal/Privacy
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposure triggers regulatory or customer notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed on the required timeline.

steps.title: Identify process/training improvements to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Document the case and focus recommendations on sharing-permission defaults, DLP rules, or training — not discipline.
steps.guidance: Keep the tone corrective; this was an accident.
steps.outcome: Process or training improvement identified and assigned.

steps.title: Determine actual access, not just exposure window
steps.desc: Check access logs to see whether the data was actually viewed/downloaded by anyone during the exposure window, or if it was exposed but not accessed.
steps.outcome: Actual access (if any) confirmed, narrowing the real-world impact.

steps.title: Confirm with the employee what happened, in a supportive manner
steps.desc: Speak with the employee to understand the sequence of events; approach as fact-finding, not blame-assigning.
steps.guidance: Frame the conversation around understanding the process gap, not punishing the individual.
steps.outcome: Clear understanding of how the error occurred.

ITID-13221.def: An employee's use of a third-party application, cloud service, or tool for organizational work without going through IT/security approval or procurement.
ITID-13221.purpose: Captures an employee's use of an unapproved third-party tool or service (shadow IT) for work purposes, a common negligent policy violation with real data-governance risk.
scopeIncludes: Using a personal cloud-storage account for work files
Adopting an unapproved SaaS tool for team collaboration
Using an unsanctioned AI tool with organizational data
scopeExcludes: Storing sensitive data in an unauthorized location within an otherwise-approved tool (ITID-13222 — a data-handling violation rather than a tool-approval one)
Deliberate personal use unrelated to work (ITID-13223)
ITID-13221.severity: Low to Medium, scaling with the sensitivity of data placed into the unapproved tool.
ITID-13221.escalation: Escalate to security/IT governance for risk assessment of the specific tool; escalate further if sensitive data was involved.
indicators: Discovery via CASB/network monitoring of traffic to an unsanctioned SaaS domain
Employee self-disclosure during an audit or incident review
Expense report or procurement request referencing an unapproved tool
vectors: Direct sign-up and use of a consumer/unmanaged SaaS tool
Browser extension or add-in installation without IT review
rootCauses: No CASB or SaaS-discovery tooling
Slow or unclear approved-tool procurement process driving workarounds
Insufficient policy awareness training
controls: CASB/SaaS discovery and governance
Streamlined tool-approval process
Policy awareness training
ITID-13221.detection: CASB and network-traffic analysis for unsanctioned SaaS domains provide real technical signal here.
ITID-13221.response: Assess the data exposure risk of the tool used, migrate data to an approved alternative, and coach the employee on policy.
metrics: Count of discovered shadow-IT tools per quarter
Percentage remediated (migrated or approved) within SLA
ITID-13221.notes: Distinguished from ITID-13222 by focus: this leaf is about using an unapproved tool at all, while 13222 is about mishandling data within tools (approved or not).

playbook.name: Response: Unapproved Third-Party Tool/Shadow IT Usage
playbook.description: An employee is using an unapproved third-party tool or service to handle company data, a policy violation typically arising from convenience rather than malice. Corrective response.

steps.title: Identify the tool and what data it touches
steps.desc: Determine which unapproved tool/service is in use, what company data has been uploaded or processed through it, and how widely it's used.
steps.outcome: Tool identified with a documented data-exposure footprint.

steps.title: Restrict or block further use of the unapproved tool
steps.desc: Block the service at the network/CASB level or disable the account, and migrate any active workflows off it.
steps.outcome: Further data flow to the unapproved tool stopped.

steps.title: Remove or retrieve company data from the third-party tool
steps.desc: Export/delete company data from the unapproved service and confirm the vendor has no ongoing retention obligation issue.
steps.outcome: Company data removed from the unapproved service where possible.
steps.abort: If the vendor won't cooperate, escalate to Legal for a data-processing/removal request.

steps.title: Provide or fast-track an approved alternative
steps.desc: Work with IT to provide an approved tool that meets the legitimate business need identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Approved alternative in place, reducing incentive to reuse shadow IT.

steps.title: Update policy awareness and tool-approval process
steps.desc: Document the case and recommend training or a faster tool-approval pathway to reduce future shadow IT adoption.
steps.guidance: Keep tone corrective and process-focused.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with process improvement assigned.

steps.title: Understand why the tool was adopted
steps.desc: Talk to the employee/team to understand the business need the unapproved tool was filling.
steps.guidance: Approach as fact-finding; shadow IT often reflects an unmet tooling need.
steps.outcome: Underlying business need documented.

ITID-13222.def: An employee's placement of sensitive organizational data into a storage location — approved or unapproved tool — that is not authorized for that data's classification level.
ITID-13222.purpose: Captures an employee storing sensitive data in an unauthorized location, distinct from using an unapproved tool entirely.
scopeIncludes: Storing regulated data in a general-purpose file share not approved for that classification
Saving confidential documents to a personal drive within an otherwise-approved productivity suite
Copying sensitive data to an unencrypted removable drive
scopeExcludes: Using an unapproved third-party tool entirely (ITID-13221)
ITID-13222.severity: Low to Medium, scaling with data sensitivity and exposure scope.
ITID-13222.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for regulated data.
ITID-13222.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal if regulated data is involved.
indicators: DLP alert on sensitive data detected in an unauthorized location
Data-classification audit finding
vectors: Direct save/copy of sensitive data to a non-approved location
Convenience-driven data movement without regard to classification policy
rootCauses: No DLP scanning of internal storage locations
Unclear or hard-to-follow data classification policy
No enforced classification-to-location mapping
mitreTechniques: T1537 Transfer Data to Cloud Account
controls: Internal DLP scanning across storage locations
Enforced classification-to-storage-location policy
Data classification training
ITID-13222.detection: Internal DLP scanning of file shares/drives provides real technical signal here.
ITID-13222.response: Move the data to an approved location, assess exposure, and coach the employee on classification policy.
metrics: Count of misplaced-data findings per quarter
Time to remediation
ITID-13222.notes: Scoped to storage-location mismatches specifically; a tool-approval violation belongs at ITID-13221 even if it also happens to involve sensitive data.

playbook.name: Response: Data Handling Policy Violation (Storing Sensitive Data in Unauthorized Location)
playbook.description: An employee has stored sensitive data in an unauthorized location (e.g., personal cloud drive, unencrypted USB, local workstation) in violation of data-handling policy. Corrective response.

steps.title: Identify the data and the unauthorized storage location
steps.desc: Determine what sensitive data was stored, where, and for how long, using DLP alerts or endpoint scanning results.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of misplaced data and its location.

steps.title: Remove the data from the unauthorized location
steps.desc: Delete or securely wipe the sensitive data from the unauthorized location, retaining a copy in the authorized system if needed.
steps.outcome: Sensitive data no longer resident in the unauthorized location.

steps.title: Confirm no further copies or synced backups remain
steps.desc: Check for cloud-sync backups, browser caches, or other residual copies of the data outside authorized systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual copies remain.

steps.title: Confirm the employee has a compliant way to do their work
steps.desc: Verify the employee has access to the approved, compliant storage location for the workflow they were trying to accomplish.
steps.outcome: Compliant workflow confirmed available.

steps.title: Reinforce data-handling training and DLP coverage
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether DLP rules should be expanded or data-handling training refreshed.
steps.guidance: Keep tone corrective, not punitive.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with training/DLP improvement assigned.

steps.title: Assess exposure risk of the unauthorized location
steps.desc: Determine whether the location was accessible to others (e.g., shared personal drive, unencrypted removable media) versus purely local and private.
steps.outcome: Exposure risk level determined.

ITID-13223.def: An employee's use of organizational systems, accounts, or resources for personal, non-work purposes in violation of the acceptable use policy.
ITID-13223.purpose: Captures an employee's personal use of corporate systems in violation of acceptable use policy, a lower-severity but common policy-violation pattern.
scopeIncludes: Using a corporate email account for significant personal business
Excessive personal internet/streaming use on corporate devices
Running a personal side business using company resources
scopeExcludes: Use of an unapproved third-party tool for work purposes (ITID-13221) — this leaf is about non-work use of approved/corporate resources
ITID-13223.severity: Low — typically an HR/conduct matter rather than a security incident, unless it introduces a real technical risk (e.g. malware exposure from personal browsing).
ITID-13223.escalation: Escalate to HR for routine policy enforcement; escalate to security only if a technical risk (malware, data exposure) resulted.
indicators: Web-filtering/DLP telemetry showing significant personal-use patterns
Manager or peer report
vectors: Direct personal use of provisioned accounts/devices
rootCauses: Unclear or unenforced acceptable use policy
No web-filtering/usage monitoring
controls: Acceptable use policy with periodic acknowledgment
Web-filtering/usage monitoring
ITID-13223.detection: Web-filtering and usage-monitoring telemetry provide the technical signal here, though this is routinely an HR-led, not security-led, matter.
ITID-13223.response: Refer to HR for standard policy enforcement; document for pattern tracking.
metrics: Count of acceptable-use violations referred to HR per quarter
ITID-13223.notes: This is the lowest-severity leaf in the Policy Violations group — most instances are routine HR matters, not security incidents; log for pattern visibility rather than heavy investigation.

playbook.name: Response: Acceptable Use Policy Violation (Personal Use of Corporate Systems)
playbook.description: An employee has used corporate systems for personal purposes in a manner that violates acceptable use policy, without malicious intent. Corrective response.

steps.title: Confirm the nature and extent of the personal use
steps.desc: Review the alert/report details (e.g., web filtering, endpoint logs) to confirm what personal use occurred and its extent.
steps.outcome: Documented description and extent of the personal use.

steps.title: Address any resulting security risk
steps.desc: Remediate any malware, unwanted software, or exposure that resulted from the personal use, if applicable.
steps.outcome: Any resulting security risk remediated.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized software or content if present
steps.desc: Uninstall any unauthorized personal software or remove personal content stored on corporate systems.
steps.outcome: Corporate systems returned to a compliant state.

steps.title: Refer to HR/management for standard policy reminder
steps.desc: Hand off to the employee's manager or HR for a standard acceptable-use policy reminder, per normal process.
steps.guidance: This is typically a routine HR/manager conversation, not a security escalation.
steps.outcome: Manager/HR informed and handling any employee conversation.

steps.title: Note any pattern for policy or filtering improvement
steps.desc: Document the case briefly; if this reflects a broader pattern, consider whether web-filtering policy needs adjustment.
steps.guidance: Keep tone light and corrective — this is a minor, common violation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Assess whether any security risk resulted from the use
steps.desc: Determine whether the personal use introduced any security risk (e.g., malware from a personal download, credential reuse on a personal site).
steps.outcome: Security risk, if any, identified and documented.

ITID-13224.def: An employee's violation of organizational security or IT policy not clearly matching a more specific Policy Violations leaf.
ITID-13224.purpose: Catch-all for negligent policy violations that do not fit the shadow-IT, data-handling, or acceptable-use leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the specific policy area is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Violations clearly matching ITID-13221 (shadow IT), ITID-13222 (data handling), or ITID-13223 (acceptable use)
ITID-13224.severity: Low; reassess once the specific policy area is confirmed.
ITID-13224.escalation: Reclassify once the specific policy violated is clarified.
indicators: Report of a policy violation with unclear specific category
vectors: Policy-non-compliant activity of unclear type
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: General security policy awareness training
ITID-13224.detection: Relies on the same reporting/monitoring channels as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-13224.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-13224.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Policy Violation
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a negligent-insider policy violation not yet classified into a more specific category (shadow IT, data handling, or acceptable use). Corrective response.

steps.title: Confirm the nature of the policy violation
steps.desc: Review the alert or report to determine which policy was violated and what systems/data were involved.
steps.outcome: Documented description of the violation.

steps.title: Address any resulting exposure or risk
steps.desc: Take corrective action to close any exposure created by the violation (e.g., revoke access, remove data, disable a tool).
steps.outcome: Any resulting exposure closed.

steps.title: Verify the environment is returned to a compliant state
steps.desc: Confirm systems/data are back in compliance with policy.
steps.outcome: Compliant state confirmed.

steps.title: Refer to manager/HR for standard policy reminder
steps.desc: Hand off to the employee's manager or HR for a standard policy conversation, per normal process.
steps.guidance: Keep this routine unless the violation reveals a larger security issue.
steps.outcome: Manager/HR informed.

steps.title: Document the case and note any policy clarity gaps
steps.desc: Record the case; if the policy itself was ambiguous or hard to follow, flag it for review.
steps.guidance: Keep tone corrective, not punitive.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Assess whether any security or data-exposure risk resulted
steps.desc: Determine whether the violation created any actual security exposure, or whether it is a procedural violation with no exposure.
steps.outcome: Risk level determined.

ITID-13231.def: An organizational laptop or mobile device reported lost by its user, with no evidence suggesting deliberate theft.
ITID-13231.purpose: Captures a lost laptop or mobile device with no indication of theft, distinguishing simple loss from a stolen-device scenario for response and notification purposes.
scopeIncludes: A device misplaced in transit, at a location, or at home with no theft indicators
A device that is later recovered unaltered
scopeExcludes: A device confirmed or strongly suspected to have been stolen (ITID-14211/ITID-14223, Device Theft under the Physical Security Breaches domain) — file there instead once theft is indicated
A device left unattended in public and never recovered (ITID-13232 — a related but distinct pattern warranting its own tracking)
ITID-13231.severity: Medium — risk depends heavily on whether the device was encrypted and whether it held sensitive data.
ITID-13231.priority: P2 for an unencrypted device with sensitive data; P3 otherwise.
ITID-13231.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately to trigger remote wipe/lock where supported; escalate to privacy/legal if unencrypted regulated data was present.
indicators: User self-report of a lost device
Device-management console showing the device offline/unreachable
vectors: N/A — this is a loss event, not an adversary-initiated attack, though a lost unencrypted device creates a real subsequent data-exposure risk
rootCauses: No full-disk encryption mandate on portable devices
No mobile device management (MDM) remote-wipe capability
No prompt loss-reporting culture/process
controls: Mandatory full-disk encryption on all portable devices
MDM with remote lock/wipe capability
Prompt loss-reporting policy
ITID-13231.detection: MDM device-status monitoring provides the technical signal; actual loss detection relies on user self-report.
ITID-13231.response: Trigger remote lock/wipe immediately, assess data exposure risk based on encryption status, and document for asset-management purposes.
metrics: Count of lost devices per quarter
Percentage of fleet under full-disk encryption
Time from loss report to remote wipe
ITID-13231.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — a lost device is a loss event, not an adversary technique, though it does create downstream exposure risk if unencrypted.

playbook.name: Response: Lost Laptop/Mobile Device (No Theft Indicated)
playbook.description: An employee has lost a corporate laptop or mobile device with no indication of theft. Corrective, device-recovery-focused response.

steps.title: Confirm the device, its encryption status, and last known data on it
steps.desc: Identify the specific device, confirm whether full-disk encryption was enabled, and determine what sensitive data resided on it.
steps.outcome: Device profile and data exposure risk documented.

steps.title: Lock the device and revoke associated session tokens
steps.desc: Remotely lock the device via MDM and revoke any active session tokens or cached credentials associated with it.
steps.outcome: Device locked and sessions revoked, preventing unauthorized use.

steps.title: Remote-wipe the device if not recovered within a reasonable window
steps.desc: Trigger a remote wipe via MDM if the device is not located within the organization's defined grace period.
steps.guidance: If disk encryption was confirmed enabled, wipe urgency is lower but still recommended.
steps.outcome: Device wiped of corporate data.
steps.abort: If the device cannot be reached (offline), the wipe will queue and execute on next connection — monitor for completion.

steps.title: Reissue a replacement device and reset any exposed credentials
steps.desc: Provision a replacement device and reset any credentials that may have been cached on the lost device.
steps.outcome: Employee back to productive work with fresh credentials.

steps.title: Confirm encryption/MDM enrollment baseline and reinforce device-handling guidance
steps.desc: Document the case and verify all corporate devices meet the encryption/MDM baseline; note if not.
steps.guidance: Keep tone corrective — losing a device happens to well-intentioned employees.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with any baseline gaps flagged.

steps.title: Attempt to locate the device
steps.desc: Use MDM/find-my-device tooling to attempt to locate the device before assuming it is unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Device located and recovered, or confirmed unrecoverable.

ITID-13232.def: An organizational device left unattended by its user in a public place (a cafe, airport, public transit, etc.) and subsequently not recovered.
ITID-13232.purpose: Captures a device left unattended in a public location and never recovered, a higher-risk pattern than a briefly-misplaced device given the extended, unrecoverable exposure window.
scopeIncludes: A device left behind in a public venue and never located again
A device confirmed unattended for an extended period before the loss was even noticed
scopeExcludes: A briefly misplaced device with no extended unattended public exposure, especially if later recovered (ITID-13231)
ITID-13232.severity: Medium to High — an extended, unrecoverable public loss carries a materially higher exposure risk than a briefly misplaced device.
ITID-13232.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately for remote wipe/lock; escalate to privacy/legal if unencrypted regulated data was present.
indicators: User self-report describing an extended unattended period in a public location
Device-management console showing the device offline for an extended period
vectors: N/A — this is a loss event; the risk is a third party finding and accessing the device before it can be remotely wiped
rootCauses: No full-disk encryption mandate
No MDM remote-wipe capability
Insufficient employee training on device custody in public spaces
controls: Mandatory full-disk encryption
MDM with remote lock/wipe
Employee training on public-space device custody
ITID-13232.detection: MDM device-status monitoring provides the technical signal; the loss itself relies on user self-report, often delayed given the public setting.
ITID-13232.response: Trigger remote lock/wipe immediately, assume a materially higher chance of third-party access than a briefly-misplaced device, and assess data exposure accordingly.
metrics: Count of unrecovered public-location device losses per quarter
ITID-13232.notes: Distinguished from ITID-13231 by the extended, unrecoverable public exposure window, which materially raises the realistic likelihood of unauthorized access.

playbook.name: Response: Device Left Unattended in Public Location and Not Recovered
playbook.description: An employee left a corporate device unattended in a public location (e.g., cafe, airport, rideshare) and it was not recovered. Corrective, device-recovery-focused response.

steps.title: Gather details of the last known location and circumstances
steps.desc: Establish where and when the device was left, and what data/sessions were active on it at the time.
steps.outcome: Circumstances and exposure window documented.

steps.title: Lock the device and revoke associated session tokens/credentials
steps.desc: Remotely lock the device and revoke any active sessions, VPN tokens, or cached credentials tied to it.
steps.outcome: Device locked and access revoked.

steps.title: Remote-wipe the device
steps.desc: Trigger a remote wipe via MDM once recovery is deemed unlikely, given the public/unattended nature of the loss.
steps.outcome: Device wiped of corporate data.
steps.abort: If the device cannot be reached, the wipe will queue and execute on next connection — monitor for completion.

steps.title: Reissue a replacement device and reset exposed credentials
steps.desc: Provision a replacement device and reset any credentials or tokens that may have been cached on the device.
steps.outcome: Employee back to productive work with fresh credentials.

steps.title: Reinforce guidance on securing devices in public spaces
steps.desc: Document the case and consider whether device-security training or screen-lock timeout policy needs reinforcement.
steps.guidance: Keep tone corrective and supportive.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with training recommendation if appropriate.

steps.title: Attempt to locate the device and check for any access attempts since it went missing
steps.desc: Use MDM find-my-device tooling and review authentication logs for any suspicious access attempts using cached credentials or sessions from the device.
steps.outcome: Device location attempted; any suspicious access identified.

ITID-13233.def: A lost or stolen organizational device incident not clearly matching a more specific Lost or Stolen Devices leaf.
ITID-13233.purpose: Catch-all for lost or stolen device incidents that do not clearly fit the no-theft-indicated or unrecovered-public-loss leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before it is clear whether theft is indicated or the device was recovered
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-13231 (lost, no theft indicated) or ITID-13232 (unrecovered public loss)
Confirmed theft (ITID-14211/ITID-14223, Device Theft)
ITID-13233.severity: Medium; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-13233.escalation: Trigger remote lock/wipe immediately regardless of final classification; reclassify once circumstances are confirmed.
indicators: Report of a missing device with unclear circumstances
vectors: N/A — a loss/theft event of unclear type
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Mandatory full-disk encryption
MDM with remote lock/wipe
ITID-13233.detection: MDM device-status monitoring, pending finer classification.
ITID-13233.response: Trigger remote lock/wipe immediately and investigate to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-13233.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one — always trigger the same immediate remote-wipe response regardless of final classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Lost or Stolen Device
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a lost or stolen corporate device not yet classified into a more specific category. Corrective, device-recovery-focused response.

steps.title: Confirm the device and gather circumstances of the loss
steps.desc: Identify the device, when/where it went missing, whether theft is suspected, and what data/sessions were active.
steps.guidance: If theft is suspected, involve physical security/law enforcement per policy.
steps.outcome: Circumstances and exposure documented.

steps.title: Lock the device and revoke associated sessions/credentials
steps.desc: Remotely lock the device and revoke any active sessions or cached credentials tied to it.
steps.outcome: Device locked and access revoked.

steps.title: Remote-wipe the device if not recovered
steps.desc: Trigger a remote wipe via MDM if the device isn't recovered within the defined grace period.
steps.outcome: Device wiped of corporate data.
steps.abort: If the device cannot be reached, the wipe will queue and execute on next connection.

steps.title: Reissue a replacement device and reset exposed credentials
steps.desc: Provision a replacement device and reset any credentials that may have been cached on it.
steps.outcome: Employee back to productive work with fresh credentials.

steps.title: Confirm encryption/MDM baseline and document the case
steps.desc: Document the case and confirm the device met encryption/MDM enrollment baselines.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

steps.title: Attempt to locate the device
steps.desc: Use MDM/find-my-device tooling to attempt recovery before assuming loss.
steps.outcome: Device located, or confirmed unrecoverable.

ITID-13311.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider's own valid credentials were obtained by an external attacker through a phishing email, SMS, voice call, or fraudulent login page, and are subsequently used to access systems as that insider. The insider did not knowingly participate; their account is the vector.
ITID-13311.purpose: Captures incidents where an external attacker successfully phished the credentials of a legitimate insider, who is thereafter an unwitting entry point rather than a willing participant.
scopeIncludes: Insider clicked a phishing link and entered credentials on a spoofed login page
Insider approved an MFA push/OTP prompt believing it was a legitimate request
Credentials harvested via a phishing kit and later used for account login by an external party
scopeExcludes: Credential theft via malware/keylogger with no phishing lure involved (sibling leaf)
Insider knowingly handing over credentials in exchange for payment (a Collusion leaf)
The attacker's subsequent actions once inside the environment (tracked under the relevant external-intrusion ITID once account takeover is confirmed)
ITID-13311.severity: High. A phished credential is a direct external-access foothold; severity should default high pending scope confirmation.
ITID-13311.priority: P1 while the credential is unrevoked and account activity is unconfirmed; downgrade to P2 once the credential is disabled and no unauthorized use is found.
ITID-13311.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC and IAM for emergency credential reset/session revocation; escalate to the insider's manager/HR only for awareness, not as a conduct matter, since the insider is a victim here.
indicators: Insider self-reports clicking a suspicious link or entering credentials on an unfamiliar page
Email gateway or phishing-simulation platform flags a click/credential-submission event tied to the account
Login from an unfamiliar ASN/geolocation immediately following a reported phishing click
Unexpected MFA push approval logged around the time of a reported lure
vectors: Spoofed corporate SSO/login page delivered via email or SMS
MFA fatigue/push-bombing following credential harvest
Voice phishing (vishing) directing the insider to a credential-harvesting site
rootCauses: Insufficient phishing-resistant MFA (SMS/push-based rather than FIDO2)
Gaps in security-awareness training or simulated-phishing follow-up
Absence of conditional-access geo/impossible-travel controls
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged accounts
Conditional access with impossible-travel/geo-velocity blocking
Email/URL sandboxing and link-rewriting at the gateway
ITID-13311.detection: Strong technical detection surface: identity provider sign-in logs, conditional-access alerts, and email-security telemetry all directly evidence this leaf.
ITID-13311.response: Force credential reset and session/token revocation immediately; review account activity from time of suspected compromise; re-enroll MFA; provide the insider with remediation guidance rather than disciplinary action.
metrics: Time from click-report to credential revocation
Count of confirmed account-takeover events following phishing
Phishing-simulation click/report rates by population
ITID-13311.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13312 by vector: phishing/social-engineering delivery of a credential-harvesting lure, versus silent technical capture via malware. Where both a lure and malware are present, classify by the actual capture mechanism confirmed by forensics.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Credential Phished by External Attacker
playbook.description: An insider's credentials were compromised via a phishing attack by an external party. The insider is a victim; response centers on securing the account and supporting the employee.

steps.title: Confirm the phishing compromise and scope of account activity
steps.desc: Review the phishing report/alert and authentication logs to confirm credentials were entered on a malicious site and identify any subsequent unauthorized account activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with a documented activity timeline.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke all active sessions/tokens
steps.desc: Force a password reset, revoke all active sessions, and invalidate OAuth/app tokens for the compromised account.
steps.outcome: Attacker access via the compromised credential terminated.

steps.title: Verify no persistence remains and enroll/verify MFA
steps.desc: Confirm no additional persistence (new app registrations, added MFA devices) remains, and ensure MFA is enforced on the account going forward.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed clean with MFA enforced.

steps.title: Support the employee and restore normal access
steps.desc: Restore the employee's access and communicate supportively — being phished is common and not the employee's fault for reporting it.
steps.guidance: Avoid blame; encourage continued prompt reporting of suspicious emails.
steps.outcome: Employee back to normal, secure access.

steps.title: Review phishing detection controls and awareness training
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether email filtering, MFA coverage, or phishing-awareness training needs improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Identify what the attacker accessed or did with the account
steps.desc: Review mailbox rules, file access, sent items, and any lateral movement performed using the compromised credentials.
steps.outcome: Scope of attacker activity documented.

steps.title: Check for and remove malicious mailbox rules or forwarding
steps.desc: Review the mailbox for attacker-created forwarding rules, delegate access, or inbox rules used to hide activity.
steps.outcome: Malicious mailbox artifacts removed.

ITID-13312.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which malware running on an insider's endpoint (keylogger, infostealer, clipboard/session-token grabber) captured that insider's valid credentials without their knowledge, and an external attacker subsequently used the captured credentials to access systems as that insider.
ITID-13312.purpose: Captures incidents where an insider's credentials were silently captured by malware (typically a keylogger or credential-stealing implant) rather than surrendered via a phishing lure.
scopeIncludes: Keylogger or infostealer malware confirmed on the insider's endpoint with exfiltrated credential data
Browser session-token or cookie theft enabling account access without needing the password itself
Credentials appearing in a known infostealer log/dump traceable to the insider's infected device
scopeExcludes: Credential harvest via a phishing page or social lure with no malware involved (sibling leaf)
Malware installed deliberately by the insider for their own malicious purposes (a Malicious Insider concern, not this branch)
General malware infection with no evidence of credential capture or subsequent account misuse
ITID-13312.severity: High. Silent credential capture combined with active malware presence typically indicates a broader endpoint compromise, not just one exposed account.
ITID-13312.priority: P1 until the endpoint is isolated/reimaged and the credential is revoked; sustain P1 if the malware family is known to harvest browser sessions beyond a single password.
ITID-13312.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/endpoint security for isolation and forensic imaging; loop in IAM for credential/session revocation across all services the insider used from that endpoint.
indicators: EDR alert for keylogging/credential-stealing malware behavior on the insider's endpoint
Insider's credentials found in a dark-web infostealer log dump
Account login using a session token/cookie that matches a device never seen for that user
Anomalous outbound traffic from the endpoint to a known infostealer C2 shortly before account misuse
vectors: Drive-by download or trojanized software install delivering an infostealer
Malicious browser extension harvesting saved credentials/session cookies
Removable media or cracked-software installer bundling a keylogger
rootCauses: Missing or outdated EDR coverage on the endpoint
Local admin rights enabling unsanctioned software installation
Browser credential storage without additional device-bound protection
mitreTechniques: T1555.003 Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
controls: EDR with behavioral detection for input-capture and credential-theft techniques
Removal of local admin rights for standard users
Session-token binding/device-bound authentication where supported
ITID-13312.detection: Strong technical detection surface: EDR telemetry, threat-intel infostealer-log matching, and anomalous session/device correlation are all directly diagnostic.
ITID-13312.response: Isolate and forensically image the endpoint; revoke all credentials and active sessions used from that device; reimage before return to service; notify the insider and provide guidance.
metrics: Mean time to isolate an infected endpoint
Count of credentials revoked following infostealer-log matches
Endpoints reimaged following confirmed keylogger detection
ITID-13312.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13311 by mechanism: silent technical capture via malware versus a phishing lure that induced the insider to disclose the credential themselves. Both may co-occur in a single campaign; classify by the confirmed initial capture vector.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Credential Compromised via Malware Keylogger
playbook.description: An insider's credentials were captured via keylogging malware on their device. The insider is a victim; response centers on device remediation and account security.

steps.title: Confirm the malware infection and credential capture
steps.desc: Confirm keylogger/infostealer malware presence via EDR alert and identify which credentials were likely captured based on the malware's logging scope.
steps.outcome: Malware confirmed and captured-credential scope documented.

steps.title: Isolate the infected device
steps.desc: Isolate the affected endpoint from the network to stop further keystroke capture and exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Device isolated and malware activity halted.

steps.title: Remove the malware and rebuild the device if necessary
steps.desc: Remove the keylogger/infostealer, or reimage the device if clean removal cannot be assured.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the employee's device and access
steps.desc: Return the remediated or replacement device to the employee and restore normal access with new credentials.
steps.outcome: Employee back to normal, secure access.

steps.title: Review endpoint protection coverage and infection vector
steps.desc: Document the case, determine how the malware was delivered, and assess whether endpoint protection or user training gaps contributed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Determine if captured credentials were used for unauthorized access
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for the affected accounts to identify any unauthorized logins or activity.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized use identified or ruled out.

steps.title: Reset all credentials that may have been captured
steps.desc: Force password resets and revoke sessions for every account the employee may have logged into on the infected device.
steps.guidance: Consider password managers or other credentials entered on the device, not just the primary corporate account.
steps.outcome: All potentially captured credentials invalidated.

ITID-13313.def: A confirmed or suspected insider credential compromise whose specific mechanism has not yet been established as phishing (ITID-13311) or malware/keylogger (ITID-13312), or that involves a mechanism genuinely distinct from both (e.g., credential reuse from a third-party breach, unattended-session hijacking). Used at initial triage and reclassified once the capture vector is confirmed.
