ITID-13313.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider credential-compromise reports where the capture mechanism (phishing versus malware) has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Credential-compromise reports pending forensic determination of vector
Credential stuffing using the insider's password reused from an unrelated third-party breach
Unattended/unlocked workstation session hijacked by an unauthorized party
scopeExcludes: Confirmed phishing-vector compromise (reclassify to ITID-13311)
Confirmed malware/keylogger-vector compromise (reclassify to ITID-13312)
Willing insider disclosure of credentials for payment or benefit (a Collusion leaf)
ITID-13313.severity: Medium-High pending triage; re-rate once the specific vector and scope of access are confirmed.
ITID-13313.priority: P2 at intake, escalating to P1 if active unauthorized use of the account is confirmed during triage.
ITID-13313.escalation: Escalate to SOC for triage; reclassify to the specific sibling leaf as soon as the vector is confirmed so the correct playbook and metrics apply.
indicators: Anomalous login flagged by identity provider with no yet-identified cause
Insider reports suspicious account activity without a known root cause
Credential found in a breach-monitoring feed with no confirmed local capture mechanism
vectors: Credential reuse across a third-party breach
Unattended authenticated session accessed by an unauthorized party
Vector not yet determined at time of report
rootCauses: Password reuse across personal and corporate accounts
Screen-lock policy not enforced or not followed
Incomplete triage tooling to rapidly distinguish phishing from malware vectors
controls: Breach-monitoring/dark-web credential exposure feeds
Enforced screen-lock and idle-session timeout policy
Password-reuse detection at authentication
ITID-13313.detection: Partial: identity-provider anomaly detection catches many cases, but root-cause attribution typically requires manual triage before this leaf can be reclassified.
ITID-13313.response: Reset credential and revoke sessions on report; conduct triage to determine vector within the SLA window; reclassify the incident once determined.
metrics: Count of incidents held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to vector determination and reclassification
ITID-13313.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not terminal. Every incident here should be actively worked toward reclassification into ITID-13311 or ITID-13312, or retained here only when the vector is genuinely something other than phishing or malware.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Credential Compromise
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected insider credential compromise not yet classified into a more specific category (phishing or malware). The insider is a victim.

steps.title: Confirm the credential compromise and its likely vector
steps.desc: Review the alert to confirm compromise and determine, if possible, the likely vector (phishing, malware, credential stuffing, etc.).
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with vector identified or under investigation.

steps.title: Reset credentials and revoke active sessions
steps.desc: Force a password reset and revoke all active sessions/tokens for the compromised account.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Verify no persistence remains on the account or device
steps.desc: Check for malicious mailbox rules, new app registrations, or malware persistence.
steps.outcome: Account and device confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the employee's normal, secure access
steps.desc: Restore access with fresh credentials and, where applicable, MFA enrollment.
steps.outcome: Employee back to normal, secure access.

steps.title: Document the case and review credential-security controls
steps.desc: Record the timeline and assess whether MFA, endpoint protection, or awareness training needs improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Determine scope of unauthorized account activity
steps.desc: Review authentication and access logs for unauthorized activity performed using the compromised credentials.
steps.outcome: Scope of unauthorized activity documented.

steps.title: Isolate any implicated device pending investigation
steps.desc: If a device is suspected as the compromise vector, isolate it for further analysis.
steps.outcome: Implicated device isolated.

ITID-13321.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an external party used blackmail, extortion, or coercive threats (e.g., threatening to expose compromising personal information, financial leverage, threats to the insider or their family) to compel an insider to grant access, exfiltrate data, or otherwise act against their employer's interests. The insider's actions are driven by duress rather than free will or personal profit motive.
ITID-13321.purpose: Captures the full scope of incidents where an insider is coerced into taking action for an attacker under threat of exposure, harm, or other leverage, as the sole leaf covering blackmail/coercion in this branch.
scopeIncludes: Sextortion or threat of reputational exposure used to compel data access or exfiltration
Financial or debt-based leverage used to coerce an insider into providing system access
Threats of harm to the insider or their family used to compel action
An insider who self-reports being blackmailed before or after taking compelled action
scopeExcludes: Voluntary, profit-motivated collaboration with no coercive threat present (a Collusion leaf)
Manipulation via a fabricated relationship or deception with no explicit threat (a Social Engineering of Insider leaf)
Credential theft via phishing or malware with no coercive element (Credential Compromise leaves)
ITID-13321.severity: High. Coercion cases frequently involve ongoing leverage and repeat compelled actions, and carry duty-of-care obligations toward the insider.
ITID-13321.priority: P1 while the coercion and any resulting unauthorized access remain active or unconfirmed as contained.
ITID-13321.escalation: Escalate immediately to security leadership, HR, Legal, and where appropriate law enforcement; treat the insider as a victim requiring support and protection, not as a subject of disciplinary action, while still containing the technical exposure.
indicators: Insider self-report of being threatened or blackmailed
Sudden, out-of-character data access or exfiltration by an otherwise trusted employee with no clear personal motive
Evidence of external contact via personal channels preceding anomalous work activity
Behavioral/HR signals of acute distress, secrecy, or financial desperation
vectors: Sextortion via a compromising image/video obtained through a fake online relationship
Debt or gambling-related financial leverage exploited by an external party
Direct threats of physical harm communicated to the insider
rootCauses: No confidential channel for employees to report coercion attempts without fear of punishment
Insufficient behavioral/HR monitoring to catch acute personal-distress indicators
Overly broad standing access that leaves a single coerced individual able to cause large impact
controls: Confidential employee reporting channel for coercion/blackmail (no-fault reporting)
Least-privilege access reducing single-individual blast radius
Employee assistance program (EAP) integration with security/HR insider-risk process
ITID-13321.detection: Weak direct technical signal; detection relies primarily on the insider's own disclosure or downstream behavioral/data-access anomalies rather than a discrete technical indicator.
ITID-13321.response: Prioritize insider safety and confidentiality; contain any resulting unauthorized access or exfiltration; involve Legal/law enforcement as appropriate; do not treat voluntary disclosure as grounds for punitive action against the insider.
metrics: Count of coercion cases self-reported vs. detected
Time from disclosure/detection to containment
ITID-13321.notes: Sole leaf under the Blackmail or Coercion Tier-4, so this definition intentionally covers the full concept rather than acting as a narrow catch-all. Differentiated from Social Engineering of Insider leaves by the presence of explicit threat/leverage rather than deception or relationship-building alone.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Blackmail or Coercion (Compromised Insider Context)
playbook.description: An insider is being blackmailed or coerced by an external party into taking harmful actions against the organization. Safety-first, confidential response prioritizing the employee's wellbeing alongside securing the environment.

steps.title: Confirm indicators of coercion and assess immediate safety concerns
steps.desc: Review the report or behavioral indicators suggesting the employee is acting under duress; assess whether there is any immediate physical safety risk to the employee.
steps.guidance: Handle with maximum discretion and empathy; this is a person in a difficult situation, not simply a threat actor.
steps.outcome: Situation understood with safety risk level assessed.

steps.title: Secure the employee's access without alarming or further endangering them
steps.desc: Coordinate carefully-timed technical containment (e.g., enhanced monitoring, access adjustment) in a way that does not visibly signal detection to the coercing party.
steps.guidance: Timing and approach should be directed by HR/Legal/EAP, factoring in the employee's safety.
steps.outcome: Technical exposure reduced without compromising the employee's safety.

steps.title: Remediate any technical compromise resulting from coerced actions
steps.desc: Remediate any malware, unauthorized access, or data exposure that resulted from actions taken under coercion.
steps.outcome: Technical impact remediated.

steps.title: Determine ongoing safety and employment path with HR/Legal/EAP
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal/EAP to determine next steps for the employee, which may include continued support, law-enforcement referral for the coercing party, or other protective measures.
steps.outcome: A supportive, safety-conscious path forward agreed.

steps.title: Conduct a confidential post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the case at an appropriate, restricted access level, focusing on how such situations can be surfaced and supported earlier.
steps.guidance: Preserve employee confidentiality in all documentation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal/EAP sign-off.

steps.title: Engage HR, Legal, and EAP confidentially and immediately
steps.desc: Loop in HR, Legal, and the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) at once, on a strictly need-to-know basis, to coordinate a safety-first and confidential response.
steps.guidance: Limit the circle of knowledge as tightly as possible; avoid any action that could endanger the employee or their family.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal/EAP engaged and coordinating response.

steps.title: Offer the employee a safe, confidential reporting channel and support
steps.desc: Ensure the employee has a confidential path to fully disclose the situation and access support resources (EAP, legal protection, law enforcement if desired).
steps.outcome: Employee supported with clear, confidential channels available.

steps.title: Assess what actions the employee may have already taken under coercion
steps.desc: Carefully and discreetly review account activity for any actions taken under the coercion, coordinating timing with HR/Legal/EAP.
steps.outcome: Scope of any coerced actions documented.

ITID-13331.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an external attacker built a long-term pretext relationship with an insider (e.g., a fabricated romantic, professional, or friendship connection cultivated over weeks or months) in order to gradually gain trust and ultimately induce the insider to grant access, disclose information, or otherwise act against their employer's interests. The insider is manipulated but not under an explicit blackmail-style threat.
ITID-13331.purpose: Captures cases where an insider was manipulated over an extended period through a cultivated fake relationship, rather than through a single deceptive interaction.
scopeIncludes: Long-running fake romantic relationship (e.g., a catfishing/'romance scam' pattern) used to build trust before requesting access or information
Fabricated recruiter, vendor, or professional-network relationship cultivated over time to gain the insider's confidence
Gradual escalation of small, seemingly harmless requests over an extended relationship, culminating in a significant compromise
scopeExcludes: A single or short-duration deception with no cultivated relationship (sibling leaf, ITID-13332)
Manipulation involving an explicit threat or blackmail leverage (a Blackmail or Coercion leaf)
Voluntary, self-initiated collaboration with an external attacker for personal gain (a Collusion leaf)
ITID-13331.severity: Medium-High. Severity depends on what the relationship ultimately induced the insider to do, but the extended grooming pattern often indicates a deliberate, well-resourced targeting effort.
ITID-13331.priority: P2, escalating to P1 once the relationship is confirmed to have resulted in actual access grant, data disclosure, or exfiltration.
ITID-13331.escalation: Escalate to security leadership and HR upon confirmation; involve Legal if the relationship involved a foreign actor or intelligence-gathering pattern; support the insider rather than treating them as the primary culpable party.
indicators: Insider discloses an online relationship with someone requesting work-related information or favors
Pattern of escalating small requests from an external contact over an extended period
Behavioral changes in the insider (secrecy, distraction, defensiveness about a personal relationship) coinciding with unusual data requests
Personal communications referencing employer systems, data, or access found during investigation
vectors: Romance-scam-style relationship built via social media or dating platforms and pivoted toward work access
Fabricated long-term professional networking relationship (e.g., a persistent fake recruiter or industry contact)
rootCauses: Lack of employee awareness training on long-con social engineering patterns
No policy or habit of reporting unusual personal-relationship-driven work requests
Employees with sensitive access not receiving targeted insider-risk awareness training
controls: Insider-risk awareness training covering long-term social engineering/romance-scam patterns
Confidential reporting channel for unusual personal-relationship-driven requests
Least-privilege access to limit impact of a single manipulated individual
ITID-13331.detection: Weak direct technical signal; this leaf relies primarily on self-disclosure, HR/behavioral observation, or downstream data-access anomalies rather than a discrete technical indicator.
ITID-13331.response: Investigate the full scope of what was disclosed or accessed over the relationship's duration; contain any resulting exposure; support the insider through the disclosure process; consider whether the pattern indicates targeted/state-linked activity.
metrics: Count of long-term social engineering cases identified
Average duration of the relationship before disclosure or detection
ITID-13331.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13332 by duration and mechanism: a cultivated relationship built over time versus a single/short deceptive interaction. Differentiated from Blackmail or Coercion by the absence of explicit threat; the insider here is manipulated through trust rather than fear.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Manipulated via Long-Term Pretext Relationship Building
playbook.description: An external attacker built a long-term trust relationship with an insider under false pretenses in order to manipulate them into taking harmful action. The insider is a victim of sustained social engineering.

steps.title: Confirm the pretext relationship and what actions resulted
steps.desc: Establish the nature of the relationship, how it was used to manipulate the employee, and what actions (data sharing, access grants, etc.) resulted.
steps.guidance: Approach the employee with empathy; they were deceived, not complicit.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the manipulation and resulting actions.

steps.title: Cut off the attacker's ongoing access or communication channel
steps.desc: Block the attacker's contact channels and revoke any access or sharing that was granted as part of the pretext relationship.
steps.outcome: Attacker's ongoing access/contact severed.

steps.title: Remediate any resulting technical exposure
steps.desc: Remove any access, malware, or data exposure that resulted from the manipulation.
steps.outcome: Technical exposure remediated.

steps.title: Assess and notify affected parties if required
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to determine notification obligations if sensitive data was exposed.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed on the required timeline.

steps.title: Reinforce social-engineering awareness training
steps.desc: Document the case and recommend targeted awareness training on long-term pretext/relationship-based social engineering.
steps.guidance: Keep tone supportive of the employee.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with training recommendation assigned.

steps.title: Review account and data activity tied to the resulting actions
steps.desc: Review logs for any data shared, access granted, or systems touched as a result of the manipulation.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure documented.

steps.title: Support the employee and involve HR discreetly if appropriate
steps.desc: Provide the employee support and loop in HR if the manipulation involved significant personal deception, handled discreetly.
steps.outcome: Employee supported; HR informed as appropriate.

ITID-13332.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an external attacker used a short, discrete deception (e.g., a fraudulent phone call impersonating IT support, a fabricated urgent request impersonating an executive, a fake vendor request) to induce an insider to unknowingly take an action — such as granting remote access, resetting a password, or forwarding information — that facilitated attacker access. The insider does not realize they are assisting an attacker and did not receive prior cultivation or grooming.
ITID-13332.purpose: Captures cases where an insider was deceived, in a single or short-duration interaction, into unknowingly taking an action that facilitated attacker access.
scopeIncludes: Vishing call impersonating IT/helpdesk to get the insider to install remote-access software or read out an MFA code
Business email compromise-style urgent request impersonating an executive, inducing the insider to grant access or reset a credential
Fraudulent vendor/support request that leads the insider to unknowingly open a door for the attacker (physical or logical)
scopeExcludes: A cultivated long-term relationship used to build trust before the request (sibling leaf, ITID-13331)
The insider knowingly and willingly assisting the attacker, even if minimally informed (a Collusion leaf)
Credential theft via a phishing page with no live deceptive interaction (a Credential Compromise leaf)
ITID-13332.severity: Medium-High, driven primarily by what access or action the deception achieved rather than by the insider's culpability, which is low to none.
ITID-13332.priority: P1 immediately following discovery, given that this pattern typically indicates active, in-progress attacker access.
ITID-13332.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC to contain any granted access; notify the insider's manager for awareness only, since the insider acted in good faith; consider organization-wide alert if the same pretext is being used against multiple employees.
indicators: Insider reports receiving an unusual urgent request purportedly from IT, a vendor, or an executive
Remote-access tool installation or unusual admin action immediately following a reported call/email
Password reset or MFA action performed outside normal helpdesk workflow
Multiple employees report similar pretext contact within a short window (campaign indicator)
vectors: Vishing impersonating internal IT/helpdesk requesting remote access or an MFA code
Business email compromise impersonating a senior executive requesting an urgent action
Fraudulent vendor/contractor request for facility or system access
rootCauses: No verified callback procedure for helpdesk/executive requests involving access or credentials
Insufficient employee training on live-interaction (vishing/BEC) pretexts specifically
Overly permissive remote-access tooling that a non-technical employee can install unsupervised
controls: Mandatory callback verification for helpdesk/IT support requests via a known number
Restriction on installation of remote-access tools by standard users
Executive-impersonation/BEC awareness training with simulated exercises
ITID-13332.detection: Moderate: the deceptive interaction itself is hard to detect directly, but the resulting technical action (remote-tool install, password reset, unusual admin activity) is generally detectable.
ITID-13332.response: Contain the granted access immediately; reverse any resulting changes (resets, installs, permission grants); debrief the insider without blame; alert the broader population if a campaign pattern is suspected.
metrics: Count of successful live-pretext deceptions per quarter
Time from deceptive action to containment of resulting access
ITID-13332.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13331 by the absence of a cultivated relationship: the deception here is a single or short-duration interaction. Differentiated from Credential Compromise leaves because the insider takes an active action under deception, rather than simply having a secret captured via a technical means.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Deceived into Unknowingly Facilitating Attacker Access
playbook.description: An insider was deceived by an external attacker into unknowingly granting access or facilitating a compromise (e.g., approving a fraudulent access request, running a disguised tool). The insider is a victim of social engineering.

steps.title: Confirm what access or action the insider was deceived into providing
steps.desc: Establish exactly what the employee did (e.g., approved an MFA push, granted remote access, ran a file) and how the deception was carried out.
steps.guidance: Approach the employee with empathy; they were deceived, not complicit.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the deception and resulting facilitated access.

steps.title: Revoke the facilitated access and terminate attacker sessions
steps.desc: Immediately revoke any access granted and terminate any active attacker sessions or remote-access tools.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Search for and remove any attacker persistence
steps.desc: Search for malware, new accounts, or other persistence mechanisms the attacker may have established using the facilitated access.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Restore affected systems and support the employee
steps.desc: Restore any affected systems and support the employee, reinforcing that they acted reasonably given a sophisticated deception.
steps.outcome: Systems restored; employee supported.

steps.title: Review the deception technique and strengthen relevant controls
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether verification procedures (e.g., MFA fatigue protection, callback verification) need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Determine what the attacker did with the facilitated access
steps.desc: Review logs to determine what the attacker accessed, modified, or exfiltrated using the access the insider unknowingly provided.
steps.outcome: Scope of attacker activity documented.

steps.title: Reset the insider's credentials as a precaution
steps.desc: Reset credentials and review MFA settings for the deceived employee's account as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Employee's account secured.

ITID-13333.def: A confirmed or suspected case of an insider being socially engineered by an external attacker into taking or facilitating an unauthorized action, where it has not yet been established whether the manipulation followed a long-term pretext relationship pattern (ITID-13331) or a single/short-duration deception pattern (ITID-13332). Used at initial triage and reclassified once the pattern is confirmed.
ITID-13333.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider social-engineering reports where the manipulation pattern (long-term relationship versus single deception) has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Social-engineering reports pending determination of manipulation pattern
Ambiguous cases with elements of both a prior relationship and a discrete triggering deception where the dominant pattern is unclear
Novel social-engineering patterns not cleanly matching either sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed long-term pretext relationship pattern (reclassify to ITID-13331)
Confirmed single/short-duration deception pattern (reclassify to ITID-13332)
Cases involving an explicit threat or coercion (a Blackmail or Coercion leaf)
ITID-13333.severity: Medium-High pending triage; re-rate once the manipulation pattern and resulting access/exposure are confirmed.
ITID-13333.priority: P2 at intake, escalating to P1 if the social engineering is confirmed to have resulted in active unauthorized access.
ITID-13333.escalation: Escalate to SOC and HR for triage; reclassify to the specific sibling leaf as soon as the pattern is confirmed so the correct playbook and metrics apply.
indicators: Insider reports being manipulated but details of the interaction timeline are not yet clear
Anomalous access or disclosure traced to an external social contact with pattern undetermined
Multiple external contact channels involved, complicating attribution to a single pattern
vectors: Vector not yet determined at time of report
rootCauses: Incomplete triage detail at time of initial report
Insufficient employee awareness training generally on social-engineering patterns
controls: Confidential employee reporting channel for social-engineering attempts
Insider-risk awareness training covering multiple social-engineering patterns
ITID-13333.detection: Weak direct technical signal at intake; detection relies primarily on self-disclosure, HR observation, or downstream data-access anomalies pending pattern confirmation.
ITID-13333.response: Contain any resulting access exposure on report; conduct triage to determine the manipulation pattern within the SLA window; reclassify the incident once determined.
metrics: Count of incidents held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to pattern determination and reclassification
ITID-13333.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not terminal. Every incident here should be actively worked toward reclassification into ITID-13331 or ITID-13332.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Social Engineering of Insider
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected social engineering of an insider not yet classified into a more specific category (pretext relationship or deceived facilitation). The insider is a victim.

steps.title: Confirm the social engineering technique and what resulted
steps.desc: Establish how the employee was deceived and what actions, access, or data disclosure resulted.
steps.guidance: Approach the employee with empathy; they were deceived, not complicit.
steps.outcome: Documented understanding of the deception and its outcome.

steps.title: Cut off attacker access and revoke any granted access
steps.desc: Terminate any attacker sessions and revoke access or sharing granted as a result of the social engineering.
steps.outcome: Attacker access severed.

steps.title: Remove any resulting persistence or unauthorized changes
steps.desc: Search for and remove any malware, new accounts, or unauthorized changes resulting from the incident.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and support the employee
steps.desc: Restore any affected systems and support the employee through the aftermath.
steps.outcome: Systems restored; employee supported.

steps.title: Document the case and reinforce awareness training
steps.desc: Record the technique used and recommend targeted awareness training or verification-process improvements.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Review account and data activity tied to the resulting actions
steps.desc: Review relevant logs for data shared, access granted, or systems touched as a result of the social engineering.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure documented.

steps.title: Secure the employee's credentials as a precaution
steps.desc: Reset credentials and review MFA for the affected employee's account.
steps.outcome: Employee's account secured.

ITID-13411.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider, using access they were legitimately granted, deliberately views, accesses, or interacts with systems, applications, or data outside the scope of their job duties or any authorized task, for reasons of curiosity, personal interest, or personal benefit — without necessarily escalating privileges or hoarding data. The insider acts entirely of their own free will and is not being directed or manipulated by an external party.
ITID-13411.purpose: Captures the full scope of insiders misusing legitimate access they hold to reach systems or data beyond what their role or task requires, as the sole leaf covering unauthorized access under Insider Privilege Abuse.
scopeIncludes: Browsing HR, payroll, or medical records of coworkers, friends, or public figures without a business need
Accessing a former partner's, neighbor's, or celebrity's customer/account record out of curiosity
Logging into a system or application outside one's assigned duties using standing access that was never revoked
Viewing case files, tickets, or records related to a personal matter (e.g., a friend's legal or HR case)
scopeExcludes: Escalating privileges beyond what was granted to gain new access (Privilege Escalation, a sibling Tier-4)
Systematically collecting or retaining large volumes of data beyond simple access (Data Hoarding, a sibling Tier-4)
Access granted or facilitated because the insider was compromised, coerced, or manipulated by an external party (a Compromised Insider leaf)
Access performed in coordination with another party toward a shared malicious goal (a Collusion leaf)
ITID-13411.severity: Medium, escalating to High where the accessed data is sensitive (medical, financial, law-enforcement, executive) or where access is repeated/patterned.
ITID-13411.priority: P2 for a single confirmed instance; P1 if access is ongoing, high-volume, or involves highly sensitive records.
ITID-13411.escalation: Escalate to the data owner, HR, and Legal/Privacy for any confirmed unauthorized access to regulated data (HR, medical, financial); involve law enforcement only if the access supports a separate crime (e.g., stalking).
indicators: Access logs showing a user viewing records with no associated ticket, case, or business justification
Repeated access to the same non-work-related record (e.g., a specific individual's file) over time
Data-loss-prevention or UEBA alert on access outside the user's normal role-based pattern
A complaint from a coworker or third party that their record was inappropriately viewed
vectors: Use of standing/legacy access never scoped down after a role change
Shared or overly broad role-based access controls granting more visibility than the job requires
rootCauses: Access not reviewed or right-sized after a role or department change
Absence of need-to-know segmentation on sensitive record types (HR, medical, law-enforcement)
No routine access-pattern auditing against role baselines
controls: Role-based access control with periodic access recertification
Need-to-know segmentation and break-glass logging on sensitive record types
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) baselining role-appropriate access patterns
ITID-13411.detection: Moderate: access and audit logs provide a real technical trail, but distinguishing unauthorized curiosity access from legitimate edge-case business need typically requires human review.
ITID-13411.response: Investigate the full scope and duration of unauthorized access; notify affected individuals/data owners per policy; apply proportionate disciplinary action via HR; right-size the insider's access.
metrics: Count of confirmed unauthorized-access cases per quarter
Average time from anomalous access to detection
Percentage of access reviews completed on schedule
ITID-13411.notes: Sole leaf under the Unauthorized Access Tier-4, so this definition intentionally covers the full concept rather than acting as a narrow catch-all. Differentiated from Privilege Escalation (gaining new access) and Data Hoarding (bulk retention) by scope: this leaf is about using existing standing access beyond legitimate need.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Unauthorized Access (Insider Privilege Abuse Context)
playbook.description: An insider has accessed systems or data beyond what their role requires, without clear malicious intent but constituting privilege abuse. Access-control and least-privilege remediation focus.

steps.title: Confirm the scope of unauthorized access
steps.desc: Review access logs to determine exactly what systems/data were accessed outside the individual's role or authorization.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of out-of-role access.

steps.title: Revoke or right-size the excess access
steps.desc: Remove the unauthorized access, adjusting the individual's permissions to match their actual role requirements.
steps.outcome: Access rescoped to least privilege.

steps.title: Audit what was done with the excess access
steps.desc: Review what actions were taken using the unauthorized access to determine if any harm resulted (data viewed, changes made).
steps.outcome: Actions taken with the excess access documented.

steps.title: Remediate any impact from actions taken with the excess access
steps.desc: Reverse any inappropriate changes or address any data exposure caused during the period of unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Any resulting impact remediated.

steps.title: Review access-provisioning and periodic access-review processes
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether access-request approval, role-based access control, or periodic access reviews need strengthening to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with access-control process improvements assigned.

steps.title: Determine why the access existed in the first place
steps.desc: Investigate whether the access was granted in error, left over from a prior role, or never should have existed — this shapes the remediation.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the excess access identified.

ITID-13421.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider, acting of their own free will and without external compromise or direction, uses their legitimate access, technical knowledge, or administrative trust to grant themselves privileges, roles, or entitlements beyond what was authorized for their role — as distinct from simply misusing access already held. This includes self-approval of access requests, modifying entitlement systems, or exploiting an administrative role to expand one's own footprint.
ITID-13421.purpose: Captures the full scope of insiders abusing legitimate standing access or trust to grant themselves elevated privileges beyond what was authorized, as the sole leaf covering privilege escalation under Insider Privilege Abuse.
scopeIncludes: An administrator adding themselves to a privileged group or role without proper approval
Self-approving one's own access request in an identity-governance workflow
Modifying permissions, entitlements, or group memberships to grant oneself access not previously held
Exploiting a shared administrative credential or break-glass account to obtain standing elevated access
scopeExcludes: Using existing access, without expanding it, beyond legitimate business need (Unauthorized Access, a sibling Tier-4)
Bulk collection or retention of data using already-held access (Data Hoarding, a sibling Tier-4)
Privilege escalation carried out at the direction of, or in exchange for benefit from, an external attacker (a Collusion leaf)
Privilege escalation resulting from the insider being compromised or manipulated by an external party (a Compromised Insider leaf)
ITID-13421.severity: High. Self-granted privilege escalation by an insider undermines the integrity of access-governance controls themselves and typically warrants high severity regardless of what was subsequently done with the access.
ITID-13421.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the governance-control failure and potential for further unauthorized action.
ITID-13421.escalation: Escalate immediately to IAM/security leadership to revoke the unauthorized entitlement and audit for other affected accounts; involve HR and Legal for disciplinary and, where warranted, criminal referral.
indicators: Identity-governance audit finding a self-approved or improperly approved access request
Privileged-group membership change with no corresponding change-management ticket
Use of a break-glass or emergency-access account outside of a declared emergency
Entitlement or role definition modified by a user who then benefits from that modification
vectors: Abuse of administrative rights over the identity-governance or IAM platform itself
Self-approval loophole in an access-request workflow lacking segregation of duties
Misuse of a shared or poorly monitored break-glass account
rootCauses: Lack of segregation of duties in access-approval workflows (requester able to also approve)
Insufficient logging/alerting on privileged-group and entitlement changes
Break-glass accounts not tightly controlled or monitored
controls: Segregation of duties enforced in access-request/approval workflows (no self-approval)
Real-time alerting on privileged-group and entitlement changes
Tightly controlled, monitored break-glass account usage with mandatory post-use review
ITID-13421.detection: Strong technical detection surface: IAM/identity-governance audit logs and privileged-group-change alerting directly evidence this leaf.
ITID-13421.response: Revoke the unauthorized entitlement immediately; audit for similar self-granted escalations by the same or other users; refer for disciplinary/legal action; close the segregation-of-duties gap that enabled it.
metrics: Count of confirmed self-escalation incidents per quarter
Time from unauthorized entitlement grant to detection
Percentage of access-approval workflows with segregation of duties enforced
ITID-13421.notes: Sole leaf under the Privilege Escalation Tier-4, so this definition intentionally covers the full concept rather than acting as a narrow catch-all. Differentiated from Unauthorized Access by mechanism: this leaf involves actively expanding one's own access footprint, not merely using access already held.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Privilege Escalation (Insider Privilege Abuse Context)
playbook.description: An insider has escalated their own privileges beyond their authorized role. Access-control and least-privilege remediation focus.

steps.title: Confirm the privilege escalation and method used
steps.desc: Determine how the individual escalated their privileges (e.g., self-approval, exploiting an approval workflow gap, using an admin tool) and to what level.
steps.outcome: Escalation method and resulting privilege level documented.

steps.title: Revert privileges to the authorized baseline
steps.desc: Remove the escalated privileges and restore the individual's access to their originally authorized level.
steps.outcome: Privileges reverted to baseline.

steps.title: Close the gap that allowed self-escalation
steps.desc: Remediate the workflow or control gap that allowed the individual to escalate their own privileges (e.g., require dual approval).
steps.outcome: Escalation path closed.

steps.title: Remediate any impact from actions taken with escalated privileges
steps.desc: Reverse any inappropriate changes made while the individual held elevated privileges.
steps.outcome: Any resulting impact remediated.

steps.title: Review privilege-management controls
steps.desc: Document the case and assess whether privileged access management (PAM), approval workflows, or monitoring for self-escalation need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with control improvements assigned.

steps.title: Determine what was done with the escalated privileges
steps.desc: Review activity logs for actions taken while operating with the elevated privileges.
steps.outcome: Scope of actions taken documented.

ITID-13431.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider, using access they legitimately hold and acting of their own free will, systematically collects, copies, downloads, or retains data in volumes or patterns beyond what their role or any authorized task requires — without necessarily exfiltrating it externally or acting in concert with another party. This includes local hoarding (personal drives, unauthorized local copies, personal cloud storage) as preparation for later use, departure, or simply out of possessiveness over 'their' work product.
ITID-13431.purpose: Captures the full scope of insiders systematically collecting or retaining data beyond what their role requires, using access they legitimately hold, as the sole leaf covering data hoarding under Insider Privilege Abuse.
scopeIncludes: Bulk downloading of files, reports, or records well beyond the volume needed for any current task
Copying data to a personal cloud-storage account, USB drive, or personal email in the weeks before a planned departure
Retaining large local caches of sensitive data long after the associated project or task has ended
Automated or scripted bulk collection of records from an internal repository with no corresponding business need
scopeExcludes: Accessing individual records outside one's role without bulk collection or retention (Unauthorized Access, a sibling Tier-4)
Expanding one's own privileges/entitlements without a data-collection component (Privilege Escalation, a sibling Tier-4)
Hoarding or exfiltration performed to benefit, or at the direction of, an external attacker or other insiders (a Collusion leaf)
Data collection resulting from the insider being compromised or manipulated by an external party (a Compromised Insider leaf)
ITID-13431.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where the hoarded data is regulated, highly sensitive, or where hoarding coincides with resignation/termination.
ITID-13431.priority: P2 for hoarding detected without evidence of external transfer; P1 if hoarding coincides with an imminent departure or shows signs of preparation for exfiltration.
ITID-13431.escalation: Escalate to security leadership, HR, and Legal immediately upon detection, particularly if the insider is departing or under performance/disciplinary review; consider legal hold on affected data and devices.
indicators: DLP or file-activity monitoring alert on abnormal bulk download/copy volume
Large data transfers to removable media or personal cloud storage, especially near a resignation date
Access to and download of records unrelated to current projects or assignments
A pattern of retention (never deleting local copies) inconsistent with data-retention policy
vectors: Bulk export functions in internal applications used without business justification
Personal cloud-storage sync clients installed on corporate endpoints
USB/removable media used to copy large volumes of data
rootCauses: No DLP or file-activity monitoring on bulk export/download actions
Departure/offboarding process not triggering heightened monitoring in advance of exit
Ambiguous or unenforced data-retention and 'this is my work product' cultural norms
mitreTechniques: T1052.001 Exfiltration Over Physical Medium: Exfiltration over USB
controls: DLP monitoring and alerting on abnormal bulk download/copy activity
Heightened monitoring during pre-resignation/notice-period and offboarding windows
Restriction or monitoring of removable media and unsanctioned cloud-sync clients
ITID-13431.detection: Strong technical detection surface: DLP, file-activity monitoring, and removable-media logging directly evidence abnormal volume and destination of data movement.
ITID-13431.response: Investigate the full scope of what was collected/retained and where it was moved; recover or delete unauthorized copies where possible; apply a legal hold if departure or litigation is anticipated; refer for disciplinary action.
metrics: Count of confirmed data-hoarding incidents per quarter
Volume of data recovered/remediated per incident
Percentage of departing employees flagged for pre-exit monitoring
ITID-13431.notes: Sole leaf under the Data Hoarding Tier-4, so this definition intentionally covers the full concept rather than acting as a narrow catch-all. Differentiated from Unauthorized Access by scale/pattern (bulk collection and retention rather than individual record viewing) and from Collusion leaves by the absence of any external or multi-insider coordination.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Data Hoarding (Insider Privilege Abuse Context)
playbook.description: An insider has accumulated or retained access to significantly more data than their role requires, creating unnecessary risk exposure. Access-control and least-privilege remediation focus.

steps.title: Confirm the extent and sensitivity of hoarded data/access
steps.desc: Identify what data the individual has accumulated access to or copies of, beyond current role requirements, and assess its sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Scope and sensitivity of hoarded data documented.

steps.title: Right-size access to current role requirements
steps.desc: Revoke access and data copies that exceed what is needed for the individual's current role.
steps.outcome: Access and data holdings rescoped to least privilege.

steps.title: Locate and remove any unauthorized local/personal copies
steps.desc: Check for local downloads, personal drives, or other copies of hoarded data and remove them from unauthorized locations.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized copies removed.

steps.title: Confirm the individual retains access needed for their actual role
steps.desc: Verify the rescoping did not remove access genuinely needed for current duties.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the individual can still perform their role.

steps.title: Implement periodic access reviews to prevent re-accumulation
steps.desc: Document the case and recommend periodic access recertification to catch data hoarding before it becomes a risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with access-review process improvement assigned.

steps.title: Determine why the access/data was accumulated
steps.desc: Investigate whether the hoarding reflects role changes over time, convenience, or a deliberate pattern of retaining broad access.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the hoarding identified.

ITID-13511.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider knowingly and willingly provides their valid access credentials (or facilitates provisioning of access) to an external attacker as part of a transactional, profit-motivated arrangement — a one-time payment or an ongoing paid relationship — with the insider's participation being voluntary rather than the product of coercion, deception, or manipulation.
ITID-13511.purpose: Captures cases where an insider knowingly sells or trades their legitimate access credentials to an external attacker in exchange for payment or other benefit.
scopeIncludes: An insider selling their VPN, SSO, or application credentials to a known or unknown external buyer for a fee
An insider accepting recurring payment to keep providing valid, working credentials to an external party
An insider deliberately provisioning a new account or access grant for an external party in exchange for payment
scopeExcludes: Casual or informal credential sharing between colleagues with no external attacker or payment involved (handled under the relevant Malicious Insider credential-sharing category, not this leaf)
Credentials obtained by an external attacker via phishing or malware without the insider's knowing participation (a Compromised Insider leaf)
Credentials surrendered under blackmail, coercion, or extortion rather than for profit (a Blackmail or Coercion leaf)
Ongoing hands-on technical assistance with lateral movement beyond simply supplying access (sibling leaf, ITID-13512)
ITID-13511.severity: High. A knowing, paid credential sale represents a deliberate breach of trust with a confirmed external buyer actively seeking access.
ITID-13511.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the near-certainty of active or imminent external account misuse.
ITID-13511.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC for credential revocation and account activity review; escalate to HR, Legal, and law enforcement given the transactional/criminal nature of the arrangement.
indicators: Financial records or communications (chat logs, cryptocurrency transactions) evidencing payment to the insider for access
Login activity for the insider's account from locations/devices inconsistent with the insider's own usage, occurring on a recurring basis
The insider provisioning access for an external party with no legitimate business justification
Insider's account credentials found for sale or referenced in underground marketplaces/forums
vectors: Underground-forum solicitation of insiders willing to sell corporate access ('insider recruitment' posts)
Direct approach/bribery of an employee with known access to a target system
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring for anomalous, recurring account usage patterns inconsistent with the legitimate user
No insider-risk program to flag financially distressed or disgruntled employees with high-value access
Weak controls preventing an individual from unilaterally provisioning access for external parties
controls: UEBA monitoring for recurring anomalous account usage patterns distinct from the legitimate user's baseline
Insider-risk program flagging financial-distress and access-sensitivity combinations
Approval workflow required for any external-party access provisioning
ITID-13511.detection: Moderate: recurring anomalous usage of the legitimate account can be detected via UEBA, but confirming the transactional/payment element typically requires financial or communications-based investigation.
ITID-13511.response: Revoke the sold credential and all associated sessions immediately; audit all activity conducted under the account since the arrangement began; refer to Legal/law enforcement given the criminal nature; pursue disciplinary/termination action.
metrics: Count of confirmed credential-sale incidents per year
Scope of account activity attributable to the sold credential
ITID-13511.notes: Distinguished from casual/informal credential sharing (handled as a Malicious Insider concern, not tracked here) by the presence of a collusive, payment-driven arrangement with an external attacker; simple credential sharing without that transactional element is out of scope for this leaf. Also distinguished from ITID-13512 by role: this leaf covers supplying the access itself, while ITID-13512 covers ongoing hands-on assistance once the attacker is already inside.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Providing Access Credentials to External Attacker for Payment
playbook.description: An insider has knowingly sold or traded access credentials to an external attacker in exchange for payment. Severe, full HR/Legal/law-enforcement-coordinated response with broad blast-radius assessment.

steps.title: Confirm the collusion and scope of credentials/access provided
steps.desc: Review evidence (financial anomalies, communications, anomalous access patterns) to confirm the individual provided credentials or access to an external party for payment.
steps.guidance: Handle with strict confidentiality; do not alert the individual before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Confirmed collusion with documented scope of access provided.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with full chain of custody across all implicated accounts
steps.desc: Image devices and preserve logs for the individual and any other implicated accounts before broad action is taken.
steps.guidance: Follow formal evidence-handling procedures suitable for potential criminal proceedings.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard across all implicated parties.

steps.title: Search for and remove all attacker persistence
steps.desc: Search every system the external attacker may have touched for backdoors, new accounts, or other persistence, and remove them.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain across affected systems.

steps.title: Assess broader exposure and execute required notifications
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine the full scope of data/systems exposed and execute any required regulatory or customer notifications.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope assessed and notifications executed as directed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case and review privileged-access monitoring, financial-anomaly detection, and insider-threat program controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with Legal/leadership sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess the blast radius — what the external attacker accessed and whether others are involved
steps.desc: Determine everything the external attacker accessed using the provided credentials, and investigate whether other employees may be similarly involved.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker access and any additional implicated individuals documented.

steps.title: Revoke access for the individual and the compromised credential path, timed per Legal/law-enforcement guidance
steps.desc: Coordinate carefully-timed revocation of all provided/compromised access across every affected system.
steps.outcome: All external attacker access via the sold credentials terminated.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership; engage law enforcement
steps.desc: Given the severity — a paid insider threat — escalate immediately; Legal should assess referral to law enforcement.
steps.guidance: Do not contact external authorities directly without Legal's coordination.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, HR engaged; law-enforcement referral decision documented.

ITID-13512.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which an insider knowingly provides ongoing, hands-on technical assistance to an external attacker who has already obtained some foothold, actively helping the attacker navigate, escalate, or move laterally within internal systems — for example, by identifying valuable targets, explaining network architecture, disabling controls, or executing actions on the attacker's behalf from inside the trusted perimeter.
ITID-13512.purpose: Captures cases where an insider goes beyond simply providing initial access and actively, ongoingly assists an external attacker's movement through internal systems.
scopeIncludes: An insider providing network diagrams, system inventories, or guidance on where sensitive data resides to an attacker already inside
An insider disabling or whitelisting around security controls (EDR, firewall rules, logging) at an attacker's request
An insider executing commands, running scripts, or performing lateral-movement actions on the attacker's behalf from inside the network
An insider providing real-time situational updates to an attacker about incident-response activity to help them evade detection
scopeExcludes: A one-time or transactional handoff of access credentials with no further ongoing assistance (sibling leaf, ITID-13511)
Passive, one-time provisioning of access with no subsequent active participation in the attacker's operations
Assistance provided under coercion or blackmail rather than voluntary collaboration (a Blackmail or Coercion leaf)
ITID-13512.severity: Critical. Ongoing insider assistance to an in-progress external attack dramatically increases the attacker's effectiveness and ability to evade detection.
ITID-13512.priority: P1, sustained, for the duration of the active intrusion; treat as a live incident-response matter, not solely an HR/insider-risk matter.
ITID-13512.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/incident-response leadership as an active intrusion; escalate in parallel to HR, Legal, and law enforcement given the insider's active participation; consider isolating the insider's access and devices without tipping them off if a controlled investigation is warranted.
indicators: Security-control changes (EDR exclusions, firewall rule changes, logging disabled) made by an insider account with no change-management justification, correlated with attacker activity elsewhere
Insider account activity (commands, queries, file access) that directly maps to and facilitates subsequent attacker lateral movement
Communications (chat, email, external messaging) between the insider and an external party discussing internal systems or ongoing incident response
Insider's access patterns shift to unusual hours or systems coinciding with observed attacker activity
vectors: Insider embedded within IT/security operations providing real-time assistance to an external intrusion
Insider with elevated access disabling detective controls to enable attacker persistence and movement
rootCauses: Insufficient separation between an individual's ability to modify security controls and independent oversight of those changes
No monitoring/alerting correlating an insider's security-relevant actions with concurrent external attacker activity
Overly trusted access for personnel with both deep system knowledge and broad administrative privileges
controls: Change-management approval and independent review required for security-control modifications (EDR exclusions, firewall/logging changes)
Correlated monitoring linking internal control changes to concurrent external attacker indicators
Segregation of duties between operational access and security-control administration
ITID-13512.detection: Moderate-strong: security-control change logs and lateral-movement telemetry provide real technical signal when correlated against the insider's account activity, though attributing intent (vs. legitimate troubleshooting) requires investigation.
ITID-13512.response: Treat as an active incident: contain the intrusion, revoke the insider's access, preserve forensic evidence of both the insider's and attacker's actions, and coordinate closely with legal/law enforcement given the active collusion.
metrics: Time from correlated internal/external activity to containment
Count of security-control changes traced to insider collusion
ITID-13512.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13511 by depth and duration of involvement: this leaf covers active, ongoing technical assistance once an attacker already has a foothold, not just the initial supply of credentials.

playbook.name: Response: Insider Actively Assisting External Attacker's Lateral Movement
playbook.description: An insider is actively and knowingly helping an external attacker move laterally through internal systems. Severe, full HR/Legal/law-enforcement-coordinated response with broad blast-radius assessment.

steps.title: Confirm active insider assistance and current attacker foothold
steps.desc: Correlate insider account activity with attacker lateral-movement indicators to confirm the insider is actively facilitating access, and establish the attacker's current foothold.
steps.guidance: Treat as an active, ongoing incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed active collusion with documented attacker foothold.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with chain of custody before broad containment
steps.desc: Preserve logs and forensic evidence across all implicated systems before taking overt containment action, if feasible given active severity.
steps.guidance: Balance evidence preservation against the need to stop active damage — Legal/leadership should direct this tradeoff.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to the extent possible given the active threat.
steps.abort: If active damage is occurring, immediate containment may need to take priority over evidence preservation — document the decision.

steps.title: Hunt for persistence across the full blast radius
steps.desc: Search every system in the blast radius for backdoors, additional accounts, or other persistence established during the collusion.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain across affected systems.

steps.title: Assess exposure and execute required notifications
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine the full scope of data/systems exposed and execute any required notifications.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope assessed and notifications executed as directed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case and review lateral-movement detection, privileged-access monitoring, and insider-threat program controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with Legal/leadership sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess blast radius across all systems the insider has touched
steps.desc: Determine every system, account, and dataset the insider has access to or has assisted the attacker in reaching.
steps.outcome: Full blast-radius map documented.

steps.title: Cut off the insider's access and the attacker's foothold simultaneously
steps.desc: Revoke the insider's access and eradicate the attacker's foothold in a coordinated, simultaneous action to prevent either from re-establishing access.
steps.outcome: Both the insider's facilitation and the attacker's foothold eliminated.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership; engage law enforcement
steps.desc: Given active, ongoing collusion, escalate immediately for coordinated response; Legal should assess law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, HR engaged; response coordinated.

ITID-13513.def: A confirmed or suspected case of an insider knowingly collaborating with an external attacker toward a shared malicious goal, where it has not yet been established whether the insider's role was primarily transactional/payment-driven credential provisioning (ITID-13511) or ongoing active technical assistance with lateral movement (ITID-13512), or where the collaboration takes a form distinct from both. Used at initial triage and reclassified once the role is confirmed.
ITID-13513.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider collaboration-with-external-attacker reports where the insider's specific role (transactional credential sale versus ongoing active assistance) has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Collaboration reports pending determination of the insider's specific role in the arrangement
Cases with early evidence of both a payment element and ongoing assistance where the dominant pattern is unclear
Novel forms of insider-external collaboration not cleanly matching either sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed transactional/payment-driven credential provisioning (reclassify to ITID-13511)
Confirmed ongoing active assistance with lateral movement (reclassify to ITID-13512)
Collaboration among multiple insiders with no external attacker involved (a Group Conspiracy leaf)
ITID-13513.severity: High pending triage; re-rate once the insider's role and the state of any resulting intrusion are confirmed.
ITID-13513.priority: P1 at intake given the likely presence of an active external intrusion, sustained or downgraded once the specific role and current containment status are confirmed.
ITID-13513.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC and incident-response leadership for triage as a potential active intrusion; reclassify to the specific sibling leaf as soon as the insider's role is confirmed so the correct playbook applies.
indicators: Evidence of insider-external collaboration surfaced during an active intrusion investigation with role not yet attributed
Financial and technical-assistance indicators both present without a clear dominant pattern
Tip or report of insider collusion lacking detail on the specific nature of involvement
vectors: Vector/role not yet determined at time of report
rootCauses: Incomplete triage detail at time of initial report
Investigation still in early stages of establishing the insider's exact role
controls: Insider-risk program with escalation path into active incident response
Correlated monitoring linking internal account activity to concurrent external attacker indicators
ITID-13513.detection: Moderate: technical correlation between insider activity and external attacker indicators can trigger this leaf, but attributing the specific role typically requires further investigation.
ITID-13513.response: Contain any active external access exposure on report; conduct triage to determine the insider's specific role within the SLA window; reclassify the incident once determined.
metrics: Count of incidents held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to role determination and reclassification
ITID-13513.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not terminal. Every incident here should be actively worked toward reclassification into ITID-13511 or ITID-13512.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Insider Collaboration with External Attacker
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected insider actively collaborating with an external attacker, not yet classified into a more specific category. Severe, full HR/Legal/law-enforcement-coordinated response.

steps.title: Confirm indicators of insider-external collusion
steps.desc: Review evidence suggesting an insider is knowingly collaborating with an external attacker, and characterize the nature of the collaboration.
steps.guidance: Handle with strict confidentiality.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or ruled-out collusion, documented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with chain of custody across implicated accounts
steps.desc: Image devices and preserve logs before broad containment action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard.

steps.title: Search for and remove all persistence
steps.desc: Hunt across affected systems for backdoors or additional accounts established during the collusion.
steps.outcome: No persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Assess exposure and execute required notifications
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine notification obligations and execute them.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case and review insider-threat detection and privileged-access controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess blast radius and whether others are involved
steps.desc: Determine the scope of systems/data accessed and whether additional employees may be involved.
steps.outcome: Blast radius and any additional implicated individuals documented.

steps.title: Revoke insider and attacker access, timed per Legal/law-enforcement guidance
steps.desc: Coordinate revocation of the insider's access and eradication of the external attacker's foothold.
steps.outcome: Both insider facilitation and attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership
steps.desc: Escalate immediately given the severity; Legal should assess law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, HR engaged.

ITID-13521.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which two or more insiders knowingly coordinate their legitimate access and approval authorities to circumvent segregation-of-duties controls — for example, colluding across the requester/approver split in a financial or procurement workflow — in order to commit, conceal, or enable fraud or another form of process abuse that neither could achieve alone.
ITID-13521.purpose: Captures cases where multiple employees deliberately coordinate to defeat segregation-of-duties controls, typically to commit or conceal fraud.
scopeIncludes: A requester and approver in a procurement or payments workflow colluding to approve fraudulent or self-dealing transactions
Two employees splitting a normally single-person-restricted task (e.g., initiating and approving a wire transfer) to bypass a dual-control requirement
Coordinated falsification of records across multiple roles (e.g., inventory count and reconciliation) to conceal a discrepancy or theft
scopeExcludes: A coordinated multi-insider effort focused on data theft/exfiltration rather than process/financial-control bypass (sibling leaf, ITID-13522)
A single insider unilaterally escalating their own privileges without a second insider's coordination (a Privilege Escalation leaf under Insider Privilege Abuse)
Collaboration between an insider and an external attacker rather than between insiders (a Collaboration with External Attackers leaf)
ITID-13521.severity: High. Segregation-of-duties controls exist specifically to prevent this pattern, and successful bypass typically indicates both a control failure and active financial or process harm.
ITID-13521.priority: P1 upon confirmation, particularly where financial loss or regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., fraud disclosure) are implicated.
ITID-13521.escalation: Escalate immediately to Internal Audit, Finance/Legal, and HR; consider regulatory or law-enforcement referral where the conspiracy involves financial fraud or falsified records.
indicators: Audit finding of a consistent pattern where the same two or more individuals appear on both sides of a control (requester/approver, preparer/reviewer)
Unusual approval velocity or rubber-stamp approval patterns between specific pairs of employees
Financial reconciliation discrepancies traced to coordinated action by multiple individuals
Whistleblower or hotline report describing coordinated control bypass
vectors: Exploiting weak or unenforced segregation-of-duties configuration in ERP/financial systems
Informal collusion agreements between colleagues in adjacent roles within the same approval chain
rootCauses: Segregation-of-duties rules not technically enforced within the relevant system (relying on policy alone)
Insufficient rotation of approval pairings or periodic audit of approval-pattern concentration
Weak whistleblower/reporting culture that allows collusion to persist undetected
mitreTechniques: T1562.008 Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
controls: System-enforced segregation of duties in financial/procurement workflows
Periodic audit of approval-pattern concentration between specific individual pairs
Confidential whistleblower/fraud reporting hotline
ITID-13521.detection: Moderate: financial/audit analytics can surface anomalous approval-pairing patterns, but confirming intentional collusion typically requires an audit or investigative process rather than a single technical alert.
ITID-13521.response: Suspend the affected individuals' access to the implicated workflow pending investigation; quantify financial/process impact via audit; refer for disciplinary and, where warranted, legal/regulatory action; remediate the segregation-of-duties control gap.
metrics: Count of confirmed segregation-of-duties bypass cases per year
Financial impact quantified per incident
Percentage of high-risk workflows with system-enforced segregation of duties
sops: Segregation of Duties Control Review SOP
ITID-13521.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13522 by focus: this leaf centers on defeating financial/process controls (typically fraud-oriented), while the sibling leaf centers on coordinated data theft/exfiltration.

playbook.name: Response: Multiple Employees Colluding to Bypass Segregation-of-Duties Controls
playbook.description: Two or more employees have conspired to bypass segregation-of-duties controls (e.g., approval chains, dual-control processes) for personal or fraudulent gain. Severe, full HR/Legal-coordinated response with broad blast-radius assessment across all implicated accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the control bypass and identify all participants
steps.desc: Review approval logs, transaction records, and access patterns to confirm the segregation-of-duties bypass and identify every employee involved.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Legal before broadly reviewing employee activity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bypass with all participating individuals identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with chain of custody across all implicated accounts
steps.desc: Preserve logs and records for every participating individual before broad action is taken.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard.

steps.title: Reinstate proper segregation-of-duties enforcement
steps.desc: Close the technical or process gap that allowed the bypass (e.g., enforce system-level dual approval rather than relying on manual process).
steps.outcome: Segregation-of-duties control technically enforced.

steps.title: Reverse or remediate improperly approved transactions
steps.desc: Work with Finance/Internal Audit to reverse or remediate any transactions improperly pushed through.
steps.outcome: Improper transactions addressed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review of control design
steps.desc: Document the case and review whether segregation-of-duties controls should be system-enforced rather than procedural.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with control-design improvements assigned.

steps.title: Assess the financial or operational impact of the bypass
steps.desc: Determine what transactions, approvals, or decisions were improperly pushed through as a result of the collusion.
steps.outcome: Documented impact of the control bypass.

steps.title: Restrict access for all implicated individuals per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict system access for each participant, timed per HR/Legal guidance.
steps.outcome: Further control bypass prevented.

steps.title: Escalate to HR, Legal, and Internal Audit
steps.desc: Notify HR, Legal, and Internal Audit given the multi-party, fraud-adjacent nature of the incident.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal/Internal Audit engaged and directing next steps.

ITID-13522.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected case in which two or more insiders knowingly coordinate their access, roles, or timing to collectively steal, collect, or exfiltrate data - for example, dividing responsibility for accessing different systems, covering for one another's absence, or combining separate partial datasets into a single stolen collection - toward a shared data-theft goal, without a primary external attacker driving the effort.
ITID-13522.purpose: Captures cases where multiple insiders coordinate together specifically to steal or exfiltrate data at a scale or with a sophistication beyond what one individual could achieve alone.
scopeIncludes: Two or more employees each exfiltrating a portion of a dataset they individually have access to, to jointly reconstruct a fuller stolen set
Insiders coordinating timing/coverage (e.g., one distracts oversight while another exfiltrates data) to jointly steal data
A group of departing employees jointly planning and executing coordinated bulk data theft ahead of starting a competing venture
scopeExcludes: A group conspiracy focused on financial/process-control bypass rather than data theft (sibling leaf, ITID-13521)
A single insider hoarding or exfiltrating data without coordinating with any other insider (a Data Hoarding leaf under Insider Privilege Abuse)
Insiders coordinating with and directed primarily by an external attacker rather than among themselves (a Collaboration with External Attackers leaf)
ITID-13522.severity: High. Coordinated multi-insider data theft typically achieves greater scope and is harder to detect than a single actor, warranting elevated severity.
ITID-13522.priority: P1 upon confirmation, especially where the theft targets trade secrets, customer data, or other data with significant competitive or regulatory sensitivity.
ITID-13522.escalation: Escalate immediately to security leadership, HR, and Legal; pursue civil/injunctive action promptly if the data supports a competing venture or was destined for a competitor; involve law enforcement where theft of trade secrets or regulated data is confirmed.
indicators: DLP/file-activity monitoring showing correlated, complementary data-access patterns across multiple individuals
Multiple employees exhibiting resignation or departure timing clustered together, coinciding with data-movement alerts
Communications among the group referencing coordinated access, division of labor, or a shared destination for the data
A single reconstructed dataset later found to combine access-scoped fragments from multiple individuals' roles
vectors: Coordinated bulk export functions used by multiple individuals within a short time window
Shared personal cloud-storage or messaging destination used to consolidate stolen data fragments
rootCauses: No correlation analytics linking data-movement anomalies across multiple individuals to a shared pattern
Departure/offboarding monitoring applied individually rather than looking for clustered departures
Insufficient monitoring of communications/collaboration tools for coordination indicators
controls: Cross-user correlation analytics on DLP/file-activity alerts to surface coordinated patterns
Clustered-departure monitoring flagging multiple resignations from the same team in a short window
DLP coverage on personal cloud-storage and messaging egress channels
ITID-13522.detection: Moderate-strong: DLP and file-activity monitoring provide real technical signal, particularly when correlated across multiple individuals rather than analyzed one user at a time.
ITID-13522.response: Investigate the full scope of coordinated activity and all individuals involved; pursue legal hold and civil/injunctive remedies promptly; refer for disciplinary and criminal/civil action; recover or contain the stolen dataset where possible.
metrics: Count of confirmed coordinated data-theft rings identified per year
Volume of data recovered/remediated per incident
Time from clustered-departure flag to investigation initiation
ITID-13522.notes: Differentiated from ITID-13521 by focus: this leaf centers on coordinated theft/exfiltration of data, while the sibling leaf centers on defeating financial/process controls. A conspiracy involving both patterns should be classified by its dominant, primary objective.

playbook.name: Response: Coordinated Multi-Insider Data Theft Ring
playbook.description: Multiple employees have conspired together to systematically steal organizational data. Severe, full HR/Legal/law-enforcement-coordinated response with broad blast-radius assessment across all implicated accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the conspiracy and identify all participants
steps.desc: Review DLP, access logs, and communications evidence to confirm coordinated data theft and identify every participating employee.
steps.guidance: Handle with strict confidentiality; do not alert participants before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Confirmed conspiracy with all participants identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with chain of custody across all implicated accounts
