steps.desc: Image devices and preserve logs for every participant before broad action is taken.
steps.guidance: Follow formal evidence-handling procedures suitable for potential criminal proceedings.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard across all implicated parties.

steps.title: Determine if exfiltrated data is recoverable or revocable
steps.desc: Assess whether remote wipe, link revocation, or third-party takedown is possible for each destination the data was sent to.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether remote remediation is possible and executed where feasible.

steps.title: Assess exposure and execute required notifications
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to determine notification obligations given the scale of the theft.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed on the required timeline.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case and review DLP coverage, access reviews, and insider-threat detection given the coordinated nature of the theft.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with Legal/leadership sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess the full scope of data stolen across all participants
steps.desc: Determine everything each participant accessed and exfiltrated, and where the data was sent.
steps.outcome: Full scope of stolen data documented across all participants.

steps.title: Restrict access for all implicated individuals simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous access restriction for every participant, timed per HR/Legal/law-enforcement direction, to prevent evidence destruction or coordination among participants.
steps.outcome: Further data theft by any participant prevented.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership; engage law enforcement
steps.desc: Given the coordinated, multi-party severity, escalate immediately; Legal should assess referral to law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, HR engaged; law-enforcement referral decision documented.

ITID-13523.def: A confirmed or suspected case of two or more insiders knowingly conspiring together toward a shared malicious goal, where it has not yet been established whether the conspiracy is primarily structured around bypassing segregation-of-duties/financial controls (ITID-13521) or coordinated data theft/exfiltration (ITID-13522), or where the conspiracy takes a form distinct from both. Used at initial triage and reclassified once the structure is confirmed.
ITID-13523.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for multi-insider conspiracy reports where the structure (segregation-of-duties bypass versus coordinated data theft) has not yet been determined.
scopeIncludes: Group conspiracy reports pending determination of the dominant structure/objective
Cases with early evidence of both financial-control bypass and data-theft elements where the dominant pattern is unclear
Novel forms of multi-insider conspiracy not cleanly matching either sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed segregation-of-duties/financial-control bypass conspiracy (reclassify to ITID-13521)
Confirmed coordinated data-theft conspiracy (reclassify to ITID-13522)
A single insider acting alone with no coordination among multiple insiders (an Insider Privilege Abuse leaf)
ITID-13523.severity: High pending triage; re-rate once the conspiracy's structure and full scope of participants and impact are confirmed.
ITID-13523.priority: P1 at intake given the multi-actor nature of the report, sustained or downgraded once the structure and containment status are confirmed.
ITID-13523.escalation: Escalate to Internal Audit, security leadership, HR, and Legal for triage; reclassify to the specific sibling leaf as soon as the dominant structure is confirmed so the correct playbook applies.
indicators: Whistleblower or hotline report describing multi-employee coordination with structure not yet clear
Audit or DLP findings implicating multiple individuals without a confirmed primary objective
Early-stage investigation with evidence pointing to more than one insider but roles/goal undetermined
vectors: Structure/vector not yet determined at time of report
rootCauses: Incomplete triage detail at time of initial report
Investigation still in early stages of establishing the conspiracy's full scope and objective
controls: Confidential whistleblower/fraud reporting hotline
Cross-functional (Audit, Security, HR, Legal) insider-conspiracy triage process
ITID-13523.detection: Weak-to-moderate at intake: multi-actor involvement may be evident from an initial tip or correlated alerts, but confirming the specific structure typically requires further investigation.
ITID-13523.response: Contain any active financial or data-exposure risk on report; conduct triage to determine the conspiracy's dominant structure within the SLA window; reclassify the incident once determined.
metrics: Count of incidents held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to structure determination and reclassification
ITID-13523.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not terminal. Every incident here should be actively worked toward reclassification into ITID-13521 or ITID-13522.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified/General Group Conspiracy
playbook.description: Intake bucket for a suspected multi-insider group conspiracy not yet classified into a more specific category (segregation-of-duties bypass or coordinated data theft). Severe, full HR/Legal-coordinated response with broad blast-radius assessment.

steps.title: Confirm the conspiracy and identify all participants
steps.desc: Review available evidence to confirm multiple employees are acting in concert and identify each participant.
steps.guidance: Handle with strict confidentiality.
steps.outcome: Confirmed conspiracy with all participants identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with chain of custody across all implicated accounts
steps.desc: Preserve logs and records for every participant before broad action is taken.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved to an evidentiary standard.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying control gap that enabled the conspiracy
steps.desc: Identify and close the process or technical gap that allowed the group to act in concert undetected.
steps.outcome: Control gap closed.

steps.title: Assess exposure and execute required notifications
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine notification obligations and execute them.
steps.outcome: Obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Conduct a post-incident review with Legal and security leadership
steps.desc: Document the case and review detection controls for coordinated, multi-party insider activity.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with sign-off and improvement actions assigned.

steps.title: Assess the full scope and impact across all participants
steps.desc: Determine what each participant did and the combined impact of the conspiracy.
steps.outcome: Full scope and impact documented.

steps.title: Restrict access for all implicated individuals simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous access restriction for every participant, timed per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further conspiracy activity prevented.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to Legal, HR, and executive leadership
steps.desc: Escalate immediately given the multi-party severity; Legal should assess law-enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Leadership, Legal, HR engaged.

ITID-14111.def: An unauthorized person follows an authorized person through a secured entry point, logged from a physical-access-control incident perspective, distinct from the pretext-technique taxonomy used for social-engineering-framed tailgating.
ITID-14111.purpose: Catch-all for tailgating logged as a physical-access-control incident, without a social-engineering pretext analysis being performed.
scopeIncludes: Access-control incident reports of tailgating logged without any pretext/technique analysis
scopeExcludes: Tailgating logged with a specific social-engineering pretext identified (the Tailgating Type under Physical Social Engineering Attacks, ITID-11811-11819)
ITID-14111.escalation: Escalate to physical security for documentation.
indicators: Access-control log showing one badge read followed by multiple entrants
vectors: Following an authorized person through a secured door
rootCauses: No badge-verification culture; courtesy/crowding allows unverified entry
controls: Anti-tailgating turnstiles/mantraps
Access-control door-position sensors
ITID-14111.detection: Badge-read-vs-entrant-count mismatch and CCTV provide a real technical signal.
ITID-14111.response: Review CCTV/badge logs and document as a physical-access-control incident.
metrics: Count of tailgating incidents logged under this Tier-2 branch per quarter
ITID-14111.notes: Scope decision: this leaf exists in parallel with the Social Engineering branch's Tailgating Type (ITID-11811-11819) to avoid forcing every access-control tailgating log entry through a pretext-classification exercise; use this leaf when no pretext analysis is performed, and the Social Engineering branch when the specific pretext technique is identified and relevant to a social-engineering awareness program.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Tailgating
playbook.description: For an incident where an unauthorized individual followed an authorized employee through an access-controlled door without badging in themselves.

steps.title: Confirm the tailgating event
steps.desc: Review CCTV and badge logs for the door to confirm a single badge event was followed by multiple people entering.
steps.outcome: Tailgating event confirmed with footage.

steps.title: Dispatch security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: If the individual may still be on-site, send security to locate, verify identity, and escort them out if unauthorized.
steps.outcome: Individual located and removed, or confirmed to have already left.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed and any impact
steps.desc: Determine whether any assets, information, or systems were exposed during the individual's presence.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: Coach the employee whose badge was used to tailgate through
steps.desc: Remind the employee of anti-tailgating policy in a corrective, non-punitive way if it appears to have been unintentional courtesy rather than deliberate misuse.
steps.outcome: Employee understands the risk and expectation going forward.
steps.abort: If the employee appears to have deliberately let the person in, handle as Access Abuse instead.

steps.title: Assess anti-tailgating controls at the door
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate whether mantraps, turnstiles, or tailgating-detection sensors are warranted for this entry point.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Identify the tailgater and their subsequent movement
steps.desc: Track the individual's movement through the facility via additional camera coverage to determine what areas they accessed.
steps.outcome: Movement path and dwell locations identified.

ITID-14121.def: An adversary creates a functional duplicate of a legitimate employee's access badge — by skimming/cloning its credential data onto a blank card — and uses it to gain unauthorized entry.
ITID-14121.purpose: Captures use of a cloned or duplicated copy of a legitimate access badge's credential to gain unauthorized entry.
scopeIncludes: Skimming/cloning a legitimate badge's credential data onto a new card
Using a cloned badge to gain entry
scopeExcludes: Fabricating an entirely fake badge with invented credentials not tied to a real employee (ITID-14122)
Using stolen blank badge stock to create a new badge (ITID-14123)
ITID-14121.severity: High, given it grants access under a real employee's identity.
ITID-14121.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and the impersonated employee's manager; deactivate the original credential pending investigation.
indicators: Two simultaneous or geographically impossible badge-read events for the same credential ID
Employee reports their badge behaving unexpectedly (e.g., denied when it should work) after a clone was used elsewhere
vectors: RFID/proximity card skimming of a legitimate badge
Cloning credential data onto a blank card
rootCauses: Legacy low-frequency RFID badges without cryptographic authentication, vulnerable to skimming/cloning
controls: Migration to cryptographically authenticated (e.g., smart card) badge technology
Anomaly detection for duplicate/impossible-travel badge-read events
ITID-14121.detection: Duplicate/impossible-travel badge-read correlation provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14121.response: Deactivate the affected credential immediately and investigate all locations where it was used.
metrics: Count of confirmed badge-cloning incidents per year
ITID-14121.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14122/14123 by method: cloning an existing, valid credential, versus fabricating an entirely new one.

playbook.name: Response: Cloned/Duplicated Access Badge
playbook.description: For discovery that an access badge was cloned/duplicated and used to gain unauthorized entry.

steps.title: Identify the badge ID used and its legitimate holder
steps.desc: Pull the access control system log for the entry event to identify which badge credential was used, and who it is issued to.
steps.outcome: Badge holder and usage event identified.

steps.title: Deactivate the compromised badge and issue a new one
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the cloned badge credential and reissue a new badge to the legitimate holder.
steps.outcome: Cloned credential no longer valid.

steps.title: Assess badge cloning technique and system vulnerability
steps.desc: Work with the access-control vendor to determine how the badge was cloned (e.g., low-frequency proximity card vulnerability) and whether the badge technology needs upgrading.
steps.outcome: Root cause and technology risk identified.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if the unauthorized access led to theft or other crime.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Evaluate upgrading badge/reader technology
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess migrating to harder-to-clone credential technology (e.g., encrypted smart cards, mobile credentials) if this is a recurring risk.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Determine whether the legitimate holder was the one who entered
steps.desc: Compare CCTV footage of the entry against the legitimate holder's known appearance/location at the time (e.g., were they badged in elsewhere or on leave).
steps.outcome: Confirmed the badge was cloned and used by someone else.
steps.abort: If the legitimate holder simply forgot they used it, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Review other recent access by the same credential
steps.desc: Audit all recent entries on the compromised badge ID to identify the full scope of unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Full history of unauthorized use established.

ITID-14122.def: An adversary manufactures a fake access badge — with a forged appearance, printed identity, and/or a fabricated (not cloned) credential — designed to visually or electronically pass as legitimate.
ITID-14122.purpose: Captures fabrication of an entirely fake access badge with invented or forged credentials, not tied to cloning a real employee's card.
scopeIncludes: Manufacturing a badge with a fabricated identity/appearance and a forged (non-cloned) credential
scopeExcludes: Cloning an existing legitimate employee's credential (ITID-14121)
Using stolen blank badge stock as the base material, when that specific sourcing method is confirmed (ITID-14123)
ITID-14122.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security; review badge-issuance controls.
indicators: Badge presented that does not match any record in the access-control credential database
Visual inspection revealing print quality, formatting, or holographic inconsistencies
vectors: Manufacturing a counterfeit badge using commercially available card printers/encoders
rootCauses: Badges lack sufficiently distinctive security features (holograms, UV features) to enable quick visual verification
controls: Badge security features (hologram, UV printing) enabling visual verification
Access-control credential database cross-check at manned checkpoints
ITID-14122.detection: Access-control credential-database cross-check provides a real technical signal at manned checkpoints.
ITID-14122.response: Detain/deny entry and cross-check the presented credential against the issuance database.
metrics: Count of confirmed fabricated-badge incidents per year
ITID-14122.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14121 by method: fabricating a new, forged credential rather than cloning a real one.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Fake Access Badge with Forged Credentials
playbook.description: For discovery of an entirely fabricated badge (not cloned from a real credential) used or attempted to gain facility access.

steps.title: Recover and document the fake badge
steps.desc: If the badge is recovered (e.g., confiscated at a checkpoint), photograph and document its construction and any forged details (name, photo, logo).
steps.guidance: Preserve the physical badge as evidence.
steps.outcome: Fake badge documented and secured.

steps.title: Alert security staff sitewide with a description
steps.desc: Circulate the individual's description and the fake badge's appearance to reception/security staff.
steps.outcome: Staff prepared to recognize and challenge the individual if they return.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed if entry was gained
steps.desc: Determine what areas or assets were reached if the fake badge succeeded in gaining entry.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Fabricating credentials to gain facility access is typically a criminal offense — report to law enforcement with the recovered badge and evidence.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Review badge design/anti-counterfeiting features
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether current badges need harder-to-forge features (holograms, encrypted chips, visible design changes).
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV and access logs for where it was used or attempted
steps.desc: Check camera footage at the checkpoint/reader and whether the reader logged a valid or rejected credential attempt.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether entry was gained or only attempted.

ITID-14123.def: An adversary steals blank, unissued badge stock from the organization's own supply and encodes it with a forged or stolen credential to create a functional unauthorized badge.
ITID-14123.purpose: Captures use of stolen blank/unissued badge stock (physical card blanks, not yet encoded for a specific person) as the source material for creating an unauthorized badge.
scopeIncludes: Theft of blank/unissued badge stock from a supply room, print station, or badge office
Encoding stolen blank stock with a forged or replayed credential
scopeExcludes: Fabricating a badge from externally sourced (non-organizational) card stock (ITID-14122)
Cloning a credential onto any card without the blank stock itself being stolen from the organization (ITID-14121)
ITID-14123.severity: High, given the badge stock's genuine physical security features make detection harder.
ITID-14123.escalation: Escalate immediately; inventory the badge-stock supply chain to determine the scope of missing stock.
indicators: Badge-stock inventory discrepancy at the badge office/print station
A badge presented with genuine physical security features but no matching issuance record
vectors: Insider or opportunistic theft of blank badge stock from an unsecured supply location
rootCauses: Blank badge stock not inventoried/reconciled or stored in an unsecured location
controls: Secured, inventory-reconciled storage of blank badge stock
Serial-number tracking of blank stock from receipt through issuance
ITID-14123.detection: Badge-stock inventory reconciliation provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14123.response: Reconcile badge-stock inventory and treat any resulting unauthorized badge as using genuine security features.
metrics: Count of badge-stock inventory discrepancies per quarter
ITID-14123.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14122 by material sourcing: stolen organizational blank stock, which retains genuine security features, versus externally sourced fabrication materials.

playbook.name: Response: Stolen Blank Badge Stock Used to Create Unauthorized Badge
playbook.description: For discovery that blank badge stock (unprogrammed cards/printer supplies) was stolen and used to create an unauthorized badge.

steps.title: Confirm the theft of blank stock and inventory the loss
steps.desc: Verify with the badge office how much blank stock is missing and when it was last confirmed present.
steps.outcome: Scope of missing stock confirmed.

steps.title: Secure remaining blank stock and printer/encoder access
steps.desc: Move remaining stock to a more secure, access-restricted location and restrict who can operate the badge printer/encoder.
steps.outcome: Further theft prevented.

steps.title: Investigate whether encoding credentials were also compromised
steps.desc: Determine whether the thief also needs system access to program a functional badge, and check whether that access is at risk too.
steps.outcome: Full risk chain assessed.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Report the theft to law enforcement, particularly given the potential for further unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Review badge stock inventory controls
steps.desc: Log the incident and implement stricter inventory counts and storage security for blank badge stock going forward.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review access to the badge stock storage area
steps.desc: Pull badge/camera logs for who had access to where the stock is stored.
steps.outcome: Access history to the storage location established.

steps.title: Watch for and identify any badge created from the stolen stock
steps.desc: Since blank stock alone typically can't grant access without programming, monitor for anomalous badge creation events or any unrecognized badge use.
steps.outcome: Any resulting unauthorized badge identified and revoked.

ITID-14124.def: Use of an unauthorized or fraudulent access badge, not clearly matching cloning, fabrication, or stolen blank stock.
ITID-14124.purpose: Catch-all for badge forgery that does not fit the more specific cloning, fabrication, or stolen-stock leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14124.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14124.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the forgery method is clarified.
indicators: Report of an unauthorized badge of unclear origin
vectors: Activity of unclear method
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14124.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14124.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14124.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Badge Forgery
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for badge forgery incidents not covered by the cloning, fabrication, or stolen-stock categories.

steps.title: Document the forged badge and how it was discovered
steps.desc: Record the badge's details and circumstances of discovery.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Revoke any associated access
steps.desc: Deactivate the forged credential in the access control system if it was recognized there.
steps.outcome: Credential no longer usable.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed
steps.desc: Determine the scope of any unauthorized access gained.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Review badge security controls
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess badge program security overall.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV and access logs
steps.desc: Pull footage and access records for where the badge was used or discovered.
steps.outcome: Access history and available footage obtained.

ITID-14131.def: An authorized employee props open a secured door — for convenience, ventilation, or repeated back-and-forth trips — creating an unmonitored, unauthorized entry point.
ITID-14131.purpose: Captures an authorized employee propping open a secured door for convenience, an insider-driven access-control weakening distinct from an outsider's tailgating pretext.
scopeIncludes: An employee wedging or propping open a badge-controlled door for their own convenience
scopeExcludes: An outsider using a specific social-engineering pretext to get a door held (the Tailgating Types, ITID-11811-11819 and ITID-14111)
ITID-14131.severity: Medium, given it is a control weakening rather than a hostile act by itself, but High if it results in a confirmed unauthorized entry.
ITID-14131.escalation: Escalate to physical security for corrective coaching; escalate further if an unauthorized entry results.
indicators: Door-held-open sensor alert with no service/delivery activity in progress
Employee observed propping a door on CCTV
vectors: N/A — this is a control-weakening insider behavior rather than an external attack vector
rootCauses: Inconvenient door/badge placement encouraging propping; insufficient consequence for policy violations
controls: Door-held-open alarms with defined response threshold
Policy enforcement/consequence management for repeat offenders
ITID-14131.detection: Door-held-open sensor alerting provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14131.response: Investigate door-held-open alerts and coach/discipline the responsible employee per policy.
metrics: Count of door-propping violations identified per month
ITID-14131.notes: Differentiated from the Tailgating Types by actor and intent: an authorized employee's own convenience-driven behavior, not a social-engineering pretext used by an outside adversary.

playbook.name: Response: Authorized Employee Propping Door Open for Unauthorized Entry
playbook.description: For an authorized employee found propping open an access-controlled door, enabling unauthorized entry — typically a policy/convenience issue rather than malicious intent.

steps.title: Identify the employee and confirm the circumstances
steps.desc: Review CCTV/badge logs to identify who propped the door and for how long, and gather context (e.g., moving equipment, frequent deliveries).
steps.outcome: Employee and circumstances identified.

steps.title: Close and re-secure the door
steps.desc: Ensure the door is closed and functioning normally.
steps.outcome: Door restored to secure state.

steps.title: Address the underlying reason for propping
steps.desc: If there's a legitimate workflow reason (e.g., frequent deliveries), work with the employee's team to find a compliant alternative (doorbell/intercom, scheduled access).
steps.outcome: Root cause addressed so propping isn't the path of least resistance.

steps.title: Coach the employee, corrective and non-punitive
steps.desc: Remind the employee of the policy and risk in a corrective conversation, not disciplinary unless this is a repeat/deliberate pattern.
steps.outcome: Employee understands the risk and expectation going forward.
steps.abort: If repeated after coaching, escalate to management/HR for a formal conversation.

steps.title: Log the incident and reinforce door-security awareness
steps.desc: Record the incident; if propping is common at this door, consider a door-ajar alarm or process fix.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced; recurring pattern flagged if seen.

steps.title: Determine whether the door was exploited
steps.desc: Check whether any unauthorized individual entered through the propped door during the window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether exploitation occurred.

ITID-14132.def: An authorized employee lends their personal access badge to another individual — a coworker, friend, or family member — allowing that person to enter using the employee's credential.
ITID-14132.purpose: Captures an authorized employee knowingly lending their access badge to someone else, breaking the badge's individual-accountability guarantee.
scopeIncludes: An employee knowingly handing their badge to another person to use for entry
scopeExcludes: A badge obtained without the owner's knowledge/consent, such as through theft or dumpster diving (ITID-11825, the Dumpster Diving branch, or the Hardware/Device Theft branches)
ITID-14132.severity: High, given it fully defeats individual accountability for the affected credential.
ITID-14132.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the borrower accesses a restricted area.
ITID-14132.escalation: Escalate to physical security and HR; badge-lending typically constitutes a policy violation subject to discipline.
indicators: Badge-read event geographically or temporally inconsistent with the badge owner's known whereabouts
CCTV showing a different individual using a specific employee's badge
vectors: N/A — this is a control-weakening insider behavior rather than an external attack vector
rootCauses: Insufficient consequence/awareness around badge-sharing; convenience culture (e.g., holding a door/badge for a forgetful coworker)
controls: Photo-ID verification at high-security checkpoints to catch badge/holder mismatches
Policy enforcement/consequence management for badge-sharing
ITID-14132.detection: CCTV-to-badge-photo comparison at monitored checkpoints provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14132.response: Investigate the CCTV/badge-photo mismatch and address the badge owner per policy.
metrics: Count of confirmed badge-lending violations per quarter
ITID-14132.notes: Differentiated from theft/recovery-based unauthorized badge use by consent: the badge owner knowingly and voluntarily lent their credential here.

playbook.name: Response: Authorized Employee Lending Badge to Unauthorized Person
playbook.description: For an authorized employee found lending their access badge to an unauthorized individual (a colleague without their own badge, a visitor, etc).

steps.title: Confirm the badge-lending event
steps.desc: Review CCTV against badge logs to confirm a mismatch between the badge holder of record and the person who entered.
steps.outcome: Lending event confirmed.

steps.title: Retrieve the badge and confirm it's back with its rightful holder
steps.desc: Ensure the badge is returned to the assigned employee and not left with the borrower.
steps.outcome: Credential back in the correct hands.

steps.title: Assess any impact from the unauthorized entrant's access
steps.desc: Determine whether the borrower accessed anything sensitive.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: Address with the employee per policy
steps.desc: Badge sharing is typically a clear policy violation — coach for a first, low-impact instance; involve HR/management for repeat or higher-risk instances.
steps.guidance: Calibrate the response to intent and impact — helping a colleague who forgot their badge is different from lending it to someone unaffiliated.
steps.outcome: Appropriate corrective or disciplinary action taken.

steps.title: Reinforce badge policy and log the incident
steps.desc: Log the incident; if this is a recurring problem, consider awareness campaigns or process fixes (e.g., easier temp-badge issuance for people who forget theirs).
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced; pattern tracked.

steps.title: Identify who used the badge and what they accessed
steps.desc: Determine the identity of the person who used the borrowed badge and what areas they subsequently entered.
steps.outcome: Identity and access scope determined where possible.

ITID-14133.def: An employee's access-control profile grants entry to one or more restricted areas that are not required for their current job function, identified through an access review or audit.
ITID-14133.purpose: Captures an employee holding physical access privileges to a restricted area beyond what their job role requires — excessive physical access provisioning, the physical-world analog of excessive logical privilege.
scopeIncludes: Access-review findings of a physical access grant exceeding job requirement
Excessive access not yet exploited but identified as a standing risk
scopeExcludes: A specific instance of an employee actually misusing that excessive access to enter an area and cause harm (log the misuse instance under the applicable theft/sabotage/tampering ITID; this leaf covers the standing over-provisioning condition)
ITID-14133.severity: Medium, as a standing risk condition; escalate if exploited.
ITID-14133.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if tied to a highly sensitive area (data center, executive floor, hazardous materials).
ITID-14133.escalation: Escalate to the area owner and access-governance team for remediation.
indicators: Periodic access-review flagging a grant with no corresponding job-role justification
Access grant with no badge-use history for the restricted area over an extended period
vectors: N/A — this is a standing over-provisioning condition rather than an active attack vector
rootCauses: No periodic physical-access recertification process; role changes not triggering access-profile updates
controls: Periodic physical-access recertification tied to job role
Automated access-profile update on role change/transfer
ITID-14133.detection: Access-review/recertification process provides the primary technical signal; badge-use-history analysis supplements it.
ITID-14133.response: Revoke unjustified access grants identified during review.
metrics: Count of excessive physical-access grants identified per review cycle
Percentage of access grants recertified on schedule
ITID-14133.notes: Scope decision: this leaf tracks the standing over-provisioning condition itself; an actual harmful act committed using that excessive access is logged under the applicable substantive ITID (theft, sabotage, tampering) to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: Response: Access Granted to Restricted Area Beyond Job Requirement (Excessive Physical Privilege)
playbook.description: For discovery that an individual holds physical access to a restricted area beyond what their role requires — an access-governance gap rather than an active breach.

steps.title: Confirm the access grant and its scope
steps.desc: Review the individual's badge access profile to confirm exactly which restricted areas they can access and compare against their role's documented requirements.
steps.outcome: Excess access confirmed and scoped.
steps.abort: If access matches a documented business need not reflected in the standard role profile, this may not be excessive — verify with the area owner.

steps.title: Revoke the excess access
steps.desc: Remove access to the restricted area(s) not required for the individual's current role, in coordination with their manager.
steps.outcome: Access rights aligned to actual job requirement.

steps.title: Determine how the excess access was granted
steps.desc: Trace the approval history to understand whether this was a provisioning error, role-change residue, or an improperly approved request.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the over-provisioning identified.

steps.title: Run a broader access review if a systemic gap is found
steps.desc: If the root cause suggests other employees may have similar excess access (e.g., a broken offboarding/role-change process), run a targeted access review.
steps.outcome: Related over-provisioning identified and corrected.

steps.title: Document and tighten access provisioning/review process
steps.desc: Log the finding and recommend periodic physical-access recertification for restricted areas.
steps.outcome: Process improvement logged.

steps.title: Review whether the excess access was actually used
steps.desc: Check badge history for whether the individual has entered the restricted area(s), and if so when and how often.
steps.outcome: Usage history established, informing risk assessment.

ITID-14134.def: Misuse of legitimately held physical access, not clearly matching door-propping, badge-lending, or excessive access-privilege provisioning.
ITID-14134.purpose: Catch-all for physical access abuse that does not fit the more specific door-propping, badge-lending, or excessive-privilege leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14134.severity: Medium; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14134.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the specific abuse pattern is clarified.
indicators: Report of an access-control anomaly of unclear cause
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14134.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14134.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14134.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Physical Access Abuse
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for physical access abuse incidents not covered by the door-propping, badge-lending, or excessive-privilege categories.

steps.title: Document the access abuse as reported
steps.desc: Record what occurred, who was involved, and when.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Correct the access issue
steps.desc: Revoke, restrict, or otherwise correct the access that was abused.
steps.outcome: Access issue resolved.

steps.title: Assess impact and root cause
steps.desc: Determine what was accessed and why the abuse was possible.
steps.outcome: Impact and root cause understood.

steps.title: Address with the individual(s) involved
steps.desc: Coach or escalate to management/HR depending on severity and intent.
steps.outcome: Appropriate follow-up action taken.

steps.title: Document and reinforce access policy
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce relevant physical access policy.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Review CCTV and badge logs
steps.desc: Pull relevant footage and access records to confirm the details.
steps.outcome: Evidence gathered.

ITID-14211.def: Confirmed theft of an individual endpoint device (laptop, phone, tablet) from an employee, desk, or facility, where theft (not loss) is established but no larger pattern is yet identified.
ITID-14211.purpose: Catch-all for a single confirmed device theft logged under the Physical Security Breaches domain, before it is clear whether it fits an organized/warehouse or data-center theft pattern.
scopeIncludes: A single confirmed device theft from an office, desk, or individual
scopeExcludes: A device reported missing with no theft indicated — treated as a loss, not a theft (ITID-13231, Lost Laptop/Mobile Device)
Organized theft-ring activity targeting IT equipment in bulk (ITID-14221)
Data center equipment theft specifically (ITID-14222)
ITID-14211.severity: Medium-High, depending on the data held on the device.
ITID-14211.escalation: Escalate to IT security for a remote-wipe/lock attempt and to assess data exposure.
indicators: Employee report of a missing device with signs of theft (broken lock, witnessed removal)
Asset-tracking/MDM check-in gap following a reported theft
vectors: Opportunistic theft from an unattended desk, bag, or vehicle
rootCauses: Devices left unsecured/unattended in accessible areas
controls: Full-disk encryption on all endpoint devices
Remote wipe/lock (MDM) capability
Cable locks for desk-bound devices
ITID-14211.detection: MDM check-in/last-seen status provides a real technical signal; theft determination itself relies on reporting.
ITID-14211.response: Trigger remote wipe/lock, assess data exposure, and file a physical security incident report.
metrics: Count of confirmed single-device theft incidents per quarter
sops: IT Asset Damage and Loss Reporting SOP
ITID-14211.notes: Scope decision: a device reported missing with no indication of theft is classified as a loss under ITID-13231, not here; this leaf requires theft to be indicated (e.g., signs of forced removal, witnessed taking) rather than simple disappearance.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Device Theft
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for the theft of a corporate device (laptop, phone, tablet, peripheral) from a facility.

steps.title: Confirm the device is missing and not misplaced
steps.desc: Check with the assigned user and search likely locations before treating as confirmed theft.
steps.outcome: Theft confirmed rather than a simple misplacement.
steps.abort: If found, close as a non-incident.

steps.title: Remote-lock or wipe the device if it holds sensitive data
steps.desc: Issue a remote lock/wipe command via MDM and revoke any active sessions/tokens tied to the device.
steps.outcome: Device access and data secured remotely.

steps.title: Assess data exposure risk
steps.desc: Determine whether the device was encrypted and what data it held.
steps.outcome: Exposure risk documented.

steps.title: File a police report and replace the device
steps.desc: Report the theft to law enforcement (required for insurance in most cases) and issue a replacement device.
steps.outcome: Report filed; user re-equipped.

steps.title: Review physical asset security practices
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce cable-lock/storage practices and encryption requirements for portable devices.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced; control gap addressed if found.

steps.title: Review CCTV and badge logs for the device's last known location
steps.desc: Pull footage and access records for the area and time window the device was last seen.
steps.outcome: Evidence of the theft and, where possible, the individual responsible.

ITID-14221.def: An organized group conducts a coordinated theft of IT equipment in bulk from a warehouse, staging area, or shipping/receiving dock, typically for resale.
ITID-14221.purpose: Captures coordinated, bulk theft of IT equipment from a warehouse or staging area by an organized theft ring, distinct from an opportunistic single-device theft.
scopeIncludes: Bulk/multi-unit theft of IT equipment from a warehouse or staging area, with indicators of planning or coordination
scopeExcludes: A single opportunistic device theft (ITID-14211)
Theft of equipment specifically from a data center (ITID-14222)
ITID-14221.severity: High, given the scale and evident planning.
ITID-14221.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, law enforcement, and asset management for a full inventory reconciliation.
indicators: Inventory reconciliation showing multiple units missing at once
Evidence of forced entry, disabled cameras, or coordinated timing at a warehouse/staging area
vectors: Coordinated break-in or insider-assisted access to a warehouse/staging area
Exploiting a shipping/receiving process gap to divert equipment
rootCauses: Insufficient physical security (access control, CCTV, inventory reconciliation) at warehouse/staging locations
controls: Regular inventory reconciliation with variance alerting
Access control and CCTV coverage of warehouse/staging areas
ITID-14221.detection: Inventory reconciliation variance provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14221.response: Engage law enforcement, reconcile full inventory, and review warehouse physical security controls.
metrics: Count of units lost in organized theft incidents per year
Inventory reconciliation variance rate
sops: IT Asset Damage and Loss Reporting SOP
ITID-14221.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14211 by scale/coordination: bulk, organized theft from a warehouse/staging area, not a single opportunistic device theft.

playbook.name: Response: Organized Theft Ring Targeting IT Equipment Warehouse
playbook.description: For evidence of an organized, likely repeat theft operation targeting bulk IT equipment from a warehouse or storage facility.

steps.title: Conduct a full inventory reconciliation
steps.desc: Reconcile warehouse inventory records against physical stock to determine the full scope and pattern of losses.
steps.outcome: Complete loss scope and pattern (timing, item types) documented.

steps.title: Tighten warehouse access and increase surveillance
steps.desc: Restrict warehouse access to essential personnel, add or reposition cameras, and increase security presence during identified high-risk windows.
steps.outcome: Further loss prevented during investigation.

steps.title: Implement stronger inventory controls
steps.desc: Introduce serialized asset tracking, two-person verification for outbound shipments, and regular cycle counts.
steps.outcome: Detection capability for future loss significantly improved.

steps.title: File a police report and pursue recovery/insurance
steps.desc: Report to law enforcement given the organized/criminal nature, and pursue insurance recovery for the loss.
steps.outcome: Report filed; recovery process underway.

steps.title: Conduct a full warehouse security review
steps.desc: Document findings and drive a broader review of warehouse physical security, access governance, and inventory audit cadence.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive improvement plan logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV, badge logs, and shipping/receiving records for patterns
steps.desc: Look for repeated access by the same individuals, timing correlated with shift changes, or manipulation of receiving records to hide shortages.
steps.guidance: Organized theft often involves an insider with warehouse access — do not limit the review to external actors.
steps.outcome: Pattern and likely method (insider, external, or collusion) identified.
steps.tool: CCTV / badge access system / inventory records

steps.title: Loop in HR/Legal if insider involvement is suspected
steps.desc: If evidence points to employee involvement, coordinate with HR and Legal before taking personnel action.
steps.outcome: Appropriate personnel-matter handling if insiders are implicated.

ITID-14222.def: An actor steals server, storage, or networking equipment from a data center, whether through unauthorized physical access or misuse of legitimate access.
ITID-14222.purpose: Captures theft of equipment specifically from a data center — a distinct, higher-severity target given the concentration of sensitive infrastructure and data.
scopeIncludes: Theft of servers, storage arrays, or networking equipment from a data center facility
scopeExcludes: Theft of general office IT equipment or warehouse-staged equipment (ITID-14221, ITID-14211)
ITID-14222.severity: Critical, given the concentration of sensitive data and infrastructure in a data center.
ITID-14222.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, IT security, and data-breach assessment given the near-certainty of sensitive data on stolen equipment.
indicators: Data center asset-inventory reconciliation showing missing equipment
Access-control log showing an unusual removal-hours access event to the data center floor
vectors: Insider-assisted or forced access to the data center floor followed by equipment removal
Exploiting decommissioning/maintenance access windows to remove active equipment
rootCauses: Insufficient two-person/escort control on data center equipment removal; no chain-of-custody process for equipment leaving the floor
controls: Two-person rule and chain-of-custody logging for all equipment removal from the data center floor
Data center asset-tracking with exit-scan verification
ITID-14222.detection: Data center asset-tracking/exit-scan verification provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14222.response: Treat as a probable data-breach incident and initiate the data-breach assessment process alongside physical investigation.
metrics: Count of confirmed data center equipment theft incidents per year
ITID-14222.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14221/14211 by target location: the data center floor specifically, given the elevated data-sensitivity and severity this warrants.

playbook.name: Response: Data Center Equipment Theft
playbook.description: For theft of equipment (servers, drives, networking gear) from a data center or server room — high sensitivity given potential data exposure.

steps.title: Confirm what equipment is missing and what data it held
steps.desc: Reconcile the data center asset inventory to identify exactly which equipment is missing and what data/systems it hosted.
steps.outcome: Missing equipment and data sensitivity documented.

steps.title: Assess and contain any operational/security impact
steps.desc: Determine if the missing equipment's absence affects service availability or if credentials/keys stored on it pose a further risk, and remediate (failover, credential rotation) as needed.
steps.outcome: Operational and downstream security risk contained.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Work with legal/privacy to determine breach-notification obligations if the missing equipment held unencrypted regulated data.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: File a police report and pursue insurance recovery
steps.desc: Report the theft to law enforcement and pursue any applicable insurance claim.
steps.outcome: Report filed; claim submitted if applicable.

steps.title: Review data center physical security layers
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate cage/rack locking, visitor escort enforcement, and access-review cadence for the data center.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review data center access controls and CCTV
steps.desc: Pull badge logs (including any biometric/mantrap logs), CCTV, and visitor/escort records for the data center over the relevant window.
steps.guidance: Data centers typically have layered access controls — review all layers, not just the outer door.
steps.outcome: Access history and, where possible, footage of the theft.

steps.title: Tighten data center access pending investigation
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict data center access to essential personnel and review all current access grants.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of further loss.

ITID-14223.def: Theft of organizational hardware, not clearly matching an organized theft ring targeting a warehouse/staging area or theft from a data center specifically.
ITID-14223.purpose: Catch-all for hardware theft that does not fit the more specific organized-theft-ring or data-center leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14223.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14223.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the theft context is clarified.
indicators: Report of missing hardware of unclear context
vectors: Activity of unclear method
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14223.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14223.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14223.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Hardware Theft
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for hardware theft incidents not covered by the warehouse or data-center categories.

steps.title: Confirm and scope the missing hardware
steps.desc: Reconcile inventory records to identify exactly what's missing.
steps.outcome: Missing hardware confirmed and scoped.

steps.title: Secure remaining hardware
steps.desc: Restrict access to remaining assets in the affected location.
steps.outcome: Further loss prevented.

steps.title: Assess data/operational exposure
steps.desc: Determine whether the missing hardware held sensitive data or affects operations.
steps.outcome: Exposure risk documented.

steps.title: File a police report and replace as needed
steps.desc: Report to law enforcement and replace/restock as needed.
steps.outcome: Report filed; operations restored.

steps.title: Review asset security controls
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess inventory/access controls for the affected location.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV and access logs
steps.desc: Pull footage and access records for the storage/use location.
steps.outcome: Evidence gathered.

ITID-14231.def: An actor physically steals confidential paper files or records — personnel files, contracts, internal reports — from an office, filing cabinet, or storage area.
ITID-14231.purpose: Captures theft of confidential paper files or records generically, distinct from the more specific financial/legal document theft leaf.
scopeIncludes: Physical theft of confidential paper files/records not specifically financial or legal in nature
scopeExcludes: Theft of specifically financial or legal documents (ITID-14232)
Retrieval of documents already discarded to waste (the Dumpster Diving Type, ITID-11822)
ITID-14231.severity: Medium-High, depending on the sensitivity of the records.
ITID-14231.escalation: Escalate to the affected data owner and, if PII is involved, to data-breach assessment.
indicators: Missing files identified during a records audit or retrieval attempt
Filing cabinet or storage room found forced/disturbed
vectors: Direct removal of files from an unsecured filing cabinet, desk, or records room
rootCauses: Confidential paper records stored without locked cabinets or access logging
controls: Locked, access-logged storage for confidential paper records
Regular records-inventory audit
ITID-14231.detection: Relies on records-audit discovery; limited real-time technical signal.
ITID-14231.response: Determine what records were taken and notify affected data owners/subjects as required.
metrics: Count of confirmed paper-record theft incidents per quarter
ITID-14231.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14232 by document type: general confidential records, versus specifically financial or legal documents. Differentiated from ITID-11822 by disposal state: files taken while still in active storage, not from waste.

playbook.name: Response: Physical Theft of Confidential Paper Files/Records
playbook.description: For the theft of confidential paper files or records (e.g., from a filing cabinet, records room, or office) rather than digital data.

steps.title: Confirm what records are missing and their sensitivity
steps.desc: Determine exactly which files/records are missing and what type of sensitive information (PII, financial, legal, HR) they contained.
steps.outcome: Missing records and their sensitivity documented.

steps.title: Secure remaining records and restrict access
steps.desc: Move remaining sensitive records to more secure storage and restrict access to essential personnel.
steps.outcome: Further theft prevented.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations
steps.desc: Engage legal/privacy to determine whether the missing records trigger regulatory notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Report the theft to law enforcement, particularly given the potential for identity theft or fraud from the missing records.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Review paper-records security and digitization plans
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate locked storage, access logging, or digitization/reduction of paper records retained on-site.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review access to the storage location
steps.desc: Pull badge logs and CCTV for the filing/records area over the likely time window.
steps.outcome: Access history and, where possible, footage of the theft.

ITID-14232.def: An actor physically steals printed financial documents (statements, invoices, payroll records) or legal documents (contracts, litigation files) from an office.
ITID-14232.purpose: Captures theft of specifically financial or legal printed documents, a higher-sensitivity subset of document theft.
scopeIncludes: Physical theft of printed financial statements, invoices, or payroll records
Physical theft of printed contracts or litigation/legal files
scopeExcludes: Theft of general confidential paper records not financial or legal in nature (ITID-14231)
ITID-14232.severity: High, given the direct financial fraud and legal-exposure risk.
ITID-14232.priority: P1, escalating given potential for direct financial fraud.
ITID-14232.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/legal and, if account numbers or PII are involved, to data-breach assessment.
indicators: Missing financial/legal files identified during an audit or retrieval attempt
Suspicious financial activity following the disappearance of financial documents
vectors: Direct removal of financial/legal files from an unsecured office or storage area
rootCauses: Financial/legal records stored without locked cabinets or restricted access
controls: Locked, access-restricted storage for financial and legal records
Regular records-inventory audit for financial/legal document stores
ITID-14232.detection: Relies on records-audit discovery or downstream fraud detection; limited real-time technical signal.
ITID-14232.response: Notify finance/legal, monitor for related fraud, and notify affected parties as required.
metrics: Count of confirmed financial/legal document theft incidents per year
ITID-14232.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14231 by document sensitivity/type: financial or legal documents specifically, warranting a higher default severity/priority than general confidential records.

playbook.name: Response: Theft of Printed Financial or Legal Documents from Office
playbook.description: For theft of printed financial or legal documents (e.g., contracts, statements, audit materials) from an office workspace.

steps.title: Confirm what documents are missing and their content
steps.desc: Identify exactly which documents were taken and what financial/legal information they contained.
steps.outcome: Missing documents and their sensitivity documented.

steps.title: Secure remaining sensitive documents
steps.desc: Move remaining sensitive printed material to locked storage and reinforce clean-desk practices.
steps.outcome: Further theft prevented.

steps.title: Assess legal/financial impact and notify Legal
steps.desc: Engage Legal to assess implications (e.g., contract confidentiality breach, insider-trading risk if financial data) and determine notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and appropriate parties notified.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Report the theft to law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Reinforce clean-desk and locked-storage policy
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce policy for handling printed financial/legal documents.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Review office access and CCTV
steps.desc: Pull badge and camera logs for the office area over the likely time window.
steps.outcome: Access history and, where possible, footage of the theft.

ITID-14233.def: Physical theft of documents, not clearly matching general confidential records or specifically financial/legal documents.
ITID-14233.purpose: Catch-all for document theft that does not fit the general confidential-records or financial/legal leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14233.severity: Medium; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14233.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the document type is clarified.
indicators: Report of missing documents of unclear type
vectors: Activity of unclear method
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14233.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14233.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14233.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Document Theft
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for document theft incidents not covered by the confidential-files or financial/legal-documents categories.

steps.title: Confirm what documents are missing
steps.desc: Identify exactly which documents are missing and their content sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Scope documented.

steps.title: Secure remaining documents
steps.desc: Restrict access to remaining sensitive material.
steps.outcome: Further theft prevented.

steps.title: Assess exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Engage legal/privacy if regulated data was involved.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Reinforce document handling policy
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce clean-desk/secure-storage policy.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Review access and CCTV
steps.desc: Pull badge and camera logs for the relevant area and time window.
steps.outcome: Evidence gathered.

ITID-14311.def: An adversary or insider deliberately physically destroys an endpoint device — laptop, desktop, mobile phone — through force, fire, water, or another destructive method, rather than removing or modifying it.
ITID-14311.purpose: Captures deliberate physical destruction of an endpoint device (crushing, smashing, submerging) intended to destroy the device or the data on it.
scopeIncludes: Deliberately smashing, crushing, or submerging a device to destroy it or its data
scopeExcludes: Modifying device hardware without destroying it (ITID-14312)
Sabotage of facility-level equipment/machinery rather than an individual endpoint (ITID-14615)
ITID-14311.severity: High, given potential data loss and evidentiary destruction.
ITID-14311.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the device held irreplaceable data or is evidence in an active investigation.
ITID-14311.escalation: Escalate to IT and, if data loss is confirmed, to data-breach/incident-response assessment.
indicators: Device reported physically destroyed with no accidental-damage explanation
Damage pattern inconsistent with accidental drop/impact
vectors: Deliberate physical force, fire, or liquid used against a device
rootCauses: Insufficient physical security of the device at the time of destruction; motive tied to data destruction or insurance fraud
controls: Endpoint backup and disk-image redundancy
Asset tracking with tamper/damage reporting
ITID-14311.detection: Relies on physical inspection and asset-management reporting; no network telemetry.
ITID-14311.response: Determine whether data is recoverable from backup and whether destruction was intended to conceal wrongdoing.
metrics: Count of confirmed deliberate device-destruction incidents per quarter
sops: IT Asset Damage and Loss Reporting SOP
ITID-14311.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14312 by outcome: destruction (device rendered inoperable/data destroyed) versus modification (device altered but still functional).

playbook.name: Response: Physical Damage to Endpoint Device (Deliberate Destruction)
playbook.description: For a laptop, desktop, or peripheral found deliberately damaged/destroyed rather than lost, stolen, or accidentally broken.

steps.title: Photograph and document the damaged device in place
steps.desc: Before moving or attempting repair, photograph the device, its location, and any surrounding damage or disturbance.
steps.guidance: Treat the immediate area as a scene until intent is established — evidence can be lost by tidying up prematurely.
steps.outcome: Dated photo/log record of the device's condition and location.

steps.title: Pull badge access and CCTV for the area and time window
steps.desc: Request door badge logs and camera footage covering the device's location for the period the damage likely occurred.
steps.outcome: Footage/logs identifying who had access to the area at the relevant time.

steps.title: Assess data loss/exposure risk
steps.desc: Determine whether the device's storage is recoverable and whether it held unencrypted sensitive data.
steps.guidance: If the drive is intact, have IT attempt imaging/recovery before final disposal.
steps.outcome: Data-loss and exposure risk documented.

steps.title: Replace hardware and restore the user's environment
steps.desc: Issue replacement hardware and restore the user's profile/data from the last known-good backup.
steps.outcome: User back to normal working capability.

steps.title: Document the incident and review area security controls
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and assess whether camera coverage, access restrictions, or after-hours monitoring in that area need improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; control gap addressed if identified.

steps.title: Determine whether the damage was deliberate
steps.desc: Interview the assigned user and any nearby staff, and inspect the damage pattern for signs consistent with intentional destruction (e.g., forced impact, multiple devices targeted, no plausible accidental cause).
steps.outcome: Classification confirmed as deliberate vs. accidental damage.
steps.abort: If clearly accidental, redirect to standard asset-damage/replacement process instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Inventory and inspect nearby assets
steps.desc: Check other devices and equipment in the same area for tampering or damage to rule out a broader incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope — isolated incident or part of a wider pattern.

steps.title: Escalate to physical security lead and consider law enforcement
steps.desc: For destruction suggesting intent to harm operations or destroy evidence (vs. a minor incident), engage the physical security lead and evaluate filing a police report.
steps.outcome: Appropriate escalation decision made and documented.

ITID-14312.def: An adversary physically opens and modifies an endpoint device's hardware — installing an implant, keylogger, or altered component — without destroying the device, so it continues to appear and function normally.
ITID-14312.purpose: Captures unauthorized physical modification of device hardware — implants, added components, or altered internals — while leaving the device outwardly functional.
scopeIncludes: Installing a hardware keylogger or implant inside/attached to a device
Swapping or altering internal components without the user's knowledge
scopeExcludes: Deliberate destruction of the device (ITID-14311)
Covert surveillance devices such as hidden cameras/GPS trackers planted in a space or on a vehicle (ITID-14731/14732, already documented)
ITID-14312.severity: High, given the covert and potentially data-exfiltrating nature.
ITID-14312.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security/forensics upon discovery of any unauthorized hardware modification.
indicators: Unexpected hardware component found during inspection/audit
Device exhibiting unexplained behavior (extra USB device enumeration, unexpected weight/seal tampering)
vectors: Brief unsupervised physical access used to install an implant
Supply-chain interdiction prior to device deployment
rootCauses: Devices left unattended without tamper-evident seals; no periodic hardware inspection program
controls: Tamper-evident seals on device chassis
Periodic physical hardware inspection/audit program
ITID-14312.detection: Physical inspection and tamper-seal verification provide the primary signal; USB device enumeration monitoring can supplement.
ITID-14312.response: Quarantine and forensically examine the device; assume compromise until proven otherwise.
metrics: Count of confirmed hardware-implant discoveries per year
sops: IT Asset Damage and Loss Reporting SOP
ITID-14312.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14731/14732 (covert surveillance device placement), which covers standalone devices placed in a room/vehicle, not modification of the endpoint device's own internals.

playbook.name: Response: Unauthorized Physical Modification of Device Hardware
playbook.description: For a device found with unauthorized internal hardware changes (e.g., an implanted skimmer, rogue USB/network implant, added chip, or swapped component).

steps.title: Confirm and document the hardware modification
steps.desc: Physically inspect the device, photograph the modification in place, and note make/model/serial of any foreign component found.
steps.guidance: Do not power-cycle or plug the device into the network if an implant is suspected — isolate it first.
steps.outcome: Modification documented with photos and component details.

steps.title: Isolate the device from the network
steps.desc: Immediately disconnect the affected device from wired/wireless networks and power it down if an active implant is suspected.
steps.outcome: Device isolated, preventing further data capture or exfiltration.

steps.title: Remove the foreign component and forensically image the device
steps.desc: Preserve the implant and device for forensic analysis, then remove the modification and restore the device to a known-good hardware/firmware baseline.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal/forensics before disturbing the implant if criminal referral is likely.
steps.outcome: Device restored to trusted state; implant retained as evidence.

steps.title: Return device to service and monitor
steps.desc: Redeploy the device after validation and place it under closer monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Device operating normally with no recurrence.

steps.title: Review physical custody controls for the device type
steps.desc: Assess tamper-evident seals, supply-chain checks, and physical access restrictions for this class of device.
steps.outcome: Control recommendation logged.

steps.title: Determine when and where the modification could have occurred
steps.desc: Review the device's custody/maintenance history and badge/camera logs for the location(s) it has been in.
steps.outcome: A window of opportunity and likely location identified.

steps.title: Check like devices in the same area or batch
steps.desc: Inspect other devices of the same type/location (e.g., other point-of-sale terminals, kiosks) for the same modification.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected devices identified.

ITID-14313.def: Unauthorized physical tampering with an endpoint device, not clearly matching deliberate destruction or hardware modification.
ITID-14313.purpose: Catch-all for device tampering that does not fit the more specific destruction or hardware-modification leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (destruction, hardware modification)
ITID-14313.severity: Medium; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14313.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once intent/method is clarified.
indicators: Report of a device found in an altered or unexplained state
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14313.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Device Tampering
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for device tampering incidents that do not clearly fit deliberate destruction or hardware modification categories.

steps.title: Document the reported tampering
steps.desc: Record what was found, by whom, when, and the device's condition, with photos.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Isolate and secure the affected device
steps.desc: Remove the device from active use/network access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Device secured against further tampering or misuse.

steps.title: Inspect and remediate the device
steps.desc: Have IT inspect the device for functional or security impact and remediate or replace as needed.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed safe to return to service or replaced.

steps.title: Return device to service
steps.desc: Restore normal use of the device or its replacement.
steps.outcome: User/business operations back to normal.

steps.title: Log the incident and note any pattern
steps.desc: Record for trend analysis — repeated tampering in an area may indicate a bigger physical security gap.
steps.outcome: Incident logged and searchable for future correlation.

steps.title: Classify the tampering type
steps.desc: Determine whether this is better classified as destruction, hardware modification, or another specific tampering type, and reroute if a more specific playbook applies.
steps.outcome: Correct classification confirmed.
steps.abort: If a specific tampering ITID clearly applies, use that playbook instead.

steps.title: Review access logs for the device's location
steps.desc: Pull badge and camera records for the area where the device is kept.
steps.outcome: Candidate list of who had physical access.

ITID-14321.def: An adversary physically obstructs, redirects, covers, or disables a security camera at the camera itself — spray, tape, physical redirection, or power disconnection — to blind coverage of an area.
ITID-14321.purpose: Captures direct physical obstruction or disabling of a security camera, distinct from tampering with the recording system it feeds.
scopeIncludes: Spraying/covering a camera lens
Physically redirecting a camera's field of view
Cutting power/data at the camera unit itself
scopeExcludes: Tampering with the CCTV recording system or feed downstream of the camera (ITID-14323)
Tampering with motion/alarm sensors rather than cameras (ITID-14322)
ITID-14321.severity: High, given it directly precedes further unauthorized activity.
ITID-14321.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security; treat as a strong precursor to an imminent intrusion.
indicators: Camera health-monitoring alert (loss of signal/obstructed view)
CCTV footage showing an object thrown/sprayed at the lens immediately before signal loss
vectors: Spray paint, tape, or physical redirection applied to a camera
Cutting camera power/data cabling
rootCauses: Cameras mounted within reach without protective housing; no automated camera-health alerting
controls: Automated camera-health/signal-loss alerting
Tamper-resistant camera housings mounted out of reach
ITID-14321.detection: Camera health-monitoring systems provide a real, immediate technical signal.
ITID-14321.response: Dispatch security to the affected area immediately upon a camera-health alert.
metrics: Count of camera obstruction/disablement events per quarter
Mean time to dispatch after a camera-health alert
ITID-14321.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14323 by point of attack: the camera unit itself, not the downstream recording system or feed.

playbook.name: Response: Security Camera Physically Obstructed or Disabled
playbook.description: For a CCTV camera found blocked, covered, redirected, or powered off, potentially to enable another act.

steps.title: Confirm the camera's status and last-known-good footage
steps.desc: Verify whether the camera is obstructed, physically turned, disconnected, or powered down, and pull the last footage before it went dark.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fault mode and the last usable footage timestamp.

steps.title: Dispatch security to physically restore the camera
steps.desc: Send a guard or facilities technician to clear the obstruction or restore power/connection.
steps.outcome: Camera returned to normal operation and confirmed recording.

steps.title: Inspect for physical tampering evidence and harden mounting
steps.desc: Check for cut cables, forced housing, or repositioned brackets, and repair/harden the mount to resist re-tampering.
steps.outcome: Camera restored to a tamper-resistant state.

steps.title: Verify continuous recording is restored
steps.desc: Confirm the camera feed is recording reliably over a follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Sustained normal operation confirmed.

steps.title: Document and consider added protection (housing, alerting)
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate tamper-alert features, protective housings, or redundant coverage for this camera.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Check for a related incident in the camera's blind spot
steps.desc: Review adjacent camera coverage, badge logs, and alarm events for the area during the outage window for signs the obstruction enabled another act (theft, unauthorized entry).
steps.outcome: Determined whether the disablement coincided with another incident.

steps.title: Increase patrol coverage of the affected area
steps.desc: Add guard patrols or temporary compensating coverage while the camera issue is resolved and investigated.
steps.outcome: Area covered despite the camera gap.

ITID-14322.def: An adversary physically tampers with a motion detector, alarm sensor, or contact sensor — masking, misaligning, or disconnecting it — to prevent an intrusion alarm from triggering.
ITID-14322.purpose: Captures tampering with motion or alarm sensors specifically, to avoid triggering an intrusion alert rather than to blind a camera.
scopeIncludes: Masking or misaligning a motion/PIR sensor
Disconnecting or bypassing an alarm contact sensor
scopeExcludes: Tampering with a security camera (ITID-14321)
Sabotage of the access-control door hardware itself (the Door Access Tampering group, ITID-14331-14333)
ITID-14322.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security; treat as a strong precursor to an imminent intrusion.
indicators: Alarm panel trouble/tamper signal from a specific sensor zone
Sensor found physically covered, misaligned, or disconnected during inspection
vectors: Applying tape/foam to mask a motion sensor's field of view
Physically disconnecting a sensor's wiring
rootCauses: Sensors mounted within reach; alarm panel not configured to alert on sensor tamper/trouble signals
controls: Alarm panel tamper/trouble-signal monitoring enabled and alerted on
Sensors mounted out of reach or in tamper-resistant housings
ITID-14322.detection: Alarm panel tamper/trouble-signal monitoring provides a real, immediate technical signal.
ITID-14322.response: Dispatch security immediately upon any sensor tamper/trouble alert.
metrics: Count of sensor tamper alerts per quarter
Mean time to dispatch after a tamper alert
ITID-14322.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14321 (cameras) and the Door Access Tampering group (locks/wiring); this leaf is scoped to motion/alarm sensor hardware specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Motion Sensor/Alarm Sensor Tampered to Avoid Detection
playbook.description: For an alarm/motion sensor found bypassed, blocked, or disabled to allow undetected movement through a monitored area.
