steps.title: Confirm the sensor fault and time of disablement
steps.desc: Pull the alarm panel's event log to determine when the sensor stopped reporting or was placed in bypass/test mode.
steps.outcome: Timestamp and mode of disablement confirmed.

steps.title: Restore the sensor and re-arm the zone
steps.desc: Have facilities/alarm vendor restore the sensor to active monitoring and re-arm the security zone.
steps.outcome: Zone back under active monitoring.

steps.title: Inspect for physical tamper evidence and secure wiring/enclosure
steps.desc: Check sensor wiring and housing for cut leads, magnets, or shielding used to defeat it, and harden against reuse.
steps.outcome: Sensor hardened against the same bypass technique.

steps.title: Test and verify sensor reliability
steps.desc: Run a test activation and confirm normal alerting resumes.
steps.outcome: Sensor confirmed fully functional.

steps.title: Document and review alarm zone design
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether redundant sensors or tamper-alerting hardware are warranted for this zone.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Cross-check adjacent coverage for unauthorized movement
steps.desc: Review nearby cameras and door logs for movement through the area during the disablement window.
steps.outcome: Determined whether the sensor gap was exploited.

steps.title: Deploy compensating guard patrols
steps.desc: Assign temporary patrols to the affected zone until the sensor is confirmed reliable.
steps.outcome: Area covered during the gap.

ITID-14323.def: An adversary sabotages the CCTV recording system, storage, or video feed — deleting footage, looping a static feed, or disabling the recorder — so that camera coverage exists but is not captured or preserved.
ITID-14323.purpose: Captures sabotage of the CCTV recording infrastructure itself — the DVR/NVR, storage, or feed — rather than the cameras that feed it.
scopeIncludes: Deleting or overwriting recorded CCTV footage
Looping a static/pre-recorded feed to a monitoring station
Physically disabling the DVR/NVR or its storage
scopeExcludes: Obstructing or disabling the camera unit itself (ITID-14321)
ITID-14323.severity: High, given the evidentiary and forensic impact.
ITID-14323.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and IT; preserve any remaining logs/metadata as evidence.
indicators: Gap or anomaly in the CCTV recording timeline
NVR/DVR system health alert or unexpected reboot/configuration change log
vectors: Physical access to the DVR/NVR to delete footage or disable recording
Feed substitution/looping at the recorder or transmission point
rootCauses: DVR/NVR located in an insufficiently access-controlled area; no off-site/redundant footage retention
controls: Off-site or cloud-redundant footage retention
Restricted, logged access to the DVR/NVR room
Recording-system health/heartbeat monitoring
ITID-14323.detection: Recording-system health monitoring and footage-timeline gap analysis provide a real technical signal.
ITID-14323.response: Investigate any recording gap immediately and check for physical access to the DVR/NVR at that time.
metrics: Count of recording-timeline gaps investigated per quarter
ITID-14323.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14321 by point of attack: the recording/storage infrastructure downstream of the camera, not the camera unit itself.

playbook.name: Response: CCTV Recording System Sabotaged or Feed Looped
playbook.description: For evidence that the CCTV recording system (DVR/NVR) itself was tampered with, or a feed was looped/spoofed to hide activity.

steps.title: Confirm the recording gap or loop and its extent
steps.desc: Compare recorded footage timestamps against real-world events to detect gaps, frozen frames, or a repeating loop, and identify which cameras/DVR channels are affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of the sabotage — which feeds, how long.

steps.title: Secure the DVR/NVR and preserve remaining evidence
steps.desc: Physically secure the recording equipment room and export/preserve any surviving footage before it is overwritten.
steps.guidance: Recording systems often overwrite on a cycle — act quickly to preserve evidence.
steps.outcome: Remaining footage preserved; equipment room access-restricted.

steps.title: Restore integrity of the recording system
steps.desc: Reset compromised credentials, patch/reconfigure the DVR/NVR, and verify recordings are genuine going forward.
steps.outcome: Recording system confirmed trustworthy again.

steps.title: Confirm sustained normal recording
steps.desc: Monitor the system over a follow-up period to confirm no further gaps or anomalies.
steps.outcome: Normal, continuous recording confirmed.

steps.title: Document and consider referral if concealing another crime
steps.desc: Log the incident; if the sabotage appears intended to conceal a separate offense, coordinate with legal/law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Check physical and network access to the DVR/NVR
steps.desc: Review who had physical access to the recording equipment room and whether it was accessed remotely, per badge and system logs.
steps.outcome: Access history to the recording system established.
steps.tool: Badge access system / DVR admin logs

steps.title: Restrict administrative access to the CCTV system
steps.desc: Review and tighten who holds credentials capable of altering recordings or feeds.
steps.outcome: Administrative access reduced to essential personnel only.

ITID-14324.def: Unauthorized disablement or tampering with a security camera or sensor, not clearly matching camera obstruction, alarm-sensor tampering, or CCTV-recording sabotage.
ITID-14324.purpose: Catch-all for camera or sensor disablement that does not fit the more specific camera, alarm-sensor, or CCTV-recording-system leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14324.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14324.priority: P2 by default given the security-blinding nature of this Type.
ITID-14324.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the specific system affected is clarified.
indicators: Report of a security system malfunction of unclear cause
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
General security-system health monitoring
ITID-14324.detection: Relies on initial human reporting or generic health alerts pending further triage.
ITID-14324.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14324.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Camera or Sensor Disablement
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for camera or sensor disablement incidents not covered by a more specific category.

steps.title: Confirm which device is disabled and since when
steps.desc: Identify the specific camera or sensor, its status, and the time it stopped functioning normally.
steps.outcome: Device and outage window confirmed.

steps.title: Restore the device to normal operation
steps.desc: Dispatch facilities/security to fix or re-enable the device.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed back in service.

steps.title: Inspect for tamper evidence and harden as needed
steps.desc: Check for signs of deliberate interference and reinforce mounting/wiring/enclosure.
steps.outcome: Device hardened against recurrence.

steps.title: Verify sustained normal function
steps.desc: Confirm the device operates reliably over a follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Normal operation confirmed.

steps.title: Log the incident for trend tracking
steps.desc: Record details to spot repeated disablement patterns across the site.
steps.outcome: Incident logged.

steps.title: Check for a related incident during the outage
steps.desc: Review adjacent coverage and access logs for signs the disablement enabled another act.
steps.outcome: Determined whether the gap coincided with another event.

ITID-14331.def: An adversary defeats a door's lock mechanism through mechanical means — lock picking, bumping, shimming, or force — without involving the electronic access-control system.
ITID-14331.purpose: Captures a purely mechanical bypass of a door lock — picking, bumping, shimming, or forcing the lock hardware itself.
scopeIncludes: Lock picking, bumping, or shimming a mechanical lock
Forcing/prying a lock or strike plate
scopeExcludes: Tampering with the electronic access-control wiring/controller to force an unlock (ITID-14332)
ITID-14331.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security upon signs of forced or picked entry.
indicators: Tool marks or scratching around a lock cylinder/strike plate
Door found unlocked/open with no corresponding valid badge/key event
vectors: Lock picking or bump-key attack against a mechanical cylinder
Prying or forcing a door/strike plate
rootCauses: Mechanical locks used on high-value doors without supplementary electronic access control or reinforced hardware
controls: High-security/pick-resistant lock cylinders on sensitive doors
Door-position sensors alerting on unauthorized opening
ITID-14331.detection: Physical inspection for tool marks and door-position sensor alerting provide a real technical signal.
ITID-14331.response: Inspect the lock for tool marks and cross-check against the access-control log for the affected door.
metrics: Count of confirmed mechanical lock-bypass incidents per quarter
ITID-14331.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14332 by mechanism: purely mechanical lock defeat, not manipulation of the electronic access-control system.

playbook.name: Response: Door Lock Mechanism Physically Bypassed or Picked
playbook.description: For a door lock found picked, shimmed, or otherwise physically bypassed rather than defeated electronically.

steps.title: Inspect the lock for tool marks and bypass method
steps.desc: Examine the lock and door frame for scratches, shim marks, or damage consistent with picking or forcing, and photograph the evidence.
steps.guidance: Avoid handling the lock more than necessary if a criminal referral is likely — fingerprint/tool evidence can be present.
steps.outcome: Bypass method and evidence documented.

steps.title: Secure or guard the compromised door
steps.desc: Post a guard, apply a temporary supplementary lock, or restrict the area until the lock is repaired/replaced.
steps.outcome: Door no longer a viable entry point.

steps.title: Replace or upgrade the lock hardware
steps.desc: Replace the compromised lock, ideally with pick/bump-resistant hardware or upgrade to electronic access control.
steps.outcome: Door restored to a secure state.

steps.title: Verify the door secures properly
steps.desc: Test the repaired/replaced lock to confirm it latches and locks correctly.
steps.outcome: Door confirmed secure.

steps.title: Document and consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: Log the incident; if entry led to theft or other crime, file a police report and retain evidence.
steps.outcome: Incident logged; referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Review badge logs and CCTV for the door and time window
steps.desc: Pull door/badge event logs (which should show no valid badge event if bypassed) and adjacent camera footage.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no legitimate access event, and footage of who used the bypassed door if captured.

steps.title: Check what the door protects for signs of intrusion
steps.desc: Inspect the space behind the door for missing/disturbed items or other signs of entry.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the bypass was actually exploited to enter.

ITID-14332.def: An adversary physically accesses and manipulates an electronic access-control door's wiring, controller, or strike-relay to force it into an unlocked state, bypassing the credential-check process entirely.
ITID-14332.purpose: Captures tampering with an electronic door access-control system's wiring or controller to force an unlock, distinct from purely mechanical lock defeat.
scopeIncludes: Manipulating access-control wiring/relay at the door controller to force an unlock
Shorting or bridging a door strike to bypass credential validation
scopeExcludes: Purely mechanical lock picking/bumping/forcing (ITID-14331)
Using a cloned or forged badge to obtain a legitimate-looking credential check (the Badge Forgery branch, ITID-14121-14123)
ITID-14332.severity: High, given it bypasses the access-control system entirely without leaving a credential log entry.
ITID-14332.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and facilities/IT for the access-control system.
indicators: Door unlock event with no corresponding badge-read/credential log entry
Access-control panel found opened or wiring found disturbed/exposed
vectors: Accessing an exposed door controller or wiring conduit to force the strike relay
Physically bridging or shorting the strike-control circuit
rootCauses: Access-control wiring/controllers mounted in accessible, unsecured locations
controls: Access-control wiring/controllers secured in locked, tamper-monitored enclosures
Door-unlock-without-credential-read alerting
ITID-14332.detection: Access-control log reconciliation (unlock event vs. credential read) provides a real technical signal.
ITID-14332.response: Investigate any unlock event lacking a corresponding credential-read log entry.
metrics: Count of unlock-without-credential-read events per quarter
ITID-14332.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14331 by mechanism: manipulation of the electronic access-control wiring/controller, not the mechanical lock cylinder itself.

playbook.name: Response: Door Access Control Wiring Tampered to Force Unlock
playbook.description: For electronic door access control wiring found manipulated (e.g., shorted, bridged, or exposed) to force a door unlocked bypassing badge authentication.

steps.title: Inspect the access control panel and wiring for tampering
steps.desc: Examine the reader, controller, and exposed wiring at the door for signs of splicing, bridging, or forced unlock devices.
steps.outcome: Tampering method documented with photos.

steps.title: Isolate and physically guard the door
steps.desc: Post a guard or apply a supplementary physical lock until wiring is repaired.
steps.outcome: Door no longer exploitable.

steps.title: Repair wiring and harden the installation
steps.desc: Repair the wiring, relocate exposed conduit/leads where possible, and add tamper-alerting on the controller enclosure.
steps.outcome: Door restored to secure, tamper-resistant operation.

steps.title: Test and confirm normal badge operation
steps.desc: Test the door with a valid badge and confirm it rejects unauthorized unlock attempts.
steps.outcome: Door confirmed functioning correctly and securely.

steps.title: Document and review access-controlled door hardening standards
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether other doors of the same install type share the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; sitewide check performed if pattern identified.

steps.title: Review access control system logs for the forced-open event
steps.desc: Check the access control panel's event log for a door-forced or unauthorized-unlock alarm, and correlate with CCTV.
steps.outcome: Time of forced unlock confirmed, and footage of who used it if captured.

steps.title: Check the controller for further compromise
steps.desc: Verify the access control panel's firmware/configuration has not also been altered, and that no rogue credentials were added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the system's integrity beyond the wiring itself.

ITID-14333.def: An adversary props open or disables the self-closing/alarm mechanism of a fire exit or emergency-only door to create an unauthorized, unmonitored entry point.
ITID-14333.purpose: Captures propping or disabling a fire exit or emergency door specifically, a distinct control surface because these doors are designed for outward egress and often lack inbound credential checks.
scopeIncludes: Propping open a fire exit/emergency door for later entry
Disabling the door-alarm or self-closing mechanism on an emergency exit
scopeExcludes: Propping a general secondary/side door such as a smoking-area door not designated as a fire exit (ITID-11816)
ITID-14333.severity: High, given both the security bypass and life-safety implications.
ITID-14333.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and facilities/life-safety compliance.
indicators: Fire-exit door alarm sounding or found disabled during inspection
Door-held-open sensor alert on a designated emergency-exit door
vectors: Physically propping a fire-exit door with an object
Taping over or disabling the exit's local alarm sounder
rootCauses: Fire-exit door alarms not centrally monitored; routine inspection of emergency egress hardware not performed
controls: Centrally monitored fire-exit door alarms
Regular life-safety/emergency-egress hardware inspection
ITID-14333.detection: Fire-exit door alarm monitoring provides a real, immediate technical signal.
ITID-14333.response: Dispatch security immediately upon any fire-exit alarm/held-open alert and coordinate with facilities on hardware repair.
metrics: Count of fire-exit tamper/held-open alerts per quarter
ITID-14333.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11816 by door designation: a fire/emergency exit specifically, not a general informal secondary entrance.

playbook.name: Response: Fire Exit/Emergency Door Propped or Disabled for Unauthorized Entry
playbook.description: For a fire exit or emergency-only door found propped open, its alarm disabled, or its hardware defeated to allow unauthorized entry — this is also a life-safety concern.

steps.title: Confirm the door's current state and safety impact
steps.desc: Physically check the door, its alarm/hardware, and whether it is currently propped or disabled, and assess any immediate fire/life-safety impact.
steps.guidance: Life safety takes priority — if the door's fire function is disabled, treat as urgent facilities issue regardless of security angle.
steps.outcome: Current state confirmed and life-safety risk assessed.

steps.title: Restore the door and its alarm immediately
steps.desc: Remove any prop, restore the door to its normal self-closing/latching state, and re-enable the alarm.
steps.outcome: Door restored to a code-compliant, secure state.

steps.title: Address root cause and consider hardware upgrades
steps.desc: If propping was for employee convenience, address the underlying workflow issue; if deliberately defeated for entry, add tamper-evident or alarmed hardware.
steps.outcome: Reduced likelihood of recurrence.

steps.title: Verify the exit meets fire code and security requirements
steps.desc: Confirm with facilities/fire safety that the door now functions correctly for both emergency egress and security.
steps.outcome: Compliance and security confirmed.

steps.title: Document and, if a known employee propped it, address via corrective coaching
steps.desc: Log the incident; if a known individual propped the door for convenience rather than malicious entry, address through corrective, non-punitive coaching.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and appropriate follow-up completed.

steps.title: Review CCTV and door alarm logs for how/when it was defeated
steps.desc: Pull camera footage of the exit and door alarm system logs to identify when and how it was propped or disabled, and by whom if visible.
steps.outcome: Timeline and likely responsible party (or that it's unclear) established.

steps.title: Check whether unauthorized entry occurred through the door
steps.desc: Inspect nearby areas for signs of unauthorized presence or missing items consistent with entry via this exit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the propped door was actually exploited.

ITID-14334.def: Unauthorized tampering with a door access mechanism, not clearly matching mechanical lock bypass, electronic access-control tampering, or fire-exit propping/disabling.
ITID-14334.purpose: Catch-all for door access tampering that does not fit the more specific mechanical-lock, electronic-wiring, or fire-exit leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14334.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14334.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the specific mechanism affected is clarified.
indicators: Report of a door found in an unexplained unlocked/open state
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14334.detection: Relies on initial human reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14334.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14334.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Door Access Tampering
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for door access tampering incidents not covered by a more specific category (lock bypass, wiring tamper, fire exit misuse).

steps.title: Document the tampering as found
steps.desc: Record which door, what form of tampering, and when it was discovered, with photos.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Secure the door pending repair
steps.desc: Guard, supplement-lock, or otherwise secure the door until it is restored to normal function.
steps.outcome: Door no longer exploitable.

steps.title: Repair the door/hardware
steps.desc: Restore or upgrade the affected hardware to a secure, functioning state.
steps.outcome: Door restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Verify normal operation
steps.desc: Test the door to confirm it functions and secures correctly.
steps.outcome: Confirmed door operating normally.

steps.title: Log the incident for pattern tracking
steps.desc: Record details to identify whether this door or area sees repeated tampering.
steps.outcome: Incident logged.

steps.title: Review badge logs and CCTV for the door
steps.desc: Pull access control event logs and camera footage covering the door for the likely window.
steps.outcome: Candidate access history and possible footage of the act.

ITID-14411.def: An adversary who has obtained shredded paper documents attempts to reconstruct their content by manually or digitally piecing the fragments back together.
ITID-14411.purpose: Captures the specific downstream exploitation technique of reconstructing shredded documents by manually or digitally piecing fragments back together.
scopeIncludes: Manual or digital (e.g., photograph-assisted) reassembly of shredded document fragments
scopeExcludes: Retrieval of intact, unshredded paper documents from waste (ITID-11822, a distinct upstream retrieval step)
ITID-14411.severity: Medium, though effort-intensive and lower-yield than intact document retrieval.
ITID-14411.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if reconstruction of sensitive content is confirmed.
ITID-14411.escalation: Escalate if reconstructed content is confirmed to include sensitive/confidential information.
indicators: Recovered/discarded shred residue found disturbed or reduced in volume
Evidence (e.g., online forum activity, physical evidence) of reconstruction attempts
vectors: Manually sorting and taping together shred-bin fragments
Using imaging/software-assisted reconstruction of cross-cut shred fragments
rootCauses: Use of strip-cut rather than cross-cut/micro-cut shredders for sensitive documents
controls: Use of cross-cut or micro-cut shredders for sensitive documents
Secure, locked collection of shred residue pending certified destruction
ITID-14411.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; relies on physical evidence or downstream misuse of reconstructed content.
ITID-14411.response: Assess what content may have been reconstructable and upgrade shredding standard if strip-cut was used.
metrics: Percentage of sensitive-document disposal using cross-cut/micro-cut shredding
ITID-14411.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11822 by exploitation stage: this leaf covers the reconstruction technique applied to already-shredded material, not the initial retrieval of intact paper.

playbook.name: Response: Paper Shredder Reconstruction (Piecing Together Shredded Documents)
playbook.description: For discovery that shredded documents were retrieved and reconstructed by an unauthorized party to recover sensitive information.

steps.title: Determine what documents were reconstructed and their sensitivity
steps.desc: Identify, as best as possible, which discarded documents were recovered and what sensitive data (PII, financials, credentials, strategy) they contained.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposed information documented.

steps.title: Secure remaining waste and shredding stock
steps.desc: Lock or restrict access to waste bins/dumpsters and shredded-document holding areas to prevent further recovery.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized access to discarded materials prevented.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations
steps.desc: If reconstructed documents contained regulated data (PII, financial, health), engage legal/privacy to determine notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Upgrade destruction method for sensitive paper
steps.desc: Move to cross-cut/micro-cut shredding or a certified third-party destruction service for sensitive document classes.
steps.outcome: Future shredded output no longer practically reconstructable.

steps.title: Document and review waste-handling policy
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether dumpster security (locked enclosures, secured collection scheduling) needs strengthening.
steps.outcome: Policy/control gap identified and addressed.

steps.title: Establish how the waste was accessed
steps.desc: Determine whether the shredded material was taken from a bin, dumpster, or waste holding area, and review CCTV/access logs for that location.
steps.outcome: Access point and, if possible, responsible party identified.

ITID-14412.def: An adversary manually sorts through mixed general waste — not separated by material type — to locate any sensitive documents or materials that happen to be present.
ITID-14412.purpose: Captures manual sorting of mixed, unsegregated waste to locate sensitive materials, distinct from targeting a specific known waste stream.
scopeIncludes: Manually sorting mixed/general waste (not a dedicated paper, e-waste, or recycling stream) to find sensitive materials
scopeExcludes: Targeting a specific, identified waste stream such as paper records or electronic media (the Dumpster Diving Type under Social Engineering, ITID-11822-11826)
Reconstruction of already-shredded material (ITID-14411)
ITID-14412.escalation: Escalate to facilities to review general waste segregation and disposal practices.
indicators: General waste receptacles found disturbed or sorted through
Sensitive materials found improperly placed in general (non-shred) waste during audits
vectors: Manually searching general/mixed waste bins with no specific material target
rootCauses: No waste-segregation policy directing sensitive materials to a dedicated secure-disposal stream
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Waste-segregation policy directing sensitive materials to secure disposal
Employee awareness training on proper disposal segregation
ITID-14412.detection: Relies on physical observation/CCTV of general waste areas.
ITID-14412.response: Audit waste-segregation compliance and reinforce policy.
metrics: Count of waste-segregation policy violations found in audits
ITID-14412.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11822-11826 by targeting: unfocused sorting of mixed general waste, rather than deliberately targeting a specific, known sensitive-material waste stream.

playbook.name: Response: Manual Sorting of Mixed Waste to Locate Sensitive Materials
playbook.description: For discovery that discarded mixed waste (not necessarily shredded) was sorted through by an unauthorized party looking for sensitive materials.

steps.title: Determine what was likely found in the waste
steps.desc: Reconstruct, based on what was discarded around the relevant time, what sensitive items (documents, drives, devices, badges) may have been recoverable.
steps.outcome: Best-effort inventory of exposed items.

steps.title: Secure the waste area
steps.desc: Lock, fence, or move waste receptacles to a controlled-access location.
steps.outcome: Waste no longer accessible to unauthorized parties.

steps.title: Assess exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Determine whether recovered materials contained regulated data and engage legal/privacy for notification obligations if so.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Introduce a secure disposal process
steps.desc: Implement a locked bin/secure-shred program for anything sensitive rather than general waste.
steps.outcome: Sensitive discards no longer end up in general waste.

steps.title: Document and train staff on disposal practices
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce clean-desk/secure-disposal training.
steps.outcome: Awareness improved; recurrence risk reduced.

steps.title: Review CCTV/access to the waste area
steps.desc: Check camera footage and site access logs for the dumpster/waste holding area around the suspected time.
steps.outcome: Footage of the activity and, where possible, identification of the individual(s).

ITID-14413.def: Recovery of information from discarded materials, not clearly matching shredder reconstruction or manual mixed-waste sorting.
ITID-14413.purpose: Catch-all for information recovery from discarded materials that does not fit the shredder-reconstruction or mixed-waste-sorting leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14413.severity: Low-to-Medium; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14413.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the recovery method is clarified.
indicators: Report of discarded-material tampering of unclear method
vectors: Activity of unclear method
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14413.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14413.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14413.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Information Recovery from Discarded Materials
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for information-recovery-from-waste incidents not covered by the shredder-reconstruction or mixed-waste categories.

steps.title: Determine what information may have been recovered
steps.desc: Identify what was discarded and what sensitive content it may have exposed.
steps.outcome: Scope of potential exposure documented.

steps.title: Secure the disposal area
steps.desc: Restrict access to the waste location pending review of disposal practices.
steps.outcome: Further recovery prevented.

steps.title: Assess and address exposure
steps.desc: Engage legal/privacy if regulated data was involved; otherwise document the exposure and close.
steps.outcome: Exposure appropriately handled.

steps.title: Improve disposal controls
steps.desc: Strengthen secure-disposal processes for the material type involved.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of recurrence.

steps.title: Log and communicate the finding
steps.desc: Record the incident and share relevant guidance with affected teams.
steps.outcome: Awareness improved.

steps.title: Review access to the disposal location
steps.desc: Check CCTV/access logs for the relevant waste location and time window.
steps.outcome: Access history established.

ITID-14421.def: An adversary who has obtained a discarded hard drive performs forensic or standard data-recovery techniques to extract data that was not properly wiped prior to disposal.
ITID-14421.purpose: Captures actual data recovery performed on a discarded hard drive that was not properly wiped before disposal — the exploitation step following retrieval.
scopeIncludes: Performing data-recovery/forensic techniques on a retrieved, improperly wiped hard drive
scopeExcludes: The act of retrieving the discarded drive itself from waste (ITID-11823/11824, a distinct upstream retrieval step)
Recovery from a mobile device or SIM card specifically (ITID-14422)
ITID-14421.severity: High, given successful recovery yields the organization's actual data.
ITID-14421.priority: P1 upon any confirmation that data was successfully recovered.
ITID-14421.escalation: Escalate immediately to data-breach assessment upon confirmation of successful recovery.
indicators: Confirmed recovery of organizational data from a disposed drive (e.g., surfaced in a security research disclosure or law-enforcement recovery)
Post-disposal audit revealing a drive was not wiped to the required standard
vectors: Applying standard forensic data-recovery tools to a drive that was not securely wiped
rootCauses: Data-wipe step skipped or improperly verified before physical disposal
controls: Certified data-wipe (or physical destruction) with verification prior to disposal
Chain-of-custody tracking through the disposal/destruction process
ITID-14421.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; typically discovered after the fact via disclosure or downstream data misuse.
ITID-14421.response: Initiate data-breach assessment and determine the full scope of data that may have been on the drive.
metrics: Percentage of decommissioned drives with a verified wipe/destruction certificate
ITID-14421.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11823/11824 by exploitation stage: this leaf covers the data-recovery act performed on a retrieved drive, not the retrieval itself.

playbook.name: Response: Data Recovery from Improperly Wiped Discarded Hard Drive
playbook.description: For discovery that a discarded hard drive was insufficiently wiped and data was recovered from it by an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Identify the drive, its origin system, and data it held
steps.desc: Determine which system/device the drive came from and what data classes it likely contained, using asset-management records.
steps.outcome: Drive identity and probable data content documented.

steps.title: Recall/quarantine similarly disposed drives if a batch failure is suspected
steps.desc: If the failure suggests a systemic issue (e.g., a vendor batch or a broken wipe process), halt further disposals and identify other drives disposed the same way.
steps.outcome: Further exposure from the same failure mode stopped.
steps.abort: If this was a one-off, isolated error, a full recall may not be warranted — document the decision.

steps.title: Assess exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Work with legal/privacy to determine breach-notification obligations based on the data recovered.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Fix and re-verify the disposal/wipe process
steps.desc: Correct the wiping/destruction procedure (e.g., switch to certified physical destruction, add verification step, change vendor) and re-verify on the next batch.
steps.outcome: Disposal process confirmed reliable going forward.

steps.title: Document and audit past disposals
steps.desc: Log the incident and review recent disposal records for similar risk.
steps.outcome: Historical exposure assessed and finding logged.

steps.title: Determine how disposal was handled and where it broke down
steps.desc: Review the asset-disposition record to see whether wiping/destruction was supposed to occur and, if so, why it failed (vendor error, skipped step, etc.).
steps.outcome: Root cause of the improper wipe identified.

ITID-14422.def: An adversary who has obtained a discarded mobile device or SIM card performs forensic recovery techniques to extract contacts, messages, credentials, or other data.
ITID-14422.purpose: Captures forensic data recovery specifically from a discarded mobile device or SIM card, distinct from hard-drive recovery given the different data types and recovery techniques involved.
scopeIncludes: Forensic recovery of data from a retrieved, improperly wiped mobile device or SIM card
scopeExcludes: Data recovery from a hard drive or other computer storage media (ITID-14421)
ITID-14422.severity: High, given mobile devices often hold authentication tokens, MFA app data, and personal/organizational messages.
ITID-14422.priority: P1 upon any confirmation that data was successfully recovered.
ITID-14422.escalation: Escalate immediately to data-breach assessment and force credential/MFA-token rotation for the affected user.
indicators: Confirmed recovery of organizational data from a disposed mobile device or SIM
Post-disposal audit revealing a mobile device was not factory-reset/wiped to the required standard
vectors: Applying mobile forensic tools to a device that was not securely wiped
Extracting SIM-stored contacts/data from an improperly destroyed SIM card
rootCauses: Mobile device decommissioning process lacks a verified factory-reset/wipe step
controls: Verified factory-reset/wipe (or physical destruction) of mobile devices and SIM cards prior to disposal
MDM-enforced remote wipe as part of device decommissioning
ITID-14422.detection: Minimal direct technical detection; typically discovered after the fact.
ITID-14422.response: Initiate data-breach assessment, rotate any credentials/MFA tokens tied to the device, and notify the affected user.
metrics: Percentage of decommissioned mobile devices with a verified wipe confirmation
ITID-14422.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14421 by device type and data category: mobile devices/SIM cards carrying communications and authentication artifacts, versus general computer storage media.

playbook.name: Response: Forensic Recovery from Discarded Mobile Device/SIM Card
playbook.description: For discovery that data was forensically recovered from a discarded mobile device or SIM card that was not properly wiped/destroyed.

steps.title: Identify the device/SIM and the data it likely held
steps.desc: Determine the device's assigned user history, and what corporate data (email, MDM-managed apps, contacts, messages) it may have contained.
steps.outcome: Device identity and probable data content documented.

steps.title: Deactivate the SIM and revoke any lingering account access
steps.desc: Confirm with the carrier the SIM is deactivated, and revoke any corporate accounts/tokens still tied to the device.
steps.outcome: No further live access via the device/SIM.

steps.title: Assess exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Engage legal/privacy to determine breach-notification obligations based on recovered data.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Fix the mobile decommissioning process
steps.desc: Correct the gap in the device retirement workflow (e.g., mandatory MDM wipe confirmation before disposal, physical destruction for devices that can't confirm wipe).
steps.outcome: Process confirmed reliable going forward.

steps.title: Document and audit other recently retired mobile devices
steps.desc: Log the incident and check whether other recently retired devices share the same gap.
steps.outcome: Historical exposure assessed and finding logged.

steps.title: Determine why the standard wipe/decommission process failed
steps.desc: Check MDM records for whether a remote wipe was issued and completed, and whether the SIM was deactivated.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the exposure identified.

ITID-14423.def: Data recovery performed on a discarded device, not clearly matching hard-drive recovery or mobile-device/SIM recovery.
ITID-14423.purpose: Catch-all for device salvaging that does not fit the hard-drive or mobile-device/SIM recovery leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14423.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14423.priority: P2 by default given the data-recovery exploitation stage.
ITID-14423.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the device type is clarified.
indicators: Report of a discarded-device data-recovery attempt of unclear device type
vectors: Activity of unclear device type
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14423.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14423.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14423.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Device Salvaging
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for data recovered from a discarded/salvaged device not covered by the hard-drive or mobile-device categories.

steps.title: Identify the device and data it may have held
steps.desc: Determine the device type, its history, and what data it likely contained.
steps.outcome: Scope of potential exposure documented.

steps.title: Halt further disposals if a systemic issue is suspected
steps.desc: Pause the disposal pipeline for this device type until the gap is understood.
steps.outcome: Further exposure prevented.

steps.title: Assess exposure and notify as required
steps.desc: Engage legal/privacy if regulated data may have been recovered.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if applicable.

steps.title: Fix the disposal process
steps.desc: Correct the wipe/destruction procedure for this device class.
steps.outcome: Process confirmed reliable going forward.

steps.title: Document and audit related disposals
steps.desc: Log the incident and review other recent disposals of the same device type.
steps.outcome: Historical exposure assessed.

steps.title: Determine why disposal controls failed
steps.desc: Review the disposition record to identify the process gap.
steps.outcome: Root cause identified.

ITID-14511.def: An adversary physically presents as someone they are not to gain facility access, logged from a physical-security-breach incident perspective, distinct from the persona-technique taxonomy used for social-engineering-framed impersonation.
ITID-14511.purpose: Catch-all for on-site impersonation logged as a physical-security-breach incident, without a specific persona-technique analysis performed.
scopeIncludes: Physical-security incident reports of impersonation logged without a specific persona identified
scopeExcludes: Impersonation logged with a specific persona identified under the Social Engineering Tier-2 branch (ITID-11831-11839)
ITID-14511.priority: P2 by default given the risk of escalation to further access.
ITID-14511.escalation: Escalate to physical security for documentation.
indicators: Report of an unfamiliar individual claiming a role without verification
vectors: Presenting a fabricated role/identity to facility staff
rootCauses: Insufficient visitor verification process
controls: Visitor verification and escort policy
ITID-14511.response: Document and investigate as a physical-security-breach incident.
metrics: Count of impersonation incidents logged under this Tier-2 branch per quarter
sops: Visitor and Vendor Access Verification SOP
ITID-14511.notes: Scope decision: this leaf exists in parallel with the Social Engineering branch's On-Site Impersonation Type (ITID-11831-11839) to avoid forcing every physical-security impersonation log entry through a persona-classification exercise; use this leaf when no persona analysis is performed, and the Social Engineering branch when the specific persona is identified and relevant to a social-engineering awareness program.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General On-Site Impersonation
playbook.description: For an individual who gained physical access or cooperation on-site by impersonating an employee, contractor, vendor, or other trusted role.

steps.title: Gather witness accounts and details of the impersonation
steps.desc: Interview staff who interacted with the individual to capture description, claimed identity/role, and what access or information they obtained.
steps.outcome: Documented account of the impersonation and its outcome.

steps.title: Revoke any access or credentials issued to the impersonator
steps.desc: Deactivate any temporary badge, guest Wi-Fi, or physical access granted during the interaction.
steps.outcome: No lingering access remains.

steps.title: Assess what was exposed or accessed
steps.desc: Determine what areas, systems, or information the impersonator reached, and take follow-up action (e.g., reviewing anything they touched).
steps.outcome: Full impact scope understood.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: If the impersonation led to theft, sabotage, or a clear criminal act, file a police report.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Reinforce visitor-verification procedures
steps.desc: Log the incident and retrain reception/security staff on ID verification and escalation for unrecognized individuals.
steps.outcome: Verification practices reinforced.

steps.title: Pull CCTV and visitor/badge records
steps.desc: Review camera footage and any visitor sign-in or temporary badge records covering the individual's presence.
steps.outcome: Visual record and access trail of the individual obtained.

steps.title: Alert front-desk/reception and security staff sitewide
steps.desc: Circulate a description and known details so staff can recognize and challenge the individual if they return.
steps.outcome: Site staff aware and prepared.

ITID-14521.def: An adversary triggers a false fire alarm or exploits a scheduled/genuine evacuation to gain access to a facility while normal occupants are evacuating and access controls are bypassed or unattended.
ITID-14521.purpose: Captures an adversary staging or exploiting a fire drill or evacuation event specifically as a pretext to gain facility access, distinct from the responder/worker persona used once an emergency is underway.
scopeIncludes: Triggering a false fire alarm to force an evacuation as an access pretext
Exploiting a genuine evacuation event (drill or real) to slip into the facility against the outbound flow
scopeExcludes: Presenting as an emergency responder/utility worker once an emergency (staged or real) is already in progress (ITID-11839, a persona-based leaf under the Social Engineering branch)
Group/crowd tailgating that exploits ordinary crowding without a staged emergency (ITID-11815)
ITID-14521.severity: High, given evacuation procedures typically disable normal access verification.
ITID-14521.priority: P1 upon any confirmed false-alarm triggering.
ITID-14521.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and facilities; treat any unexplained alarm activation with subsequent unauthorized entry as a coordinated attack.
indicators: Fire alarm activation with no confirmed fire/smoke cause
CCTV showing an individual entering against the outbound evacuation flow
vectors: Manually triggering a fire alarm pull station to force an evacuation
Timing entry to coincide with a scheduled fire drill
rootCauses: Evacuation procedures lack a re-entry verification/headcount process; alarm pull stations not monitored by CCTV
controls: CCTV coverage of alarm pull stations
Post-evacuation re-entry verification/headcount procedure
ITID-14521.detection: Alarm-activation-to-confirmed-cause correlation and CCTV of pull stations provide a real technical signal.
ITID-14521.response: Investigate any unconfirmed alarm activation and reconcile re-entry against the pre-evacuation headcount.
metrics: Count of false-alarm-triggered evacuation events investigated per year
detections: CCTV coverage of alarm pull stations
ITID-14521.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11839 by causal role: this leaf covers staging/exploiting the emergency event itself, while ITID-11839 covers the responder persona used once an emergency is already in play.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Fire Drill/Evacuation Used as Access Pretext
playbook.description: For an incident where a false fire alarm or evacuation was triggered as a pretext to gain unauthorized facility access or bypass security during the confusion.

steps.title: Confirm the alarm was false and how it was triggered
steps.desc: Work with facilities/fire safety to confirm no genuine fire event occurred and identify which alarm point was activated.
steps.outcome: Confirmed false alarm and trigger location.
steps.abort: If there is any doubt about a genuine fire, treat as a real emergency until cleared by fire safety/responders.

steps.title: Account for all personnel and verify no unauthorized individuals remain
steps.desc: Complete the evacuation headcount and check whether anyone unfamiliar entered during the confusion.
steps.outcome: All areas confirmed clear of unauthorized presence.

steps.title: Secure the alarm-triggering mechanism
steps.desc: Inspect and, if needed, add protective covers or camera coverage on accessible pull stations/alarm points to deter reuse.
steps.outcome: Alarm point hardened against casual/deliberate false triggering.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: If the false alarm was used to facilitate theft or another crime, file a police report.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Review evacuation-security procedures
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether evacuation procedures should include securing sensitive areas or a post-evacuation sweep before re-entry.
steps.outcome: Procedure improvement identified.

steps.title: Review CCTV and badge logs during the evacuation window
steps.desc: Check camera footage and access logs for unusual activity, unaccounted individuals, or access-controlled doors used during the chaos.
steps.outcome: Suspicious activity during the evacuation identified if present.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed or taken during the evacuation
steps.desc: Check sensitive areas and assets for signs of tampering, theft, or unauthorized access that coincided with the false alarm.
steps.outcome: Scope of any exploitation determined.

ITID-14522.def: An adversary stages a fake emergency vehicle (ambulance, fire truck) or a group presenting as emergency personnel at a facility's exterior to create a plausible pretext for facility access or staff cooperation.
ITID-14522.purpose: Captures an adversary staging a fake emergency vehicle or personnel presence at a facility as a pretext for access, distinct from triggering an internal alarm/evacuation.
scopeIncludes: Staging a fake or unauthorized emergency vehicle at or near a facility as an access pretext
A group presenting as an emergency response team without a genuine dispatched call
scopeExcludes: Triggering an internal fire alarm/evacuation as the pretext mechanism (ITID-14521)
A single individual presenting as an emergency responder/utility worker once an emergency is already in progress (ITID-11839)
ITID-14522.severity: High, given the elevated authority and urgency the staged vehicle/personnel presence conveys.
ITID-14522.escalation: Escalate immediately and cross-check with local emergency services dispatch.
indicators: No corresponding dispatch record with local emergency services for the vehicle/personnel observed
Vehicle markings/equipment inconsistent with the claimed agency
vectors: Staging an unmarked or improperly marked vehicle resembling an emergency vehicle at the facility
rootCauses: Staff trained to grant immediate cooperation to any emergency vehicle/personnel presence without a verification step
controls: Dispatch verification call as part of the emergency-vehicle-response procedure where feasible
Security desk immediate notification protocol for any unscheduled emergency-vehicle arrival
ITID-14522.detection: Dispatch-record cross-check provides a real technical signal when time permits.
ITID-14522.response: Where safe and time permits, verify with dispatch before granting cooperation/access.
metrics: Count of emergency-vehicle-persona events reconciled against dispatch records
ITID-14522.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14521 by mechanism (staging an external vehicle/team presence rather than triggering an internal alarm) and from ITID-11839 by scope (the staged vehicle/group presence itself, not an individual responder persona already inside an in-progress emergency).

playbook.name: Response: Fake Emergency Vehicle/Personnel Staged for Facility Access
playbook.description: For an incident where an individual used a fake emergency vehicle, uniform, or claimed first-responder role to gain unauthorized facility access.

steps.title: Gather witness accounts and details of the fake responders
steps.desc: Interview staff who interacted with the individual(s) to document vehicle description, claimed agency/role, and what access was granted.
steps.outcome: Documented account with descriptive details.

steps.title: Revoke any access granted and alert site staff
steps.desc: Deactivate any temporary access issued and circulate a description sitewide.
steps.outcome: No lingering access; staff alerted.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed or taken
steps.desc: Determine what areas or assets the individuals reached during the visit.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Impersonating emergency personnel is typically a criminal offense — report to local law enforcement with the gathered evidence.
steps.outcome: Report filed and evidence handed over.

steps.title: Reinforce verification procedures for emergency-responder claims
steps.desc: Log the incident and train reception/security to verify emergency-responder credentials (e.g., confirming with dispatch) before granting expedited access.
steps.outcome: Verification practice reinforced.

steps.title: Verify with local emergency services whether a call was genuine
steps.desc: Contact local fire/police/EMS dispatch to confirm whether any legitimate call or dispatch corresponds to the visit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the visit was not a genuine emergency response.
steps.abort: If it turns out to be genuine, close this as a false positive.

steps.title: Pull CCTV of the vehicle and individuals
steps.desc: Review camera footage capturing the vehicle (plate if visible) and individuals for later identification.
steps.outcome: Visual record obtained for investigation or police report.

ITID-14523.def: A staged fake emergency used as an access pretext, not clearly matching a triggered fire drill/evacuation or a staged emergency vehicle/personnel presence.
ITID-14523.purpose: Catch-all for fake emergency services incidents that do not fit the fire-drill/evacuation or fake-vehicle leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14523.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14523.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the staging mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Report of a suspected fake-emergency pretext of unclear mechanism
vectors: Activity of unclear mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14523.detection: Relies on initial reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14523.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14523.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Emergency Services
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for fake-emergency-services incidents not covered by the fire-drill or emergency-vehicle categories.

steps.title: Gather witness accounts of the claimed emergency
steps.desc: Interview staff involved to capture details of the pretext used and access gained.
steps.outcome: Documented account of the incident.

steps.title: Revoke any access granted and alert staff
steps.desc: Deactivate temporary access and circulate a description sitewide.
steps.outcome: No lingering access; staff alerted.

steps.title: Assess what was accessed or taken
steps.desc: Determine the scope of any exploitation during the incident.
steps.outcome: Impact scope understood.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if warranted by the outcome.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Reinforce verification procedures
steps.desc: Log the incident and retrain staff on verifying emergency claims before granting access.
steps.outcome: Verification practice reinforced.

steps.title: Verify the claimed emergency with the relevant authority
steps.desc: Contact the appropriate agency to confirm whether the emergency claim was genuine.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the claim was false.
steps.abort: If genuine, close as a false positive.

ITID-14611.def: An external or unidentified actor causes property damage to a facility's exterior, signage, landscaping, or grounds, without targeting security hardware, life-safety systems, or on-site equipment specifically.
ITID-14611.purpose: Captures vandalism/property damage to a facility's exterior or grounds — the lowest-severity, most common form of facility sabotage.
scopeIncludes: Graffiti, broken windows, or damaged signage/landscaping on facility exterior or grounds
scopeExcludes: Damage specifically targeting access-control/security hardware (ITID-14612)
Sabotage committed by an insider/employee, which is classified under the Insider Sabotage branch (ITID-13121/13122/13123) rather than this branch
ITID-14611.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if damage recurs or affects security-adjacent infrastructure.
ITID-14611.escalation: Escalate to facilities and, if a pattern emerges, to physical security for surveillance review.
indicators: Facilities report of exterior damage or graffiti with no known cause
Repeated vandalism incidents at the same location
vectors: Opportunistic exterior vandalism by an unidentified external actor
rootCauses: Insufficient exterior lighting/CCTV coverage of perimeter and grounds
controls: Exterior CCTV coverage and lighting
Perimeter patrol
ITID-14611.detection: CCTV of the exterior perimeter, where present, provides a real technical signal; otherwise relies on facilities reporting.
ITID-14611.response: Document damage, repair, and review CCTV if coverage exists.
metrics: Count of exterior vandalism incidents per quarter
ITID-14611.notes: Scope decision: sabotage/vandalism committed by an insider or employee is out of scope here and is tracked under ITID-13121/13122/13123 (Insider Sabotage); this branch covers external or unattributed actors.

playbook.name: Response: Vandalism/Property Damage to Facility Exterior or Grounds
playbook.description: For vandalism or property damage to a facility's exterior, signage, grounds, or perimeter.

steps.title: Document the damage
steps.desc: Photograph and inventory the damage, noting extent and estimated cost.
steps.outcome: Damage documented for insurance/police reporting.

steps.title: Secure and, if needed, temporarily repair the affected area
steps.desc: Address any immediate safety or security exposure created by the damage (e.g., a breached fence line).
steps.outcome: No ongoing safety/security gap from the damage.

steps.title: Repair the damage
steps.desc: Schedule permanent repair of the damaged property.
steps.outcome: Facility restored to normal condition.

steps.title: File a police report and insurance claim as applicable
steps.desc: Report the vandalism to local law enforcement and submit an insurance claim if damage exceeds the deductible.
steps.outcome: Report filed; claim submitted if applicable.

steps.title: Assess perimeter security improvements
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate lighting, camera coverage, or fencing improvements for the affected area.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV and perimeter sensor logs
steps.desc: Check exterior cameras and perimeter alarm logs for the time window the damage likely occurred.
steps.outcome: Footage of the act if captured, or a narrowed time window.

ITID-14612.def: An actor deliberately damages or disables physical access-control or security hardware — badge readers, turnstiles, security fencing, gates — to degrade the facility's security posture.
ITID-14612.purpose: Captures sabotage specifically targeting physical access-control or security hardware (readers, barriers, fencing, gates), a more severe form of facility sabotage than general vandalism.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate damage to badge readers, turnstiles, security gates, or perimeter fencing
scopeExcludes: General exterior vandalism not targeting security hardware (ITID-14611)

Tampering with cameras/sensors (the Camera or Sensor Disablement Type, ITID-14321-14324) or door lock/access-control wiring (the Door Access Tampering Type, ITID-14331-14334), which are classified under those more specific Types
Insider-perpetrated sabotage (ITID-13122)
ITID-14612.severity: High, given direct degradation of the security perimeter.
ITID-14612.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security for perimeter reinforcement pending repair.
indicators: Security hardware found damaged/inoperable during patrol or inspection
Hardware health-monitoring alert for a reader/gate/turnstile
vectors: Physical force or tools used against access-control hardware or perimeter fencing
rootCauses: Security hardware not covered by tamper/health monitoring; insufficient perimeter patrol frequency
controls: Hardware tamper/health monitoring on access-control equipment
Regular perimeter patrol and inspection
ITID-14612.detection: Hardware health monitoring, where deployed, provides a real technical signal; otherwise relies on patrol.
ITID-14612.response: Dispatch security and initiate emergency repair/compensating controls for the affected access point.
metrics: Count of security-hardware sabotage incidents per quarter
Mean time to restore damaged access-control hardware
ITID-14612.notes: Scope decision: camera/sensor tampering and door-lock/wiring tampering are classified under their own dedicated Types (ITID-14321-14324, ITID-14331-14334); this leaf covers other perimeter/access hardware such as fencing, gates, and turnstiles. Insider-perpetrated sabotage is out of scope, covered under ITID-13122.

playbook.name: Response: Sabotage of Physical Access Control/Security Hardware
playbook.description: For deliberate sabotage of physical security hardware itself (badge readers, gates, turnstiles, barriers, security lighting) beyond simple tampering of a single door.

steps.title: Inventory affected hardware and assess security impact
steps.desc: Identify which security devices/systems are disabled or damaged and what security gap this creates.
steps.outcome: Impacted hardware list and resulting exposure documented.

steps.title: Deploy compensating controls
steps.desc: Post guards, add temporary barriers, or otherwise compensate for the disabled security hardware until repaired.
steps.outcome: Security gap covered during repair.

steps.title: Repair or replace the sabotaged hardware
steps.desc: Restore the affected security equipment to full working order, hardening against reuse of the same method where practical.
steps.outcome: Hardware restored and confirmed functional.

steps.title: Verify full restoration and consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: Confirm the hardware is functioning normally; file a police report if the sabotage appears intended to facilitate a separate crime.
steps.outcome: Hardware confirmed restored; referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Document and review hardware hardening across the site
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether similar hardware elsewhere on-site shares the same vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Sitewide check performed if pattern identified.

steps.title: Review CCTV and system logs for the sabotage event
steps.desc: Pull footage and access-control system logs covering the affected hardware and time window.
steps.outcome: Evidence of how/when the sabotage occurred.

ITID-14613.def: An actor deliberately disables, discharges, or tampers with a fire suppression system, sprinkler system, fire alarm panel, or other life-safety system.
ITID-14613.purpose: Captures sabotage of fire suppression or life-safety systems, a high-severity form of facility sabotage with direct life-safety implications.
scopeIncludes: Disabling or discharging a fire suppression/sprinkler system
Tampering with a fire alarm control panel
scopeExcludes: Propping/disabling a fire-exit door specifically (ITID-14333, the Door Access Tampering branch)
Arson/incendiary use (ITID-14614, a distinct and more severe act)
ITID-14613.escalation: Escalate immediately to facilities, life-safety compliance, and local fire authority as required.
indicators: Fire alarm panel trouble/tamper signal
Sprinkler/suppression system found discharged or disabled during inspection
vectors: Physical tampering with a fire panel or suppression system valve/control
rootCauses: Fire-safety system control panels located in insufficiently access-controlled areas
controls: Restricted, logged access to fire-control rooms/panels
Fire panel tamper/trouble-signal monitoring
ITID-14613.detection: Fire panel tamper/trouble-signal monitoring provides a real, immediate technical signal.
ITID-14613.response: Treat as a life-safety emergency; notify facilities and fire authority per regulatory requirement.
metrics: Count of fire/life-safety system tamper incidents per year
ITID-14613.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14614 (arson), which involves actively setting a fire, versus disabling the systems meant to detect/suppress one.

playbook.name: Response: Sabotage of Fire Suppression/Life Safety Systems
playbook.description: For deliberate tampering with fire suppression, sprinkler, alarm, or other life-safety systems — a life-safety emergency in addition to a security incident.

steps.title: Immediately notify facilities/fire safety and assess life-safety risk
steps.desc: Treat this as an urgent life-safety issue first — confirm with facilities/fire safety what protection is currently disabled and the risk to occupants.
steps.guidance: This takes priority over the security investigation — building occupancy decisions may be needed.
steps.outcome: Life-safety risk assessed and facilities/fire safety engaged immediately.

steps.title: Restore fire/life-safety protection or implement a fire watch
steps.desc: Repair the system immediately if possible; if not, institute a continuous fire watch per code requirements until restored.
steps.guidance: Consult local fire code requirements for fire-watch procedures during suppression-system outages.
steps.outcome: Occupants protected despite the sabotage.

steps.title: Fully repair and certify the system
steps.desc: Have a qualified fire-safety contractor repair and re-certify the suppression/alarm system as code-compliant.
steps.outcome: System restored and certified.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Sabotage of life-safety systems is a serious offense — report to law enforcement and the local fire marshal.
steps.outcome: Report filed with evidence provided.

steps.title: Review physical protection of life-safety infrastructure
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether fire panels/control valves need better physical protection or monitoring.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Document the sabotage and review access to the affected system
steps.desc: Photograph the tampering and pull badge/CCTV records for who had access to the fire panel, sprinkler control valves, or alarm system.
steps.outcome: Evidence and access history documented.

ITID-14614.def: An actor deliberately sets a fire or deploys an incendiary device against a facility, intending to cause damage, disruption, or harm.
ITID-14614.purpose: Captures the most severe form of facility sabotage: deliberately setting a fire or using an incendiary device against a facility.
scopeIncludes: Deliberately setting a fire at a facility
Deploying an incendiary device against facility structures or equipment
scopeExcludes: Disabling fire suppression/life-safety systems without setting a fire (ITID-14613)
ITID-14614.escalation: Escalate immediately as a life-safety emergency and notify law enforcement/fire authority.
indicators: Fire investigation determination of arson/incendiary cause
Discovery of an incendiary device or accelerant residue
vectors: Deliberate ignition using an accelerant or incendiary device
rootCauses: Insufficient perimeter security allowing unauthorized access to combustible storage/staging areas
controls: Perimeter security around combustible material storage
Fire detection and suppression system coverage
ITID-14614.detection: Fire/smoke detection systems provide the primary real-time technical signal; cause determination requires post-incident fire investigation.
ITID-14614.response: Evacuate per life-safety procedure, notify emergency services, and preserve the scene for fire investigation and law enforcement.
metrics: Count of confirmed arson/incendiary incidents per year
ITID-14614.notes: This is the most severe leaf in the Sabotage of Facilities group; differentiated from ITID-14613 by the presence of an actual fire/incendiary act rather than disabling the systems that would detect or suppress one.

playbook.name: Response: Arson or Incendiary Device Used Against Facility
playbook.description: For a confirmed or suspected arson attack or incendiary device used against the facility — a life-safety emergency requiring immediate emergency-services response.

steps.title: Ensure evacuation and call emergency services immediately
steps.desc: If fire/device is active or suspected, evacuate the area and call the fire department/police immediately — do not investigate further until cleared by responders.
steps.guidance: Life safety overrides all other priorities in this scenario.
steps.outcome: Occupants safe; emergency services engaged.

steps.title: Assess and address structural/operational impact
steps.desc: Work with facilities and fire officials to determine building safety status and any needed temporary relocation of operations.
steps.outcome: Occupant safety and business continuity addressed.

steps.title: Cooperate fully with fire/police investigation
steps.desc: Provide all requested records (CCTV, badge logs, personnel info) to investigating authorities.
steps.outcome: Full cooperation with official investigation.

steps.title: Repair the facility and restore operations
steps.desc: Coordinate repair/restoration once the scene is released by investigators, and support insurance claims.
steps.outcome: Facility restored to safe, operational condition.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident security and safety review
steps.desc: Review perimeter security, fire detection coverage, and emergency response performance; brief leadership and update continuity plans.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive review completed with improvement actions tracked.

steps.title: Preserve the scene and gather evidence for investigators
steps.desc: Once cleared by responders, avoid disturbing the scene; pull CCTV covering the area and time window for fire investigators/police.
steps.guidance: Defer to fire investigators/police on scene handling — do not attempt to independently examine potential arson evidence.
steps.outcome: Scene preserved; evidence available for official investigation.

ITID-14615.def: An actor deliberately damages or disables on-site operational equipment or machinery (manufacturing lines, HVAC units, generators, general facility equipment) not classified as security hardware or a life-safety system.
ITID-14615.purpose: Captures sabotage of on-site equipment or machinery not otherwise covered by the security-hardware or life-safety leaves — e.g., manufacturing, HVAC, or general operational equipment.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate damage to manufacturing/operational machinery
Sabotage of HVAC or other building-operations equipment not tied to a utility line
scopeExcludes: Security/access-control hardware (ITID-14612)
Fire suppression/life-safety systems (ITID-14613)
Sabotage of a utility supply line itself, such as power or water (the Utility Disruption Type, ITID-14621-14623)
Insider-perpetrated sabotage of equipment (ITID-13122)
ITID-14615.severity: Medium-High, depending on the operational criticality of the equipment.
ITID-14615.escalation: Escalate to facilities/operations management to assess business-continuity impact.
indicators: Equipment found damaged or disabled with no maintenance/accidental-failure explanation
Operational downtime with a root cause traced to deliberate tampering
vectors: Physical tampering with machinery controls, wiring, or moving parts
rootCauses: Equipment located in insufficiently access-controlled operational areas
controls: Access control on operational/equipment rooms
Equipment health/anomaly monitoring where available
ITID-14615.detection: Relies on operational monitoring/maintenance reporting; limited security-specific technical signal.
ITID-14615.response: Assess operational impact and coordinate repair; investigate for deliberate cause.
metrics: Count of confirmed equipment sabotage incidents per quarter
ITID-14615.notes: Scope decision: sabotage of a utility supply line (power/water/gas) is classified under the Utility Disruption Type rather than here; insider-perpetrated equipment sabotage is tracked under ITID-13122.

playbook.name: Response: Sabotage of On-Site Equipment/Machinery
playbook.description: For deliberate sabotage of operational equipment or machinery on-site (e.g., HVAC, manufacturing/production equipment, generators).

steps.title: Assess operational and safety impact
steps.desc: Determine what the equipment does, the impact of it being down, and whether the sabotage created any immediate safety hazard.
steps.outcome: Operational/safety impact documented.

steps.title: Isolate the equipment and implement workarounds
steps.desc: Take the affected equipment offline safely and put interim workarounds in place to sustain operations.
steps.outcome: Operations sustained despite the outage.

steps.title: Repair the equipment and verify safe operation
steps.desc: Have qualified technicians repair the equipment and test it before returning to service.
steps.outcome: Equipment confirmed safe and functional.

steps.title: Resume normal operations and consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: Restore full operations; file a police report if the sabotage was clearly malicious/criminal.
steps.outcome: Operations restored; referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Review physical access controls for equipment areas
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether access to critical equipment areas needs tighter restriction or monitoring.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review access to the equipment and CCTV
steps.desc: Check who had physical access to the equipment area and pull relevant camera footage.
steps.outcome: Access history and, if available, footage of the act.

ITID-14616.def: Deliberate sabotage or damage to a facility, not clearly matching vandalism, security-hardware sabotage, life-safety system sabotage, arson, or equipment sabotage.
ITID-14616.purpose: Catch-all for facility sabotage that does not fit the more specific vandalism, security-hardware, life-safety, arson, or equipment leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14616.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14616.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the target and method are clarified.
indicators: Report of facility damage of unclear target/method
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14616.detection: Relies on initial human reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14616.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14616.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Sabotage of Facilities
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for facility sabotage incidents not covered by a more specific category.

steps.title: Assess impact and immediate safety risk
steps.desc: Determine what was sabotaged and whether it poses an immediate safety or operational risk.
steps.outcome: Impact and risk documented.

steps.title: Contain the immediate impact
steps.desc: Take any necessary steps to prevent the sabotage from causing further harm or disruption.
steps.outcome: Immediate risk contained.

steps.title: Repair the damage
steps.desc: Restore the affected facility/system to normal working order.
steps.outcome: Facility restored.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Document and review physical security controls
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate whether access, monitoring, or hardening improvements are needed.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review access and CCTV for the affected area
steps.desc: Pull badge logs and camera footage for the relevant location and time window.
steps.outcome: Access history and available footage obtained.

ITID-14621.def: An actor deliberately cuts, disconnects, or otherwise disables an electrical power line or supply feeding a facility, causing a power disruption.
ITID-14621.purpose: Captures deliberate cutting or disabling of an electrical power line/supply serving a facility, not motivated specifically by causing an IT outage.
scopeIncludes: Cutting or disconnecting an electrical supply line/feed serving the facility
scopeExcludes: Power/cooling sabotage specifically motivated by and escalating into an IT/data-center outage, which is tracked as a cyber-adjacent disruption incident (ITID-54712)
ITID-14621.severity: High, given broad facility-wide operational impact.
ITID-14621.escalation: Escalate immediately to facilities and utility provider; assess backup power/UPS status.
indicators: Unplanned facility-wide or zone power loss with no utility-provider outage reported
Physical inspection showing a cut/damaged power line or disabled electrical panel
vectors: Physical access to an exterior electrical line, transformer, or panel
rootCauses: Electrical infrastructure located in an unsecured, unmonitored exterior area
controls: Secured/fenced enclosure around exterior electrical infrastructure
Power-loss alerting integrated with facilities monitoring
ITID-14621.detection: Facilities power-monitoring systems provide a real, immediate technical signal.
