ITID-14621.response: Verify against utility-provider outage status, dispatch facilities to inspect, and activate backup power if available.
metrics: Count of confirmed deliberate power-disruption incidents per year
ITID-14621.notes: Scope decision: power/cooling sabotage specifically aimed at causing an IT/data-center outage is tracked under ITID-54712 to avoid double-counting; this leaf covers general facility power disruption without a confirmed IT-targeting motive.

playbook.name: Response: Electrical Power Line Cut or Disabled
playbook.description: For deliberate cutting or disabling of an electrical power line/feed serving the facility, potentially to disable security systems or disrupt operations.

steps.title: Confirm the outage scope and safety hazard
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities/electrical staff to confirm which circuits are affected and whether there is a live-wire or fire hazard requiring evacuation of the area.
steps.guidance: Treat exposed/cut electrical lines as a safety hazard first — do not approach.
steps.outcome: Hazard assessed and area secured if needed.

steps.title: Deploy compensating security coverage
steps.desc: Post guards or add temporary lighting/monitoring for areas that lost camera or alarm coverage.
steps.outcome: Security gap covered during the outage.

steps.title: Repair the power line and restore systems
steps.desc: Have a qualified electrician repair the line and confirm all dependent systems (security and operational) are back online.
steps.outcome: Power and dependent systems fully restored.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if the cut appears deliberate and intended to facilitate another crime.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Review backup power and line protection for critical security systems
steps.desc: Log the incident and evaluate UPS/generator coverage and physical protection of external power lines.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Verify status of security systems dependent on power
steps.desc: Check whether cameras, alarms, or access control on the affected circuit lost power (and whether they failed to battery backup as designed).
steps.outcome: Confirmed which security systems are degraded.

ITID-14622.def: An actor deliberately cuts, disconnects, or contaminates a water supply line feeding a facility, causing a disruption or safety hazard.
ITID-14622.purpose: Captures deliberate cutting or contamination of a facility's water supply line.
scopeIncludes: Cutting or disconnecting a water supply line
Deliberately introducing a contaminant into a facility's water supply
scopeExcludes: Sabotage of fire suppression/sprinkler systems specifically, even though they carry water (ITID-14613, a life-safety system)
ITID-14622.severity: High, given both operational and potential health/safety impact.
ITID-14622.priority: P1 upon detection, especially if contamination is suspected.
ITID-14622.escalation: Escalate immediately to facilities and, if contamination is suspected, to public health/water authority.
indicators: Unplanned loss of water supply with no utility-provider outage reported
Water quality testing anomaly with no known environmental cause
vectors: Physical access to an exterior water main, valve, or supply line
rootCauses: Water supply infrastructure located in an unsecured, unmonitored area
controls: Secured enclosure around exterior water supply infrastructure
Water-quality/flow monitoring where feasible
ITID-14622.detection: Facilities water-flow monitoring provides a technical signal where deployed; contamination requires water-quality testing.
ITID-14622.response: Verify against utility-provider status, dispatch facilities to inspect, and halt water use if contamination is suspected pending testing.
metrics: Count of confirmed water-supply disruption/contamination incidents per year
ITID-14622.notes: Differentiated from ITID-14613, which covers sabotage of the fire suppression/sprinkler system specifically as a life-safety system, not the general water supply line.

playbook.name: Response: Water Supply Line Cut or Contaminated
playbook.description: For deliberate cutting or contamination of the facility's water supply — a potential health hazard requiring immediate facilities/public-health coordination.

steps.title: Shut off consumption and assess health hazard
steps.desc: If contamination is suspected, immediately advise staff not to drink/use the water and coordinate with facilities and, if warranted, local public health authorities.
steps.guidance: Treat suspected contamination as a health emergency first.
steps.outcome: Consumption halted; health risk assessed.

steps.title: Isolate the affected supply and arrange alternate water
steps.desc: Shut off the affected line/zone and arrange bottled/alternate water supply for affected areas until resolved.
steps.outcome: Ongoing exposure stopped; staff needs met.

steps.title: Repair, flush, and test the water system
steps.desc: Repair the line, flush the system, and have water tested by a certified lab before restoring normal use.
steps.outcome: Water confirmed safe before resuming normal use.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Deliberate contamination or sabotage of a water supply is a serious offense — report to law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Report filed with evidence provided.

steps.title: Review access controls to water infrastructure
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether water supply access points need better physical protection or monitoring.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Confirm the cause and scope of the disruption/contamination
steps.desc: Work with facilities/water utility to determine whether the line was physically cut and/or a contaminant was introduced, and how far it spread.
steps.outcome: Cause and scope confirmed.

ITID-14623.def: An actor deliberately cuts, disconnects, or tampers with a gas or fuel supply line feeding a facility or backup generator, creating a disruption and a potential explosion/fire hazard.
ITID-14623.purpose: Captures deliberate tampering with or cutting of a facility's gas or fuel line, a high-severity utility disruption given explosion/fire risk.
scopeIncludes: Tampering with or cutting a natural gas supply line
Tampering with a backup generator's fuel supply line
scopeExcludes: Setting a fire or deploying an incendiary device (ITID-14614), even if a tampered gas/fuel line is the fuel source for a subsequent fire (classify the ignition act itself under ITID-14614 and the line-tampering precursor under this leaf)
ITID-14623.priority: P1, immediate, with fire authority notification.
ITID-14623.escalation: Escalate immediately as a life-safety emergency; evacuate the area if a gas leak is suspected.
indicators: Gas leak detected by sensor or odor with no accidental/maintenance cause identified
Physical inspection showing a cut/damaged gas or fuel line
vectors: Physical access to an exterior gas meter, fuel tank, or supply line
rootCauses: Gas/fuel infrastructure located in an unsecured, unmonitored area; no gas-leak detection sensors installed
controls: Secured enclosure around exterior gas/fuel infrastructure
Gas-leak detection sensors with alerting
ITID-14623.detection: Gas-leak detection sensors, where installed, provide a real, immediate technical signal.
ITID-14623.response: Evacuate if a leak is suspected, notify fire authority, and dispatch facilities to isolate the supply.
metrics: Count of confirmed gas/fuel line tampering incidents per year
ITID-14623.notes: Scope decision: the line-tampering act itself is logged here; a subsequent deliberate ignition is logged separately under ITID-14614 to keep the two distinct causal acts separable in reporting.

playbook.name: Response: Gas/Fuel Line Tampered or Cut
playbook.description: For deliberate tampering with or cutting of a gas or fuel line serving the facility — an urgent explosion/fire hazard requiring immediate evacuation and emergency-services involvement.

steps.title: Evacuate immediately and call emergency services/gas utility
steps.desc: Treat any suspected gas leak as an immediate explosion/fire hazard — evacuate the area, avoid triggering any spark source (no light switches, phones), and call the fire department and gas utility emergency line immediately.
steps.guidance: This is a life-safety emergency — do not attempt to investigate the source yourself.
steps.outcome: Area evacuated; emergency responders engaged.

steps.title: Confirm the line is isolated and the area is safe
steps.desc: Verify with the gas utility/fire department that the line has been shut off/repaired and the area is safe to reoccupy.
steps.outcome: Area confirmed safe.

steps.title: Repair and re-certify the line
steps.desc: Have a licensed contractor repair the line and obtain any required safety re-certification before resuming normal use.
steps.outcome: Line repaired and certified safe.

steps.title: File a police report
steps.desc: Deliberate tampering with a gas/fuel line is a serious criminal offense — report to law enforcement with all evidence gathered.
steps.outcome: Report filed.

steps.title: Review physical protection of fuel/gas infrastructure
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether gas/fuel lines and shutoff valves need better physical protection, signage, or monitoring.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Support responders and preserve evidence once cleared
steps.desc: Once the area is declared safe, provide CCTV and access records covering the affected line/area to investigators.
steps.outcome: Investigators have the evidence needed.

ITID-14624.def: Deliberate disruption of a facility utility, not clearly matching power, water, or gas/fuel line tampering.
ITID-14624.purpose: Catch-all for utility disruption that does not fit the more specific power, water, or gas/fuel leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID
ITID-14624.severity: Medium-to-High; reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-14624.escalation: Escalate for documentation; reclassify once the affected utility is clarified.
indicators: Report of a utility outage of unclear cause or affected system
vectors: Activity of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report
controls: Awareness training
ITID-14624.detection: Relies on initial human/facilities reporting pending further triage.
ITID-14624.response: Document, investigate, and attempt to reclassify.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-14624.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Utility Disruption
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for utility disruption incidents not covered by the electrical, water, or gas categories.

steps.title: Assess the disruption and any immediate safety hazard
steps.desc: Determine which utility is affected, the scope, and whether there is an immediate hazard requiring evacuation.
steps.guidance: Default to treating unknown utility hazards as a safety issue first.
steps.outcome: Hazard assessed and addressed.

steps.title: Implement workarounds for affected operations
steps.desc: Put interim measures in place to sustain critical operations during the outage.
steps.outcome: Operational impact minimized.

steps.title: Repair the utility infrastructure
steps.desc: Coordinate repair with the relevant utility provider or facilities contractor.
steps.outcome: Utility service restored.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if the disruption appears deliberate.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Review protection of utility infrastructure
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether access to utility infrastructure needs better protection or monitoring.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review access and CCTV for the utility infrastructure
steps.desc: Pull badge/camera records for the location of the affected infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Access history and available footage obtained.

ITID-14711.def: The unauthorized photographing of security systems, access control hardware, or the physical security layout at a facility, performed to gather visual intelligence supporting a future physical intrusion or social-engineering pretext, rather than for espionage or business-intelligence purposes.
ITID-14711.purpose: Captures an adversary's use of photography specifically to document a target facility's physical security controls — camera placement, badge readers, door hardware, guard posts — as preparatory reconnaissance for a later intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Photographing CCTV camera positions or blind spots
Photographing badge readers, keypads, or door hardware
Photographing posted security schedules or guard rosters
Photography performed by a person physically present at or near the facility
scopeExcludes: Espionage-motivated covert photography of a target's business activity or documents (ITID-52542, ITID-52942)
Drone-based aerial photography of a restricted facility (ITID-14712)
Photography taken as part of an already-in-progress intrusion rather than pre-intrusion reconnaissance
ITID-14711.severity: Typically Low-to-Medium in isolation; escalate to Medium-High if discovered alongside other reconnaissance indicators (casing, device placement) suggesting an imminent intrusion attempt.
ITID-14711.priority: P3 by default; P2 if corroborated by other reconnaissance activity against the same facility within a short window.
ITID-14711.escalation: Escalate to physical security/facilities management immediately upon discovery; escalate to SOC/investigations if the individual is later linked to an actual intrusion attempt.
indicators: Employee or guard report of a stranger photographing entrances or security equipment
Loitering near access points with a camera or phone raised toward security hardware
Facility security details appearing in later phishing or pretexting material
vectors: In-person photography using a phone or camera
Photography from a public vantage point (street, parking lot, adjacent building)
Photography performed under a cover pretext (e.g., posing as a tourist or delivery driver)
rootCauses: Security hardware visible from publicly accessible areas with no visual barriers
No policy or staff awareness prohibiting or challenging photography near secured areas
Lack of a guard or reception challenge process for individuals photographing the premises
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Physical security awareness training
Visitor challenge procedures
Sightline and landscaping controls limiting visibility of security hardware from public areas
ITID-14711.detection: Not a technical-telemetry detection surface — relies on human reporting (guard force, reception, employees) and, where deployed, camera analytics flagging loitering near entrances.
ITID-14711.response: Confirm the individual's identity or purpose where safe to do so, document the incident (time, location, description), and notify facilities/physical security; treat as a precursor indicator warranting heightened vigilance at that location for a defined period.
metrics: Count of reported unauthorized photography incidents per facility per quarter
Time from report to facilities/security notification
ITID-14711.notes: Genuinely difficult to detect technically; effectiveness depends heavily on staff and guard-force awareness and willingness to report. Repeated reports at the same facility should be correlated as a single tracked reconnaissance campaign rather than treated as independent events.

playbook.name: Response: Photographing Security Systems/Access Control Layout Without Authorization
playbook.description: For an individual observed or reported photographing security systems, camera placements, or access control layouts without authorization — likely pre-attack reconnaissance.

steps.title: Gather witness accounts and any recovered images
steps.desc: Interview whoever reported the activity and, if the individual was stopped, review any images captured (with appropriate authority/consent).
steps.outcome: Details of what was photographed documented.

steps.title: Challenge and, if unauthorized, remove the individual
steps.desc: Have security approach the individual, verify their purpose/authorization, and escort off-site if unauthorized.
steps.outcome: Individual identified or removed from the premises.

steps.title: Assess whether security layout is now considered exposed
steps.desc: Evaluate whether camera/access-control placements captured in the photos should be treated as known to a potential adversary, and adjust posture if warranted (e.g., don't rely solely on visible deterrents).
steps.outcome: Risk from the exposure assessed and addressed.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement notification
steps.desc: If this appears to be pre-attack reconnaissance (e.g., preceded a subsequent incident, or the individual has no legitimate reason to be on-site), notify local law enforcement.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Document and heighten vigilance
steps.desc: Log the incident, share with the security team as a possible precursor indicator, and heighten monitoring for follow-on activity.
steps.outcome: Awareness raised; follow-on activity more likely to be caught.

steps.title: Review CCTV of the individual's activity
steps.desc: Pull camera footage covering the individual's presence and movement on-site.
steps.outcome: Visual record of the individual and their activity pattern.

steps.title: Alert security staff sitewide
steps.desc: Circulate a description in case the individual returns or is scouting multiple sites.
steps.outcome: Staff prepared to recognize the individual.

ITID-14712.def: The unauthorized use of an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) to capture aerial photography or video of a restricted facility's grounds, perimeter, rooftop, or parking areas as reconnaissance for a physical intrusion or to assess physical security coverage.
ITID-14712.purpose: Captures the use of a drone to photograph or film a restricted facility from the air, gathering layout, perimeter, and rooftop/parking intelligence that ground-level photography cannot easily obtain.
scopeIncludes: Drone overflight of a facility's roof, grounds, or perimeter to capture photo/video
Drone use to map camera coverage, fence lines, or unmonitored approach routes
Drone flights conducted outside any authorized facility drone policy or airspace permission
scopeExcludes: Ground-level unauthorized photography (ITID-14711)
Drone use for authorized facility inspection, survey, or security assessment
Drone-borne physical attacks or payload delivery (a physical sabotage or device-placement scenario, not reconnaissance)
ITID-14712.severity: Medium by default given the difficulty of intercepting a drone operator; escalate to High for repeated overflights of the same facility or overflights of a high-sensitivity site (data center, executive location).
ITID-14712.priority: P2 by default given limited real-time response options.
ITID-14712.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and, where local law permits, law enforcement — drone reconnaissance of critical infrastructure or sensitive sites may itself be a reportable/regulated event in some jurisdictions.
indicators: Visual or acoustic detection of a drone hovering over or near the facility
Drone detection system (RF/radar) alerts, where deployed
Repeated sightings of the same drone/operator pattern over time
vectors: Consumer or prosumer drone flown by an operator at or beyond visual line of sight
Flights timed to low-staffing periods (nights, weekends) to reduce chance of observation
rootCauses: No drone-detection capability at the facility
No defined response procedure when a drone is sighted
Rooftop or perimeter security features designed without considering aerial visibility
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Drone detection (RF/radar) system
No-fly zone registration where applicable
Staff procedure for reporting and responding to drone sightings
ITID-14712.detection: Limited to physical/RF drone-detection sensors where deployed; otherwise relies entirely on staff visual/acoustic observation and reporting.
ITID-14712.response: Document sighting details (time, description, flight pattern, any visible operator location), notify physical security and, where warranted, local law enforcement; increase visual monitoring of the facility for a follow-up period.
metrics: Count of confirmed drone sightings per facility per quarter
Mean time to physical-security notification after sighting
ITID-14712.notes: Response options are inherently limited without a dedicated counter-drone capability; the realistic goal for most organizations is documentation, escalation, and pattern tracking rather than interdiction.

playbook.name: Response: Drone-Based Aerial Photography of Restricted Facility
playbook.description: For an unauthorized drone observed conducting aerial photography/surveillance of a restricted facility.

steps.title: Document the drone sighting
steps.desc: Record time, location, drone description, flight pattern, and any operator sighted, with photos/video if safely possible.
steps.outcome: Sighting documented with as much detail as possible.

steps.title: Assess and mitigate exposure of sensitive areas
steps.desc: Determine what the drone could have observed (e.g., yard layout, security posture, exposed materials) and take interim measures (covering, shielding) if warranted.
steps.outcome: Sensitive exposure minimized going forward.

steps.title: Report to the relevant aviation/regulatory authority and law enforcement
steps.desc: Unauthorized drone surveillance of private property may violate aviation regulations and privacy/trespass law — report to the appropriate authority and local law enforcement.
steps.guidance: Do not attempt to disable or shoot down a drone yourself — this can be illegal and dangerous; leave counter-measures to authorized personnel.
steps.outcome: Report filed with the appropriate authority.

steps.title: Increase monitoring for follow-up drone activity
steps.desc: Brief security staff to watch for and report further drone sightings, especially if this appears to be repeated reconnaissance.
steps.outcome: Improved detection of follow-on activity.

steps.title: Evaluate counter-UAS or airspace-monitoring investment
steps.desc: Log the incident and, for high-sensitivity sites, evaluate investment in drone detection capability.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Check for a drone detection/counter-UAS system alert
steps.desc: If the site has drone-detection capability, correlate with system logs for flight path and any RF/operator location data.
steps.outcome: Additional technical detail on the drone and, if available, operator location.
steps.abort: If no such system exists, rely on visual/witness reporting.

ITID-14713.def: Unauthorized photography of a facility or its surroundings, taken as apparent physical security reconnaissance, that does not clearly match a more specific Unauthorized Photography leaf.
ITID-14713.purpose: Catch-all for unauthorized photography of a facility's security posture that does not fit the more specific drone or access-control-focused leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized photography of a facility's general exterior, signage, or grounds where the specific target (security hardware vs. general layout) is unclear
Cases initially logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific leaf
scopeExcludes: Photography clearly targeting security systems/access control (ITID-14711)
Drone-based aerial photography (ITID-14712)
ITID-14713.severity: Low-to-Medium; reassess and reclassify once more detail is available.
ITID-14713.escalation: Escalate to physical security for documentation; reclassify to a more specific ITID once the target/intent of the photography is clarified.
indicators: Employee or guard report of unexplained photography of the premises
vectors: In-person photography of unclear intent
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report to determine specific intent
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Physical security awareness training
Visitor challenge procedures
ITID-14713.response: Document the incident, attempt to gather enough detail to reclassify under a more specific leaf, and notify physical security.
metrics: Count of Unclassified photography reports pending reclassification
ITID-14713.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one — analysts should reclassify to ITID-14711 or ITID-14712 once the target of the photography is known.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Unauthorized Photography
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for unauthorized photography incidents not covered by the security-systems or drone categories.

steps.title: Document the reported photography
steps.desc: Record what was photographed, by whom, and when.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Challenge and address the individual if still present
steps.desc: Have security verify authorization and address the individual per policy (request deletion, escort out, etc.).
steps.outcome: Situation resolved on-site.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity of what was captured
steps.desc: Determine whether the photography captured anything sensitive requiring further action.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: File a police report if warranted.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Document and reinforce photography policy
steps.desc: Log the incident and reinforce facility photography rules with staff and visitors.
steps.outcome: Awareness reinforced.

steps.title: Review CCTV of the activity
steps.desc: Pull footage covering the individual's presence and activity.
steps.outcome: Visual record obtained if available.

ITID-14721.def: An adversary's in-person walk-through or casing of a facility's exterior or interior to identify unmonitored entry points, camera blind spots, unlocked doors, or other physical security gaps, performed as direct preparation for a later intrusion.
ITID-14721.purpose: Captures an adversary physically walking a facility's grounds or interior to identify entry points, blind spots, and weaknesses ahead of an intrusion attempt.
scopeIncludes: Walking or driving the perimeter of a facility to map entry points and camera coverage
Testing which doors are unlocked or propped without attempting entry
Mapping the interior layout during a legitimate visit (e.g., posing as a visitor) for later use
scopeExcludes: Observation focused specifically on guard patrol timing/shift changes (ITID-14722)
Active probing of alarms or access-control points (ITID-14723)
An actual intrusion attempt itself, rather than pre-intrusion casing
ITID-14721.severity: Medium; escalate to High if the same individual/vehicle is observed casing the facility on multiple occasions.
ITID-14721.escalation: Escalate to physical security immediately for real-time response if the individual is still on-site; escalate to SOC/investigations for pattern tracking across multiple sightings.
indicators: Unfamiliar individual or vehicle observed repeatedly near the facility with no legitimate purpose
Person observed testing doors or walking non-public areas without authorization
Guard or employee report of a visitor lingering beyond the scope of their stated purpose
vectors: In-person casing on foot or by vehicle
Casing conducted under a cover pretext (delivery, visitor, contractor)
rootCauses: Unrestricted public access to areas adjacent to sensitive entry points
No challenge procedure for individuals lingering in non-public areas
Insufficient perimeter camera coverage to detect repeated casing
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Perimeter camera coverage with analytics for repeated presence
Visitor escort and challenge procedures
Guard force training on casing indicators
ITID-14721.detection: Primarily human observation (guards, employees); camera analytics (loitering/repeated-presence detection) provide partial coverage where deployed.
ITID-14721.response: Challenge or document the individual where safe to do so, notify physical security, and increase monitoring of the facility for a follow-up period.
metrics: Count of reported casing incidents per facility per quarter
Recurrence rate of the same individual/vehicle at a given facility
ITID-14721.notes: Casing is often the single strongest available leading indicator of an imminent physical intrusion attempt — correlating repeated sightings across shifts and days is more valuable than treating each report in isolation.

playbook.name: Response: Facility Walk-Through/Casing to Identify Entry Points and Blind Spots
playbook.description: For an individual observed conducting a suspicious walk-through of the facility perimeter/interior consistent with casing entry points and camera blind spots.

steps.title: Gather witness/guard accounts of the behavior
steps.desc: Interview whoever reported the activity to capture the individual's description, route, and behavior pattern (e.g., lingering, testing doors, avoiding cameras).
steps.outcome: Documented behavioral account.

steps.title: Dispatch security to locate and challenge the individual
steps.desc: If still on or near the premises, have security approach, verify identity/purpose, and document the interaction.
steps.outcome: Individual identified or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Address any blind spots identified
steps.desc: If the review reveals genuine camera/coverage blind spots the individual could exploit, address them (reposition cameras, add patrol coverage).
steps.outcome: Identified vulnerabilities reduced.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement notification
steps.desc: If behavior is clearly consistent with pre-attack reconnaissance, notify local law enforcement for situational awareness.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Document as a possible precursor indicator
steps.desc: Log the incident and flag for correlation with any subsequent security events at the site.
steps.outcome: Incident logged for future correlation.

steps.title: Review CCTV of the individual's route
steps.desc: Pull footage covering the full path the individual walked to understand what they observed and any blind spots they identified.
steps.outcome: Full route and behavior captured on video.

steps.title: Alert security staff and increase vigilance sitewide
steps.desc: Circulate the individual's description and heighten awareness for follow-on activity.
steps.outcome: Staff prepared for potential follow-up attempt.

ITID-14722.def: An adversary's observation of a facility's security guard patrol patterns, rounds, or shift-change timing, performed to identify predictable gaps in physical security coverage.
ITID-14722.purpose: Captures an adversary specifically observing guard patrol routines and shift-change timing to identify a window of reduced coverage for a later intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Timing and logging guard patrol rounds from a nearby vantage point
Observing shift-change timing and guard-force staffing levels at different times of day
Repeated visits or loitering timed to coincide with guard rotations
scopeExcludes: General facility walk-through/casing not focused on guard timing (ITID-14721)
Active testing of alarms or access points (ITID-14723)
ITID-14722.severity: Medium; escalate to High if combined with other casing indicators suggesting a specific, imminent intrusion plan.
ITID-14722.escalation: Escalate to physical security for guard-force awareness and possible schedule randomization; escalate to SOC/investigations if the pattern recurs.
indicators: Individual or vehicle repeatedly present at times coinciding with shift changes
Guard report of being watched or followed during rounds
Predictable, unvaried patrol schedule identified as a risk during a security review
vectors: Extended in-person observation from a fixed or roaming vantage point
Repeated visits timed to different points in the guard rotation to map the full schedule
rootCauses: Fixed, unvaried guard patrol schedule and route
Guard rotations and shift changes visible from publicly accessible vantage points
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Randomized guard patrol routes and timing
Guard-force training on surveillance-detection
Camera coverage of areas with a clear view of the guard force
ITID-14722.detection: Relies primarily on guard-force awareness and reporting of being observed; camera analytics can help identify repeated presence at consistent times.
ITID-14722.response: Document the observation, notify physical security leadership, and consider randomizing patrol schedules if a specific pattern of observation is confirmed.
metrics: Count of reported guard-observation incidents per facility per quarter
Patrol schedule randomization coverage across facilities
ITID-14722.notes: A fixed, predictable patrol schedule is itself a root cause worth addressing independent of any specific observed incident.

playbook.name: Response: Observation of Security Patrol Patterns/Shift Changes
playbook.description: For an individual observed monitoring/timing guard patrol routes or shift-change windows, consistent with planning to exploit a coverage gap.

steps.title: Gather details of the observed behavior
steps.desc: Document what was observed — location, duration, apparent focus on patrol timing/shift changes.
steps.outcome: Behavioral account documented.

steps.title: Vary patrol patterns and shift-change timing
steps.desc: Immediately randomize guard patrol routes and timing to reduce the value of the reconnaissance already gathered.
steps.outcome: Predictability the individual observed is no longer reliable.

steps.title: Assess whether the observation point should be restricted
steps.desc: Determine if the vantage point used (e.g., adjacent public space, parking area) can be obstructed or monitored going forward.
steps.outcome: Reduced ability to repeat the observation.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement notification
steps.desc: Notify local law enforcement if this appears consistent with pre-attack planning.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Document and review patrol program design
steps.desc: Log the incident and assess whether the patrol program should adopt more built-in unpredictability by design.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV covering the observation point
steps.desc: Pull footage of the individual's vantage point and duration of observation.
steps.outcome: Visual record of the activity.

steps.title: Increase vigilance for a follow-up attempt
steps.desc: Brief guard staff to watch for the same individual or related activity, particularly around shift changes.
steps.outcome: Staff prepared for potential exploitation attempt.

ITID-14723.def: An adversary's deliberate, low-level testing of a facility's physical security response — triggering a door alarm, testing a badge reader with an invalid credential, or similar — to observe and learn how security personnel or systems respond, as preparation for a later intrusion.
ITID-14723.purpose: Captures an adversary actively probing a facility's alarms or access points — deliberately triggering or testing them — to learn how the security system responds, rather than passively observing.
scopeIncludes: Deliberately propping or opening a door to see how quickly an alarm is triggered and responded to
Testing an access point with an invalid or cloned credential to observe the system's response
Triggering a low-priority alarm to gauge response time without attempting further intrusion
scopeExcludes: Passive observation of patrols or facility layout (ITID-14721, ITID-14722)
An actual intrusion attempt following successful probing, which should be classified under the relevant intrusion ITID instead
ITID-14723.severity: Medium-High — active probing is a stronger indicator of imminent intent than passive observation.
ITID-14723.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if probing is confirmed alongside other casing indicators.
ITID-14723.escalation: Escalate to physical security and SOC immediately upon a confirmed probing event; treat as a strong precursor to an imminent intrusion attempt and increase monitoring accordingly.
indicators: Alarm triggered with no corresponding legitimate cause identified
Access-control system logs showing a rejected credential attempt with no plausible legitimate explanation
Guard or system response time being visibly timed or observed by an onlooker after an alarm
vectors: Deliberately propping/opening a monitored door
Presenting a cloned, stolen, or fabricated badge to a reader
Triggering a motion sensor or door contact and observing response
rootCauses: Alarm response times not randomized or reviewed for predictability
Access-control rejection events not actively monitored/alerted on
No process to investigate an isolated, unexplained alarm as a potential probing event
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Active monitoring and alerting on access-control rejection events
Alarm response time review and randomization
Guard-force training to treat isolated unexplained alarms as potential probing
ITID-14723.detection: Access-control and alarm system logs provide a real technical signal here (rejected credentials, unexplained alarms) — this leaf has meaningfully better detection coverage than passive-observation reconnaissance.
ITID-14723.response: Investigate every unexplained alarm or access-control rejection as a potential probing event rather than dismissing it as noise; increase physical presence/monitoring at the affected access point for a follow-up period.
metrics: Count of unexplained alarm/access-rejection events investigated as potential probing per quarter
Percentage of such events resolved with a confirmed benign cause
ITID-14723.notes: This is the one Physical Reconnaissance leaf with a genuine technical detection surface (access-control/alarm logs) — prioritize building alerting here over the purely observation-based sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Testing Physical Security Response (Probing Alarms/Access Points)
playbook.description: For evidence someone deliberately triggered alarms or tested access points to observe and measure the security response, without a clear theft/entry motive of their own at that time.

steps.title: Confirm the probing pattern
steps.desc: Review alarm system logs and access-control logs for a pattern of triggered-then-abandoned events (e.g., repeated door-forced alarms, badge attempts) rather than a single incident.
steps.outcome: Pattern of deliberate probing confirmed.
steps.abort: If it looks like a one-off system malfunction, redirect to a facilities ticket instead.

steps.title: Vary and reinforce the security response process
steps.desc: Adjust alarm-response procedures/timing so the response the individual observed is no longer predictable, and reinforce guard staffing during identified risk windows.
steps.outcome: The information gathered by the probing is devalued.

steps.title: Harden the specific points that were probed
steps.desc: Reinforce or add monitoring to the specific alarms/access points that were tested.
steps.outcome: Probed points hardened against exploitation.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement given the deliberate, targeted nature
steps.desc: This behavior strongly suggests planning for a future incident — notify local law enforcement for situational awareness and, if the individual is identified, consider a trespass warning.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement informed; formal warning issued if identity known.

steps.title: Document as a high-priority precursor indicator
steps.desc: Log the incident prominently and correlate with any subsequent security events at the site — this is a strong indicator of intent to act.
steps.outcome: Incident flagged for close monitoring going forward.

steps.title: Review CCTV for each probing event
steps.desc: Pull footage for each identified event to determine if the same individual(s) are responsible and observe their behavior after triggering the alarm (e.g., timing the guard response).
steps.outcome: Visual confirmation and behavior pattern established.

ITID-14724.def: Physical reconnaissance of a facility, performed as apparent preparation for a later intrusion, that does not clearly match a more specific Physical Reconnaissance leaf.
ITID-14724.purpose: Catch-all for physical reconnaissance activity that does not fit the more specific casing, patrol-observation, or probing leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Reconnaissance reports lacking enough detail to determine whether the focus was general casing, patrol timing, or active probing
Cases initially logged before enough information is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Facility walk-through/casing with a clear focus on entry points and blind spots (ITID-14721)
Guard patrol/shift-change observation (ITID-14722)
Active probing of alarms or access points (ITID-14723)
ITID-14724.severity: Medium; reassess and reclassify once more detail is available.
ITID-14724.escalation: Escalate to physical security for documentation; reclassify to a more specific ITID once the nature of the reconnaissance is clarified.
indicators: Guard or employee report of suspicious activity near the facility with unclear intent
vectors: In-person reconnaissance of unclear focus
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of report to determine the specific reconnaissance focus
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Physical security awareness training
Guard-force reporting procedures
ITID-14724.response: Document the incident, attempt to gather enough detail to reclassify under a more specific leaf, and notify physical security.
metrics: Count of Unclassified reconnaissance reports pending reclassification
ITID-14724.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one — analysts should reclassify to a more specific sibling leaf once the nature of the reconnaissance is known.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Physical Reconnaissance
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for physical reconnaissance incidents not covered by the casing, patrol-observation, or security-testing categories.

steps.title: Document the reconnaissance behavior observed
steps.desc: Record what was observed, by whom, and when.
steps.outcome: Baseline incident record established.

steps.title: Challenge the individual if still present
steps.desc: Have security verify identity/purpose and document the interaction.
steps.outcome: Individual identified or confirmed to have left.

steps.title: Address any identified vulnerability
steps.desc: Fix any specific weakness the reconnaissance appeared to target.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability reduced.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement notification
steps.desc: Notify law enforcement if behavior suggests planning for a future incident.
steps.outcome: Referral made if warranted.

steps.title: Document as a possible precursor indicator
steps.desc: Log for future correlation with subsequent security events.
steps.outcome: Incident logged.

steps.title: Review CCTV of the activity
steps.desc: Pull footage covering the individual's presence and behavior.
steps.outcome: Visual record obtained where available.

ITID-14731.def: The covert physical placement of a hidden camera or audio recording device within a facility or vehicle to capture video or audio without the knowledge or consent of the people present, for surveillance or intelligence-gathering purposes.
ITID-14731.purpose: Captures the covert physical placement of a hidden camera or audio recording device to surveil a location or conversation, as distinct from cyber-network implants or espionage-context hardware.
scopeIncludes: Hidden camera placed in an office, meeting room, restroom, or common area
Covert audio recording device ('bug') placed in a room or on an object
Devices discovered during routine sweeps or by facility staff/occupants
scopeExcludes: GPS trackers placed on vehicles or assets (ITID-14732)
Network/peripheral hardware implants used for cyber exfiltration (ITID-34331 through ITID-34334)
Hardware keyloggers (ITID-12123)
Espionage-context hardware implants aimed at business intelligence (ITID-52911)
ITID-14731.severity: High — a discovered covert recording device indicates active, targeted surveillance and may have privacy, legal, and regulatory implications beyond the security incident itself.
ITID-14731.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, legal/privacy, and executive leadership if the location suggests targeting of sensitive discussions (e.g., a boardroom or executive office); preserve the device and its placement for forensic and, where applicable, law-enforcement handling.
indicators: Physical discovery of an unfamiliar device during a room sweep or routine cleaning
Unexplained small holes, tape residue, or disturbed fixtures suggesting device concealment
Anomalous RF emissions detected by a TSCM (technical surveillance countermeasures) sweep
vectors: Device planted by an insider with legitimate physical access
Device planted by an outsider during an unescorted visit or brief unauthorized access window
Device disguised as or embedded within an everyday object (charger, smoke detector, power strip)
rootCauses: No routine TSCM sweeps of sensitive meeting spaces
Unescorted visitor or contractor access to sensitive areas
Sensitive discussions held in spaces without any physical security review
controls: Routine TSCM sweeps of high-sensitivity spaces
Visitor escort policy for sensitive areas
Physical inspection procedures for unfamiliar objects/devices
ITID-14731.detection: Primarily physical discovery (staff observation, cleaning crew, dedicated TSCM sweeps) — no network-based detection applies to a device with no network presence.
ITID-14731.response: Do not immediately disturb or remove the device if forensic/legal evidence preservation may be needed; notify physical security, legal, and executive leadership; conduct a broader sweep of related spaces.
metrics: Count of covert devices discovered per year
Coverage percentage of sensitive spaces under routine TSCM sweep
ITID-14731.notes: Treat every discovery as a potential legal/evidentiary matter, not just an operational security incident — involve legal counsel early, particularly if the device may have captured privileged or regulated information.

playbook.name: Response: Hidden Camera or Audio Recording Device Planted
playbook.description: For discovery of a covert camera or audio recording device planted in a facility (meeting room, office, break room, etc.).

steps.title: Do not disturb the device — document and photograph in place
steps.desc: Photograph the device exactly as found, noting exact location, orientation, and any visible model/markings, without removing it yet.
steps.guidance: Preserving the device undisturbed maximizes forensic value if the case proceeds to investigation.
steps.outcome: Device documented in situ.

steps.title: Notify legal before removing or analyzing the device
steps.desc: Loop in Legal immediately — a planted recording device may indicate espionage, harassment, or a legal dispute, and evidence handling needs to follow a defensible chain of custody.
steps.outcome: Legal engaged and guiding next steps.

steps.title: Recover and analyze the device under proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Remove and forensically analyze the device (or engage law enforcement/a specialist to do so) to identify its origin, data captured, and any retrieval mechanism (e.g., remote transmission).
steps.outcome: Device analyzed; source and data captured understood where possible.

steps.title: Assess and notify affected parties if warranted
steps.desc: Work with Legal/HR to determine whether individuals whose conversations were captured need to be informed, and consider law enforcement referral.
steps.outcome: Appropriate notification and referral decisions made.

steps.title: Document and review sensitive-space physical security
steps.desc: Log the incident (discreetly, given sensitivity) and consider periodic TSCM sweeps for high-value spaces going forward.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Determine what the device could have captured and for how long
steps.desc: Assess the device's field of view/audio range, battery/storage capacity, and how long it may have been in place, and what meetings/conversations occurred in range.
steps.outcome: Scope of potential exposure (what was said/shown, for how long) estimated.

steps.title: Sweep the area and related spaces for additional devices
steps.desc: Conduct a technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) sweep of the room and other sensitive spaces (executive offices, board rooms) for further devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether this was an isolated device or part of a broader operation.

ITID-14732.def: The covert physical attachment of a GPS or other location-tracking device to a vehicle or physical asset, without the knowledge or consent of its owner or operator, to monitor movement patterns.
ITID-14732.purpose: Captures the covert placement of a GPS tracking device on a vehicle or physical asset to monitor its location and movement over time.
scopeIncludes: GPS tracker discovered attached to a company or personal vehicle
Location tracker discovered attached to a shipped or transported asset (outside the supply-chain-interdiction context)
Devices discovered during routine vehicle inspection or by the vehicle's operator
scopeExcludes: Hidden cameras or audio recording devices (ITID-14731)
Hardware interdiction of shipped goods during transit for supply-chain compromise purposes (ITID-61431)
ITID-14732.severity: High — indicates active, targeted physical surveillance of a specific individual's or asset's movements, often preceding a physical confrontation, theft, or further targeting.
ITID-14732.priority: P1 upon discovery, particularly if attached to an executive's or high-risk individual's vehicle.
ITID-14732.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and, for executive or high-risk-individual targeting, executive protection; preserve the device for forensic handling and consider law-enforcement involvement.
indicators: Physical discovery of an unfamiliar device attached to a vehicle's undercarriage, wheel well, or exterior
Unexplained battery drain or unfamiliar Bluetooth/Wi-Fi device names detected near the vehicle
Pattern of an individual or vehicle repeatedly encountered at the target's frequent locations
vectors: Magnetic GPS tracker attached during a brief window when the vehicle is unattended (parking lot, valet, service visit)
Tracker concealed within an item placed in or on the vehicle
rootCauses: Vehicles left unattended in publicly accessible or unmonitored areas
No routine physical inspection procedure for executive or high-risk-individual vehicles
No policy addressing electronic sweep of vehicles for at-risk personnel
controls: Routine physical/electronic sweeps of executive or high-risk-individual vehicles
Secure, monitored parking for at-risk personnel
Executive protection program covering physical surveillance countermeasures
ITID-14732.detection: Relies on physical or electronic (Bluetooth/Wi-Fi scanning) inspection of the vehicle — no network- or endpoint-based detection applies.
ITID-14732.response: Do not immediately remove or destroy the device if evidence preservation may be needed; notify physical/executive security, assess whether the affected individual is at heightened personal risk, and consider law-enforcement involvement.
metrics: Count of tracking devices discovered per year
Coverage percentage of at-risk-personnel vehicles under routine sweep
ITID-14732.notes: A discovered tracker on a specific individual's vehicle should immediately raise the question of personal safety, not just information security — coordinate with executive protection/personal security resources where they exist.

playbook.name: Response: GPS Tracker Covertly Placed on Vehicle/Asset
playbook.description: For discovery of a covert GPS tracking device placed on a company vehicle or asset (or an employee's vehicle on company property).

steps.title: Document the device in place before removal
steps.desc: Photograph the tracker's location and mounting on the vehicle/asset, and note make/model if identifiable.
steps.outcome: Device documented in situ.

steps.title: Notify legal and, if it affects an individual's personal vehicle, HR
steps.desc: Loop in Legal (and HR if an employee's personal vehicle/safety is involved) before further action — this may indicate stalking, an insider risk, or corporate espionage.
steps.outcome: Legal/HR engaged and guiding next steps.

steps.title: Remove and preserve the device for analysis
steps.desc: Remove the tracker under proper chain of custody and analyze/have it analyzed for origin and data retrieval method.
steps.outcome: Device secured; origin understood where possible.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral, especially for personal-safety concerns
steps.desc: If an employee's personal safety may be at risk (e.g., a stalking scenario), prioritize law enforcement referral and support for the affected employee.
steps.outcome: Referral made and employee support provided if warranted.

steps.title: Document and review fleet/asset security
steps.desc: Log the incident and consider periodic vehicle/asset inspection as part of routine fleet security.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Determine how long it may have been in place and what it could reveal
steps.desc: Assess the vehicle/asset's recent usage and movement history to estimate what location/pattern data may have been exposed.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposed movement data estimated.

steps.title: Check other vehicles/assets for similar devices
steps.desc: Sweep other company vehicles or high-value assets for similar covert trackers.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether this is isolated or part of a broader pattern.

ITID-14733.def: The covert physical placement of a surveillance device — of a type not clearly a hidden camera/audio recorder or a GPS tracker — performed without the knowledge or consent of the affected individual(s).
ITID-14733.purpose: Catch-all for covert surveillance device placement that does not fit the more specific hidden-camera/audio or GPS-tracker leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Discovered devices of unclear or mixed function pending forensic examination
Cases initially logged before the device type is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Confirmed hidden camera or audio recording device (ITID-14731)
Confirmed GPS or location tracker (ITID-14732)
ITID-14733.severity: High, pending confirmation of the device's actual function — treat with the same urgency as ITID-14731/14732 until ruled out.
ITID-14733.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security and legal; reclassify to ITID-14731 or ITID-14732 once forensic examination confirms the device's function.
indicators: Physical discovery of an unfamiliar electronic device of unclear function
vectors: Device planted by an insider or outsider with physical access
rootCauses: No routine physical or electronic sweeps of sensitive spaces or vehicles
controls: Routine TSCM sweeps
Physical inspection procedures for unfamiliar objects/devices
ITID-14733.response: Preserve the device for forensic examination, notify physical security and legal, and reclassify once the device's function is confirmed.
metrics: Count of Unclassified device discoveries pending forensic confirmation
ITID-14733.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one — reclassify to ITID-14731 or ITID-14732 once the device's function is forensically confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Covert Surveillance Device Placement
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for covert surveillance device incidents not covered by the hidden-camera/audio or GPS-tracker categories.

steps.title: Document the device in place
steps.desc: Photograph and note the device's location and characteristics before disturbing it.
steps.outcome: Device documented in situ.

steps.title: Notify legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in Legal given the sensitivity of covert surveillance discoveries.
steps.outcome: Legal engaged.

steps.title: Recover and analyze the device
steps.desc: Remove under proper chain of custody and analyze for origin.
steps.outcome: Device secured; origin understood where possible.

steps.title: Consider law enforcement referral
steps.desc: Refer to law enforcement if warranted by the circumstances.
steps.outcome: Referral made if applicable.

steps.title: Document and review sensitive-space security
steps.desc: Log the incident and consider periodic sweeps for sensitive spaces.
steps.outcome: Improvement recommendation logged.

steps.title: Assess what the device could have captured
steps.desc: Determine the scope of potential exposure based on the device's placement and capability.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope estimated.

steps.title: Sweep for additional devices
steps.desc: Check related areas/assets for similar devices.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of the operation.
